decls.name: TauCeti.integrable_innerProbChar
decls.statement:
theorem integrable_innerProbChar (a : E) :
    Integrable (fun y => exp (⟪y, a⟫ * I)) μ

decls.name: TauCeti.exp_mul_conj_exp_inner
decls.statement:
theorem exp_mul_conj_exp_inner (y a b : E) :
    exp (⟪y, a⟫ * I) * conj (exp (⟪y, b⟫ * I)) = exp (⟪y, a - b⟫ * I)

decls.name: TauCeti.normSq_finset_sum_exp_eq_sum
decls.statement:
theorem normSq_finset_sum_exp_eq_sum {ι : Type*} (s : Finset ι) (c : ι → ℂ)
    (t : ι → E) (y : E) :
    ((normSq (∑ i ∈ s, c i * exp (⟪y, t i⟫ * I)) : ℝ) : ℂ)
      = ∑ i ∈ s, ∑ j ∈ s, c i * conj (c j) * exp (⟪y, t i - t j⟫ * I)

decls.name: TauCeti.charFun_sum_mul_conj_eq_integral
decls.doc:
The Hermitian form of `charFun μ` over a finite family `(cᵢ, tᵢ)` equals the integral of a
squared modulus. This is the engine behind positive-definiteness: the right-hand side is the
integral of a manifestly nonnegative function.
decls.statement:
theorem charFun_sum_mul_conj_eq_integral {ι : Type*} (s : Finset ι) (c : ι → ℂ) (t : ι → E) :
    ∑ i ∈ s, ∑ j ∈ s, c i * conj (c j) * charFun μ (t i - t j)
      = ((∫ y, normSq (∑ i ∈ s, c i * exp (⟪y, t i⟫ * I)) ∂μ : ℝ) : ℂ)

decls.name: TauCeti.charFun_sum_mul_conj_nonneg
decls.doc:
The Hermitian form of `charFun μ` over a finite family `(cᵢ, tᵢ)` is a nonnegative real:
`charFun μ` is a positive-definite function. This is `pd_quadratic_form_of_measure`.
decls.statement:
theorem charFun_sum_mul_conj_nonneg {ι : Type*} (s : Finset ι) (c : ι → ℂ) (t : ι → E) :
    0 ≤ ∑ i ∈ s, ∑ j ∈ s, c i * conj (c j) * charFun μ (t i - t j)

decls.name: TauCeti.charFun_fintype_sum_mul_conj_nonneg
decls.doc:
The `Fintype`-indexed form of positive-definiteness: summing over all of a finite index
type.
decls.statement:
theorem charFun_fintype_sum_mul_conj_nonneg {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] (c : ι → ℂ) (t : ι → E) :
    0 ≤ ∑ i, ∑ j, c i * conj (c j) * charFun μ (t i - t j)

decls.name: TauCeti.charFun_posSemidef
decls.doc:
The matrix `(charFun μ (tᵢ - tⱼ))ᵢⱼ` of a finite measure is positive semidefinite: the
matrix reformulation of the positive-definiteness of `charFun μ`.
decls.statement:
theorem charFun_posSemidef {ι : Type*} (t : ι → E) :
    (Matrix.of fun i j => charFun μ (t i - t j)).PosSemidef

decls.name: TauCeti.charFun_isPositiveDefiniteKernel
decls.doc:
The translation-invariant characteristic-function kernel
`(a, b) ↦ charFun μ (a - b)` is positive definite. This repackages the existing Gram-matrix
statement `charFun_posSemidef` as a `TauCeti.IsPositiveDefiniteKernel`.
decls.statement:
theorem charFun_isPositiveDefiniteKernel :
    IsPositiveDefiniteKernel (fun a b : E => MeasureTheory.charFun μ (a - b))

decls.name: TauCeti.charFun_star_kernel_isPositiveDefiniteKernel_of_star_eq_neg
decls.doc:
With an explicit `star = -` involution, the kernel associated to `charFun μ` by the generic
positive-definite-function construction, `(a, b) ↦ charFun μ (a + star b)`, is positive
definite. Under `hstar` this kernel coincides with the translation-invariant kernel of
`charFun_isPositiveDefiniteKernel`.
decls.statement:
theorem charFun_star_kernel_isPositiveDefiniteKernel_of_star_eq_neg [StarAddMonoid E]
    (hstar : ∀ x : E, star x = -x) :
    IsPositiveDefiniteKernel (fun a b : E => MeasureTheory.charFun μ (a + star b))

decls.name: TauCeti.charFun_isPositiveDefinite_of_star_eq_neg
decls.doc:
The characteristic function of a finite measure is positive definite for any additive-group
involution that is explicitly negation. This is the generic-predicate form of
`charFun_fintype_sum_mul_conj_nonneg`, using
`F (vᵢ + star vⱼ) = charFun μ (vᵢ - vⱼ)`.
decls.statement:
theorem charFun_isPositiveDefinite_of_star_eq_neg [StarAddMonoid E]
    (hstar : ∀ x : E, star x = -x) :
    IsPositiveDefinite (MeasureTheory.charFun μ)

decls.name: TauCeti.continuous_charFun_and_isPositiveDefinite_of_star_eq_neg
decls.doc:
The characteristic function of a finite measure on a second-countable real inner product space
is continuous and positive definite, provided the chosen involution is negation. This is the
forward bridge toward Bochner's theorem in the language of `TauCeti.IsPositiveDefinite`.
decls.statement:
theorem continuous_charFun_and_isPositiveDefinite_of_star_eq_neg [StarAddMonoid E]
    (hstar : ∀ x : E, star x = -x) :
    Continuous (MeasureTheory.charFun μ) ∧ IsPositiveDefinite (MeasureTheory.charFun μ)

decls.name: TauCeti.integral_exp_neg_two_pi_inner_eq_charFun_neg_two_pi_smul
decls.doc:
The Fourier-convention integral of a finite measure, written in exponential normal form,
is Mathlib's characteristic function evaluated at `(-2π) • a`.
decls.statement:
theorem integral_exp_neg_two_pi_inner_eq_charFun_neg_two_pi_smul (a : V) :
    ∫ q, Complex.exp (-(2 * Real.pi * Complex.I * (inner ℝ q a : ℝ))) ∂μ =
      MeasureTheory.charFun μ ((-2 * Real.pi) • a)

decls.name: TauCeti.integral_fourierAtom_eq_charFun_neg_two_pi_smul
decls.doc:
The Fourier-convention integral of a finite measure, written with the atom
`exp (-2πi⟪a, q⟫)`, is Mathlib's characteristic function evaluated at `(-2π) • a`.
decls.statement:
theorem integral_fourierAtom_eq_charFun_neg_two_pi_smul (a : V) :
    ∫ q, fourierAtom a q ∂μ = MeasureTheory.charFun μ ((-2 * Real.pi) • a)

decls.name: TauCeti.fourierConventionCharFun_isPositiveDefinite_of_star_eq_neg
decls.doc:
The Fourier-convention transform of a finite measure is positive definite for any additive
group involution that is explicitly negation. This transports the positive-definiteness of
`charFun μ` through the `-2π` additive rescaling.
decls.statement:
theorem fourierConventionCharFun_isPositiveDefinite_of_star_eq_neg [StarAddMonoid W]
    (hstar : ∀ x : W, star x = -x) :
    IsPositiveDefinite (fun a : W => ∫ q, fourierAtom a q ∂ν)

decls.name: TauCeti.fourierConventionCharFun_isPositiveDefiniteKernel
decls.doc:
The translation-invariant kernel attached to the Fourier-convention transform of a finite
measure is positive definite. This is the kernel form of
`fourierConventionCharFun_isPositiveDefinite_of_star_eq_neg`, avoiding any explicit choice of
involution on the domain.
decls.statement:
theorem fourierConventionCharFun_isPositiveDefiniteKernel :
    IsPositiveDefiniteKernel fun a b : W => ∫ q, fourierAtom (a - b) q ∂ν

decls.name: TauCeti.continuous_fourierConventionCharFun
decls.doc:
The Fourier-convention transform of a finite measure is continuous. This is just Mathlib's
continuity of `charFun`, transported through the `-2π` rescaling.
decls.statement:
theorem continuous_fourierConventionCharFun [SecondCountableTopology W] :
    Continuous fun a : W => ∫ q, fourierAtom a q ∂ν

decls.name: TauCeti.continuous_cexp_neg_mul_sq_norm
decls.doc: The Gaussian `a ↦ exp (-c‖a‖²)` is continuous on `V` for every real `c`.
decls.statement:
theorem continuous_cexp_neg_mul_sq_norm (c : ℝ) :
    Continuous fun a : V => Complex.exp (-(c * ‖a‖ ^ 2 : ℝ))

decls.name: TauCeti.charFun_stdGaussian_sqrt_smul
decls.doc:
The characteristic function of the standard Gaussian measure on `V`, with its argument
rescaled by `√(2c)`, is the Gaussian `a ↦ exp (-c‖a‖²)`.
decls.statement:
theorem charFun_stdGaussian_sqrt_smul {c : ℝ} (hc : 0 ≤ c) (a : V) :
    charFun (stdGaussian V) (Real.sqrt (2 * c) • a) = Complex.exp (-(c * ‖a‖ ^ 2 : ℝ))

decls.name: TauCeti.isPositiveDefinite_cexp_neg_mul_sq_norm
decls.doc:
The Gaussian `a ↦ exp (-c‖a‖²)` on a finite-dimensional real inner-product space is positive
definite for every `c ≥ 0`, under the negation involution `a⋆ = -a`.

It is the characteristic function of the standard Gaussian measure with the argument rescaled
by `√(2c)`.
decls.statement:
theorem isPositiveDefinite_cexp_neg_mul_sq_norm [StarAddMonoid V]
    (hstar : ∀ x : V, star x = -x) {c : ℝ} (hc : 0 ≤ c) :
    IsPositiveDefinite fun a : V => Complex.exp (-(c * ‖a‖ ^ 2 : ℝ))

decls.name: TauCeti.isPositiveDefiniteKernel_cexp_neg_mul_sq_norm
decls.doc:
The translation-invariant kernel attached to the Gaussian, `(a, b) ↦ exp (-c‖a - b‖²)`, is
positive definite for every `c ≥ 0`. This is the kernel form of
`isPositiveDefinite_cexp_neg_mul_sq_norm`, avoiding any explicit choice of involution on the
domain.
decls.statement:
theorem isPositiveDefiniteKernel_cexp_neg_mul_sq_norm {c : ℝ} (hc : 0 ≤ c) :
    IsPositiveDefiniteKernel fun a b : V => Complex.exp (-(c * ‖a - b‖ ^ 2 : ℝ))

decls.name: TauCeti.isPositiveDefinite_cexp_neg_sq_norm
decls.doc:
The positive-definiteness half of the Gaussian acceptance example (`c = 1`):
`a ↦ exp (-‖a‖²)` is positive definite under the negation involution.
decls.statement:
theorem isPositiveDefinite_cexp_neg_sq_norm [StarAddMonoid V] (hstar : ∀ x : V, star x = -x) :
    IsPositiveDefinite fun a : V => Complex.exp (-(‖a‖ ^ 2 : ℝ))

decls.name: TauCeti.isPositiveDefiniteKernel_cexp_neg_sq_norm
decls.doc:
The involution-free kernel form of the Gaussian acceptance example (`c = 1`):
`(a, b) ↦ exp (-‖a - b‖²)` is a positive-definite kernel. Unlike
`isPositiveDefinite_cexp_neg_sq_norm`, this requires no choice of involution on `V`.
decls.statement:
theorem isPositiveDefiniteKernel_cexp_neg_sq_norm :
    IsPositiveDefiniteKernel fun a b : V => Complex.exp (-(‖a - b‖ ^ 2 : ℝ))

decls.name: TauCeti.dslope_eq_integral_deriv
decls.doc:
The `dslope` integral representation on a convex open set: when `f` is
differentiable on `U` and both `c, w ∈ U` (so the segment `[c, w] ⊆ U`), then
`dslope f c w` equals the integral of the derivative of `f` along the segment.
decls.statement:
theorem dslope_eq_integral_deriv {U : Set ℂ} (hU : Convex ℝ U) (hU_open : IsOpen U)
    (hf : DifferentiableOn ℂ f U) {c w : ℂ} (hc : c ∈ U) (hw : w ∈ U) :
    dslope f c w = ∫ t in (0 : ℝ)..1, deriv f (c + t • (w - c))

decls.name: TauCeti.exists_compact_tube_prod
decls.statement:
lemma exists_compact_tube_prod {U : Set ℂ} (hU : Convex ℝ U) (hU_open : IsOpen U)
    {c₀ w₀ : ℂ} (hc₀ : c₀ ∈ U) (hw₀ : w₀ ∈ U) :
    ∃ ε > 0, ∃ K ⊆ U, IsCompact K ∧
      ∀ c ∈ Metric.ball c₀ ε, ∀ w ∈ Metric.ball w₀ ε,
        ∀ t ∈ Icc (0 : ℝ) 1, c + t • (w - c) ∈ K

decls.name: TauCeti.continuousOn_dslope_prod_of_convex
decls.doc:
Joint continuity of `(c, w) ↦ dslope f c w` on `U × U` for `f` differentiable
on open convex `U`.
decls.statement:
theorem continuousOn_dslope_prod_of_convex {U : Set ℂ} (hU : Convex ℝ U)
    (hU_open : IsOpen U) (hf : DifferentiableOn ℂ f U) :
    ContinuousOn (fun p : ℂ × ℂ ↦ dslope f p.1 p.2) (U ×ˢ U)

decls.name: TauCeti.continuousOn_dslope_prod
decls.doc:
**Joint continuity of `(c, w) ↦ dslope f c w` on `U ×ˢ U`** for `f` differentiable on an
arbitrary open set `U` (no convexity assumption).
decls.title: Joint continuity of `(c, w) ↦ dslope f c w` on `U ×ˢ U`
decls.statement:
theorem continuousOn_dslope_prod {U : Set ℂ} (hU_open : IsOpen U)
    (hf : DifferentiableOn ℂ f U) :
    ContinuousOn (fun p : ℂ × ℂ ↦ dslope f p.1 p.2) (U ×ˢ U)

decls.name: TauCeti.continuousOn_dslope_first_arg
decls.doc:
**Continuity of `c ↦ dslope f c w₀` on any open set `U`** (no convexity).
Follows from `continuousOn_dslope_prod` by partial application.
decls.title: Continuity of `c ↦ dslope f c w₀` on any open set `U`
decls.statement:
theorem continuousOn_dslope_first_arg {U : Set ℂ} (hU_open : IsOpen U)
    (hf : DifferentiableOn ℂ f U) {w₀ : ℂ} (hw₀ : w₀ ∈ U) :
    ContinuousOn (fun c ↦ dslope f c w₀) U

decls.name: TauCeti.deriv_dslope_bounded_on_compact
decls.doc:
**Uniform bound on `deriv (dslope f c) w`.** For `f` differentiable on an open set `U`, with `c`
ranging over a compact subset of `U` and `w` over a small ball around a point `w₀ ∈ U`, the norm
`‖deriv (dslope f c) w‖` is bounded by a single constant.
decls.title: Uniform bound on `deriv (dslope f c) w`
decls.statement:
theorem deriv_dslope_bounded_on_compact {U : Set ℂ} (hU_open : IsOpen U)
    (hf : DifferentiableOn ℂ f U) {K_c : Set ℂ} (hK_compact : IsCompact K_c)
    (hK_sub : K_c ⊆ U) {w₀ : ℂ} (hw₀ : w₀ ∈ U) :
    ∃ C > 0, ∃ δ > 0, ∀ c ∈ K_c, ∀ w ∈ Metric.ball w₀ δ,
      ‖deriv (dslope f c) w‖ ≤ C

decls.name: TauCeti.deriv_deriv_nonpos_of_isLocalMax
decls.doc:
**Necessary second-derivative test.** At a local maximum of a continuous function
`g : ℝ → ℝ`, the value `deriv (deriv g) t₀` is nonpositive.
decls.title: Necessary second-derivative test

decls.name: TauCeti.deriv_deriv_nonneg_of_isLocalMin
decls.doc:
**Necessary second-derivative test, minimum version.** At a local minimum of a continuous
function `g : ℝ → ℝ`, the value `deriv (deriv g) t₀` is nonnegative.
decls.title: Necessary second-derivative test, minimum version

decls.name: TauCeti.halfLinePrimitive
decls.doc:
The primitive of `f` on the nonnegative half-line. The `max` canonically extends the
integrand to negative arguments; on `[0, ∞)` this is `∫₀ᵗ f`.
decls.statement: def halfLinePrimitive (f : ℝ → ℝ) (t : ℝ) : ℝ

decls.name: TauCeti.halfLinePrimitive_def
decls.doc:
The unconditional defining equation of `halfLinePrimitive`, usable in downstream files where
the body of the definition is not available.
decls.statement:
theorem halfLinePrimitive_def (f : ℝ → ℝ) (t : ℝ) :
    halfLinePrimitive f t = ∫ x in (0 : ℝ)..t, f (max x 0)

decls.name: TauCeti.continuous_comp_max_zero
decls.doc:
If `f` is continuous on `[0, ∞)`, then its extension `x ↦ f (max x 0)` is continuous on all
of `ℝ`.
decls.statement:
theorem continuous_comp_max_zero (hf : ContinuousOn f (Ici 0)) :
    Continuous fun x : ℝ ↦ f (max x 0)

decls.name: TauCeti.halfLinePrimitive_eq_integral_of_nonneg
decls.doc:
On the nonnegative half-line, `halfLinePrimitive` is the ordinary integral of `f` from
zero.
decls.statement:
theorem halfLinePrimitive_eq_integral_of_nonneg (ht : 0 ≤ t) :
    halfLinePrimitive f t = ∫ x in (0 : ℝ)..t, f x

decls.name: TauCeti.halfLinePrimitive_of_nonpos
decls.doc: On the nonpositive half-line, `halfLinePrimitive` is the linear extension `t ↦ t * f 0`.
decls.statement: theorem halfLinePrimitive_of_nonpos (ht : t ≤ 0) : halfLinePrimitive f t = t * f 0

decls.name: TauCeti.halfLinePrimitive_zero
decls.doc: The value of `halfLinePrimitive f` at the origin is `0`.
decls.statement: theorem halfLinePrimitive_zero (f : ℝ → ℝ) : halfLinePrimitive f 0 = 0

decls.name: TauCeti.continuous_halfLinePrimitive
decls.doc:
If `f` is continuous on `[0, ∞)`, then `halfLinePrimitive f` is continuous on all of `ℝ`; the
`max` extension of the integrand makes the primitive continuous through the origin.
decls.statement:
theorem continuous_halfLinePrimitive (hf : ContinuousOn f (Ici 0)) :
    Continuous (halfLinePrimitive f)

decls.name: TauCeti.hasDerivAt_halfLinePrimitive
decls.doc:
If `f` is continuous on `[0, ∞)`, then `halfLinePrimitive f` has derivative `f t` at every
`t ≥ 0`. The `max` extension of the integrand makes the derivative at `t = 0` two-sided.
decls.statement:
theorem hasDerivAt_halfLinePrimitive (hf : ContinuousOn f (Ici 0)) (ht : 0 ≤ t) :
    HasDerivAt (halfLinePrimitive f) (f t) t

decls.name: TauCeti.deriv_halfLinePrimitive
decls.doc:
If `f` is continuous on `[0, ∞)`, then the derivative of `halfLinePrimitive f` is `f` at
every `t ≥ 0`.
decls.statement:
theorem deriv_halfLinePrimitive (hf : ContinuousOn f (Ici 0)) (ht : 0 ≤ t) :
    deriv (halfLinePrimitive f) t = f t

decls.name: TauCeti.ContDiffOn.hasDerivAt_iteratedDerivWithin
decls.doc:
At a point `x` in the interior of a unique-differentiability set `s` (`s ∈ 𝓝 x`),
the derivative of the `k`-th iterated derivative-within-`s` of a `C^(k+1)` function is the
`(k+1)`-th iterated derivative-within-`s`.
decls.statement:
theorem ContDiffOn.hasDerivAt_iteratedDerivWithin
    {𝕜 E : Type*} [NontriviallyNormedField 𝕜] [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace 𝕜 E]
    {g : 𝕜 → E} {s : Set 𝕜} {k : ℕ}
    (hf : ContDiffOn 𝕜 ((k + 1 : ℕ) : WithTop ℕ∞) g s)
    (hs : UniqueDiffOn 𝕜 s) {x : 𝕜} (hx : s ∈ nhds x) :
    HasDerivAt (iteratedDerivWithin k g s) (iteratedDerivWithin (k + 1) g s x) x

decls.name: TauCeti.hasDerivWithinAt_Ioi_of_tendsto_deriv
decls.doc:
A function continuous at `t₀`, eventually differentiable on the right, whose derivative
tends to `L` from the right, has right derivative `L` at `t₀`.
decls.statement:
theorem hasDerivWithinAt_Ioi_of_tendsto_deriv {γ : ℝ → E} {t₀ : ℝ} {L : E}
    (hγ_cont : ContinuousAt γ t₀)
    (hγ_diff : ∀ᶠ t in 𝓝[>] t₀, DifferentiableAt ℝ γ t)
    (hL : Tendsto (deriv γ) (𝓝[>] t₀) (𝓝 L)) :
    HasDerivWithinAt γ L (Ioi t₀) t₀

decls.name: TauCeti.hasDerivWithinAt_Iio_of_tendsto_deriv
decls.doc:
A function continuous at `t₀`, eventually differentiable on the left, whose derivative
tends to `L` from the left, has left derivative `L` at `t₀`.
decls.statement:
theorem hasDerivWithinAt_Iio_of_tendsto_deriv {γ : ℝ → E} {t₀ : ℝ} {L : E}
    (hγ_cont : ContinuousAt γ t₀)
    (hγ_diff : ∀ᶠ t in 𝓝[<] t₀, DifferentiableAt ℝ γ t)
    (hL : Tendsto (deriv γ) (𝓝[<] t₀) (𝓝 L)) :
    HasDerivWithinAt γ L (Iio t₀) t₀

decls.name: TauCeti.IsCompletelyMonotone
decls.doc:
A function `f : ℝ → ℝ` is **completely monotone** if it is `C^∞` on the closed half-line
`[0, ∞)` and its iterated derivatives within `[0, ∞)` alternate in sign:
`0 ≤ (-1)ⁿ f⁽ⁿ⁾(t)` for every `n` and every `t ≥ 0`. The smoothness clause prevents the sign
condition from being satisfied vacuously by a junk iterated derivative.
decls.statement: def IsCompletelyMonotone (f : ℝ → ℝ) : Prop

decls.name: TauCeti.isCompletelyMonotone_iff
decls.doc:
`IsCompletelyMonotone f` unfolds to its defining conjunction: `f` is `C^∞` on `[0, ∞)`
and its iterated derivatives within `[0, ∞)` alternate in sign.
decls.statement:
lemma isCompletelyMonotone_iff {f : ℝ → ℝ} :
    IsCompletelyMonotone f ↔
      ContDiffOn ℝ ∞ f (Ici 0) ∧
        ∀ n : ℕ, ∀ t : ℝ, 0 ≤ t → 0 ≤ (-1) ^ n * iteratedDerivWithin n f (Ici 0) t

decls.name: TauCeti.isCompletelyMonotone_iff_absolutelyMonotoneOn_comp_neg
decls.doc:
Completely monotone functions are exactly absolutely monotone functions after reflecting the
closed half-line through zero.
decls.statement:
lemma isCompletelyMonotone_iff_absolutelyMonotoneOn_comp_neg {f : ℝ → ℝ} :
    IsCompletelyMonotone f ↔ AbsolutelyMonotoneOn (fun u => f (-u)) (Iic 0)

decls.name: TauCeti.IsCompletelyMonotone.contDiffOn
decls.doc: A completely monotone function is `C^∞` on `[0, ∞)`.
decls.statement: lemma contDiffOn (hf : IsCompletelyMonotone f) : ContDiffOn ℝ ∞ f (Ici 0)

decls.name: TauCeti.IsCompletelyMonotone.neg_one_pow_mul_iteratedDerivWithin_nonneg
decls.doc:
The sign-alternation property of the iterated derivatives of a completely monotone
function: `0 ≤ (-1)ⁿ f⁽ⁿ⁾(t)` for every `n` and every `t ≥ 0`.
decls.statement:
lemma neg_one_pow_mul_iteratedDerivWithin_nonneg (hf : IsCompletelyMonotone f) (n : ℕ) {t : ℝ}
    (ht : 0 ≤ t) : 0 ≤ (-1) ^ n * iteratedDerivWithin n f (Ici 0) t

decls.name: TauCeti.IsCompletelyMonotone.neg_one_pow_mul_iteratedDeriv_nonneg
decls.doc:
On the open half-line, the completely monotone sign condition can be read using ordinary
iterated derivatives instead of derivatives within `[0, ∞)`.
decls.statement:
lemma neg_one_pow_mul_iteratedDeriv_nonneg (hf : IsCompletelyMonotone f) (n : ℕ) {t : ℝ}
    (ht : 0 < t) : 0 ≤ (-1) ^ n * iteratedDeriv n f t

decls.name: TauCeti.IsCompletelyMonotone.nonneg
decls.doc: A completely monotone function is nonnegative on `[0, ∞)`.
decls.statement: lemma nonneg (hf : IsCompletelyMonotone f) {t : ℝ} (ht : 0 ≤ t) : 0 ≤ f t

decls.name: TauCeti.IsCompletelyMonotone.derivWithin_nonpos
decls.doc:
The derivative within `[0, ∞)` of a completely monotone function is nonpositive: it is
nonincreasing.
decls.statement:
lemma derivWithin_nonpos (hf : IsCompletelyMonotone f) {t : ℝ} (ht : 0 ≤ t) :
    derivWithin f (Ici 0) t ≤ 0

decls.name: TauCeti.IsCompletelyMonotone.congr
decls.doc:
Complete monotonicity is determined by the values of the function on `[0, ∞)`: if `g` agrees
with a completely monotone `f` throughout `[0, ∞)`, then `g` is completely monotone too. Both the
smoothness clause and the sign condition only see the function within `[0, ∞)`.
decls.statement:
lemma congr (hf : IsCompletelyMonotone f) (h : Set.EqOn g f (Ici 0)) :
    IsCompletelyMonotone g

decls.name: TauCeti.IsCompletelyMonotone.antitoneOn
decls.doc: A completely monotone function is nonincreasing on `[0, ∞)`.
decls.statement: lemma antitoneOn (hf : IsCompletelyMonotone f) : AntitoneOn f (Ici 0)

decls.name: TauCeti.IsCompletelyMonotone.exists_nonneg_tendsto_atTop
decls.doc:
A completely monotone function has a limit `L ≥ 0` at infinity: it is antitone on `[0, ∞)`
and bounded below by `0`.
decls.statement:
lemma exists_nonneg_tendsto_atTop (hf : IsCompletelyMonotone f) :
    ∃ L, Tendsto f atTop (nhds L) ∧ 0 ≤ L

decls.name: TauCeti.IsCompletelyMonotone.le_of_tendsto_atTop
decls.doc: A completely monotone function lies above its limit at infinity on `[0, ∞)`.
decls.statement:
lemma le_of_tendsto_atTop (hcm : IsCompletelyMonotone f) {L : ℝ}
    (hL : Tendsto f atTop (nhds L)) {T : ℝ} (hT : 0 ≤ T) : L ≤ f T

decls.name: TauCeti.IsCompletelyMonotone.hasDerivAt_iteratedDerivWithin_succ
decls.doc:
For a completely monotone `f`, the `k`-th iterated derivative within `[0, ∞)` is
differentiable at any `t > 0`, with derivative the `(k+1)`-th iterated derivative.
decls.statement:
lemma hasDerivAt_iteratedDerivWithin_succ
    (hcm : IsCompletelyMonotone f) (k : ℕ) {t : ℝ} (ht : 0 < t) :
    HasDerivAt (iteratedDerivWithin k f (Ici 0))
      (iteratedDerivWithin (k + 1) f (Ici 0) t) t

decls.name: TauCeti.IsCompletelyMonotone.add
decls.doc: Completely monotone functions are closed under addition.
decls.statement:
lemma add (hf : IsCompletelyMonotone f) (hg : IsCompletelyMonotone g) :
    IsCompletelyMonotone (f + g)

decls.name: TauCeti.IsCompletelyMonotone.smul
decls.doc: Completely monotone functions are closed under multiplication by a nonnegative constant.
decls.statement:
lemma smul (hf : IsCompletelyMonotone f) {c : ℝ} (hc : 0 ≤ c) :
    IsCompletelyMonotone (c • f)

decls.name: TauCeti.isCompletelyMonotone_const
decls.doc: A nonnegative constant function is completely monotone.
decls.statement:
lemma isCompletelyMonotone_const {c : ℝ} (hc : 0 ≤ c) :
    IsCompletelyMonotone (fun _ : ℝ => c)

decls.name: TauCeti.IsCompletelyMonotone.sum
decls.doc: Completely monotone functions are closed under finite sums.

decls.name: TauCeti.isCompletelyMonotone_exp_neg_mul
decls.doc:
The prototype completely monotone function `t ↦ e^{-x t}` for `x ≥ 0`. Its `n`-th
derivative is `(-x)ⁿ e^{-x t}`, so `(-1)ⁿ` times it is `xⁿ e^{-x t} ≥ 0`.
decls.statement:
lemma isCompletelyMonotone_exp_neg_mul {x : ℝ} (hx : 0 ≤ x) :
    IsCompletelyMonotone (fun t => Real.exp (-x * t))

decls.name: TauCeti.IsCompletelyMonotoneOnIoi
decls.doc:
Complete monotonicity on the open half-line `(0, ∞)`: the function is `C^∞` there and its
ordinary iterated derivatives alternate in sign. This is the version used for derivatives of
Bernstein functions, whose right derivatives need not be finite at `0`.
decls.statement: def IsCompletelyMonotoneOnIoi (f : ℝ → ℝ) : Prop

decls.name: TauCeti.IsCompletelyMonotoneOnIoi.contDiffOn
decls.doc: A completely monotone function on `(0, ∞)` is smooth there.
decls.statement: lemma contDiffOn (hf : IsCompletelyMonotoneOnIoi f) : ContDiffOn ℝ ∞ f (Ioi 0)

decls.name: TauCeti.IsCompletelyMonotoneOnIoi.neg_one_pow_mul_iteratedDeriv_nonneg
decls.doc: The sign-alternation property on `(0, ∞)`.
decls.statement:
lemma neg_one_pow_mul_iteratedDeriv_nonneg (hf : IsCompletelyMonotoneOnIoi f) (n : ℕ) {t : ℝ}
    (ht : 0 < t) : 0 ≤ (-1) ^ n * iteratedDeriv n f t

decls.name: TauCeti.IsCompletelyMonotoneOnIoi.nonneg
decls.doc: A completely monotone function on `(0, ∞)` is nonnegative there.
decls.statement: lemma nonneg (hf : IsCompletelyMonotoneOnIoi f) {t : ℝ} (ht : 0 < t) : 0 ≤ f t

decls.name: TauCeti.IsCompletelyMonotoneOnIoi.nonneg_of_continuousWithinAt
decls.doc:
A function completely monotone on `(0, ∞)` that is continuous within `[0, ∞)` at the origin
is nonnegative on all of `[0, ∞)`: nonnegativity on `(0, ∞)` passes to the boundary point `0` in
the limit.
decls.statement:
lemma nonneg_of_continuousWithinAt (hf : IsCompletelyMonotoneOnIoi f)
    (hcont : ContinuousWithinAt f (Ici 0) 0) {t : ℝ} (ht : 0 ≤ t) : 0 ≤ f t

decls.name: TauCeti.IsCompletelyMonotoneOnIoi.deriv_nonpos
decls.doc: The derivative of a completely monotone function on `(0, ∞)` is nonpositive there.
decls.statement:
lemma deriv_nonpos (hf : IsCompletelyMonotoneOnIoi f) {t : ℝ} (ht : 0 < t) :
    deriv f t ≤ 0

decls.name: TauCeti.IsCompletelyMonotoneOnIoi.congr
decls.doc: Complete monotonicity on `(0, ∞)` is preserved by pointwise equality there.
decls.statement:
lemma congr (hf : IsCompletelyMonotoneOnIoi f) (h : Set.EqOn g f (Ioi 0)) :
    IsCompletelyMonotoneOnIoi g

decls.name: TauCeti.IsCompletelyMonotoneOnIoi.add
decls.doc: Complete monotonicity on `(0, ∞)` is closed under addition.
decls.statement:
lemma add (hf : IsCompletelyMonotoneOnIoi f) (hg : IsCompletelyMonotoneOnIoi g) :
    IsCompletelyMonotoneOnIoi (f + g)

decls.name: TauCeti.IsCompletelyMonotoneOnIoi.smul
decls.doc: Complete monotonicity on `(0, ∞)` is closed under multiplication by a nonnegative constant.
decls.statement:
lemma smul (hf : IsCompletelyMonotoneOnIoi f) {c : ℝ} (hc : 0 ≤ c) :
    IsCompletelyMonotoneOnIoi (c • f)

decls.name: TauCeti.IsCompletelyMonotone.isCompletelyMonotoneOnIoi
decls.doc: The closed-half-line Tau Ceti predicate restricts to complete monotonicity on `(0, ∞)`.
decls.statement:
lemma _root_.TauCeti.IsCompletelyMonotone.isCompletelyMonotoneOnIoi
    (hf : IsCompletelyMonotone f) : IsCompletelyMonotoneOnIoi f

decls.name: TauCeti.IsBernsteinFunction
decls.doc:
A function `f : ℝ → ℝ` is a **Bernstein function** if it is continuous and nonnegative on
`[0, ∞)`, `C^∞` on `(0, ∞)`, and its ordinary derivative is completely monotone on `(0, ∞)`.
The open-half-line derivative condition is the standard one and permits boundary singularities
such as the right derivative of `sqrt` at `0`.
decls.statement: def IsBernsteinFunction (f : ℝ → ℝ) : Prop

decls.name: TauCeti.isBernsteinFunction_iff
decls.doc:
A function is Bernstein exactly when it is continuous and nonnegative on `[0, ∞)`, smooth
on `(0, ∞)`, and has completely monotone derivative there. The body of `IsBernsteinFunction` is
not `@[expose]`d, so this is how downstream files build the predicate from its four clauses.
decls.statement:
theorem isBernsteinFunction_iff {f : ℝ → ℝ} :
    IsBernsteinFunction f ↔
      ContinuousOn f (Ici 0) ∧ ContDiffOn ℝ ∞ f (Ioi 0) ∧
        (∀ t : ℝ, 0 ≤ t → 0 ≤ f t) ∧ IsCompletelyMonotoneOnIoi (deriv f)

decls.name: TauCeti.IsBernsteinFunction.continuousOn
decls.doc: A Bernstein function is continuous on `[0, ∞)`.
decls.statement: lemma continuousOn (hf : IsBernsteinFunction f) : ContinuousOn f (Ici 0)

decls.name: TauCeti.IsBernsteinFunction.contDiffOn
decls.doc: A Bernstein function is `C^∞` on `(0, ∞)`.
decls.statement: lemma contDiffOn (hf : IsBernsteinFunction f) : ContDiffOn ℝ ∞ f (Ioi 0)

decls.name: TauCeti.IsBernsteinFunction.nonneg
decls.doc: A Bernstein function is nonnegative on `[0, ∞)`.
decls.statement: lemma nonneg (hf : IsBernsteinFunction f) {t : ℝ} (ht : 0 ≤ t) : 0 ≤ f t

decls.name: TauCeti.IsBernsteinFunction.deriv_isCompletelyMonotoneOnIoi
decls.doc: The ordinary derivative of a Bernstein function is completely monotone on `(0, ∞)`.
decls.statement:
lemma deriv_isCompletelyMonotoneOnIoi (hf : IsBernsteinFunction f) :
    IsCompletelyMonotoneOnIoi (deriv f)

decls.name: TauCeti.IsBernsteinFunction.differentiableOn
decls.doc: A Bernstein function is differentiable on `(0, ∞)`.
decls.statement: lemma differentiableOn (hf : IsBernsteinFunction f) : DifferentiableOn ℝ f (Ioi 0)

decls.name: TauCeti.IsBernsteinFunction.deriv_nonneg
decls.doc:
The derivative of a Bernstein function is nonnegative on `(0, ∞)`: a Bernstein function is
nondecreasing.
decls.statement: lemma deriv_nonneg (hf : IsBernsteinFunction f) {t : ℝ} (ht : 0 < t) : 0 ≤ deriv f t

decls.name: TauCeti.IsBernsteinFunction.monotoneOn
decls.doc: A Bernstein function is nondecreasing on `[0, ∞)`.
decls.statement: lemma monotoneOn (hf : IsBernsteinFunction f) : MonotoneOn f (Ici 0)

decls.name: TauCeti.IsBernsteinFunction.concaveOn
decls.doc: A Bernstein function is concave on `[0, ∞)`: its derivative is nonincreasing.
decls.statement: lemma concaveOn (hf : IsBernsteinFunction f) : ConcaveOn ℝ (Ici 0) f

decls.name: TauCeti.IsBernsteinFunction.congr
decls.doc: Being a Bernstein function depends only on the values on `[0, ∞)`.
decls.statement:
theorem congr (hf : IsBernsteinFunction f) (h : Set.EqOn g f (Ici 0)) :
    IsBernsteinFunction g

decls.name: TauCeti.IsBernsteinFunction.add
decls.doc: Bernstein functions are closed under addition.
decls.statement:
theorem add (hf : IsBernsteinFunction f) (hg : IsBernsteinFunction g) :
    IsBernsteinFunction (f + g)

decls.name: TauCeti.IsBernsteinFunction.smul
decls.doc: Bernstein functions are closed under multiplication by a nonnegative constant.
decls.statement:
theorem smul (hf : IsBernsteinFunction f) {c : ℝ} (hc : 0 ≤ c) :
    IsBernsteinFunction (c • f)

decls.name: TauCeti.isBernsteinFunction_const
decls.doc: A nonnegative constant function is a Bernstein function.
decls.statement:
theorem isBernsteinFunction_const {c : ℝ} (hc : 0 ≤ c) :
    IsBernsteinFunction (fun _ : ℝ => c)

decls.name: TauCeti.isBernsteinFunction_zero
decls.doc: The zero function is a Bernstein function.
decls.statement: theorem isBernsteinFunction_zero : IsBernsteinFunction (fun _ : ℝ => (0 : ℝ))

decls.name: TauCeti.IsBernsteinFunction.const_add
decls.doc: Adding a nonnegative constant to a Bernstein function again gives a Bernstein function.
decls.statement:
theorem const_add {f : ℝ → ℝ} (hf : IsBernsteinFunction f) {c : ℝ} (hc : 0 ≤ c) :
    IsBernsteinFunction (fun t => c + f t)

decls.name: TauCeti.IsBernsteinFunction.sum
decls.doc: Bernstein functions are closed under finite sums.

decls.name: TauCeti.isBernsteinFunction_id
decls.doc:
The identity function is a Bernstein function: it is nonnegative on `[0, ∞)` with constant
derivative `1`.
decls.statement: theorem isBernsteinFunction_id : IsBernsteinFunction (fun t : ℝ => t)

decls.name: TauCeti.isBernsteinFunction_affine
decls.doc: An affine function `t ↦ c + d t` with nonnegative coefficients is a Bernstein function.
decls.statement:
theorem isBernsteinFunction_affine {c d : ℝ} (hc : 0 ≤ c) (hd : 0 ≤ d) :
    IsBernsteinFunction (fun t : ℝ => c + d * t)

decls.name: TauCeti.isBernsteinFunction_one_sub_exp_neg_mul
decls.doc:
The prototype Bernstein function `t ↦ 1 - e^{-x t}` for `x ≥ 0`: it is nonnegative on
`[0, ∞)` and its derivative `t ↦ x e^{-x t}` is completely monotone.
decls.statement:
theorem isBernsteinFunction_one_sub_exp_neg_mul {x : ℝ} (hx : 0 ≤ x) :
    IsBernsteinFunction (fun t : ℝ => 1 - Real.exp (-x * t))

decls.name: TauCeti.IsCompletelyMonotoneOnIoi.isBernsteinFunction_halfLinePrimitive
decls.doc:
The primitive on `[0, ∞)` of a function that is completely monotone on `(0, ∞)` and
continuous on `[0, ∞)` is a Bernstein function.
decls.statement:
theorem isBernsteinFunction_halfLinePrimitive (hf : IsCompletelyMonotoneOnIoi f)
    (hcont : ContinuousOn f (Ici 0)) : IsBernsteinFunction (halfLinePrimitive f)

decls.name: TauCeti.IsCompletelyMonotoneOnIoi.isBernsteinFunction_integral
decls.doc:
The primitive `t ↦ ∫₀ᵗ f` of a function that is completely monotone on `(0, ∞)` and
continuous on `[0, ∞)` is a Bernstein function.
decls.statement:
theorem isBernsteinFunction_integral (hf : IsCompletelyMonotoneOnIoi f)
    (hcont : ContinuousOn f (Ici 0)) :
    IsBernsteinFunction fun t ↦ ∫ x in (0 : ℝ)..t, f x

decls.name: TauCeti.IsCompletelyMonotone.isBernsteinFunction_halfLinePrimitive
decls.doc: The primitive on `[0, ∞)` of a completely monotone function is a Bernstein function.
decls.statement:
theorem isBernsteinFunction_halfLinePrimitive (hf : IsCompletelyMonotone f) :
    IsBernsteinFunction (halfLinePrimitive f)

decls.name: TauCeti.IsCompletelyMonotone.isBernsteinFunction_integral
decls.doc: The primitive `t ↦ ∫₀ᵗ f` of a completely monotone function is a Bernstein function.
decls.statement:
theorem isBernsteinFunction_integral (hf : IsCompletelyMonotone f) :
    IsBernsteinFunction fun t ↦ ∫ x in (0 : ℝ)..t, f x

decls.name: TauCeti.nat_le_top
decls.statement: lemma nat_le_top (n : ℕ) : (n : WithTop ℕ∞) ≤ ∞

decls.name: TauCeti.chafaiDensity
decls.doc:
The density `ρ_n(t) = (-1)ⁿ/(n-1)! · tⁿ⁻¹ · f⁽ⁿ⁾(t)` for nonzero `n`, used for the `n`-th
approximating measure in the Bernstein proof (Chafaï 2013). By convention the `n = 0` branch
returns `0`.
decls.statement: def chafaiDensity (f : ℝ → ℝ) (n : ℕ) (t : ℝ) : ℝ

decls.name: TauCeti.chafaiDensity_zero
decls.doc: `chafaiDensity f 0 = 0`.
decls.statement: lemma chafaiDensity_zero (f : ℝ → ℝ) (t : ℝ) : chafaiDensity f 0 t = 0

decls.name: TauCeti.chafaiDensity_of_ne_zero
decls.doc: The defining formula for `chafaiDensity` at a nonzero order.
decls.statement:
lemma chafaiDensity_of_ne_zero {n : ℕ} (hn : n ≠ 0) (f : ℝ → ℝ) (t : ℝ) :
    chafaiDensity f n t = (-1 : ℝ) ^ n / (Nat.factorial (n - 1) : ℝ) *
      t ^ (n - 1) * iteratedDerivWithin n f (Ici 0) t

decls.name: TauCeti.continuousOn_chafaiDensity
decls.doc:
`chafaiDensity f n` is continuous on `[0, ∞)` when `f` has `n` continuous derivatives
there.

decls.name: TauCeti.chafaiMeasure
decls.doc:
The `n`-th Chafaï approximating measure `σ_n` for the Bernstein representation, with density
`ρ_n` on
`(0, ∞)`.
decls.statement: def chafaiMeasure (f : ℝ → ℝ) (n : ℕ) : Measure ℝ

decls.name: TauCeti.chafaiMeasure_eq_withDensity
decls.doc: `chafaiMeasure` as a `withDensity`, exposed as a lemma rather than an unfoldable body.
decls.statement:
lemma chafaiMeasure_eq_withDensity (f : ℝ → ℝ) (n : ℕ) :
    chafaiMeasure f n =
      (volume.restrict (Ioi 0)).withDensity (fun t => ENNReal.ofReal (chafaiDensity f n t))

decls.name: TauCeti.chafaiMeasure_apply
decls.doc: The mass `chafaiMeasure f n` assigns to a measurable set, as a set lintegral of the density.
decls.statement:
lemma chafaiMeasure_apply (f : ℝ → ℝ) (n : ℕ) {s : Set ℝ} (hs : MeasurableSet s) :
    chafaiMeasure f n s =
      ∫⁻ t in s, ENNReal.ofReal (chafaiDensity f n t) ∂(volume.restrict (Ioi 0))

decls.name: TauCeti.chafaiDensity_nonneg
decls.doc:
The density `ρ_n(t)` is nonnegative when `t ≥ 0` and the `n`-th derivative has the
alternating sign at `t`.
decls.statement:
lemma chafaiDensity_nonneg {n : ℕ} {t : ℝ} (ht : 0 ≤ t)
    (hsign : 0 ≤ (-1 : ℝ) ^ n * iteratedDerivWithin n f (Ici 0) t) :
    0 ≤ chafaiDensity f n t

decls.name: TauCeti.chafaiDensity_one
decls.doc: For `n = 1`, the density simplifies to `-f'(t)`.
decls.statement:
lemma chafaiDensity_one (t : ℝ) :
    chafaiDensity f 1 t = -iteratedDerivWithin 1 f (Ici 0) t

decls.name: TauCeti.chafaiDensity_succ_succ_sub_succ
decls.doc:
Difference of two successive Chafaï densities, in the algebraic form used by integration by
parts.
decls.statement:
lemma chafaiDensity_succ_succ_sub_succ (f : ℝ → ℝ) (m : ℕ) (t : ℝ) :
    chafaiDensity f (m + 2) t - chafaiDensity f (m + 1) t =
      ↑(m + 1) * t ^ m *
          (((-1 : ℝ) ^ (m + 2) / ↑(m + 1).factorial) *
            iteratedDerivWithin (m + 1) f (Ici 0) t) +
        t ^ (m + 1) *
          (((-1 : ℝ) ^ (m + 2) / ↑(m + 1).factorial) *
            iteratedDerivWithin (m + 2) f (Ici 0) t)

decls.name: TauCeti.bernsteinKernel
decls.doc:
The Bernstein kernel `φ_n(x,p) = max(1 - xp/(n-1), 0)ⁿ⁻¹` for `n ≥ 2`. After the change of
variable `p = (n-1)/t`, the Taylor integral kernel on `[0, T]` becomes `φ_n(x, p)`, which
converges pointwise to `e^{-xp}` as `n → ∞` (the classical `(1-x/n)ⁿ → e^{-x}` limit).
decls.statement: def bernsteinKernel (n : ℕ) (x p : ℝ) : ℝ

decls.name: TauCeti.bernsteinKernel_of_le_one
decls.doc: The Bernstein kernel vanishes for `n ≤ 1`.
decls.statement:
lemma bernsteinKernel_of_le_one {n : ℕ} (hn : n ≤ 1) (x p : ℝ) :
    bernsteinKernel n x p = 0

decls.name: TauCeti.bernsteinKernel_of_two_le
decls.doc: The defining formula for the Bernstein kernel at `2 ≤ n`.
decls.statement:
lemma bernsteinKernel_of_two_le {n : ℕ} (hn : 2 ≤ n) (x p : ℝ) :
    bernsteinKernel n x p = (max (1 - x * p / (↑(n - 1) : ℝ)) 0) ^ (n - 1)

decls.name: TauCeti.continuous_bernsteinKernel
decls.doc: The Bernstein kernel is continuous in `p` for fixed `n` and `x`.
decls.statement: lemma continuous_bernsteinKernel (n : ℕ) (x : ℝ) : Continuous (bernsteinKernel n x)

decls.name: TauCeti.bernsteinKernel_nonneg
decls.doc: The Bernstein kernel is nonnegative.
decls.statement: lemma bernsteinKernel_nonneg (n : ℕ) (x p : ℝ) : 0 ≤ bernsteinKernel n x p

decls.name: TauCeti.bernsteinKernel_le_one
decls.doc: On the nonnegative half-plane, the Bernstein kernel is bounded above by `1`.
decls.statement:
lemma bernsteinKernel_le_one {n : ℕ} {x p : ℝ} (hx : 0 ≤ x) (hp : 0 ≤ p) :
    bernsteinKernel n x p ≤ 1

decls.name: TauCeti.bernsteinKernelBoundedContinuous
decls.doc:
The Bernstein kernel as a bundled bounded continuous test function of the nonnegative
variable `p`, for fixed `n` and nonnegative `x`.
decls.statement:
def bernsteinKernelBoundedContinuous (n : ℕ) {x : ℝ} (hx : 0 ≤ x) :
    ℝ≥0 →ᵇ ℝ

decls.name: TauCeti.bernsteinKernelBoundedContinuous_apply
decls.doc: The bundled Bernstein kernel evaluates to the unbundled kernel on `ℝ≥0`.
decls.statement:
lemma bernsteinKernelBoundedContinuous_apply (n : ℕ) {x : ℝ} (hx : 0 ≤ x) (p : ℝ≥0) :
    bernsteinKernelBoundedContinuous n hx p = bernsteinKernel n x (p : ℝ)

decls.name: TauCeti.laplaceKernelBoundedContinuous
decls.doc:
The limiting Laplace kernel as a bundled bounded continuous test function of the
nonnegative variable `p`, for fixed nonnegative `x`.
decls.statement: def laplaceKernelBoundedContinuous {x : ℝ} (hx : 0 ≤ x) : ℝ≥0 →ᵇ ℝ

decls.name: TauCeti.laplaceKernelBoundedContinuous_apply
decls.doc: The bundled limiting Laplace kernel evaluates to the usual exponential kernel on `ℝ≥0`.
decls.statement:
lemma laplaceKernelBoundedContinuous_apply {x : ℝ} (hx : 0 ≤ x) (p : ℝ≥0) :
    laplaceKernelBoundedContinuous hx p = Real.exp (-(x * (p : ℝ)))

decls.name: TauCeti.integrable_exp_neg_mul
decls.doc:
**The Laplace kernel is integrable against a finite measure.** For `0 ≤ x` the kernel
`p ↦ e^{-xp}` is bounded and continuous on `ℝ≥0`, hence integrable against any finite measure.
decls.title: The Laplace kernel is integrable against a finite measure
decls.statement:
lemma integrable_exp_neg_mul (μ : Measure ℝ≥0) [IsFiniteMeasure μ] {x : ℝ} (hx : 0 ≤ x) :
    Integrable (fun p : ℝ≥0 => Real.exp (-(x * (p : ℝ)))) μ

decls.name: TauCeti.integral_exp_neg_mul_add_smul_dirac_zero
decls.doc:
**An atom at `0` shifts the Laplace transform by its mass.** The kernel takes the value `1` at
`p = 0`, so adjoining `c • δ₀` to a finite measure adds exactly `c`.
decls.title: An atom at `0` shifts the Laplace transform by its mass
decls.statement:
lemma integral_exp_neg_mul_add_smul_dirac_zero (μ : Measure ℝ≥0) [IsFiniteMeasure μ] (c : ℝ≥0)
    {x : ℝ} (hx : 0 ≤ x) :
    ∫ p : ℝ≥0, Real.exp (-(x * (p : ℝ))) ∂(μ + c • Measure.dirac (0 : ℝ≥0))
      = (∫ p : ℝ≥0, Real.exp (-(x * (p : ℝ))) ∂μ) + c

decls.name: TauCeti.measurable_bernsteinKernel
decls.doc: The Bernstein kernel is measurable in `p` for fixed `n` and `x`.
decls.statement: lemma measurable_bernsteinKernel (n : ℕ) (x : ℝ) : Measurable (bernsteinKernel n x)

decls.name: TauCeti.bernsteinKernel_tendsto
decls.doc:
**Pointwise convergence of the Bernstein kernel** to the Laplace kernel:
`φ_n(x,p) → e^{-xp}` as `n → ∞`.
decls.title: Pointwise convergence of the Bernstein kernel
decls.statement:
lemma bernsteinKernel_tendsto (x p : ℝ) :
    Tendsto (fun n : ℕ => bernsteinKernel n x p) atTop (nhds (Real.exp (-(x * p))))

decls.name: TauCeti.chafaiRescaling
decls.doc: The rescaling map `t ↦ max ((n-1)/t) 0`, valued in `ℝ≥0`.
decls.statement: def chafaiRescaling (n : ℕ) (t : ℝ) : ℝ≥0

decls.name: TauCeti.measurable_chafaiRescaling
decls.doc: The rescaling map `t ↦ max ((n-1)/t) 0`, valued in `ℝ≥0`, is measurable.
decls.statement:
lemma measurable_chafaiRescaling (n : ℕ) :
    Measurable (chafaiRescaling n)

decls.name: TauCeti.chafaiRescaling_coe_of_pos
decls.doc: On the positive part of the source, the `ℝ≥0` rescaling coerces back to `(n-1)/t`.
decls.statement:
lemma chafaiRescaling_coe_of_pos {n : ℕ} (hn : 1 ≤ n) {t : ℝ} (ht : 0 < t) :
    (chafaiRescaling n t : ℝ) = ((n : ℝ) - 1) / t

decls.name: TauCeti.chafaiRescaled
decls.doc: The rescaled measure `σ̃_n`: pushforward of `chafaiMeasure f n` under the `ℝ≥0` rescaling.
decls.statement: def chafaiRescaled (f : ℝ → ℝ) (n : ℕ) : Measure ℝ≥0

decls.name: TauCeti.chafaiRescaled_eq_map
decls.doc: `chafaiRescaled` as a pushforward, exposed as a lemma rather than an unfoldable body.
decls.statement:
lemma chafaiRescaled_eq_map (f : ℝ → ℝ) (n : ℕ) :
    chafaiRescaled f n = Measure.map (chafaiRescaling n) (chafaiMeasure f n)

decls.name: TauCeti.chafaiRescaled_apply
decls.doc: The mass `chafaiRescaled f n` assigns to a measurable set, as the pushforward formula.
decls.statement:
lemma chafaiRescaled_apply (f : ℝ → ℝ) (n : ℕ) {s : Set ℝ≥0} (hs : MeasurableSet s) :
    chafaiRescaled f n s = chafaiMeasure f n ((chafaiRescaling n) ⁻¹' s)

decls.name: TauCeti.chafaiRescaled_integral
decls.doc:
Integrating against `chafaiRescaled f n` is integrating the pullback along the Chafaï
rescaling against `chafaiMeasure f n`.
decls.statement:
lemma chafaiRescaled_integral (f : ℝ → ℝ) (n : ℕ) {g : ℝ≥0 → ℝ}
    (hg : AEStronglyMeasurable g (chafaiRescaled f n)) :
    ∫ x, g x ∂(chafaiRescaled f n) =
      ∫ t, g (chafaiRescaling n t) ∂(chafaiMeasure f n)

decls.name: TauCeti.bernsteinKernel_chafaiRescaling_of_pos
decls.doc:
On positive source points, pulling the Bernstein kernel back along the Chafaï rescaling
gives the classical finite-order kernel `(max (1 - x / t) 0) ^ (n - 1)`.

decls.name: TauCeti.ae_nonneg_bernsteinKernel_chafaiRescaled
decls.doc:
The Bernstein kernel is nonnegative almost everywhere against every rescaled Chafaï measure.
This is the public positivity lemma consumers need before using monotone or positivity facts for
the kernel pairing.
decls.statement:
lemma ae_nonneg_bernsteinKernel_chafaiRescaled (f : ℝ → ℝ) (n : ℕ) (x : ℝ) :
    0 ≤ᵐ[chafaiRescaled f n] fun p : ℝ≥0 => bernsteinKernel n x (p : ℝ)

decls.name: TauCeti.ae_nonneg_bernsteinKernelBoundedContinuous_chafaiRescaled
decls.doc:
Bundled version of `ae_nonneg_bernsteinKernel_chafaiRescaled` for the bounded-continuous
Bernstein kernel.
decls.statement:
lemma ae_nonneg_bernsteinKernelBoundedContinuous_chafaiRescaled
    (f : ℝ → ℝ) (n : ℕ) {x : ℝ} (hx : 0 ≤ x) :
    0 ≤ᵐ[chafaiRescaled f n] fun p : ℝ≥0 => bernsteinKernelBoundedContinuous n hx p

decls.name: TauCeti.chafaiRescaled_integral_bernsteinKernel
decls.doc:
Characteristic pairing of the rescaled Chafaï measure with the Bernstein kernel: integrating
`p ↦ φ_n(x,p)` against `chafaiRescaled f n` is the same as integrating its Chafaï-rescaling
pullback against the original Chafaï measure.
decls.statement:
lemma chafaiRescaled_integral_bernsteinKernel (f : ℝ → ℝ) (n : ℕ) (x : ℝ) :
    ∫ p, bernsteinKernel n x (p : ℝ) ∂(chafaiRescaled f n) =
      ∫ t, bernsteinKernel n x (chafaiRescaling n t : ℝ) ∂(chafaiMeasure f n)

decls.name: TauCeti.chafaiRescaled_integral_bernsteinKernelBoundedContinuous
decls.doc:
Bounded-continuous characteristic pairing of the rescaled Chafaï measure with the Bernstein
kernel. This lets weak-convergence consumers use the bundled test function while the right-hand
side is the concrete pullback along the Chafaï rescaling.
decls.statement:
lemma chafaiRescaled_integral_bernsteinKernelBoundedContinuous
    (f : ℝ → ℝ) (n : ℕ) {x : ℝ} (hx : 0 ≤ x) :
    ∫ p, bernsteinKernelBoundedContinuous n hx p ∂(chafaiRescaled f n) =
      ∫ t, bernsteinKernel n x (chafaiRescaling n t : ℝ) ∂(chafaiMeasure f n)

decls.name: TauCeti.chafaiMeasure_compl_Ioi
decls.doc: `chafaiMeasure f n` lives on `(0, ∞)`: its complement has zero mass.
decls.statement:
lemma chafaiMeasure_compl_Ioi (f : ℝ → ℝ) (n : ℕ) :
    (chafaiMeasure f n) (Ioi 0)ᶜ = 0

decls.name: TauCeti.chafaiRescaled_mass_eq
decls.doc: Pushforward preserves total mass.
decls.statement:
lemma chafaiRescaled_mass_eq (f : ℝ → ℝ) (n : ℕ) :
    (chafaiRescaled f n) univ = (chafaiMeasure f n) univ

decls.name: TauCeti.aemeasurable_chafaiDensity_ofReal
decls.statement:
lemma aemeasurable_chafaiDensity_ofReal (f : ℝ → ℝ)
    (hcm : IsCompletelyMonotone f) (n : ℕ) :
    AEMeasurable (fun t => ENNReal.ofReal (chafaiDensity f n t))
      (volume.restrict (Ioi 0))

decls.name: TauCeti.chafaiDensity_neg_derivWithin_pred
decls.statement:
lemma chafaiDensity_neg_derivWithin_pred (f : ℝ → ℝ)
    {n : ℕ} (hn : 2 ≤ n) {t : ℝ} (ht : 0 < t) :
    chafaiDensity (fun t => -derivWithin f (Ici 0) t) (n - 1) t =
      ((n : ℝ) - 1) / t * chafaiDensity f n t

decls.name: TauCeti.chafaiRescaled_lintegral_coe_eq_chafaiMeasure_neg_derivWithin
decls.statement:
lemma chafaiRescaled_lintegral_coe_eq_chafaiMeasure_neg_derivWithin
    (f : ℝ → ℝ) (hcm : IsCompletelyMonotone f) {n : ℕ} (hn : 2 ≤ n) :
    ∫⁻ p : ℝ≥0, ENNReal.ofReal (p : ℝ) ∂(chafaiRescaled f n) =
      (chafaiMeasure (fun t => -derivWithin f (Ici 0) t) (n - 1)) univ

decls.name: TauCeti.intervalIntegrable_chafaiDensity
decls.doc:
The Chafaï density of order `n` is interval-integrable on `[0, T]`: it is continuous on
`Ici 0` given `n`-fold differentiability there, and `[0, T]` sits inside that ray.

decls.name: TauCeti.chafaiDensity_ibp_identity
decls.doc:
**IBP identity** for the CM density:
`∫₀ᵀ ρ_{m+2}(t) dt = B_{m+2}(T) + ∫₀ᵀ ρ_{m+1}(t) dt`.
decls.title: IBP identity
decls.statement:
lemma chafaiDensity_ibp_identity (f : ℝ → ℝ) {m : ℕ}
    (hf : ContDiffOn ℝ ((m + 2 : ℕ) : WithTop ℕ∞) f (Ici 0)) (T : ℝ) (hT : 0 < T) :
    ∫ t in (0 : ℝ)..T, chafaiDensity f (m + 2) t =
    (-1 : ℝ) ^ (m + 2) * T ^ (m + 1) / ↑(m + 1).factorial *
      iteratedDerivWithin (m + 1) f (Ici 0) T +
    ∫ t in (0 : ℝ)..T, chafaiDensity f (m + 1) t

decls.name: TauCeti.integral_chafaiDensity_le_pred
decls.doc:
Monotonicity of the finite-interval Chafaï-density integrals in the order:
for `2 ≤ k` and `0 ≤ T`, the integral of the `k`-th density on `[0,T]` is bounded above by the
integral of the preceding density, assuming the endpoint has the required alternating sign.
decls.statement:
lemma integral_chafaiDensity_le_pred (f : ℝ → ℝ) {k : ℕ} (hk : 2 ≤ k)
    (hf : ContDiffOn ℝ (k : WithTop ℕ∞) f (Ici 0))
    (T : ℝ) (hT : 0 ≤ T)
    (hsign : 0 ≤ (-1 : ℝ) ^ (k - 1) * iteratedDerivWithin (k - 1) f (Ici 0) T) :
    ∫ t in (0 : ℝ)..T, chafaiDensity f k t ≤ ∫ t in (0 : ℝ)..T, chafaiDensity f (k - 1) t

decls.name: TauCeti.chafaiMeasure_zero
decls.doc:
The public `n = 0` convention for Chafaï measures: the zeroth approximating measure is
zero.
decls.statement: lemma chafaiMeasure_zero (f : ℝ → ℝ) : chafaiMeasure f 0 = 0

decls.name: TauCeti.chafaiRescaled_zero
decls.doc:
The rescaled Chafaï measure on the target type `ℝ≥0` shares the `n = 0` zero convention:
`chafaiRescaled f 0 = 0`, as the pushforward of the zero measure.
decls.statement: lemma chafaiRescaled_zero (f : ℝ → ℝ) : chafaiRescaled f 0 = 0

decls.name: TauCeti.integral_chafaiDensity_one_eq
decls.statement:
lemma integral_chafaiDensity_one_eq (f : ℝ → ℝ) (hcm : IsCompletelyMonotone f)
    (T : ℝ) (hT : 0 < T) :
    ∫ t in (0 : ℝ)..T, chafaiDensity f 1 t = f 0 - f T

decls.name: TauCeti.integral_chafaiDensity_le_sub
decls.statement:
lemma integral_chafaiDensity_le_sub (f : ℝ → ℝ) (hcm : IsCompletelyMonotone f)
    (j : ℕ) (hj : 1 ≤ j) (T : ℝ) (hT : 0 < T) :
    ∫ t in (0 : ℝ)..T, chafaiDensity f j t ≤ f 0 - f T

decls.name: TauCeti.integral_chafaiDensity_le_tendsto_sub
decls.statement:
lemma integral_chafaiDensity_le_tendsto_sub (f : ℝ → ℝ)
    (hcm : IsCompletelyMonotone f) (n : ℕ) (hn : 1 ≤ n) (L : ℝ)
    (hL : Tendsto f atTop (nhds L)) (T : ℝ) (hT : 0 < T) :
    ∫ t in (0 : ℝ)..T, chafaiDensity f n t ≤ f 0 - L

decls.name: TauCeti.chafaiDensity_integrableOn_Ioi_of_tendsto
decls.statement:
lemma chafaiDensity_integrableOn_Ioi_of_tendsto (f : ℝ → ℝ)
    (hcm : IsCompletelyMonotone f) (n : ℕ) (hn : 1 ≤ n) (L : ℝ)
    (hL : Tendsto f atTop (nhds L)) :
    IntegrableOn (chafaiDensity f n) (Ioi 0)

decls.name: TauCeti.chafaiMeasure_mass_le_of_tendsto
decls.statement:
lemma chafaiMeasure_mass_le_of_tendsto (f : ℝ → ℝ)
    (hcm : IsCompletelyMonotone f) (n : ℕ) (hn : 1 ≤ n) (L : ℝ)
    (hL : Tendsto f atTop (nhds L))
    (hint : IntegrableOn (chafaiDensity f n) (Ioi 0)) :
    (chafaiMeasure f n) univ ≤ ENNReal.ofReal (f 0 - L)

decls.name: TauCeti.chafaiMeasure_finite_mass_of_tendsto
decls.doc:
**Total mass bound with a chosen limit**: `chafaiMeasure f n` is finite with total mass
`≤ f(0) - L` whenever `f(t) → L` at infinity.
decls.title: Total mass bound with a chosen limit
decls.statement:
lemma chafaiMeasure_finite_mass_of_tendsto (f : ℝ → ℝ) (hcm : IsCompletelyMonotone f)
    (n : ℕ) (L : ℝ) (hL : Tendsto f atTop (nhds L)) :
    IsFiniteMeasure (chafaiMeasure f n) ∧
    (chafaiMeasure f n) univ ≤ ENNReal.ofReal (f 0 - L)

decls.name: TauCeti.chafaiMeasure_finite_mass
decls.doc:
**Natural total mass bound**: for a completely monotone `f`, the Chafaï measures are finite
and uniformly bounded by `f(0) - L`, where `L` is the automatically obtained limit of `f` at
infinity.
decls.title: Natural total mass bound
decls.statement:
lemma chafaiMeasure_finite_mass (f : ℝ → ℝ) (hcm : IsCompletelyMonotone f) :
    ∃ L : ℝ, Tendsto f atTop (nhds L) ∧ 0 ≤ L ∧
      ∀ n,
        IsFiniteMeasure (chafaiMeasure f n) ∧
        (chafaiMeasure f n) univ ≤ ENNReal.ofReal (f 0 - L)

decls.name: TauCeti.chafaiRescaled_finite_mass
decls.doc:
**Natural rescaled total mass bound**: for a completely monotone `f`, the rescaled
Chafaï measures on `ℝ≥0` are finite and uniformly bounded by `f(0) - L`, where `L` is the
automatically obtained limit of `f` at infinity.
decls.title: Natural rescaled total mass bound
decls.statement:
lemma chafaiRescaled_finite_mass (f : ℝ → ℝ) (hcm : IsCompletelyMonotone f) :
    ∃ L : ℝ, Tendsto f atTop (nhds L) ∧ 0 ≤ L ∧
      ∀ n,
        IsFiniteMeasure (chafaiRescaled f n) ∧
        (chafaiRescaled f n) univ ≤ ENNReal.ofReal (f 0 - L)

decls.name: TauCeti.chafaiRescaled_lintegral_coe_le
decls.doc: Uniform first-moment bound for the rescaled Chafaï measures.
decls.statement:
lemma chafaiRescaled_lintegral_coe_le (f : ℝ → ℝ) (hcm : IsCompletelyMonotone f) :
    ∀ n,
      ∫⁻ p : ℝ≥0, ENNReal.ofReal (p : ℝ) ∂(chafaiRescaled f n) ≤
        ENNReal.ofReal (-derivWithin f (Ici 0) 0)

decls.name: TauCeti.chafaiRescaled_prokhorov_mass_bound
decls.doc:
Prokhorov-ready mass bound for the rescaled Chafaï measures: a completely monotone function
supplies a nonnegative real mass constant `C = f(0) - L`, where `L` is the limit of `f` at
infinity, such that every `chafaiRescaled f n` is finite and has total mass at most `C`.
decls.statement:
lemma chafaiRescaled_prokhorov_mass_bound (f : ℝ → ℝ) (hcm : IsCompletelyMonotone f) :
    ∃ L : ℝ, ∃ C : ℝ≥0, Tendsto f atTop (nhds L) ∧ 0 ≤ L ∧ (C : ℝ) = f 0 - L ∧
      ∀ n,
        IsFiniteMeasure (chafaiRescaled f n) ∧
        (chafaiRescaled f n) univ ≤ (C : ENNReal)

decls.name: TauCeti.chafai_kernel_density_eq
decls.statement:
lemma chafai_kernel_density_eq (f : ℝ → ℝ)
    (n : ℕ) (hn : 2 ≤ n) (x : ℝ) (hx : 0 ≤ x) :
    ∫ t in Ioi 0, bernsteinKernel n x (((n : ℝ) - 1) / t) *
      chafaiDensity f n t =
    ∫ t in Ioi x, (-1 : ℝ) ^ n / ↑(n - 1).factorial *
      (t - x) ^ (n - 1) * iteratedDerivWithin n f (Ici 0) t

decls.name: TauCeti.div_factorial_mul_natCast
decls.doc:
For `k ≠ 0`, dividing by `k!` and multiplying by `k` is dividing by `(k - 1)!`. This is the
coefficient bookkeeping produced by differentiating the order-`k` kernel.
decls.statement:
lemma div_factorial_mul_natCast {k : ℕ} (hk : k ≠ 0) (c z : ℝ) :
    c / ↑k.factorial * ((k : ℝ) * z) = c / ↑(k - 1).factorial * z

decls.name: TauCeti.ibp_finite_interval
decls.statement:
lemma ibp_finite_interval (f : ℝ → ℝ) (hcm : IsCompletelyMonotone f)
    (k : ℕ) (hk : k ≠ 0) (x T : ℝ) (hx : 0 ≤ x) (hxT : x < T) :
    ∫ t in x..T, (-1 : ℝ) ^ (k + 1) / ↑k.factorial * (t - x) ^ k *
      iteratedDerivWithin (k + 1) f (Ici 0) t =
    (-1 : ℝ) ^ (k + 1) / ↑k.factorial * (T - x) ^ k *
      iteratedDerivWithin k f (Ici 0) T -
    ∫ t in x..T, (-1 : ℝ) ^ (k + 1) / ↑(k - 1).factorial * (t - x) ^ (k - 1) *
      iteratedDerivWithin k f (Ici 0) t

decls.name: TauCeti.normalized_iteratedDerivWithin_nonneg_antitone
decls.statement:
lemma normalized_iteratedDerivWithin_nonneg_antitone (f : ℝ → ℝ)
    (hcm : IsCompletelyMonotone f) (k : ℕ) :
    (∀ T, 0 ≤ T → 0 ≤ (-1 : ℝ) ^ k * iteratedDerivWithin k f (Ici 0) T) ∧
      AntitoneOn (fun T => (-1 : ℝ) ^ k * iteratedDerivWithin k f (Ici 0) T) (Ici 0)

decls.name: TauCeti.chafaiDensity_ge_const_on_Icc
decls.doc:
Pointwise lower bound for the density on `Icc (T/2) T`: at each such point `t`,
`chafaiDensity f k` is at least the constant `(1/(k-1)!)·(T/2)^(k-1)·h T`.
decls.statement:
lemma chafaiDensity_ge_const_on_Icc (f : ℝ → ℝ) (k : ℕ) (h : ℝ → ℝ)
    (T : ℝ) (hhT_nonneg : 0 ≤ h T) {t : ℝ} (ht : t ∈ Icc (T / 2) T) (hT_le_ht : h T ≤ h t)
    (h_density_eq_t :
      chafaiDensity f k t = (1 / ↑((k - 1).factorial)) * t ^ (k - 1) * h t) :
    (1 / ↑((k - 1).factorial)) * (T / 2) ^ (k - 1) * h T ≤ chafaiDensity f k t

decls.name: TauCeti.const_le_intervalIntegral_chafaiDensity
decls.doc:
Interval-integral form of the tail lower bound: integrating the pointwise bound
`chafaiDensity_ge_const_on_Icc` over `[T/2, T]` gives
`(1/(k-1)!)·(T/2)^k·h T ≤ ∫ t in T/2..T, chafaiDensity f k t`.
decls.statement:
lemma const_le_intervalIntegral_chafaiDensity (f : ℝ → ℝ) (k : ℕ) (hk : k ≠ 0)
    (h : ℝ → ℝ) (h_antitone : AntitoneOn h (Ici 0)) (T : ℝ) (hT_nonneg : 0 ≤ T)
    (h_density_eq :
      ∀ t ∈ Icc (T / 2) T,
        chafaiDensity f k t = (1 / ↑((k - 1).factorial)) * t ^ (k - 1) * h t)
    (hdens_int : IntervalIntegrable (chafaiDensity f k) volume (T / 2) T)
    (hhT_nonneg : 0 ≤ h T) :
    (1 / ↑((k - 1).factorial)) * (T / 2) ^ k * h T ≤
      ∫ t in T / 2..T, chafaiDensity f k t

decls.name: TauCeti.density_tail_lower_bound_eventually
decls.doc:
Boundary-term tail estimate factored out of `boundary_term_decay`: `(T-x)^k · h T` is
eventually squeezed by a multiple of the vanishing density tail `∫_{Ioi (T/2)}`.
decls.statement:
lemma density_tail_lower_bound_eventually (f : ℝ → ℝ)
    (hcm : IsCompletelyMonotone f) (k : ℕ) (hk : k ≠ 0) (x : ℝ) (hx : 0 ≤ x)
    (h : ℝ → ℝ) (h_nonneg : ∀ T, 0 ≤ T → 0 ≤ h T)
    (h_antitone : AntitoneOn h (Ici 0))
    (h_density_eq : ∀ t, chafaiDensity f k t =
      (1 / ↑((k - 1).factorial)) * t ^ (k - 1) * h t)
    (hint_density : IntegrableOn (chafaiDensity f k) (Ioi 0)) :
    ∀ᶠ T in atTop,
      (T - x) ^ k * h T ≤
        ((2 : ℝ) ^ k * ↑((k - 1).factorial)) *
          ∫ t in Ioi (T / 2), chafaiDensity f k t

decls.name: TauCeti.boundary_term_decay
decls.statement:
lemma boundary_term_decay (f : ℝ → ℝ) (hcm : IsCompletelyMonotone f)
    (k : ℕ) (hk : k ≠ 0) (x : ℝ) (hx : 0 ≤ x)
    (L : ℝ) (hL : Tendsto f atTop (nhds L)) :
    Tendsto (fun T => (-1 : ℝ) ^ (k + 1) / ↑k.factorial * (T - x) ^ k *
      iteratedDerivWithin k f (Ici 0) T) atTop (nhds 0)

decls.name: TauCeti.norm_ibp_kernel_le_chafaiDensity
decls.doc:
**The shifted order-`k` kernel is dominated by the Chafaï density.** For `0 ≤ x ≤ t` the
kernel built from `(t - x) ^ (k - 1)` is nonnegative and bounded by the density built from
`t ^ (k - 1)`.
decls.title: The shifted order-`k` kernel is dominated by the Chafaï density
decls.statement:
lemma norm_ibp_kernel_le_chafaiDensity (f : ℝ → ℝ)
    {k : ℕ} (hk0 : k ≠ 0) {x t : ℝ} (hx : 0 ≤ x) (ht : x ≤ t)
    (hcm_sign : 0 ≤ (-1 : ℝ) ^ k * iteratedDerivWithin k f (Ici 0) t) :
    ‖(-1 : ℝ) ^ k / ↑(k - 1).factorial * (t - x) ^ (k - 1) *
      iteratedDerivWithin k f (Ici 0) t‖ ≤ chafaiDensity f k t

decls.name: TauCeti.ibp_kernel_integrableOn
decls.statement:
lemma ibp_kernel_integrableOn (f : ℝ → ℝ) (hcm : IsCompletelyMonotone f)
    (k : ℕ) (hk : 1 ≤ k) (x : ℝ) (hx : 0 ≤ x)
    (L : ℝ) (hL : Tendsto f atTop (nhds L)) :
    IntegrableOn (fun t => (-1 : ℝ) ^ k / ↑(k - 1).factorial * (t - x) ^ (k - 1) *
      iteratedDerivWithin k f (Ici 0) t) (Ioi x)

decls.name: TauCeti.intervalIntegral_neg_one_pow_succ_kernel
decls.doc: Raising the sign exponent of the order-`k` kernel by one negates its integral.
decls.statement:
lemma intervalIntegral_neg_one_pow_succ_kernel (f : ℝ → ℝ) (k : ℕ) (x T : ℝ) :
    ∫ t in x..T, (-1 : ℝ) ^ (k + 1) / ↑(k - 1).factorial * (t - x) ^ (k - 1) *
        iteratedDerivWithin k f (Ici 0) t =
      -(∫ t in x..T, (-1 : ℝ) ^ k / ↑(k - 1).factorial * (t - x) ^ (k - 1) *
        iteratedDerivWithin k f (Ici 0) t)

decls.name: TauCeti.chafai_repeated_ibp_succ
decls.doc:
For a completely monotone `f` with limit `L` at infinity, `0 ≤ x` and `k ≠ 0`, the order-`k`
kernel identity implies the order-`k + 1` one: if the order-`k` kernel integrates against the
`k`-th derivative to `f x - L` on `(x, ∞)`, then so does the order-`k + 1` kernel against the
`(k + 1)`-st derivative.
decls.statement:
lemma chafai_repeated_ibp_succ (f : ℝ → ℝ) (hcm : IsCompletelyMonotone f)
    (k : ℕ) (hk : k ≠ 0) (x : ℝ) (hx : 0 ≤ x) (L : ℝ) (hL : Tendsto f atTop (nhds L))
    (ih : ∫ t in Ioi x, (-1 : ℝ) ^ k / ↑(k - 1).factorial * (t - x) ^ (k - 1) *
      iteratedDerivWithin k f (Ici 0) t = f x - L) :
    ∫ t in Ioi x, (-1 : ℝ) ^ (k + 1) / ↑k.factorial * (t - x) ^ k *
      iteratedDerivWithin (k + 1) f (Ici 0) t = f x - L

decls.name: TauCeti.chafai_repeated_ibp
decls.doc:
**Repeated integration by parts for a completely monotone function.** For `n ≥ 1`, `0 ≤ x`
and `f` tending to `L` at infinity, integrating the order-`n` kernel
`(-1) ^ n / (n - 1)! * (t - x) ^ (n - 1)` against the `n`-th derivative of `f` over `(x, ∞)`
recovers `f x - L`. This is the analytic identity behind the Chafaï reconstruction of `f` from
its derivatives.
decls.title: Repeated integration by parts for a completely monotone function
decls.statement:
lemma chafai_repeated_ibp (f : ℝ → ℝ) (hcm : IsCompletelyMonotone f)
    (n : ℕ) (hn : 1 ≤ n) (x : ℝ) (hx : 0 ≤ x)
    (L : ℝ) (hL : Tendsto f atTop (nhds L)) :
    ∫ t in Ioi x, (-1 : ℝ) ^ n / ↑(n - 1).factorial *
      (t - x) ^ (n - 1) *
      iteratedDerivWithin n f (Ici 0) t = f x - L

decls.name: TauCeti.chafaiRescaled_integral_bernsteinKernel_eq_sub_tendsto_atTop
decls.doc: **Chafaï reconstruction identity** for the nonconstant part.
decls.title: Chafaï reconstruction identity
decls.statement:
lemma chafaiRescaled_integral_bernsteinKernel_eq_sub_tendsto_atTop
    (f : ℝ → ℝ) (hcm : IsCompletelyMonotone f)
    (n : ℕ) (hn : 2 ≤ n) (x : ℝ) (hx : 0 ≤ x)
    (L : ℝ) (hL : Tendsto f atTop (nhds L)) :
    ∫ p, bernsteinKernel n x (p : ℝ) ∂(chafaiRescaled f n) = f x - L

decls.name: TauCeti.bernsteinKernel_le_exp
decls.statement:
lemma bernsteinKernel_le_exp {n : ℕ} (hn : 2 ≤ n) {x p : ℝ} (_hx : 0 ≤ x)
    (_hp : 0 ≤ p) :
    bernsteinKernel n x p ≤ Real.exp (-(x * p))

decls.name: TauCeti.exp_neg_mul_sub_one_sub_pow_le
decls.doc:
**Local error bound for the Bernstein truncation.** For `0 ≤ u < 1` and `m : ℕ`, the
difference `exp (-(m·u)) - (1 - u) ^ m` is bounded above by the second-order term
`m·u² / (1 - u)`. This is the pointwise estimate driving the uniform convergence of the
Bernstein kernel to the Laplace kernel.
decls.title: Local error bound for the Bernstein truncation
decls.statement:
lemma exp_neg_mul_sub_one_sub_pow_le (u : ℝ) (hu_nn : 0 ≤ u) (hu_lt_1 : u < 1) (m : ℕ) :
    Real.exp (-(↑m * u)) - (1 - u) ^ m ≤ ↑m * u ^ 2 / (1 - u)

decls.name: TauCeti.sq_div_sub_lt_div_two
decls.doc:
**Compact-support tail estimate.** Once `M` exceeds `C + 2C²/ε`, the error parameter
`xp² / (M - xp)` stays below `ε / 2` for every `0 ≤ xp ≤ C`. Positivity of `M - C` follows
from the size hypothesis, so the only inputs are the pointwise bounds on `xp`.
decls.title: Compact-support tail estimate
decls.statement:
lemma sq_div_sub_lt_div_two (xp C ε M : ℝ) (hxp_nn : 0 ≤ xp) (hxp_le_C : xp ≤ C)
    (hε : 0 < ε) (hM : 2 * C ^ 2 / ε < M - C) :
    xp ^ 2 / (M - xp) < ε / 2

decls.name: TauCeti.kernel_uniform_conv_compact
decls.statement:
lemma kernel_uniform_conv_compact (x R ε : ℝ) (hx : 0 < x) (hR : 0 < R)
    (hε : 0 < ε) :
    ∃ N : ℕ, ∀ n, N ≤ n → ∀ p, 0 ≤ p → p ≤ R →
      |bernsteinKernel n x p - Real.exp (-(x * p))| < ε

decls.name: TauCeti.kernel_uniform_conv
decls.statement:
lemma kernel_uniform_conv (x : ℝ) (hx : 0 < x) (ε : ℝ) (hε : 0 < ε) :
    ∃ N : ℕ, ∀ n, N ≤ n → ∀ p, 0 ≤ p →
      |bernsteinKernel n x p - Real.exp (-(x * p))| < ε

decls.name: TauCeti.integral_bernsteinKernel_sub_laplaceKernel_tendsto_zero_of_mass_bound
decls.doc: Bernstein-to-Laplace replacement against a uniformly finite sequence of measures.
decls.statement:
lemma integral_bernsteinKernel_sub_laplaceKernel_tendsto_zero_of_mass_bound
    (σ : ℕ → Measure ℝ≥0)
    (hmass : ∀ᶠ n in atTop, (σ n) univ ≤ ENNReal.ofReal C)
    (x : ℝ) (hx : 0 ≤ x) :
    Tendsto (fun n => ∫ p : ℝ≥0,
        (bernsteinKernel n x (p : ℝ) - Real.exp (-(x * (p : ℝ)))) ∂(σ n))
      atTop (nhds 0)

decls.name: TauCeti.chafaiRescaled_tendsto_laplace_integral_of_weak
decls.statement:
lemma chafaiRescaled_tendsto_laplace_integral_of_weak
    {μ₀ : Measure ℝ≥0} {l : Filter ℕ}
    (hweak : ∀ g : BoundedContinuousFunction ℝ≥0 ℝ,
        Tendsto (fun n => ∫ p, g p ∂(chafaiRescaled f n)) l
          (nhds (∫ p, g p ∂μ₀)))
    {x : ℝ} (hx : 0 ≤ x) :
    Tendsto (fun n => ∫ p, Real.exp (-(x * (p : ℝ))) ∂(chafaiRescaled f n)) l
      (nhds (∫ p, Real.exp (-(x * (p : ℝ))) ∂μ₀))

decls.name: TauCeti.sub_eq_integral_exp_neg_mul_of_weak_limit
decls.doc:
**The weak limit represents the non-constant part.** Along the ultrafilter `U`, the Chafaï
measures converge weakly to `μ₀`; passing the reconstruction identity to that limit replaces the
Bernstein kernel by `e^{-tp}` and exhibits `μ₀` as a representing measure for `f - L`, where `L` is
the limit of `f` at infinity. The atom carrying `L` itself is added by the caller.

Stated pointwise in `t`, which is how the caller consumes it.
decls.title: The weak limit represents the non-constant part
decls.statement:
theorem sub_eq_integral_exp_neg_mul_of_weak_limit {L : ℝ} {C : ℝ≥0} {μ₀ : Measure ℝ≥0}
    {U : Ultrafilter ℕ} (hcm : IsCompletelyMonotone f) (hL : Tendsto f atTop (nhds L))
    (hmass' : ∀ᶠ n in atTop, (chafaiRescaled f n) univ ≤ (C : ℝ≥0∞)) (hU : (U : Filter ℕ) ≤ atTop)
    (hweak : ∀ g : BoundedContinuousFunction ℝ≥0 ℝ,
      Tendsto (fun n => ∫ x, g x ∂(chafaiRescaled f n)) (U : Filter ℕ) (nhds (∫ x, g x ∂μ₀)))
    {t : ℝ} (ht : 0 ≤ t) :
    f t - L = ∫ p : ℝ≥0, Real.exp (-(t * (p : ℝ))) ∂μ₀

decls.name: TauCeti.exists_isFiniteMeasure_integral_exp_neg_mul_eq_of_isCompletelyMonotone
decls.doc:
**Bernstein's theorem, existence half.** A completely monotone function on `[0, ∞)` is the
Laplace transform of a finite positive measure on `ℝ≥0`.

Uniqueness of that measure is not asserted here; see the module docstring.
decls.title: Bernstein's theorem, existence half
decls.statement:
theorem exists_isFiniteMeasure_integral_exp_neg_mul_eq_of_isCompletelyMonotone
    (hcm : IsCompletelyMonotone f) :
    ∃ μ : Measure ℝ≥0, IsFiniteMeasure μ ∧
      ∀ t : ℝ, 0 ≤ t → f t = ∫ x, Real.exp (-t * (x : ℝ)) ∂μ

decls.name: TauCeti.chafaiRescaled_measure_Ioi_le
decls.doc:
The rescaled Chafaï measures satisfy the uniform Markov tail estimate

`chafaiRescaled f n (R, ∞) ≤ ofReal (-f'(0)) / R`

for every positive `R`. The derivative is taken within `[0, ∞)`, as in the definition of
complete monotonicity.
decls.statement:
lemma chafaiRescaled_measure_Ioi_le (hcm : IsCompletelyMonotone f) (n : ℕ)
    {R : ℝ≥0} (hR : R ≠ 0) :
    chafaiRescaled f n (Ioi R) ≤
      ENNReal.ofReal (-derivWithin f (Ici 0) 0) / (R : ℝ≥0∞)

decls.name: TauCeti.isTightMeasureSet_range_chafaiRescaled
decls.doc:
The family of all rescaled Chafaï approximating measures of a completely monotone function
is tight. Equivalently, for every positive error tolerance there is a compact interval
`[0, R] ⊆ ℝ≥0` whose complement has at most that much mass for every approximation order.
decls.statement:
theorem isTightMeasureSet_range_chafaiRescaled (hcm : IsCompletelyMonotone f) :
    IsTightMeasureSet (range (chafaiRescaled f))

decls.name: TauCeti.IsCompletelyMonotone.mul
decls.doc: Completely monotone functions are closed under pointwise multiplication.
decls.statement:
theorem mul (hf : IsCompletelyMonotone f) (hg : IsCompletelyMonotone g) :
    IsCompletelyMonotone (f * g)

decls.name: TauCeti.IsCompletelyMonotone.prod
decls.doc: Completely monotone functions are closed under finite products.

decls.name: TauCeti.IsCompletelyMonotone.pow
decls.doc: Completely monotone functions are closed under taking natural powers.
decls.statement: theorem pow (hf : IsCompletelyMonotone f) (k : ℕ) : IsCompletelyMonotone (f ^ k)

decls.name: TauCeti.IsCompletelyMonotone.neg_one_pow_mul_iteratedDerivWithin
decls.doc:
Every alternating iterated derivative of a completely monotone function is completely
monotone.
decls.statement:
theorem neg_one_pow_mul_iteratedDerivWithin (hf : IsCompletelyMonotone f) (k : ℕ) :
    IsCompletelyMonotone (fun t => (-1 : ℝ) ^ k * iteratedDerivWithin k f (Ici 0) t)

decls.name: TauCeti.IsCompletelyMonotone.neg_derivWithin
decls.doc:
The negated derivative within `[0, ∞)` of a completely monotone function is completely
monotone.
decls.statement:
theorem neg_derivWithin (hf : IsCompletelyMonotone f) :
    IsCompletelyMonotone (fun t => -derivWithin f (Ici 0) t)

decls.name: TauCeti.finiteExponentialMixture
decls.doc:
A finite positive mixture of the exponential extreme rays `t ↦ exp (-p * t)`.

The weights and rates are indexed by a finset. Both take values in `ℝ≥0`, making their
nonnegativity intrinsic to the data.
decls.statement:
def finiteExponentialMixture {ι : Type*} (s : Finset ι)
    (w p : ι → ℝ≥0) (t : ℝ) : ℝ

decls.name: TauCeti.finiteExponentialMixture_empty
decls.doc: The empty exponential mixture is the zero function.
decls.statement:
theorem finiteExponentialMixture_empty {ι : Type*} (w p : ι → ℝ≥0) :
    finiteExponentialMixture ∅ w p = 0

decls.name: TauCeti.finiteExponentialMixture_singleton
decls.doc: A singleton exponential mixture is one weighted exponential extreme ray.
decls.statement:
theorem finiteExponentialMixture_singleton {ι : Type*} (i : ι) (w p : ι → ℝ≥0) (t : ℝ) :
    finiteExponentialMixture {i} w p t =
      (w i : ℝ) * Real.exp (-(p i : ℝ) * t)

decls.name: TauCeti.isCompletelyMonotone_finiteExponentialMixture
decls.doc: Every finite positive mixture of exponential extreme rays is completely monotone.
decls.statement:
theorem isCompletelyMonotone_finiteExponentialMixture {ι : Type*} (s : Finset ι)
    (w p : ι → ℝ≥0) :
    IsCompletelyMonotone (finiteExponentialMixture s w p)

decls.name: TauCeti.finiteExponentialMixtureMeasure
decls.doc:
The finite positive measure that places weight `w i` at each rate `p i`.

Repeated rates are intentionally allowed: measure addition combines their weights.
decls.statement:
def finiteExponentialMixtureMeasure {ι : Type*} (s : Finset ι)
    (w p : ι → ℝ≥0) : Measure ℝ≥0

decls.name: TauCeti.finiteExponentialMixtureMeasure_apply
decls.doc: The representing measure of a measurable set is the sum of the weights at rates in the set.
decls.statement:
theorem finiteExponentialMixtureMeasure_apply {ι : Type*} (s : Finset ι)
    (w p : ι → ℝ≥0) {A : Set ℝ≥0} (hA : MeasurableSet A) :
    finiteExponentialMixtureMeasure s w p A =
      ∑ i ∈ s, A.indicator (fun _ => (w i : ℝ≥0∞)) (p i)

decls.name: TauCeti.finiteExponentialMixtureMeasure_empty
decls.doc: The empty exponential mixture has the zero representing measure.
decls.statement:
theorem finiteExponentialMixtureMeasure_empty {ι : Type*} (w p : ι → ℝ≥0) :
    finiteExponentialMixtureMeasure ∅ w p = 0

decls.name: TauCeti.finiteExponentialMixtureMeasure_singleton
decls.doc: A singleton mixture has the corresponding weighted Dirac representing measure.
decls.statement:
theorem finiteExponentialMixtureMeasure_singleton {ι : Type*} (i : ι)
    (w p : ι → ℝ≥0) :
    finiteExponentialMixtureMeasure {i} w p =
      (w i : ℝ≥0∞) • Measure.dirac (p i)

decls.name: TauCeti.finiteExponentialMixture_eq_integral
decls.doc: A finite exponential mixture is the Laplace transform of its discrete representing measure.
decls.statement:
theorem finiteExponentialMixture_eq_integral {ι : Type*} (s : Finset ι)
    (w p : ι → ℝ≥0) (t : ℝ) :
    finiteExponentialMixture s w p t =
      ∫ q : ℝ≥0, Real.exp (-t * (q : ℝ)) ∂finiteExponentialMixtureMeasure s w p

decls.name: TauCeti.integral_exp_neg_mul_dirac_one
decls.doc:
The Laplace transform of the unit Dirac mass at `1` is `t ↦ exp (-t)`.

This is the discrete representing-measure acceptance example for Bernstein's theorem.
decls.statement:
theorem integral_exp_neg_mul_dirac_one (t : ℝ) :
    (∫ q : ℝ≥0, Real.exp (-t * (q : ℝ)) ∂Measure.dirac 1) = Real.exp (-t)

decls.name: TauCeti.finiteExponentialMixture_singleton_one
decls.doc: The exponential `t ↦ exp (-t)` is the unit-weight, unit-rate finite exponential mixture.
decls.statement:
theorem finiteExponentialMixture_singleton_one (t : ℝ) :
    finiteExponentialMixture ({()} : Finset Unit) (fun _ => 1) (fun _ => 1) t =
      Real.exp (-t)

decls.name: TauCeti.nat_le_top
decls.statement: lemma nat_le_top (n : ℕ) : (n : WithTop ℕ∞) ≤ ∞

decls.name: TauCeti.IsCompletelyMonotone.iteratedDerivWithin_Icc_eq_Ici
decls.doc:
For a completely monotone function the `n`-th iterated derivative within a compact interval
`[x, T]` agrees with the one taken within the half-line `[0, ∞)` at any strictly positive interior
point. Complete monotonicity supplies the local `ContDiffAt` hypothesis, and both sides reduce to
the unrestricted iterated derivative at `t`.
decls.statement:
lemma IsCompletelyMonotone.iteratedDerivWithin_Icc_eq_Ici (hf : IsCompletelyMonotone f)
    {x T t : ℝ} {n : ℕ} (ht_pos : 0 < t) (ht : t ∈ Ioo x T) :
    iteratedDerivWithin n f (Icc x T) t = iteratedDerivWithin n f (Ici 0) t

decls.name: TauCeti.IsCompletelyMonotone.neg_one_pow_mul_taylor_remainder_nonneg
decls.doc:
**CM sign of the Taylor remainder.** For a completely monotone function the Taylor
integral remainder `∫ₓᵀ (T-t)ⁿ⁻¹/(n-1)! · f⁽ⁿ⁾(t) dt` has sign `(-1)ⁿ`:
`0 ≤ (-1)ⁿ` times it.
decls.title: CM sign of the Taylor remainder
decls.statement:
lemma neg_one_pow_mul_taylor_remainder_nonneg (hf : IsCompletelyMonotone f) {x T : ℝ} {n : ℕ}
    (hx : 0 ≤ x) (hxT : x ≤ T) :
    0 ≤ (-1 : ℝ) ^ n * ∫ t in x..T,
      (↑(n - 1).factorial)⁻¹ * (T - t) ^ (n - 1) *
      iteratedDerivWithin n f (Icc x T) t

decls.name: TauCeti.IsCompletelyMonotone.iteratedDerivWithin_one_nonpos
decls.doc:
The first iterated derivative within `[0, ∞)` of a completely monotone function is
nonpositive (the `derivWithin` sign condition restated for `iteratedDerivWithin 1`).
decls.statement:
lemma IsCompletelyMonotone.iteratedDerivWithin_one_nonpos
    (hf : IsCompletelyMonotone f) {t : ℝ} (ht : 0 ≤ t) :
    iteratedDerivWithin 1 f (Ici 0) t ≤ 0

decls.name: TauCeti.IsCompletelyMonotone.continuousOn_iteratedDerivWithin_uIcc
decls.doc:
Every iterated derivative within `[0, ∞)` of a completely monotone function is continuous on
the interval spanned by any two nonnegative endpoints. The endpoints need no ordering: `uIcc` is
the unordered interval, and `[0, ∞)` is order-connected.
decls.statement:
lemma IsCompletelyMonotone.continuousOn_iteratedDerivWithin_uIcc (hcm : IsCompletelyMonotone f)
    (m : ℕ) {x T : ℝ} (hx : 0 ≤ x) (hT : 0 ≤ T) :
    ContinuousOn (iteratedDerivWithin m f (Ici 0)) (uIcc x T)

decls.name: TauCeti.IsCompletelyMonotone.integral_neg_iteratedDerivWithin_one_Ici_eq_sub
decls.doc:
On a compact interval in `[0, ∞)`, the integral of `-f'` for a completely monotone
function is the endpoint drop, with the derivative taken within `[0, ∞)`.
decls.statement:
lemma IsCompletelyMonotone.integral_neg_iteratedDerivWithin_one_Ici_eq_sub
    (hcm : IsCompletelyMonotone f) {x T : ℝ} (hx : 0 ≤ x) (hxT : x ≤ T) :
    ∫ t in x..T, -iteratedDerivWithin 1 f (Ici 0) t = f x - f T

decls.name: TauCeti.IsCompletelyMonotone.neg_iteratedDerivWithin_one_integrableOn
decls.doc:
`-f'` is integrable on `(0, ∞)` for a completely monotone function, where the derivative is
taken within the closed half-line `[0, ∞)`.
decls.statement:
lemma IsCompletelyMonotone.neg_iteratedDerivWithin_one_integrableOn
    (hcm : IsCompletelyMonotone f) :
    IntegrableOn (fun t => -iteratedDerivWithin 1 f (Ici 0) t) (Ioi 0)

decls.name: TauCeti.IsCompletelyMonotone.integral_Ioi_neg_iteratedDerivWithin_one_of_nonneg
decls.doc:
The improper integral `∫ₓ^∞ (-f') dt = f x - L` from an arbitrary nonnegative endpoint `x`,
for a completely monotone function with limit `L` at infinity.
decls.statement:
lemma IsCompletelyMonotone.integral_Ioi_neg_iteratedDerivWithin_one_of_nonneg
    (hcm : IsCompletelyMonotone f) {x : ℝ} (hx : 0 ≤ x) {L : ℝ}
    (hL : Tendsto f atTop (nhds L)) :
    ∫ t in Ioi x, -iteratedDerivWithin 1 f (Ici 0) t = f x - L

decls.name: TauCeti.IsCompletelyMonotone.integral_Ioi_neg_iteratedDerivWithin_one
decls.doc: The improper integral `∫₀^∞ (-f') dt = f(0) - L` for completely monotone functions.
decls.statement:
lemma IsCompletelyMonotone.integral_Ioi_neg_iteratedDerivWithin_one
    (hcm : IsCompletelyMonotone f) {L : ℝ} (hL : Tendsto f atTop (nhds L)) :
    ∫ t in Ioi 0, -iteratedDerivWithin 1 f (Ici 0) t = f 0 - L

decls.name: TauCeti.iteratedDeriv_iteratedDeriv
decls.statement:
theorem iteratedDeriv_iteratedDeriv (f : ℝ → ℝ) (n k : ℕ) :
    iteratedDeriv n (iteratedDeriv k f) = iteratedDeriv (n + k) f

decls.name: TauCeti.IsCompletelyMonotoneOnIoi.mul
decls.doc: Completely monotone functions on `(0, ∞)` are closed under pointwise multiplication.
decls.statement:
theorem mul (hf : IsCompletelyMonotoneOnIoi f) (hg : IsCompletelyMonotoneOnIoi g) :
    IsCompletelyMonotoneOnIoi (f * g)

decls.name: TauCeti.IsCompletelyMonotoneOnIoi.prod
decls.doc: Completely monotone functions on `(0, ∞)` are closed under finite products.

decls.name: TauCeti.IsCompletelyMonotoneOnIoi.pow
decls.doc: Completely monotone functions on `(0, ∞)` are closed under taking natural powers.
decls.statement: theorem pow (hf : IsCompletelyMonotoneOnIoi f) (k : ℕ) : IsCompletelyMonotoneOnIoi (f ^ k)

decls.name: TauCeti.IsCompletelyMonotoneOnIoi.neg_one_pow_mul_iteratedDeriv
decls.doc:
Every alternating ordinary iterated derivative of a completely monotone function on
`(0, ∞)` is completely monotone there.
decls.statement:
theorem neg_one_pow_mul_iteratedDeriv (hf : IsCompletelyMonotoneOnIoi f) (k : ℕ) :
    IsCompletelyMonotoneOnIoi (fun t => (-1 : ℝ) ^ k * iteratedDeriv k f t)

decls.name: TauCeti.IsCompletelyMonotoneOnIoi.neg_deriv
decls.doc:
The negated ordinary derivative of a completely monotone function on `(0, ∞)` is completely
monotone there.
decls.statement:
theorem neg_deriv (hf : IsCompletelyMonotoneOnIoi f) :
    IsCompletelyMonotoneOnIoi (fun t => -deriv f t)

decls.name: TauCeti.neg_one_pow_mul_descPochhammer_neg_nonneg
decls.doc:
The falling factorial `(-s)(-s-1)⋯(-s-n+1) = (descPochhammer ℝ n)(-s)` carries the sign
`(-1)ⁿ` when `s ≥ 0`: multiplying it by `(-1)ⁿ` yields the nonnegative rising factorial
`s(s+1)⋯(s+n-1)`. This is the sign bookkeeping behind complete monotonicity of `t ↦ t^{-s}`.
decls.statement:
lemma neg_one_pow_mul_descPochhammer_neg_nonneg {s : ℝ} (hs : 0 ≤ s) (n : ℕ) :
    0 ≤ (-1 : ℝ) ^ n * (descPochhammer ℝ n).eval (-s)

decls.name: TauCeti.isCompletelyMonotoneOnIoi_rpow_neg
decls.doc:
For `s ≥ 0`, the negative power `t ↦ t^{-s}` is completely monotone on the open half-line
`(0, ∞)`. The case `s = 1` is `t ↦ 1/t`, whose representing measure is (infinite) Lebesgue
measure; the demand for smoothness only on `(0, ∞)` is essential, as `t^{-s}` blows up at the
boundary for `s > 0`.
decls.statement:
theorem isCompletelyMonotoneOnIoi_rpow_neg {s : ℝ} (hs : 0 ≤ s) :
    IsCompletelyMonotoneOnIoi (fun t => t ^ (-s))

decls.name: TauCeti.isCompletelyMonotone_inv_const_add
decls.doc:
For `a > 0`, the reciprocal `t ↦ (a + t)⁻¹` is completely monotone. This is the resolvent
kernel `t ↦ (λ + t)⁻¹` of the roadmap's semigroup theory.
decls.statement:
theorem isCompletelyMonotone_inv_const_add {a : ℝ} (ha : 0 < a) :
    IsCompletelyMonotone (fun t => (a + t)⁻¹)

decls.name: TauCeti.isCompletelyMonotone_one_div_const_add
decls.doc:
For `a > 0`, the reciprocal `t ↦ 1 / (a + t)` is completely monotone. This is the `1 / (a + t)`
phrasing of the resolvent kernel `isCompletelyMonotone_inv_const_add`.
decls.statement:
theorem isCompletelyMonotone_one_div_const_add {a : ℝ} (ha : 0 < a) :
    IsCompletelyMonotone (fun t => 1 / (a + t))

decls.name: TauCeti.isCompletelyMonotone_one_div_one_add
decls.doc:
The roadmap acceptance example: `t ↦ 1 / (1 + t)` is completely monotone. Its representing
measure under Bernstein's theorem is the exponential distribution `e^{-x} dx`.
decls.statement:
theorem isCompletelyMonotone_one_div_one_add :
    IsCompletelyMonotone (fun t => 1 / (1 + t))

decls.name: TauCeti.IsCompletelyMonotone.comp_const_mul
decls.doc:
Completely monotone functions are closed under scaling the argument by a nonnegative
constant: if `f` is completely monotone and `0 ≤ c`, then `t ↦ f (c · t)` is completely
monotone. The `n`-th alternating derivative is multiplied by the nonnegative factor `cⁿ`.
decls.statement:
theorem comp_const_mul (hf : IsCompletelyMonotone f) {c : ℝ} (hc : 0 ≤ c) :
    IsCompletelyMonotone (fun t => f (c * t))

decls.name: TauCeti.IsCompletelyMonotone.comp_add_const
decls.doc:
Completely monotone functions are closed under shifting the argument by a nonnegative
constant: if `f` is completely monotone and `0 ≤ a`, then `t ↦ f (t + a)` is completely
monotone. The alternating derivative is unchanged, evaluated at the shifted point.
decls.statement:
theorem comp_add_const (hf : IsCompletelyMonotone f) {a : ℝ} (ha : 0 ≤ a) :
    IsCompletelyMonotone (fun t => f (t + a))

decls.name: TauCeti.IsCompletelyMonotone.comp_affine
decls.doc:
Completely monotone functions are closed under nonnegative affine reparametrization of the
argument: if `f` is completely monotone and `0 ≤ c`, `0 ≤ a`, then `t ↦ f (c · t + a)` is
completely monotone.
decls.statement:
theorem comp_affine (hf : IsCompletelyMonotone f) {c a : ℝ} (hc : 0 ≤ c) (ha : 0 ≤ a) :
    IsCompletelyMonotone (fun t => f (c * t + a))

decls.name: TauCeti.differentiableAt_of_continuousOn_exp_comp
decls.doc:
**The local upgrade.** A continuous branch `L` of `log ∘ g` on an open set is complex
differentiable wherever `g` is, because near any point it coincides with an honest local branch of
`log` composed with `g`.
decls.title: The local upgrade
decls.statement:
theorem differentiableAt_of_continuousOn_exp_comp {U : Set ℂ} (hU : IsOpen U)
    {L g : ℂ → ℂ} (hL : ContinuousOn L U) (hEq : EqOn (Complex.exp ∘ L) g U)
    (hg : DifferentiableOn ℂ g U) {z₀ : ℂ} (hz₀ : z₀ ∈ U) :
    DifferentiableAt ℂ L z₀

decls.name: TauCeti.exists_differentiableOn_eqOn_exp_comp
decls.doc:
**A holomorphic branch of `log ∘ g` on a simply connected domain.** If `g` is holomorphic and
nowhere zero on a simply connected open `U ⊆ ℂ`, there is a holomorphic `f` on `U` with
`exp ∘ f = g`. Mathlib's `Complex.exists_continuousOn_eqOn_exp_comp` supplies the branch; only its
holomorphy is added here.
decls.title: A holomorphic branch of `log ∘ g` on a simply connected domain
decls.statement:
theorem exists_differentiableOn_eqOn_exp_comp {U : Set ℂ} (hUc : IsSimplyConnected U)
    (hUo : IsOpen U) {g : ℂ → ℂ} (hg : DifferentiableOn ℂ g U) (hU₀ : 0 ∉ g '' U) :
    ∃ f : ℂ → ℂ, DifferentiableOn ℂ f U ∧ EqOn (Complex.exp ∘ f) g U

decls.name: TauCeti.exists_differentiableOn_pow_eq
decls.doc:
**A holomorphic `n`-th root on a simply connected domain.** The Koebe square-root step of the
Riemann mapping theorem is the case `n = 2`.
