decls.title: A holomorphic `n`-th root on a simply connected domain
decls.statement:
theorem exists_differentiableOn_pow_eq {U : Set ℂ} (hUc : IsSimplyConnected U) (hUo : IsOpen U)
    {g : ℂ → ℂ} (hg : DifferentiableOn ℂ g U) (hU₀ : 0 ∉ g '' U) {n : ℕ} (hn : n ≠ 0) :
    ∃ f : ℂ → ℂ, DifferentiableOn ℂ f U ∧ EqOn (fun z => f z ^ n) g U

decls.name: TauCeti.DifferentiableOn.toOpenPartialHomeomorph
decls.doc:
Package an injective holomorphic map on an open set as an open partial homeomorphism onto its
image.

On the image, `Function.invFunOn f U` selects the unique preimage in `U`; no injectivity of `f`
outside `U` is required.
decls.statement:
def DifferentiableOn.toOpenPartialHomeomorph
    (hf : DifferentiableOn ℂ f U) (hU : IsOpen U) (hinj : InjOn f U) :
    OpenPartialHomeomorph ℂ ℂ

decls.name: TauCeti.DifferentiableOn.toOpenPartialHomeomorph_source
decls.doc:
The source of the partial homeomorphism associated to an injective holomorphic map is its
given domain.
decls.statement:
theorem DifferentiableOn.toOpenPartialHomeomorph_source
    (hf : DifferentiableOn ℂ f U) (hU : IsOpen U) (hinj : InjOn f U) :
    (TauCeti.DifferentiableOn.toOpenPartialHomeomorph hf hU hinj).source = U

decls.name: TauCeti.DifferentiableOn.toOpenPartialHomeomorph_target
decls.doc:
The target of the partial homeomorphism associated to an injective holomorphic map is its
image.
decls.statement:
theorem DifferentiableOn.toOpenPartialHomeomorph_target
    (hf : DifferentiableOn ℂ f U) (hU : IsOpen U) (hinj : InjOn f U) :
    (TauCeti.DifferentiableOn.toOpenPartialHomeomorph hf hU hinj).target = f '' U

decls.name: TauCeti.DifferentiableOn.toOpenPartialHomeomorph_apply
decls.doc:
The partial homeomorphism associated to an injective holomorphic map applies as the original
map.
decls.statement:
theorem DifferentiableOn.toOpenPartialHomeomorph_apply
    (hf : DifferentiableOn ℂ f U) (hU : IsOpen U) (hinj : InjOn f U) (z : ℂ) :
    TauCeti.DifferentiableOn.toOpenPartialHomeomorph hf hU hinj z = f z

decls.name: TauCeti.DifferentiableOn.toOpenPartialHomeomorph_coe
decls.doc:
The underlying function of the partial homeomorphism associated to an injective holomorphic
map is the original map.
decls.statement:
theorem DifferentiableOn.toOpenPartialHomeomorph_coe
    (hf : DifferentiableOn ℂ f U) (hU : IsOpen U) (hinj : InjOn f U) :
    (TauCeti.DifferentiableOn.toOpenPartialHomeomorph hf hU hinj : ℂ → ℂ) = f

decls.name: TauCeti.DifferentiableOn.toOpenPartialHomeomorph_symm_apply
decls.doc:
The inverse of the partial homeomorphism associated to an injective holomorphic map is
`Function.invFunOn` for the specified domain.
decls.statement:
theorem DifferentiableOn.toOpenPartialHomeomorph_symm_apply
    (hf : DifferentiableOn ℂ f U) (hU : IsOpen U) (hinj : InjOn f U) (w : ℂ) :
    (TauCeti.DifferentiableOn.toOpenPartialHomeomorph hf hU hinj).symm w =
      Function.invFunOn f U w

decls.name: TauCeti.DifferentiableOn.toOpenPartialHomeomorph_coe_symm
decls.doc:
The underlying inverse function of the partial homeomorphism associated to an injective
holomorphic map is `Function.invFunOn` for the specified domain.
decls.statement:
theorem DifferentiableOn.toOpenPartialHomeomorph_coe_symm
    (hf : DifferentiableOn ℂ f U) (hU : IsOpen U) (hinj : InjOn f U) :
    ((TauCeti.DifferentiableOn.toOpenPartialHomeomorph hf hU hinj).symm : ℂ → ℂ) =
      Function.invFunOn f U

decls.name: TauCeti.DifferentiableOn.toHomeomorphOfBijOn
decls.doc:
Package a holomorphic bijection from an open set `U` onto a set `V` as a homeomorphism between
the corresponding subtypes.

This is the subtype equivalence carried by
`TauCeti.DifferentiableOn.toOpenPartialHomeomorph`, with its target identified using the supplied
`BijOn` hypothesis.
decls.statement:
def DifferentiableOn.toHomeomorphOfBijOn {V : Set ℂ}
    (hf : DifferentiableOn ℂ f U) (hU : IsOpen U) (hbij : BijOn f U V) : U ≃ₜ V

decls.name: TauCeti.DifferentiableOn.toHomeomorphOfBijOn_apply
decls.doc: The homeomorphism induced by a holomorphic bijection applies as the original map.

decls.name: TauCeti.DifferentiableOn.toHomeomorphOfBijOn_symm_apply
decls.doc:
The inverse homeomorphism induced by a holomorphic bijection applies as
`Function.invFunOn`.
decls.statement:
theorem DifferentiableOn.toHomeomorphOfBijOn_symm_apply {V : Set ℂ}
    (hf : DifferentiableOn ℂ f U) (hU : IsOpen U) (hbij : BijOn f U V) (w : V) :
    (((TauCeti.DifferentiableOn.toHomeomorphOfBijOn hf hU hbij).symm w : U) : ℂ) =
      Function.invFunOn f U w

decls.name: TauCeti.DifferentiableOn.differentiableOn_toOpenPartialHomeomorph_symm
decls.doc:
The inverse of the open partial homeomorphism associated to an injective holomorphic map is
holomorphic on its target.
decls.statement:
theorem DifferentiableOn.differentiableOn_toOpenPartialHomeomorph_symm
    (hf : DifferentiableOn ℂ f U) (hU : IsOpen U) (hinj : InjOn f U) :
    DifferentiableOn ℂ
      (TauCeti.DifferentiableOn.toOpenPartialHomeomorph hf hU hinj).symm (f '' U)

decls.name: TauCeti.DifferentiableOn.conformalAt_of_isOpen_of_injOn
decls.doc: An injective holomorphic map on an open set is conformal at every point of that set.
decls.statement:
theorem DifferentiableOn.conformalAt_of_isOpen_of_injOn
    (hf : DifferentiableOn ℂ f U) (hU : IsOpen U) (hinj : InjOn f U)
    {z : ℂ} (hz : z ∈ U) : ConformalAt f z

decls.name: TauCeti.DifferentiableOn.conformalAt_toOpenPartialHomeomorph
decls.doc:
The open partial homeomorphism associated to an injective holomorphic map is conformal on its
source.
decls.statement:
theorem DifferentiableOn.conformalAt_toOpenPartialHomeomorph
    (hf : DifferentiableOn ℂ f U) (hU : IsOpen U) (hinj : InjOn f U)
    {z : ℂ} (hz : z ∈ U) :
    ConformalAt (TauCeti.DifferentiableOn.toOpenPartialHomeomorph hf hU hinj) z

decls.name: TauCeti.DifferentiableOn.conformalAt_toOpenPartialHomeomorph_symm
decls.doc:
The inverse of the open partial homeomorphism associated to an injective holomorphic map is
conformal on its target.
decls.statement:
theorem DifferentiableOn.conformalAt_toOpenPartialHomeomorph_symm
    (hf : DifferentiableOn ℂ f U) (hU : IsOpen U) (hinj : InjOn f U)
    {w : ℂ} (hw : w ∈ f '' U) :
    ConformalAt
      (TauCeti.DifferentiableOn.toOpenPartialHomeomorph hf hU hinj).symm w

decls.name: TauCeti.eventuallyEq_nhds_of_analyticOnNhd_ball
decls.doc:
Two functions analytic on a ball whose germs agree at one point of the ball have equal germs
at every point of the ball. This is the identity principle in germ form: the ball is preconnected,
so agreement near one of its points propagates to all of it, and the ball is open, so agreement on
it is agreement near each of its points.

decls.name: TauCeti.eventually_eventuallyEq_iff_of_analyticAt
decls.doc:
**Germ agreement is locally constant.** If `F` and `G` are both analytic at `z`, then for all
`w` near `z` the germs of `F` and `G` agree at `w` exactly when they agree at `z`.
decls.title: Germ agreement is locally constant
decls.statement:
theorem eventually_eventuallyEq_iff_of_analyticAt {F G : ℂ → ℂ} {z : ℂ} (hF : AnalyticAt ℂ F z)
    (hG : AnalyticAt ℂ G z) :
    ∀ᶠ w in 𝓝 z, ((F =ᶠ[𝓝 w] G) ↔ (F =ᶠ[𝓝 z] G))

decls.name: TauCeti.eq_of_isPreconnected_of_eventually_iff
decls.doc:
A property that is locally constant along a preconnected set is constant along it.

This is `IsLocallyConstant.apply_eq_of_preconnectedSpace` transported to the subspace `s`; it is
kept private because the general-topology statement belongs upstream rather than in a
complex-analysis file.

decls.name: TauCeti.IsAnalyticContinuationAlong
decls.doc:
`IsAnalyticContinuationAlong f γ s` says that the family `f` is an **analytic continuation
along the path `γ`** over the parameter set `s`: for each parameter time `t ∈ s` the function `f t`
is analytic at the point `γ t`, and the germ carried at time `t` is locally constant in `t`, in the
sense that `f u` and `f t` have the same germ at `γ u` for every `u ∈ s` close enough to `t`.

Only the germ of `f t` at `γ t` matters; the values of `f t` away from `γ t` are unconstrained.
Reading the germs as points of the étale space of holomorphic germs over `ℂ`, the condition says
precisely that `t ↦ (germ of f t at γ t)` is a continuous lift of `γ`.
decls.statement: structure IsAnalyticContinuationAlong (f : X → ℂ → ℂ) (γ : X → ℂ) (s : Set X) : Prop

decls.name: TauCeti.IsAnalyticContinuationAlong.mono
decls.doc: A continuation restricts to any smaller parameter set.
decls.statement:
theorem mono (hf : IsAnalyticContinuationAlong f γ s) {s' : Set X} (hs' : s' ⊆ s) :
    IsAnalyticContinuationAlong f γ s'

decls.name: TauCeti.IsAnalyticContinuationAlong.const
decls.doc:
The constant family is a continuation: a function analytic at every point of the path
continues itself along it.
decls.statement:
theorem const {F : ℂ → ℂ} (hγ : ContinuousOn γ s) (hF : ∀ t ∈ s, AnalyticAt ℂ F (γ t)) :
    IsAnalyticContinuationAlong (fun _ => F) γ s

decls.name: TauCeti.IsAnalyticContinuationAlong.of_differentiableOn
decls.doc:
A holomorphic function on an open set continues itself along any path that stays in that
set. This is the source of the continuations that a single-valued function admits.
decls.statement:
theorem of_differentiableOn {U : Set ℂ} {F : ℂ → ℂ} (hU : IsOpen U) (hF : DifferentiableOn ℂ F U)
    (hγ : ContinuousOn γ s) (hmem : ∀ t ∈ s, γ t ∈ U) :
    IsAnalyticContinuationAlong (fun _ => F) γ s

decls.name: TauCeti.IsAnalyticContinuationAlong.congr
decls.doc:
**A continuation depends only on the germs it carries.** Replacing each `f t` by a function
with the same germ at `γ t` again gives a continuation along `γ`.
decls.title: A continuation depends only on the germs it carries
decls.statement:
theorem congr (hf : IsAnalyticContinuationAlong f γ s) {f' : X → ℂ → ℂ}
    (h : ∀ t ∈ s, f' t =ᶠ[𝓝 (γ t)] f t) : IsAnalyticContinuationAlong f' γ s

decls.name: TauCeti.IsAnalyticContinuationAlong.deriv
decls.doc: Differentiating a continuation term by term gives a continuation of the derivative germ.
decls.statement:
theorem deriv (hf : IsAnalyticContinuationAlong f γ s) :
    IsAnalyticContinuationAlong (fun t => _root_.deriv (f t)) γ s

decls.name: TauCeti.IsAnalyticContinuationAlong.add
decls.doc: Continuations add: the pointwise sum family `f + g` continues along `γ` as well.
decls.statement:
theorem add (hf : IsAnalyticContinuationAlong f γ s)
    (hg : IsAnalyticContinuationAlong g γ s) :
    IsAnalyticContinuationAlong (f + g) γ s

decls.name: TauCeti.IsAnalyticContinuationAlong.mul
decls.doc: Continuations multiply: the pointwise product family `f * g` continues along `γ` as well.
decls.statement:
theorem mul (hf : IsAnalyticContinuationAlong f γ s)
    (hg : IsAnalyticContinuationAlong g γ s) :
    IsAnalyticContinuationAlong (f * g) γ s

decls.name: TauCeti.IsAnalyticContinuationAlong.eventually_eventuallyEq_iff
decls.doc:
Agreement of two continuations along the same path is a locally constant property of the
parameter. This is the local step of the uniqueness theorem.
decls.statement:
theorem eventually_eventuallyEq_iff (hf : IsAnalyticContinuationAlong f γ s)
    (hg : IsAnalyticContinuationAlong g γ s) {t : X} (ht : t ∈ s) :
    ∀ᶠ u in 𝓝[s] t, ((f u =ᶠ[𝓝 (γ u)] g u) ↔ (f t =ᶠ[𝓝 (γ t)] g t))

decls.name: TauCeti.IsAnalyticContinuationAlong.eventuallyEq
decls.doc:
**Uniqueness of analytic continuation along a path.** Two analytic continuations along the same
path, over a preconnected parameter set, that carry the same germ at one parameter time carry the
same germ at every parameter time.

Preconnectedness of the parameter set cannot be dropped: over a two-point parameter set the
hypotheses put no relation at all between the germs carried at its two points.
decls.title: Uniqueness of analytic continuation along a path
decls.statement:
theorem eventuallyEq (hf : IsAnalyticContinuationAlong f γ s)
    (hg : IsAnalyticContinuationAlong g γ s) (hs : IsPreconnected s) {a b : X} (ha : a ∈ s)
    (hb : b ∈ s) (hab : f a =ᶠ[𝓝 (γ a)] g a) :
    f b =ᶠ[𝓝 (γ b)] g b

decls.name: TauCeti.IsAnalyticContinuationAlong.eq_of_eventuallyEq
decls.doc:
Two continuations along the same path that carry the same germ at one parameter time take the
same value at every parameter time.
decls.statement:
theorem eq_of_eventuallyEq (hf : IsAnalyticContinuationAlong f γ s)
    (hg : IsAnalyticContinuationAlong g γ s) (hs : IsPreconnected s) {a b : X} (ha : a ∈ s)
    (hb : b ∈ s) (hab : f a =ᶠ[𝓝 (γ a)] g a) :
    f b (γ b) = g b (γ b)

decls.name: TauCeti.IsAnalyticContinuationAlong.eventuallyEq_of_mapsTo
decls.doc:
**A single-valued function is its own continuation.** If a path stays inside an open set on
which `F` is holomorphic, then any continuation along that path which starts at the germ of `F`
carries the germ of `F` throughout. So continuing a holomorphic function inside its domain never
produces a new branch: new branches can only appear once the path leaves the domain.
decls.title: A single-valued function is its own continuation
decls.statement:
theorem eventuallyEq_of_mapsTo {U : Set ℂ} {F : ℂ → ℂ} (hf : IsAnalyticContinuationAlong f γ s)
    (hs : IsPreconnected s) (hU : IsOpen U) (hF : DifferentiableOn ℂ F U)
    (hmem : ∀ t ∈ s, γ t ∈ U) {a b : X} (ha : a ∈ s) (hb : b ∈ s) (hab : f a =ᶠ[𝓝 (γ a)] F) :
    f b =ᶠ[𝓝 (γ b)] F

decls.name: TauCeti.exists_sq_eq_sub_injOn_ne_zero
decls.doc:
**A holomorphic square root of `z - a`.** On a simply connected open `U` avoiding `a` the
function `z - a` is nonvanishing, so it has a holomorphic square root. Squaring such a root
recovers `z - a`, which pins down `z` because `a` is fixed, so `z ↦ h z ^ 2` is injective on `U`;
and `h` is nonvanishing, because its square is.
decls.title: A holomorphic square root of `z - a`
decls.statement:
lemma exists_sq_eq_sub_injOn_ne_zero {U : Set ℂ} (hUc : IsSimplyConnected U)
    (hUo : IsOpen U) {a : ℂ} (ha : a ∉ U) :
    ∃ h : ℂ → ℂ, DifferentiableOn ℂ h U ∧ (∀ z ∈ U, h z ^ 2 = z - a) ∧
      InjOn (fun z => h z ^ 2) U ∧ ∀ z ∈ U, h z ≠ 0

decls.name: TauCeti.le_norm_add_of_ball_subset_image
decls.doc:
**A square-injective function avoids its own negation, quantitatively.** If squaring `h` is
injective on `U` and `h` is nonvanishing there, and a ball of radius `r` about `w₀` lies inside
`h '' U`, then `-h z` stays outside that ball for every `z ∈ U`: otherwise `-h z = h z'` for some
`z' ∈ U`, and equal squares force `z' = z`, hence `h z = 0`.
decls.title: A square-injective function avoids its own negation, quantitatively
decls.statement:
lemma le_norm_add_of_ball_subset_image {U : Set ℂ} {h : ℂ → ℂ} {w₀ : ℂ} {r : ℝ}
    (hsq_inj : Set.InjOn (fun z => h z ^ 2) U) (hne : ∀ z ∈ U, h z ≠ 0)
    (hball : ball w₀ r ⊆ h '' U) :
    ∀ z ∈ U, r ≤ ‖h z + w₀‖

decls.name: TauCeti.exists_differentiableOn_injOn_mapsTo_unitBall
decls.doc:
**A simply connected proper domain injects into the unit disc.** The Riemann mapping theorem's
competing family — injective holomorphic maps `U → 𝔻` — is nonempty.
decls.title: A simply connected proper domain injects into the unit disc
decls.statement:
theorem exists_differentiableOn_injOn_mapsTo_unitBall {U : Set ℂ} (hUc : IsSimplyConnected U)
    (hUo : IsOpen U) (hUne : U ≠ univ) :
    ∃ f : ℂ → ℂ, DifferentiableOn ℂ f U ∧ InjOn f U ∧ MapsTo f U (ball (0 : ℂ) 1)

decls.name: TauCeti.exists_differentiableOn_injOn_mapsTo_unitBall_apply_eq_zero
decls.doc:
**The normalized competing family is nonempty.** The roadmap's maximization step ranges over
injective holomorphic maps `U → 𝔻` that *fix a chosen base point* `z₀`, so the nonemptiness it needs
is this one, not the bare version above.

The normalization is the textbook one: post-compose with the disc automorphism centred at
`c = f z₀`, `w ↦ (w - c) / (1 - conj c * w)`. That is the L2 disc-automorphism API of this roadmap,
already available here as `TauCeti.unitDiscMoebius` and its scalar formula, so this step consumes
it rather than substituting a weaker correction:

* holomorphy — `TauCeti.differentiableOn_unitDiscMoebiusFormula_of_norm_lt_one`;
* self-map of `𝔻` — `TauCeti.mapsTo_ball_unitDiscMoebiusFormula_of_norm_lt_one`;
* injectivity on `𝔻` — the factor centred at `-c` is a left inverse
  (`TauCeti.leftInvOn_unitDiscMoebiusFormula_of_norm_lt_one`).

Each is stated for a scalar centre of norm `< 1`, which is exactly what `f z₀ ∈ 𝔻` supplies, so no
passage through the bundled `Complex.UnitDisc` is needed. The Moebius factor is onto `𝔻`, which the
uniqueness half of the Riemann mapping theorem will need; the *nonempty normalized family*
obligation proved here uses only the three properties above.
decls.title: The normalized competing family is nonempty

decls.name: TauCeti.IsPointedDiscInjectionOn
decls.doc:
A **pointed disc injection** on `Ω` at the base point `z₀`: a holomorphic injection of `Ω`
into the open unit disc sending `z₀` to the origin. It is the pointed form of the maps produced by
`TauCeti.exists_differentiableOn_injOn_mapsTo_unitBall` in `DiscInjection.lean`.

Such maps are classically called *schlicht*, the traditional name for an injective holomorphic map;
the name here deliberately avoids *normalized*, which conventionally demands the further
normalization `deriv f z₀ = 1` that this predicate does not impose.

This is the competing family of the Riemann mapping theorem's extremal problem: the theorem is
proved by maximizing `‖deriv f z₀‖` over all such `f`.
decls.statement: structure IsPointedDiscInjectionOn (f : ℂ → ℂ) (Ω : Set ℂ) (z₀ : ℂ) : Prop

decls.name: TauCeti.IsPointedDiscInjectionOn.norm_le_one
decls.doc: A pointed disc injection is bounded by `1`, since it lands in the unit disc.
decls.statement: theorem norm_le_one (hf : IsPointedDiscInjectionOn f Ω z₀) {z : ℂ} (hz : z ∈ Ω) : ‖f z‖ ≤ 1

decls.name: TauCeti.IsPointedDiscInjectionOn.deriv_ne_zero
decls.doc:
A pointed disc injection has nonvanishing derivative throughout `Ω`: it is injective on a
neighbourhood of each point, which by the local injectivity criterion forces `deriv f z ≠ 0`.
decls.statement:
theorem deriv_ne_zero (hf : IsPointedDiscInjectionOn f Ω z₀) (hΩo : IsOpen Ω) {z : ℂ} (hz : z ∈ Ω) :
    deriv f z ≠ 0

decls.name: TauCeti.exists_isPointedDiscInjectionOn
decls.doc:
**The competing family is nonempty.** Every base point of a nonempty, simply connected, open,
proper subset of `ℂ` admits a pointed disc injection.

This repackages `TauCeti.exists_differentiableOn_injOn_mapsTo_unitBall_apply_eq_zero`.
decls.title: The competing family is nonempty
decls.statement:
theorem exists_isPointedDiscInjectionOn (hΩc : IsSimplyConnected Ω) (hΩo : IsOpen Ω)
    (hΩne : Ω ≠ univ) (hz₀ : z₀ ∈ Ω) :
    ∃ f : ℂ → ℂ, IsPointedDiscInjectionOn f Ω z₀

decls.name: TauCeti.bddAbove_norm_deriv
decls.doc:
Cauchy's estimate bounds the derivatives at the base point uniformly over the family: on a
closed ball of radius `r` inside `Ω`, every member is bounded by `1`, hence its derivative at the
centre is bounded by `1 / r`.
decls.statement:
theorem bddAbove_norm_deriv (hΩo : IsOpen Ω) (hz₀ : z₀ ∈ Ω) :
    BddAbove ((fun f : ℂ → ℂ => ‖deriv f z₀‖) '' {f | IsPointedDiscInjectionOn f Ω z₀})

decls.name: TauCeti.deriv_eq_zero_of_forall_eq
decls.doc: A function constant on an open set has vanishing derivative there.
decls.statement:
theorem deriv_eq_zero_of_forall_eq (hΩo : IsOpen Ω) {v z : ℂ} (hz : z ∈ Ω)
    (h : ∀ w ∈ Ω, g w = v) : deriv g z = 0

decls.name: TauCeti.mapsTo_ball_of_forall_norm_le_one
decls.doc:
A holomorphic map bounded by `1` on a preconnected open set, vanishing somewhere, maps into the
**open** unit disc. A boundary value would be an interior maximum of `‖g‖`, and the maximum modulus
principle would then force `‖g‖` to be constantly `1`, contradicting the vanishing.
decls.statement:
theorem mapsTo_ball_of_forall_norm_le_one (hΩo : IsOpen Ω) (hconn : IsPreconnected Ω)
    (hgd : DifferentiableOn ℂ g Ω) (hle : ∀ z ∈ Ω, ‖g z‖ ≤ 1) (hz₀ : z₀ ∈ Ω) (hg₀ : g z₀ = 0) :
    MapsTo g Ω (ball (0 : ℂ) 1)

decls.name: TauCeti.exists_isMaxOn_norm_deriv
decls.doc:
**The extremal problem has a solution.** If the competing family at a base point `z₀` of an
open preconnected set `Ω` is nonempty, then some member maximizes `‖deriv · z₀‖` over the whole
family.

The compactness argument needs nothing beyond these hypotheses: preconnectedness for the maximum
modulus principle and for Hurwitz's theorem, and one competitor to make the supremum positive.
Simple connectivity enters only through
`TauCeti.exists_isPointedDiscInjectionOn`, which supplies that competitor; see the corollary
`TauCeti.exists_isMaxOn_norm_deriv_of_isSimplyConnected`.

This is the compactness half of the Riemann mapping theorem. It does **not** assert that the
maximizer is surjective; that is the Koebe square-root argument, proved elsewhere.
decls.title: The extremal problem has a solution
decls.statement:
theorem exists_isMaxOn_norm_deriv (hΩo : IsOpen Ω) (hconn : IsPreconnected Ω) (hz₀ : z₀ ∈ Ω)
    (hne : ∃ f : ℂ → ℂ, IsPointedDiscInjectionOn f Ω z₀) :
    ∃ g : ℂ → ℂ, IsPointedDiscInjectionOn g Ω z₀ ∧
      ∀ f : ℂ → ℂ, IsPointedDiscInjectionOn f Ω z₀ → ‖deriv f z₀‖ ≤ ‖deriv g z₀‖

decls.name: TauCeti.exists_isMaxOn_norm_deriv_of_isSimplyConnected
decls.doc:
**The extremal problem has a solution on a simply connected proper subdomain.** This is the
form the Riemann mapping theorem uses: on a nonempty, simply connected, open, proper subset `Ω` of
`ℂ` with base point `z₀`, some pointed disc injection maximizes `‖deriv · z₀‖`.

Simple connectivity and properness serve only to produce one competitor; the compactness argument
itself is `TauCeti.exists_isMaxOn_norm_deriv`.
decls.title: The extremal problem has a solution on a simply connected proper subdomain
decls.statement:
theorem exists_isMaxOn_norm_deriv_of_isSimplyConnected (hΩc : IsSimplyConnected Ω) (hΩo : IsOpen Ω)
    (hΩne : Ω ≠ univ) (hz₀ : z₀ ∈ Ω) :
    ∃ g : ℂ → ℂ, IsPointedDiscInjectionOn g Ω z₀ ∧
      ∀ f : ℂ → ℂ, IsPointedDiscInjectionOn f Ω z₀ → ‖deriv f z₀‖ ≤ ‖deriv g z₀‖

decls.name: TauCeti.exists_radius_sphere_ne_zero
decls.doc:
**A circle on which `g` does not vanish.** If `g` is zero-free on some punctured
neighbourhood of `z₀ ∈ Ω` with `Ω` open — `z₀` itself may be a zero, or not — there is a radius
whose *closed* ball lies in `Ω` and on whose bounding circle `g` does not vanish. That circle is
what Rouché's theorem is applied to.
decls.title: A circle on which `g` does not vanish

decls.name: TauCeti.eventually_ne_of_not_forall_eq
decls.doc:
**An analytic function on a preconnected set attains a value it does not attain identically
only in isolation.** If `g` is analytic on `Ω` and is not constantly `v` there, then `g z ≠ v` on
a punctured neighbourhood of any `x ∈ Ω`.
decls.statement:
theorem eventually_ne_of_not_forall_eq {Ω : Set ℂ} (hconn : IsPreconnected Ω)
    {g : ℂ → ℂ} (hgA : AnalyticOnNhd ℂ g Ω) {v : ℂ} (hnc : ¬ ∀ z ∈ Ω, g z = v)
    {x : ℂ} (hx : x ∈ Ω) : ∀ᶠ z in 𝓝[≠] x, g z ≠ v

decls.name: TauCeti.hurwitz
decls.doc:
**Hurwitz's theorem.** On a connected open set, a locally uniform limit of holomorphic
functions that are nowhere zero is itself either nowhere zero or identically zero.

The dichotomy is genuine: the constant sequence `F n = 1 / (n + 1)` on any `Ω` converges locally
uniformly to `0`, so the second alternative cannot be dropped.
decls.title: Hurwitz's theorem
decls.statement:
theorem hurwitz {ι : Type*} {l : Filter ι} [l.NeBot] {Ω : Set ℂ} (hΩ : IsOpen Ω)
    (hconn : IsPreconnected Ω) {F : ι → ℂ → ℂ} {g : ℂ → ℂ}
    (hF : ∀ᶠ i in l, DifferentiableOn ℂ (F i) Ω)
    (hconv : TendstoLocallyUniformlyOn F g l Ω)
    (hne : ∀ᶠ i in l, ∀ z ∈ Ω, F i z ≠ 0) :
    (∀ z ∈ Ω, g z ≠ 0) ∨ (∀ z ∈ Ω, g z = 0)

decls.name: TauCeti.eventually_exists_eq
decls.doc:
If `g - v` has an isolated zero at `a` inside a disc, then for all large `n` the approximant
`F n` also attains the value `v` in that disc. This is the Rouché step behind `hurwitz_injOn`.
decls.statement:
lemma eventually_exists_eq {ι : Type*} {l : Filter ι} {Ω : Set ℂ} {F : ι → ℂ → ℂ}
    {g : ℂ → ℂ} (hF : ∀ᶠ i in l, DifferentiableOn ℂ (F i) Ω) (hΩ : IsOpen Ω)
    (hg : AnalyticOnNhd ℂ g Ω) (hconv : TendstoLocallyUniformlyOn F g l Ω)
    {a v : ℂ} {ρ : ℝ} (hρ : 0 < ρ) (hball : closedBall a ρ ⊆ Ω)
    (hga : g a = v) (hzf : ∀ z ∈ closedBall a ρ, z ≠ a → g z ≠ v) :
    ∀ᶠ i in l, ∃ z ∈ ball a ρ, F i z = v

decls.name: TauCeti.hurwitz_injOn
decls.doc:
**Hurwitz's theorem for injectivity.** On a connected open set, a locally uniform limit of
*injective* holomorphic functions is either injective or constant.

This is the form the Riemann mapping theorem consumes: it is what keeps the extremal map injective
in the limit. Both alternatives genuinely occur — the injective maps `z ↦ z / (n + 1)` converge
locally uniformly to the constant `0`.

The proof does not route through `hurwitz` on the punctured domain `Ω \ {b}`, which would need
that set to be connected — a fact Mathlib does not currently provide for an open connected subset
of `ℂ`. Instead, if `g` were non-constant with `g a = g b` for `a ≠ b`, we place disjoint discs
about `a` and `b` and use `eventually_exists_eq` on each: for large `n` the injective `F n` would
attain the single value `g a` in both discs, hence at two distinct points.
decls.title: Hurwitz's theorem for injectivity
decls.statement:
theorem hurwitz_injOn {ι : Type*} {l : Filter ι} [l.NeBot] {Ω : Set ℂ} (hΩ : IsOpen Ω)
    (hconn : IsPreconnected Ω) {F : ι → ℂ → ℂ} {g : ℂ → ℂ}
    (hF : ∀ᶠ i in l, DifferentiableOn ℂ (F i) Ω)
    (hconv : TendstoLocallyUniformlyOn F g l Ω)
    (hinj : ∀ᶠ i in l, Set.InjOn (F i) Ω) :
    Set.InjOn g Ω ∨ ∃ v, ∀ z ∈ Ω, g z = v

decls.name: TauCeti.hyperbolicDist
decls.doc:
The hyperbolic (Poincaré) distance on the complex unit disc, written as a total
real-valued function `Real.artanh p` of the pseudo-hyperbolic expression
`p = pseudoHyperbolicExpr z w`.

On the open unit disc this is the hyperbolic distance, normalised to agree with the
infinitesimal Poincaré metric `|dz| / (1 - |z| ^ 2)`.  Outside the disc, where `p` may reach
or exceed one, the formula remains a total Lean expression with no geometric meaning.
decls.statement: def hyperbolicDist (z w : ℂ) : ℝ

decls.name: TauCeti.hyperbolicDist_def
decls.doc: The defining formula for the hyperbolic distance.
decls.statement:
lemma hyperbolicDist_def (z w : ℂ) :
    hyperbolicDist z w = Real.artanh (pseudoHyperbolicExpr z w)

decls.name: TauCeti.hyperbolicDist_comm
decls.doc: The hyperbolic distance is symmetric.
decls.statement: lemma hyperbolicDist_comm (z w : ℂ) : hyperbolicDist z w = hyperbolicDist w z

decls.name: TauCeti.hyperbolicDist_self
decls.doc: The hyperbolic distance from a point to itself is zero.
decls.statement: lemma hyperbolicDist_self (z : ℂ) : hyperbolicDist z z = 0

decls.name: TauCeti.hyperbolicDist_zero_right
decls.doc:
The hyperbolic distance from a point of the disc to the origin has the closed form
`artanh ‖z‖`.
decls.statement:
lemma hyperbolicDist_zero_right (z : ℂ) :
    hyperbolicDist z 0 = Real.artanh ‖z‖

decls.name: TauCeti.hyperbolicDist_nonneg
decls.doc: The hyperbolic distance is nonnegative.
decls.statement: lemma hyperbolicDist_nonneg (z w : ℂ) : 0 ≤ hyperbolicDist z w

decls.name: TauCeti.hyperbolicDist_eq_zero_iff_of_mem_ball
decls.doc: On the open unit disc the hyperbolic distance vanishes exactly on the diagonal.

decls.name: TauCeti.hyperbolicDist_map_le
decls.doc:
**Schwarz--Pick, distance form.** A holomorphic self-map of the complex unit disc does not
increase the hyperbolic distance.
decls.title: Schwarz--Pick, distance form
decls.statement:
theorem hyperbolicDist_map_le {f : ℂ → ℂ}
    (hf : DifferentiableOn ℂ f (ball (0 : ℂ) 1))
    (hmaps : MapsTo f (ball (0 : ℂ) 1) (ball (0 : ℂ) 1))
    {z w : ℂ} (hz : z ∈ ball (0 : ℂ) 1) (hw : w ∈ ball (0 : ℂ) 1) :
    hyperbolicDist (f z) (f w) ≤ hyperbolicDist z w

decls.name: TauCeti.hyperbolicDist_map_le_unitDisc
decls.doc: Bundled unit-disc form of Schwarz--Pick in distance form.
decls.statement:
theorem hyperbolicDist_map_le_unitDisc {f : ℂ → ℂ}
    (hf : DifferentiableOn ℂ f (ball (0 : ℂ) 1))
    (hmaps : MapsTo f (ball (0 : ℂ) 1) (ball (0 : ℂ) 1))
    (z w : Complex.UnitDisc) :
    hyperbolicDist (f z) (f w) ≤ hyperbolicDist (z : ℂ) (w : ℂ)

decls.name: TauCeti.hyperbolicDist_unitDiscMoebius
decls.doc: The disc Moebius factor `z ↦ (z - a) / (1 - conj a * z)` is a hyperbolic isometry.
decls.statement:
theorem hyperbolicDist_unitDiscMoebius (a z w : Complex.UnitDisc) :
    hyperbolicDist (((z : ℂ) - (a : ℂ)) / (1 - (starRingEnd ℂ) (a : ℂ) * (z : ℂ)))
        (((w : ℂ) - (a : ℂ)) / (1 - (starRingEnd ℂ) (a : ℂ) * (w : ℂ)))
      = hyperbolicDist (z : ℂ) (w : ℂ)

decls.name: TauCeti.hyperbolicDist_unitDiscStandardAutomorphismEquiv
decls.doc:
Every standard disc automorphism `z ↦ u * (z - a) / (1 - conj a * z)` is a hyperbolic
isometry.
decls.statement:
theorem hyperbolicDist_unitDiscStandardAutomorphismEquiv
    (u : Circle) (a z w : Complex.UnitDisc) :
    hyperbolicDist (unitDiscStandardAutomorphismEquiv u a z : ℂ)
        (unitDiscStandardAutomorphismEquiv u a w : ℂ)
      = hyperbolicDist (z : ℂ) (w : ℂ)

decls.name: TauCeti.artanh_add
decls.doc:
**Addition formula for the inverse hyperbolic tangent.** For `a, b ∈ (-1, 1)`,
`artanh a + artanh b = artanh ((a + b) / (1 + a * b))`. This is the additive law by which the
hyperbolic distance turns the pseudo-hyperbolic expression into a genuine metric.
decls.title: Addition formula for the inverse hyperbolic tangent
decls.statement:
lemma artanh_add {a b : ℝ} (ha : a ∈ Ioo (-1 : ℝ) 1) (hb : b ∈ Ioo (-1 : ℝ) 1) :
    Real.artanh a + Real.artanh b = Real.artanh ((a + b) / (1 + a * b))

decls.name: TauCeti.pseudoHyperbolicExpr_le_add_div_one_add_mul_of_norm_lt_one
decls.doc:
**Strong pseudo-hyperbolic triangle inequality (origin form).** For two points of the open
unit disc, `pseudoHyperbolicExpr z w ≤ (‖z‖ + ‖w‖) / (1 + ‖z‖ * ‖w‖)`. This is the
`ρ(z, w) ≤ (ρ(z, 0) + ρ(0, w)) / (1 + ρ(z, 0) ρ(0, w))` form of the pseudo-hyperbolic triangle
inequality.
decls.title: Strong pseudo-hyperbolic triangle inequality (origin form)

decls.name: TauCeti.hyperbolicDist_triangle_zero
decls.doc:
**Hyperbolic triangle inequality against the origin.** For two points of the open unit
disc, `hyperbolicDist z w ≤ hyperbolicDist z 0 + hyperbolicDist 0 w`.
decls.title: Hyperbolic triangle inequality against the origin

decls.name: TauCeti.hyperbolicDist_triangle_unitDisc
decls.doc:
**Hyperbolic triangle inequality (bundled unit-disc form).**
`hyperbolicDist z w ≤ hyperbolicDist z u + hyperbolicDist u w`, proved by sending the middle
point `u` to the origin with the Moebius isometry `unitDiscMoebius u`.
decls.title: Hyperbolic triangle inequality (bundled unit-disc form)
decls.statement:
theorem hyperbolicDist_triangle_unitDisc (u z w : Complex.UnitDisc) :
    hyperbolicDist (z : ℂ) (w : ℂ)
      ≤ hyperbolicDist (z : ℂ) (u : ℂ) + hyperbolicDist (u : ℂ) (w : ℂ)

decls.name: TauCeti.hyperbolicDist_triangle
decls.doc:
**Hyperbolic triangle inequality.** The hyperbolic (Poincaré) distance on the complex open
unit disc satisfies `hyperbolicDist z w ≤ hyperbolicDist z u + hyperbolicDist u w`.
decls.title: Hyperbolic triangle inequality

decls.name: TauCeti.isOpen_image_of_differentiableOn_of_injOn
decls.doc:
**The image of an open set under an injective holomorphic map is open.** No connectivity
hypothesis is needed: openness is local, and on a small ball around any point of `Ω` the map is
analytic and nonconstant, so the open mapping theorem applies there.
decls.title: The image of an open set under an injective holomorphic map is open
decls.statement:
theorem isOpen_image_of_differentiableOn_of_injOn (hΩo : IsOpen Ω)
    (hgd : DifferentiableOn ℂ g Ω) (hgi : InjOn g Ω) : IsOpen (g '' Ω)

decls.name: TauCeti.isOpenMap_restrict_of_differentiableOn_of_injOn
decls.doc:
Restricted to its open domain, an injective holomorphic map is an open map into `ℂ`: an open
subset of the subtype `↥Ω` is `Ω` met with an open set, and the image of that is open by
`TauCeti.isOpen_image_of_differentiableOn_of_injOn`.
decls.statement:
theorem isOpenMap_restrict_of_differentiableOn_of_injOn (hΩo : IsOpen Ω)
    (hgd : DifferentiableOn ℂ g Ω) (hgi : InjOn g Ω) : IsOpenMap (Ω.restrict g)

decls.name: TauCeti.isSimplyConnected_image_of_differentiableOn_of_injOn
decls.doc:
**Injective holomorphic maps preserve simple connectivity.** The image of an open simply
connected set under a holomorphic map injective on it is again simply connected.

The mathematical content beyond openness is Mathlib's
`Topology.IsEmbedding.isSimplyConnected_image`: the restriction of `g` to `Ω` is a topological
embedding, because it is continuous, injective, and open.
decls.title: Injective holomorphic maps preserve simple connectivity
decls.statement:
theorem isSimplyConnected_image_of_differentiableOn_of_injOn (hΩo : IsOpen Ω)
    (hΩc : IsSimplyConnected Ω) (hgd : DifferentiableOn ℂ g Ω) (hgi : InjOn g Ω) :
    IsSimplyConnected (g '' Ω)

decls.name: TauCeti.isOpen_image_of_injOn
decls.doc: Deprecated compatibility alias for the old name, which named only the injectivity hypothesis.
decls.statement: alias isOpen_image_of_injOn

decls.name: TauCeti.isSimplyConnected_image_of_injOn
decls.doc: Deprecated compatibility alias for the old name, which named only the injectivity hypothesis.
decls.statement: alias isSimplyConnected_image_of_injOn

decls.name: TauCeti.DifferentiableOn.invFunOn
decls.doc:
The inverse of a holomorphic injection on an open set is holomorphic on its image.

The inverse is `Function.invFunOn f U`, which chooses the unique preimage lying in `U`. No global
injectivity of `f` outside `U` is required.
decls.statement:
theorem DifferentiableOn.invFunOn {f : ℂ → ℂ} {U : Set ℂ} (hf : DifferentiableOn ℂ f U)
    (hU : IsOpen U) (hinj : InjOn f U) :
    DifferentiableOn ℂ (Function.invFunOn f U) (f '' U)

decls.name: TauCeti.OpenPartialHomeomorph.differentiableOn_symm
decls.doc: The inverse of a holomorphic open partial homeomorphism of `ℂ` is holomorphic on its target.

decls.name: TauCeti.moebius
decls.doc:
The scalar unit-disc Möbius factor `z ↦ (z - c) / (1 - conj c * z)`, as a function of its
centre `c`. This is a private abbreviation for the expression that `Conformal/Moebius.lean` states
its lemmas about; it keeps the Koebe construction, which juggles four of these factors, readable.
decls.statement: def moebius (c z : ℂ) : ℂ

decls.name: TauCeti.moebius_apply_zero
decls.statement: theorem moebius_apply_zero (c : ℂ) : moebius c 0 = -c

decls.name: TauCeti.moebius_self
decls.statement: theorem moebius_self (c : ℂ) : moebius c c = 0

decls.name: TauCeti.sq_mem_ball_of_mem_ball
decls.doc: The disc is closed under squaring.
decls.statement:
theorem sq_mem_ball_of_mem_ball {w : ℂ} (hw : w ∈ ball (0 : ℂ) 1) :
    w ^ 2 ∈ ball (0 : ℂ) 1

decls.name: TauCeti.zero_notMem_image_moebius
decls.doc:
**The Möbius factor at an omitted point never vanishes.** If `a` lies in the disc and `U` is a
subset of the disc avoiding `a`, then `moebius a` omits `0` on `U`.
decls.title: The Möbius factor at an omitted point never vanishes
decls.statement:
theorem zero_notMem_image_moebius {U : Set ℂ} {a : ℂ} (ha1 : ‖a‖ < 1)
    (hUd : U ⊆ ball 0 1) (haU : a ∉ U) : (0 : ℂ) ∉ moebius a '' U

decls.name: TauCeti.mem_ball_of_sq_eq_moebius
decls.doc: **A square root of a Möbius factor lies in the disc**, since its square does.
decls.title: A square root of a Möbius factor lies in the disc
decls.statement:
theorem mem_ball_of_sq_eq_moebius {a z w : ℂ} (ha1 : ‖a‖ < 1) (hz : z ∈ ball (0 : ℂ) 1)
    (hw : w ^ 2 = moebius a z) : w ∈ ball (0 : ℂ) 1

decls.name: TauCeti.not_injOn_moebius_sq_moebius
decls.doc:
**Squaring makes the Möbius-conjugated square map non-injective on the disc**: the two points
that `moebius (-b)` sends to `±½` collide.
decls.title: Squaring makes the Möbius-conjugated square map non-injective on the disc
decls.statement:
theorem not_injOn_moebius_sq_moebius {a b : ℂ} (hb1 : ‖b‖ < 1) :
    ¬ InjOn (fun w : ℂ => moebius (-a) (moebius (-b) w ^ 2)) (ball (0 : ℂ) 1)

decls.name: TauCeti.moebius_sq_moebius_apply_zero
decls.doc:
**The Möbius-conjugated square map fixes the origin** when the two centres are related by
`b ^ 2 = -a`, which is how the square root of the Möbius factor is normalised.
decls.title: The Möbius-conjugated square map fixes the origin
decls.statement:
theorem moebius_sq_moebius_apply_zero {a b : ℂ} (hb2 : b ^ 2 = -a) :
    moebius (-a) (moebius (-b) 0 ^ 2) = 0

decls.name: TauCeti.one_lt_norm_deriv_of_leftInvOn
decls.doc:
**A left inverse with a contracting derivative forces an expanding one.** If `G` inverts `f` on
a neighbourhood of `z₀`, `f` is differentiable at `z₀`, and `G` is differentiable and contracting at
`f z₀`, then `f` expands at `z₀`. This turns the strict Schwarz bound into the Koebe gain.
decls.title: A left inverse with a contracting derivative forces an expanding one
decls.statement:
theorem one_lt_norm_deriv_of_leftInvOn {U : Set ℂ} {f G : ℂ → ℂ} {z₀ : ℂ}
    (hU : U ∈ 𝓝 z₀) (hfd : DifferentiableAt ℂ f z₀) (hGd : DifferentiableAt ℂ G (f z₀))
    (hGf : LeftInvOn G f U) (hG : ‖deriv G (f z₀)‖ < 1) :
    1 < ‖deriv f z₀‖

decls.name: TauCeti.one_lt_norm_deriv_of_moebius_sq_moebius_leftInvOn
decls.doc:
**The Koebe gain.** If `f` is differentiable at the origin, fixes it, and is inverted on a
neighbourhood `U` of the origin by the Möbius-conjugated square map with centres related by
`b ^ 2 = -a`, then `f` expands at the origin. The inverting map is a holomorphic self-map of the
disc fixing `0` that squaring makes non-injective, so the strict Schwarz lemma contracts it.
decls.title: The Koebe gain
decls.statement:
theorem one_lt_norm_deriv_of_moebius_sq_moebius_leftInvOn {U : Set ℂ} {f : ℂ → ℂ} {a b : ℂ}
    (hU : U ∈ 𝓝 (0 : ℂ)) (hb1 : ‖b‖ < 1) (hb2 : b ^ 2 = -a)
    (hfd : DifferentiableAt ℂ f 0) (hf0 : f 0 = 0)
    (hGf : LeftInvOn (fun w : ℂ => moebius (-a) (moebius (-b) w ^ 2)) f U) :
    1 < ‖deriv f 0‖

decls.name: TauCeti.exists_isPointedDiscInjectionOn_one_lt_norm_deriv
decls.doc:
**A proper simply connected subdomain of the disc containing the origin expands.** If `U` is an
open simply connected proper subset of the unit disc with `0 ∈ U`, then there is a holomorphic
injection of `U` into the disc fixing the origin whose derivative there has norm exceeding `1`.

This is the engine of the Riemann mapping theorem: no proper subdomain can be extremal.
decls.title: A proper simply connected subdomain of the disc containing the origin expands
decls.statement:
theorem exists_isPointedDiscInjectionOn_one_lt_norm_deriv {U : Set ℂ} (hUo : IsOpen U)
    (hUc : IsSimplyConnected U) (hU₀ : (0 : ℂ) ∈ U) (hUd : U ⊆ ball 0 1) (hUne : U ≠ ball 0 1) :
    ∃ f : ℂ → ℂ, IsPointedDiscInjectionOn f U 0 ∧ 1 < ‖deriv f 0‖

decls.name: TauCeti.surjOn_ball_of_isMaxOn
decls.doc:
**An extremal pointed disc injection is surjective onto the disc.** If `g` maximizes
`‖deriv · z₀‖` over the holomorphic injections of `Ω` into the disc fixing `z₀`, then `g` omits no
value of the disc.

Otherwise `U := g '' Ω` would be an open simply connected proper subdomain of the disc containing
`0`, and composing `g` with the map that
`TauCeti.exists_isPointedDiscInjectionOn_one_lt_norm_deriv` produces on `U` would beat `g`.
decls.title: An extremal pointed disc injection is surjective onto the disc
decls.statement:
theorem surjOn_ball_of_isMaxOn {Ω : Set ℂ} (hΩo : IsOpen Ω) (hΩc : IsSimplyConnected Ω) {z₀ : ℂ}
    (hz₀ : z₀ ∈ Ω) {g : ℂ → ℂ} (hg : IsPointedDiscInjectionOn g Ω z₀)
    (hmax : ∀ f : ℂ → ℂ, IsPointedDiscInjectionOn f Ω z₀ → ‖deriv f z₀‖ ≤ ‖deriv g z₀‖) :
    SurjOn g Ω (ball 0 1)

decls.name: TauCeti.count_eq_single
decls.doc:
If `z₀` is the only zero of `f` in the open disc, the total zero count collapses to the order
of vanishing at `z₀`.
decls.statement:
lemma count_eq_single {f : ℂ → ℂ} {c z₀ : ℂ} {R : ℝ}
    (hf : AnalyticOnNhd ℂ f (closedBall c R)) (hz₀ : z₀ ∈ ball c R)
    (hone : ∀ z ∈ ball c R, z ≠ z₀ → f z ≠ 0) :
    (∑ᶠ z ∈ ball c R, analyticOrderNatAt f z) = analyticOrderNatAt f z₀

decls.name: TauCeti.localDegree
decls.doc:
**The open-mapping degree**, count form. If `f` is holomorphic on the closed disc `C(z₀, r)`
and `z₀` is the only solution there of `f z = f z₀`, then every `w` close enough to `f z₀` is
attained in the open disc exactly as often as `f z₀` is — that is, `analyticOrderNatAt` of
`f - f z₀` at `z₀` times, counted with multiplicity.
decls.title: The open-mapping degree
decls.statement:
theorem localDegree {f : ℂ → ℂ} {z₀ : ℂ} {r : ℝ} (hr : 0 < r)
    (hf : AnalyticOnNhd ℂ f (closedBall z₀ r))
    (hisol : ∀ z ∈ closedBall z₀ r, z ≠ z₀ → f z ≠ f z₀) :
    ∃ δ > 0, ∀ w : ℂ, ‖w - f z₀‖ < δ →
      (∑ᶠ z ∈ ball z₀ r, analyticOrderNatAt (fun ζ => f ζ - w) z)
        = analyticOrderNatAt (fun ζ => f ζ - f z₀) z₀

decls.name: TauCeti.count_eq_ncard
decls.doc:
When every zero in the disc is simple, the count with multiplicity is the number of *distinct*
zeros.
decls.statement:
lemma count_eq_ncard {A : ℂ → ℂ} {c : ℂ} {R : ℝ} (hA : AnalyticOnNhd ℂ A (closedBall c R))
    (hsimple : ∀ z ∈ ball c R, A z = 0 → analyticOrderNatAt A z = 1) :
    (∑ᶠ z ∈ ball c R, analyticOrderNatAt A z) = {z ∈ ball c R | A z = 0}.ncard

decls.name: TauCeti.zeros_finite
decls.doc:
The fiber counted by `count_eq_ncard` is finite, which is what makes its cardinality
statement mean "exactly this many preimages".
decls.statement:
lemma zeros_finite {A : ℂ → ℂ} {c : ℂ} {R : ℝ} (hA : AnalyticOnNhd ℂ A (closedBall c R))
    (hsimple : ∀ z ∈ ball c R, A z = 0 → analyticOrderNatAt A z = 1) :
    {z ∈ ball c R | A z = 0}.Finite

decls.name: TauCeti.localDegree_card
decls.doc:
**The open-mapping degree**, distinct-and-simple form. Under the additional hypothesis that
`f'` is zero-free on the punctured disc, every `w ≠ f z₀` close enough to `f z₀` has exactly `n`
*distinct* preimages in the open disc, each of them a simple zero of `f - w`.
decls.title: The open-mapping degree
decls.statement:
theorem localDegree_card {f : ℂ → ℂ} {z₀ : ℂ} {r : ℝ} (hr : 0 < r)
    (hf : AnalyticOnNhd ℂ f (closedBall z₀ r))
    (hisol : ∀ z ∈ closedBall z₀ r, z ≠ z₀ → f z ≠ f z₀)
    (hderiv : ∀ z ∈ ball z₀ r, z ≠ z₀ → deriv f z ≠ 0) :
    ∃ δ > 0, ∀ w : ℂ, w ≠ f z₀ → ‖w - f z₀‖ < δ →
      {z ∈ ball z₀ r | f z = w}.Finite ∧
        {z ∈ ball z₀ r | f z = w}.ncard = analyticOrderNatAt (fun ζ => f ζ - f z₀) z₀ ∧
        ∀ z ∈ ball z₀ r, f z = w → analyticOrderNatAt (fun ζ => f ζ - w) z = 1

decls.name: TauCeti.exists_localDegree
decls.doc:
**The open-mapping degree**, textbook form. If `f` is analytic at `z₀` and `z₀` is an isolated
solution of `f z = f z₀` — equivalently, `f` is not constant near `z₀` — then there are radii `r`
and `δ` for which `localDegree` applies.
decls.title: The open-mapping degree
decls.statement:
theorem exists_localDegree {f : ℂ → ℂ} {z₀ : ℂ} (hf : AnalyticAt ℂ f z₀)
    (hisol : ∀ᶠ z in 𝓝[≠] z₀, f z ≠ f z₀) :
    ∃ r > 0, AnalyticOnNhd ℂ f (closedBall z₀ r) ∧
      ∃ δ > 0, ∀ w : ℂ, ‖w - f z₀‖ < δ →
        (∑ᶠ z ∈ ball z₀ r, analyticOrderNatAt (fun ζ => f ζ - w) z)
          = analyticOrderNatAt (fun ζ => f ζ - f z₀) z₀

decls.name: TauCeti.not_injOn_ball_of_deriv_eq_zero
decls.doc:
Non-injectivity on a disc that has already been chosen small enough for the fiber of `f z₀` to
be a singleton and for `f'` to be zero-free off `z₀`. The public statement
`not_injOn_of_deriv_eq_zero` produces such a disc from analyticity alone; this is the step that
uses the degree.
decls.statement:
lemma not_injOn_ball_of_deriv_eq_zero {f : ℂ → ℂ} {z₀ : ℂ} {r : ℝ} (hr : 0 < r)
    (hf : AnalyticOnNhd ℂ f (closedBall z₀ r))
    (hisol : ∀ z ∈ closedBall z₀ r, z ≠ z₀ → f z ≠ f z₀)
    (hderiv : ∀ z ∈ ball z₀ r, z ≠ z₀ → deriv f z ≠ 0)
    (hd₀ : deriv f z₀ = 0) :
    ¬ Set.InjOn f (ball z₀ r)

decls.name: TauCeti.eventually_deriv_ne_zero_of_eventually_ne
decls.doc:
**A non-locally-constant analytic function has eventually nonvanishing derivative.** If `f` is
analytic at `z₀` and takes a value different from `f z₀` at every point of some punctured
neighbourhood, then `deriv f` is nonzero on a punctured neighbourhood of `z₀`.
decls.title: A non-locally-constant analytic function has eventually nonvanishing derivative

decls.name: TauCeti.not_injOn_of_deriv_eq_zero
decls.doc:
**Local injectivity fails at a critical point.** An analytic function whose derivative vanishes
at `z₀` is not injective on *any* neighbourhood of `z₀`.

No non-constancy hypothesis is needed: if `f` is constant near `z₀` the conclusion is immediate,
and otherwise `f - f z₀` vanishes at `z₀` to finite order `n`, which `deriv f z₀ = 0` forces to be
at least `2`, so `localDegree_card` produces two distinct preimages of a nearby value.
decls.title: Local injectivity fails at a critical point
decls.statement:
theorem not_injOn_of_deriv_eq_zero {f : ℂ → ℂ} {z₀ : ℂ}
    (hf : AnalyticAt ℂ f z₀) (hd₀ : deriv f z₀ = 0)
    {V : Set ℂ} (hV : V ∈ 𝓝 z₀) :
    ¬ Set.InjOn f V

decls.name: TauCeti.exists_injOn_nhds_iff_deriv_ne_zero
decls.doc:
**The local injectivity criterion.** An analytic function is injective on some neighbourhood of
`z₀` exactly when its derivative there is nonzero.

The forward direction is `not_injOn_of_deriv_eq_zero`; the reverse is Mathlib's inverse function
theorem, consumed rather than reproved.
decls.title: The local injectivity criterion
decls.statement:
theorem exists_injOn_nhds_iff_deriv_ne_zero {f : ℂ → ℂ} {z₀ : ℂ} (hf : AnalyticAt ℂ f z₀) :
    (∃ V ∈ 𝓝 z₀, Set.InjOn f V) ↔ deriv f z₀ ≠ 0

decls.name: TauCeti.unitDiscMoebius
decls.doc: The standard Moebius factor of the unit disc sending `a` to `0`.
decls.statement: def unitDiscMoebius (a z : Complex.UnitDisc) : Complex.UnitDisc

decls.name: TauCeti.coe_unitDiscMoebius
decls.doc: The defining formula for the unit-disc Moebius factor.
decls.statement:
lemma coe_unitDiscMoebius (a z : Complex.UnitDisc) :
    (unitDiscMoebius a z : ℂ) =
      ((z : ℂ) - (a : ℂ)) / (1 - (starRingEnd ℂ) (a : ℂ) * (z : ℂ))

decls.name: TauCeti.unitDiscMoebius_zero
decls.doc: The unit-disc Moebius factor centered at zero is the identity.
decls.statement:
lemma unitDiscMoebius_zero (z : Complex.UnitDisc) :
    unitDiscMoebius 0 z = z

decls.name: TauCeti.unitDiscMoebius_self
decls.doc: The unit-disc Moebius factor sends its center to zero.
decls.statement:
lemma unitDiscMoebius_self (a : Complex.UnitDisc) :
    unitDiscMoebius a a = 0

decls.name: TauCeti.unitDiscMoebius_apply_zero
decls.doc: The unit-disc Moebius factor sends zero to the negative of its center.
decls.statement:
lemma unitDiscMoebius_apply_zero (a : Complex.UnitDisc) :
    unitDiscMoebius a 0 = -a

decls.name: TauCeti.norm_unitDiscMoebius
decls.doc: The norm of the Moebius factor is the pseudo-hyperbolic expression.
decls.statement:
lemma norm_unitDiscMoebius (a z : Complex.UnitDisc) :
    ‖(unitDiscMoebius a z : ℂ)‖ = pseudoHyperbolicExpr (z : ℂ) (a : ℂ)

decls.name: TauCeti.unitDiscMoebius_eq_zero_iff
decls.doc: A unit-disc Moebius factor vanishes exactly at its center.
decls.statement:
lemma unitDiscMoebius_eq_zero_iff (a z : Complex.UnitDisc) :
    unitDiscMoebius a z = 0 ↔ z = a

decls.name: TauCeti.mapsTo_ball_unitDiscMoebiusFormula_of_norm_lt_one
decls.doc: The scalar unit-disc Moebius formula maps the open unit disc to itself.
decls.statement:
lemma mapsTo_ball_unitDiscMoebiusFormula_of_norm_lt_one {a : ℂ} (ha : ‖a‖ < 1) :
    MapsTo
      (fun z : ℂ => (z - a) / (1 - (starRingEnd ℂ) a * z))
      (ball (0 : ℂ) 1) (ball (0 : ℂ) 1)

decls.name: TauCeti.mapsTo_ball_unitDiscMoebiusFormula
decls.doc: The scalar formula of a unit-disc Moebius factor maps the open unit disc to itself.
decls.statement:
lemma mapsTo_ball_unitDiscMoebiusFormula (a : Complex.UnitDisc) :
    MapsTo
      (fun z : ℂ => (z - (a : ℂ)) / (1 - (starRingEnd ℂ) (a : ℂ) * z))
      (ball (0 : ℂ) 1) (ball (0 : ℂ) 1)

decls.name: TauCeti.differentiableOn_unitDiscMoebiusFormula_of_norm_lt_one
decls.doc: The scalar Moebius formula with center of norm less than one is holomorphic on the unit disc.
decls.statement:
lemma differentiableOn_unitDiscMoebiusFormula_of_norm_lt_one {a : ℂ} (ha : ‖a‖ < 1) :
    DifferentiableOn ℂ
      (fun z : ℂ => (z - a) / (1 - (starRingEnd ℂ) a * z))
      (ball (0 : ℂ) 1)

decls.name: TauCeti.hasDerivAt_unitDiscMoebiusFormula
decls.doc:
The complex derivative of the scalar unit-disc Moebius factor
`z ↦ (z - a) / (1 - conj a * z)` at a point `p` where the denominator is nonzero.  Its value at
`p = 0` (with center `-z`) is `1 - ‖z‖ ^ 2`, and at `p = a` it is `1 / (1 - ‖a‖ ^ 2)`, the two
factors that appear in the infinitesimal Schwarz--Pick estimate.
decls.statement:
lemma hasDerivAt_unitDiscMoebiusFormula (a p : ℂ)
    (hp : 1 - (starRingEnd ℂ) a * p ≠ 0) :
    HasDerivAt (fun z : ℂ => (z - a) / (1 - (starRingEnd ℂ) a * z))
      ((1 - (starRingEnd ℂ) a * a) / (1 - (starRingEnd ℂ) a * p) ^ 2) p

decls.name: TauCeti.differentiableOn_unitDiscMoebiusFormula
decls.doc: The scalar formula of the unit-disc Moebius factor is holomorphic on the unit disc.
decls.statement:
lemma differentiableOn_unitDiscMoebiusFormula (a : Complex.UnitDisc) :
    DifferentiableOn ℂ
      (fun z : ℂ => (z - (a : ℂ)) / (1 - (starRingEnd ℂ) (a : ℂ) * z))
      (ball (0 : ℂ) 1)

decls.name: TauCeti.differentiableOn_and_mapsTo_ball_and_apply_zero_schwarzPickConjugate
decls.doc:
**Schwarz--Pick conjugation scaffold.** For a holomorphic self-map `f` of the open unit
disc and a disc point `a`, conjugating `f` by the Moebius automorphisms centred at `a` (on the
source) and at `f a` (on the target) yields a holomorphic self-map of the disc that fixes the
origin.  This is the common scaffold of the finite and infinitesimal Schwarz--Pick estimates:
applying Schwarz's lemma at `0` to the conjugate `g` unwinds to the contraction estimate for
`f`.
decls.title: Schwarz--Pick conjugation scaffold
decls.statement:
lemma differentiableOn_and_mapsTo_ball_and_apply_zero_schwarzPickConjugate {f : ℂ → ℂ}
    (hf : DifferentiableOn ℂ f (ball (0 : ℂ) 1))
    (hmaps : MapsTo f (ball (0 : ℂ) 1) (ball (0 : ℂ) 1)) {a : ℂ} (ha : ‖a‖ < 1) :
    DifferentiableOn ℂ
        ((fun η => (η - f a) / (1 - (starRingEnd ℂ) (f a) * η)) ∘ f ∘
          fun ξ => (ξ - (-a)) / (1 - (starRingEnd ℂ) (-a) * ξ)) (ball (0 : ℂ) 1) ∧
      MapsTo
        ((fun η => (η - f a) / (1 - (starRingEnd ℂ) (f a) * η)) ∘ f ∘
          fun ξ => (ξ - (-a)) / (1 - (starRingEnd ℂ) (-a) * ξ)) (ball (0 : ℂ) 1) (ball (0 : ℂ) 1) ∧
      ((fun η => (η - f a) / (1 - (starRingEnd ℂ) (f a) * η)) ∘ f ∘
          fun ξ => (ξ - (-a)) / (1 - (starRingEnd ℂ) (-a) * ξ)) 0 = 0

decls.name: TauCeti.unitDiscMoebius_neg_apply_unitDiscMoebius_apply_scalar
decls.statement:
lemma unitDiscMoebius_neg_apply_unitDiscMoebius_apply_scalar {a z : ℂ}
    (hden : 1 - (starRingEnd ℂ) a * z ≠ 0)
    (hnorm : 1 - (starRingEnd ℂ) a * a ≠ 0) :
    (((z - a) / (1 - (starRingEnd ℂ) a * z) + a) /
        (1 + (starRingEnd ℂ) a * ((z - a) / (1 - (starRingEnd ℂ) a * z)))) = z

decls.name: TauCeti.unitDiscMoebius_neg_apply_unitDiscMoebius_apply
decls.statement:
lemma unitDiscMoebius_neg_apply_unitDiscMoebius_apply (a z : Complex.UnitDisc) :
    unitDiscMoebius (-a) (unitDiscMoebius a z) = z

decls.name: TauCeti.unitDiscMoebius_neg_comp_unitDiscMoebius
decls.doc: The inverse of the unit-disc Moebius factor centered at `a` is the factor centered at `-a`.
decls.statement:
lemma unitDiscMoebius_neg_comp_unitDiscMoebius (a : Complex.UnitDisc) :
    unitDiscMoebius (-a) ∘ unitDiscMoebius a = id

decls.name: TauCeti.unitDiscMoebius_comp_unitDiscMoebius_neg
decls.doc: The unit-disc Moebius factors centered at `a` and `-a` compose in the other order too.
decls.statement:
lemma unitDiscMoebius_comp_unitDiscMoebius_neg (a : Complex.UnitDisc) :
    unitDiscMoebius a ∘ unitDiscMoebius (-a) = id

decls.name: TauCeti.leftInvOn_unitDiscMoebiusFormula_of_norm_lt_one
decls.doc:
The scalar unit-disc Moebius formula centered at `-a` is a left inverse for the scalar
formula centered at `a` on the open unit disc.
decls.statement:
lemma leftInvOn_unitDiscMoebiusFormula_of_norm_lt_one {a : ℂ} (ha : ‖a‖ < 1) :
    LeftInvOn
      (fun z : ℂ => (z - (-a)) / (1 - (starRingEnd ℂ) (-a) * z))
      (fun z : ℂ => (z - a) / (1 - (starRingEnd ℂ) a * z))
      (ball (0 : ℂ) 1)

decls.name: TauCeti.unitDiscMoebiusEquiv
decls.doc: The standard Moebius self-equivalence of the unit disc sending `a` to `0`.
decls.statement:
def unitDiscMoebiusEquiv (a : Complex.UnitDisc) :
    Complex.UnitDisc ≃ Complex.UnitDisc

decls.name: TauCeti.unitDiscMoebiusEquiv_apply
decls.doc: The equivalence applies by the unit-disc Moebius formula.
decls.statement:
lemma unitDiscMoebiusEquiv_apply (a z : Complex.UnitDisc) :
    unitDiscMoebiusEquiv a z = unitDiscMoebius a z

decls.name: TauCeti.unitDiscMoebiusEquiv_symm
decls.doc: The inverse equivalence is the Moebius equivalence centered at `-a`.
decls.statement:
lemma unitDiscMoebiusEquiv_symm (a : Complex.UnitDisc) :
    (unitDiscMoebiusEquiv a).symm = unitDiscMoebiusEquiv (-a)

decls.name: TauCeti.continuous_unitDiscMoebius
decls.doc: The unit-disc Moebius factor is continuous as a map of the bundled open disc.
decls.statement:
lemma continuous_unitDiscMoebius (a : Complex.UnitDisc) :
    Continuous (unitDiscMoebius a)

decls.name: TauCeti.unitDiscMoebiusHomeomorph
decls.doc: The standard Moebius self-map of the unit disc, bundled as a homeomorphism.
decls.statement:
def unitDiscMoebiusHomeomorph (a : Complex.UnitDisc) :
    Complex.UnitDisc ≃ₜ Complex.UnitDisc

decls.name: TauCeti.unitDiscMoebiusHomeomorph_apply
decls.doc: The Moebius homeomorphism applies by the existing Moebius factor.
decls.statement:
lemma unitDiscMoebiusHomeomorph_apply (a z : Complex.UnitDisc) :
    unitDiscMoebiusHomeomorph a z = unitDiscMoebius a z

decls.name: TauCeti.unitDiscMoebiusHomeomorph_toEquiv
decls.doc: The underlying equivalence of the Moebius homeomorphism is the existing equivalence.
decls.statement:
lemma unitDiscMoebiusHomeomorph_toEquiv (a : Complex.UnitDisc) :
    (unitDiscMoebiusHomeomorph a).toEquiv = unitDiscMoebiusEquiv a

decls.name: TauCeti.unitDiscMoebiusHomeomorph_symm
decls.doc: The inverse Moebius homeomorphism is the Moebius homeomorphism centered at `-a`.
decls.statement:
lemma unitDiscMoebiusHomeomorph_symm (a : Complex.UnitDisc) :
    (unitDiscMoebiusHomeomorph a).symm = unitDiscMoebiusHomeomorph (-a)

decls.name: TauCeti.coe_unitDiscMoebiusHomeomorph_apply
decls.doc: The scalar formula for the Moebius homeomorphism.
decls.statement:
lemma coe_unitDiscMoebiusHomeomorph_apply (a z : Complex.UnitDisc) :
    (unitDiscMoebiusHomeomorph a z : ℂ) =
      ((z : ℂ) - (a : ℂ)) / (1 - (starRingEnd ℂ) (a : ℂ) * (z : ℂ))

decls.name: TauCeti.montel
decls.doc:
**Montel's selection theorem.** A locally bounded family of holomorphic functions on an open
set `Ω ⊆ ℂ` is normal: every sequence from it has a subsequence converging locally uniformly on
`Ω`, and the limit is holomorphic.

The local boundedness hypothesis cannot be dropped: on any *nonempty* open `Ω`, the holomorphic
family `F n z = n` has no locally uniformly convergent subsequence. (On `Ω = ∅` the conclusion is
vacuous, so nonemptiness is needed for the counterexample.)
decls.title: Montel's selection theorem
decls.statement:
theorem montel (hΩ : IsOpen Ω) (hF : ∀ n, DifferentiableOn ℂ (F n) Ω)
    (hb : IsLocallyBoundedOn F Ω) :
    ∃ (φ : ℕ → ℕ) (g : ℂ → ℂ), StrictMono φ ∧ DifferentiableOn ℂ g Ω ∧
      TendstoLocallyUniformlyOn (fun n => F (φ n)) g atTop Ω

decls.name: TauCeti.IsLocallyBoundedOn
decls.doc:
A family `F : ι → ℂ → ℂ` is **locally bounded** on `s` if it is uniformly bounded — with a
single constant, independent of the index — on every compact subset of `s`.

This is the hypothesis of Montel's theorem, in the form fixed by the conformal-mapping roadmap.
decls.statement: def IsLocallyBoundedOn (F : ι → ℂ → ℂ) (s : Set ℂ) : Prop

decls.name: TauCeti.isLocallyBoundedOn_def
decls.doc: The defining compact-set characterization of local boundedness.
decls.statement:
theorem isLocallyBoundedOn_def :
    IsLocallyBoundedOn F U ↔
      ∀ K ⊆ U, IsCompact K → ∃ C, ∀ i, ∀ z ∈ K, ‖F i z‖ ≤ C

decls.name: TauCeti.IsLocallyBoundedOn.mono
decls.doc: Local boundedness is inherited by subsets.
decls.statement:
theorem IsLocallyBoundedOn.mono {s t : Set ℂ} (hb : IsLocallyBoundedOn F s) (hts : t ⊆ s) :
    IsLocallyBoundedOn F t

decls.name: TauCeti.IsLocallyBoundedOn.exists_forall_norm_le
decls.doc:
A locally bounded family is bounded at each point of the set, uniformly in the index.

Together with `IsLocallyBoundedOn.equicontinuousOn`, this supplies the pointwise bounds used in
an Arzelà--Ascoli exhaustion argument.
decls.statement:
theorem IsLocallyBoundedOn.exists_forall_norm_le {s : Set ℂ} (hb : IsLocallyBoundedOn F s) {z : ℂ}
    (hz : z ∈ s) : ∃ C, ∀ i, ‖F i z‖ ≤ C

decls.name: TauCeti.isLocallyBoundedOn_of_forall_norm_le
decls.doc: A family bounded by a single constant on all of `s` is locally bounded on `s`.
decls.statement:
theorem isLocallyBoundedOn_of_forall_norm_le {s : Set ℂ} {C : ℝ}
    (h : ∀ i, ∀ z ∈ s, ‖F i z‖ ≤ C) : IsLocallyBoundedOn F s

decls.name: TauCeti.exists_pos_closedBall_two_mul_subset
decls.doc:
Every point of an open set admits a radius `r > 0` with `closedBall z (2 * r) ⊆ U`.

The doubled radius is what lets the Cauchy estimate below be applied at every point of
`ball z r`, not just at `z`.
decls.statement:
theorem exists_pos_closedBall_two_mul_subset (hU : IsOpen U) {z : ℂ} (hz : z ∈ U) :
    ∃ r > 0, closedBall z (2 * r) ⊆ U

decls.name: TauCeti.norm_deriv_le_of_forall_mem_closedBall_norm_le
decls.doc:
**Cauchy's estimate on a closed ball.** If `f` is holomorphic on an open set `U` containing
`closedBall c r` and `‖f‖ ≤ M` on that closed ball, then `‖deriv f c‖ ≤ M / r`.

This is Mathlib's `Complex.norm_deriv_le_of_forall_mem_sphere_norm_le` with its `DiffContOnCl`
hypothesis and its bound on the boundary circle both supplied from a sup bound on a closed ball
inside the domain of holomorphy, which is the form the family estimates below consume.
decls.title: Cauchy's estimate on a closed ball

decls.name: TauCeti.norm_deriv_le_of_forall_mem_closedBall_two_mul_norm_le
decls.doc:
**Cauchy's estimate, uniformly on a ball.** If `f` is holomorphic on an open set `U` containing
`closedBall c (2 * r)` and `‖f‖ ≤ M` on that closed ball, then `‖deriv f z‖ ≤ M / r` at *every*
point `z` of `ball c r`, not just at the centre.

Halving the radius is what leaves room to recentre `norm_deriv_le_of_forall_mem_closedBall_norm_le`
at an arbitrary `z ∈ ball c r`: the ball `closedBall z r` is still inside `closedBall c (2 * r)`.
decls.title: Cauchy's estimate, uniformly on a ball
decls.statement:
theorem norm_deriv_le_of_forall_mem_closedBall_two_mul_norm_le (hf : DifferentiableOn ℂ f U)
    {c : ℂ} {r M : ℝ} (hr : 0 < r) (hsub : closedBall c (2 * r) ⊆ U)
    (hM : ∀ w ∈ closedBall c (2 * r), ‖f w‖ ≤ M) {z : ℂ} (hz : z ∈ ball c r) :
    ‖deriv f z‖ ≤ M / r

decls.name: TauCeti.dist_le_of_forall_mem_closedBall_two_mul_norm_le
decls.doc:
**A sup bound makes a holomorphic function Lipschitz on half the ball.** If `f` is holomorphic
on an open `U ⊇ closedBall c (2 * r)` and `‖f‖ ≤ M` there, then `f` moves points of `ball c r` by
at most `M / r` times the distance between them.

The constant `M / r` depends only on the sup bound and the radius, which is what makes this
estimate usable uniformly across a family; see `IsLocallyBoundedOn.equicontinuousOn`.
decls.title: A sup bound makes a holomorphic function Lipschitz on half the ball
decls.statement:
theorem dist_le_of_forall_mem_closedBall_two_mul_norm_le (hU : IsOpen U)
    (hf : DifferentiableOn ℂ f U) {c : ℂ} {r M : ℝ} (hr : 0 < r) (hsub : closedBall c (2 * r) ⊆ U)
    (hM : ∀ w ∈ closedBall c (2 * r), ‖f w‖ ≤ M) {z w : ℂ} (hz : z ∈ ball c r)
    (hw : w ∈ ball c r) : dist (f z) (f w) ≤ M / r * dist z w

decls.name: TauCeti.lipschitzOnWith_of_forall_mem_closedBall_two_mul_norm_le
decls.doc: The `LipschitzOnWith` form of `dist_le_of_forall_mem_closedBall_two_mul_norm_le`.
decls.statement:
theorem lipschitzOnWith_of_forall_mem_closedBall_two_mul_norm_le (hU : IsOpen U)
    (hf : DifferentiableOn ℂ f U) {c : ℂ} {r M : ℝ} (hr : 0 < r)
    (hsub : closedBall c (2 * r) ⊆ U) (hM : ∀ w ∈ closedBall c (2 * r), ‖f w‖ ≤ M) :
    LipschitzOnWith (Real.toNNReal (M / r)) f (ball c r)

decls.name: TauCeti.IsLocallyBoundedOn.equicontinuousOn
decls.doc:
**The equicontinuity half of Montel's theorem.** A locally bounded family of holomorphic
functions on an open set `U ⊆ ℂ` is equicontinuous on `U`.

Around a point `z₀ ∈ U` pick `r > 0` with `closedBall z₀ (2 * r) ⊆ U`; local boundedness supplies
one constant `C` bounding the whole family on that compact ball, and
`dist_le_of_forall_mem_closedBall_two_mul_norm_le` then makes every member of the family
`C / r`-Lipschitz on `ball z₀ r`.  A single Lipschitz constant is a common continuity modulus.
decls.title: The equicontinuity half of Montel's theorem
decls.statement:
theorem IsLocallyBoundedOn.equicontinuousOn (hb : IsLocallyBoundedOn F U) (hU : IsOpen U)
    (hF : ∀ i, DifferentiableOn ℂ (F i) U) : EquicontinuousOn F U

decls.name: TauCeti.IsLocallyBoundedOn.deriv
decls.doc:
**The derivatives of a locally bounded family of holomorphic functions are locally bounded.**

On a compact `K ⊆ U` choose `δ > 0` with `cthickening δ K ⊆ U`; a bound `C` for the family on that
compact thickening bounds each derivative on `K` by `C / δ`, by Cauchy's estimate on
`closedBall z δ` for `z ∈ K`.
decls.title: The derivatives of a locally bounded family of holomorphic functions are locally bounded
decls.statement:
theorem IsLocallyBoundedOn.deriv (hb : IsLocallyBoundedOn F U) (hU : IsOpen U)
    (hF : ∀ i, DifferentiableOn ℂ (F i) U) :
    IsLocallyBoundedOn (fun i => _root_.deriv (F i)) U

decls.name: TauCeti.IsLocallyBoundedOn.equicontinuousOn_deriv
decls.doc:
The derivatives of a locally bounded family of holomorphic functions are equicontinuous.

The result follows by applying the preceding equicontinuity theorem to the locally bounded
derivative family.
decls.statement:
theorem IsLocallyBoundedOn.equicontinuousOn_deriv (hb : IsLocallyBoundedOn F U) (hU : IsOpen U)
    (hF : ∀ i, DifferentiableOn ℂ (F i) U) : EquicontinuousOn (fun i => _root_.deriv (F i)) U

decls.name: TauCeti.PoincareDisc.isometryEquivOfHyperbolicDistEq
decls.doc:
A hyperbolic-distance-preserving equivalence of the unit disc induces an isometric
equivalence of the Poincaré disc.
decls.statement:
def isometryEquivOfHyperbolicDistEq
    (e : Complex.UnitDisc ≃ Complex.UnitDisc)
    (he : ∀ z w : Complex.UnitDisc,
      hyperbolicDist (e z : ℂ) (e w : ℂ) = hyperbolicDist (z : ℂ) (w : ℂ)) :
    PoincareDisc ≃ᵢ PoincareDisc

decls.name: TauCeti.PoincareDisc.isometryEquivOfHyperbolicDistEq_apply
decls.doc:
The underlying function of the transported isometric equivalence is the original unit-disc
equivalence, conjugated by the identity reinterpretation maps.
decls.statement:
lemma isometryEquivOfHyperbolicDistEq_apply (e : Complex.UnitDisc ≃ Complex.UnitDisc)
    (he : ∀ z w : Complex.UnitDisc,
      hyperbolicDist (e z : ℂ) (e w : ℂ) = hyperbolicDist (z : ℂ) (w : ℂ))
    (z : PoincareDisc) :
    isometryEquivOfHyperbolicDistEq e he z =
      Complex.UnitDisc.toPoincare (e (toUnitDisc z))

decls.name: TauCeti.PoincareDisc.isometryEquivOfHyperbolicDistEq_symm
decls.doc:
Taking the inverse commutes with transporting a hyperbolic-distance-preserving equivalence
to the Poincaré disc.
decls.statement:
lemma isometryEquivOfHyperbolicDistEq_symm (e : Complex.UnitDisc ≃ Complex.UnitDisc)
    (he : ∀ z w : Complex.UnitDisc,
      hyperbolicDist (e z : ℂ) (e w : ℂ) = hyperbolicDist (z : ℂ) (w : ℂ)) :
    (isometryEquivOfHyperbolicDistEq e he).symm =
      isometryEquivOfHyperbolicDistEq e.symm
        (fun z w => by
          rw [← he (e.symm z) (e.symm w)]
          simp)

decls.name: TauCeti.PoincareDisc.unitDiscStandardAutomorphismIsometryEquiv
decls.doc:
The standard disc automorphism with rotation `u` and center `a` as an isometric
equivalence of the Poincaré disc.
decls.statement:
def unitDiscStandardAutomorphismIsometryEquiv
    (u : Circle) (a : Complex.UnitDisc) : PoincareDisc ≃ᵢ PoincareDisc

decls.name: TauCeti.PoincareDisc.unitDiscStandardAutomorphismIsometryEquiv_apply
decls.doc: The standard Poincaré isometry acts by the standard unit-disc automorphism.
decls.statement:
lemma unitDiscStandardAutomorphismIsometryEquiv_apply
    (u : Circle) (a : Complex.UnitDisc) (z : PoincareDisc) :
    unitDiscStandardAutomorphismIsometryEquiv u a z =
      Complex.UnitDisc.toPoincare
        (unitDiscStandardAutomorphismEquiv u a (toUnitDisc z))

decls.name: TauCeti.PoincareDisc.unitDiscStandardAutomorphismIsometryEquiv_symm_apply
decls.doc:
The inverse of the standard Poincaré isometry applies the inverse rotation followed by the
inverse Moebius factor.
decls.statement:
lemma unitDiscStandardAutomorphismIsometryEquiv_symm_apply
    (u : Circle) (a : Complex.UnitDisc) (z : PoincareDisc) :
    (unitDiscStandardAutomorphismIsometryEquiv u a).symm z =
      Complex.UnitDisc.toPoincare
        (unitDiscMoebiusEquiv (-a) (u⁻¹ • toUnitDisc z))

decls.name: TauCeti.PoincareDisc.unitDiscMoebiusIsometryEquiv
decls.doc:
The disc Moebius automorphism centred at `a` as an isometric equivalence of the Poincaré
disc.
decls.statement:
def unitDiscMoebiusIsometryEquiv (a : Complex.UnitDisc) :
    PoincareDisc ≃ᵢ PoincareDisc

decls.name: TauCeti.PoincareDisc.unitDiscMoebiusIsometryEquiv_apply
decls.doc: The Moebius Poincaré isometry acts by the usual unit-disc Moebius automorphism.
decls.statement:
lemma unitDiscMoebiusIsometryEquiv_apply (a : Complex.UnitDisc) (z : PoincareDisc) :
    unitDiscMoebiusIsometryEquiv a z =
      Complex.UnitDisc.toPoincare (unitDiscMoebius a (toUnitDisc z))

decls.name: TauCeti.PoincareDisc.unitDiscMoebiusIsometryEquiv_symm
decls.doc: The inverse of the Moebius Poincaré isometry centred at `a` is the one centred at `-a`.
decls.statement:
lemma unitDiscMoebiusIsometryEquiv_symm (a : Complex.UnitDisc) :
    (unitDiscMoebiusIsometryEquiv a).symm = unitDiscMoebiusIsometryEquiv (-a)

decls.name: TauCeti.PoincareDisc.unitDiscStandardAutomorphismIsometryEquiv_one
decls.doc: With unit rotation factor, the standard Poincaré isometry is the Moebius isometry.
decls.statement:
lemma unitDiscStandardAutomorphismIsometryEquiv_one (a : Complex.UnitDisc) :
    unitDiscStandardAutomorphismIsometryEquiv 1 a = unitDiscMoebiusIsometryEquiv a

decls.name: TauCeti.PoincareDisc.unitDiscStandardAutomorphismIsometryEquiv_self
decls.doc: The standard Poincaré isometry sends its center to the origin.
decls.statement:
lemma unitDiscStandardAutomorphismIsometryEquiv_self
    (u : Circle) (a : Complex.UnitDisc) :
    unitDiscStandardAutomorphismIsometryEquiv u a
      (Complex.UnitDisc.toPoincare a) = Complex.UnitDisc.toPoincare 0

decls.name: TauCeti.PoincareDisc
decls.doc:
The complex open unit disc equipped with the hyperbolic (Poincaré) metric.

This is a type synonym for `Complex.UnitDisc`, introduced so that the Poincaré distance can be
registered as a `MetricSpace` instance without clashing with the Euclidean subspace metric that
`Complex.UnitDisc` already carries. Move between the two views with the identity equivalences
`Complex.UnitDisc.toPoincare` and `PoincareDisc.toUnitDisc`.
decls.statement: def PoincareDisc : Type

decls.name: Complex.UnitDisc.toPoincare
decls.doc: Reinterpret a point of the unit disc as a point of the Poincaré disc (the identity map).
decls.statement: def _root_.Complex.UnitDisc.toPoincare : Complex.UnitDisc ≃ PoincareDisc

decls.name: TauCeti.PoincareDisc.toUnitDisc
decls.doc: Reinterpret a point of the Poincaré disc as a point of the unit disc (the identity map).
decls.statement: def toUnitDisc : PoincareDisc ≃ Complex.UnitDisc

decls.name: TauCeti.PoincareDisc.toUnitDisc_toPoincare
decls.statement:
lemma toUnitDisc_toPoincare (z : Complex.UnitDisc) :
    toUnitDisc (Complex.UnitDisc.toPoincare z) = z

decls.name: TauCeti.PoincareDisc.toPoincare_toUnitDisc
decls.statement:
lemma toPoincare_toUnitDisc (z : PoincareDisc) :
    Complex.UnitDisc.toPoincare (toUnitDisc z) = z

decls.name: TauCeti.PoincareDisc.coe_mem_ball
decls.doc: Every point of the Poincaré disc lies in the open unit ball.
decls.statement: lemma coe_mem_ball (z : PoincareDisc) : (toUnitDisc z : ℂ) ∈ ball (0 : ℂ) 1

decls.name: TauCeti.PoincareDisc.instMetricSpace
decls.doc:
The Poincaré (hyperbolic) metric space on the complex open unit disc. Its distance is the
hyperbolic distance `hyperbolicDist` on the underlying disc points.
decls.statement: instance instMetricSpace : MetricSpace PoincareDisc

decls.name: TauCeti.PoincareDisc.dist_eq
decls.doc: The Poincaré distance between two disc points is their hyperbolic distance.
decls.statement:
lemma dist_eq (z w : PoincareDisc) :
    dist z w = hyperbolicDist (toUnitDisc z : ℂ) (toUnitDisc w : ℂ)

decls.name: TauCeti.PoincareDisc.dist_toPoincare_zero_right
decls.doc: The Poincaré distance from a point to the origin has the closed form `artanh ‖z‖`.
decls.statement:
lemma dist_toPoincare_zero_right (z : PoincareDisc) :
    dist z (Complex.UnitDisc.toPoincare 0) = Real.artanh ‖(toUnitDisc z : ℂ)‖

decls.name: TauCeti.PoincareDisc.isometry_of_hyperbolicDist_eq
decls.doc:
A hyperbolic-distance-preserving self-map of the unit disc induces a self-isometry of the
Poincaré disc (transported along the identification `Complex.UnitDisc.toPoincare`).
decls.statement:
theorem isometry_of_hyperbolicDist_eq {g : Complex.UnitDisc → Complex.UnitDisc}
    (hg : ∀ z w : Complex.UnitDisc,
      hyperbolicDist (g z : ℂ) (g w : ℂ) = hyperbolicDist (z : ℂ) (w : ℂ)) :
    Isometry fun z : PoincareDisc => Complex.UnitDisc.toPoincare (g (toUnitDisc z))

decls.name: TauCeti.PoincareDisc.isometry_unitDiscMoebius
decls.doc: The disc Moebius factor `z ↦ (z - a) / (1 - conj a * z)` is a Poincaré self-isometry.
decls.statement:
theorem isometry_unitDiscMoebius (a : Complex.UnitDisc) :
    Isometry fun z : PoincareDisc =>
      Complex.UnitDisc.toPoincare (unitDiscMoebius a (toUnitDisc z))

decls.name: TauCeti.PoincareDisc.isometry_unitDiscStandardAutomorphismEquiv
decls.doc:
Every standard disc automorphism `z ↦ u * (z - a) / (1 - conj a * z)` is a Poincaré
self-isometry.
decls.statement:
theorem isometry_unitDiscStandardAutomorphismEquiv (u : Circle) (a : Complex.UnitDisc) :
    Isometry fun z : PoincareDisc =>
      Complex.UnitDisc.toPoincare (unitDiscStandardAutomorphismEquiv u a (toUnitDisc z))

decls.name: TauCeti.continuousOn_artanh
decls.doc:
`Real.artanh` is continuous on the interval `(-1, 1)` on which it inverts `Real.tanh`.

Mathlib's `Analysis/SpecialFunctions/Artanh.lean` proves the monotonicity and inversion
properties of `Real.artanh` but records no continuity statement. This is a local proof helper
for `continuousOn_hyperbolicDist`, kept private so that a general real-analysis fact is not
exported from a file about the Poincaré metric.
decls.statement: lemma continuousOn_artanh : ContinuousOn Real.artanh (Ioo (-1 : ℝ) 1)

decls.name: TauCeti.norm_sub_le_two_mul_pseudoHyperbolicExpr
decls.doc:
The Euclidean distance between two points of the open unit disc is at most twice their
pseudo-hyperbolic expression: the Moebius denominator `1 - conj w * z` has norm at most `2`.
decls.statement:
lemma norm_sub_le_two_mul_pseudoHyperbolicExpr {z w : ℂ} (hz : ‖z‖ < 1) (hw : ‖w‖ < 1) :
    ‖z - w‖ ≤ 2 * pseudoHyperbolicExpr z w

decls.name: TauCeti.continuousOn_pseudoHyperbolicExpr
decls.doc:
The pseudo-hyperbolic expression is continuous on the product of two copies of the open
unit disc, where its Moebius denominator does not vanish.
decls.statement:
lemma continuousOn_pseudoHyperbolicExpr :
    ContinuousOn (fun p : ℂ × ℂ => pseudoHyperbolicExpr p.1 p.2)
      (ball (0 : ℂ) 1 ×ˢ ball (0 : ℂ) 1)

decls.name: TauCeti.continuousOn_hyperbolicDist
decls.doc:
The hyperbolic distance is jointly continuous on the product of two copies of the open unit
disc, for the Euclidean topology of `ℂ`.
decls.statement:
lemma continuousOn_hyperbolicDist :
    ContinuousOn (fun p : ℂ × ℂ => hyperbolicDist p.1 p.2)
      (ball (0 : ℂ) 1 ×ˢ ball (0 : ℂ) 1)

decls.name: TauCeti.continuous_hyperbolicDist_unitDisc
decls.doc:
For a fixed base point, the hyperbolic distance is a continuous function on
`Complex.UnitDisc` with its Euclidean subspace topology.
decls.statement:
lemma continuous_hyperbolicDist_unitDisc (w : Complex.UnitDisc) :
    Continuous fun z : Complex.UnitDisc => hyperbolicDist (z : ℂ) (w : ℂ)

decls.name: TauCeti.hyperbolicDist_zero_le_iff_norm_le_tanh
decls.doc:
A point of the open unit disc lies within hyperbolic distance `r` of the origin exactly when
its Euclidean norm is at most `Real.tanh r`: the closed hyperbolic ball about the origin is the
closed Euclidean ball of radius `Real.tanh r`.
decls.statement:
lemma hyperbolicDist_zero_le_iff_norm_le_tanh {z : ℂ} (hz : ‖z‖ < 1) (r : ℝ) :
    hyperbolicDist z 0 ≤ r ↔ ‖z‖ ≤ Real.tanh r

decls.name: TauCeti.PoincareDisc.continuous_toUnitDisc
decls.doc:
The identity map from the Poincaré disc to `Complex.UnitDisc` is continuous: two points at
small hyperbolic distance are at small Euclidean distance, since `‖z - w‖ ≤ 2 * p` while the
hyperbolic distance is the increasing reparametrisation `Real.artanh p`.
decls.statement:
theorem continuous_toUnitDisc :
    Continuous (toUnitDisc : PoincareDisc → Complex.UnitDisc)

decls.name: Complex.UnitDisc.continuous_toPoincare
decls.doc:
The identity map from `Complex.UnitDisc` to the Poincaré disc is continuous, because the
hyperbolic distance to a fixed point is a continuous function for the Euclidean topology and
vanishes at that point.
decls.statement:
theorem _root_.Complex.UnitDisc.continuous_toPoincare :
    Continuous (Complex.UnitDisc.toPoincare : Complex.UnitDisc → PoincareDisc)

decls.name: TauCeti.PoincareDisc.toUnitDiscHomeomorph
decls.doc:
**The Poincaré disc carries the Euclidean topology.** The identification of the Poincaré
disc with `Complex.UnitDisc` is a homeomorphism, so the hyperbolic metric may be used
interchangeably with the Euclidean one for topological purposes.

The body is not exposed: the two `simp` lemmas below characterise both directions, so consumers
never depend on how the homeomorphism is assembled.
decls.title: The Poincaré disc carries the Euclidean topology
decls.statement: def toUnitDiscHomeomorph : PoincareDisc ≃ₜ Complex.UnitDisc

decls.name: TauCeti.PoincareDisc.toUnitDiscHomeomorph_apply
decls.doc: The homeomorphism acts as the identification `PoincareDisc.toUnitDisc`.
decls.statement:
lemma toUnitDiscHomeomorph_apply (z : PoincareDisc) :
    toUnitDiscHomeomorph z = toUnitDisc z

decls.name: TauCeti.PoincareDisc.toUnitDiscHomeomorph_symm_apply
decls.doc: The inverse homeomorphism acts as the identification `Complex.UnitDisc.toPoincare`.
decls.statement:
lemma toUnitDiscHomeomorph_symm_apply (z : Complex.UnitDisc) :
    toUnitDiscHomeomorph.symm z = Complex.UnitDisc.toPoincare z

decls.name: TauCeti.PoincareDisc.instProperSpace
decls.doc:
**The Poincaré disc is a proper metric space.** A closed hyperbolic ball of radius `r` about
`x` consists of points at hyperbolic distance at most `r + hyperbolicDist x 0` from the origin,
hence of Euclidean norm at most `Real.tanh (r + hyperbolicDist x 0) < 1`; it is therefore a
closed subset of a compact subset of the open disc.

Concretely, every bounded hyperbolic ball is contained in a Euclidean subdisc of radius strictly
less than one. Together with the instances Mathlib derives from `ProperSpace`, this makes the
Poincaré disc a complete and locally compact metric space.
decls.title: The Poincaré disc is a proper metric space
decls.statement: instance PoincareDisc.instProperSpace : ProperSpace PoincareDisc

decls.name: TauCeti.pseudoHyperbolicExpr
decls.doc:
The pseudo-hyperbolic expression on `ℂ`, written as a total real-valued function.

On the open unit disc this is the pseudo-hyperbolic expression.  Outside the disc the same
formula is still meaningful as a total expression in Lean, with division by zero evaluating
to zero as usual.
decls.statement: def pseudoHyperbolicExpr (z w : ℂ) : ℝ

decls.name: TauCeti.pseudoHyperbolicExpr_def
decls.doc: The defining formula for the pseudo-hyperbolic expression.
decls.statement:
lemma pseudoHyperbolicExpr_def (z w : ℂ) :
    pseudoHyperbolicExpr z w = ‖(z - w) / (1 - (starRingEnd ℂ) w * z)‖

decls.name: TauCeti.pseudoHyperbolicExpr_nonneg
decls.statement: lemma pseudoHyperbolicExpr_nonneg (z w : ℂ) : 0 ≤ pseudoHyperbolicExpr z w

decls.name: TauCeti.pseudoHyperbolicExpr_self
decls.doc: The pseudo-hyperbolic expression from a point to itself is zero.
decls.statement: lemma pseudoHyperbolicExpr_self (z : ℂ) : pseudoHyperbolicExpr z z = 0

decls.name: TauCeti.norm_one_sub_conj_mul_comm
decls.statement:
lemma norm_one_sub_conj_mul_comm (z w : ℂ) :
    ‖1 - (starRingEnd ℂ) w * z‖ = ‖1 - (starRingEnd ℂ) z * w‖

decls.name: TauCeti.pseudoHyperbolicExpr_comm
decls.doc: The pseudo-hyperbolic expression is symmetric in its two arguments.
decls.statement:
lemma pseudoHyperbolicExpr_comm (z w : ℂ) :
    pseudoHyperbolicExpr z w = pseudoHyperbolicExpr w z

decls.name: TauCeti.pseudoHyperbolicExpr_eq_zero_of_eq
decls.doc: If the two points are equal, their pseudo-hyperbolic expression is zero.
decls.statement:
lemma pseudoHyperbolicExpr_eq_zero_of_eq {z w : ℂ} (h : z = w) :
    pseudoHyperbolicExpr z w = 0

decls.name: TauCeti.pseudoHyperbolicExpr_zero_right
decls.doc: The pseudo-hyperbolic expression with right endpoint zero is the norm.
decls.statement: lemma pseudoHyperbolicExpr_zero_right (z : ℂ) : pseudoHyperbolicExpr z 0 = ‖z‖

decls.name: TauCeti.pseudoHyperbolicExpr_zero_left
decls.doc: The pseudo-hyperbolic expression with left endpoint zero is the norm.
decls.statement: lemma pseudoHyperbolicExpr_zero_left (w : ℂ) : pseudoHyperbolicExpr 0 w = ‖w‖

decls.name: TauCeti.pseudoHyperbolicExpr_const_mul
decls.doc:
**Rotation invariance.** Multiplying both arguments by a unit-modulus constant leaves the
pseudo-hyperbolic expression unchanged.  This is a purely algebraic identity valid for all
`z`, `w`; it is the rotation half of the disc-automorphism group.
decls.title: Rotation invariance
decls.statement:
lemma pseudoHyperbolicExpr_const_mul {c : ℂ} (hc : ‖c‖ = 1) (z w : ℂ) :
    pseudoHyperbolicExpr (c * z) (c * w) = pseudoHyperbolicExpr z w

decls.name: TauCeti.pseudoHyperbolicExpr_eq_zero_iff_of_den_ne_zero
decls.doc: If the denominator is nonzero, zero pseudo-hyperbolic expression characterizes equality.

decls.name: TauCeti.one_sub_conj_mul_ne_zero_of_norm_lt_one
decls.doc: On the open unit disc, the denominator in the pseudo-hyperbolic expression is nonzero.

decls.name: TauCeti.one_sub_conj_mul_ne_zero_of_mem_ball
decls.doc:
For points in the open unit ball, the denominator in the pseudo-hyperbolic expression is
nonzero.

decls.name: TauCeti.one_sub_conj_mul_ne_zero_unitDisc
decls.doc:
For bundled unit-disc points, the denominator in the pseudo-hyperbolic expression is
nonzero.
decls.statement:
lemma one_sub_conj_mul_ne_zero_unitDisc (z w : Complex.UnitDisc) :
    1 - (starRingEnd ℂ) (w : ℂ) * (z : ℂ) ≠ 0

decls.name: TauCeti.norm_one_sub_conj_mul_self_of_norm_le_one
decls.doc:
For a point of norm at most one, the denominator of the Moebius factor evaluated at the
factor's own center has norm `1 - ‖w‖ ^ 2`.
decls.statement:
lemma norm_one_sub_conj_mul_self_of_norm_le_one {w : ℂ} (hw : ‖w‖ ≤ 1) :
    ‖(1 : ℂ) - (starRingEnd ℂ) w * w‖ = 1 - ‖w‖ ^ 2

decls.name: TauCeti.pseudoHyperbolicExpr_eq_zero_iff_of_norm_lt_one
decls.doc: On the open unit disc, zero pseudo-hyperbolic expression characterizes equality.

decls.name: TauCeti.pseudoHyperbolicExpr_eq_zero_iff_of_mem_ball
decls.doc: For points in the open unit ball, zero pseudo-hyperbolic expression characterizes equality.

decls.name: TauCeti.pseudoHyperbolicExpr_eq_zero_iff_unitDisc
