decls.doc: For bundled unit-disc points, zero pseudo-hyperbolic expression characterizes equality.
decls.statement:
lemma pseudoHyperbolicExpr_eq_zero_iff_unitDisc (z w : Complex.UnitDisc) :
    pseudoHyperbolicExpr (z : ℂ) (w : ℂ) = 0 ↔ z = w

decls.name: TauCeti.normSq_one_sub_conj_mul_sub_normSq_sub
decls.statement:
lemma normSq_one_sub_conj_mul_sub_normSq_sub (z w : ℂ) :
    Complex.normSq (1 - (starRingEnd ℂ) w * z) - Complex.normSq (z - w) =
      (1 - Complex.normSq z) * (1 - Complex.normSq w)

decls.name: TauCeti.norm_sq_one_sub_conj_mul_sub_norm_sq_sub
decls.doc:
**Poincaré defect identity (norm form).** The difference of the squared norms of the Moebius
denominator and numerator factors is the product of the two hyperbolic defects:
`‖1 - conj w * z‖ ^ 2 - ‖z - w‖ ^ 2 = (1 - ‖z‖ ^ 2) * (1 - ‖w‖ ^ 2)`.
decls.title: Poincaré defect identity (norm form)
decls.statement:
lemma norm_sq_one_sub_conj_mul_sub_norm_sq_sub (z w : ℂ) :
    ‖(1 : ℂ) - (starRingEnd ℂ) w * z‖ ^ 2 - ‖z - w‖ ^ 2 = (1 - ‖z‖ ^ 2) * (1 - ‖w‖ ^ 2)

decls.name: TauCeti.norm_sub_lt_norm_one_sub_conj_mul_of_norm_lt_one
decls.doc:
For two points of norm less than one, the numerator norm is smaller than the denominator
norm in the pseudo-hyperbolic expression.

decls.name: TauCeti.pseudoHyperbolicExpr_lt_one_of_norm_lt_one
decls.doc:
The pseudo-hyperbolic expression of two points of norm less than one is strictly less
than one.

decls.name: TauCeti.pseudoHyperbolicExpr_lt_one_of_mem_ball
decls.doc:
The pseudo-hyperbolic expression of two points in the open unit ball is strictly less
than one.

decls.name: TauCeti.pseudoHyperbolicExpr_lt_one_unitDisc
decls.doc:
The pseudo-hyperbolic expression of two bundled unit-disc points is strictly less
than one.
decls.statement:
lemma pseudoHyperbolicExpr_lt_one_unitDisc (z w : Complex.UnitDisc) :
    pseudoHyperbolicExpr (z : ℂ) (w : ℂ) < 1

decls.name: TauCeti.chartedSchwarzReflection
decls.doc:
The Schwarz-reflection extension transported through source and target biholomorphic charts.

The source chart `e` straightens the source arc, and the target chart `d` straightens the target
arc. Thus the middle function in real-axis coordinates is `w ↦ d (f (e.symm w))`. The definition
is total, while its characteristic properties only concern the sources and targets of the two
partial homeomorphisms.
decls.statement: def chartedSchwarzReflection (z : ℂ) : ℂ

decls.name: TauCeti.chartedSchwarzReflection_def
decls.doc: The defining formula for Schwarz reflection transported through biholomorphic charts.
decls.statement:
theorem chartedSchwarzReflection_def (z : ℂ) :
    chartedSchwarzReflection e d f z =
      d.symm (schwarzReflection (fun w => d (f (e.symm w))) (e z))

decls.name: TauCeti.mapsTo_symm_inter_im
decls.doc: The inverse chart preserves a cut expressed in chart coordinates.
decls.statement:
theorem mapsTo_symm_inter_im {P : ℝ → Prop} :
    MapsTo e.symm (e.target ∩ {w : ℂ | P w.im})
      (e.source ∩ {z : ℂ | P (e z).im})

decls.name: TauCeti.mapsTo_schwarzReflection
decls.doc:
If both coordinate domains are conjugation-invariant, the reflected coordinate values stay
in the target coordinate domain.
decls.statement:
theorem mapsTo_schwarzReflection
    (he_symm : MapsTo (starRingEnd ℂ) e.target e.target)
    (hd_symm : MapsTo (starRingEnd ℂ) d.target d.target)
    (hf : MapsTo f (e.source ∩ {z : ℂ | 0 ≤ (e z).im}) d.source) :
    MapsTo (schwarzReflection (fun w => d (f (e.symm w)))) e.target d.target

decls.name: TauCeti.mapsTo_chartedSchwarzReflection
decls.doc: Charted Schwarz reflection maps the source chart domain into the target chart domain.
decls.statement:
theorem mapsTo_chartedSchwarzReflection
    (he_symm : MapsTo (starRingEnd ℂ) e.target e.target)
    (hd_symm : MapsTo (starRingEnd ℂ) d.target d.target)
    (hf : MapsTo f (e.source ∩ {z : ℂ | 0 ≤ (e z).im}) d.source) :
    MapsTo (chartedSchwarzReflection e d f) e.source d.source

decls.name: TauCeti.chartedSchwarzReflection_of_coord_im_nonneg
decls.doc:
On the closed positive side of the source arc, charted Schwarz reflection agrees with the
original function.
decls.statement:
theorem chartedSchwarzReflection_of_coord_im_nonneg
    (hf : MapsTo f (e.source ∩ {z : ℂ | 0 ≤ (e z).im}) d.source)
    {z : ℂ} (hz : z ∈ e.source) (him : 0 ≤ (e z).im) :
    chartedSchwarzReflection e d f z = f z

decls.name: TauCeti.chartedSchwarzReflection_of_coord_im_neg
decls.doc:
On the negative side of the source arc, charted Schwarz reflection is obtained by reflecting
the argument and value in the two coordinate charts.
decls.statement:
theorem chartedSchwarzReflection_of_coord_im_neg {z : ℂ} (him : (e z).im < 0) :
    chartedSchwarzReflection e d f z =
      d.symm ((starRingEnd ℂ) (d (f (e.symm ((starRingEnd ℂ) (e z))))))

decls.name: TauCeti.continuousOn_in_coordinates
decls.doc: In source coordinates, the original branch is continuous on the closed upper half-plane.
decls.statement:
theorem continuousOn_in_coordinates
    (he : DifferentiableOn ℂ e e.source) (hd : DifferentiableOn ℂ d d.source)
    (hf_maps : MapsTo f (e.source ∩ {z : ℂ | 0 ≤ (e z).im}) d.source)
    (hf : ContinuousOn f (e.source ∩ {z : ℂ | 0 ≤ (e z).im})) :
    ContinuousOn (fun w => d (f (e.symm w)))
      (e.target ∩ {w : ℂ | 0 ≤ w.im})

decls.name: TauCeti.differentiableOn_in_coordinates
decls.doc: In source coordinates, the original branch is holomorphic on the open upper half-plane.
decls.statement:
theorem differentiableOn_in_coordinates
    (he : DifferentiableOn ℂ e e.source) (hd : DifferentiableOn ℂ d d.source)
    (hf_maps : MapsTo f (e.source ∩ {z : ℂ | 0 ≤ (e z).im}) d.source)
    (hf : DifferentiableOn ℂ f (e.source ∩ {z : ℂ | 0 < (e z).im})) :
    DifferentiableOn ℂ (fun w => d (f (e.symm w)))
      (e.target ∩ {w : ℂ | 0 < w.im})

decls.name: TauCeti.apply_im_eq_zero_in_coordinates
decls.doc:
The real-boundary condition for the original branch becomes the usual real-axis condition in
the two coordinate charts.
decls.statement:
theorem apply_im_eq_zero_in_coordinates
    (hf : ∀ z ∈ e.source, (e z).im = 0 → (d (f z)).im = 0) :
    ∀ w ∈ e.target, w.im = 0 → (d (f (e.symm w))).im = 0

decls.name: TauCeti.differentiableOn_chartedSchwarzReflection_of_symmetric
decls.doc:
**Schwarz reflection across an analytic arc.** Let `e` and `d` be holomorphic open partial
homeomorphisms whose coordinate domains are invariant under conjugation. If `f` is continuous on
the closed positive side of the source arc, holomorphic on its open positive side, maps that side
into the source of `d`, and maps the arc into the target arc, then its charted Schwarz-reflection
extension is holomorphic throughout the source of `e`.

The source and target arcs are the inverse images of the real axis under `e` and `d`. Holomorphy
of the inverse charts is a consequence of holomorphy and injectivity of their forward maps, so it
is not imposed as an additional hypothesis.
decls.title: Schwarz reflection across an analytic arc
decls.statement:
theorem differentiableOn_chartedSchwarzReflection_of_symmetric
    (he : DifferentiableOn ℂ e e.source) (hd : DifferentiableOn ℂ d d.source)
    (he_symm : MapsTo (starRingEnd ℂ) e.target e.target)
    (hd_symm : MapsTo (starRingEnd ℂ) d.target d.target)
    (hf_maps : MapsTo f (e.source ∩ {z : ℂ | 0 ≤ (e z).im}) d.source)
    (hf_cont : ContinuousOn f (e.source ∩ {z : ℂ | 0 ≤ (e z).im}))
    (hf_diff : DifferentiableOn ℂ f (e.source ∩ {z : ℂ | 0 < (e z).im}))
    (hf_real : ∀ z ∈ e.source, (e z).im = 0 → (d (f z)).im = 0) :
    DifferentiableOn ℂ (chartedSchwarzReflection e d f) e.source

decls.name: TauCeti.chartedSchwarzReflection_sourceReflection
decls.doc:
Charted Schwarz reflection intertwines the source and target reflections induced by the two
biholomorphic charts.
decls.statement:
theorem chartedSchwarzReflection_sourceReflection
    (he_symm : MapsTo (starRingEnd ℂ) e.target e.target)
    (hd_symm : MapsTo (starRingEnd ℂ) d.target d.target)
    (hf_maps : MapsTo f (e.source ∩ {z : ℂ | 0 ≤ (e z).im}) d.source)
    (hf_real : ∀ z ∈ e.source, (e z).im = 0 → (d (f z)).im = 0)
    {z : ℂ} (hz : z ∈ e.source) :
    chartedSchwarzReflection e d f
        (e.symm ((starRingEnd ℂ) (e z))) =
      d.symm ((starRingEnd ℂ) (d (chartedSchwarzReflection e d f z)))

decls.name: TauCeti.exists_differentiableOn_eqOn_chartedReflection_of_symmetric
decls.doc:
**Packaged Schwarz reflection across an analytic arc.** Under the hypotheses of
`differentiableOn_chartedSchwarzReflection_of_symmetric`, there is a holomorphic extension that
agrees with the original function on the closed positive side and intertwines the source and
target reflections induced by the charts. The witness is `chartedSchwarzReflection e d f`.
decls.title: Packaged Schwarz reflection across an analytic arc
decls.statement:
theorem exists_differentiableOn_eqOn_chartedReflection_of_symmetric
    (he : DifferentiableOn ℂ e e.source) (hd : DifferentiableOn ℂ d d.source)
    (he_symm : MapsTo (starRingEnd ℂ) e.target e.target)
    (hd_symm : MapsTo (starRingEnd ℂ) d.target d.target)
    (hf_maps : MapsTo f (e.source ∩ {z : ℂ | 0 ≤ (e z).im}) d.source)
    (hf_cont : ContinuousOn f (e.source ∩ {z : ℂ | 0 ≤ (e z).im}))
    (hf_diff : DifferentiableOn ℂ f (e.source ∩ {z : ℂ | 0 < (e z).im}))
    (hf_real : ∀ z ∈ e.source, (e z).im = 0 → (d (f z)).im = 0) :
    ∃ F : ℂ → ℂ,
      DifferentiableOn ℂ F e.source ∧
      EqOn F f (e.source ∩ {z : ℂ | 0 ≤ (e z).im}) ∧
      ∀ z ∈ e.source,
        F (e.symm ((starRingEnd ℂ) (e z))) =
          d.symm ((starRingEnd ℂ) (d (F z)))

decls.name: TauCeti.schwarzReflection
decls.doc:
The explicit real-axis Schwarz-reflection extension of a function from the closed upper
half-plane to the plane.

On `0 ≤ z.im` this is `f z`; on the lower half-plane it is `conj (f (conj z))`.
decls.statement: def schwarzReflection (f : ℂ → ℂ) (z : ℂ) : ℂ

decls.name: TauCeti.schwarzReflection_def
decls.doc: The Schwarz-reflection extension is the explicit upper/lower half-plane witness.

decls.name: TauCeti.schwarzReflection_of_im_nonneg
decls.doc: On the closed upper half-plane, Schwarz reflection agrees with the original function.
decls.statement:
lemma schwarzReflection_of_im_nonneg {z : ℂ} (hz : 0 ≤ z.im) :
    schwarzReflection f z = f z

decls.name: TauCeti.schwarzReflection_of_im_neg
decls.doc: On the lower half-plane, Schwarz reflection is `z ↦ conj (f (conj z))`.
decls.statement:
lemma schwarzReflection_of_im_neg {z : ℂ} (hz : z.im < 0) :
    schwarzReflection f z = (starRingEnd ℂ) (f ((starRingEnd ℂ) z))

decls.name: TauCeti.schwarzReflection_of_im_zero
decls.doc: On the real axis, Schwarz reflection agrees with the original function.
decls.statement:
lemma schwarzReflection_of_im_zero {z : ℂ} (hz : z.im = 0) :
    schwarzReflection f z = f z

decls.name: TauCeti.eqOn_schwarzReflection_of_subset_im_nonneg
decls.doc:
On any subset of the closed upper half-plane, Schwarz reflection agrees with the original
function.
decls.statement:
lemma eqOn_schwarzReflection_of_subset_im_nonneg
    (hS : S ⊆ {z : ℂ | 0 ≤ z.im}) :
    Set.EqOn (schwarzReflection f) f S

decls.name: TauCeti.eqOn_schwarzReflection_of_subset_im_neg
decls.doc:
On any subset of the lower half-plane, Schwarz reflection agrees with the reflected
branch.
decls.statement:
lemma eqOn_schwarzReflection_of_subset_im_neg
    (hS : S ⊆ {z : ℂ | z.im < 0}) :
    Set.EqOn (schwarzReflection f) (fun z => (starRingEnd ℂ) (f ((starRingEnd ℂ) z))) S

decls.name: TauCeti.schwarzReflection_conj_of_im_pos
decls.doc: Conjugating a point in the upper half-plane evaluates the reflected lower branch.
decls.statement:
lemma schwarzReflection_conj_of_im_pos {z : ℂ} (hz : 0 < z.im) :
    schwarzReflection f ((starRingEnd ℂ) z) = (starRingEnd ℂ) (f z)

decls.name: TauCeti.conj_schwarzReflection_of_im_neg
decls.doc: Conjugating the lower-half-plane value recovers the original function at `conj z`.
decls.statement:
lemma conj_schwarzReflection_of_im_neg {z : ℂ} (hz : z.im < 0) :
    (starRingEnd ℂ) (schwarzReflection f z) = f ((starRingEnd ℂ) z)

decls.name: TauCeti.apply_eq_conj_apply_conj_of_im_zero_of_apply_im_zero
decls.doc:
At a real-axis point where `f` has a real value, `f` commutes with conjugation:
`f z = conj (f (conj z))`.
decls.statement:
lemma apply_eq_conj_apply_conj_of_im_zero_of_apply_im_zero
    {z : ℂ} (hz : z.im = 0) (hreal : (f z).im = 0) :
    f z = (starRingEnd ℂ) (f ((starRingEnd ℂ) z))

decls.name: TauCeti.schwarzReflection_conj
decls.doc:
The Schwarz-reflection extension is conjugation-symmetric when the original function has real
value at the real-axis point under consideration.
decls.statement:
lemma schwarzReflection_conj
    (z : ℂ) (hreal : z.im = 0 → ((f z).im = 0)) :
    schwarzReflection f ((starRingEnd ℂ) z) =
      (starRingEnd ℂ) (schwarzReflection f z)

decls.name: TauCeti.schwarzReflection_conj_of_real_on_axis
decls.doc:
On a domain where the original function is real-valued on the real axis, the Schwarz-reflection
extension is conjugation-symmetric at each point of the domain.
decls.statement:
lemma schwarzReflection_conj_of_real_on_axis {Ω : Set ℂ}
    (hreal : ∀ z ∈ Ω, z.im = 0 → (f z).im = 0) {z : ℂ} (hz : z ∈ Ω) :
    schwarzReflection f ((starRingEnd ℂ) z) =
      (starRingEnd ℂ) (schwarzReflection f z)

decls.name: TauCeti.eqOn_schwarzReflection_conj_of_real_on_axis
decls.doc:
On a domain where the original function is real-valued on the real axis, the Schwarz-reflection
extension is conjugation-symmetric on that domain.
decls.statement:
lemma eqOn_schwarzReflection_conj_of_real_on_axis {Ω : Set ℂ}
    (hreal : ∀ z ∈ Ω, z.im = 0 → (f z).im = 0) :
    Set.EqOn (fun z => schwarzReflection f ((starRingEnd ℂ) z))
      (fun z => (starRingEnd ℂ) (schwarzReflection f z)) Ω

decls.name: TauCeti.image_conj_inter_im_pos_of_symmetric
decls.doc:
For a domain closed under conjugation, conjugation carries the upper half-plane part of the
domain to its lower half-plane part.

decls.name: TauCeti.image_conj_inter_im_neg_of_symmetric
decls.doc:
For a domain closed under conjugation, conjugation carries the lower half-plane part of the
domain to its upper half-plane part.

decls.name: TauCeti.continuousOn_conj_conj
decls.doc: Conjugating both source and target preserves continuity on reflected sets.
decls.statement:
lemma continuousOn_conj_conj (hf : ContinuousOn f S) :
    ContinuousOn (fun z => (starRingEnd ℂ) (f ((starRingEnd ℂ) z)))
      ((starRingEnd ℂ) '' S)

decls.name: TauCeti.continuousOn_conj_conj_iff
decls.doc: Conjugating both source and target preserves continuity on reflected sets, in both directions.
decls.statement:
lemma continuousOn_conj_conj_iff :
    ContinuousOn (fun z => (starRingEnd ℂ) (f ((starRingEnd ℂ) z)))
        ((starRingEnd ℂ) '' S) ↔
      ContinuousOn f S

decls.name: TauCeti.continuousOn_schwarzReflection_of_subset_im_nonneg
decls.doc:
On any subset of the closed upper half-plane, the explicit Schwarz-reflection extension is
continuous whenever the original function is.
decls.statement:
lemma continuousOn_schwarzReflection_of_subset_im_nonneg
    (hS : S ⊆ {z : ℂ | 0 ≤ z.im}) (hf : ContinuousOn f S) :
    ContinuousOn (schwarzReflection f) S

decls.name: TauCeti.continuousOn_conj_conj_inter_im_neg_of_symmetric
decls.doc:
If a domain is closed under conjugation and `f` is continuous on its upper half-plane
part, then the reflected branch `z ↦ conj (f (conj z))` is continuous on the lower
half-plane part.
decls.statement:
lemma continuousOn_conj_conj_inter_im_neg_of_symmetric {Ω : Set ℂ}
    (hΩ : Set.MapsTo (starRingEnd ℂ) Ω Ω)
    (hf : ContinuousOn f (Ω ∩ {z | 0 < z.im})) :
    ContinuousOn (fun z => (starRingEnd ℂ) (f ((starRingEnd ℂ) z)))
      (Ω ∩ {z | z.im < 0})

decls.name: TauCeti.continuousOn_schwarzReflection_inter_im_neg_of_symmetric
decls.doc:
On the lower half-plane part of a domain closed under conjugation, the explicit Schwarz
reflection extension is continuous whenever the original function is continuous on the
upper half-plane part.
decls.statement:
lemma continuousOn_schwarzReflection_inter_im_neg_of_symmetric {Ω : Set ℂ}
    (hΩ : Set.MapsTo (starRingEnd ℂ) Ω Ω)
    (hf : ContinuousOn f (Ω ∩ {z | 0 < z.im})) :
    ContinuousOn (schwarzReflection f) (Ω ∩ {z | z.im < 0})

decls.name: TauCeti.image_conj_inter_im_nonneg_of_symmetric
decls.doc:
For a domain closed under conjugation, conjugation carries the closed upper half-plane part of
the domain to its closed lower half-plane part.

decls.name: TauCeti.continuousOn_schwarzReflection_of_symmetric
decls.doc:
If a domain `Ω` is closed under conjugation, `f` is continuous on its closed upper half-plane
part, and `f` takes real values at the real-axis points of `Ω`, then the explicit
Schwarz-reflection extension is continuous on `Ω`.
decls.statement:
lemma continuousOn_schwarzReflection_of_symmetric {Ω : Set ℂ}
    (hΩ : Set.MapsTo (starRingEnd ℂ) Ω Ω)
    (hf : ContinuousOn f (Ω ∩ {z : ℂ | 0 ≤ z.im}))
    (hreal : ∀ z ∈ Ω, z.im = 0 → (f z).im = 0) :
    ContinuousOn (schwarzReflection f) Ω

decls.name: TauCeti.continuous_schwarzReflection
decls.doc:
If `f` is continuous on the closed upper half-plane and takes real values on the real axis,
then its explicit Schwarz-reflection extension is continuous on the plane.
decls.statement:
lemma continuous_schwarzReflection
    (hf : ContinuousOn f {z : ℂ | 0 ≤ z.im})
    (hreal : ∀ z : ℂ, z.im = 0 → (f z).im = 0) :
    Continuous (schwarzReflection f)

decls.name: TauCeti.starRingEnd_eq_starL
decls.statement:
lemma starRingEnd_eq_starL (z : ℂ) :
    (starRingEnd ℂ) z = (starL ℂ : ℂ ≃L⋆[ℂ] ℂ) z

decls.name: TauCeti.HasFDerivWithinAt.comp_semilinear_preimage
decls.statement:
lemma HasFDerivWithinAt.comp_semilinear_preimage
    {𝕜 V V' W W' : Type*} [NontriviallyNormedField 𝕜] {σ σ' : RingHom 𝕜 𝕜}
    [NormedAddCommGroup V] [NormedSpace 𝕜 V]
    [NormedAddCommGroup V'] [NormedSpace 𝕜 V']
    [NormedAddCommGroup W] [NormedSpace 𝕜 W]
    [NormedAddCommGroup W'] [NormedSpace 𝕜 W']
    [RingHomIsometric σ] [RingHomInvPair σ σ']
    (L : W →SL[σ] W') (R : V' →SL[σ'] V)
    {g : V → W} {g' : V →L[𝕜] W} {T : Set V} {x : V'}
    (hg : HasFDerivWithinAt g g' T (R x)) :
    HasFDerivWithinAt (L ∘ g ∘ R) (L.comp (g'.comp R)) (R ⁻¹' T) x

decls.name: TauCeti.differentiableOn_conj_conj
decls.doc:
Antiholomorphic-composition prerequisite for Schwarz reflection.

If `f` is holomorphic on `S`, then `z ↦ conj (f (conj z))` is holomorphic on the reflected
set `conj '' S`.
decls.statement:
lemma differentiableOn_conj_conj (hf : DifferentiableOn ℂ f S) :
    DifferentiableOn ℂ (fun z => (starRingEnd ℂ) (f ((starRingEnd ℂ) z)))
      ((starRingEnd ℂ) '' S)

decls.name: TauCeti.differentiableOn_schwarzReflection_of_subset_im_nonneg
decls.doc:
On any subset of the closed upper half-plane, the explicit Schwarz-reflection extension is
holomorphic whenever the original function is.
decls.statement:
lemma differentiableOn_schwarzReflection_of_subset_im_nonneg
    (hS : S ⊆ {z : ℂ | 0 ≤ z.im}) (hf : DifferentiableOn ℂ f S) :
    DifferentiableOn ℂ (schwarzReflection f) S

decls.name: TauCeti.differentiableOn_conj_conj_iff
decls.doc: Conjugating both source and target preserves holomorphicity on domains, in both directions.
decls.statement:
lemma differentiableOn_conj_conj_iff :
    DifferentiableOn ℂ (fun z => (starRingEnd ℂ) (f ((starRingEnd ℂ) z)))
        ((starRingEnd ℂ) '' S) ↔
      DifferentiableOn ℂ f S

decls.name: TauCeti.differentiableOn_conj_conj_inter_im_neg_of_symmetric
decls.doc:
If a domain is closed under conjugation and `f` is holomorphic on its upper half-plane
part, then the reflected branch `z ↦ conj (f (conj z))` is holomorphic on the lower
half-plane part.
decls.statement:
lemma differentiableOn_conj_conj_inter_im_neg_of_symmetric {Ω : Set ℂ}
    (hΩ : Set.MapsTo (starRingEnd ℂ) Ω Ω)
    (hf : DifferentiableOn ℂ f (Ω ∩ {z | 0 < z.im})) :
    DifferentiableOn ℂ (fun z => (starRingEnd ℂ) (f ((starRingEnd ℂ) z)))
      (Ω ∩ {z | z.im < 0})

decls.name: TauCeti.differentiableOn_schwarzReflection_inter_im_neg_of_symmetric
decls.doc:
On the lower half-plane part of a domain closed under conjugation, the explicit Schwarz
reflection extension is holomorphic whenever the original function is holomorphic on the
upper half-plane part.
decls.statement:
lemma differentiableOn_schwarzReflection_inter_im_neg_of_symmetric {Ω : Set ℂ}
    (hΩ : Set.MapsTo (starRingEnd ℂ) Ω Ω)
    (hf : DifferentiableOn ℂ f (Ω ∩ {z | 0 < z.im})) :
    DifferentiableOn ℂ (schwarzReflection f) (Ω ∩ {z | z.im < 0})

decls.name: TauCeti.differentiableOn_schwarzReflection_inter_im_ne_zero_of_symmetric
decls.doc:
Away from the real axis, the Schwarz-reflection extension is holomorphic on a
conjugation-symmetric domain whenever the original function is holomorphic on its upper
half-plane part.
decls.statement:
lemma differentiableOn_schwarzReflection_inter_im_ne_zero_of_symmetric {Ω : Set ℂ}
    (hΩ : Set.MapsTo (starRingEnd ℂ) Ω Ω)
    (hf : DifferentiableOn ℂ f (Ω ∩ {z | 0 < z.im})) :
    DifferentiableOn ℂ (schwarzReflection f) (Ω ∩ {z | z.im ≠ 0})

decls.name: TauCeti.hasDerivAt_schwarzReflection_of_im_pos
decls.doc:
At a point in the open upper half-plane, the Schwarz-reflection extension has the same
derivative as the original function.
decls.statement:
lemma hasDerivAt_schwarzReflection_of_im_pos {z f' : ℂ} (hz : 0 < z.im)
    (hf : HasDerivAt f f' z) :
    HasDerivAt (schwarzReflection f) f' z

decls.name: TauCeti.hasDerivAt_schwarzReflection_of_im_neg
decls.doc:
At a point in the open lower half-plane, the derivative of the Schwarz-reflection
extension is the conjugate of the derivative of `f` at the conjugate point.
decls.statement:
lemma hasDerivAt_schwarzReflection_of_im_neg {z f' : ℂ} (hz : z.im < 0)
    (hf : HasDerivAt f f' ((starRingEnd ℂ) z)) :
    HasDerivAt (schwarzReflection f) ((starRingEnd ℂ) f') z

decls.name: TauCeti.deriv_schwarzReflection_of_im_pos
decls.doc:
On the open upper half-plane, the derivative of the Schwarz-reflection extension agrees
with the derivative of the original function.
decls.statement:
lemma deriv_schwarzReflection_of_im_pos {z : ℂ} (hz : 0 < z.im) :
    deriv (schwarzReflection f) z = deriv f z

decls.name: TauCeti.deriv_schwarzReflection_of_im_neg
decls.doc:
On the open lower half-plane, the derivative of the Schwarz-reflection extension is the
conjugate of the derivative of the original function at the conjugate point.
decls.statement:
lemma deriv_schwarzReflection_of_im_neg {z : ℂ} (hz : z.im < 0) :
    deriv (schwarzReflection f) z =
      (starRingEnd ℂ) (deriv f ((starRingEnd ℂ) z))

decls.name: TauCeti.inversion_eq_conj_reciprocal
decls.doc:
Euclidean inversion in `ℂ` is given by the standard conjugate-reciprocal formula for
reflection in a circle.
decls.statement:
theorem inversion_eq_conj_reciprocal (c : ℂ) (r : ℝ) (z : ℂ) :
    inversion c r z = c + (r : ℂ) ^ 2 / (starRingEnd ℂ) (z - c)

decls.name: TauCeti.circleReflectionHomeomorph
decls.doc: Euclidean inversion restricts to a self-homeomorphism of the punctured complex plane.
decls.statement:
def circleReflectionHomeomorph (c : ℂ) (r : ℝ) (hr : r ≠ 0) :
    ({c}ᶜ : Set ℂ) ≃ₜ ({c}ᶜ : Set ℂ)

decls.name: TauCeti.coe_circleReflectionHomeomorph_apply
decls.doc: The punctured-plane circle-reflection homeomorphism acts by Euclidean inversion.
decls.statement:
theorem coe_circleReflectionHomeomorph_apply (c : ℂ) (r : ℝ) (hr : r ≠ 0)
    (z : ({c}ᶜ : Set ℂ)) :
    (circleReflectionHomeomorph c r hr z : ℂ) = inversion c r z

decls.name: TauCeti.circleReflectionHomeomorph_symm
decls.doc: The punctured-plane circle-reflection homeomorphism is its own inverse.
decls.statement:
theorem circleReflectionHomeomorph_symm (c : ℂ) (r : ℝ) (hr : r ≠ 0) :
    (circleReflectionHomeomorph c r hr).symm = circleReflectionHomeomorph c r hr

decls.name: TauCeti.dist_inversion_center_lt_iff
decls.doc:
Inversion in a positive-radius circle sends a point into its open ball exactly when the
original point is in the exterior of its closed ball.
decls.statement:
theorem dist_inversion_center_lt_iff {c z : ℂ} {r : ℝ} (hr : 0 < r) (hz : z ≠ c) :
    dist (inversion c r z) c < r ↔ r < dist z c

decls.name: TauCeti.lt_dist_inversion_center_iff
decls.doc:
Inversion in a positive-radius circle sends a point outside its closed ball exactly when the
original point is in its open ball.
decls.statement:
theorem lt_dist_inversion_center_iff {c z : ℂ} {r : ℝ} (hr : 0 < r) (hz : z ≠ c) :
    r < dist (inversion c r z) c ↔ dist z c < r

decls.name: TauCeti.circleReflectionConjugate
decls.doc:
Conjugate a map by reflections in a source circle and a target circle.

The source circle has centre `c` and radius `r`, and the target circle has centre `d` and radius
`s`. Thus the value at `z` is `R_{d,s} (f (R_{c,r} z))`, where `R` denotes Euclidean inversion.
The definition is total; analytic results exclude the centres where the inversion formula has a
pole.
decls.statement:
def circleReflectionConjugate (c : ℂ) (r : ℝ) (d : ℂ) (s : ℝ)
    (f : ℂ → ℂ) (z : ℂ) : ℂ

decls.name: TauCeti.circleReflectionConjugate_apply
decls.doc: The circle-reflection conjugate is the composite of the two inversions and the map.
decls.statement:
lemma circleReflectionConjugate_apply (c : ℂ) (r : ℝ) (d : ℂ) (s : ℝ)
    (f : ℂ → ℂ) (z : ℂ) :
    circleReflectionConjugate c r d s f z = inversion d s (f (inversion c r z))

decls.name: TauCeti.circleReflectionConjugate_zero_source_radius
decls.doc: With zero source radius, the circle-reflection conjugate is constant.
decls.statement:
theorem circleReflectionConjugate_zero_source_radius (c d : ℂ) (s : ℝ)
    (f : ℂ → ℂ) :
    circleReflectionConjugate c 0 d s f = fun _ => inversion d s (f c)

decls.name: TauCeti.circleReflectionConjugate_zero_target_radius
decls.doc: With zero target radius, the circle-reflection conjugate is constant.
decls.statement:
theorem circleReflectionConjugate_zero_target_radius (c : ℂ) (r : ℝ) (d : ℂ)
    (f : ℂ → ℂ) : circleReflectionConjugate c r d 0 f = fun _ => d

decls.name: TauCeti.circleReflectionConjugate_eqOn_sphere
decls.doc:
The circle-reflection conjugate agrees with the original map on the source circle when the
map sends the source circle into the target circle.
decls.statement:
theorem circleReflectionConjugate_eqOn_sphere (c : ℂ) (r : ℝ) (d : ℂ) (s : ℝ)
    (f : ℂ → ℂ) (hmap : MapsTo f (Metric.sphere c r) (Metric.sphere d s)) :
    EqOn (circleReflectionConjugate c r d s f) f (Metric.sphere c r)

decls.name: TauCeti.circleReflectionConjugate_circleReflectionConjugate
decls.doc: Applying the same circle-reflection conjugation twice recovers the original map.
decls.statement:
theorem circleReflectionConjugate_circleReflectionConjugate (c : ℂ) {r : ℝ} (d : ℂ)
    {s : ℝ} (hr : r ≠ 0) (hs : s ≠ 0) (f : ℂ → ℂ) :
    circleReflectionConjugate c r d s (circleReflectionConjugate c r d s f) = f

decls.name: TauCeti.circleReflectionCoord
decls.doc:
The holomorphic coordinate whose complex conjugate is reflection in the circle centred at
`c` with radius `r`.
decls.statement: def circleReflectionCoord (c : ℂ) (r : ℝ) (z : ℂ) : ℂ

decls.name: TauCeti.conj_circleReflectionCoord
decls.statement:
lemma conj_circleReflectionCoord (c : ℂ) (r : ℝ) (z : ℂ) :
    (starRingEnd ℂ) (circleReflectionCoord c r z) = inversion c r z

decls.name: TauCeti.differentiableOn_circleReflectionCoord
decls.statement:
lemma differentiableOn_circleReflectionCoord {c : ℂ} {r : ℝ} {S : Set ℂ}
    (hc : c ∉ S) : DifferentiableOn ℂ (circleReflectionCoord c r) S

decls.name: TauCeti.differentiableOn_circleReflectionConjugate
decls.doc:
Conjugating a holomorphic map by source and target circle reflections is holomorphic away
from the inversion centres.

When both radii are nonzero, the set `S` is mapped into the original holomorphy domain `Ω` by
source reflection, and the two nonincidence hypotheses remove the poles of the source and target
inversions. These hypotheses are unnecessary when either radius is zero, since the conjugate is
then constant.
decls.statement:
theorem differentiableOn_circleReflectionConjugate {c : ℂ} {r : ℝ} {d : ℂ} {s : ℝ}
    {f : ℂ → ℂ} {Ω S : Set ℂ}
    (hf : r ≠ 0 ∧ s ≠ 0 → DifferentiableOn ℂ f Ω)
    (hmap : r ≠ 0 ∧ s ≠ 0 → MapsTo (inversion c r) S Ω)
    (hc : r ≠ 0 ∧ s ≠ 0 → c ∉ S)
    (hd : r ≠ 0 ∧ s ≠ 0 → ∀ z ∈ S, f (inversion c r z) ≠ d) :
    DifferentiableOn ℂ (circleReflectionConjugate c r d s f) S

decls.name: TauCeti.circleSchwarzReflection
decls.doc:
The explicit extension used for Schwarz reflection across a circle. Inside the closed source
disc it is `f`; outside it is `f` conjugated by reflection in the source and target circles.
decls.statement:
def circleSchwarzReflection (c : ℂ) (r : ℝ) (d : ℂ) (s : ℝ)
    (f : ℂ → ℂ) (z : ℂ) : ℂ

decls.name: TauCeti.circleSchwarzReflection_def
decls.doc: The circle Schwarz-reflection extension is the explicit inside/outside piecewise function.
decls.statement:
theorem circleSchwarzReflection_def (c : ℂ) (r : ℝ) (d : ℂ) (s : ℝ) (f : ℂ → ℂ) :
    circleSchwarzReflection c r d s f =
      (by
        classical
        exact (closedBall c r).piecewise f (circleReflectionConjugate c r d s f))

decls.name: TauCeti.circleSchwarzReflection_of_mem_closedBall
decls.doc: On the closed source disc, the circle-reflection extension agrees with the original map.
decls.statement:
lemma circleSchwarzReflection_of_mem_closedBall {c : ℂ} {r : ℝ} (d : ℂ) (s : ℝ)
    (f : ℂ → ℂ) {z : ℂ} (hz : z ∈ closedBall c r) :
    circleSchwarzReflection c r d s f z = f z

decls.name: TauCeti.circleSchwarzReflection_of_notMem_closedBall
decls.doc: Outside the closed source disc, the extension is the circle-reflection conjugate.
decls.statement:
lemma circleSchwarzReflection_of_notMem_closedBall (c : ℂ) (r : ℝ) (d : ℂ) (s : ℝ)
    (f : ℂ → ℂ) {z : ℂ} (hz : z ∉ closedBall c r) :
    circleSchwarzReflection c r d s f z =
      circleReflectionConjugate c r d s f z

decls.name: TauCeti.continuousOn_circleSchwarzReflection_of_symmetric
decls.doc:
If `Ω` is mapped into itself by inversion in the source circle, the circle-reflection
extension is continuous when the original map is continuous on the closed inside part, maps the
source-circle boundary to the target circle, and avoids the target centre in the punctured open
inside part.
decls.statement:
theorem continuousOn_circleSchwarzReflection_of_symmetric {Ω : Set ℂ} {c d : ℂ} {r s : ℝ}
    {f : ℂ → ℂ} (hr : 0 < r) (hs : 0 < s)
    (hsymm : MapsTo (inversion c r) Ω Ω)
    (hcont : ContinuousOn f (Ω ∩ closedBall c r))
    (hboundary : MapsTo f (Ω ∩ sphere c r) (sphere d s))
    (havoid : ∀ z ∈ Ω ∩ ball c r, z ≠ c → f z ≠ d) :
    ContinuousOn (circleSchwarzReflection c r d s f) Ω

decls.name: TauCeti.differentiableOn_circleSchwarzReflection_of_symmetric
decls.doc:
**Schwarz reflection principle across a circle.** Let `Ω` be an open set invariant under
reflection in the source circle. If `f` is continuous on the closed inside part, holomorphic on
the open inside part, sends the source-circle boundary into the
target circle, and avoids the target centre in the punctured interior, then its explicit
circle-reflection extension is holomorphic throughout `Ω`.

The target-centre avoidance is exactly the non-pole condition for reflection in the target
circle.
decls.title: Schwarz reflection principle across a circle
decls.statement:
theorem differentiableOn_circleSchwarzReflection_of_symmetric
    {Ω : Set ℂ} {c d : ℂ} {r s : ℝ} {f : ℂ → ℂ}
    (hr : 0 < r) (hs : 0 < s) (hΩ : IsOpen Ω)
    (hsymm : MapsTo (inversion c r) Ω Ω)
    (hcont : ContinuousOn f (Ω ∩ closedBall c r))
    (hholo : DifferentiableOn ℂ f (Ω ∩ ball c r))
    (hboundary : MapsTo f (Ω ∩ sphere c r) (sphere d s))
    (havoid : ∀ z ∈ Ω ∩ ball c r, z ≠ c → f z ≠ d) :
    DifferentiableOn ℂ (circleSchwarzReflection c r d s f) Ω

decls.name: TauCeti.lineSchwarzReflection
decls.doc:
The explicit Schwarz-reflection extension across affine source and target lines.

The source line has base point `p` and direction `a`, while the target line has base point `q`
and direction `b`. In affine coordinates, this is exactly the real-axis extension:
`q + b * schwarzReflection (w ↦ (f (p + a * w) - q) / b) ((z - p) / a)`.
The definition is total. Agreement with the original branch and the reflection symmetry assume
`a ≠ 0` and `b ≠ 0`; holomorphy itself only needs `a ≠ 0`, since `b = 0` makes the function
constant.
decls.statement: def lineSchwarzReflection (p a q b : ℂ) (f : ℂ → ℂ) (z : ℂ) : ℂ

decls.name: TauCeti.lineSchwarzReflection_def
decls.doc: The affine-line Schwarz-reflection extension in source and target coordinates.
decls.statement:
theorem lineSchwarzReflection_def (p a q b : ℂ) (f : ℂ → ℂ) (z : ℂ) :
    lineSchwarzReflection p a q b f z =
      q + b * schwarzReflection (fun w => (f (p + a * w) - q) / b) ((z - p) / a)

decls.name: TauCeti.lineSchwarzReflection_of_coord_im_nonneg
decls.doc:
On the closed positive side of the source line, affine-line Schwarz reflection agrees with
the original function.
decls.statement:
lemma lineSchwarzReflection_of_coord_im_nonneg {p a q b z : ℂ} (f : ℂ → ℂ)
    (ha : a ≠ 0) (hb : b ≠ 0) (hz : 0 ≤ ((z - p) / a).im) :
    lineSchwarzReflection p a q b f z = f z

decls.name: TauCeti.lineSchwarzReflection_of_coord_im_neg
decls.doc:
On the negative side of the source line, affine-line Schwarz reflection is obtained by
reflecting the argument in the source line and the value in the target line.
decls.statement:
lemma lineSchwarzReflection_of_coord_im_neg {p a q b z : ℂ} (f : ℂ → ℂ)
    (hz : ((z - p) / a).im < 0) :
    lineSchwarzReflection p a q b f z =
      q + b * (starRingEnd ℂ)
        ((f (p + a * (starRingEnd ℂ) ((z - p) / a)) - q) / b)

decls.name: TauCeti.affineChart_left_inv
decls.statement:
lemma affineChart_left_inv {p a : ℂ} (ha : a ≠ 0) (z : ℂ) :
    p + a * ((z - p) / a) = z

decls.name: TauCeti.affineChart_right_inv
decls.statement:
lemma affineChart_right_inv {p a : ℂ} (ha : a ≠ 0) (w : ℂ) :
    (p + a * w - p) / a = w

decls.name: TauCeti.affineChart_reflection_coord
decls.statement:
lemma affineChart_reflection_coord {p a z : ℂ} (ha : a ≠ 0) :
    (p + a * (starRingEnd ℂ) ((z - p) / a) - p) / a =
      (starRingEnd ℂ) ((z - p) / a)

decls.name: TauCeti.mapsTo_affineChart_inter_im
decls.doc:
**The affine chart carries a pulled-back imaginary-coordinate cut to the original one.** For
any predicate `P` on the imaginary part, the chart `w ↦ p + a·w` maps `φ⁻¹(Ω)` cut by `P ∘ im`
into `Ω` cut by `P` on the *rotated* imaginary part `((z - p)/a).im`. Taking `P` to be `0 ≤ ·`
and `0 < ·` gives the closed and open half-planes, which is how the continuity and holomorphy
transports below use it; the statement itself constrains `P` no further.
decls.title: The affine chart carries a pulled-back imaginary-coordinate cut to the original one
decls.statement:
lemma mapsTo_affineChart_inter_im {p a : ℂ} (ha : a ≠ 0) {Ω : Set ℂ} {P : ℝ → Prop} :
    MapsTo (fun w : ℂ => p + a * w)
      ((fun w : ℂ => p + a * w) ⁻¹' Ω ∩ {w : ℂ | P w.im})
      (Ω ∩ {z : ℂ | P ((z - p) / a).im})

decls.name: TauCeti.mapsTo_conj_affineChart_preimage
decls.doc:
**The chart pullback of a line-symmetric domain is conjugation-symmetric.** If `Ω` is carried
into itself by reflection in the line `p + a·ℝ`, then its pullback along `w ↦ p + a·w` is carried
into itself by ordinary complex conjugation — which is what the half-plane reflection theorem asks
for.
decls.title: The chart pullback of a line-symmetric domain is conjugation-symmetric
decls.statement:
lemma mapsTo_conj_affineChart_preimage {p a : ℂ} (ha : a ≠ 0) {Ω : Set ℂ}
    (hΩ : MapsTo (fun z => p + a * (starRingEnd ℂ) ((z - p) / a)) Ω Ω) :
    MapsTo (starRingEnd ℂ) ((fun w : ℂ => p + a * w) ⁻¹' Ω)
      ((fun w : ℂ => p + a * w) ⁻¹' Ω)

decls.name: TauCeti.continuousOn_targetChart_comp_affineChart
decls.doc:
**Continuity transports along the chart.** Reading `f` in the source coordinate `w ↦ p + a·w`
and normalizing its values by `(· - q) / b` turns continuity on the closed positive side of the line
into continuity on the closed upper half-plane.
decls.title: Continuity transports along the chart
decls.statement:
lemma continuousOn_targetChart_comp_affineChart {p a q b : ℂ} (ha : a ≠ 0) {Ω : Set ℂ}
    {f : ℂ → ℂ} (hcont : ContinuousOn f (Ω ∩ {z : ℂ | 0 ≤ ((z - p) / a).im})) :
    ContinuousOn (fun w : ℂ => (f (p + a * w) - q) / b)
      ((fun w : ℂ => p + a * w) ⁻¹' Ω ∩ {w : ℂ | 0 ≤ w.im})

decls.name: TauCeti.differentiableOn_targetChart_comp_affineChart
decls.doc:
**Holomorphy transports along the chart**, the open-side companion of
`continuousOn_targetChart_comp_affineChart`.
decls.title: Holomorphy transports along the chart
decls.statement:
lemma differentiableOn_targetChart_comp_affineChart {p a q b : ℂ} (ha : a ≠ 0) {Ω : Set ℂ}
    {f : ℂ → ℂ} (hholo : DifferentiableOn ℂ f (Ω ∩ {z : ℂ | 0 < ((z - p) / a).im})) :
    DifferentiableOn ℂ (fun w : ℂ => (f (p + a * w) - q) / b)
      ((fun w : ℂ => p + a * w) ⁻¹' Ω ∩ {w : ℂ | 0 < w.im})

decls.name: TauCeti.im_targetChart_comp_affineChart_eq_zero
decls.doc:
**The boundary condition transports to the real axis.** In the source coordinate the line
`p + a·ℝ` is the real axis, so the hypothesis that the normalized values `(f z - q) / b` are real on
the line becomes the hypothesis that the transported function is real on the reals. For `b ≠ 0` that
says `f` maps the source line into the target line `q + b·ℝ`; at `b = 0` the normalization is
identically `0`, so both conditions are vacuous.
decls.title: The boundary condition transports to the real axis
decls.statement:
lemma im_targetChart_comp_affineChart_eq_zero {p a q b : ℂ} (ha : a ≠ 0) {Ω : Set ℂ}
    {f : ℂ → ℂ} (hline : ∀ z ∈ Ω, ((z - p) / a).im = 0 → ((f z - q) / b).im = 0) :
    ∀ w ∈ (fun w : ℂ => p + a * w) ⁻¹' Ω, w.im = 0 →
      ((fun w : ℂ => (f (p + a * w) - q) / b) w).im = 0

decls.name: TauCeti.differentiableOn_lineSchwarzReflection_of_symmetric
decls.doc:
**Schwarz reflection principle across an affine line, holomorphy form.** Let the source line
be `p + a * ℝ`, with `a ≠ 0`. Suppose an open domain `Ω` is invariant under reflection in this
line. If `f` is continuous on the closed positive side, holomorphic on the open positive side,
and its boundary values have real target coordinate, then `lineSchwarzReflection p a q b f` is
holomorphic throughout `Ω`.

The side and boundary conditions are expressed in the affine coordinates `(z - p) / a` and
`(f z - q) / b`. The target direction `b` need not be nonzero for holomorphy: when `b = 0`, the
conclusion is the constant function with value `q`. The packaged reflection theorem below assumes
`b ≠ 0` to obtain branch agreement and target-line symmetry.
decls.title: Schwarz reflection principle across an affine line, holomorphy form
decls.statement:
theorem differentiableOn_lineSchwarzReflection_of_symmetric
    {Ω : Set ℂ} {p a q b : ℂ} {f : ℂ → ℂ}
    (ha : a ≠ 0) (hΩopen : IsOpen Ω)
    (hΩ : MapsTo (fun z => p + a * (starRingEnd ℂ) ((z - p) / a)) Ω Ω)
    (hcont : ContinuousOn f (Ω ∩ {z : ℂ | 0 ≤ ((z - p) / a).im}))
    (hholo : DifferentiableOn ℂ f (Ω ∩ {z : ℂ | 0 < ((z - p) / a).im}))
    (hline : ∀ z ∈ Ω, ((z - p) / a).im = 0 → ((f z - q) / b).im = 0) :
    DifferentiableOn ℂ (lineSchwarzReflection p a q b f) Ω

decls.name: TauCeti.lineSchwarzReflection_sourceReflection
decls.doc:
Affine-line Schwarz reflection intertwines reflection in the source line with reflection in
the target line. The boundary hypothesis says precisely that the original function takes the
source line into the target line.
decls.statement:
theorem lineSchwarzReflection_sourceReflection
    {Ω : Set ℂ} {p a q b : ℂ} {f : ℂ → ℂ}
    (ha : a ≠ 0) (hb : b ≠ 0)
    (hline : ∀ z ∈ Ω, ((z - p) / a).im = 0 → ((f z - q) / b).im = 0)
    {z : ℂ} (hz : z ∈ Ω) :
    lineSchwarzReflection p a q b f
        (p + a * (starRingEnd ℂ) ((z - p) / a)) =
      q + b * (starRingEnd ℂ)
        ((lineSchwarzReflection p a q b f z - q) / b)

decls.name: TauCeti.exists_differentiableOn_eqOn_lineReflection_of_symmetric
decls.doc:
**Schwarz reflection principle across affine source and target lines, packaged form.**
Under the hypotheses of `differentiableOn_lineSchwarzReflection_of_symmetric`, with both line
directions nonzero, there is a holomorphic extension which agrees with `f` on the closed positive
side and intertwines reflection in the source and target lines. The witness is the explicit
function `lineSchwarzReflection p a q b f`.
decls.title: Schwarz reflection principle across affine source and target lines, packaged form
decls.statement:
theorem exists_differentiableOn_eqOn_lineReflection_of_symmetric
    {Ω : Set ℂ} {p a q b : ℂ} {f : ℂ → ℂ}
    (ha : a ≠ 0) (hb : b ≠ 0) (hΩopen : IsOpen Ω)
    (hΩ : MapsTo (fun z => p + a * (starRingEnd ℂ) ((z - p) / a)) Ω Ω)
    (hcont : ContinuousOn f (Ω ∩ {z : ℂ | 0 ≤ ((z - p) / a).im}))
    (hholo : DifferentiableOn ℂ f (Ω ∩ {z : ℂ | 0 < ((z - p) / a).im}))
    (hline : ∀ z ∈ Ω, ((z - p) / a).im = 0 → ((f z - q) / b).im = 0) :
    ∃ F : ℂ → ℂ,
      DifferentiableOn ℂ F Ω ∧
      EqOn F f (Ω ∩ {z : ℂ | 0 ≤ ((z - p) / a).im}) ∧
      ∀ z ∈ Ω,
        F (p + a * (starRingEnd ℂ) ((z - p) / a)) =
          q + b * (starRingEnd ℂ) ((F z - q) / b)

decls.name: TauCeti.differentiableOn_schwarzReflection_of_symmetric
decls.doc:
**Schwarz reflection principle (real axis).** On a conjugation-symmetric open set `Ω`, if `f`
is continuous on the closed upper part, holomorphic on the open upper part, and real-valued on
the real axis of `Ω`, then the explicit reflection extension `schwarzReflection f` is holomorphic
on all of `Ω` — in particular across the real axis.

The gluing calculus (continuity everywhere, holomorphy off the axis, the conjugation symmetry) is
`Reflection/Basic.lean`; the missing holomorphy at the axis is Painlevé removability,
`differentiableOn_of_continuousOn_of_differentiableOn_im_ne_zero`.
decls.title: Schwarz reflection principle (real axis)
decls.statement:
theorem differentiableOn_schwarzReflection_of_symmetric {Ω : Set ℂ}
    (hΩopen : IsOpen Ω) (hΩ : Set.MapsTo (starRingEnd ℂ) Ω Ω)
    (hcont : ContinuousOn f (Ω ∩ {z : ℂ | 0 ≤ z.im}))
    (hholo : DifferentiableOn ℂ f (Ω ∩ {z : ℂ | 0 < z.im}))
    (hreal : ∀ z ∈ Ω, z.im = 0 → (f z).im = 0) :
    DifferentiableOn ℂ (schwarzReflection f) Ω

decls.name: TauCeti.exists_differentiableOn_eqOn_conj_of_symmetric
decls.doc:
**Schwarz reflection principle**, packaged existential form (the L4 milestone of
`ConformalMapping/Suggested.lean`). On a conjugation-symmetric open `Ω`, a function continuous on
the closed upper part, holomorphic on the open upper part, and real on the real axis extends to a
function holomorphic on all of `Ω` that agrees with `f` on the closed upper part and satisfies the
reflection symmetry `F (conj z) = conj (F z)`. The explicit witness is `schwarzReflection f`.
decls.title: Schwarz reflection principle
decls.statement:
theorem exists_differentiableOn_eqOn_conj_of_symmetric {Ω : Set ℂ}
    (hΩopen : IsOpen Ω) (hΩ : Set.MapsTo (starRingEnd ℂ) Ω Ω)
    (hcont : ContinuousOn f (Ω ∩ {z : ℂ | 0 ≤ z.im}))
    (hholo : DifferentiableOn ℂ f (Ω ∩ {z : ℂ | 0 < z.im}))
    (hreal : ∀ z ∈ Ω, z.im = 0 → (f z).im = 0) :
    ∃ F : ℂ → ℂ, DifferentiableOn ℂ F Ω ∧ Set.EqOn F f (Ω ∩ {z : ℂ | 0 ≤ z.im}) ∧
      ∀ z ∈ Ω, F ((starRingEnd ℂ) z) = (starRingEnd ℂ) (F z)

decls.name: TauCeti.differentiableOn_of_continuousOn_of_differentiableOn_diff_of_subset_coord_im_eq_zero
decls.doc:
**Painlevé removability across a charted analytic arc.** Let `e` be an open partial
homeomorphism of `ℂ` that is holomorphic on an open subset `Ω` of its source, and let `S` meet `Ω`
only where the chart coordinate is real. A function continuous on `Ω` and holomorphic there away
from `S` is holomorphic throughout `Ω`.

The hypothesis on `S` only constrains its intersection with `Ω`, since points outside the domain
under consideration do not affect the conclusion.
decls.title: Painlevé removability across a charted analytic arc
decls.statement:
theorem
    differentiableOn_of_continuousOn_of_differentiableOn_diff_of_subset_coord_im_eq_zero
    (e : OpenPartialHomeomorph ℂ ℂ) {Ω S : Set ℂ} (he : DifferentiableOn ℂ e Ω)
    (hΩ : IsOpen Ω) (hΩe : Ω ⊆ e.source)
    (hcont : ContinuousOn F Ω) (hdiff : DifferentiableOn ℂ F (Ω \ S))
    (hS : Ω ∩ S ⊆ {z : ℂ | (e z).im = 0}) :
    DifferentiableOn ℂ F Ω

decls.name: TauCeti.differentiableOn_of_continuousOn_of_differentiableOn_diff_coord_im_eq_zero
decls.doc:
**Painlevé removability of the full real locus of a holomorphic chart.** If a function is
continuous on an open part of the chart source and holomorphic wherever the chart coordinate has
nonzero imaginary part, then it is holomorphic throughout that open set.
decls.title: Painlevé removability of the full real locus of a holomorphic chart
decls.statement:
theorem differentiableOn_of_continuousOn_of_differentiableOn_diff_coord_im_eq_zero
    (e : OpenPartialHomeomorph ℂ ℂ) {Ω : Set ℂ} (he : DifferentiableOn ℂ e Ω)
    (hΩ : IsOpen Ω) (hΩe : Ω ⊆ e.source) (hcont : ContinuousOn F Ω)
    (hdiff : DifferentiableOn ℂ F (Ω \ {z : ℂ | (e z).im = 0})) :
    DifferentiableOn ℂ F Ω

decls.name: TauCeti.differentiableOn_of_continuousOn_of_differentiableOn_coord_im_pos_of_differentiableOn_coord_im_neg
decls.doc:
**Gluing across a charted analytic arc.** A continuous function on an open part of the source
of a holomorphic chart that is holomorphic on both open sides of the charted real locus is
holomorphic throughout that open set.
decls.title: Gluing across a charted analytic arc
decls.statement:
theorem
  differentiableOn_of_continuousOn_of_differentiableOn_coord_im_pos_of_differentiableOn_coord_im_neg
    (e : OpenPartialHomeomorph ℂ ℂ) {Ω : Set ℂ} (he : DifferentiableOn ℂ e Ω)
    (hΩ : IsOpen Ω) (hΩe : Ω ⊆ e.source) (hcont : ContinuousOn F Ω)
    (hpos : DifferentiableOn ℂ F (Ω ∩ {z : ℂ | 0 < (e z).im}))
    (hneg : DifferentiableOn ℂ F (Ω ∩ {z : ℂ | (e z).im < 0})) :
    DifferentiableOn ℂ F Ω

decls.name: TauCeti.boundaryIntegral_eq_zero_off_axis
decls.doc:
A rectangle whose open interior avoids the real axis has a vanishing boundary integral for
any function continuous on a domain `Ω` containing the (closed) rectangle and holomorphic on the
part of `Ω` off the real axis. This is the per-rectangle input to Morera's theorem; it is applied
both to axis-avoiding rectangles directly and to the two axis-bounded halves of a straddling
rectangle.
decls.statement:
lemma boundaryIntegral_eq_zero_off_axis
    (hcont : ContinuousOn F Ω) (hdiff : DifferentiableOn ℂ F (Ω ∩ {z : ℂ | z.im ≠ 0}))
    {z w : ℂ} (hsub : Complex.Rectangle z w ⊆ Ω)
    (haxis : (0 : ℝ) ∉ Set.Ioo (min z.im w.im) (max z.im w.im)) :
    ((∫ x : ℝ in z.re..w.re, F (x + z.im * I)) - (∫ x : ℝ in z.re..w.re, F (x + w.im * I)) +
        I • (∫ y : ℝ in z.im..w.im, F (w.re + y * I)) -
        I • (∫ y : ℝ in z.im..w.im, F (z.re + y * I))) = 0

decls.name: TauCeti.boundaryIntegral_eq_zero_of_edge_on_axis
decls.doc:
A rectangle with a horizontal edge *on* the real axis — one of its imaginary coordinates is `0`
— has a vanishing boundary integral. This is `boundaryIntegral_eq_zero_off_axis` in the case where
the axis meets an edge rather than being avoided outright: an endpoint at `0` still keeps `0` out of
the *open* imaginary interior. It is the form applied to the two axis-bounded halves of a straddling
rectangle.
decls.statement:
lemma boundaryIntegral_eq_zero_of_edge_on_axis
    (hcont : ContinuousOn F Ω) (hdiff : DifferentiableOn ℂ F (Ω ∩ {z : ℂ | z.im ≠ 0}))
    {z w : ℂ} (hsub : Complex.Rectangle z w ⊆ Ω) (haxis : z.im = 0 ∨ w.im = 0) :
    ((∫ x : ℝ in z.re..w.re, F (x + z.im * I)) - (∫ x : ℝ in z.re..w.re, F (x + w.im * I)) +
        I • (∫ y : ℝ in z.im..w.im, F (w.re + y * I)) -
        I • (∫ y : ℝ in z.im..w.im, F (z.re + y * I))) = 0

decls.name: TauCeti.vertical_edge_split_at_zero
decls.doc:
The integral of `F` along a vertical edge of the rectangle — the edge with fixed real part `a`
— splits at the real axis: the interval integral over `[[z.im, w.im]]` equals the sum of the
integrals over `z.im → 0` and `0 → w.im`, whenever `F` is continuous on a domain `Ω` containing the
rectangle and `0` lies in the imaginary range `[[z.im, w.im]]`. This is the edge-splitting step
used to recombine the two halves of a straddling rectangle.
decls.statement:
lemma vertical_edge_split_at_zero
    (hcont : ContinuousOn F Ω) {z w : ℂ} (hsub : Complex.Rectangle z w ⊆ Ω)
    (h0mem : (0 : ℝ) ∈ [[z.im, w.im]]) {a : ℝ} (ha : a ∈ [[z.re, w.re]]) :
    (∫ y : ℝ in z.im..w.im, F (↑a + ↑y * I)) =
      (∫ y : ℝ in z.im..(0 : ℝ), F (↑a + ↑y * I)) +
        ∫ y : ℝ in (0 : ℝ)..w.im, F (↑a + ↑y * I)

decls.name: TauCeti.boundaryIntegral_eq_zero_of_straddling
decls.doc:
A rectangle that *straddles* the real axis — `0` lies strictly inside its imaginary range — has
a vanishing boundary integral: split it at the axis into a lower and an upper half, each an
axis-bounded rectangle handled by `boundaryIntegral_eq_zero_of_edge_on_axis`, and recombine, the
shared axis edge cancelling. Same hypotheses as `boundaryIntegral_eq_zero_off_axis`, but with `0`
in the open imaginary interior instead of outside it.
decls.statement:
lemma boundaryIntegral_eq_zero_of_straddling
    (hcont : ContinuousOn F Ω) (hdiff : DifferentiableOn ℂ F (Ω ∩ {z : ℂ | z.im ≠ 0}))
    {z w : ℂ} (hsub : Complex.Rectangle z w ⊆ Ω)
    (hstr : (0 : ℝ) ∈ Set.Ioo (min z.im w.im) (max z.im w.im)) :
    ((∫ x : ℝ in z.re..w.re, F (x + z.im * I)) - (∫ x : ℝ in z.re..w.re, F (x + w.im * I)) +
        I • (∫ y : ℝ in z.im..w.im, F (w.re + y * I)) -
        I • (∫ y : ℝ in z.im..w.im, F (z.re + y * I))) = 0

decls.name: TauCeti.differentiableOn_of_continuousOn_of_differentiableOn_im_ne_zero
decls.doc:
**Painlevé removability of the real axis.** A function continuous on an open set `Ω ⊆ ℂ` and
holomorphic on the part of `Ω` off the real axis is holomorphic on all of `Ω`.

This is the base case of removability across a line: an arbitrary line is reduced to it by an
affine change of variable in
`TauCeti.differentiableOn_of_continuousOn_of_differentiableOn_diff_of_subset_range_lineMap`.
decls.title: Painlevé removability of the real axis
decls.statement:
theorem differentiableOn_of_continuousOn_of_differentiableOn_im_ne_zero
    (hΩ : IsOpen Ω) (hcont : ContinuousOn F Ω)
    (hdiff : DifferentiableOn ℂ F (Ω ∩ {z : ℂ | z.im ≠ 0})) :
    DifferentiableOn ℂ F Ω

decls.name: TauCeti.differentiableOn_of_continuousOn_of_differentiableOn_im_pos_of_differentiableOn_im_neg
decls.doc:
**Gluing across the real axis.** A function on an open set `Ω ⊆ ℂ` that is holomorphic on the
open upper part and on the open lower part of `Ω`, and merely *continuous* on `Ω`, is holomorphic
on all of `Ω`. This is the form in which removability is used to glue two separately defined
holomorphic branches along the axis, as in the Schwarz reflection principle.
decls.title: Gluing across the real axis
decls.statement:
theorem differentiableOn_of_continuousOn_of_differentiableOn_im_pos_of_differentiableOn_im_neg
    (hΩ : IsOpen Ω) (hcont : ContinuousOn F Ω)
    (hpos : DifferentiableOn ℂ F (Ω ∩ {z : ℂ | 0 < z.im}))
    (hneg : DifferentiableOn ℂ F (Ω ∩ {z : ℂ | z.im < 0})) :
    DifferentiableOn ℂ F Ω

decls.name: TauCeti.mem_range_lineMap_iff
decls.doc:
Membership in the line through two points, in the "base point plus real multiple of the
direction" form used by the affine chart below.
decls.statement:
lemma mem_range_lineMap_iff {p q z : ℂ} :
    z ∈ Set.range (AffineMap.lineMap (k := ℝ) p q) ↔ ∃ t : ℝ, z = p + t * (q - p)

decls.name: TauCeti.differentiableOn_of_continuousOn_of_differentiableOn_diff_of_subset_range_lineMap_of_ne
decls.statement:
theorem
    differentiableOn_of_continuousOn_of_differentiableOn_diff_of_subset_range_lineMap_of_ne
    {p q : ℂ} {S : Set ℂ}
    (hpq : p ≠ q) (hS : S ⊆ Set.range (AffineMap.lineMap (k := ℝ) p q))
    (hΩ : IsOpen Ω) (hcont : ContinuousOn F Ω) (hdiff : DifferentiableOn ℂ F (Ω \ S)) :
    DifferentiableOn ℂ F Ω

decls.name: TauCeti.differentiableOn_of_continuousOn_of_differentiableOn_diff_of_subset_range_lineMap
decls.doc:
**Painlevé removability across a line.** Let `S` be any subset of the line through points
`p` and `q`, such as the whole line or a segment. A function continuous on an open set `Ω ⊆ ℂ`
and holomorphic on `Ω \ S` is holomorphic on all of `Ω`.

For distinct `p` and `q`, the line is straightened to the real axis by the affine chart
`w ↦ p + (q - p) * w`; when `p = q`, `S` is a singleton and is contained in any nondegenerate
line through `p`.
decls.title: Painlevé removability across a line
decls.statement:
theorem differentiableOn_of_continuousOn_of_differentiableOn_diff_of_subset_range_lineMap
    {p q : ℂ} {S : Set ℂ}
    (hS : S ⊆ Set.range (AffineMap.lineMap (k := ℝ) p q))
    (hΩ : IsOpen Ω) (hcont : ContinuousOn F Ω) (hdiff : DifferentiableOn ℂ F (Ω \ S)) :
    DifferentiableOn ℂ F Ω

decls.name: TauCeti.differentiableOn_of_continuousOn_of_differentiableOn_diff_im_eq
decls.doc:
**Painlevé removability across a horizontal line.** A function continuous on an open set
`Ω ⊆ ℂ` and holomorphic off the horizontal line `{z | z.im = c}` is holomorphic on all of `Ω`.
decls.title: Painlevé removability across a horizontal line
decls.statement:
theorem differentiableOn_of_continuousOn_of_differentiableOn_diff_im_eq {c : ℝ}
    (hΩ : IsOpen Ω) (hcont : ContinuousOn F Ω)
    (hdiff : DifferentiableOn ℂ F (Ω \ {z : ℂ | z.im = c})) :
    DifferentiableOn ℂ F Ω

decls.name: TauCeti.differentiableOn_of_continuousOn_of_differentiableOn_diff_re_eq
decls.doc:
**Painlevé removability across a vertical line.** A function continuous on an open set
`Ω ⊆ ℂ` and holomorphic off the vertical line `{z | z.re = c}` is holomorphic on all of `Ω`.
decls.title: Painlevé removability across a vertical line
decls.statement:
theorem differentiableOn_of_continuousOn_of_differentiableOn_diff_re_eq {c : ℝ}
    (hΩ : IsOpen Ω) (hcont : ContinuousOn F Ω)
    (hdiff : DifferentiableOn ℂ F (Ω \ {z : ℂ | z.re = c})) :
    DifferentiableOn ℂ F Ω

decls.statement: def circleLineMapInv (c a z : ℂ) : ℂ

decls.name: TauCeti.differentiableOn_circleLineMap
TauCeti.differentiableOn_circleLineMapInv
TauCeti.circleLineMap_circleLineMapInv
TauCeti.circleLineMap_ne_neg_I

lemma circleLineMap_ne_neg_I {c a z : ℂ} (ha : a ≠ 0)

    circleLineMapInv c a z ≠ -I

decls.name: TauCeti.circleLineMap_mem_sphere_iff
TauCeti.differentiableOn_of_continuousOn_of_differentiableOn_diff_sphere_omit
decls.statement:
theorem differentiableOn_of_continuousOn_of_differentiableOn_diff_sphere_omit

decls.name: TauCeti.differentiableOn_of_continuousOn_of_differentiableOn_diff_sphere
decls.doc:
**Painlevé removability across a circle.** A function continuous on an open set `Ω ⊆ ℂ`
and holomorphic off a positive-radius circle is holomorphic throughout `Ω`.
decls.title: Painlevé removability across a circle
decls.statement:
theorem differentiableOn_of_continuousOn_of_differentiableOn_diff_sphere
    {Ω : Set ℂ} {F : ℂ → ℂ} {c : ℂ} {r : ℝ} (hr : 0 < r)
    (hΩ : IsOpen Ω) (hcont : ContinuousOn F Ω)
    (hdiff : DifferentiableOn ℂ F (Ω \ sphere c r)) :
    DifferentiableOn ℂ F Ω

decls.name: TauCeti.riemannMapping_homeomorph
decls.doc:
**The Riemann mapping theorem as a homeomorphism.** A simply connected open proper subset of
`ℂ`, regarded as a subtype, is homeomorphic to `Complex.UnitDisc`.

The homeomorphism is induced by the holomorphic bijection supplied by `TauCeti.riemannMapping`;
its forward and inverse formulas are
`DifferentiableOn.toHomeomorphOfBijOn_apply` and
`DifferentiableOn.toHomeomorphOfBijOn_symm_apply`.
decls.title: The Riemann mapping theorem as a homeomorphism

decls.name: TauCeti.riemannMapping_openPartialHomeomorph
decls.doc:
**The Riemann mapping theorem as a conformal open partial homeomorphism.** A simply connected
open proper subset `Ω` of `ℂ` is the source of an open partial homeomorphism whose target is the
open unit disc. The map and its inverse are holomorphic and conformal throughout their respective
domains.
decls.title: The Riemann mapping theorem as a conformal open partial homeomorphism
decls.statement:
theorem riemannMapping_openPartialHomeomorph {Ω : Set ℂ}
    (hΩo : IsOpen Ω) (hΩc : IsSimplyConnected Ω) (hΩ : Ω ≠ univ) :
    ∃ e : OpenPartialHomeomorph ℂ ℂ,
      e.source = Ω ∧
      e.target = ball (0 : ℂ) 1 ∧
      DifferentiableOn ℂ e Ω ∧
      DifferentiableOn ℂ e.symm (ball (0 : ℂ) 1) ∧
      (∀ z ∈ Ω, ConformalAt e z) ∧
      ∀ w ∈ ball (0 : ℂ) 1, ConformalAt e.symm w

decls.name: TauCeti.bijOn_invFunOn_of_bijOn_ball
decls.doc: The inverse of a Riemann map, as a bijection of the open unit disc onto the domain.
decls.statement:
lemma bijOn_invFunOn_of_bijOn_ball {g : ℂ → ℂ} (hbij : BijOn g Ω (ball 0 1)) :
    BijOn (Function.invFunOn g Ω) (ball 0 1) Ω

decls.name: TauCeti.differentiableOn_invFunOn_of_bijOn
decls.doc:
A holomorphic bijection of an open set onto its image has a holomorphic inverse there.

This repackages `TauCeti.DifferentiableOn.invFunOn` with the image identified by a `Set.BijOn`
hypothesis, which is the form the constructions in this file produce.
decls.statement:
lemma differentiableOn_invFunOn_of_bijOn {f : ℂ → ℂ} (hΩo : IsOpen Ω)
    (hfd : DifferentiableOn ℂ f Ω) (hbij : BijOn f Ω Ω') :
    DifferentiableOn ℂ (Function.invFunOn f Ω) Ω'

decls.name: TauCeti.exists_bijOn_differentiableOn_invFunOn_of_isSimplyConnected
decls.doc:
**Any two simply connected proper domains of `ℂ` are conformally equivalent.** If `Ω` and `Ω'`
are simply connected open proper subsets of `ℂ`, then some holomorphic `f` maps `Ω` bijectively
onto `Ω'`, and its inverse `Function.invFunOn f Ω` is holomorphic on `Ω'`.

Neither domain is required to be bounded, and no normalization is imposed: the map is one of a
whole `Aut(𝔻)`-torsor of such maps. Together with
`TauCeti.not_bijOn_univ_of_isSimplyConnected` this is a complete classification of the simply
connected domains of `ℂ` up to biholomorphism: there are exactly two classes, `ℂ` and everything
else.
decls.title: Any two simply connected proper domains of `ℂ` are conformally equivalent
decls.statement:
theorem exists_bijOn_differentiableOn_invFunOn_of_isSimplyConnected
    (hΩo : IsOpen Ω) (hΩc : IsSimplyConnected Ω) (hΩ : Ω ≠ univ)
    (hΩ'o : IsOpen Ω') (hΩ'c : IsSimplyConnected Ω') (hΩ' : Ω' ≠ univ) :
    ∃ f : ℂ → ℂ, BijOn f Ω Ω' ∧ DifferentiableOn ℂ f Ω ∧
      DifferentiableOn ℂ (Function.invFunOn f Ω) Ω' ∧
      LeftInvOn (Function.invFunOn f Ω) f Ω ∧
      RightInvOn (Function.invFunOn f Ω) f Ω'

decls.name: TauCeti.exists_openPartialHomeomorph_of_isSimplyConnected
decls.doc:
**Conformal equivalence of simply connected proper domains, packaged.** A biholomorphism of
`Ω` onto `Ω'` as an `OpenPartialHomeomorph ℂ ℂ` whose source is `Ω` and whose target is `Ω'`,
holomorphic and conformal in both directions. It is the Riemann map of `Ω` followed by the inverse
of the Riemann map of `Ω'`, both taken from `TauCeti.riemannMapping_openPartialHomeomorph`.

This is the packaged-equivalence companion the generality bar of
`TauCetiRoadmap/ConformalMapping/README.md` asks for, in the same form as
`TauCeti.riemannMapping_openPartialHomeomorph` for the disc.
decls.title: Conformal equivalence of simply connected proper domains, packaged
decls.statement:
theorem exists_openPartialHomeomorph_of_isSimplyConnected
    (hΩo : IsOpen Ω) (hΩc : IsSimplyConnected Ω) (hΩ : Ω ≠ univ)
    (hΩ'o : IsOpen Ω') (hΩ'c : IsSimplyConnected Ω') (hΩ' : Ω' ≠ univ) :
    ∃ e : OpenPartialHomeomorph ℂ ℂ,
      e.source = Ω ∧
      e.target = Ω' ∧
      DifferentiableOn ℂ e Ω ∧
      DifferentiableOn ℂ e.symm Ω' ∧
      (∀ z ∈ Ω, ConformalAt e z) ∧
      ∀ w ∈ Ω', ConformalAt e.symm w

decls.name: TauCeti.nonempty_homeomorph_unitDisc_of_isSimplyConnected
decls.doc:
**Every simply connected domain of `ℂ` is homeomorphic to the disc**, properness included.
For a proper domain this is `TauCeti.riemannMapping_homeomorph`; the whole plane is homeomorphic
to the disc as well, by `Homeomorph.unitBall`, even though it is not biholomorphic to it.
decls.title: Every simply connected domain of `ℂ` is homeomorphic to the disc
decls.statement:
lemma nonempty_homeomorph_unitDisc_of_isSimplyConnected
    (hΩo : IsOpen Ω) (hΩc : IsSimplyConnected Ω) :
    Nonempty (Ω ≃ₜ Complex.UnitDisc)

decls.name: TauCeti.nonempty_homeomorph_of_isSimplyConnected
decls.doc:
**Any two simply connected domains of `ℂ` are homeomorphic**, as subtypes.

Unlike the biholomorphism statements above this needs no properness hypothesis: the plane is not
biholomorphic to the disc, but it is homeomorphic to it.
decls.title: Any two simply connected domains of `ℂ` are homeomorphic
decls.statement:
theorem nonempty_homeomorph_of_isSimplyConnected
    (hΩo : IsOpen Ω) (hΩc : IsSimplyConnected Ω)
    (hΩ'o : IsOpen Ω') (hΩ'c : IsSimplyConnected Ω') :
    Nonempty (Ω ≃ₜ Ω')

decls.name: TauCeti.bijOn_ball_of_unitDiscEquiv
decls.doc:
A self-equivalence of `Complex.UnitDisc`, read through a scalar representative, is a bijection
of `Metric.ball 0 1` onto itself.

decls.name: TauCeti.exists_bijOn_ball_apply_eq
decls.doc:
A holomorphic automorphism of the open unit disc carrying a prescribed point to another, as a
scalar map of `Metric.ball 0 1`.

The automorphism comes from the transitivity of `TauCeti.unitDiscAut` on `Complex.UnitDisc`,
namely `TauCeti.exists_mem_unitDiscAut_apply_eq`; the classification
`TauCeti.mem_unitDiscAut_iff` then names its scalar formula, whose holomorphy is
`TauCeti.differentiableOn_unitDiscStandardAutomorphismFormula`.
decls.statement:
lemma exists_bijOn_ball_apply_eq {a b : ℂ} (ha : ‖a‖ < 1) (hb : ‖b‖ < 1) :
    ∃ φ : ℂ → ℂ, BijOn φ (ball 0 1) (ball 0 1) ∧ DifferentiableOn ℂ φ (ball 0 1) ∧ φ a = b

decls.name: TauCeti.exists_bijOn_self_apply_eq_of_isSimplyConnected
decls.doc:
**A simply connected domain is homogeneous.** The biholomorphic self-maps of a simply
connected open `Ω ⊆ ℂ` act transitively on `Ω`: given `z₀, z₁ ∈ Ω` there is a holomorphic
bijection of `Ω` onto itself, with holomorphic inverse, carrying `z₀` to `z₁`.

Unlike the equivalence statements above, this needs no properness hypothesis: for `Ω = Set.univ`
the translation `z ↦ z + (z₁ - z₀)` already does the job. Otherwise transitivity is inherited from
the disc, where `TauCeti.unitDiscAut` already acts transitively, and the Riemann map transports the
action. It fails badly without simple connectivity — the punctured disc, for instance, is not
homogeneous.
decls.title: A simply connected domain is homogeneous
decls.statement:
theorem exists_bijOn_self_apply_eq_of_isSimplyConnected
    (hΩo : IsOpen Ω) (hΩc : IsSimplyConnected Ω) {z₀ z₁ : ℂ}
    (hz₀ : z₀ ∈ Ω) (hz₁ : z₁ ∈ Ω) :
    ∃ f : ℂ → ℂ, BijOn f Ω Ω ∧ DifferentiableOn ℂ f Ω ∧
      DifferentiableOn ℂ (Function.invFunOn f Ω) Ω ∧ f z₀ = z₁

decls.name: TauCeti.Differentiable.exists_const_forall_eq_of_isSimplyConnected
decls.doc:
**An entire function with values in a simply connected proper domain is constant.** Composing
with the Riemann map of `Ω` turns such a function into a bounded entire function, which Liouville's
theorem forces to be constant; the Riemann map is injective, so the original function is constant
too.

For bounded `Ω` this is Liouville's theorem itself, but the statement covers unbounded `Ω` such as
the slit plane, where the Riemann map is doing genuine work.
decls.title: An entire function with values in a simply connected proper domain is constant
decls.statement:
theorem Differentiable.exists_const_forall_eq_of_isSimplyConnected {f : ℂ → ℂ}
    (hf : Differentiable ℂ f) (hΩo : IsOpen Ω) (hΩc : IsSimplyConnected Ω) (hΩ : Ω ≠ univ)
    (hmaps : ∀ z, f z ∈ Ω) :
    ∃ c, ∀ z, f z = c

decls.name: TauCeti.not_injOn_univ_of_isSimplyConnected
decls.doc:
**No injective entire function takes its values in a simply connected proper domain.** Such a
function is constant by `TauCeti.Differentiable.exists_const_forall_eq_of_isSimplyConnected`, and a
constant map on `ℂ` is not injective.

Only the values of `f` are constrained, not the image: `f` is not required to cover `Ω`.
decls.title: No injective entire function takes its values in a simply connected proper domain
decls.statement:
theorem not_injOn_univ_of_isSimplyConnected {f : ℂ → ℂ} (hf : Differentiable ℂ f)
    (hΩo : IsOpen Ω) (hΩc : IsSimplyConnected Ω) (hΩ : Ω ≠ univ) (hmaps : MapsTo f univ Ω) :
    ¬ InjOn f univ

decls.name: TauCeti.not_bijOn_univ_of_isSimplyConnected
decls.doc:
**`ℂ` is conformally equivalent to no simply connected proper domain.** No entire function maps
`ℂ` bijectively onto a simply connected open proper subset of `ℂ`: it is already barred from being
injective there by `TauCeti.not_injOn_univ_of_isSimplyConnected`.

So the properness hypothesis in
`TauCeti.exists_bijOn_differentiableOn_invFunOn_of_isSimplyConnected` cannot be dropped: `ℂ` is a
simply connected domain lying in a biholomorphism class of its own.
decls.title: `ℂ` is conformally equivalent to no simply connected proper domain
decls.statement:
theorem not_bijOn_univ_of_isSimplyConnected {f : ℂ → ℂ} (hf : Differentiable ℂ f)
    (hΩo : IsOpen Ω) (hΩc : IsSimplyConnected Ω) (hΩ : Ω ≠ univ) :
    ¬ BijOn f univ Ω

decls.name: TauCeti.riemannMapping
decls.doc:
**The Riemann mapping theorem.** A simply connected open proper subset `Ω` of `ℂ` admits a
holomorphic bijection onto the open unit disc, with nonvanishing derivative throughout `Ω`.

Existence only: the map is not asserted to be unique, and no normalization is imposed.
decls.title: The Riemann mapping theorem
decls.statement:
theorem riemannMapping {Ω : Set ℂ} (hΩo : IsOpen Ω) (hΩc : IsSimplyConnected Ω) (hΩ : Ω ≠ univ) :
    ∃ f : ℂ → ℂ, BijOn f Ω (ball 0 1) ∧ DifferentiableOn ℂ f Ω ∧ ∀ z ∈ Ω, deriv f z ≠ 0

decls.name: TauCeti.exists_bijOn_ball_differentiableOn_invFunOn
decls.doc:
**The Riemann mapping theorem as a biholomorphism.** The map of `TauCeti.riemannMapping` has a
holomorphic inverse: `Function.invFunOn f Ω` is holomorphic on the disc and inverts `f` on both
sides, so `Ω` and the disc are biholomorphic, not merely in holomorphic bijection.

Stated unbundled, in the idiom of `Set.BijOn` used throughout this development: the inverse is named
explicitly as `Function.invFunOn f Ω` rather than hidden inside a bundled equivalence, so a consumer
can rewrite with it directly.
decls.title: The Riemann mapping theorem as a biholomorphism
decls.statement:
theorem exists_bijOn_ball_differentiableOn_invFunOn {Ω : Set ℂ} (hΩo : IsOpen Ω)
    (hΩc : IsSimplyConnected Ω) (hΩ : Ω ≠ univ) :
    ∃ f : ℂ → ℂ, BijOn f Ω (ball 0 1) ∧ DifferentiableOn ℂ f Ω ∧
      DifferentiableOn ℂ (Function.invFunOn f Ω) (ball 0 1) ∧
      LeftInvOn (Function.invFunOn f Ω) f Ω ∧
      RightInvOn (Function.invFunOn f Ω) f (ball 0 1)

decls.name: TauCeti.bijOn_ball_const_mul
decls.doc:
Multiplying by a unimodular constant preserves a bijection onto a ball about the origin:
rotations of the ball are bijections of it. Neither the domain nor the radius plays any role, so
this is stated for an arbitrary source set and an arbitrary radius.

decls.name: TauCeti.eq_one_of_norm_eq_one_of_mul_pos
decls.doc:
A unimodular constant carrying one positive real to another is `1`: the modulus forces the two
positive reals to be equal, and cancelling them leaves `u = 1`. This is the rigidity behind the
uniqueness of the normalized Riemann map.
decls.statement:
theorem eq_one_of_norm_eq_one_of_mul_pos {u a b : ℂ} (hu : ‖u‖ = 1) (ha : 0 < a)
    (hb : 0 < b) (hab : u * a = b) : u = 1

decls.name: TauCeti.IsNormalizedRiemannMapOn
decls.doc:
A **normalized Riemann map** of a domain `Ω` at a base point `z₀ ∈ Ω`: a holomorphic bijection
of `Ω` onto the open unit disc that sends `z₀` to the origin and has a *positive real* derivative
there.

The order on `deriv f z₀` is the scoped `ComplexOrder` one, so `0 < deriv f z₀` unfolds to
`0 < (deriv f z₀).re ∧ 0 = (deriv f z₀).im`.

This normalization is what makes the Riemann map unique: `TauCeti.riemannMapping` produces a map
only up to a disc automorphism, whereas by `TauCeti.riemannMapping_normalized` any two functions
satisfying the predicate below agree on `Ω`. Uniqueness can only be uniqueness on `Ω`, since the
predicate says nothing about the values of `f` outside `Ω`.
decls.statement: structure IsNormalizedRiemannMapOn (f : ℂ → ℂ) (Ω : Set ℂ) (z₀ : ℂ) : Prop

decls.name: TauCeti.IsNormalizedRiemannMapOn.mapsTo
decls.statement: theorem mapsTo : MapsTo f Ω (ball (0 : ℂ) 1)

decls.name: TauCeti.IsNormalizedRiemannMapOn.injOn
decls.statement: theorem injOn : InjOn f Ω

decls.name: TauCeti.IsNormalizedRiemannMapOn.surjOn
decls.statement: theorem surjOn : SurjOn f Ω (ball (0 : ℂ) 1)

decls.name: TauCeti.IsNormalizedRiemannMapOn.image_eq
decls.statement: theorem image_eq : f '' Ω = ball (0 : ℂ) 1

decls.name: TauCeti.IsNormalizedRiemannMapOn.isPointedDiscInjectionOn
decls.doc:
A normalized Riemann map competes in the extremal family of `ExtremalFamily.lean`: it is a
holomorphic injection into the disc fixing the base point.
decls.statement: theorem isPointedDiscInjectionOn : IsPointedDiscInjectionOn f Ω z₀

decls.name: TauCeti.IsNormalizedRiemannMapOn.deriv_ne_zero_base
decls.statement: theorem deriv_ne_zero_base : deriv f z₀ ≠ 0

decls.name: TauCeti.IsNormalizedRiemannMapOn.coe_norm_deriv
decls.doc: The derivative of a normalized Riemann map at the base point is its own modulus.
decls.statement: theorem coe_norm_deriv : ((‖deriv f z₀‖ : ℝ) : ℂ) = deriv f z₀

decls.name: TauCeti.exists_isNormalizedRiemannMapOn
decls.doc:
**Existence of the normalized Riemann map.** Every nonempty, simply connected, open, proper
subset `Ω` of `ℂ` carries, at each of its points `z₀`, a holomorphic bijection onto the open unit
disc sending `z₀` to `0` with positive real derivative there.

The extremal map of `TauCeti.exists_isMaxOn_norm_deriv_of_isSimplyConnected` already fixes the base
point and is onto by `TauCeti.surjOn_ball_of_isMaxOn`; only a rotation is needed to make its
derivative positive.
decls.title: Existence of the normalized Riemann map
decls.statement:
theorem exists_isNormalizedRiemannMapOn (hΩo : IsOpen Ω) (hΩc : IsSimplyConnected Ω)
    (hΩ : Ω ≠ univ) (hz₀ : z₀ ∈ Ω) :
    ∃ f : ℂ → ℂ, IsNormalizedRiemannMapOn f Ω z₀

decls.name: TauCeti.IsNormalizedRiemannMapOn.eqOn
decls.doc:
**Uniqueness of the normalized Riemann map.** Two normalized Riemann maps of the same domain at
the same base point agree on that domain.

Together with `TauCeti.exists_isNormalizedRiemannMapOn` this makes the normalized Riemann map a
genuinely well-defined function of `(Ω, z₀)` *on* `Ω`: what is determined is the restriction
`Ω → 𝔻`, not the values of a representative off `Ω`. Note that neither simple connectivity nor
properness of `Ω` is needed here: uniqueness holds wherever two such maps happen to exist.
decls.title: Uniqueness of the normalized Riemann map
decls.statement:
theorem IsNormalizedRiemannMapOn.eqOn (hg : IsNormalizedRiemannMapOn g Ω z₀)
    (hf : IsNormalizedRiemannMapOn f Ω z₀) (hΩo : IsOpen Ω) : EqOn g f Ω

decls.name: TauCeti.riemannMapping_normalized
decls.doc:
**The Riemann mapping theorem, normalized.** A nonempty, simply connected, open, proper subset
`Ω` of `ℂ` with a base point `z₀` carries a holomorphic bijection onto the open unit disc that
sends `z₀` to `0` with positive real derivative there, and that map is unique: any other one agrees
with it on `Ω`.

This is the pinned-down form of `TauCeti.riemannMapping`, which asserts existence only.
decls.title: The Riemann mapping theorem, normalized
decls.statement:
theorem riemannMapping_normalized (hΩo : IsOpen Ω) (hΩc : IsSimplyConnected Ω) (hΩ : Ω ≠ univ)
    (hz₀ : z₀ ∈ Ω) :
    ∃ f : ℂ → ℂ, IsNormalizedRiemannMapOn f Ω z₀ ∧
      ∀ g : ℂ → ℂ, IsNormalizedRiemannMapOn g Ω z₀ → EqOn g f Ω

decls.name: TauCeti.isNormalizedRiemannMapOn_id_ball
decls.doc: The identity is the normalized Riemann map of the unit disc at the origin.
decls.statement: theorem isNormalizedRiemannMapOn_id_ball : IsNormalizedRiemannMapOn id (ball (0 : ℂ) 1) 0

decls.name: TauCeti.eqOn_id_of_isNormalizedRiemannMapOn_ball
decls.doc:
**Rigidity of the disc.** A holomorphic bijection of the open unit disc onto itself that fixes
the origin and has positive real derivative there is the identity.

This strengthens `TauCeti.eqOn_id_of_leftInvOn_ball_of_map_zero_of_deriv_zero_eq_one`, which
assumes the derivative at the origin is exactly `1`: here it is only assumed to be a positive real,
and uniqueness of the normalized Riemann map supplies the rest.
decls.title: Rigidity of the disc
decls.statement:
theorem eqOn_id_of_isNormalizedRiemannMapOn_ball
    (hf : IsNormalizedRiemannMapOn f (ball (0 : ℂ) 1) 0) : EqOn f id (ball (0 : ℂ) 1)

decls.name: TauCeti.exists_eqOn_unitDiscStandardAutomorphismFormula_comp
decls.doc:
**Uniqueness in the Riemann mapping theorem, up to a disc automorphism.** If `f` and `g` are
holomorphic injections from an open set `U` onto the open unit disc, then there are `u` on the
unit circle and `a` in the unit disc such that

`g z = u * (f z - a) / (1 - conj a * f z)`

for every `z ∈ U`.
decls.title: Uniqueness in the Riemann mapping theorem, up to a disc automorphism
decls.statement:
theorem exists_eqOn_unitDiscStandardAutomorphismFormula_comp {U : Set ℂ} (hU : IsOpen U)
    {f g : ℂ → ℂ} (hf : DifferentiableOn ℂ f U) (hg : DifferentiableOn ℂ g U)
    (hfi : InjOn f U) (hgi : InjOn g U)
    (hfimage : f '' U = ball (0 : ℂ) 1) (hgimage : g '' U = ball (0 : ℂ) 1) :
    ∃ (u : Circle) (a : Complex.UnitDisc),
      EqOn g
        (fun z =>
          (u : ℂ) *
            ((f z - (a : ℂ)) / (1 - (starRingEnd ℂ) (a : ℂ) * f z)))
        U

decls.name: TauCeti.exists_eqOn_const_mul_of_image_eq_ball_of_apply_eq_zero
decls.doc:
**Normalized uniqueness in the Riemann mapping theorem.** If two biholomorphic maps onto the unit
disc send the same point of their domain to zero, then they differ by a rotation of the disc.
decls.title: Normalized uniqueness in the Riemann mapping theorem
decls.statement:
theorem exists_eqOn_const_mul_of_image_eq_ball_of_apply_eq_zero {U : Set ℂ} (hU : IsOpen U)
    {f g : ℂ → ℂ} (hf : DifferentiableOn ℂ f U) (hg : DifferentiableOn ℂ g U)
    (hfi : InjOn f U) (hgi : InjOn g U)
    (hfimage : f '' U = ball (0 : ℂ) 1) (hgimage : g '' U = ball (0 : ℂ) 1)
    {z₀ : ℂ} (hz₀ : z₀ ∈ U) (hfzero : f z₀ = 0) (hgzero : g z₀ = 0) :
    ∃ u : Circle, EqOn g (fun z => (u : ℂ) * f z) U

decls.name: TauCeti.ne_zero_left
decls.doc:
The symmetric Rouché hypothesis forces `f` to be zero-free: at a zero of `f` it would read
`‖g z‖ < ‖g z‖`.
decls.statement: lemma ne_zero_left {z : ℂ} (h : ‖f z - g z‖ < ‖f z‖ + ‖g z‖) : f z ≠ 0

decls.name: TauCeti.ne_zero_right
decls.doc:
The symmetric Rouché hypothesis forces `g` to be zero-free too: at a zero of `g` it would read
`‖f z‖ < ‖f z‖`.
decls.statement: lemma ne_zero_right {z : ℂ} (h : ‖f z - g z‖ < ‖f z‖ + ‖g z‖) : g z ≠ 0

decls.name: TauCeti.mem_slitPlane_of_norm_one_sub_lt
decls.doc:
If the triangle inequality `‖1 - w‖ ≤ 1 + ‖w‖` is strict at `w`, then `w` lies in the slit
plane. Indeed equality holds exactly on the nonpositive reals — there `‖1 - w‖` and `1 + ‖w‖` are
both `1 - w.re` — and those are exactly the points the slit plane omits. This is the geometric
content of the symmetric Rouché hypothesis.
decls.statement:
lemma mem_slitPlane_of_norm_one_sub_lt {w : ℂ} (h : ‖1 - w‖ < 1 + ‖w‖) :
    w ∈ slitPlane

decls.name: TauCeti.div_mem_slitPlane
decls.doc:
The quotient `g / f` of the symmetric Rouché hypothesis lands in the slit plane: dividing the
hypothesis by `‖f z‖ > 0` turns it into the hypothesis of `mem_slitPlane_of_norm_one_sub_lt`.
decls.statement:
lemma div_mem_slitPlane {z : ℂ} (h : ‖f z - g z‖ < ‖f z‖ + ‖g z‖) :
    g z / f z ∈ slitPlane

decls.name: TauCeti.order_eq_zero
decls.doc:
A holomorphic function has meromorphic order `0` exactly where it does not vanish. This is the
form the argument principle's circle hypothesis takes.
decls.statement:
lemma order_eq_zero (hf : AnalyticOnNhd ℂ f (closedBall c R)) {z : ℂ}
    (hz : z ∈ closedBall c R) (hne : f z ≠ 0) : meromorphicOrderAt f z = 0

decls.name: TauCeti.circleIntegrable_logDeriv
decls.doc:
The logarithmic derivative of a function holomorphic and zero-free on a circle is continuous
there, hence circle-integrable.
decls.statement:
lemma circleIntegrable_logDeriv (hR : 0 < R)
    (hf : AnalyticOnNhd ℂ f (closedBall c R))
    (hne : ∀ z ∈ sphere c R, f z ≠ 0) : CircleIntegrable (logDeriv f) c R

decls.name: TauCeti.circleIntegral_logDeriv_div_eq_zero
decls.doc:
The contour integral of `logDeriv (g / f)` around the circle vanishes: the hypothesis confines
`g / f` to the slit plane there, where `Complex.log` supplies a primitive.
decls.statement:
lemma circleIntegral_logDeriv_div_eq_zero (hR : 0 < R)
    (hf : AnalyticOnNhd ℂ f (closedBall c R)) (hg : AnalyticOnNhd ℂ g (closedBall c R))
    (hs : ∀ z ∈ sphere c R, ‖f z - g z‖ < ‖f z‖ + ‖g z‖) :
    (∮ z in C(c, R), logDeriv (fun w => g w / f w) z) = 0

decls.name: TauCeti.finsum_divisor_cast
decls.doc:
The count produced by the argument principle, in the vocabulary of orders of vanishing: the
finitely supported sum of the divisor equals the cast of the finitely supported sum of
`analyticOrderNatAt` over the open disc. Both sides assign `0` at a point of infinite order, so
this counts zeros of finite order; the caller supplies the hypotheses that exclude the other
kind.
decls.statement:
lemma finsum_divisor_cast {h : ℂ → ℂ} (hh : AnalyticOnNhd ℂ h (closedBall c R)) :
    (∑ᶠ z, ((MeromorphicOn.divisor h (ball c R) z : ℤ) : ℂ))
      = ((∑ᶠ z ∈ ball c R, analyticOrderNatAt h z : ℕ) : ℂ)

decls.name: TauCeti.rouche_symm
decls.doc:
**Rouché's theorem, symmetric form** (Estermann). If `f` and `g` are holomorphic on the closed
disc `closedBall c R` and `‖f z - g z‖ < ‖f z‖ + ‖g z‖` at every point `z` of the bounding circle,
then `f` and `g` have the same number of zeros in `ball c R`, each counted with multiplicity. The
hypothesis forces both functions to be zero-free on the circle, hence of finite order throughout
the disc, so every zero is genuinely counted.

The hypothesis is the strict form of the triangle inequality `‖f z - g z‖ ≤ ‖f z‖ + ‖g z‖`, so it
says exactly that `f z` and `g z` never point in *opposite* directions on the circle. It is
symmetric in `f` and `g` and strictly weaker than the classical `‖f z - g z‖ < ‖f z‖` of
`TauCeti.rouche`.

The counts are the canonical finitely supported sums `∑ᶠ z ∈ ball c R, analyticOrderNatAt · z`;
no finiteness witness appears in the statement.
decls.title: Rouché's theorem, symmetric form
decls.statement:
theorem rouche_symm (hR : 0 < R)
    (hf : AnalyticOnNhd ℂ f (closedBall c R)) (hg : AnalyticOnNhd ℂ g (closedBall c R))
    (hs : ∀ z ∈ sphere c R, ‖f z - g z‖ < ‖f z‖ + ‖g z‖) :
    (∑ᶠ z ∈ ball c R, analyticOrderNatAt f z)
      = ∑ᶠ z ∈ ball c R, analyticOrderNatAt g z

decls.name: TauCeti.rouche
decls.doc:
**Rouché's theorem** for a disc, classical form. If `f` and `g` are holomorphic on the closed
disc `closedBall c R` and `‖f z - g z‖ < ‖f z‖` at every point `z` of the bounding circle, then `f`
and `g` have the same number of zeros in `ball c R`, each counted with multiplicity.

This is the special case of `TauCeti.rouche_symm` obtained by discarding the nonnegative summand
`‖g z‖` from the symmetric hypothesis.
decls.title: Rouché's theorem
decls.statement:
theorem rouche (hR : 0 < R)
    (hf : AnalyticOnNhd ℂ f (closedBall c R)) (hg : AnalyticOnNhd ℂ g (closedBall c R))
    (hs : ∀ z ∈ sphere c R, ‖f z - g z‖ < ‖f z‖) :
    (∑ᶠ z ∈ ball c R, analyticOrderNatAt f z)
      = ∑ᶠ z ∈ ball c R, analyticOrderNatAt g z

decls.name: TauCeti.rouche_add
decls.doc:
**Rouché's theorem**, in the additive phrasing of most textbooks: a holomorphic perturbation
`g` that is dominated by `f` on the bounding circle does not change the number of zeros inside.
decls.title: Rouché's theorem
decls.statement:
theorem rouche_add (hR : 0 < R)
