    (hf : AnalyticOnNhd ℂ f (closedBall c R)) (hg : AnalyticOnNhd ℂ g (closedBall c R))
    (hs : ∀ z ∈ sphere c R, ‖g z‖ < ‖f z‖) :
    (∑ᶠ z ∈ ball c R, analyticOrderNatAt f z)
      = ∑ᶠ z ∈ ball c R, analyticOrderNatAt (fun w => f w + g w) z

decls.name: TauCeti.exists_mem_closedBall_ne_zero
decls.doc:
A function that is zero-free on the bounding circle of a disc of positive radius does not
vanish identically on the closed disc — the boundary point `c + R` witnesses it. This is the shape
in which `TauCeti.finsum_analyticOrderNatAt_ball_eq_zero_iff` wants the Rouché hypothesis.
decls.statement:
lemma exists_mem_closedBall_ne_zero (hR : 0 < R) (hs : ∀ z ∈ sphere c R, f z ≠ 0) :
    ∃ z ∈ closedBall c R, f z ≠ 0

decls.name: TauCeti.rouche_symm_exists_eq_zero_iff
decls.doc:
**Rouché's theorem as a zero-detection principle**, symmetric form. Under the hypothesis
`‖f z - g z‖ < ‖f z‖ + ‖g z‖` on the bounding circle, `f` has a zero in the open disc if and only
if `g` does. This is how Rouché is normally used: to import a zero of a comparison function.
decls.title: Rouché's theorem as a zero-detection principle
decls.statement:
theorem rouche_symm_exists_eq_zero_iff (hR : 0 < R)
    (hf : AnalyticOnNhd ℂ f (closedBall c R)) (hg : AnalyticOnNhd ℂ g (closedBall c R))
    (hs : ∀ z ∈ sphere c R, ‖f z - g z‖ < ‖f z‖ + ‖g z‖) :
    (∃ z ∈ ball c R, f z = 0) ↔ ∃ z ∈ ball c R, g z = 0

decls.name: TauCeti.rouche_exists_eq_zero_iff
decls.doc:
**Rouché's theorem as a zero-detection principle**, classical form: under
`‖f z - g z‖ < ‖f z‖` on the bounding circle, `f` has a zero in the open disc if and only if `g`
does.
decls.title: Rouché's theorem as a zero-detection principle
decls.statement:
theorem rouche_exists_eq_zero_iff (hR : 0 < R)
    (hf : AnalyticOnNhd ℂ f (closedBall c R)) (hg : AnalyticOnNhd ℂ g (closedBall c R))
    (hs : ∀ z ∈ sphere c R, ‖f z - g z‖ < ‖f z‖) :
    (∃ z ∈ ball c R, f z = 0) ↔ ∃ z ∈ ball c R, g z = 0

decls.name: TauCeti.rouche_add_exists_eq_zero_iff
decls.doc:
**Rouché's theorem as a zero-detection principle**, additive form: a holomorphic perturbation
`g` dominated by `f` on the bounding circle neither creates nor destroys zeros inside, so `f` has a
zero in the open disc if and only if `f + g` does. This is the phrasing that reads a zero of a
perturbed function off the unperturbed one, the existence counterpart of `TauCeti.rouche_add`.
decls.title: Rouché's theorem as a zero-detection principle
decls.statement:
theorem rouche_add_exists_eq_zero_iff (hR : 0 < R)
    (hf : AnalyticOnNhd ℂ f (closedBall c R)) (hg : AnalyticOnNhd ℂ g (closedBall c R))
    (hs : ∀ z ∈ sphere c R, ‖g z‖ < ‖f z‖) :
    (∃ z ∈ ball c R, f z = 0) ↔ ∃ z ∈ ball c R, f z + g z = 0

decls.name: TauCeti.norm_deriv_lt_div_of_not_injOn
decls.doc:
**Strict Schwarz lemma.** A holomorphic map of `ball c R₁` into `closedBall (g c) R₂` that is
**not** injective has `‖deriv g c‖ < R₂ / R₁`.

Schwarz's lemma gives `‖deriv g c‖ ≤ R₂ / R₁`; in the equality case the map is affine with nonzero
slope, hence injective. Both radii must be positive: for `R₂ = 0` the map is constant, so it is
not injective and the strict bound fails.
decls.title: Strict Schwarz lemma
decls.statement:
theorem norm_deriv_lt_div_of_not_injOn {g : ℂ → E} {c : ℂ} {R₁ R₂ : ℝ} (hR₁ : 0 < R₁)
    (hR₂ : 0 < R₂) (hgd : DifferentiableOn ℂ g (ball c R₁))
    (hgm : MapsTo g (ball c R₁) (closedBall (g c) R₂)) (hgi : ¬ InjOn g (ball c R₁)) :
    ‖deriv g c‖ < R₂ / R₁

decls.name: TauCeti.norm_deriv_lt_one_of_not_injOn
decls.doc:
**Strict Schwarz lemma, equal radii.** A holomorphic map of `ball c R` into
`closedBall (g c) R` that is **not** injective has `‖deriv g c‖ < 1`.
decls.title: Strict Schwarz lemma, equal radii
decls.statement:
theorem norm_deriv_lt_one_of_not_injOn {g : ℂ → E} {c : ℂ} {R : ℝ} (hR : 0 < R)
    (hgd : DifferentiableOn ℂ g (ball c R)) (hgm : MapsTo g (ball c R) (closedBall (g c) R))
    (hgi : ¬ InjOn g (ball c R)) : ‖deriv g c‖ < 1

decls.name: TauCeti.poincare_defect_quotient
decls.doc:
**Value-level equality case of the infinitesimal Schwarz--Pick lemma.** The quotient built
from the Moebius derivative value `(1 - conj a * a) / (1 - conj a * z) ^ 2` and the Moebius
image `(z - a) / (1 - conj a * z)` collapses to the reciprocal Poincaré factor `1 / (1 - ‖z‖ ^ 2)`.
Both public isometry theorems below rewrite their derivative to this value and apply this
computation.
decls.title: Value-level equality case of the infinitesimal Schwarz--Pick lemma
decls.statement:
lemma poincare_defect_quotient {a : ℂ} (ha : ‖a‖ < 1) {z : ℂ} (hz : ‖z‖ < 1) :
    ‖(1 - (starRingEnd ℂ) a * a) / (1 - (starRingEnd ℂ) a * z) ^ 2‖
        / (1 - ‖(z - a) / (1 - (starRingEnd ℂ) a * z)‖ ^ 2)
      = 1 / (1 - ‖z‖ ^ 2)

decls.name: TauCeti.norm_deriv_div_one_sub_norm_sq_unitDiscStandardAutomorphismFormula_of_norm_lt_one
decls.doc:
**The standard disc automorphism is an infinitesimal isometry of the Poincaré metric.** For a
rotation factor `u` of norm `1` and `‖a‖ < 1` the automorphism `z ↦ u * (z - a) / (1 - conj a * z)`
attains equality in the infinitesimal Schwarz--Pick inequality at every disc point: its Poincaré
metric distortion is exactly `1`.  The rotation factor `u` does not change the distortion.
decls.title: The standard disc automorphism is an infinitesimal isometry of the Poincaré metric
decls.statement:
theorem norm_deriv_div_one_sub_norm_sq_unitDiscStandardAutomorphismFormula_of_norm_lt_one
    {u : ℂ} (hu : ‖u‖ = 1) {a : ℂ} (ha : ‖a‖ < 1) {z : ℂ} (hz : ‖z‖ < 1) :
    ‖deriv (fun ξ : ℂ => u * ((ξ - a) / (1 - (starRingEnd ℂ) a * ξ))) z‖
        / (1 - ‖u * ((z - a) / (1 - (starRingEnd ℂ) a * z))‖ ^ 2)
      = 1 / (1 - ‖z‖ ^ 2)

decls.name: TauCeti.norm_deriv_div_one_sub_norm_sq_unitDiscMoebiusFormula_of_norm_lt_one
decls.doc:
**The Moebius factor is an infinitesimal isometry of the Poincaré metric.** For `‖a‖ < 1`
the disc automorphism `z ↦ (z - a) / (1 - conj a * z)` attains equality in the infinitesimal
Schwarz--Pick inequality `norm_deriv_div_one_sub_norm_sq_le`: at every point of the open unit
disc its Poincaré metric distortion is exactly `1`.  This is the `u = 1` (no rotation) case of
`norm_deriv_div_one_sub_norm_sq_unitDiscStandardAutomorphismFormula_of_norm_lt_one`.
decls.title: The Moebius factor is an infinitesimal isometry of the Poincaré metric
decls.statement:
theorem norm_deriv_div_one_sub_norm_sq_unitDiscMoebiusFormula_of_norm_lt_one {a : ℂ}
    (ha : ‖a‖ < 1) {z : ℂ} (hz : ‖z‖ < 1) :
    ‖deriv (fun ξ : ℂ => (ξ - a) / (1 - (starRingEnd ℂ) a * ξ)) z‖
        / (1 - ‖(z - a) / (1 - (starRingEnd ℂ) a * z)‖ ^ 2)
      = 1 / (1 - ‖z‖ ^ 2)

decls.name: TauCeti.norm_deriv_div_one_sub_norm_sq_unitDiscStandardAutomorphismFormula_unitDisc
decls.doc:
Bundled unit-disc form of the automorphism Poincaré-isometry: for disc points `a z` the
standard automorphism formula centred at `a` has Poincaré metric distortion exactly `1` at `z`.
decls.statement:
theorem norm_deriv_div_one_sub_norm_sq_unitDiscStandardAutomorphismFormula_unitDisc
    (u : Circle) (a z : Complex.UnitDisc) :
    ‖deriv (fun ξ : ℂ => (u : ℂ) * (((ξ : ℂ) - (a : ℂ)) /
          (1 - (starRingEnd ℂ) (a : ℂ) * ξ))) (z : ℂ)‖
        / (1 - ‖(u : ℂ) * (((z : ℂ) - (a : ℂ)) /
          (1 - (starRingEnd ℂ) (a : ℂ) * (z : ℂ)))‖ ^ 2)
      = 1 / (1 - ‖(z : ℂ)‖ ^ 2)

decls.name: TauCeti.pseudoHyperbolicExpr_map_le
decls.doc:
The Schwarz--Pick contraction estimate for the pseudo-hyperbolic expression on the open unit
disc.
decls.statement:
theorem pseudoHyperbolicExpr_map_le {f : ℂ → ℂ}
    (hf : DifferentiableOn ℂ f (ball (0 : ℂ) 1))
    (hmaps : MapsTo f (ball (0 : ℂ) 1) (ball (0 : ℂ) 1))
    {z w : ℂ} (hz : z ∈ ball (0 : ℂ) 1) (hw : w ∈ ball (0 : ℂ) 1) :
    pseudoHyperbolicExpr (f z) (f w) ≤ pseudoHyperbolicExpr z w

decls.name: TauCeti.pseudoHyperbolicExpr_map_le_unitDisc
decls.doc: Bundled unit-disc form of the Schwarz--Pick contraction estimate.
decls.statement:
theorem pseudoHyperbolicExpr_map_le_unitDisc {f : ℂ → ℂ}
    (hf : DifferentiableOn ℂ f (ball (0 : ℂ) 1))
    (hmaps : MapsTo f (ball (0 : ℂ) 1) (ball (0 : ℂ) 1))
    (z w : Complex.UnitDisc) :
    pseudoHyperbolicExpr (f z) (f w) ≤ pseudoHyperbolicExpr (z : ℂ) (w : ℂ)

decls.name: TauCeti.norm_deriv_schwarzPickConjugate_at_zero
decls.doc:
**Chain rule for the infinitesimal Schwarz--Pick conjugate.** For the composite
`target ∘ f ∘ source` of two unit-disc Moebius factors around `f`, given the factor derivatives
`1 - conj z * z` (of `source` at `0`, where `source 0 = z`) and `1 / (1 - conj (f z) * f z)` (of
`target` at `f z`), the norm of the derivative of the composite at the origin equals the Poincaré
distortion `‖df‖ * (1 - ‖z‖ ^ 2) / (1 - ‖f z‖ ^ 2)`.
decls.title: Chain rule for the infinitesimal Schwarz--Pick conjugate
decls.statement:
lemma norm_deriv_schwarzPickConjugate_at_zero {source target f : ℂ → ℂ} {df z : ℂ}
    (hz : ‖z‖ ≤ 1) (hfz : ‖f z‖ ≤ 1)
    (hs : HasDerivAt source (1 - (starRingEnd ℂ) z * z) 0) (hsz : source 0 = z)
    (hf : HasDerivAt f df z)
    (ht : HasDerivAt target (1 / (1 - (starRingEnd ℂ) (f z) * f z)) (f z)) :
    ‖deriv (target ∘ f ∘ source) 0‖ = ‖df‖ * (1 - ‖z‖ ^ 2) / (1 - ‖f z‖ ^ 2)

decls.name: TauCeti.norm_deriv_div_one_sub_norm_sq_le
decls.doc:
**The infinitesimal Schwarz--Pick inequality.** A holomorphic self-map `f` of the open
unit disc contracts the Poincaré metric: at every point `z` of the disc,
`‖deriv f z‖ / (1 - ‖f z‖ ^ 2) ≤ 1 / (1 - ‖z‖ ^ 2)`.
decls.title: The infinitesimal Schwarz--Pick inequality
decls.statement:
theorem norm_deriv_div_one_sub_norm_sq_le {f : ℂ → ℂ}
    (hf : DifferentiableOn ℂ f (ball (0 : ℂ) 1))
    (hmaps : MapsTo f (ball (0 : ℂ) 1) (ball (0 : ℂ) 1))
    {z : ℂ} (hz : z ∈ ball (0 : ℂ) 1) :
    ‖deriv f z‖ / (1 - ‖f z‖ ^ 2) ≤ 1 / (1 - ‖z‖ ^ 2)

decls.name: TauCeti.norm_deriv_div_one_sub_norm_sq_le_unitDisc
decls.doc:
Bundled unit-disc form of the infinitesimal Schwarz--Pick inequality: a holomorphic
self-map `f` of the open unit disc contracts the Poincaré metric at every disc point `z`.
decls.statement:
theorem norm_deriv_div_one_sub_norm_sq_le_unitDisc {f : ℂ → ℂ}
    (hf : DifferentiableOn ℂ f (ball (0 : ℂ) 1))
    (hmaps : MapsTo f (ball (0 : ℂ) 1) (ball (0 : ℂ) 1))
    (z : Complex.UnitDisc) :
    ‖deriv f (z : ℂ)‖ / (1 - ‖f (z : ℂ)‖ ^ 2) ≤ 1 / (1 - ‖(z : ℂ)‖ ^ 2)

decls.name: TauCeti.pseudoHyperbolicExpr_map_eq
decls.doc:
**Schwarz--Pick equality.** A holomorphic self-map of the unit disc that admits a
holomorphic self-map left inverse preserves the pseudo-hyperbolic expression: the Schwarz--Pick
contraction, applied to the map and to its inverse, forces equality.
decls.title: Schwarz--Pick equality
decls.statement:
theorem pseudoHyperbolicExpr_map_eq {f g : ℂ → ℂ}
    (hf : DifferentiableOn ℂ f (ball (0 : ℂ) 1)) (hfmaps : MapsTo f (ball 0 1) (ball 0 1))
    (hg : DifferentiableOn ℂ g (ball (0 : ℂ) 1)) (hgmaps : MapsTo g (ball 0 1) (ball 0 1))
    (hgf : LeftInvOn g f (ball 0 1))
    {z w : ℂ} (hz : z ∈ ball (0 : ℂ) 1) (hw : w ∈ ball (0 : ℂ) 1) :
    pseudoHyperbolicExpr (f z) (f w) = pseudoHyperbolicExpr z w

decls.name: TauCeti.pseudoHyperbolicExpr_unitDiscMoebiusFormula_of_norm_lt_one
decls.doc:
**Moebius invariance (scalar form).** The Moebius factor `z ↦ (z - a) / (1 - conj a * z)`
with `‖a‖ < 1` is a pseudo-hyperbolic isometry of the open unit disc.
decls.title: Moebius invariance (scalar form)
decls.statement:
theorem pseudoHyperbolicExpr_unitDiscMoebiusFormula_of_norm_lt_one {a : ℂ} (ha : ‖a‖ < 1)
    {z w : ℂ} (hz : z ∈ ball (0 : ℂ) 1) (hw : w ∈ ball (0 : ℂ) 1) :
    pseudoHyperbolicExpr ((z - a) / (1 - (starRingEnd ℂ) a * z))
        ((w - a) / (1 - (starRingEnd ℂ) a * w))
      = pseudoHyperbolicExpr z w

decls.name: TauCeti.pseudoHyperbolicExpr_unitDiscMoebius
decls.doc:
**Moebius invariance (bundled form).** The bundled unit-disc Moebius factor
`unitDiscMoebius a` preserves the pseudo-hyperbolic expression.
decls.title: Moebius invariance (bundled form)
decls.statement:
theorem pseudoHyperbolicExpr_unitDiscMoebius (a z w : Complex.UnitDisc) :
    pseudoHyperbolicExpr (((z : ℂ) - (a : ℂ)) / (1 - (starRingEnd ℂ) (a : ℂ) * (z : ℂ)))
        (((w : ℂ) - (a : ℂ)) / (1 - (starRingEnd ℂ) (a : ℂ) * (w : ℂ)))
      = pseudoHyperbolicExpr (z : ℂ) (w : ℂ)

decls.name: TauCeti.pseudoHyperbolicExpr_unitDiscStandardAutomorphismEquiv
decls.doc:
**Standard automorphism invariance.** Every standard disc automorphism bundled as
`unitDiscStandardAutomorphismEquiv u a` preserves the pseudo-hyperbolic expression.
decls.title: Standard automorphism invariance
decls.statement:
theorem pseudoHyperbolicExpr_unitDiscStandardAutomorphismEquiv
    (u : Circle) (a z w : Complex.UnitDisc) :
    pseudoHyperbolicExpr (unitDiscStandardAutomorphismEquiv u a z : ℂ)
        (unitDiscStandardAutomorphismEquiv u a w : ℂ)
      = pseudoHyperbolicExpr (z : ℂ) (w : ℂ)

decls.name: TauCeti.unitDiscStandardAutomorphismEquiv
decls.doc:
The standard automorphism of the complex unit disc
`z ↦ u * (z - a) / (1 - conj a * z)`.

The center-removing factor is `unitDiscMoebiusEquiv a`; the circle element `u` supplies the
rotation factor in the usual classification formula for disc automorphisms.
decls.statement:
def unitDiscStandardAutomorphismEquiv (u : Circle) (a : Complex.UnitDisc) :
    Complex.UnitDisc ≃ Complex.UnitDisc

decls.name: TauCeti.unitDiscStandardAutomorphismEquiv_apply
decls.doc: The standard automorphism applies by first sending `a` to `0`, then rotating.
decls.statement:
lemma unitDiscStandardAutomorphismEquiv_apply (u : Circle) (a z : Complex.UnitDisc) :
    unitDiscStandardAutomorphismEquiv u a z = u • unitDiscMoebius a z

decls.name: TauCeti.coe_unitDiscStandardAutomorphismEquiv_apply
decls.doc: The scalar formula for the standard disc automorphism.
decls.statement:
lemma coe_unitDiscStandardAutomorphismEquiv_apply (u : Circle) (a z : Complex.UnitDisc) :
    (unitDiscStandardAutomorphismEquiv u a z : ℂ) =
      (u : ℂ) *
        (((z : ℂ) - (a : ℂ)) / (1 - (starRingEnd ℂ) (a : ℂ) * (z : ℂ)))

decls.name: TauCeti.unitDiscStandardAutomorphismEquiv_zero
decls.doc: With zero center, the standard automorphism is just rotation.
decls.statement:
lemma unitDiscStandardAutomorphismEquiv_zero (u : Circle) :
    unitDiscStandardAutomorphismEquiv u 0 =
      (MulAction.toPerm u : Equiv.Perm Complex.UnitDisc)

decls.name: TauCeti.unitDiscStandardAutomorphismEquiv_one
decls.doc: With unit rotation factor, the standard automorphism is the Moebius equivalence.
decls.statement:
lemma unitDiscStandardAutomorphismEquiv_one (a : Complex.UnitDisc) :
    unitDiscStandardAutomorphismEquiv 1 a = unitDiscMoebiusEquiv a

decls.name: TauCeti.unitDiscStandardAutomorphismEquiv_self
decls.doc: The standard automorphism sends its center to zero.
decls.statement:
lemma unitDiscStandardAutomorphismEquiv_self (u : Circle) (a : Complex.UnitDisc) :
    unitDiscStandardAutomorphismEquiv u a a = 0

decls.name: TauCeti.unitDiscStandardAutomorphismEquiv_apply_zero
decls.doc: The standard automorphism sends zero to `-u * a`.
decls.statement:
lemma unitDiscStandardAutomorphismEquiv_apply_zero (u : Circle) (a : Complex.UnitDisc) :
    unitDiscStandardAutomorphismEquiv u a 0 = u • (-a)

decls.name: TauCeti.norm_unitDiscStandardAutomorphismEquiv
decls.doc: The norm of a standard automorphism value is the pseudo-hyperbolic expression.
decls.statement:
lemma norm_unitDiscStandardAutomorphismEquiv (u : Circle) (a z : Complex.UnitDisc) :
    ‖(unitDiscStandardAutomorphismEquiv u a z : ℂ)‖ = pseudoHyperbolicExpr (z : ℂ) (a : ℂ)

decls.name: TauCeti.unitDiscStandardAutomorphismEquiv_eq_zero_iff
decls.doc: A standard disc automorphism vanishes exactly at its center.
decls.statement:
lemma unitDiscStandardAutomorphismEquiv_eq_zero_iff (u : Circle) (a z : Complex.UnitDisc) :
    unitDiscStandardAutomorphismEquiv u a z = 0 ↔ z = a

decls.name: TauCeti.differentiableOn_unitDiscStandardAutomorphismFormula_of_norm_lt_one
decls.doc: The scalar formula of a standard automorphism is holomorphic on the unit disc.
decls.statement:
lemma differentiableOn_unitDiscStandardAutomorphismFormula_of_norm_lt_one
    (u : ℂ) {a : ℂ} (ha : ‖a‖ < 1) :
    DifferentiableOn ℂ
      (fun z : ℂ =>
        u * ((z - a) / (1 - (starRingEnd ℂ) a * z)))
      (Metric.ball (0 : ℂ) 1)

decls.name: TauCeti.differentiableOn_unitDiscStandardAutomorphismFormula
decls.doc: The scalar formula of the standard automorphism is holomorphic on the unit disc.
decls.statement:
lemma differentiableOn_unitDiscStandardAutomorphismFormula (u : Circle) (a : Complex.UnitDisc) :
    DifferentiableOn ℂ
      (fun z : ℂ =>
        (u : ℂ) *
          ((z - (a : ℂ)) / (1 - (starRingEnd ℂ) (a : ℂ) * z)))
      (Metric.ball (0 : ℂ) 1)

decls.name: TauCeti.unitDiscStandardAutomorphismEquiv_symm
decls.doc:
The inverse of a standard automorphism as a composition of the inverse rotation and
the inverse Moebius factor.
decls.statement:
lemma unitDiscStandardAutomorphismEquiv_symm (u : Circle) (a : Complex.UnitDisc) :
    (unitDiscStandardAutomorphismEquiv u a).symm =
      (MulAction.toPerm u⁻¹ : Equiv.Perm Complex.UnitDisc).trans (unitDiscMoebiusEquiv (-a))

decls.name: TauCeti.exists_forall_unitDisc_eq_unitDiscStandardAutomorphismEquiv
decls.doc:
**Classification of holomorphic disc automorphisms.** A holomorphic self-map `f` of the open
unit disc with a holomorphic two-sided inverse `g` has the standard form. Its center is `g 0`,
and its rotation factor lies on the unit circle.
decls.title: Classification of holomorphic disc automorphisms
decls.statement:
theorem exists_forall_unitDisc_eq_unitDiscStandardAutomorphismEquiv
    (hf : DifferentiableOn ℂ f (ball (0 : ℂ) 1))
    (hg : DifferentiableOn ℂ g (ball (0 : ℂ) 1))
    (hfmaps : MapsTo f (ball (0 : ℂ) 1) (ball (0 : ℂ) 1))
    (hgmaps : MapsTo g (ball (0 : ℂ) 1) (ball (0 : ℂ) 1))
    (hgf : LeftInvOn g f (ball (0 : ℂ) 1))
    (hfg : RightInvOn g f (ball (0 : ℂ) 1)) :
    ∃ (u : Circle) (a : Complex.UnitDisc), (a : ℂ) = g 0 ∧
      ∀ z : Complex.UnitDisc, f z = (unitDiscStandardAutomorphismEquiv u a z : ℂ)

decls.name: TauCeti.IsHolomorphicUnitDiscPerm
decls.doc:
A permutation of the complex unit disc is *holomorphic* when it is the restriction of a
function `ℂ → ℂ` that is holomorphic on the open unit ball.

Holomorphy of a map of the bundled disc is phrased through a scalar representative, matching the
generality bar of the conformal-mapping roadmap (everything is stated for `f : ℂ → ℂ`) and the
hypotheses of `exists_forall_unitDisc_eq_unitDiscStandardAutomorphismEquiv`.
decls.statement: def IsHolomorphicUnitDiscPerm (e : Equiv.Perm Complex.UnitDisc) : Prop

decls.name: TauCeti.mapsTo_ball_of_forall_unitDisc_coe_eq
decls.doc: A scalar representative of a self-map of the disc maps the open unit ball into itself.

decls.name: TauCeti.unitDiscAut
decls.doc:
**The automorphism group of the unit disc.** A permutation of `Complex.UnitDisc` is a
holomorphic automorphism when both it and its inverse extend to functions that are holomorphic
on the open unit ball.
decls.title: The automorphism group of the unit disc
decls.statement: def unitDiscAut : Subgroup (Equiv.Perm Complex.UnitDisc)

decls.name: TauCeti.mem_unitDiscAut
decls.statement:
lemma mem_unitDiscAut {e : Equiv.Perm Complex.UnitDisc} :
    e ∈ unitDiscAut ↔ IsHolomorphicUnitDiscPerm e ∧ IsHolomorphicUnitDiscPerm e.symm

decls.name: TauCeti.unitDiscStandardAutomorphismEquiv_symm_eq
decls.doc:
The inverse of a standard disc automorphism is again one: inverting `z ↦ u * (z - a) /
(1 - conj a * z)` replaces the rotation `u` by `u⁻¹` and the centre `a` by `u • (-a)`, the image
of the origin under the original automorphism.  (The inverse itself sends `0` to `a`, since the
original sends `a` to `0`.)
decls.statement:
lemma unitDiscStandardAutomorphismEquiv_symm_eq (u : Circle) (a : Complex.UnitDisc) :
    (unitDiscStandardAutomorphismEquiv u a).symm =
      unitDiscStandardAutomorphismEquiv u⁻¹ (u • (-a))

decls.name: TauCeti.isHolomorphicUnitDiscPerm_unitDiscStandardAutomorphismEquiv
decls.doc: A standard disc automorphism is holomorphic.
decls.statement:
lemma isHolomorphicUnitDiscPerm_unitDiscStandardAutomorphismEquiv
    (u : Circle) (a : Complex.UnitDisc) :
    IsHolomorphicUnitDiscPerm (unitDiscStandardAutomorphismEquiv u a)

decls.name: TauCeti.unitDiscStandardAutomorphismEquiv_mem_unitDiscAut
decls.doc: Every standard disc automorphism is a holomorphic automorphism of the disc.
decls.statement:
lemma unitDiscStandardAutomorphismEquiv_mem_unitDiscAut (u : Circle) (a : Complex.UnitDisc) :
    unitDiscStandardAutomorphismEquiv u a ∈ unitDiscAut

decls.name: TauCeti.mem_unitDiscAut_iff
decls.doc:
**`Aut(𝔻) = {e^{iθ}(z − a)/(1 − āz)}`.** A permutation of the complex unit disc is a
holomorphic automorphism exactly when it is a standard automorphism.

The forward direction is the classification theorem
`exists_forall_unitDisc_eq_unitDiscStandardAutomorphismEquiv`, which rests on the Schwarz lemma;
the converse is the holomorphy of the standard formula and of its inverse.
decls.title: `Aut(𝔻) = {e^{iθ}(z − a)/(1 − āz)}`
decls.statement:
theorem mem_unitDiscAut_iff {e : Equiv.Perm Complex.UnitDisc} :
    e ∈ unitDiscAut ↔
      ∃ (u : Circle) (a : Complex.UnitDisc), e = unitDiscStandardAutomorphismEquiv u a

decls.name: TauCeti.coe_unitDiscAut
decls.doc:
The underlying set of `Aut(𝔻)` is the range of the standard parametrisation by a rotation
and a centre.
decls.statement:
theorem coe_unitDiscAut :
    (unitDiscAut : Set (Equiv.Perm Complex.UnitDisc)) =
      range fun p : Circle × Complex.UnitDisc => unitDiscStandardAutomorphismEquiv p.1 p.2

decls.name: TauCeti.exists_mul_eq_unitDiscStandardAutomorphismEquiv
decls.doc:
The standard disc automorphisms are closed under composition.

This is a corollary of the group structure and the classification: no computation with the
composite of two Moebius factors is needed.
decls.statement:
theorem exists_mul_eq_unitDiscStandardAutomorphismEquiv
    (u₁ u₂ : Circle) (a₁ a₂ : Complex.UnitDisc) :
    ∃ (u : Circle) (a : Complex.UnitDisc),
      unitDiscStandardAutomorphismEquiv u₁ a₁ * unitDiscStandardAutomorphismEquiv u₂ a₂ =
        unitDiscStandardAutomorphismEquiv u a

decls.name: TauCeti.unitDiscAut.isPretransitive
decls.doc:
**`Aut(𝔻)` acts transitively on the disc.** Any point of the disc can be moved to any other
by a holomorphic automorphism, namely the composite of the Moebius factor centred at the source
with the inverse of the one centred at the target.
decls.title: `Aut(𝔻)` acts transitively on the disc
decls.statement:
instance unitDiscAut.isPretransitive :
    MulAction.IsPretransitive unitDiscAut Complex.UnitDisc

decls.name: TauCeti.exists_mem_unitDiscAut_apply_eq
decls.doc: Transitivity of `Aut(𝔻)` on the disc, phrased for the ambient permutations.
decls.statement:
theorem exists_mem_unitDiscAut_apply_eq (z w : Complex.UnitDisc) :
    ∃ e ∈ unitDiscAut, e z = w

decls.name: TauCeti.unitDiscRotation
decls.doc:
The rotations `z ↦ u * z`, as a subgroup of the permutations of the unit disc.  It is the
image of `Circle` under its multiplicative action on the disc.
decls.statement: def unitDiscRotation : Subgroup (Equiv.Perm Complex.UnitDisc)

decls.name: TauCeti.unitDiscStandardAutomorphismEquiv_zero_mem_unitDiscRotation
decls.statement:
lemma unitDiscStandardAutomorphismEquiv_zero_mem_unitDiscRotation (u : Circle) :
    unitDiscStandardAutomorphismEquiv u 0 ∈ unitDiscRotation

decls.name: TauCeti.mem_unitDiscRotation_iff
decls.doc:
**The stabiliser of the origin in `Aut(𝔻)` is the rotation group.** A permutation of the disc
is a rotation exactly when it is a holomorphic automorphism fixing the origin.

The forward implication is immediate; the converse is the classification, which forces the centre
of a standard automorphism fixing `0` to be `0`.  This is the group-theoretic form of the
rigidity statement behind the Schwarz lemma.
decls.title: The stabiliser of the origin in `Aut(𝔻)` is the rotation group
decls.statement:
theorem mem_unitDiscRotation_iff {e : Equiv.Perm Complex.UnitDisc} :
    e ∈ unitDiscRotation ↔ e ∈ unitDiscAut ∧ e 0 = 0

decls.name: TauCeti.unitDiscRotation_le_unitDiscAut
decls.doc: The rotations are holomorphic automorphisms of the disc.
decls.statement: theorem unitDiscRotation_le_unitDiscAut : unitDiscRotation ≤ unitDiscAut

decls.name: TauCeti.stabilizer_zero_eq_unitDiscRotation_subgroupOf
decls.doc:
**The stabiliser of the origin in `Aut(𝔻)` is the rotation group**, as subgroups of `Aut(𝔻)`
itself: the rotations sit inside `Aut(𝔻)` as `unitDiscRotation.subgroupOf unitDiscAut`, and that
subgroup is exactly `MulAction.stabilizer unitDiscAut 0`.
decls.title: The stabiliser of the origin in `Aut(𝔻)` is the rotation group
decls.statement:
theorem stabilizer_zero_eq_unitDiscRotation_subgroupOf :
    MulAction.stabilizer unitDiscAut (0 : Complex.UnitDisc) =
      unitDiscRotation.subgroupOf unitDiscAut

decls.name: TauCeti.norm_map_of_leftInvOn_ball_of_map_zero
decls.doc:
A holomorphic self-map of the open unit disc fixing the origin and admitting a holomorphic left
inverse that is itself a self-map of the disc preserves the modulus: `‖f z‖ = ‖z‖` for every
`z` in the disc.

This is the `w = 0` case of the Schwarz--Pick equality `pseudoHyperbolicExpr_map_eq`, where the
pseudo-hyperbolic expression to the origin is just the norm.
decls.statement:
theorem norm_map_of_leftInvOn_ball_of_map_zero
    (hf : DifferentiableOn ℂ f (ball (0 : ℂ) 1))
    (hg : DifferentiableOn ℂ g (ball (0 : ℂ) 1))
    (hfmaps : MapsTo f (ball (0 : ℂ) 1) (ball (0 : ℂ) 1))
    (hgmaps : MapsTo g (ball (0 : ℂ) 1) (ball (0 : ℂ) 1))
    (hgf : ∀ z ∈ ball (0 : ℂ) 1, g (f z) = z) (hf0 : f 0 = 0)
    {z : ℂ} (hz : z ∈ ball (0 : ℂ) 1) : ‖f z‖ = ‖z‖

decls.name: TauCeti.exists_eqOn_const_mul_of_leftInvOn_ball_of_map_zero
decls.doc:
**Rotation rigidity for the unit disc.** A holomorphic self-map `f` of the open unit disc with a
holomorphic left inverse `g` that is also a self-map of the disc, fixing the origin, is a
rotation: there is a constant `c` of modulus one with `f z = c * z` throughout the disc.
decls.title: Rotation rigidity for the unit disc
decls.statement:
theorem exists_eqOn_const_mul_of_leftInvOn_ball_of_map_zero
    (hf : DifferentiableOn ℂ f (ball (0 : ℂ) 1))
    (hg : DifferentiableOn ℂ g (ball (0 : ℂ) 1))
    (hfmaps : MapsTo f (ball (0 : ℂ) 1) (ball (0 : ℂ) 1))
    (hgmaps : MapsTo g (ball (0 : ℂ) 1) (ball (0 : ℂ) 1))
    (hgf : ∀ z ∈ ball (0 : ℂ) 1, g (f z) = z) (hf0 : f 0 = 0) :
    ∃ c : ℂ, ‖c‖ = 1 ∧ EqOn f (fun z => c * z) (ball (0 : ℂ) 1)

decls.name: TauCeti.eqOn_deriv_zero_mul_of_leftInvOn_ball_of_map_zero
decls.doc:
The rotation factor of an origin-fixing self-map of the disc with a holomorphic self-map left
inverse is its derivative at the origin: with the hypotheses of
`exists_eqOn_const_mul_of_leftInvOn_ball_of_map_zero`, the map equals `z ↦ deriv f 0 * z` on the
disc, and `‖deriv f 0‖ = 1`.
decls.statement:
theorem eqOn_deriv_zero_mul_of_leftInvOn_ball_of_map_zero
    (hf : DifferentiableOn ℂ f (ball (0 : ℂ) 1))
    (hg : DifferentiableOn ℂ g (ball (0 : ℂ) 1))
    (hfmaps : MapsTo f (ball (0 : ℂ) 1) (ball (0 : ℂ) 1))
    (hgmaps : MapsTo g (ball (0 : ℂ) 1) (ball (0 : ℂ) 1))
    (hgf : ∀ z ∈ ball (0 : ℂ) 1, g (f z) = z) (hf0 : f 0 = 0) :
    ‖deriv f 0‖ = 1 ∧ EqOn f (fun z => deriv f 0 * z) (ball (0 : ℂ) 1)

decls.name: TauCeti.eqOn_id_of_leftInvOn_ball_of_map_zero_of_deriv_zero_eq_one
decls.doc:
**Uniqueness of the identity.** An origin-fixing holomorphic self-map of the unit disc with a
holomorphic self-map left inverse, whose derivative at the origin is `1`, is the identity on the
disc.
decls.title: Uniqueness of the identity
decls.statement:
theorem eqOn_id_of_leftInvOn_ball_of_map_zero_of_deriv_zero_eq_one
    (hf : DifferentiableOn ℂ f (ball (0 : ℂ) 1))
    (hg : DifferentiableOn ℂ g (ball (0 : ℂ) 1))
    (hfmaps : MapsTo f (ball (0 : ℂ) 1) (ball (0 : ℂ) 1))
    (hgmaps : MapsTo g (ball (0 : ℂ) 1) (ball (0 : ℂ) 1))
    (hgf : ∀ z ∈ ball (0 : ℂ) 1, g (f z) = z) (hf0 : f 0 = 0)
    (hderiv : deriv f 0 = 1) : EqOn f id (ball (0 : ℂ) 1)

decls.name: TauCeti.unitDiscStandardAutomorphismHomeomorph
decls.doc:
The standard automorphism of the complex unit disc, bundled as a homeomorphism.

It is the composition of the Moebius homeomorphism sending `a` to `0` with the fixed
circle rotation by `u`.
decls.statement:
def unitDiscStandardAutomorphismHomeomorph
    (u : Circle) (a : Complex.UnitDisc) : Complex.UnitDisc ≃ₜ Complex.UnitDisc

decls.name: TauCeti.unitDiscStandardAutomorphismHomeomorph_apply
decls.doc: The standard automorphism homeomorphism applies by the existing equivalence formula.
decls.statement:
lemma unitDiscStandardAutomorphismHomeomorph_apply
    (u : Circle) (a z : Complex.UnitDisc) :
    unitDiscStandardAutomorphismHomeomorph u a z =
      unitDiscStandardAutomorphismEquiv u a z

decls.name: TauCeti.unitDiscStandardAutomorphismHomeomorph_toEquiv
decls.doc: The underlying equivalence of the standard automorphism homeomorphism is the existing one.
decls.statement:
lemma unitDiscStandardAutomorphismHomeomorph_toEquiv
    (u : Circle) (a : Complex.UnitDisc) :
    (unitDiscStandardAutomorphismHomeomorph u a).toEquiv =
      unitDiscStandardAutomorphismEquiv u a

decls.name: TauCeti.unitDiscStandardAutomorphismHomeomorph_symm
decls.doc:
The inverse standard automorphism homeomorphism is inverse rotation followed by the
inverse Moebius homeomorphism.
decls.statement:
lemma unitDiscStandardAutomorphismHomeomorph_symm
    (u : Circle) (a : Complex.UnitDisc) :
    (unitDiscStandardAutomorphismHomeomorph u a).symm =
      (Homeomorph.smul u⁻¹).trans (unitDiscMoebiusHomeomorph (-a))

decls.name: TauCeti.coe_unitDiscStandardAutomorphismHomeomorph_apply
decls.doc: The scalar formula for the standard disc-automorphism homeomorphism.
decls.statement:
lemma coe_unitDiscStandardAutomorphismHomeomorph_apply
    (u : Circle) (a z : Complex.UnitDisc) :
    (unitDiscStandardAutomorphismHomeomorph u a z : ℂ) =
      (u : ℂ) *
        (((z : ℂ) - (a : ℂ)) / (1 - (starRingEnd ℂ) (a : ℂ) * (z : ℂ)))

decls.name: TauCeti.unitDiscStandardAutomorphismHomeomorph_zero
decls.doc: With zero center, the standard automorphism homeomorphism is just rotation.
decls.statement:
lemma unitDiscStandardAutomorphismHomeomorph_zero (u : Circle) :
    unitDiscStandardAutomorphismHomeomorph u 0 =
      Homeomorph.smul u

decls.name: TauCeti.unitDiscStandardAutomorphismHomeomorph_one
decls.doc: With unit rotation factor, the standard automorphism homeomorphism is the Moebius one.
decls.statement:
lemma unitDiscStandardAutomorphismHomeomorph_one (a : Complex.UnitDisc) :
    unitDiscStandardAutomorphismHomeomorph 1 a = unitDiscMoebiusHomeomorph a

decls.name: TauCeti.eqOn_of_subseq_limits
decls.doc:
Two locally uniform subsequential limits agree on a set where the original sequence converges
pointwise.
decls.statement:
theorem eqOn_of_subseq_limits
    (hAΩ : A ⊆ Ω)
    (hpoint : ∀ z ∈ A, ∃ w, Tendsto (fun n => F n z) atTop (𝓝 w))
    {φ ψ : ℕ → ℕ} (hφ : Tendsto φ atTop atTop) (hψ : Tendsto ψ atTop atTop)
    {g q : ℂ → ℂ}
    (hg : TendstoLocallyUniformlyOn (fun n => F (φ n)) g atTop Ω)
    (hq : TendstoLocallyUniformlyOn (fun n => F (ψ n)) q atTop Ω) :
    A.EqOn g q

decls.name: TauCeti.vitali
decls.doc:
**Vitali's convergence theorem.** Let `Ω` be an open preconnected subset of `ℂ`. A locally
bounded sequence of holomorphic functions on `Ω` which converges pointwise on a subset `A ⊆ Ω`
having an accumulation point in `Ω` converges locally uniformly on `Ω` to a holomorphic function.

The pointwise limit on `A` need not be supplied: its existence is enough to determine the
holomorphic limit uniquely.
decls.title: Vitali's convergence theorem
decls.statement:
theorem vitali (hΩ : IsOpen Ω) (hconn : IsPreconnected Ω)
    (hF : ∀ n, DifferentiableOn ℂ (F n) Ω) (hb : IsLocallyBoundedOn F Ω)
    (hAΩ : A ⊆ Ω) {z₀ : ℂ} (hz₀ : z₀ ∈ Ω) (hacc : AccPt z₀ (𝓟 A))
    (hpoint : ∀ z ∈ A, ∃ w, Tendsto (fun n => F n z) atTop (𝓝 w)) :
    ∃ g : ℂ → ℂ, DifferentiableOn ℂ g Ω ∧ TendstoLocallyUniformlyOn F g atTop Ω

decls.name: TauCeti.vitali_of_tendsto
decls.doc:
**Vitali's theorem with prescribed pointwise values.** Under the hypotheses of `vitali`, if
the sequence converges pointwise on `A` to a specified function `g`, its locally uniform
holomorphic limit agrees with `g` throughout `A`.

No regularity of `g` away from `A` is assumed or concluded.
decls.title: Vitali's theorem with prescribed pointwise values
decls.statement:
theorem vitali_of_tendsto (hΩ : IsOpen Ω) (hconn : IsPreconnected Ω)
    (hF : ∀ n, DifferentiableOn ℂ (F n) Ω) (hb : IsLocallyBoundedOn F Ω)
    (hAΩ : A ⊆ Ω) {z₀ : ℂ} (hz₀ : z₀ ∈ Ω) (hacc : AccPt z₀ (𝓟 A))
    {g : ℂ → ℂ} (hpoint : ∀ z ∈ A, Tendsto (fun n => F n z) atTop (𝓝 (g z))) :
    ∃ q : ℂ → ℂ, DifferentiableOn ℂ q Ω ∧ A.EqOn q g ∧
      TendstoLocallyUniformlyOn F q atTop Ω

decls.name: TauCeti.exists_pos_le_norm_of_mem_sphere
decls.doc:
A continuous zero-free function on a sphere is bounded below there by a positive constant,
compactness of the sphere supplying the bound.

No hypothesis on the radius. At `ρ = 0` the sphere is the set of points at zero distance from
`a` — the single point `a` when `E` is a metric space, but not in general, since the domain is
only assumed pseudometric. For `ρ < 0` it is empty, nothing is attained, and the bound holds
vacuously.
decls.statement:
theorem exists_pos_le_norm_of_mem_sphere {E F : Type*} [PseudoMetricSpace E] [ProperSpace E]
    [NormedAddCommGroup F] {f : E → F} {a : E} {ρ : ℝ}
    (hcont : ContinuousOn f (sphere a ρ)) (hne : ∀ z ∈ sphere a ρ, f z ≠ 0) :
    ∃ δ > 0, ∀ z ∈ sphere a ρ, δ ≤ ‖f z‖

decls.name: TauCeti.analyticOrderAt_ne_top_of_forall_ne_zero
decls.doc:
**A function with no zero off the centre does not vanish identically there.** If `f` is
nonzero at every point of an open ball of positive radius other than its centre `a`, then `f`
has finite analytic order at `a`: were the order `⊤`, `f` would vanish on a whole
neighbourhood of `a`, and that neighbourhood meets the ball away from `a`.

Nothing is assumed about `f a`, which may or may not be zero, nor about analyticity of `f`.
decls.title: A function with no zero off the centre does not vanish identically there
decls.statement:
theorem analyticOrderAt_ne_top_of_forall_ne_zero {f : ℂ → ℂ} {a : ℂ} {ρ : ℝ} (hρ : 0 < ρ)
    (hzf : ∀ z ∈ ball a ρ, z ≠ a → f z ≠ 0) : analyticOrderAt f a ≠ ⊤

decls.name: TauCeti.analyticOrderAt_ne_top_of_zeros_subset
decls.doc:
**A function whose zeros are confined to a finite set has finite order.** If every zero of `f`
in an open set `U` lies in a finite set `S`, then `f` does not vanish identically near any point of
`U`, so `analyticOrderAt f z ≠ ⊤` there.

The point `z` itself is allowed to be a zero — indeed to lie in `S` — since vanishing identically
near `z` would force a whole punctured neighbourhood of zeros, of which all but finitely many are
outside `S`. This is the finite-set form of
`TauCeti.analyticOrderAt_ne_top_of_forall_ne_zero`, and reduces to it on a small enough ball.
decls.title: A function whose zeros are confined to a finite set has finite order

decls.name: TauCeti.Complex.UnitDisc.circle_smul_zero
decls.doc:
Rotating the disc origin by a circle element fixes it. This is the `smul_zero`
normalization for Mathlib's `Circle` action on `Complex.UnitDisc`, which is a bare
`MulAction` and so does not get the generic `smul_zero` simp lemma.
decls.statement: lemma circle_smul_zero (u : Circle) : u • (0 : _root_.Complex.UnitDisc) = 0

decls.name: TauCeti.Complex.UnitDisc.circle_smul_eq_zero_iff
decls.doc:
A circle rotation of a disc point vanishes exactly when the point does. This is the
`smul_eq_zero` normalization for Mathlib's `Circle` action on `Complex.UnitDisc`.
decls.statement:
lemma circle_smul_eq_zero_iff (u : Circle) {z : _root_.Complex.UnitDisc} :
    u • z = 0 ↔ z = 0

decls.name: TauCeti.Complex.UnitDisc.isCompact_setOf_norm_le
decls.doc:
The set of unit-disc points of Euclidean norm at most `ρ < 1` is compact: it is carried by
the embedding into `ℂ` onto the closed Euclidean ball of radius `ρ`, which the hypothesis
`ρ < 1` places inside the open disc.
decls.statement:
lemma isCompact_setOf_norm_le {ρ : ℝ} (hρ : ρ < 1) :
    IsCompact {z : _root_.Complex.UnitDisc | ‖(z : ℂ)‖ ≤ ρ}

decls.name: TauCeti.continuous_circle_smul_unitDisc
decls.doc: A fixed circle rotation is continuous on the bundled open disc.
decls.statement:
lemma continuous_circle_smul_unitDisc (u : Circle) :
    Continuous fun z : Complex.UnitDisc => u • z

decls.name: TauCeti.instContinuousConstSMulCircleUnitDisc
decls.doc: Circle rotations act continuously on the bundled open unit disc.
decls.statement:
instance instContinuousConstSMulCircleUnitDisc :
    ContinuousConstSMul Circle Complex.UnitDisc

decls.name: TauCeti.analyticOrderNatAt_le_finsum_ball
decls.doc:
The order of vanishing at a single point of the open disc is at most the total zero count.
Both sides read `0` at a point of infinite order, so the bound is trivially true there too.

The finiteness the sum needs is `MeromorphicOn.divisor_ball_support_finite`, transported along
`TauCeti.Contour.divisor_eq_analyticOrderNatAt`.
decls.statement:
theorem analyticOrderNatAt_le_finsum_ball (hf : AnalyticOnNhd ℂ f (closedBall c R))
    {z₀ : ℂ} (hz₀ : z₀ ∈ ball c R) :
    analyticOrderNatAt f z₀ ≤ ∑ᶠ z ∈ ball c R, analyticOrderNatAt f z

decls.name: TauCeti.finsum_analyticOrderNatAt_ball_eq_zero_of_forall_ne_zero
decls.doc: A function holomorphic and zero-free on the open disc has zero count `0` there.
decls.statement:
theorem finsum_analyticOrderNatAt_ball_eq_zero_of_forall_ne_zero
    (hf : AnalyticOnNhd ℂ f (ball c R)) (hne : ∀ z ∈ ball c R, f z ≠ 0) :
    (∑ᶠ z ∈ ball c R, analyticOrderNatAt f z) = 0

decls.name: TauCeti.finsum_analyticOrderNatAt_ball_eq_zero_iff
decls.doc:
**The zero count detects zeros.** For `f` holomorphic on `closedBall c R` and nonvanishing at
*some* point of that closed disc, the count `∑ᶠ z ∈ ball c R, analyticOrderNatAt f z` vanishes
precisely when `f` has no zero in the open disc.

The nontrivial direction is that a zero contributes a *nonzero* order. That fails without a
hypothesis of this kind: `analyticOrderNatAt` sends a point of infinite order to `0`, so the
identically zero function has count `0` while vanishing everywhere. A single point of
nonvanishing rules that out, the closed disc being preconnected.
decls.title: The zero count detects zeros
decls.statement:
theorem finsum_analyticOrderNatAt_ball_eq_zero_iff (hf : AnalyticOnNhd ℂ f (closedBall c R))
    (hne : ∃ z ∈ closedBall c R, f z ≠ 0) :
    (∑ᶠ z ∈ ball c R, analyticOrderNatAt f z) = 0 ↔ ∀ z ∈ ball c R, f z ≠ 0

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.integral_comp_mul_eq_sub_of_hasDerivAt
decls.doc:
**FTC along a contour, explicit-velocity form.** If `γ' t` is the derivative of the curve
`γ` and `G' = g` at the points `γ t`, then the contour integral of `g` along `γ` is the endpoint
difference `G (γ b) - G (γ a)`. The integrability hypothesis is stated directly on the contour
integrand, so this lemma can be used with any regularity package that supplies it.
decls.title: FTC along a contour, explicit-velocity form
decls.statement:
theorem integral_comp_mul_eq_sub_of_hasDerivAt
    (hcont : ContinuousOn (G ∘ γ) (Set.uIcc a b))
    (hγ : ∀ t ∈ Set.Ioo (min a b) (max a b), HasDerivAt γ (γ' t) t)
    (hG : ∀ t ∈ Set.Ioo (min a b) (max a b), HasDerivAt G (g (γ t)) (γ t))
    (hint : IntervalIntegrable (fun t => g (γ t) * γ' t) volume a b) :
    ∫ t in a..b, g (γ t) * γ' t = G (γ b) - G (γ a)

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.integral_comp_mul_deriv_eq_sub_of_hasDerivAt
decls.doc:
**FTC along a contour, `deriv` form.** If `G' = g` along the image of a differentiable curve,
then the contour integral written with `deriv γ` is the endpoint difference
`G (γ b) - G (γ a)`.
decls.title: FTC along a contour, `deriv` form
decls.statement:
theorem integral_comp_mul_deriv_eq_sub_of_hasDerivAt
    (hcont : ContinuousOn (G ∘ γ) (Set.uIcc a b))
    (hγ : ∀ t ∈ Set.Ioo (min a b) (max a b), DifferentiableAt ℝ γ t)
    (hG : ∀ t ∈ Set.Ioo (min a b) (max a b), HasDerivAt G (g (γ t)) (γ t))
    (hint : IntervalIntegrable (fun t => g (γ t) * deriv γ t) volume a b) :
    ∫ t in a..b, g (γ t) * deriv γ t = G (γ b) - G (γ a)

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.integral_comp_mul_eq_zero_of_hasDerivAt_of_closed
decls.doc: A contour integral of an exact derivative vanishes on a closed curve, explicit-velocity form.
decls.statement:
theorem integral_comp_mul_eq_zero_of_hasDerivAt_of_closed
    (hcont : ContinuousOn (G ∘ γ) (Set.uIcc a b))
    (hγ : ∀ t ∈ Set.Ioo (min a b) (max a b), HasDerivAt γ (γ' t) t)
    (hG : ∀ t ∈ Set.Ioo (min a b) (max a b), HasDerivAt G (g (γ t)) (γ t))
    (hint : IntervalIntegrable (fun t => g (γ t) * γ' t) volume a b)
    (hclosed : γ a = γ b) :
    ∫ t in a..b, g (γ t) * γ' t = 0

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.integral_comp_mul_deriv_eq_zero_of_hasDerivAt_of_closed
decls.doc: A contour integral of an exact derivative vanishes on a closed curve, `deriv` form.
decls.statement:
theorem integral_comp_mul_deriv_eq_zero_of_hasDerivAt_of_closed
    (hcont : ContinuousOn (G ∘ γ) (Set.uIcc a b))
    (hγ : ∀ t ∈ Set.Ioo (min a b) (max a b), DifferentiableAt ℝ γ t)
    (hG : ∀ t ∈ Set.Ioo (min a b) (max a b), HasDerivAt G (g (γ t)) (γ t))
    (hint : IntervalIntegrable (fun t => g (γ t) * deriv γ t) volume a b)
    (hclosed : γ a = γ b) :
    ∫ t in a..b, g (γ t) * deriv γ t = 0

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.argumentPrinciple_nullHomologous
decls.doc:
**The argument principle for an arbitrary null-homologous cycle.** Let `U` be open, `S` a
finite set collecting every zero and pole of `f` in `U`: `f` is analytic and non-vanishing at each
point of `U ∖ S`, and meromorphic of order `ord s` at each `s ∈ S` lying in `U`. Let `γ` be a
closed piecewise-`C¹` curve in `U`, **null-homologous** in `U`, that **avoids** `S`. Then the
contour integral of the logarithmic derivative counts the orders, each weighted by the winding
number of `γ` about it:

`∫ t in a..b, γ' t • logDeriv f (γ t) = 2πi · ∑_{z ∈ S} n_z(γ) · ord z`.

Since `ord` is positive at a zero and negative at a pole, this is `2πi` times the number of zeros
minus poles counted with multiplicity *and* with winding multiplicity — for a simple loop
enclosing them once, the classical zero-minus-pole count.

As in `TauCeti.Contour.classicalResidueTheorem_nullHomologous`, points of `S` outside `U` are
harmless rather than excluded: null-homology forces their winding number, hence their
contribution, to vanish, so nothing is asked of `f` there. Likewise `S` may list regular
non-vanishing points of `f`, whose order is `0`.

The round-circle case, which asks nothing pointwise of `f` because it may pass to the meromorphic
normal form, is `TauCeti.Contour.argumentPrinciple`.
decls.title: The argument principle for an arbitrary null-homologous cycle
decls.statement:
theorem argumentPrinciple_nullHomologous {f : ℂ → ℂ} {S : Finset ℂ} {U : Set ℂ} {ord : ℂ → ℤ}
    (hU : IsOpen U) (hoff : ∀ z ∈ U, z ∉ S → AnalyticAt ℂ f z ∧ f z ≠ 0)
    (hmero : ∀ s ∈ S, s ∈ U → MeromorphicAt f s)
    (hord : ∀ s ∈ S, s ∈ U → meromorphicOrderAt f s = (ord s : WithTop ℤ))
    {γ : ℝ → ℂ} {a b : ℝ} (hγ : IsPiecewiseC1On γ a b)
    (hγU : ∀ t ∈ uIcc a b, γ t ∈ U) (hclosed : γ a = γ b)
    (hγoff : ∀ t ∈ uIcc a b, γ t ∉ (↑S : Set ℂ)) (hnull : IsNullHomologous γ a b U) :
    ∫ t in a..b, deriv γ t • logDeriv f (γ t)
      = 2 * (Real.pi : ℂ) * Complex.I * ∑ z ∈ S, windingNumber γ a b z * (ord z : ℂ)

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.argumentPrinciple_nullHomologous_local
decls.doc:
**The argument principle for a cycle around a single zero or pole.** If `z₀` is the only point
of an open `U` at which `f` fails to be analytic and non-vanishing, of order `n` there, and `γ` is a
closed piecewise-`C¹` curve in `U`, null-homologous in `U`, missing `z₀`, then

`∫ t in a..b, γ' t • logDeriv f (γ t) = 2πi · n_{z₀}(γ) · n`.

This is the `S = {z₀}` case of `TauCeti.Contour.argumentPrinciple_nullHomologous`, and the
arbitrary-cycle counterpart of `TauCeti.Contour.argumentPrinciple_local`: a loop winding `k` times
around a zero of order `n` integrates `f'/f` to `2πi · k · n`.

Membership `z₀ ∈ U` is not required, and nothing at all is asked of `f` at `z₀` unless it holds:
if `z₀` lies outside `U` then `f` is analytic and non-vanishing on all of `U`, and null-homology
makes `n_{z₀}(γ)` vanish, so both sides are `0` for any `n`. Accordingly the meromorphy and the
order hypotheses are conditional on `z₀ ∈ U`, exactly as they are in
`TauCeti.Contour.argumentPrinciple_nullHomologous`.
decls.title: The argument principle for a cycle around a single zero or pole
decls.statement:
theorem argumentPrinciple_nullHomologous_local {f : ℂ → ℂ} {U : Set ℂ} {z₀ : ℂ} {n : ℤ}
    (hU : IsOpen U) (hmero : z₀ ∈ U → MeromorphicAt f z₀)
    (hn : z₀ ∈ U → meromorphicOrderAt f z₀ = (n : WithTop ℤ))
    (hoff : ∀ z ∈ U, z ≠ z₀ → AnalyticAt ℂ f z ∧ f z ≠ 0)
    {γ : ℝ → ℂ} {a b : ℝ} (hγ : IsPiecewiseC1On γ a b)
    (hγU : ∀ t ∈ uIcc a b, γ t ∈ U) (hclosed : γ a = γ b)
    (hγoff : ∀ t ∈ uIcc a b, γ t ≠ z₀) (hnull : IsNullHomologous γ a b U) :
    ∫ t in a..b, deriv γ t • logDeriv f (γ t)
      = 2 * (Real.pi : ℂ) * Complex.I * (windingNumber γ a b z₀ * (n : ℂ))

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.argumentPrinciple_nullHomologous_of_analyticOnNhd
decls.doc:
**Winding-weighted zero counting.** Let `f` be analytic on an open `U` with all its zeros in a
finite set `S`, and let `γ` be a closed piecewise-`C¹` curve in `U`, null-homologous in `U`, along
which `f` does not vanish. Then

`∫ t in a..b, γ' t • logDeriv f (γ t) = 2πi · ∑_{z ∈ S} n_z(γ) · analyticOrderNatAt f z`:

the contour integral of `f'/f` counts the zeros of `f` with multiplicity, each weighted by the
winding number of `γ` about it. This is the pole-free specialisation of
`TauCeti.Contour.argumentPrinciple_nullHomologous`, with the orders read off by
`analyticOrderNatAt` instead of by a caller-supplied `ord`.

Only the *zeros* need be avoided, not all of `S`: `S` may list points where `f` does not vanish,
and `γ` is free to run through them, since `logDeriv f` is holomorphic there and their order — and
so their term in the sum — is `0`.

The zeros are automatically of finite order (`TauCeti.analyticOrderAt_ne_top_of_zeros_subset`):
confining them to a finite set already rules out `f` vanishing identically near a point of `U`.
decls.title: Winding-weighted zero counting
decls.statement:
theorem argumentPrinciple_nullHomologous_of_analyticOnNhd {f : ℂ → ℂ} {S : Finset ℂ} {U : Set ℂ}
    (hU : IsOpen U) (hf : AnalyticOnNhd ℂ f U) (hzeros : ∀ z ∈ U, f z = 0 → z ∈ S)
    {γ : ℝ → ℂ} {a b : ℝ} (hγ : IsPiecewiseC1On γ a b)
    (hγU : ∀ t ∈ uIcc a b, γ t ∈ U) (hclosed : γ a = γ b)
    (hγoff : ∀ t ∈ uIcc a b, f (γ t) ≠ 0) (hnull : IsNullHomologous γ a b U) :
    ∫ t in a..b, deriv γ t • logDeriv f (γ t)
      = 2 * (Real.pi : ℂ) * Complex.I *
          ∑ z ∈ S, windingNumber γ a b z * (analyticOrderNatAt f z : ℂ)

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.divisor_eq_analyticOrderNatAt
decls.doc:
Where a meromorphic function is analytic, its divisor records the order of vanishing. The
identity also holds at a point of infinite order, where both sides read `0`.

This is the bridge between `MeromorphicOn.divisor` — whose support is finite on a ball by
`MeromorphicOn.divisor_ball_support_finite` — and the `analyticOrderNatAt` vocabulary that zero
counts are stated in, so zero-counting arguments can reuse it instead of rebuilding the
correspondence. Note the finiteness is of the divisor's *support*, equivalently of the zeros of
finite order: a point where `f` vanishes identically has divisor value `0` and is absent from it.

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.argumentPrinciple_divisor
decls.doc:
**The argument principle, against the divisor.** For `f` meromorphic on the closed disc
`C(c, R)` with no zero or pole on the bounding circle, the contour integral of the logarithmic
derivative is `2πi` times the sum of `MeromorphicOn.divisor` over the open disc.

This is `TauCeti.Contour.argumentPrinciple` with the finite set and the order function supplied by
Mathlib's divisor API rather than by the caller.
decls.title: The argument principle, against the divisor
decls.statement:
theorem argumentPrinciple_divisor {f : ℂ → ℂ} {c : ℂ} {R : ℝ} (hR : 0 < R)
    (hf : MeromorphicOn f (closedBall c R))
    (hsphere : ∀ z ∈ sphere c R, meromorphicOrderAt f z = 0) :
    circleIntegral (logDeriv f) c R
      = 2 * (Real.pi : ℂ) * Complex.I *
        (∑ᶠ z, ((MeromorphicOn.divisor f (ball c R) z : ℤ) : ℂ))

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.exists_uniform_modulus_avoiding
decls.doc:
For a continuous function `γ : ℝ → ℂ` avoiding `w` on a compact interval, there
exists `δ > 0` such that on any sub-interval of length `< δ`, `γ` varies by less than
half the minimum distance to `w`. This gives a partition where each segment of
`γ - w` lies in a ball avoiding `0`.
decls.statement:
theorem exists_uniform_modulus_avoiding {γ : ℝ → ℂ} {w : ℂ} {a b : ℝ} (hab : a ≤ b)
    (hγ : ContinuousOn γ (Icc a b))
    (h_avoid : ∀ t ∈ Icc a b, γ t ≠ w) :
    ∃ δ' > 0, ∃ ρ > 0, (∀ t ∈ Icc a b, ρ ≤ ‖γ t - w‖) ∧
      ∀ t s, t ∈ Icc a b → s ∈ Icc a b → |t - s| < δ' →
        ‖γ t - γ s‖ < ρ / 2

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.segClamp
decls.doc: Helper: clamp `t` to `[s_j, s_{j+1}]`. For partition segment `j`.
decls.statement: def segClamp (s_j s_jp1 t : ℝ) : ℝ

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.segClamp_continuous
decls.statement:
theorem segClamp_continuous (s_j s_jp1 : ℝ) :
    Continuous (segClamp s_j s_jp1)

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.segClamp_mem_Icc
decls.statement:
theorem segClamp_mem_Icc (s_j s_jp1 t : ℝ) (h : s_j ≤ s_jp1) :
    segClamp s_j s_jp1 t ∈ Icc s_j s_jp1

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.segClamp_eq_left
decls.statement:
theorem segClamp_eq_left {s_j s_jp1 t : ℝ} (ht : t ≤ s_j) :
    segClamp s_j s_jp1 t = s_j

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.segClamp_eq_self
decls.statement:
theorem segClamp_eq_self {s_j s_jp1 t : ℝ} (ht_lo : s_j ≤ t) (ht_hi : t ≤ s_jp1) :
    segClamp s_j s_jp1 t = t

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.segClamp_eq_right
decls.statement:
theorem segClamp_eq_right {s_j s_jp1 t : ℝ} (h : s_j ≤ s_jp1) (ht : s_jp1 ≤ t) :
    segClamp s_j s_jp1 t = s_jp1

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.segRatio
decls.doc:
The **segment ratio** `(γ (segClamp s_j s_jp1 t) - w) / (γ s_j - w)`: on the partition segment
`[s_j, s_{j+1}]` it measures `γ t - w` against its value at the left endpoint `s_j`, held constant
in `t` outside the segment. Summing the `Complex.log`s of these ratios over a partition yields a
continuous argument lift of `t ↦ γ t - w`.
decls.statement: def segRatio (γ : ℝ → ℂ) (w : ℂ) (s_j s_jp1 t : ℝ) : ℂ

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.segRatio_eq_one_of_le
decls.doc: Before its segment (`t ≤ s_j`), the segment ratio equals `1`.

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.segRatio_eq_div_of_mem_Icc
decls.doc:
On its segment (`t ∈ [s_j, s_{j+1}]`), the segment ratio is `(γ t - w) / (γ s_j - w)` — the
primary meaning of `segRatio`.

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.segRatio_eq_endpoint_div_of_le
decls.doc:
After its segment (`s_{j+1} ≤ t`), the segment ratio equals the full endpoint ratio
`(γ s_{j+1} - w) / (γ s_j - w)`.

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.segRatio_mem_ball_one
decls.doc:
For partition with mesh < δ' and segments [s_j, s_{j+1}] of length ≤ mesh,
on the j-th segment, `γ(clamp t) - γ s_j` is small, so `segRatio j t ∈ ball(1, 1/2)`.
decls.statement:
theorem segRatio_mem_ball_one
    {γ : ℝ → ℂ} {w : ℂ} {a b δ' ρ : ℝ} (hρ_pos : 0 < ρ)
    (h_dist_lb : ∀ t ∈ Icc a b, ρ ≤ ‖γ t - w‖)
    (h_unif : ∀ t s : ℝ, t ∈ Icc a b → s ∈ Icc a b →
      |t - s| < δ' → ‖γ t - γ s‖ < ρ / 2)
    {s_j s_jp1 : ℝ} (hsj : s_j ∈ Icc a b) (hsjp1 : s_jp1 ∈ Icc a b)
    (h_le : s_j ≤ s_jp1) (h_mesh : s_jp1 - s_j < δ') (t : ℝ) :
    ‖segRatio γ w s_j s_jp1 t - 1‖ < 1 / 2

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.continuousOn_segRatio
decls.doc: Continuity of `t ↦ segRatio γ w s_j s_jp1 t` on `Icc a b`.
decls.statement:
theorem continuousOn_segRatio {γ : ℝ → ℂ} {a b : ℝ} (hγ : ContinuousOn γ (Icc a b))
    {w : ℂ} {s_j s_jp1 : ℝ} (hsj : s_j ∈ Icc a b)
    (hsjp1 : s_jp1 ∈ Icc a b) (h_le : s_j ≤ s_jp1) :
    ContinuousOn (fun t ↦ segRatio γ w s_j s_jp1 t) (Icc a b)

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.segRatio_mem_slitPlane
decls.doc: Combined: for partition with mesh < δ', `segRatio j t ∈ slitPlane`.
decls.statement:
theorem segRatio_mem_slitPlane
    {γ : ℝ → ℂ} {w : ℂ} {a b δ' ρ : ℝ} (hρ_pos : 0 < ρ)
    (h_dist_lb : ∀ t ∈ Icc a b, ρ ≤ ‖γ t - w‖)
    (h_unif : ∀ t s : ℝ, t ∈ Icc a b → s ∈ Icc a b →
      |t - s| < δ' → ‖γ t - γ s‖ < ρ / 2)
    {s_j s_jp1 : ℝ} (hsj : s_j ∈ Icc a b) (hsjp1 : s_jp1 ∈ Icc a b)
    (h_le : s_j ≤ s_jp1) (h_mesh : s_jp1 - s_j < δ') (t : ℝ) :
    segRatio γ w s_j s_jp1 t ∈ Complex.slitPlane

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.prod_range_div_complex
decls.doc:
Telescoping product in `ℂ` over `Finset.range`. For `a : ℕ → ℂ` nonzero on indices `0..k`,
`∏ j ∈ range k, a (j+1)/a j = a k / a 0`. The nonzero-field analogue of the group telescoping lemma
`Finset.prod_range_div`, obtained from it by lifting the nonzero values into `ℂˣ`.
decls.statement:
lemma prod_range_div_complex (a : ℕ → ℂ) (k : ℕ)
    (ha : ∀ j ≤ k, a j ≠ 0) :
    ∏ j ∈ Finset.range k, (a (j + 1) / a j) = a k / a 0

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.prod_segRatio_telescope
decls.doc:
Telescoping product: for `t ∈ [s_k, s_{k+1}]` along a monotone partition
`s : ℕ → ℝ` with `γ(s_j) ≠ w` for `0 ≤ j ≤ N`, the product
`∏_{j < N} segRatio γ w (s j) (s (j+1)) t` collapses to `(γ t - w) / (γ (s 0) - w)`.

This is the key identity making `Im(log)` of each `segRatio` add up to a
continuous argument lift of `t ↦ γ t - w`.
decls.statement:
theorem prod_segRatio_telescope
    {γ : ℝ → ℂ} {w : ℂ} {N : ℕ} {s : ℕ → ℝ}
    (hs_mono : Monotone s)
    (h_avoid : ∀ j ≤ N, γ (s j) - w ≠ 0)
    {t : ℝ} {k : ℕ} (hk : k < N) (hk_lo : s k ≤ t) (hk_hi : t ≤ s (k + 1)) :
    ∏ j ∈ Finset.range N, segRatio γ w (s j) (s (j + 1)) t = (γ t - w) / (γ (s 0) - w)

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.continuousOn_im_log_segRatio
decls.doc: Each summand in the telescoping arg-lift sum is continuous.
decls.statement:
theorem continuousOn_im_log_segRatio {γ : ℝ → ℂ} {a b : ℝ}
    (hγ : ContinuousOn γ (Icc a b)) {w : ℂ} {δ' ρ : ℝ} (hρ_pos : 0 < ρ)
    (h_dist_lb : ∀ t ∈ Icc a b, ρ ≤ ‖γ t - w‖)
    (h_unif : ∀ t s : ℝ, t ∈ Icc a b → s ∈ Icc a b →
      |t - s| < δ' → ‖γ t - γ s‖ < ρ / 2)
    {s_j s_jp1 : ℝ} (hsj : s_j ∈ Icc a b) (hsjp1 : s_jp1 ∈ Icc a b)
    (h_le : s_j ≤ s_jp1) (h_mesh : s_jp1 - s_j < δ') :
    ContinuousOn (fun t ↦ (Complex.log (segRatio γ w s_j s_jp1 t)).im)
      (Icc a b)

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.div_norm_eq_exp_arg_mul_I
decls.doc:
**A nonzero complex number over its norm is the exponential of its argument**:
`w / ↑‖w‖ = exp(arg w · I)`.
decls.title: A nonzero complex number over its norm is the exponential of its argument
decls.statement:
theorem div_norm_eq_exp_arg_mul_I {w : ℂ} (hw : w ≠ 0) :
    w / (‖w‖ : ℂ) = Complex.exp ((Complex.arg w : ℂ) * Complex.I)

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.exp_I_log_im_eq_div_norm
decls.doc: For a nonzero complex number `z`, `exp(I · Im(log z)) = z / ↑‖z‖`.
decls.statement:
lemma exp_I_log_im_eq_div_norm {z : ℂ} (hz : z ≠ 0) :
    Complex.exp (Complex.I * ((Complex.log z).im : ℂ)) = z / (‖z‖ : ℂ)

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.polar_form_of_prod
decls.doc:
If `z = z0 · ∏ zs j` with `z0` and each factor `zs j` nonzero, then
`z = ‖z‖ · exp (I · θ)` with `θ = arg z0 + ∑ Im (log (zs j))`: the arguments of the factors add
and the norms multiply out to `‖z‖`. This packages the argument bookkeeping of the continuous
lift, whose telescoped product `(γ a - w) · ∏ segRatio = γ t - w` has exactly this shape.
decls.statement:
lemma polar_form_of_prod {N : ℕ} {z0 : ℂ} {zs : ℕ → ℂ} {z : ℂ}
    (hz0 : z0 ≠ 0) (hzs : ∀ j ∈ Finset.range N, zs j ≠ 0)
    (hprod : z0 * ∏ j ∈ Finset.range N, zs j = z) :
    z = (‖z‖ : ℂ) * Complex.exp (Complex.I *
      ((Complex.arg z0 + ∑ j ∈ Finset.range N, (Complex.log (zs j)).im : ℝ) : ℂ))

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.exists_covering_segment
decls.doc:
On a monotone partition covering `[s 0, s N]`, every point `t` with `s 0 ≤ t ≤ s N` lies in
some segment `[s k, s (k+1)]` with `k < N`.
decls.statement:
lemma exists_covering_segment {N : ℕ} (hN : 0 < N) {s : ℕ → ℝ} (hmono : Monotone s)
    {t : ℝ} (h_lo : s 0 ≤ t) (h_hi : t ≤ s N) :
    ∃ k, k < N ∧ s k ≤ t ∧ t ≤ s (k + 1)

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.exists_monotone_partition_mesh_lt
decls.doc:
**Monotone partition with mesh below `δ`.** For `a ≤ b` and `δ > 0`, the interval `[a, b]`
admits a monotone partition `a = s 0 ≤ ⋯ ≤ s N = b` with `N > 0` segments (so `N + 1` nodes), each
node in `[a, b]`, and every gap `s (j + 1) - s j` strictly below `δ`. Built from Mathlib's
fixed-step `Set.Icc.addNSMul` partition (step `δ / 2`, stabilising at `b`).
decls.title: Monotone partition with mesh below `δ`
decls.statement:
theorem exists_monotone_partition_mesh_lt {a b δ : ℝ} (hab : a ≤ b) (hδ : 0 < δ) :
    ∃ (N : ℕ) (s : ℕ → ℝ), 0 < N ∧ s 0 = a ∧ s N = b ∧ Monotone s ∧
      (∀ j ≤ N, s j ∈ Icc a b) ∧ ∀ j, s (j + 1) - s j < δ

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.exists_continuousOn_arg_lift_with_partition
decls.doc:
**Argument lift on `[a, b]`, with a partition.** For `γ` continuous on `[a, b]` (`a ≤ b`) and
avoiding `w`, there is a monotone partition `a = s 0 ≤ ⋯ ≤ s N = b` and a real function
`θ t = arg (γ a - w) + ∑_{j < N} (log (segRatio γ w (s j) (s (j+1)) t)).im`, continuous on `[a, b]`,
satisfying `γ t - w = ‖γ t - w‖ · exp (I · θ t)` there. Each node has `γ (s j) ≠ w`, and on each
segment `j` the ratio `(γ t - w) / (γ (s j) - w)` lies in `Complex.slitPlane`.
decls.title: Argument lift on `[a, b]`, with a partition
decls.statement:
theorem exists_continuousOn_arg_lift_with_partition
    {γ : ℝ → ℂ} {w : ℂ} {a b : ℝ} (hab : a ≤ b)
    (hγ : ContinuousOn γ (Icc a b))
    (h_avoid : ∀ t ∈ Icc a b, γ t ≠ w) :
    ∃ (N : ℕ) (s : ℕ → ℝ),
      0 < N ∧ s 0 = a ∧ s N = b ∧ Monotone s ∧
      (∀ j ≤ N, s j ∈ Icc a b) ∧
      (∀ j ≤ N, γ (s j) - w ≠ 0) ∧
      (∀ j, j < N → ∀ t ∈ Icc (s j) (s (j + 1)),
        (γ t - w) / (γ (s j) - w) ∈ Complex.slitPlane) ∧
      ContinuousOn
        (fun t ↦ Complex.arg (γ a - w) +
          ∑ j ∈ Finset.range N, (Complex.log (segRatio γ w (s j) (s (j + 1)) t)).im)
        (Icc a b) ∧
      (∀ t ∈ Icc a b, γ t - w = (‖γ t - w‖ : ℂ) * Complex.exp (Complex.I *
        ((Complex.arg (γ a - w) +
          ∑ j ∈ Finset.range N,
            (Complex.log (segRatio γ w (s j) (s (j + 1)) t)).im : ℝ) : ℂ)))

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.analyticAt_logDeriv_of_analyticAt
decls.doc:
At a point where a function is analytic and non-vanishing, its logarithmic derivative
`logDeriv f = deriv f / f` is analytic. Exposed for the residue-form of the argument principle
(`TauCeti.Contour.residue_logDeriv_eq_meromorphicOrderAt`).
decls.statement:
lemma analyticAt_logDeriv_of_analyticAt {f : ℂ → ℂ} {z : ℂ} (hf : AnalyticAt ℂ f z)
    (hz : f z ≠ 0) : AnalyticAt ℂ (logDeriv f) z

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.logDeriv_eq_of_eventuallyEq
decls.doc: The logarithmic derivative depends only on the germ.
decls.statement:
lemma logDeriv_eq_of_eventuallyEq {f g : ℂ → ℂ} {z : ℂ} (h : f =ᶠ[𝓝 z] g) :
    logDeriv f z = logDeriv g z

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.logDeriv_zpow_sub_mul
decls.doc:
Logarithmic derivative of a local factorisation `(· - c) ^ n · g`, away from the base point `c`.
Since `logDeriv` turns products into sums and `logDeriv ((· - c) ^ n) = n · (· - c)⁻¹`, we get
`logDeriv ((· - c) ^ n · g) = n · (· - c)⁻¹ + logDeriv g`.
decls.statement:
lemma logDeriv_zpow_sub_mul {g : ℂ → ℂ} {c z : ℂ} {n : ℤ} (hz : z ≠ c) (hg_ne : g z ≠ 0)
    (hg_diff : DifferentiableAt ℂ g z) :
    logDeriv (fun w => (w - c) ^ n * g w) z = (n : ℂ) * (z - c)⁻¹ + logDeriv g z

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.logDeriv_eventuallyEq_principalPart
decls.doc:
**Simple-pole splitting of the logarithmic derivative.** Near a point `s` where `F` is
meromorphic of order `n`, the logarithmic derivative equals its simple-pole principal part
`n · (· - s)⁻¹` plus an analytic term: there is `g` analytic and non-vanishing at `s` (the local
factor of `F = (· - s) ^ n • g`) with `logDeriv F = n · (· - s)⁻¹ + logDeriv g` on a punctured
neighbourhood of `s`. Exposed for the residue-form of the argument principle
(`TauCeti.Contour.residue_logDeriv_eq_meromorphicOrderAt`).
decls.title: Simple-pole splitting of the logarithmic derivative
decls.statement:
theorem logDeriv_eventuallyEq_principalPart {F : ℂ → ℂ} {s : ℂ} {n : ℤ}
    (hF : MeromorphicAt F s) (hn : meromorphicOrderAt F s = (n : WithTop ℤ)) :
    ∃ g : ℂ → ℂ, AnalyticAt ℂ g s ∧ g s ≠ 0 ∧
      logDeriv F =ᶠ[𝓝[≠] s] fun z => (n : ℂ) * (z - s)⁻¹ + logDeriv g z

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.circleIntegral_logDeriv_toMeromorphicNFOn
decls.doc:
Passing to the meromorphic normal form leaves the log-derivative's circle integral unchanged:
the two functions agree off a discrete set, which the circle integral does not see.
decls.statement:
theorem circleIntegral_logDeriv_toMeromorphicNFOn {f : ℂ → ℂ} {c : ℂ} {R : ℝ} (hR : 0 < R)
    (hf : MeromorphicOn f (Metric.closedBall c R)) :
    circleIntegral (logDeriv f) c R
      = circleIntegral (logDeriv (toMeromorphicNFOn f (Metric.closedBall c R))) c R

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.circleIntegral_principalPart
decls.doc:
The circle integral of the principal part `∑_{s∈S} ord s · (z − s)⁻¹`, with all poles `s`
strictly inside the disc, is `2πi · ∑_{s∈S} ord s` (each simple pole contributes `2πi · ord s`).
decls.statement:
theorem circleIntegral_principalPart {c : ℂ} {R : ℝ} (hR : 0 < R) (S : Finset ℂ)
    (ord : ℂ → ℤ) (hS : (S : Set ℂ) ⊆ Metric.ball c R) :
    circleIntegral (fun z => ∑ s ∈ S, (ord s : ℂ) * (z - s)⁻¹) c R
      = 2 * (Real.pi : ℂ) * Complex.I * (∑ z ∈ S, (ord z : ℂ))

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.circleIntegral_logDeriv_sub_principalPart_eq_zero
decls.doc:
Subtracting the principal part cancels every simple pole of `logDeriv F`: if `F` is meromorphic
on the disc with order `ord z` at each `z ∈ S` and is analytic and non-vanishing off `S`, then
`logDeriv F − ∑_{s∈S} ord s · (· − s)⁻¹` is pole-free, so its circle integral vanishes.
decls.statement:
theorem circleIntegral_logDeriv_sub_principalPart_eq_zero {F : ℂ → ℂ} {c : ℂ} {R : ℝ}
    (hR : 0 < R) (S : Finset ℂ) (ord : ℂ → ℤ)
    (hF_mero : MeromorphicOn F (Metric.closedBall c R))
    (hord_F : ∀ z ∈ S, meromorphicOrderAt F z = (ord z : WithTop ℤ))
    (hoffF : ∀ z ∈ Metric.closedBall c R, z ∉ S → AnalyticAt ℂ F z ∧ F z ≠ 0) :
    circleIntegral (fun z => logDeriv F z - ∑ s ∈ S, (ord s : ℂ) * (z - s)⁻¹) c R = 0

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.argumentPrinciple
decls.doc:
**The argument principle.** If `f` is meromorphic on the closed disc `C(c, R)` (`R > 0`) with
all its nonzero-order points contained in a finite set `S` inside the open disc, with orders `ord`,
then the contour integral of the logarithmic derivative counts the zeros minus the poles with
multiplicity:
`∮_{C(c,R)} f'/f = 2πi · ∑_{z ∈ S} ord z`.
decls.title: The argument principle
decls.statement:
theorem argumentPrinciple {f : ℂ → ℂ} {c : ℂ} {R : ℝ} (hR : 0 < R) (S : Finset ℂ) (ord : ℂ → ℤ)
    (hf : MeromorphicOn f (Metric.closedBall c R))
    (hS : (S : Set ℂ) ⊆ Metric.ball c R)
    (hsupp : ∀ z ∈ Metric.closedBall c R, meromorphicOrderAt f z ≠ 0 → z ∈ S)
    (hord : ∀ z ∈ S, meromorphicOrderAt f z = (ord z : WithTop ℤ)) :
    circleIntegral (logDeriv f) c R = 2 * (Real.pi : ℂ) * Complex.I * (∑ z ∈ S, (ord z : ℂ))

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.argumentPrinciple_local
decls.doc:
**Local argument principle.** If `f` is meromorphic on the closed disc `C(c, R)` (`R > 0`) and
the centre `c` is the only point of the disc that may have nonzero meromorphic order — every other
point is at worst a removable singularity — then the contour integral of the logarithmic derivative
recovers the order `n = meromorphicOrderAt f c` at the centre:
`∮_{C(c,R)} f'/f = 2πi · n`. Thus the integral counts the zero (`n > 0`) or pole (`n < 0`) at the
centre with multiplicity, and vanishes when `c` too has order `0`. This is the `S = {c}` case of
`argumentPrinciple`.
decls.title: Local argument principle
decls.statement:
theorem argumentPrinciple_local {f : ℂ → ℂ} {c : ℂ} {R : ℝ} {n : ℤ} (hR : 0 < R)
    (hf : MeromorphicOn f (Metric.closedBall c R))
    (honly : ∀ z ∈ Metric.closedBall c R, meromorphicOrderAt f z ≠ 0 → z = c)
    (hn : meromorphicOrderAt f c = (n : WithTop ℤ)) :
    circleIntegral (logDeriv f) c R = 2 * (Real.pi : ℂ) * Complex.I * (n : ℂ)

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.circleIntegral_eq_zero_of_meromorphicOrderAt_nonneg
decls.doc:
**Cauchy–Goursat for a pole-free meromorphic function.** If `A` is meromorphic on the closed
disc `C(c, R)` (`R ≥ 0`) and has non-negative meromorphic order at every point of the disc, then
`∮_{C(c,R)} A = 0`.
decls.title: Cauchy–Goursat for a pole-free meromorphic function
decls.statement:
lemma circleIntegral_eq_zero_of_meromorphicOrderAt_nonneg {A : ℂ → ℂ} {c : ℂ} {R : ℝ}
    (hR : 0 ≤ R) (hA : MeromorphicOn A (closedBall c R))
    (hord : ∀ z ∈ closedBall c R, 0 ≤ meromorphicOrderAt A z) :
    circleIntegral A c R = 0

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.cauchyIntegralFormula_iteratedDeriv_nullHomologous
decls.doc:
**Cauchy's integral formula for the `k`-th derivative, homology form.** Let `f` be holomorphic
on an open `U`, let `γ` be a closed piecewise-`C¹` curve in `U` that is null-homologous there, and
let `z ∈ U` lie off the curve. Then for every `k`,

`∫ t in a..b, γ' t • (f (γ t) / (γ t − z) ^ (k + 1)) = 2πi · n_z(γ) · f⁽ᵏ⁾(z) / k !`,

the `k`-th Taylor coefficient of `f` at `z` weighted by the generalized winding number of `γ` about
`z`. Only the residue at `z` contributes: the residue theorem for a null-homologous cycle applied
to the Cauchy kernel `w ↦ f w / (w − z) ^ (k + 1)`, whose only possible singularity in `U` is at
`z`, leaves the single residue `iteratedDeriv k f z / k !`.
decls.title: Cauchy's integral formula for the `k`-th derivative, homology form
decls.statement:
theorem cauchyIntegralFormula_iteratedDeriv_nullHomologous {f : ℂ → ℂ} {U : Set ℂ} {γ : ℝ → ℂ}
    {a b : ℝ} {z : ℂ} (hU : IsOpen U) (hf : DifferentiableOn ℂ f U) (hγ : IsPiecewiseC1On γ a b)
    (hγU : ∀ t ∈ uIcc a b, γ t ∈ U) (hclosed : γ a = γ b) (hnull : IsNullHomologous γ a b U)
    (hz : z ∈ U) (hoff : ∀ t ∈ uIcc a b, γ t ≠ z) (k : ℕ) :
    ∫ t in a..b, deriv γ t • (f (γ t) / (γ t - z) ^ (k + 1))
      = 2 * (Real.pi : ℂ) * Complex.I * windingNumber γ a b z *
          (iteratedDeriv k f z / (k.factorial : ℂ))

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.cauchyIntegralFormula_nullHomologous
decls.doc:
**Cauchy's integral formula, homology form** (roadmap Layer 3). For `f` holomorphic on an open
`U`, `γ` a closed piecewise-`C¹` curve in `U` that is null-homologous there, and `z ∈ U` off the
curve,

`∫ t in a..b, γ' t • (f (γ t) / (γ t − z)) = 2πi · n_z(γ) · f z`,

so that `f z · n_z(γ) = (2πi)⁻¹ ∮_γ f(w)/(w − z) dw`: the Cauchy-type integral recovers the value of
`f` at `z`, counted with the multiplicity with which `γ` winds around it. The `S = ∅` companion of
this statement is the homology Cauchy theorem `TauCeti.Contour.homologyCauchyTheorem`.
decls.title: Cauchy's integral formula, homology form
decls.statement:
theorem cauchyIntegralFormula_nullHomologous {f : ℂ → ℂ} {U : Set ℂ} {γ : ℝ → ℂ} {a b : ℝ} {z : ℂ}
    (hU : IsOpen U) (hf : DifferentiableOn ℂ f U) (hγ : IsPiecewiseC1On γ a b)
    (hγU : ∀ t ∈ uIcc a b, γ t ∈ U) (hclosed : γ a = γ b) (hnull : IsNullHomologous γ a b U)
    (hz : z ∈ U) (hoff : ∀ t ∈ uIcc a b, γ t ≠ z) :
    ∫ t in a..b, deriv γ t • (f (γ t) / (γ t - z))
      = 2 * (Real.pi : ℂ) * Complex.I * windingNumber γ a b z * f z

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.cauchyIntegralFormula_deriv_nullHomologous
decls.doc:
**Cauchy's integral formula for the first derivative, homology form.** The `k = 1` case of
`TauCeti.Contour.cauchyIntegralFormula_iteratedDeriv_nullHomologous`, stated with `deriv f z`:

`∫ t in a..b, γ' t • (f (γ t) / (γ t − z) ^ 2) = 2πi · n_z(γ) · f' z`.
decls.title: Cauchy's integral formula for the first derivative, homology form
decls.statement:
theorem cauchyIntegralFormula_deriv_nullHomologous {f : ℂ → ℂ} {U : Set ℂ} {γ : ℝ → ℂ} {a b : ℝ}
    {z : ℂ} (hU : IsOpen U) (hf : DifferentiableOn ℂ f U) (hγ : IsPiecewiseC1On γ a b)
    (hγU : ∀ t ∈ uIcc a b, γ t ∈ U) (hclosed : γ a = γ b) (hnull : IsNullHomologous γ a b U)
    (hz : z ∈ U) (hoff : ∀ t ∈ uIcc a b, γ t ≠ z) :
    ∫ t in a..b, deriv γ t • (f (γ t) / (γ t - z) ^ 2)
      = 2 * (Real.pi : ℂ) * Complex.I * windingNumber γ a b z * deriv f z

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.windingNumber_eq_zero_of_pathHomotopy_refl
decls.doc:
A loop smoothly homotopic to its constant path through points avoiding `w` has winding number
zero about `w`.
decls.statement:
theorem windingNumber_eq_zero_of_pathHomotopy_refl {x w : ℂ} {p : Path x x}
    (φ : p.Homotopy (Path.refl x))
    (hφsmooth : ContDiffOn ℝ 2
      (fun st : ℝ × ℝ ↦ Set.IccExtend zero_le_one (φ.toHomotopy.extend st.1) st.2)
      (Set.Icc 0 1))
    (havoid : ∀ st : Set.Icc (0 : ℝ) 1 × Set.Icc (0 : ℝ) 1, φ st ≠ w) :
    windingNumber p.extend 0 1 w = 0

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.isNullHomologous_of_pathHomotopy_refl
decls.doc:
**Null-homotopic implies null-homologous.** If a loop admits a `C²` path homotopy to its
constant path whose image lies in `Ω`, then its generalized winding number vanishes at every point
outside `Ω`. Thus the loop is null-homologous in `Ω`.

This is one direction only: a null-homologous loop need not be null-homotopic.
decls.title: Null-homotopic implies null-homologous
decls.statement:
theorem isNullHomologous_of_pathHomotopy_refl {x : ℂ} {p : Path x x} {Ω : Set ℂ}
    (φ : p.Homotopy (Path.refl x))
    (hφsmooth : ContDiffOn ℝ 2
      (fun st : ℝ × ℝ ↦ Set.IccExtend zero_le_one (φ.toHomotopy.extend st.1) st.2)
      (Set.Icc 0 1))
    (hφΩ : ∀ st : Set.Icc (0 : ℝ) 1 × Set.Icc (0 : ℝ) 1, φ st ∈ Ω) :
    IsNullHomologous p.extend 0 1 Ω

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.cauchyTheorem_of_pathHomotopy_refl
decls.doc:
**Cauchy's theorem for a null-homotopic contour.** Let `p` be a piecewise-`C¹` loop admitting
a `C²` path homotopy to its constant path inside an open set `Ω`. If `f` is holomorphic on `Ω`,
then the contour integral of `f` along `p` vanishes.

The smooth homotopy supplies the piecewise-`C¹` regularity expected by
`homologyCauchyTheorem`, as well as containment of the source path in `Ω` and its null-homology
there.
decls.title: Cauchy's theorem for a null-homotopic contour
decls.statement:
theorem cauchyTheorem_of_pathHomotopy_refl {f : ℂ → ℂ} {Ω : Set ℂ} (hΩ : IsOpen Ω)
    {x : ℂ} (p : Path x x)
    (φ : p.Homotopy (Path.refl x))
    (hφsmooth : ContDiffOn ℝ 2
      (fun st : ℝ × ℝ ↦ Set.IccExtend zero_le_one (φ.toHomotopy.extend st.1) st.2)
      (Set.Icc 0 1))
    (hφΩ : ∀ st : Set.Icc (0 : ℝ) 1 × Set.Icc (0 : ℝ) 1, φ st ∈ Ω)
    (hf : DifferentiableOn ℂ f Ω) :
    ∫ t in (0 : ℝ)..1, deriv p.extend t • f (p.extend t) = 0

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.dixonH2_eq_windingNumber_mul_f_of_dixonFunction_eq_zero
decls.doc:
**Cauchy's integral formula from pointwise Dixon-vanishing.** If Dixon's glued function vanishes
at `w ∈ U` (`dixonFunction f U γ a b w = 0`), then for `γ` continuous on `uIcc a b` and avoiding `w`
with the Cauchy-type and index integrands interval-integrable, the Cauchy-type integral evaluates to
`dixonH2 f γ a b w = 2πi · n(γ, w) · f w`: on `U` the vanishing collapses the `h₁`/`h₂` identity,
whose winding term is exactly this value. Discharging the vanishing hypothesis via
`dixonFunction_eq_zero` gives Cauchy's integral formula for a null-homologous curve.
decls.title: Cauchy's integral formula from pointwise Dixon-vanishing
decls.statement:
theorem dixonH2_eq_windingNumber_mul_f_of_dixonFunction_eq_zero {f : ℂ → ℂ} {U : Set ℂ} {γ : ℝ → ℂ}
    {a b : ℝ} {w : ℂ} (h_cont : ContinuousOn γ (uIcc a b)) (hw : w ∈ U)
    (hoff : ∀ t ∈ uIcc a b, γ t ≠ w) (h_zero_at : dixonFunction f U γ a b w = 0)
    (h_cauchy_int : IntervalIntegrable (fun t ↦ f (γ t) / (γ t - w) * deriv γ t) volume a b)
    (h_base_int : IntervalIntegrable (fun t ↦ (γ t - w)⁻¹ * deriv γ t) volume a b) :
    dixonH2 f γ a b w = 2 * (Real.pi : ℂ) * Complex.I * windingNumber γ a b w * f w

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.intervalIntegral_deriv_smul_eq_zero_of_dixonFunction_eq_zero
decls.doc:
**The pointwise homology Cauchy theorem** `∮_γ f = 0`. Applying the Cauchy integral formula to
the twist `g z = (z - w₀) · f z`, which satisfies `g w₀ = 0`, forces `dixonH2 g γ a b w₀ = 0`; and
since `g (γ t) / (γ t - w₀) = f (γ t)` for `γ` off `w₀`, that Cauchy-type integral is the contour
integral of `f`. Hence `∫ t in a..b, deriv γ t • f (γ t) = 0`, given the pointwise vanishing
`dixonFunction (fun z ↦ (z - w₀) * f z) U γ a b w₀ = 0`, interval-integrability of the contour
integrand `deriv γ • f ∘ γ`, and of the index integrand. Discharging the vanishing via
`dixonFunction_eq_zero` yields the roadmap `homologyCauchyTheorem`.
decls.title: The pointwise homology Cauchy theorem
decls.statement:
theorem intervalIntegral_deriv_smul_eq_zero_of_dixonFunction_eq_zero {f : ℂ → ℂ} {U : Set ℂ}
    {γ : ℝ → ℂ} {a b : ℝ} (h_cont : ContinuousOn γ (uIcc a b)) (w₀ : ℂ) (hw₀_in_U : w₀ ∈ U)
    (hw₀_off : ∀ t ∈ uIcc a b, γ t ≠ w₀)
    (h_zero_at : dixonFunction (fun z ↦ (z - w₀) * f z) U γ a b w₀ = 0)
    (h_int : IntervalIntegrable (fun t ↦ deriv γ t • f (γ t)) volume a b)
    (h_base_int : IntervalIntegrable (fun t ↦ (γ t - w₀)⁻¹ * deriv γ t) volume a b) :
    ∫ t in a..b, deriv γ t • f (γ t) = 0

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.HasCauchyPVAt
decls.doc:
The **Cauchy principal value at `z₀`** of the contour integral `∮_γ f` exists with value `L`:
the truncated integrand along `γ` over `[a, b]`, excluding the symmetric `ε`-ball about `z₀`, is
eventually `IntervalIntegrable`, and its integral tends to `L` as `ε → 0⁺`. The integrability clause
prevents the `Tendsto` clause from being met vacuously through the convention that a Bochner
integral of a non-integrable function is `0`. Primary API predicate (raw `γ : ℝ → ℂ`, `[a, b]`).
decls.statement: def HasCauchyPVAt (γ : ℝ → ℂ) (a b : ℝ) (f : ℂ → ℂ) (z₀ : ℂ) (L : ℂ) : Prop

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.hasCauchyPVAt_iff
decls.doc:
Restatement of `HasCauchyPVAt` as the conjunction of its two defining clauses — eventual
integrability of the excised integrand and convergence of the excised integrals — so consumers can
characterize the predicate without unfolding its definition.
decls.statement:
theorem hasCauchyPVAt_iff {γ : ℝ → ℂ} {a b : ℝ} {f : ℂ → ℂ} {z₀ : ℂ} {L : ℂ} :
    HasCauchyPVAt γ a b f z₀ L ↔
      (∀ᶠ ε in 𝓝[>] (0 : ℝ), IntervalIntegrable
          (fun t => if ‖γ t - z₀‖ > ε then f (γ t) * deriv γ t else 0) MeasureTheory.volume a b) ∧
        Tendsto (fun ε ↦ ∫ t in a..b, if ‖γ t - z₀‖ > ε then f (γ t) * deriv γ t else 0)
          (𝓝[>] 0) (𝓝 L)

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.cauchyPVAt
decls.doc:
The **Cauchy principal value at `z₀`** of `∮_γ f`, excluding the symmetric `ε`-ball about `z₀`.
`limUnder`-based; returns junk when the limit does not exist, so use `HasCauchyPVAt` for the
predicate and `HasCauchyPVAt.cauchyPVAt_eq` to read the value off it.
decls.statement: def cauchyPVAt (γ : ℝ → ℂ) (a b : ℝ) (f : ℂ → ℂ) (z₀ : ℂ) : ℂ

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.CauchyPVExistsAt
decls.doc: The Cauchy principal value at `z₀` exists: shorthand for `∃ L, HasCauchyPVAt γ a b f z₀ L`.
decls.statement: def CauchyPVExistsAt (γ : ℝ → ℂ) (a b : ℝ) (f : ℂ → ℂ) (z₀ : ℂ) : Prop

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.cauchyPVExistsAt_iff
decls.doc:
Characterization of `CauchyPVExistsAt` as the existence of a principal value — the
eliminator/constructor interface, so downstream users need not unfold the definition.
decls.statement:
theorem cauchyPVExistsAt_iff {γ : ℝ → ℂ} {a b : ℝ} {f : ℂ → ℂ} {z₀ : ℂ} :
    CauchyPVExistsAt γ a b f z₀ ↔ ∃ L, HasCauchyPVAt γ a b f z₀ L

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.CauchyPVExistsAt.intro
decls.doc: Constructor for `CauchyPVExistsAt` from a `HasCauchyPVAt` witness.
decls.statement:
theorem CauchyPVExistsAt.intro {γ : ℝ → ℂ} {a b : ℝ} {f : ℂ → ℂ} {z₀ : ℂ} {L : ℂ}
    (h : HasCauchyPVAt γ a b f z₀ L) : CauchyPVExistsAt γ a b f z₀

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.intervalIntegrable_truncated_mul_deriv
decls.doc:
**The `ε`-truncated integrand is interval-integrable from a bound off the ball**: whenever
`f ∘ γ` is bounded by `M` at distance `> ε` from `z₀` and the truncated integrand is
a.e.-strongly measurable, the truncated integrand is dominated by `M · ‖deriv γ‖`.
decls.title: The `ε`-truncated integrand is interval-integrable from a bound off the ball
decls.statement:
theorem intervalIntegrable_truncated_mul_deriv {γ : ℝ → ℂ} {f : ℂ → ℂ} {z₀ : ℂ}
    {a b M ε : ℝ}
    (hderiv_int : IntervalIntegrable (fun t => deriv γ t) MeasureTheory.volume a b)
    (h_aesm : MeasureTheory.AEStronglyMeasurable
      (fun t => if ‖γ t - z₀‖ > ε then f (γ t) * deriv γ t else 0)
      (MeasureTheory.volume.restrict (Set.uIoc a b)))
    (h_bd : ∀ t : ℝ, ε < ‖γ t - z₀‖ → ‖f (γ t)‖ ≤ M) :
    IntervalIntegrable (fun t => if ‖γ t - z₀‖ > ε then f (γ t) * deriv γ t else 0)
      MeasureTheory.volume a b

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.HasCauchyPVAt.intro
decls.doc:
Constructor for `HasCauchyPVAt` from its two clauses — eventual integrability of the excised
integrand and convergence of the excised integrals — without unfolding the definition.
decls.statement:
theorem HasCauchyPVAt.intro {γ : ℝ → ℂ} {a b : ℝ} {f : ℂ → ℂ} {z₀ : ℂ} {L : ℂ}
    (hint : ∀ᶠ ε in 𝓝[>] (0 : ℝ), IntervalIntegrable
      (fun t => if ‖γ t - z₀‖ > ε then f (γ t) * deriv γ t else 0) MeasureTheory.volume a b)
    (htendsto : Tendsto
      (fun ε ↦ ∫ t in a..b, if ‖γ t - z₀‖ > ε then f (γ t) * deriv γ t else 0) (𝓝[>] 0) (𝓝 L)) :
    HasCauchyPVAt γ a b f z₀ L

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.HasCauchyPVAt.of_dist_lower_bound
decls.doc:
**Away from the pole the principal value is the ordinary integral.** On an interval where the
curve keeps distance `≥ m > 0` from `z₀`, every small enough truncation leaves the integrand
untouched, so the principal value at `z₀` is the plain integral. Continuity of the curve is not
needed — the distance bound and the eventual integrability carry both clauses. The endpoints
are not assumed ordered; the bound is stated on `uIcc a b`.
decls.title: Away from the pole the principal value is the ordinary integral
decls.statement:
theorem HasCauchyPVAt.of_dist_lower_bound {γ : ℝ → ℂ} {z₀ : ℂ} {f : ℂ → ℂ}
    {a b m : ℝ} (hm_pos : 0 < m)
    (h_far : ∀ t ∈ Set.uIcc a b, m ≤ ‖γ t - z₀‖)
    (h_int_tr : ∀ᶠ ε in 𝓝[>] (0 : ℝ), IntervalIntegrable
      (fun t => if ‖γ t - z₀‖ > ε then f (γ t) * deriv γ t else 0) MeasureTheory.volume a b) :
    HasCauchyPVAt γ a b f z₀ (∫ t in a..b, f (γ t) * deriv γ t)

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.HasCauchyPVAt.tendsto
decls.doc: The convergence clause of `HasCauchyPVAt`: the excised integrals tend to the value.
decls.statement:
theorem HasCauchyPVAt.tendsto {γ : ℝ → ℂ} {a b : ℝ} {f : ℂ → ℂ} {z₀ : ℂ} {L : ℂ}
    (h : HasCauchyPVAt γ a b f z₀ L) :
    Tendsto (fun ε ↦ ∫ t in a..b, if ‖γ t - z₀‖ > ε then f (γ t) * deriv γ t else 0)
      (𝓝[>] 0) (𝓝 L)

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.HasCauchyPVAt.eventually_intervalIntegrable
decls.doc: The integrability clause of `HasCauchyPVAt`: the excised integrand is eventually integrable.
decls.statement:
theorem HasCauchyPVAt.eventually_intervalIntegrable {γ : ℝ → ℂ} {a b : ℝ} {f : ℂ → ℂ} {z₀ : ℂ}
    {L : ℂ} (h : HasCauchyPVAt γ a b f z₀ L) :
    ∀ᶠ ε in 𝓝[>] (0 : ℝ), IntervalIntegrable
      (fun t => if ‖γ t - z₀‖ > ε then f (γ t) * deriv γ t else 0) MeasureTheory.volume a b

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.HasCauchyPVAt.cauchyPVAt_eq
decls.doc:
If `HasCauchyPVAt γ a b f z₀ L`, then `cauchyPVAt γ a b f z₀ = L`: the value function reads off
the limit whenever it exists.
decls.statement:
theorem HasCauchyPVAt.cauchyPVAt_eq {γ : ℝ → ℂ} {a b : ℝ} {f : ℂ → ℂ} {z₀ : ℂ} {L : ℂ}
