    (h : HasCauchyPVAt γ a b f z₀ L) : cauchyPVAt γ a b f z₀ = L

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.HasCauchyPVAt.unique
decls.doc: The value of the Cauchy principal value at `z₀` is unique.
decls.statement:
theorem HasCauchyPVAt.unique {γ : ℝ → ℂ} {a b : ℝ} {f : ℂ → ℂ} {z₀ : ℂ} {L₁ L₂ : ℂ}
    (h₁ : HasCauchyPVAt γ a b f z₀ L₁) (h₂ : HasCauchyPVAt γ a b f z₀ L₂) : L₁ = L₂

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.CauchyPVExistsAt.hasCauchyPVAt_cauchyPVAt
decls.doc:
If the principal value exists, it holds at the canonical value `cauchyPVAt`. This recovers a
`HasCauchyPVAt` statement from mere existence, as the winding-number value definition needs.

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.HasCauchyPVAt.congr_along_curve
decls.doc:
The principal value depends on the integrand only through its values along `γ` on the open
interval between `a` and `b`: if `f = g` on the image of `γ` restricted to `Set.uIoo a b`, their
principal values agree (endpoint values are invisible to the interval integral).

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.cauchyPVAt_congr_along_curve
decls.doc:
Value form of `HasCauchyPVAt.congr_along_curve`: the raw `cauchyPVAt` value only depends on
the integrand along `γ` on the open interval between `a` and `b`.

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.aeEq_restrict_uIoc_of_eqOn_uIoo
decls.doc:
`EqOn` on the open interval gives almost-everywhere equality on the half-open integration
interval: the two differ only at the right endpoint, which is null.

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.truncated_integrand_congr_ae
decls.doc:
The `ε`-truncated integrands of two curves that agree almost everywhere — with derivatives
agreeing almost everywhere off `z₀` — are themselves equal almost everywhere, for every positive
`ε`. Positivity is what makes the derivative hypothesis enough: at a point with `γ₁ t = z₀` the
truncation deletes both integrands.
decls.statement:
theorem truncated_integrand_congr_ae {γ₁ γ₂ : ℝ → ℂ} {a b : ℝ} {f : ℂ → ℂ} {z₀ : ℂ}
    (h_eq : γ₁ =ᵐ[MeasureTheory.volume.restrict (Set.uIoc a b)] γ₂)
    (h_deriv : ∀ᵐ t ∂MeasureTheory.volume.restrict (Set.uIoc a b),
      γ₁ t ≠ z₀ → deriv γ₁ t = deriv γ₂ t)
    {ε : ℝ} (hε : 0 < ε) :
    (fun t => if ‖γ₁ t - z₀‖ > ε then f (γ₁ t) * deriv γ₁ t else 0)
      =ᵐ[MeasureTheory.volume.restrict (Set.uIoc a b)]
    (fun t => if ‖γ₂ t - z₀‖ > ε then f (γ₂ t) * deriv γ₂ t else 0)

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.HasCauchyPVAt.congr_curve_ae
decls.doc:
**The principal value depends on the curve only up to null sets.** If `γ₁` and `γ₂` agree
almost everywhere on the integration interval, and their derivatives agree almost everywhere
*where the curve misses `z₀`*, their contour principal values agree.

Derivative agreement is only needed off `z₀`: the `ε`-truncation deletes the integrand wherever
`‖γ t - z₀‖ ≤ ε`, so for the positive `ε` the principal value ranges over, a point with
`γ₁ t = z₀` contributes `0` whatever the derivative there is. Curve agreement alone is still not
enough — the integrand contains `deriv γ`.
decls.title: The principal value depends on the curve only up to null sets
decls.statement:
theorem HasCauchyPVAt.congr_curve_ae {γ₁ γ₂ : ℝ → ℂ} {a b : ℝ} {f : ℂ → ℂ} {z₀ : ℂ} {L : ℂ}
    (h : HasCauchyPVAt γ₁ a b f z₀ L)
    (h_eq : γ₁ =ᵐ[MeasureTheory.volume.restrict (Set.uIoc a b)] γ₂)
    (h_deriv : ∀ᵐ t ∂MeasureTheory.volume.restrict (Set.uIoc a b),
      γ₁ t ≠ z₀ → deriv γ₁ t = deriv γ₂ t) :
    HasCauchyPVAt γ₂ a b f z₀ L

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.HasCauchyPVAt.congr_curve
decls.doc:
The principal value depends on the **curve** only through its values on the open interval
between `a` and `b`. Agreement on the *open* interval is enough even though the integrand involves
`deriv γ`, because an open set is a neighbourhood of each of its points (`Set.EqOn.deriv`), and
the endpoints are invisible to the interval integral.

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.CauchyPVExistsAt.congr_curve_ae
decls.doc: Existence form of `HasCauchyPVAt.congr_curve_ae`.
decls.statement:
theorem CauchyPVExistsAt.congr_curve_ae {γ₁ γ₂ : ℝ → ℂ} {a b : ℝ} {f : ℂ → ℂ} {z₀ : ℂ}
    (h : CauchyPVExistsAt γ₁ a b f z₀)
    (h_eq : γ₁ =ᵐ[MeasureTheory.volume.restrict (Set.uIoc a b)] γ₂)
    (h_deriv : ∀ᵐ t ∂MeasureTheory.volume.restrict (Set.uIoc a b),
      γ₁ t ≠ z₀ → deriv γ₁ t = deriv γ₂ t) :
    CauchyPVExistsAt γ₂ a b f z₀

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.CauchyPVExistsAt.congr_curve
decls.doc: Existence form of `HasCauchyPVAt.congr_curve`.

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.cauchyPVAt_congr_curve_ae
decls.doc:
Value form of `HasCauchyPVAt.congr_curve_ae`: the raw `cauchyPVAt` value is unchanged when the
curves agree almost everywhere on the integration interval and their derivatives agree almost
everywhere where the curve misses `z₀`. Curve equality alone does not suffice — the integrand
contains `deriv γ`.
decls.statement:
theorem cauchyPVAt_congr_curve_ae {γ₁ γ₂ : ℝ → ℂ} {a b : ℝ} {f : ℂ → ℂ} {z₀ : ℂ}
    (h_eq : γ₁ =ᵐ[MeasureTheory.volume.restrict (Set.uIoc a b)] γ₂)
    (h_deriv : ∀ᵐ t ∂MeasureTheory.volume.restrict (Set.uIoc a b),
      γ₁ t ≠ z₀ → deriv γ₁ t = deriv γ₂ t) :
    cauchyPVAt γ₁ a b f z₀ = cauchyPVAt γ₂ a b f z₀

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.cauchyPVAt_congr_curve
decls.doc: Value form of `HasCauchyPVAt.congr_curve`.

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.HasCauchyPVAt.const_mul
decls.doc: Scalar multiplication: if the principal value of `f` is `L`, that of `c • f` is `c • L`.

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.HasCauchyPVAt.add
decls.doc:
Additivity: the principal values of `f` and `g` add to that of `f + g`. Together with
`HasCauchyPVAt.const_mul` this is the `ℂ`-linearity of the principal value in the integrand.

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.HasCauchyPVAt.zero
decls.doc:
The principal value of the zero integrand is `0` — the additive identity for
`HasCauchyPVAt.add`.
decls.statement:
theorem HasCauchyPVAt.zero {γ : ℝ → ℂ} {a b : ℝ} {z₀ : ℂ} :
    HasCauchyPVAt γ a b (fun _ => 0) z₀ 0

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.cauchyPVAt_zero
decls.doc: The value form of `HasCauchyPVAt.zero`: the principal value of the zero integrand is `0`.
decls.statement:
theorem cauchyPVAt_zero {γ : ℝ → ℂ} {a b : ℝ} {z₀ : ℂ} :
    cauchyPVAt γ a b (fun _ => 0) z₀ = 0

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.HasCauchyPVAt.refl
decls.doc: The Cauchy principal value at a single point over a zero-length interval is `0`.
decls.statement:
theorem HasCauchyPVAt.refl (γ : ℝ → ℂ) (a : ℝ) (f : ℂ → ℂ) (z₀ : ℂ) :
    HasCauchyPVAt γ a a f z₀ 0

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.HasCauchyPVAt.of_eq
decls.doc: If the two endpoints are equal, the single-point Cauchy principal value is `0`.
decls.statement:
theorem HasCauchyPVAt.of_eq (γ : ℝ → ℂ) {a b : ℝ} (hab : a = b) (f : ℂ → ℂ) (z₀ : ℂ) :
    HasCauchyPVAt γ a b f z₀ 0

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.CauchyPVExistsAt.refl
decls.doc:
Existence form of `HasCauchyPVAt.refl`: a zero-length interval always has a single-point
Cauchy principal value.
decls.statement:
theorem CauchyPVExistsAt.refl (γ : ℝ → ℂ) (a : ℝ) (f : ℂ → ℂ) (z₀ : ℂ) :
    CauchyPVExistsAt γ a a f z₀

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.CauchyPVExistsAt.of_eq
decls.doc: Existence form of `HasCauchyPVAt.of_eq`.
decls.statement:
theorem CauchyPVExistsAt.of_eq (γ : ℝ → ℂ) {a b : ℝ} (hab : a = b) (f : ℂ → ℂ) (z₀ : ℂ) :
    CauchyPVExistsAt γ a b f z₀

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.cauchyPVAt_same
decls.doc:
Value form of `HasCauchyPVAt.refl`: the single-point Cauchy principal value on `[a, a]` is
`0`.
decls.statement:
theorem cauchyPVAt_same (γ : ℝ → ℂ) (a : ℝ) (f : ℂ → ℂ) (z₀ : ℂ) :
    cauchyPVAt γ a a f z₀ = 0

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.cauchyPVAt_eq_zero_of_eq
decls.doc: Value form of `HasCauchyPVAt.of_eq`.
decls.statement:
theorem cauchyPVAt_eq_zero_of_eq (γ : ℝ → ℂ) {a b : ℝ} (hab : a = b) (f : ℂ → ℂ) (z₀ : ℂ) :
    cauchyPVAt γ a b f z₀ = 0

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.HasCauchyPVAt.sum
decls.doc:
**Finite additivity.** The principal value of a finite sum of integrands is the sum of their
principal values. With `HasCauchyPVAt.zero` and `HasCauchyPVAt.add` this extends the `ℂ`-linearity
of the principal value to finite sums, as the generalized residue theorem's residue sum needs.
decls.title: Finite additivity

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.HasCauchyPVAt.of_avoidance
decls.doc:
**Avoidance.** If `γ` stays away from `z₀` throughout `[a, b]` and the ordinary contour
integrand is integrable there, the symmetric excision is eventually inert, so the principal value
exists and equals the ordinary contour integral.
decls.title: Avoidance
decls.statement:
theorem HasCauchyPVAt.of_avoidance {γ : ℝ → ℂ} {a b : ℝ} {f : ℂ → ℂ} {z₀ : ℂ}
    (h_cont : ContinuousOn γ (Set.uIcc a b))
    (h_avoid : ∀ t ∈ Set.uIcc a b, γ t ≠ z₀)
    (hf_int : IntervalIntegrable (fun t => f (γ t) * deriv γ t) MeasureTheory.volume a b) :
    HasCauchyPVAt γ a b f z₀ (∫ t in a..b, f (γ t) * deriv γ t)

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.HasCauchyPVAt.concat
decls.doc:
**Concatenation.** The principal values along adjacent subcurves `[a, b]` and `[b, c]` add to
the principal value along `[a, c]`. The integrability of the excised integrand across `[a, c]` and
the additivity of the integral both follow from the two given principal values, so no ordering or
separate integrability hypothesis is needed.
decls.title: Concatenation

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.cauchyPVExistsAt_of_dist_lower_bound
decls.doc: Existence form of `HasCauchyPVAt.of_dist_lower_bound`.
decls.statement:
theorem cauchyPVExistsAt_of_dist_lower_bound {γ : ℝ → ℂ} {z₀ : ℂ} {f : ℂ → ℂ} {a b m : ℝ}
    (hm_pos : 0 < m) (h_far : ∀ t ∈ Set.uIcc a b, m ≤ ‖γ t - z₀‖)
    (h_int_tr : ∀ᶠ ε in 𝓝[>] (0 : ℝ), IntervalIntegrable
      (fun t => if ‖γ t - z₀‖ > ε then f (γ t) * deriv γ t else 0) MeasureTheory.volume a b) :
    CauchyPVExistsAt γ a b f z₀

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.cauchyPVExistsAt_of_avoidance
decls.doc: Existence form of `HasCauchyPVAt.of_avoidance`.
decls.statement:
theorem cauchyPVExistsAt_of_avoidance {γ : ℝ → ℂ} {a b : ℝ} {f : ℂ → ℂ} {z₀ : ℂ}
    (h_cont : ContinuousOn γ (Set.uIcc a b))
    (h_avoid : ∀ t ∈ Set.uIcc a b, γ t ≠ z₀)
    (hf_int : IntervalIntegrable (fun t => f (γ t) * deriv γ t) MeasureTheory.volume a b) :
    CauchyPVExistsAt γ a b f z₀

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.CauchyPVExistsAt.const_mul
decls.doc: Existence-level scalar multiplication: scaling preserves existence of the principal value.

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.CauchyPVExistsAt.add
decls.doc:
Existence-level additivity: existence of the principal values of `f` and `g` gives that of
`f + g`.

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.CauchyPVExistsAt.zero
decls.doc: Existence-level: the zero integrand has a principal value.
decls.statement:
theorem CauchyPVExistsAt.zero {γ : ℝ → ℂ} {a b : ℝ} {z₀ : ℂ} :
    CauchyPVExistsAt γ a b (fun _ => 0) z₀

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.CauchyPVExistsAt.sum
decls.doc:
Existence-level finite additivity: if each summand has a principal value, so does the finite
sum of integrands.

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.HasCauchyPVAt.translate
decls.doc:
Simultaneously translating the curve and the excision point preserves a single-point Cauchy
principal value, provided the integrand is translated back by the same amount.

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.CauchyPVExistsAt.translate
decls.doc:
Existence form of `HasCauchyPVAt.translate`: simultaneous translation preserves existence of a
single-point Cauchy principal value.

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.cauchyPVAt_translate
decls.doc:
Value form of `HasCauchyPVAt.translate`: simultaneous translation preserves the single-point
Cauchy principal value.
decls.statement:
theorem cauchyPVAt_translate {γ : ℝ → ℂ} {a b : ℝ} {f : ℂ → ℂ} {z₀ : ℂ} (c : ℂ) :
    cauchyPVAt (fun t => γ t + c) a b (fun z => f (z - c)) (z₀ + c)
      = cauchyPVAt γ a b f z₀

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.truncated_const_mul_curve_eq
decls.doc:
Pointwise identity behind the scaling lemmas: multiplying the curve and excision point by a
nonzero `c` and rescaling the integrand by `z ↦ c⁻¹ * f (c⁻¹ * z)` turns the scaled truncated
integrand at radius `ε` into the original truncated integrand at radius `ε / ‖c‖`. The rescaling
factor `c⁻¹` cancels the derivative factor `c`, and the excision radius rescales by `‖c‖`. Shared by
`HasCauchyPVAt.const_mul_curve` and `cauchyPVAt_const_mul_curve`.
decls.statement:
theorem truncated_const_mul_curve_eq {γ : ℝ → ℂ} {f : ℂ → ℂ} {z₀ c : ℂ} (hc : c ≠ 0)
    (ε t : ℝ) :
    (if ‖c * γ t - c * z₀‖ > ε then
        (fun z => c⁻¹ * f (c⁻¹ * z)) (c * γ t) * deriv (fun t => c * γ t) t else 0)
      = if ‖γ t - z₀‖ > ε / ‖c‖ then f (γ t) * deriv γ t else 0

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.HasCauchyPVAt.const_mul_curve
decls.doc:
Simultaneously scaling the curve and the excision point by a nonzero complex number `c`
preserves a single-point Cauchy principal value, provided the integrand is rescaled by
`z ↦ c⁻¹ * f (c⁻¹ * z)`: the excision radius rescales by `‖c‖` and, after this rescaling, the two
truncated integrands agree along the scaled curve.

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.CauchyPVExistsAt.const_mul_curve
decls.doc:
Existence form of `HasCauchyPVAt.const_mul_curve`: nonzero scaling of the curve and excision
point preserves existence of a single-point Cauchy principal value.

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.limUnder_comp_of_map_eq
decls.doc:
Reindexing a `limUnder` by a self-map of the source filter that fixes it leaves the value
unchanged: if `Filter.map φ F = F`, then `limUnder F (g ∘ φ) = limUnder F g`, even when the limit
does not exist.
decls.statement:
theorem limUnder_comp_of_map_eq {α : Type*} {β : Type*} [TopologicalSpace β] [Nonempty β]
    {F : Filter α} {φ : α → α} (hφ : Filter.map φ F = F) (g : α → β) :
    Filter.limUnder F (g ∘ φ) = Filter.limUnder F g

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.cauchyPVAt_const_mul_curve
decls.doc:
Value form of `HasCauchyPVAt.const_mul_curve`: simultaneous nonzero scaling of the curve and the
excision point preserves the raw single-point Cauchy principal *value*, with no existence
hypothesis. Scaling only reindexes the excision radius by the order-isomorphism `ε ↦ ε / ‖c‖`, which
fixes the filter `𝓝[>] 0`, so the underlying `limUnder` is unchanged even when it does not
converge.
decls.statement:
theorem cauchyPVAt_const_mul_curve {γ : ℝ → ℂ} {a b : ℝ} {f : ℂ → ℂ} {z₀ c : ℂ} (hc : c ≠ 0) :
    cauchyPVAt (fun t => c * γ t) a b (fun z => c⁻¹ * f (c⁻¹ * z)) (c * z₀)
      = cauchyPVAt γ a b f z₀

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.HasCauchyPVAt.symm
decls.doc: Reversing the interval orientation negates a single-point Cauchy principal value.

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.CauchyPVExistsAt.symm
decls.doc:
Existence of a single-point Cauchy principal value is invariant under reversing the interval
orientation.

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.cauchyPVAt_symm
decls.doc:
Value form of `HasCauchyPVAt.symm`: if the single-point principal value exists on `[a, b]`,
then the value on `[b, a]` is its negative.

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.CauchyPVExistsAt.concat
decls.doc: Existence form of `HasCauchyPVAt.concat`.

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.HasCauchyPVWith.concat
decls.doc:
**Concatenation.** Principal values along the adjacent subcurves `[a, b]` and `[b, c]` that
excise the *same* finite set add to the principal value along `[a, c]`. As for
`HasCauchyPVAt.concat`, the integrability of the excised integrand across `[a, c]` and the
additivity of the integral both follow from the two given principal values, so no ordering or
separate integrability hypothesis is needed.
decls.title: Concatenation

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.HasCauchyPVWith.sub_right
decls.doc:
**Splitting off the far piece.** If the principal value along `[a, c]` and the one along
`[b, c]` excise the same finite set, then their difference is the principal value along `[a, b]`.
This is the direction that decomposes a contour: knowing the whole and one arc gives the rest.
decls.title: Splitting off the far piece

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.HasCauchyPVWith
decls.doc:
**The Cauchy principal value with a prescribed excision set.** Identical to `HasCauchyPV`
except that the finite set `S` of excised points is an explicit parameter rather than
existentially bound, which is what makes the principal values along adjacent subcurves
concatenable.
decls.title: The Cauchy principal value with a prescribed excision set
decls.statement: def HasCauchyPVWith (γ : ℝ → ℂ) (a b : ℝ) (f : ℂ → ℂ) (S : Finset ℂ) (v : ℂ) : Prop

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.hasCauchyPVWith_iff
decls.doc:
`HasCauchyPVWith` unfolded into its two clauses — eventual integrability of the excised
integrand and convergence of the excised integrals — so consumers need not unfold the
definition.
decls.statement:
theorem hasCauchyPVWith_iff {γ : ℝ → ℂ} {a b : ℝ} {f : ℂ → ℂ} {S : Finset ℂ} {v : ℂ} :
    HasCauchyPVWith γ a b f S v ↔
      (∀ᶠ ε in 𝓝[>] (0 : ℝ), IntervalIntegrable
          (fun t => if ∃ s ∈ S, ‖γ t - s‖ ≤ ε then 0 else f (γ t) * deriv γ t)
        MeasureTheory.volume a b) ∧
        Tendsto (fun ε ↦ ∫ t in a..b, if ∃ s ∈ S, ‖γ t - s‖ ≤ ε then 0 else f (γ t) * deriv γ t)
          (𝓝[>] 0) (𝓝 v)

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.HasCauchyPV
decls.doc:
The **Cauchy principal value on a set** of the contour integral `∮_γ f` exists with value `v`:
there is a finite set `S ⊆ ℂ` such that the truncated integrand along `γ` over `[a, b]`, zeroed
within a symmetric `ε`-ball of any point of `S`, is eventually `IntervalIntegrable` and its integral
tends to `v` as `ε → 0⁺`. The set is existential so the predicate stays `S`-free, intrinsic to
`(γ, f)`; the integrability clause prevents the `Tendsto` clause from being met vacuously through
the convention that a Bochner integral of a non-integrable function is `0`. Set-level companion of
`HasCauchyPVAt` (raw `γ : ℝ → ℂ`, `[a, b]`).
decls.statement: def HasCauchyPV (γ : ℝ → ℂ) (a b : ℝ) (f : ℂ → ℂ) (v : ℂ) : Prop

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.hasCauchyPV_iff
decls.doc:
Restatement of `HasCauchyPV` as the existence of a finite excision set making the excised
integrand eventually integrable and its integrals convergent, so consumers can characterize the
predicate without unfolding its definition.
decls.statement:
theorem hasCauchyPV_iff {γ : ℝ → ℂ} {a b : ℝ} {f : ℂ → ℂ} {v : ℂ} :
    HasCauchyPV γ a b f v ↔
      ∃ S : Finset ℂ,
        (∀ᶠ ε in 𝓝[>] (0 : ℝ), IntervalIntegrable
            (fun t => if ∃ s ∈ S, ‖γ t - s‖ ≤ ε then 0 else f (γ t) * deriv γ t)
            MeasureTheory.volume a b) ∧
          Tendsto (fun ε ↦ ∫ t in a..b, if ∃ s ∈ S, ‖γ t - s‖ ≤ ε then 0 else f (γ t) * deriv γ t)
            (𝓝[>] 0) (𝓝 v)

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.HasCauchyPV.intro
decls.doc:
Constructor for `HasCauchyPV` from a witnessing finite set `S` and its two clauses — eventual
integrability of the `S`-excised integrand and convergence of the excised integrals — without
unfolding the definition.
decls.statement:
theorem HasCauchyPV.intro {γ : ℝ → ℂ} {a b : ℝ} {f : ℂ → ℂ} {v : ℂ} (S : Finset ℂ)
    (h_int : ∀ᶠ ε in 𝓝[>] (0 : ℝ), IntervalIntegrable
        (fun t => if ∃ s ∈ S, ‖γ t - s‖ ≤ ε then 0 else f (γ t) * deriv γ t)
        MeasureTheory.volume a b)
    (h_tendsto : Tendsto
        (fun ε ↦ ∫ t in a..b, if ∃ s ∈ S, ‖γ t - s‖ ≤ ε then 0 else f (γ t) * deriv γ t)
        (𝓝[>] 0) (𝓝 v)) :
    HasCauchyPV γ a b f v

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.HasCauchyPVWith.hasCauchyPV
decls.doc: Forgetting the witness recovers the existentially-bound form.
decls.statement:
theorem HasCauchyPVWith.hasCauchyPV {γ : ℝ → ℂ} {a b : ℝ} {f : ℂ → ℂ} {S : Finset ℂ} {v : ℂ}
    (h : HasCauchyPVWith γ a b f S v) : HasCauchyPV γ a b f v

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.hasCauchyPV_iff_exists_hasCauchyPVWith
decls.doc:
`HasCauchyPV` is exactly `HasCauchyPVWith` with the excision set existentially quantified.

This is the abstraction-preserving bridge between the two forms, and is **not** redundant with
the definition: under the module system `HasCauchyPV`'s body is not exposed outside this file,
so `Iff.rfl` proves this only here and consumers elsewhere cannot unfold their way across. The
sibling `hasCauchyPV_iff` expands the truncation body instead, which loses the abstraction.
decls.statement:
theorem hasCauchyPV_iff_exists_hasCauchyPVWith {γ : ℝ → ℂ} {a b : ℝ} {f : ℂ → ℂ} {v : ℂ} :
    HasCauchyPV γ a b f v ↔ ∃ S : Finset ℂ, HasCauchyPVWith γ a b f S v

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.CauchyPVExists
decls.doc: The Cauchy principal value on a set exists: shorthand for `∃ v, HasCauchyPV γ a b f v`.
decls.statement: def CauchyPVExists (γ : ℝ → ℂ) (a b : ℝ) (f : ℂ → ℂ) : Prop

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.cauchyPVExists_iff
decls.doc:
Characterization of `CauchyPVExists` as the existence of a principal value — the
eliminator/constructor interface, so downstream users need not unfold the definition.
decls.statement:
theorem cauchyPVExists_iff {γ : ℝ → ℂ} {a b : ℝ} {f : ℂ → ℂ} :
    CauchyPVExists γ a b f ↔ ∃ v, HasCauchyPV γ a b f v

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.CauchyPVExists.intro
decls.doc: Constructor for `CauchyPVExists` from a `HasCauchyPV` witness.
decls.statement:
theorem CauchyPVExists.intro {γ : ℝ → ℂ} {a b : ℝ} {f : ℂ → ℂ} {v : ℂ}
    (h : HasCauchyPV γ a b f v) : CauchyPVExists γ a b f

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.HasCauchyPVAt.hasCauchyPV
decls.doc:
**From a point to a set.** The single-point principal value at `z₀` is the set-level principal
value with `S = {z₀}`: the single-point excision `‖γ t − z₀‖ > ε` (keep) is exactly the negation of
the set excision `∃ s ∈ {z₀}, ‖γ t − s‖ ≤ ε` (zero).
decls.title: From a point to a set
decls.statement:
theorem HasCauchyPVAt.hasCauchyPV {γ : ℝ → ℂ} {a b : ℝ} {f : ℂ → ℂ} {z₀ : ℂ} {L : ℂ}
    (h : HasCauchyPVAt γ a b f z₀ L) : HasCauchyPV γ a b f L

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.CauchyPVExistsAt.cauchyPVExists
decls.doc:
Existence form of `HasCauchyPVAt.hasCauchyPV`: if the single-point principal value at `z₀`
exists, so does the set-level principal value.
decls.statement:
theorem CauchyPVExistsAt.cauchyPVExists {γ : ℝ → ℂ} {a b : ℝ} {f : ℂ → ℂ} {z₀ : ℂ}
    (h : CauchyPVExistsAt γ a b f z₀) : CauchyPVExists γ a b f

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.HasCauchyPV.of_integrable
decls.doc:
**Integrable integrand.** If the ordinary contour integrand `t ↦ f (γ t) · γ'(t)` is
`IntervalIntegrable` on `[a, b]`, then the empty excision (`S = ∅`) is inert, so the principal value
exists and equals the ordinary contour integral `∫_a^b f (γ t) · γ'(t) dt`.
decls.title: Integrable integrand

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.eventually_not_exists_mem_le
decls.doc:
If `z` is none of the finitely many points of `S`, then for all small enough `ε > 0` the point
`z` is farther than `ε` from every point of `S`; i.e. the excision at `S` eventually keeps `z`.
decls.statement:
theorem eventually_not_exists_mem_le (z : ℂ) (S : Finset ℂ) (h : ∀ s ∈ S, z ≠ s) :
    ∀ᶠ ε in 𝓝[>] (0 : ℝ), ¬ ∃ s ∈ S, ‖z - s‖ ≤ ε

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.HasCauchyPVWith.of_integrable_of_crossings_measure_zero
decls.doc:
**An integrable integrand has principal value the ordinary integral, for *any* prescribed
excision set.** Where the contour integrand is interval-integrable and the curve meets the excised
points only on a null set of parameters, shrinking the excised neighbourhoods recovers the ordinary
integral: for each fixed `ε` the excision may perturb the integrand on a set of positive measure,
but as `ε → 0⁺` the excised integrands converge almost everywhere to the original one, since the
limiting crossing set is null.

The strength here is that `S` is arbitrary: the conclusion holds for whatever excision set another
principal value happens to be witnessed by, which is what lets an arc carrying no singularity be
subtracted off via `HasCauchyPVWith.sub_right` without knowing that witness. Compare
`HasCauchyPV.of_integrable`, which proves the weaker existential form by exhibiting `S = ∅`.
decls.statement:
theorem HasCauchyPVWith.of_integrable_of_crossings_measure_zero {γ : ℝ → ℂ} {a b : ℝ} {f : ℂ → ℂ}
    (S : Finset ℂ) (hγ : AEMeasurable γ (MeasureTheory.volume.restrict (Set.uIoc a b)))
    (h_int : IntervalIntegrable (fun t => f (γ t) * deriv γ t) MeasureTheory.volume a b)
    (h_null : MeasureTheory.volume (⋃ s ∈ S, Set.uIoc a b ∩ γ ⁻¹' {s}) = 0) :
    HasCauchyPVWith γ a b f S (∫ t in a..b, f (γ t) * deriv γ t)

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.HasCauchyPVWith.of_integrable_of_finite_crossings
decls.doc:
Finite-crossings form of `HasCauchyPVWith.of_integrable_of_crossings_measure_zero`: a curve
meeting each excised point only finitely often meets them on a null set of parameters. This is
the form contour arguments consume: `IsPwC1ImmersionOn.finite_crossings` (HW Prop 2.2) supplies
finiteness on the closed interval, from which this follows by `Set.Finite.subset` along
`Set.uIoc_subset_uIcc`.
decls.statement:
theorem HasCauchyPVWith.of_integrable_of_finite_crossings {γ : ℝ → ℂ} {a b : ℝ} {f : ℂ → ℂ}
    (S : Finset ℂ) (hγ : AEMeasurable γ (MeasureTheory.volume.restrict (Set.uIoc a b)))
    (h_int : IntervalIntegrable (fun t => f (γ t) * deriv γ t) MeasureTheory.volume a b)
    (h_fin : ∀ s ∈ S, (Set.uIoc a b ∩ γ ⁻¹' {s}).Finite) :
    HasCauchyPVWith γ a b f S (∫ t in a..b, f (γ t) * deriv γ t)

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.HasCauchyPV.zero
decls.doc:
**Zero integrand.** The principal value of the zero integrand is `0`, witnessed by the empty
excision: the truncated integrand is identically `0`, hence integrable with vanishing integral.
decls.title: Zero integrand
decls.statement: theorem HasCauchyPV.zero {γ : ℝ → ℂ} {a b : ℝ} : HasCauchyPV γ a b (fun _ => 0) 0

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.HasCauchyPV.const_mul
decls.doc:
**Scaling by a constant.** Scaling the integrand by `c : ℂ` scales the principal value by `c`,
reusing the same excision set: the truncation and the integral both commute with multiplication by
the constant `c`.
decls.title: Scaling by a constant
decls.statement:
theorem HasCauchyPV.const_mul {γ : ℝ → ℂ} {a b : ℝ} {f : ℂ → ℂ} {v : ℂ}
    (h : HasCauchyPV γ a b f v) (c : ℂ) : HasCauchyPV γ a b (fun z => c * f z) (c * v)

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.HasCauchyPVWith.congr_curve
decls.doc:
**Changing the curve.** Two curves that agree on the open parameter interval
have the same principal value: both the excision test `‖γ t - s‖ ≤ ε` and the integrand
`f (γ t) * deriv γ t` are computed pointwise from the curve, the derivatives agree automatically
because the interval is open, and the endpoints do not affect an interval integral.

This is what lets a contour identity be restated along a more convenient parametrization — for
instance replacing a piece of a closed contour by the straight line it traces.
decls.title: Changing the curve

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.HasCauchyPV.congr_curve
decls.doc:
Curve congruence for the primary predicate: `HasCauchyPVWith.congr_curve` with the excision
set re-hidden, so consumers need not name it.

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.CauchyPVExists.congr_curve
decls.doc: Existence form of `HasCauchyPV.congr_curve`.

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.HasCauchyPV.congr_along_curve
decls.doc:
**Congruence along the curve.** If `f` and `g` agree along `γ` on the open interval `Set.uIoo a
b`, they share the same principal value there, with the same excision set (the endpoints are
invisible to the interval integral; the excised integrand reads `f` only through `f (γ t)`).
decls.title: Congruence along the curve

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.CauchyPVExists.zero
decls.doc: Existence form of `HasCauchyPV.zero`: the principal value of the zero integrand exists.
decls.statement: theorem CauchyPVExists.zero {γ : ℝ → ℂ} {a b : ℝ} : CauchyPVExists γ a b (fun _ => 0)

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.CauchyPVExists.const_mul
decls.doc:
Existence form of `HasCauchyPV.const_mul`: if the principal value of `f` exists, so does that of
`fun z => c * f z`.
decls.statement:
theorem CauchyPVExists.const_mul {γ : ℝ → ℂ} {a b : ℝ} {f : ℂ → ℂ}
    (h : CauchyPVExists γ a b f) (c : ℂ) : CauchyPVExists γ a b (fun z => c * f z)

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.CauchyPVExists.congr_along_curve
decls.doc:
Existence form of `HasCauchyPV.congr_along_curve`: agreement along `γ` on `Set.uIoo a b`
transports existence of the principal value from `f` to `g`.

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.truncatedIntegrand
decls.doc:
The `S`-excised contour integrand `t ↦ f (γ t) · γ'(t)`, set to `0` within a symmetric
`ε`-ball of any point of the finite set `S`. This names the integrand whose truncated integral
defines the set-level principal value, keeping the enlargement-inertness proof readable.
decls.statement:
def truncatedIntegrand (γ : ℝ → ℂ) (f : ℂ → ℂ) (S : Finset ℂ) (ε t : ℝ) :
    ℂ

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.countable_setOf_deriv_ne_zero_on_fiber
decls.doc:
On the level set `{x | g x = c}`, the derivative of `g` vanishes off a countable set: a point
of the level set with nonzero derivative cannot be an accumulation point of the level set (else its
derivative would be `0` by `deriv_zero_of_frequently_const`), hence it is isolated on the left in
the level set, and left-isolated points of a set in `ℝ` form a countable set.
decls.statement:
theorem countable_setOf_deriv_ne_zero_on_fiber (g : ℝ → ℂ) (c : ℂ) :
    {x : ℝ | g x = c ∧ deriv g x ≠ 0}.Countable

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.exists_pos_separating_intervalIntegrable_truncatedIntegrand
decls.doc:
**A separating, integrable excision radius.** If the truncated integrands for `S₁` and `S₂` are
eventually integrable as `ε → 0⁺`, there is a single `ε₀ > 0` at which both are integrable and at
which distinct points of `S₁` and `S₂` are more than `2 * ε₀` apart.
decls.title: A separating, integrable excision radius
decls.statement:
theorem exists_pos_separating_intervalIntegrable_truncatedIntegrand {γ : ℝ → ℂ} {a b : ℝ}
    {f : ℂ → ℂ} (S₁ S₂ : Finset ℂ)
    (hint₁ : ∀ᶠ ε in 𝓝[>] (0 : ℝ),
      IntervalIntegrable (truncatedIntegrand γ f S₁ ε) MeasureTheory.volume a b)
    (hint₂ : ∀ᶠ ε in 𝓝[>] (0 : ℝ),
      IntervalIntegrable (truncatedIntegrand γ f S₂ ε) MeasureTheory.volume a b) :
    ∃ ε₀ : ℝ, 0 < ε₀ ∧ (∀ s₁ ∈ S₁, ∀ s₂ ∈ S₂, s₁ ≠ s₂ → 2 * ε₀ < ‖s₁ - s₂‖) ∧
      IntervalIntegrable (truncatedIntegrand γ f S₁ ε₀) MeasureTheory.volume a b ∧
      IntervalIntegrable (truncatedIntegrand γ f S₂ ε₀) MeasureTheory.volume a b

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.norm_truncatedIntegrand_sub_le
decls.doc:
**Pointwise domination of the truncated difference.** When distinct points of `S₁` and `S₂` are
more than `2 * ε₀` apart and `ε < ε₀`, the truncated-integrand difference at `ε` is bounded
pointwise by the sum of the `ε₀`-truncation norms: a point excised at `ε` by one set but not the
other is, by the `2·ε₀`-separation, more than `ε₀` from that other set — so the other set's
`ε₀`-truncation retains the full integrand value there, and that value dominates the difference.
decls.title: Pointwise domination of the truncated difference
decls.statement:
theorem norm_truncatedIntegrand_sub_le {γ : ℝ → ℂ} {f : ℂ → ℂ} {S₁ S₂ : Finset ℂ}
    {ε ε₀ : ℝ} (t : ℝ) (hεlt : ε < ε₀)
    (hP1 : ∀ s₁ ∈ S₁, ∀ s₂ ∈ S₂, s₁ ≠ s₂ → 2 * ε₀ < ‖s₁ - s₂‖) :
    ‖truncatedIntegrand γ f S₁ ε t - truncatedIntegrand γ f S₂ ε t‖ ≤
      ‖truncatedIntegrand γ f S₁ ε₀ t‖ + ‖truncatedIntegrand γ f S₂ ε₀ t‖

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.tendsto_truncatedIntegrand_sub_ae
decls.doc:
**Pointwise a.e. vanishing of the truncated difference.** For almost every `t`, the
truncated-integrand difference tends to `0` as `ε → 0⁺`: off the null set where `γ` meets `S₁ ∪ S₂`
with nonzero derivative, either the excess `f (γ t) · γ' t` already vanishes, or `γ t` avoids both
excision sets and both truncations eventually keep it.
decls.title: Pointwise a.e. vanishing of the truncated difference
decls.statement:
theorem tendsto_truncatedIntegrand_sub_ae {γ : ℝ → ℂ} {a b : ℝ} {f : ℂ → ℂ}
    (S₁ S₂ : Finset ℂ) :
    ∀ᵐ t ∂MeasureTheory.volume, t ∈ Set.uIoc a b →
      Tendsto (fun ε => truncatedIntegrand γ f S₁ ε t - truncatedIntegrand γ f S₂ ε t)
        (𝓝[>] (0 : ℝ)) (𝓝 (0 : ℂ))

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.tendsto_integral_truncatedIntegrand_sub
decls.doc:
**Enlargement inertness of the excision set (difference form).** For finite excision sets `S₁`
and `S₂` whose truncated integrands are eventually integrable, the difference of the two truncated
contour integrals tends to `0` as `ε → 0⁺`. On the overlap the truncations agree; the mass on the
symmetric difference sits within `ε` of finitely many points and, being dominated by a fixed-`ε₀`
truncation (using that the excision sets are finite and disjoint from each other's excess points),
is killed in the limit by dominated convergence, the excess `f (γ ·) · γ'` vanishing a.e. on each
singleton fibre of `γ`.
decls.title: Enlargement inertness of the excision set (difference form)
decls.statement:
theorem tendsto_integral_truncatedIntegrand_sub {γ : ℝ → ℂ} {a b : ℝ} {f : ℂ → ℂ}
    (S₁ S₂ : Finset ℂ)
    (hint₁ : ∀ᶠ ε in 𝓝[>] (0 : ℝ),
      IntervalIntegrable (truncatedIntegrand γ f S₁ ε) MeasureTheory.volume a b)
    (hint₂ : ∀ᶠ ε in 𝓝[>] (0 : ℝ),
      IntervalIntegrable (truncatedIntegrand γ f S₂ ε) MeasureTheory.volume a b) :
    Tendsto (fun ε => (∫ t in a..b, truncatedIntegrand γ f S₁ ε t)
        - ∫ t in a..b, truncatedIntegrand γ f S₂ ε t) (𝓝[>] (0 : ℝ)) (𝓝 0)

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.HasCauchyPV.unique
decls.doc:
**Uniqueness of the set-level principal value.** Any two values of the Cauchy principal value on
a set coincide. Unlike the single-point case, the two witnesses may use *different* finite excision
sets; enlargement inertness (`tendsto_integral_truncatedIntegrand_sub`) shows the difference of
their truncated integrals vanishes in the limit, so the two limits agree.
decls.title: Uniqueness of the set-level principal value
decls.statement:
theorem HasCauchyPV.unique {γ : ℝ → ℂ} {a b : ℝ} {f : ℂ → ℂ} {v₁ v₂ : ℂ}
    (h₁ : HasCauchyPV γ a b f v₁) (h₂ : HasCauchyPV γ a b f v₂) : v₁ = v₂

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.cauchyPV
decls.doc:
The **value** of the set-level Cauchy principal value: the common limit when it exists, and the
junk value `0` otherwise. Read it off a `HasCauchyPV` witness via `HasCauchyPV.cauchyPV_eq`.
decls.statement: def cauchyPV (γ : ℝ → ℂ) (a b : ℝ) (f : ℂ → ℂ) : ℂ

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.HasCauchyPV.cauchyPV_eq
decls.doc:
If `HasCauchyPV γ a b f v`, then `cauchyPV γ a b f = v`: the value function reads off the
principal value whenever it exists, by uniqueness.
decls.statement:
theorem HasCauchyPV.cauchyPV_eq {γ : ℝ → ℂ} {a b : ℝ} {f : ℂ → ℂ} {v : ℂ}
    (h : HasCauchyPV γ a b f v) : cauchyPV γ a b f = v

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.cauchyPV_congr_curve
decls.doc:
Value form of `HasCauchyPV.congr_curve`: curves agreeing on the open parameter interval have
the same principal value, whether or not it exists (both sides are `0` when it does not).
decls.statement:
theorem cauchyPV_congr_curve {γ₁ γ₂ : ℝ → ℂ} {a b : ℝ} {f : ℂ → ℂ}
    (h_eq : Set.EqOn γ₁ γ₂ (Set.uIoo a b)) : cauchyPV γ₁ a b f = cauchyPV γ₂ a b f

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.cauchyPV_zero
decls.doc: The value form of `HasCauchyPV.zero`: the principal value of the zero integrand is `0`.
decls.statement:
theorem cauchyPV_zero {γ : ℝ → ℂ} {a b : ℝ} :
    cauchyPV γ a b (fun _ => 0) = 0

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.HasCauchyPV.refl
decls.doc: The set-level Cauchy principal value over a zero-length interval is `0`.
decls.statement:
theorem HasCauchyPV.refl (γ : ℝ → ℂ) (a : ℝ) (f : ℂ → ℂ) :
    HasCauchyPV γ a a f 0

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.HasCauchyPV.of_eq
decls.doc: If the two endpoints are equal, the set-level Cauchy principal value is `0`.
decls.statement:
theorem HasCauchyPV.of_eq (γ : ℝ → ℂ) {a b : ℝ} (hab : a = b) (f : ℂ → ℂ) :
    HasCauchyPV γ a b f 0

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.CauchyPVExists.refl
decls.doc:
Existence form of `HasCauchyPV.refl`: a zero-length interval always has a set-level Cauchy
principal value.
decls.statement:
theorem CauchyPVExists.refl (γ : ℝ → ℂ) (a : ℝ) (f : ℂ → ℂ) :
    CauchyPVExists γ a a f

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.CauchyPVExists.of_eq
decls.doc: Existence form of `HasCauchyPV.of_eq`.
decls.statement:
theorem CauchyPVExists.of_eq (γ : ℝ → ℂ) {a b : ℝ} (hab : a = b) (f : ℂ → ℂ) :
    CauchyPVExists γ a b f

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.cauchyPV_same
decls.doc: Value form of `HasCauchyPV.refl`: the set-level Cauchy principal value on `[a, a]` is `0`.
decls.statement:
theorem cauchyPV_same (γ : ℝ → ℂ) (a : ℝ) (f : ℂ → ℂ) :
    cauchyPV γ a a f = 0

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.cauchyPV_eq_zero_of_eq
decls.doc: Value form of `HasCauchyPV.of_eq`.
decls.statement:
theorem cauchyPV_eq_zero_of_eq (γ : ℝ → ℂ) {a b : ℝ} (hab : a = b) (f : ℂ → ℂ) :
    cauchyPV γ a b f = 0

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.CauchyPVExists.hasCauchyPV_cauchyPV
decls.doc:
If the set-level principal value exists, it holds at the canonical value `cauchyPV`. This
recovers a `HasCauchyPV` statement from mere existence.
decls.statement:
theorem CauchyPVExists.hasCauchyPV_cauchyPV {γ : ℝ → ℂ} {a b : ℝ} {f : ℂ → ℂ}
    (h : CauchyPVExists γ a b f) : HasCauchyPV γ a b f (cauchyPV γ a b f)

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.HasCauchyPV.symm
decls.doc: Reversing the interval orientation negates a set-level Cauchy principal value.

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.CauchyPVExists.symm
decls.doc:
Existence of a set-level Cauchy principal value is invariant under reversing the interval
orientation.

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.cauchyPV_symm
decls.doc:
Value form of `HasCauchyPV.symm`: if the set-level principal value exists on `[a, b]`, then
the value on `[b, a]` is its negative.

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.truncatedIntegrand_union_integrable
decls.doc:
Enlarging the excision set preserves interval-integrability of the truncated integrand: the
extra excision at `S'` only zeroes the integrand within the `[[a, b]]`-closed set where some
`s ∈ S'` comes within `ε` of the curve, so integrability transfers from `S` to `S ∪ S'`. Needs
the curve continuous on `[[a, b]]`.
decls.statement:
theorem truncatedIntegrand_union_integrable {γ : ℝ → ℂ} {a b : ℝ} {f : ℂ → ℂ}
    (hγ_cont : ContinuousOn γ (Set.uIcc a b)) {S : Finset ℂ} {ε : ℝ} (S' : Finset ℂ)
    (h : IntervalIntegrable (truncatedIntegrand γ f S ε) MeasureTheory.volume a b) :
    IntervalIntegrable (truncatedIntegrand γ f (S ∪ S') ε) MeasureTheory.volume a b

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.HasCauchyPV.add
decls.doc:
**Additivity.** The set-level principal value is additive: if `f₁` and `f₂` each have a
principal value along `γ`, so does `f₁ + f₂`, with the sum as value. The summands may excise
different finite sets, reconciled on the union `S₁ ∪ S₂`; this needs the curve continuous on
`[[a, b]]`, unlike `const_mul`, which reuses a single excision set.
decls.title: Additivity
decls.statement:
theorem HasCauchyPV.add {γ : ℝ → ℂ} {a b : ℝ} {f₁ f₂ : ℂ → ℂ} {v₁ v₂ : ℂ}
    (hγ_cont : ContinuousOn γ (Set.uIcc a b))
    (h₁ : HasCauchyPV γ a b f₁ v₁) (h₂ : HasCauchyPV γ a b f₂ v₂) :
    HasCauchyPV γ a b (fun z => f₁ z + f₂ z) (v₁ + v₂)

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.HasCauchyPV.sum
decls.doc:
**Finite additivity.** A finite sum of set-level principal values is the principal value of the
summed integrand — the additive companion to `HasCauchyPV.const_mul`, built from `zero` and `add`
(hence the curve-continuity hypothesis).
decls.title: Finite additivity
decls.statement:
theorem HasCauchyPV.sum {ι : Type*} {γ : ℝ → ℂ} {a b : ℝ} {f : ι → ℂ → ℂ} {v : ι → ℂ}
    {s : Finset ι} (hγ_cont : ContinuousOn γ (Set.uIcc a b))
    (h : ∀ i ∈ s, HasCauchyPV γ a b (f i) (v i)) :
    HasCauchyPV γ a b (fun z => ∑ i ∈ s, f i z) (∑ i ∈ s, v i)

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.HasCauchyPV.congr_along_curve_off
decls.doc:
**Congruence along the curve off excised points**: if `f` and `g` agree along `γ` at every
parameter where `γ` avoids the finite set `P`, a principal value of `f` is one of `g` — the
witnessing excision enlarges to include `P`, and off the enlarged excision the curve avoids
`P`. Needs the curve continuous on `[[a, b]]` for the enlargement.
decls.title: Congruence along the curve off excised points
decls.statement:
theorem HasCauchyPV.congr_along_curve_off {γ : ℝ → ℂ} {a b : ℝ} {f g : ℂ → ℂ} {v : ℂ}
    (hγ_cont : ContinuousOn γ (Set.uIcc a b)) (P : Finset ℂ)
    (h : HasCauchyPV γ a b f v)
    (h_eq : ∀ t ∈ Set.uIoo a b, γ t ∉ (P : Set ℂ) → f (γ t) = g (γ t)) :
    HasCauchyPV γ a b g v

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.CauchyPVExists.add
decls.doc: Existence form of `HasCauchyPV.add`.
decls.statement:
theorem CauchyPVExists.add {γ : ℝ → ℂ} {a b : ℝ} {f g : ℂ → ℂ}
    (hγ_cont : ContinuousOn γ (Set.uIcc a b))
    (hf : CauchyPVExists γ a b f) (hg : CauchyPVExists γ a b g) :
    CauchyPVExists γ a b (fun z => f z + g z)

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.CauchyPVExists.sum
decls.doc: Existence form of `HasCauchyPV.sum`.
decls.statement:
theorem CauchyPVExists.sum {ι : Type*} {γ : ℝ → ℂ} {a b : ℝ} {f : ι → ℂ → ℂ} {s : Finset ι}
    (hγ_cont : ContinuousOn γ (Set.uIcc a b))
    (h : ∀ i ∈ s, CauchyPVExists γ a b (f i)) :
    CauchyPVExists γ a b (fun z => ∑ i ∈ s, f i z)

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.tendsto_normalize_slope
decls.doc: Normalising a slope with a non-zero limit converges to the normalised limit.
decls.statement:
theorem tendsto_normalize_slope {l : Filter ℝ} (hL : L ≠ 0)
    (hslope : Tendsto (slope γ t₀) l (𝓝 L)) :
    Tendsto (fun t => NormedSpace.normalize (slope γ t₀ t)) l
      (𝓝 (NormedSpace.normalize L))

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.tendsto_normalize_sub_nhdsGT
decls.doc:
**The outgoing chord direction.** As `t → t₀⁺` the direction of `γ t - z₀` tends to that
of the one-sided slope limit.
decls.title: The outgoing chord direction
decls.statement:
theorem tendsto_normalize_sub_nhdsGT (hcross : γ t₀ = z₀) (hL : L ≠ 0)
    (hslope : Tendsto (slope γ t₀) (𝓝[>] t₀) (𝓝 L)) :
    Tendsto (fun t => NormedSpace.normalize (γ t - z₀)) (𝓝[>] t₀)
      (𝓝 (NormedSpace.normalize L))

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.tendsto_normalize_sub_nhdsLT
decls.doc:
**The incoming chord direction, reversed.** As `t → t₀⁻` the direction of `γ t - z₀` tends
to the *negative* of that of the one-sided slope limit, since `t - t₀` is negative there.
decls.title: The incoming chord direction, reversed
decls.statement:
theorem tendsto_normalize_sub_nhdsLT (hcross : γ t₀ = z₀) (hL : L ≠ 0)
    (hslope : Tendsto (slope γ t₀) (𝓝[<] t₀) (𝓝 L)) :
    Tendsto (fun t => NormedSpace.normalize (γ t - z₀)) (𝓝[<] t₀)
      (𝓝 (-NormedSpace.normalize L))

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.chord_quotient_tendsto
decls.doc:
**Chord-to-tangent quotient limit.** Given `HasDerivWithinAt γ L u t₀` with `t₀ ∉ u` and
`γ t₀ = s`, the chord quotient `(γ t - s) / (t - t₀)` tends to `L` along `𝓝[u] t₀`.
Specialises to the one-sided limits at `u = Ioi t₀` (right) and `u = Iio t₀` (left).
decls.title: Chord-to-tangent quotient limit
decls.statement:
theorem chord_quotient_tendsto {u : Set ℝ} (hu : t₀ ∉ u)
    (h_deriv : HasDerivWithinAt γ L u t₀) (h_at : γ t₀ = s) :
    Tendsto (fun t : ℝ => (γ t - s) / ((t - t₀ : ℝ) : ℂ)) (𝓝[u] t₀) (𝓝 L)

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.eventually_normalized_chord_close
decls.doc:
**The normalized chord is eventually close to `1`**: for any `ρ > 0`, eventually along
`𝓝[u] t₀`, `‖(γ t - s) / (L (t - t₀)) - 1‖ ≤ ρ`.
decls.title: The normalized chord is eventually close to `1`
decls.statement:
theorem eventually_normalized_chord_close {u : Set ℝ} (hu : t₀ ∉ u)
    (h_deriv : HasDerivWithinAt γ L u t₀) (h_at : γ t₀ = s) (hL : L ≠ 0)
    {ρ : ℝ} (hρ_pos : 0 < ρ) :
    ∀ᶠ t in 𝓝[u] t₀, ‖(γ t - s) / (L * ((t - t₀ : ℝ) : ℂ)) - 1‖ ≤ ρ

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.exists_normalized_chord_bound_right
decls.doc:
**Fixed-radius normalized chord bound (right side)**: a positive radius `r` on whose
right interval `(t₀, t₀ + r]` the normalized chord is uniformly `ρ`-close to `1`.
decls.title: Fixed-radius normalized chord bound (right side)
decls.statement:
theorem exists_normalized_chord_bound_right
    (h_deriv : HasDerivWithinAt γ L (Ioi t₀) t₀) (h_at : γ t₀ = s) (hL : L ≠ 0)
    {ρ : ℝ} (hρ_pos : 0 < ρ) :
    ∃ r > 0, ∀ t ∈ Ioc t₀ (t₀ + r),
      ‖(γ t - s) / (L * ((t - t₀ : ℝ) : ℂ)) - 1‖ ≤ ρ

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.exists_normalized_chord_bound_left
decls.doc:
**Fixed-radius normalized chord bound (left side)**: the counterpart of
`exists_normalized_chord_bound_right` on `[t₀ - r, t₀)`.
decls.title: Fixed-radius normalized chord bound (left side)
decls.statement:
theorem exists_normalized_chord_bound_left
    (h_deriv : HasDerivWithinAt γ L (Iio t₀) t₀) (h_at : γ t₀ = s) (hL : L ≠ 0)
    {ρ : ℝ} (hρ_pos : 0 < ρ) :
    ∃ r > 0, ∀ t ∈ Ico (t₀ - r) t₀,
      ‖(γ t - s) / (L * ((t - t₀ : ℝ) : ℂ)) - 1‖ ≤ ρ

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.div_mem_slitPlane_of_close_to_one
decls.doc:
**Slit-plane condition for quotients near `1`.** If `‖z - 1‖ ≤ 1/4` and `‖w - 1‖ ≤ 1/4`,
then `z / w ∈ Complex.slitPlane`: the quotient stays in the unit ball around `1`.
decls.title: Slit-plane condition for quotients near `1`

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.ofReal_pos_mul_mem_slitPlane
decls.doc: Multiplication by a positive real preserves membership in `Complex.slitPlane`.
decls.statement:
theorem ofReal_pos_mul_mem_slitPlane {c : ℝ} (hc : 0 < c) {z : ℂ}
    (hz : z ∈ Complex.slitPlane) : ((c : ℝ) : ℂ) * z ∈ Complex.slitPlane

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.chord_quotient_mem_slitPlane
decls.doc:
**Chord quotient in the slit plane (algebraic core).** If the normalized chords at `a` and
`b` are `1/4`-close to `1` and `a`, `b` lie on a common side of `t₀` — so that
`(b - t₀) / (a - t₀) > 0` — then `(γ b - s) / (γ a - s) ∈ Complex.slitPlane`.
decls.title: Chord quotient in the slit plane (algebraic core)
decls.statement:
theorem chord_quotient_mem_slitPlane (hL : L ≠ 0) {a b : ℝ}
    (ha : ‖(γ a - s) / (L * ((a - t₀ : ℝ) : ℂ)) - 1‖ ≤ 1 / 4)
    (hb : ‖(γ b - s) / (L * ((b - t₀ : ℝ) : ℂ)) - 1‖ ≤ 1 / 4)
    (hab : 0 < (b - t₀) / (a - t₀)) :
    (γ b - s) / (γ a - s) ∈ Complex.slitPlane

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.exists_chord_quotient_mem_slitPlane_right
decls.doc:
**Chord quotients on a small right interval lie in the slit plane**: there is `r > 0` such
that `(γ b - s) / (γ a - s) ∈ Complex.slitPlane` whenever `t₀ < a ≤ b ≤ t₀ + r`.
decls.title: Chord quotients on a small right interval lie in the slit plane
decls.statement:
theorem exists_chord_quotient_mem_slitPlane_right
    (h_deriv : HasDerivWithinAt γ L (Ioi t₀) t₀) (h_at : γ t₀ = s) (hL : L ≠ 0) :
    ∃ r > 0, ∀ a b, t₀ < a → a ≤ b → b ≤ t₀ + r →
      (γ b - s) / (γ a - s) ∈ Complex.slitPlane

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.exists_chord_quotient_mem_slitPlane_left
decls.doc:
**Chord quotients on a small left interval lie in the slit plane**: there is `r > 0` such
that `(γ b - s) / (γ a - s) ∈ Complex.slitPlane` whenever `t₀ - r ≤ a ≤ b < t₀`. Stated with
`a` the left endpoint — the form in which the argument-lift fundamental theorem of calculus
consumes it on the left excised piece.
decls.title: Chord quotients on a small left interval lie in the slit plane
decls.statement:
theorem exists_chord_quotient_mem_slitPlane_left
    (h_deriv : HasDerivWithinAt γ L (Iio t₀) t₀) (h_at : γ t₀ = s) (hL : L ≠ 0) :
    ∃ r > 0, ∀ a b, t₀ - r ≤ a → a ≤ b → b < t₀ →
      (γ b - s) / (γ a - s) ∈ Complex.slitPlane

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.arg_tendsto_of_pos_mul_tendsto
decls.doc:
**Positive real scaling does not move the argument**: if `Q ∈ slitPlane`, `c ε > 0`
eventually, and `(c ε : ℂ) * f ε → Q`, then `arg (f ε) → arg Q`.
decls.title: Positive real scaling does not move the argument
decls.statement:
theorem arg_tendsto_of_pos_mul_tendsto {α : Type*} {l : Filter α} {c : α → ℝ} {f : α → ℂ}
    {Q : ℂ} (hQ : Q ∈ Complex.slitPlane) (hc : ∀ᶠ ε in l, 0 < c ε)
    (h : Tendsto (fun ε => ((c ε : ℝ) : ℂ) * f ε) l (𝓝 Q)) :
    Tendsto (fun ε => (f ε).arg) l (𝓝 Q.arg)

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.arg_annular_quotient_tendsto_right
decls.doc:
**Right annular quotient argument convergence**: along a positive cutoff `δ(ε) → 0⁺`, the
argument of the annular quotient `(γ (t₀ + r) - s) / (γ (t₀ + δ ε) - s)` converges to the
argument of `(γ (t₀ + r) - s) / L`.
decls.title: Right annular quotient argument convergence
decls.statement:
theorem arg_annular_quotient_tendsto_right
    (h_deriv : HasDerivWithinAt γ L (Ioi t₀) t₀) (h_at : γ t₀ = s)
    {δ : ℝ → ℝ} {r : ℝ}
    (h_slit : (γ (t₀ + r) - s) / L ∈ Complex.slitPlane)
    (hδ_pos : ∀ᶠ ε in 𝓝[>] (0 : ℝ), 0 < δ ε)
    (hδ_to_zero : Tendsto δ (𝓝[>] (0 : ℝ)) (𝓝[>] (0 : ℝ))) :
    Tendsto (fun ε : ℝ => Complex.arg ((γ (t₀ + r) - s) / (γ (t₀ + δ ε) - s)))
      (𝓝[>] (0 : ℝ)) (𝓝 ((γ (t₀ + r) - s) / L).arg)

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.arg_annular_quotient_tendsto_left
decls.doc:
**Left annular quotient argument convergence**: along a positive cutoff `δ(ε) → 0⁺`, the
argument of the annular quotient `(γ (t₀ - δ ε) - s) / (γ (t₀ - r) - s)` converges to the
argument of `(-L) / (γ (t₀ - r) - s)`.
decls.title: Left annular quotient argument convergence
decls.statement:
theorem arg_annular_quotient_tendsto_left
    (h_deriv : HasDerivWithinAt γ L (Iio t₀) t₀) (h_at : γ t₀ = s)
    {δ : ℝ → ℝ} {r : ℝ}
    (h_slit : (-L) / (γ (t₀ - r) - s) ∈ Complex.slitPlane)
    (hδ_pos : ∀ᶠ ε in 𝓝[>] (0 : ℝ), 0 < δ ε)
    (hδ_to_zero : Tendsto δ (𝓝[>] (0 : ℝ)) (𝓝[>] (0 : ℝ))) :
    Tendsto (fun ε : ℝ => Complex.arg ((γ (t₀ - δ ε) - s) / (γ (t₀ - r) - s)))
      (𝓝[>] (0 : ℝ)) (𝓝 ((-L) / (γ (t₀ - r) - s)).arg)

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.neg_inv_mem_slitPlane_of_neg_close_to_one
decls.doc:
For `q` with `‖-q - 1‖ ≤ 1/4`, the negated inverse `-1/q` lies in the slit plane: the
`z = 1`, `w = -q` instance of `div_mem_slitPlane_of_close_to_one`.
decls.statement:
theorem neg_inv_mem_slitPlane_of_neg_close_to_one {q : ℂ} (hq : ‖-q - 1‖ ≤ 1 / 4) :
    -1 / q ∈ Complex.slitPlane

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.exists_chord_div_tangent_mem_slitPlane_right
decls.doc:
**Boundary chord-to-tangent quotients in the slit plane (right)**: there is a window radius
`r > 0` such that `(γ (t₀ + r') - s) / L ∈ Complex.slitPlane` for every `0 < r' ≤ r` — the
`h_slit` input of `arg_annular_quotient_tendsto_right` at any admissible window radius.
decls.title: Boundary chord-to-tangent quotients in the slit plane (right)
decls.statement:
theorem exists_chord_div_tangent_mem_slitPlane_right
    (h_deriv : HasDerivWithinAt γ L (Ioi t₀) t₀) (h_at : γ t₀ = s) (hL : L ≠ 0) :
    ∃ r > 0, ∀ r', 0 < r' → r' ≤ r → (γ (t₀ + r') - s) / L ∈ Complex.slitPlane

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.exists_neg_tangent_div_chord_mem_slitPlane_left
decls.doc:
**Boundary chord-to-tangent quotients in the slit plane (left)**: there is a window radius
`r > 0` such that `(-L) / (γ (t₀ - r') - s) ∈ Complex.slitPlane` for every `0 < r' ≤ r` — the
`h_slit` input of `arg_annular_quotient_tendsto_left` at any admissible window radius.
decls.title: Boundary chord-to-tangent quotients in the slit plane (left)
decls.statement:
theorem exists_neg_tangent_div_chord_mem_slitPlane_left
    (h_deriv : HasDerivWithinAt γ L (Iio t₀) t₀) (h_at : γ t₀ = s) (hL : L ≠ 0) :
    ∃ r > 0, ∀ r', 0 < r' → r' ≤ r →
      (-L) / (γ (t₀ - r') - s) ∈ Complex.slitPlane

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.exists_crossing_slitPlane_radius
decls.doc:
**The per-crossing slit-plane radius package**: at a transverse crossing with non-zero
one-sided derivatives, a single radius `r > 0` carries all four slit-plane properties — the
two-sided chord quotients and the two boundary tangent quotients at every admissible offset —
so a common minimum over the crossings of a pole inherits them all.
decls.title: The per-crossing slit-plane radius package
decls.statement:
theorem exists_crossing_slitPlane_radius {γ : ℝ → ℂ} {t₀ : ℝ} {s L_R L_L : ℂ}
    (h_deriv_R : HasDerivWithinAt γ L_R (Ioi t₀) t₀)
    (h_deriv_L : HasDerivWithinAt γ L_L (Iio t₀) t₀)
    (h_at : γ t₀ = s) (hL_R : L_R ≠ 0) (hL_L : L_L ≠ 0) :
    ∃ r > 0,
      (∀ a b, t₀ < a → a ≤ b → b ≤ t₀ + r →
        (γ b - s) / (γ a - s) ∈ Complex.slitPlane) ∧
      (∀ a b, t₀ - r ≤ a → a ≤ b → b < t₀ →
        (γ b - s) / (γ a - s) ∈ Complex.slitPlane) ∧
      (∀ r', 0 < r' → r' ≤ r → (γ (t₀ + r') - s) / L_R ∈ Complex.slitPlane) ∧
      (∀ r', 0 < r' → r' ≤ r → (-L_L) / (γ (t₀ - r') - s) ∈ Complex.slitPlane)

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.orthogonalProjectionComplex
decls.doc:
**Projection of `w` on the direction `L`** in the plane: the component of `w` along the real
line `ℝ • L`, namely `(Re(w · conj L) / ‖L‖²) • L` (zero for `L = 0`). Implementation device for
`tangentDeviation`; consumers work with the deviation and `norm_tangentDeviation`.
decls.title: Projection of `w` on the direction `L`
decls.statement: def orthogonalProjectionComplex (w L : ℂ) : ℂ

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.tangentDeviation
decls.doc:
**Orthogonal deviation of `w` from the direction `L`**: the remainder
`w - orthogonalProjectionComplex w L`, the component of `w` perpendicular to the line `ℝ • L`.
decls.title: Orthogonal deviation of `w` from the direction `L`
decls.statement: def tangentDeviation (w L : ℂ) : ℂ

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.tangentDeviation_add
decls.doc: `tangentDeviation` is additive in its vector argument.
decls.statement:
theorem tangentDeviation_add (a b L : ℂ) :
    tangentDeviation (a + b) L = tangentDeviation a L + tangentDeviation b L

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.tangentDeviation_zero
decls.doc: `tangentDeviation` sends the zero vector to `0`.
decls.statement: theorem tangentDeviation_zero (L : ℂ) : tangentDeviation 0 L = 0

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.tangentDeviation_sub
decls.doc: `tangentDeviation` respects subtraction in its vector argument.
decls.statement:
theorem tangentDeviation_sub (a b L : ℂ) :
    tangentDeviation (a - b) L = tangentDeviation a L - tangentDeviation b L

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.tangentDeviation_neg
decls.doc: `tangentDeviation` negates in its vector argument.
decls.statement:
theorem tangentDeviation_neg (w L : ℂ) :
    tangentDeviation (-w) L = -tangentDeviation w L

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.tangentDeviation_real_smul
decls.doc:
`tangentDeviation` is homogeneous over real scalars in its vector argument. (Not `@[simp]`:
`simp` normalizes the real smul `c • w` to `↑c * w`, so this left-hand side never fires.)
decls.statement:
theorem tangentDeviation_real_smul (c : ℝ) (w L : ℂ) :
    tangentDeviation (c • w) L = c • tangentDeviation w L

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.tangentDeviation_ofReal_mul
decls.doc:
The `simp`-normal companion of `tangentDeviation_real_smul`: `simp` normalizes the real smul
`c • w` to `↑c * w`, so this is the form that fires for `simp`-driven automation.
decls.statement:
theorem tangentDeviation_ofReal_mul (c : ℝ) (w L : ℂ) :
    tangentDeviation ((c : ℂ) * w) L = (c : ℂ) * tangentDeviation w L

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.norm_tangentDeviation
decls.doc:
The norm of the orthogonal deviation is the distance from `w` to the line `ℝ • L`:
`‖tangentDeviation w L‖ = |Im(w · conj L)| / ‖L‖` — the quantity `Contour.FlatOfOrder` bounds.
decls.statement:
theorem norm_tangentDeviation {L : ℂ} (hL : L ≠ 0) (w : ℂ) :
    ‖tangentDeviation w L‖ = |(w * starRingEnd ℂ L).im| / ‖L‖

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.norm_tangentDeviation_le
decls.doc:
The deviation norm is bounded by the vector norm: the perpendicular component is no longer
than the vector.
decls.statement:
theorem norm_tangentDeviation_le {L : ℂ} (hL : L ≠ 0) (w : ℂ) :
    ‖tangentDeviation w L‖ ≤ ‖w‖

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.norm_tangentDeviation_neg
decls.doc:
The deviation norm is direction-line invariant: measuring against `-L` gives the same
distance to the line `ℝ • L`.
decls.statement:
theorem norm_tangentDeviation_neg {L : ℂ} (hL : L ≠ 0) (w : ℂ) :
    ‖tangentDeviation w (-L)‖ = ‖tangentDeviation w L‖

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.norm_tangentDeviation_smul_real
decls.doc:
The deviation norm is invariant under real rescaling of the direction: it measures the
distance to the line `ℝ • L`.
decls.statement:
theorem norm_tangentDeviation_smul_real {c : ℝ} (hc : c ≠ 0) {L : ℂ} (hL : L ≠ 0) (w : ℂ) :
    ‖tangentDeviation w (c • L)‖ = ‖tangentDeviation w L‖

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.exists_real_smul_of_im_mul_conj_eq_zero
decls.doc:
A complex number with real pairing against a nonzero direction lies on its real line:
`Im(L · conj v) = 0` forces `L = c • v` for a real `c`.
decls.statement:
theorem exists_real_smul_of_im_mul_conj_eq_zero {L v : ℂ} (hv : v ≠ 0)
    (h : (L * starRingEnd ℂ v).im = 0) :
    ∃ c : ℝ, L = c • v

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.proj_sq_add_dev_sq
decls.doc:
**Pythagoras for the plane projection.** The squared norm of `w` decomposes into the squared
norms of its projection on `L` and its orthogonal deviation.
decls.title: Pythagoras for the plane projection
decls.statement:
theorem proj_sq_add_dev_sq (w L : ℂ) :
    ‖orthogonalProjectionComplex w L‖ ^ 2 + ‖tangentDeviation w L‖ ^ 2 = ‖w‖ ^ 2

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.sub_sqrt_le
decls.doc:
**Square-root shortfall bound.** For `0 ≤ δ ≤ ε` with `0 < ε`:
`ε - √(ε² - δ²) ≤ δ²/ε`.
decls.title: Square-root shortfall bound
decls.statement:
theorem sub_sqrt_le {ε δ : ℝ} (hε : 0 < ε) (hδ : 0 ≤ δ) (hle : δ ≤ ε) :
    ε - Real.sqrt (ε ^ 2 - δ ^ 2) ≤ δ ^ 2 / ε

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.norm_sub_norm_orthogonalProjectionComplex_le
decls.doc:
**Norm shortfall of the projection.** For `‖w‖ > 0`, the projection is shorter than `w` by at
most `‖tangentDeviation w L‖² / ‖w‖`.
decls.title: Norm shortfall of the projection
decls.statement:
theorem norm_sub_norm_orthogonalProjectionComplex_le {w : ℂ} (L : ℂ) (hw : 0 < ‖w‖) :
    ‖w‖ - ‖orthogonalProjectionComplex w L‖ ≤ ‖tangentDeviation w L‖ ^ 2 / ‖w‖

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.norm_orthogonalProjectionComplex_sub_target_eq
decls.doc:
**Projection-to-target distance in the `+L` hemisphere.** If `Re(w · conj L) ≥ 0`, the
distance from the projection to the same-magnitude target `(‖w‖/‖L‖) • L` on the `+L` ray equals
the norm shortfall `‖w‖ - ‖orthogonalProjectionComplex w L‖`.
decls.title: Projection-to-target distance in the `+L` hemisphere
decls.statement:
theorem norm_orthogonalProjectionComplex_sub_target_eq {w L : ℂ} (hL : L ≠ 0)
    (h_pos : 0 ≤ (w * starRingEnd ℂ L).re) :
    ‖orthogonalProjectionComplex w L - (‖w‖ / ‖L‖ : ℝ) • L‖ =
      ‖w‖ - ‖orthogonalProjectionComplex w L‖

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.norm_chord_to_tangent_target_le
decls.doc:
**Chord-to-tangent-target bound.** For `w` in the `+L` hemisphere with `‖w‖ > 0`, the chord
from `w` to the natural tangent target `(‖w‖/‖L‖) • L` is controlled by the orthogonal
deviation: `‖w - (‖w‖/‖L‖) • L‖ ≤ ‖tangentDeviation w L‖ + ‖tangentDeviation w L‖² / ‖w‖`.
decls.title: Chord-to-tangent-target bound
decls.statement:
theorem norm_chord_to_tangent_target_le {w L : ℂ} (hL : L ≠ 0) (hw : 0 < ‖w‖)
    (h_pos : 0 ≤ (w * starRingEnd ℂ L).re) :
    ‖w - (‖w‖ / ‖L‖ : ℝ) • L‖ ≤
      ‖tangentDeviation w L‖ + ‖tangentDeviation w L‖ ^ 2 / ‖w‖

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.mem_Ioo_of_closed_of_ne
decls.doc:
**Interior crossings from a closed curve rooted off the point**: if `γ a = γ b ≠ z`, every
parameter of `[a, b]` where `γ` takes the value `z` is interior.
decls.title: Interior crossings from a closed curve rooted off the point

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.interior_mem_minmax
decls.doc: Interior membership in the `min`/`max` form the condition clauses use.
decls.statement:
theorem interior_mem_minmax {a b t : ℝ} (hab : a ≤ b) (ht : t ∈ Ioo a b) :
    t ∈ Ioo (min a b) (max a b)

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.tendsto_deriv_ne_zero_right
decls.doc:
At an interior parameter, a limit of `deriv γ` from the right is the immersion's one-sided
tangent, hence non-zero.

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.tendsto_deriv_ne_zero_left
decls.doc:
At an interior parameter, a limit of `deriv γ` from the left is the immersion's one-sided
tangent, hence non-zero.

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.PolarPartDecomposition.coeff_eq_meromorphicPolarCoeffAt
decls.doc:
**A decomposition of canonical order has the canonical coefficients**: near `s ∈ S` the
decomposition exhibits `f` as its polar part at `s` plus a function analytic there, so by
uniqueness of finite principal-part expansions its coefficients are
`meromorphicPolarCoeffAt`.
decls.title: A decomposition of canonical order has the canonical coefficients
decls.statement:
theorem coeff_eq_meromorphicPolarCoeffAt (decomp : PolarPartDecomposition f S U)
    (hU : IsOpen U) (hSU : (S : Set ℂ) ⊆ U) (s : S) (hMero : MeromorphicAt f ↑s)
    (h_ord : decomp.order s = meromorphicPolarOrderAt f ↑s) (k : Fin (decomp.order s)) :
    decomp.coeff s k = meromorphicPolarCoeffAt hMero ⟨k.val, h_ord ▸ k.isLt⟩

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.ConditionAprime.flatOfOrder_of_crossing
decls.doc:
**Condition (A′) discharges the flatness hypothesis** of the polar-part principal-value
theorem: at each crossing of `s`, the pole's canonical order pins `meromorphicOrderAt`, the
condition gives flatness of the full order, and the downward restriction gives it at each
surviving coefficient's order.
decls.title: Condition (A′) discharges the flatness hypothesis
decls.statement:
theorem ConditionAprime.flatOfOrder_of_crossing {γ : ℝ → ℂ} {a b : ℝ} {f : ℂ → ℂ}
    {S' : Finset ℂ} (hA : ConditionAprime γ a b f S') {S : Finset ℂ} {U : Set ℂ}
    (decomp : PolarPartDecomposition f S U) (s : S) (hsS' : (s : ℂ) ∈ S')
    (h_imm : IsPwC1ImmersionOn γ a b) (hab : a ≤ b)
    (h_interior : ∀ t ∈ Icc a b, γ t = (s : ℂ) → t ∈ Ioo a b)
    (h_ord : decomp.order s = meromorphicPolarOrderAt f ↑s) :
    ∀ k : Fin (decomp.order s), 1 ≤ k.val →
      ∀ t ∈ Icc a b, γ t = (s : ℂ) → FlatOfOrder γ t (k.val + 1)

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.ConditionB.pow_unit_tangent_eq_of_coeff_ne_zero
decls.doc:
**Condition (B) discharges the sector hypothesis** of the polar-part principal-value
theorem: a surviving coefficient of index `≥ 1` makes `s` a pole of order `> 1`, the
condition's sector compatibility at the crossing angle carries a Laurent witness whose
coefficients are the decomposition's by uniqueness, and its resonance transfers to the unit
tangent powers through the crossing-angle bridge.
decls.title: Condition (B) discharges the sector hypothesis
decls.statement:
theorem ConditionB.pow_unit_tangent_eq_of_coeff_ne_zero {γ : ℝ → ℂ} {a b : ℝ} {f : ℂ → ℂ}
    (hB : ConditionB γ a b f) {S : Finset ℂ} {U : Set ℂ}
    (decomp : PolarPartDecomposition f S U) (hU : IsOpen U) (hSU : (S : Set ℂ) ⊆ U)
    (s : S) (hMero : MeromorphicAt f ↑s)
    (h_imm : IsPwC1ImmersionOn γ a b) (hab : a ≤ b)
    (h_interior : ∀ t ∈ Icc a b, γ t = (s : ℂ) → t ∈ Ioo a b)
    (h_ord : decomp.order s = meromorphicPolarOrderAt f ↑s) :
    ∀ k : Fin (decomp.order s), 1 ≤ k.val → decomp.coeff s k ≠ 0 →
      ∀ t ∈ Icc a b, γ t = (s : ℂ) → ∀ L_R L_L : ℂ,
        Tendsto (deriv γ) (𝓝[>] t) (𝓝 L_R) → Tendsto (deriv γ) (𝓝[<] t) (𝓝 L_L) →
        (L_R / (‖L_R‖ : ℂ)) ^ k.val = ((-L_L) / (‖L_L‖ : ℂ)) ^ k.val

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.deriv_ne_zero_off_breakpoints
decls.doc:
Differentiability and a non-zero derivative at interior non-breakpoint parameters, relative
to a breakpoint witness of the immersion clause.
decls.statement:
theorem deriv_ne_zero_off_breakpoints {p : Finset ℝ}
    (hpieces : ∀ c d : ℝ, c < d → Icc c d ⊆ uIcc a b → Disjoint (↑p : Set ℝ) (Ioo c d) →
      ContDiffOn ℝ 1 γ (Icc c d) ∧ ∀ t ∈ Icc c d, derivWithin γ (Icc c d) t ≠ 0)
    {t : ℝ} (ht : t ∈ Ioo (min a b) (max a b)) (htp : t ∉ (↑p : Set ℝ)) :
    DifferentiableAt ℝ γ t ∧ deriv γ t ≠ 0

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.crossing_atMostOne_of_dual_deriv_pos
decls.doc:
**At-most-one-crossing core.** If a continuous linear functional is positive on `deriv γ`
throughout an open interval on which `γ` is differentiable, then that functional of `γ - z₀` is
strictly monotone on the closed interval, so `γ` meets `z₀` at most once there.
decls.title: At-most-one-crossing core
decls.statement:
theorem crossing_atMostOne_of_dual_deriv_pos {f : StrongDual ℝ ℂ} {c d : ℝ}
    (hγ_cont : ContinuousOn γ (Icc c d))
    (h_cond : ∀ t ∈ Ioo c d, DifferentiableAt ℝ γ t ∧ 0 < f (deriv γ t)) :
    ∀ t₁ ∈ Icc c d, ∀ t₂ ∈ Icc c d, γ t₁ = z₀ → γ t₂ = z₀ → t₁ = t₂

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.Icc_subset_uIcc_of_Ioo_subset
decls.doc: A nonempty open interval inside `(min a b, max a b)` has its closure inside `[[a, b]]`.
decls.statement:
theorem Icc_subset_uIcc_of_Ioo_subset {c d : ℝ} (hcd : c < d)
    (h : Ioo c d ⊆ Ioo (min a b) (max a b)) : Icc c d ⊆ uIcc a b

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.eventually_interior_off_pos
decls.doc:
The parameters near `t₀` (from the given side) that lie in the interior, avoid the
breakpoints, and see a positive dual value of `deriv γ`.
decls.statement:
theorem eventually_interior_off_pos {p : Finset ℝ} {t₀ : ℝ} {L : ℂ}
    {f : StrongDual ℝ ℂ} {l : Filter ℝ} (hl : l ≤ 𝓝 t₀) (hne : ∀ᶠ t in l, t ≠ t₀)
    (h_Ioo : ∀ᶠ t in l, t ∈ Ioo (min a b) (max a b))
    (hL_tendsto : Tendsto (deriv γ) l (𝓝 L)) (hfL_pos : 0 < f L) :
    ∀ᶠ t in l, (t ∈ Ioo (min a b) (max a b) ∧ t ∉ (↑p : Set ℝ)) ∧ 0 < f (deriv γ t)

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.crossing_isolated_right
decls.doc:
Crossings of an immersion are isolated from the right: if `γ t₀ = z₀` with
`t₀ ∈ [min, max)`, then `γ t ≠ z₀` for `t` in a punctured right neighbourhood of `t₀`.

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.crossing_isolated_left
decls.doc:
Crossings of an immersion are isolated from the left: if `γ t₀ = z₀` with
`t₀ ∈ (min, max]`, then `γ t ≠ z₀` for `t` in a punctured left neighbourhood of `t₀`.

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.IsPwC1ImmersionOn.eventually_ne_nhdsNE
decls.doc:
**Crossings of an immersion are isolated**: at every interior crossing there is a punctured
neighbourhood on which the immersion avoids `z₀`.
decls.title: Crossings of an immersion are isolated

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.IsPwC1ImmersionOn.finite_crossings
decls.doc:
**HW Proposition 2.2: the crossing set of a piecewise-`C¹` immersion is finite** — the
geometric input that makes the on-cycle singularities of the generalized residue theorem a
finite crossing family.
decls.title: HW Proposition 2.2: the crossing set of a piecewise-`C¹` immersion is finite
decls.statement:
theorem IsPwC1ImmersionOn.finite_crossings (h : IsPwC1ImmersionOn γ a b) :
    (uIcc a b ∩ γ ⁻¹' {z₀}).Finite

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.IsPwC1ImmersionOn.mem_toFinset_finite_crossings
decls.doc:
**Membership in the crossing finset.** The finset supplied by
`IsPwC1ImmersionOn.finite_crossings` consists of exactly the parameters of `[[a, b]]` at which
`γ` takes the value `z₀`. Multi-crossing principal-value arguments index their windows by this
finset, so they need the characterisation and not just the finiteness; for ordered endpoints
follow with `uIcc_of_le`.
decls.title: Membership in the crossing finset
decls.statement:
theorem IsPwC1ImmersionOn.mem_toFinset_finite_crossings (h : IsPwC1ImmersionOn γ a b) {t : ℝ} :
    t ∈ (h.finite_crossings (z₀ := z₀)).toFinset ↔ t ∈ uIcc a b ∧ γ t = z₀

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.abs_inner_chord_deriv_sub_le
decls.doc:
**Two-sided inner-product expansion bound.** Near a one-sided derivative limit `L`, the
derivative of `‖γ t - s‖²` (up to the factor `2`) deviates from its leading term
`(t - t₀)‖L‖²` by at most `|t - t₀|‖L‖²/2`. Both one-sided strict-monotonicity statements read
off their sign from this single bound.
decls.title: Two-sided inner-product expansion bound
decls.statement:
theorem abs_inner_chord_deriv_sub_le {γ : ℝ → F} {t₀ : ℝ} {s : F} (h_at : γ t₀ = s)
    {L : F} (hL : L ≠ 0) {u : Set ℝ}
    (h_deriv : HasDerivWithinAt γ L u t₀)
    (hL_tendsto : Tendsto (deriv γ) (𝓝[u] t₀) (𝓝 L)) :
    ∀ᶠ t in 𝓝[u] t₀,
      |inner ℝ (γ t - s) (deriv γ t) - (t - t₀) * ‖L‖ ^ 2| ≤ |t - t₀| * ‖L‖ ^ 2 / 2

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.exists_strictMonoOn_norm_sub_right
decls.doc:
**The distance to a crossed point is strictly increasing to the right of the crossing**:
for a curve through `s = γ t₀` with non-zero right derivative limit `L`, continuity at `t₀`,
and eventual differentiability on the right, `‖γ t - s‖` is strictly monotone on `[t₀, t₀ + r]`
for some `r > 0` — the curve exits each small disc around `s` exactly once.
decls.title: The distance to a crossed point is strictly increasing to the right of the crossing
decls.statement:
theorem exists_strictMonoOn_norm_sub_right {γ : ℝ → F} {t₀ : ℝ} {s : F} (h_at : γ t₀ = s)
    {L : F} (hL : L ≠ 0)
    (hL_right : Tendsto (deriv γ) (𝓝[>] t₀) (𝓝 L))
    (hγ_cont : ContinuousAt γ t₀)
    (hγ_diff : ∀ᶠ t in 𝓝[>] t₀, DifferentiableAt ℝ γ t) :
    ∃ r > 0, StrictMonoOn (fun t => ‖γ t - s‖) (Icc t₀ (t₀ + r))

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.tendsto_reflection_nhdsGT
decls.doc:
The reflection `t ↦ 2t₀ - t` carries the right-sided neighbourhood filter at `t₀` to the
left-sided one.
decls.statement:
theorem tendsto_reflection_nhdsGT (t₀ : ℝ) :
    Tendsto (fun t => 2 * t₀ - t) (𝓝[>] t₀) (𝓝[<] t₀)

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.exists_strictAntiOn_norm_sub_left
decls.doc:
**The distance to a crossed point is strictly decreasing to the left of the crossing**: the
counterpart of `exists_strictMonoOn_norm_sub_right`, derived from it by the reflection
`t ↦ 2t₀ - t` (which carries the left data of `γ` to right data of the reflected curve with
derivative limit `-L`).
decls.title: The distance to a crossed point is strictly decreasing to the left of the crossing
decls.statement:
theorem exists_strictAntiOn_norm_sub_left {γ : ℝ → F} {t₀ : ℝ} {s : F} (h_at : γ t₀ = s)
    {L : F} (hL : L ≠ 0)
    (hL_left : Tendsto (deriv γ) (𝓝[<] t₀) (𝓝 L))
    (hγ_cont : ContinuousAt γ t₀)
    (hγ_diff : ∀ᶠ t in 𝓝[<] t₀, DifferentiableAt ℝ γ t) :
    ∃ r > 0, StrictAntiOn (fun t => ‖γ t - s‖) (Icc (t₀ - r) t₀)

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.eventually_intervalIntegrable_truncated_window
decls.doc:
The truncated integrand is eventually interval-integrable on a crossing window lying in
`[a, b]`, by restriction.
decls.statement:
theorem eventually_intervalIntegrable_truncated_window {γ : ℝ → ℂ} {s : ℂ}
    {g : ℂ → ℂ} {a b r t : ℝ} (hab : a ≤ b) (h_lo : a ≤ t - r) (h_hi : t + r ≤ b)
    (hr_nonneg : 0 ≤ r)
    (h_int_tr : ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε →
      IntervalIntegrable (fun u => if ‖γ u - s‖ > ε then g (γ u) * deriv γ u else 0)
        MeasureTheory.volume a b) :
    ∀ᶠ ε in 𝓝[>] (0 : ℝ),
      IntervalIntegrable (fun u => if ‖γ u - s‖ > ε then g (γ u) * deriv γ u else 0)
        MeasureTheory.volume (t - r) (t + r)

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.hasCauchyPVAt_plain_piece
decls.doc:
The between-piece principal value on a subinterval of `[a, b]` keeping distance `≥ m` from
`s`: the plain integral, with the truncated integrability restricted from `[a, b]`. Both public
aggregations discharge their piece hypothesis through this.
decls.statement:
theorem hasCauchyPVAt_plain_piece {γ : ℝ → ℂ} {s : ℂ} {g : ℂ → ℂ} {a b m : ℝ}
    (hab : a ≤ b) (hm_pos : 0 < m)
    (h_int_tr : ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε →
      IntervalIntegrable (fun t => if ‖γ t - s‖ > ε then g (γ t) * deriv γ t else 0)
        MeasureTheory.volume a b)
    {l u : ℝ} (hA : a ≤ l) (hlu : l ≤ u) (hu : u ≤ b)
    (h_far : ∀ t ∈ Icc l u, m ≤ ‖γ t - s‖) :
    HasCauchyPVAt γ l u g s (∫ t in l..u, g (γ t) * deriv γ t)

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.windowPieceSum
decls.doc:
The aggregated value along a sorted crossing list: between-piece values `p` interleaved
with window values `w`.
decls.statement:
def windowPieceSum (r : ℝ) (p : ℝ → ℝ → ℂ) (w : ℝ → ℂ) (b : ℝ) :
    List ℝ → ℝ → ℂ

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.hasCauchyPVAt_along_sorted
decls.doc:
**The shared aggregation induction**: with windows of disjoint interiors lying in `[a, b]`,
window principal values `w t`, and between-piece principal values `p l u` available on
intervals where the curve keeps distance `≥ m` from `s`, the principal value on `[a, b]` is
the interleaved sum `windowPieceSum`. Both public aggregation theorems instantiate this.
decls.title: The shared aggregation induction
decls.statement:
theorem hasCauchyPVAt_along_sorted {γ : ℝ → ℂ} {s : ℂ} {g : ℂ → ℂ}
    {p : ℝ → ℝ → ℂ} {w : ℝ → ℂ} {A b r m : ℝ}
    (h_piece : ∀ l u : ℝ, A ≤ l → l ≤ u → u ≤ b → (∀ t ∈ Icc l u, m ≤ ‖γ t - s‖) →
      HasCauchyPVAt γ l u g s (p l u)) :
    ∀ (sorted : List ℝ), sorted.SortedLT → (sorted ≠ [] → 0 ≤ r) →
    ∀ a : ℝ, A ≤ a → a ≤ b → (∀ t ∈ sorted, a ≤ t - r) → (∀ t ∈ sorted, t + r ≤ b) →
      (∀ t ∈ sorted, ∀ t' ∈ sorted, t' ≠ t → 2 * r ≤ |t - t'|) →
      (∀ t ∈ sorted, HasCauchyPVAt γ (t - r) (t + r) g s (w t)) →
      (∀ u ∈ Icc a b, (∀ t ∈ sorted, u ∉ Ioo (t - r) (t + r)) → m ≤ ‖γ u - s‖) →
      HasCauchyPVAt γ a b g s (windowPieceSum r p w b sorted a)

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.cauchyPVExistsAt_of_perWindow_tendsto_of_interiorDisjoint
decls.doc:
**The single-point principal value from per-window convergence**: if the `ε`-truncated
integral of `g (γ t) * deriv γ t` converges on each crossing window (disjoint interiors,
lying in `[a, b]` — they may touch each other, or touch `a` or `b`), the truncations are
integrable on `[a, b]`, and the curve keeps a
positive distance from `s` off the windows, then the principal value at `s` exists on
`[a, b]`. The per-window limits are hypotheses, so both the simple-pole and higher-order
per-window theorems discharge them.
decls.title: The single-point principal value from per-window convergence
decls.statement:
theorem cauchyPVExistsAt_of_perWindow_tendsto_of_interiorDisjoint {γ : ℝ → ℂ} {s : ℂ} {g : ℂ → ℂ}
    {a b r : ℝ} (hab : a ≤ b) (crossings : Finset ℝ)
    (hr_nonneg : crossings.Nonempty → 0 ≤ r)
    (h_lo : ∀ t ∈ crossings, a ≤ t - r) (h_hi : ∀ t ∈ crossings, t + r ≤ b)
    (h_pair : ∀ t ∈ crossings, ∀ t' ∈ crossings, t' ≠ t → 2 * r ≤ |t - t'|)
    (h_int_tr : ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε →
      IntervalIntegrable (fun t => if ‖γ t - s‖ > ε then g (γ t) * deriv γ t else 0)
        MeasureTheory.volume a b)
    (h_win : ∀ t ∈ crossings, ∃ v : ℂ, Tendsto (fun ε : ℝ => ∫ u in (t - r)..(t + r),
        if ‖γ u - s‖ > ε then g (γ u) * deriv γ u else 0) (𝓝[>] (0 : ℝ)) (𝓝 v))
    (h_far : ∃ m : ℝ, 0 < m ∧ ∀ u ∈ Icc a b, (∀ t ∈ crossings, u ∉ Ioo (t - r) (t + r)) →
      m ≤ ‖γ u - s‖) :
    CauchyPVExistsAt γ a b g s

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.windowLexEmb
decls.doc:
The window map `t ↦ (t - r, t + r)` into the lexicographic plane, as an order embedding:
`Prod.Lex` compares first coordinates first and `t ↦ t - r` is strictly monotone.
decls.statement: def windowLexEmb (r : ℝ) : ℝ ↪o (ℝ ×ₗ ℝ)

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.orderEmbOfFin_window_fst_snd
decls.doc:
The two edges of window `i`, read off the order embedding of the pair set.

Sorting commutes with the strictly monotone window map — that is Mathlib's
`StrictMonoOn.map_finsetSort` — so the `i`-th sorted pair is the `i`-th sorted crossing
shifted by `±r`.

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.windowPieceSum_eq_sum_intervalGapsWithin_add_sum
decls.doc:
**The piece/window sum is Mathlib's interval-gap sum.** Along the suffix of the sorted
crossings from index `j`, the aggregated value splits into the gap pieces from `j` onwards and the
window values of that suffix. The `j = 0` case identifies `windowPieceSum` with
`Finset.intervalGapsWithin`.
decls.title: The piece/window sum is Mathlib's interval-gap sum
decls.statement:
theorem windowPieceSum_eq_sum_intervalGapsWithin_add_sum {p : ℝ → ℝ → ℂ} {w : ℝ → ℂ}
    {a b r : ℝ} {k : ℕ} {crossings : Finset ℝ} (hc : crossings.card = k)
    {F : Finset (ℝ ×ₗ ℝ)} (hFdef : F = crossings.image fun t : ℝ => (t - r, t + r))
    (hF : F.card = k) :
    ∀ j : ℕ, j ≤ k →
      windowPieceSum r p w b ((crossings.sort (· ≤ ·)).drop j)
          (F.intervalGapsWithin hF a b j).1
        = (∑ i ∈ Finset.Ico j (k + 1),
            p (F.intervalGapsWithin hF a b i).1 (F.intervalGapsWithin hF a b i).2)
          + (((crossings.sort (· ≤ ·)).drop j).map w).sum

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.windowPieceSum_boundary
decls.doc:
**The window aggregation telescopes to the endpoint difference.** Reading the pieces as the
gaps of the window finset `F = {(t - r, t + r) : t ∈ crossings}` inside `[a, b]`, this is exactly
`Finset.sum_intervalGapsWithin_add_sum_eq_sub` for `g = Φ ∘ γ`.
decls.title: The window aggregation telescopes to the endpoint difference
decls.statement:
theorem windowPieceSum_boundary {γ : ℝ → ℂ} {Φ : ℂ → ℂ} {a b r : ℝ}
    {crossings : Finset ℝ} :
    windowPieceSum r (fun l u => Φ (γ u) - Φ (γ l))
        (fun t => Φ (γ (t + r)) - Φ (γ (t - r))) b (crossings.sort (· ≤ ·)) a
      = Φ (γ b) - Φ (γ a)

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.hasCauchyPVAt_of_perWindow_boundary_tendsto_of_interiorDisjoint
decls.doc:
**Telescoping per-window aggregation**: when the plain integrand has a curve-antiderivative
`Φ` on pole-free pieces and each window limit is the boundary difference of `Φ ∘ γ`, the
principal value on `[a, b]` is `Φ (γ b) - Φ (γ a)` — in particular zero around a closed curve.
The higher-order per-window limits have exactly this boundary-difference shape.
decls.title: Telescoping per-window aggregation
decls.statement:
theorem hasCauchyPVAt_of_perWindow_boundary_tendsto_of_interiorDisjoint {γ : ℝ → ℂ} {s : ℂ}
    {g : ℂ → ℂ}
    {Φ : ℂ → ℂ} {a b r : ℝ} (hab : a ≤ b) (crossings : Finset ℝ)
    (hr_nonneg : crossings.Nonempty → 0 ≤ r)
    (h_lo : ∀ t ∈ crossings, a ≤ t - r) (h_hi : ∀ t ∈ crossings, t + r ≤ b)
    (h_pair : ∀ t ∈ crossings, ∀ t' ∈ crossings, t' ≠ t → 2 * r ≤ |t - t'|)
    (h_int_tr : ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε →
      IntervalIntegrable (fun t => if ‖γ t - s‖ > ε then g (γ t) * deriv γ t else 0)
        MeasureTheory.volume a b)
    (h_plain_eq : ∀ l u : ℝ, a ≤ l → l ≤ u → u ≤ b → (∀ t ∈ Icc l u, γ t ≠ s) →
      ∫ t in l..u, g (γ t) * deriv γ t = Φ (γ u) - Φ (γ l))
    (h_win : ∀ t ∈ crossings, Tendsto (fun ε : ℝ => ∫ u in (t - r)..(t + r),
        if ‖γ u - s‖ > ε then g (γ u) * deriv γ u else 0) (𝓝[>] (0 : ℝ))
        (𝓝 (Φ (γ (t + r)) - Φ (γ (t - r)))))
    (h_far : ∃ m : ℝ, 0 < m ∧ ∀ u ∈ Icc a b, (∀ t ∈ crossings, u ∉ Ioo (t - r) (t + r)) →
      m ≤ ‖γ u - s‖) :
    HasCauchyPVAt γ a b g s (Φ (γ b) - Φ (γ a))

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.cauchyPVExistsAt_of_perWindow_tendsto
decls.doc:
**Compatibility form of `cauchyPVExistsAt_of_perWindow_tendsto_of_interiorDisjoint`** with
windows strictly separated from each other and starting strictly after `a`; the right edges may
equal `b`, since `h_hi` is `t + r ≤ b`. Prefer the general form, which additionally admits windows
that touch each other or start at `a`.
decls.title: Compatibility form of `cauchyPVExistsAt_of_perWindow_tendsto_of_interiorDisjoint`
decls.statement:
theorem cauchyPVExistsAt_of_perWindow_tendsto {γ : ℝ → ℂ} {s : ℂ} {g : ℂ → ℂ}
    {a b r : ℝ} (hr_pos : 0 < r) (hab : a ≤ b) (crossings : Finset ℝ)
    (h_lo : ∀ t ∈ crossings, a < t - r) (h_hi : ∀ t ∈ crossings, t + r ≤ b)
    (h_pair : ∀ t ∈ crossings, ∀ t' ∈ crossings, t' ≠ t → 2 * r < |t - t'|)
    (h_int_tr : ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε →
      IntervalIntegrable (fun t => if ‖γ t - s‖ > ε then g (γ t) * deriv γ t else 0)
        MeasureTheory.volume a b)
    (h_win : ∀ t ∈ crossings, ∃ v : ℂ, Tendsto (fun ε : ℝ => ∫ u in (t - r)..(t + r),
        if ‖γ u - s‖ > ε then g (γ u) * deriv γ u else 0) (𝓝[>] (0 : ℝ)) (𝓝 v))
    (h_far : ∃ m : ℝ, 0 < m ∧ ∀ u ∈ Icc a b, (∀ t ∈ crossings, u ∉ Ioo (t - r) (t + r)) →
      m ≤ ‖γ u - s‖) :
    CauchyPVExistsAt γ a b g s

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.hasCauchyPVAt_of_perWindow_boundary_tendsto
decls.doc:
**Compatibility form of `hasCauchyPVAt_of_perWindow_boundary_tendsto_of_interiorDisjoint`**
with windows strictly separated from each other and starting strictly after `a`; the right edges
may equal `b`. Prefer the general form.
decls.title: Compatibility form of `hasCauchyPVAt_of_perWindow_boundary_tendsto_of_interiorDisjoint`
decls.statement:
theorem hasCauchyPVAt_of_perWindow_boundary_tendsto {γ : ℝ → ℂ} {s : ℂ} {g : ℂ → ℂ}
    {Φ : ℂ → ℂ} {a b r : ℝ} (hr_pos : 0 < r) (hab : a ≤ b) (crossings : Finset ℝ)
    (h_lo : ∀ t ∈ crossings, a < t - r) (h_hi : ∀ t ∈ crossings, t + r ≤ b)
    (h_pair : ∀ t ∈ crossings, ∀ t' ∈ crossings, t' ≠ t → 2 * r < |t - t'|)
    (h_int_tr : ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε →
      IntervalIntegrable (fun t => if ‖γ t - s‖ > ε then g (γ t) * deriv γ t else 0)
        MeasureTheory.volume a b)
    (h_plain_eq : ∀ l u : ℝ, a ≤ l → l ≤ u → u ≤ b → (∀ t ∈ Icc l u, γ t ≠ s) →
      ∫ t in l..u, g (γ t) * deriv γ t = Φ (γ u) - Φ (γ l))
    (h_win : ∀ t ∈ crossings, Tendsto (fun ε : ℝ => ∫ u in (t - r)..(t + r),
        if ‖γ u - s‖ > ε then g (γ u) * deriv γ u else 0) (𝓝[>] (0 : ℝ))
        (𝓝 (Φ (γ (t + r)) - Φ (γ (t - r)))))
