decls.statement:
theorem analyticAt_taylor_decomp {g : ℂ → ℂ} {s : ℂ}
    (hg : AnalyticAt ℂ g s) (k : ℕ) :
    ∃ (c : Fin k → ℂ) (R : ℂ → ℂ), AnalyticAt ℂ R s ∧
      ∀ᶠ z in 𝓝 s, g z = (∑ j : Fin k, c j * (z - s) ^ j.val) + (z - s) ^ k * R z

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.pow_div_pow_neg
decls.statement:
theorem pow_div_pow_neg {w : ℂ} (hw : w ≠ 0) {k j : ℕ} (hjk : j < k) :
    w ^ j * (w ^ k)⁻¹ = (w ^ (k - j))⁻¹

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.reindex_sum_fin_neg
decls.statement:
theorem reindex_sum_fin_neg {k : ℕ} (c : Fin k → ℂ) (w : ℂ) :
    (∑ j : Fin k, c j / w ^ (k - j.val)) =
      ∑ i : Fin k,
        c ⟨k - 1 - i.val, by have := i.isLt; omega⟩ / w ^ (i.val + 1)

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.laurent_data_of_zpow_factor
decls.doc:
Laurent data of length exactly `k` from a `(z - s)^(-k)`-factorisation with analytic
cofactor: Taylor-expand the cofactor to order `k` and divide.
decls.statement:
theorem laurent_data_of_zpow_factor {f g₀ : ℂ → ℂ} {s : ℂ} (k : ℕ)
    (hg₀_an : AnalyticAt ℂ g₀ s)
    (hg₀_eq : ∀ᶠ z in 𝓝[≠] s, f z = (z - s) ^ (-(k : ℤ)) • g₀ z) :
    ∃ (a : Fin k → ℂ) (g : ℂ → ℂ),
      AnalyticAt ℂ g s ∧
      ∀ᶠ z in 𝓝[≠] s, f z = g z + ∑ i : Fin k, a i / (z - s) ^ (i.val + 1)

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.exists_laurent_data_of_meromorphicAt
decls.doc:
**Canonical Laurent data of a meromorphic function**: near `s`,
`f = g + ∑ k, a k / (z - s)^(k+1)` with `g` analytic at `s`, where the tail length is the
canonical polar order `meromorphicPolarOrderAt f s` — pinned, not existentially chosen, so it is
provable (`1` at a simple pole).
decls.title: Canonical Laurent data of a meromorphic function
decls.statement:
theorem exists_laurent_data_of_meromorphicAt {f : ℂ → ℂ} {s : ℂ} (hMero : MeromorphicAt f s) :
    ∃ (a : Fin (meromorphicPolarOrderAt f s) → ℂ) (g : ℂ → ℂ),
      AnalyticAt ℂ g s ∧
      ∀ᶠ z in 𝓝[≠] s,
        f z = g z + ∑ k : Fin (meromorphicPolarOrderAt f s), a k / (z - s) ^ (k.val + 1)

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.meromorphicPolarCoeffAt
decls.doc: The `k`-th canonical Laurent coefficient of `f` at `s`.
decls.statement:
def meromorphicPolarCoeffAt {f : ℂ → ℂ} {s : ℂ} (hMero : MeromorphicAt f s)
    (k : Fin (meromorphicPolarOrderAt f s)) : ℂ

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.meromorphicPolarPartAt
decls.doc:
The canonical finite polar part of `f` at `s`: the Laurent tail of length
`meromorphicPolarOrderAt f s`.
decls.statement: def meromorphicPolarPartAt {f : ℂ → ℂ} {s : ℂ} (hMero : MeromorphicAt f s) (z : ℂ) : ℂ

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.meromorphicAnalyticPartAt
decls.doc: The canonical analytic part of `f` at `s`.
decls.statement: def meromorphicAnalyticPartAt {f : ℂ → ℂ} {s : ℂ} (hMero : MeromorphicAt f s) : ℂ → ℂ

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.meromorphicAnalyticPartAt_analyticAt
decls.doc: The analytic part is analytic at `s`.
decls.statement:
theorem meromorphicAnalyticPartAt_analyticAt {f : ℂ → ℂ} {s : ℂ}
    (hMero : MeromorphicAt f s) : AnalyticAt ℂ (meromorphicAnalyticPartAt hMero) s

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.eventuallyEq_meromorphicAnalyticPartAt_add_meromorphicPolarPartAt
decls.doc:
**The canonical Laurent decomposition**: near `s`, `f` is the analytic part plus the polar
part.
decls.title: The canonical Laurent decomposition

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.meromorphicPolarPartAt_eq_sum
decls.doc:
The polar part as its explicit Laurent sum — the characteristic unfolding of
`meromorphicPolarPartAt`.
decls.statement:
theorem meromorphicPolarPartAt_eq_sum {f : ℂ → ℂ} {s : ℂ}
    (hMero : MeromorphicAt f s) (z : ℂ) :
    meromorphicPolarPartAt hMero z =
      ∑ k : Fin (meromorphicPolarOrderAt f s),
        meromorphicPolarCoeffAt hMero k / (z - s) ^ (k.val + 1)

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.meromorphicPolarPartAt_analyticAt_of_ne
decls.doc: The polar part is analytic away from its pole.

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.meromorphicPolarCoeffAt_zero_eq_residue
decls.doc: **The leading canonical Laurent coefficient is the residue.**
decls.title: The leading canonical Laurent coefficient is the residue

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.coeff_top_eq_zero_of_eventuallyEq
decls.doc:
The top coefficient of a finite principal part that agrees with a function continuous at
`s` vanishes.
decls.statement:
theorem coeff_top_eq_zero_of_eventuallyEq {s : ℂ} {N : ℕ} {c : ℕ → ℂ}
    {g : ℂ → ℂ} (hg : ContinuousAt g s)
    (h_eq : ∀ᶠ z in 𝓝[≠] s,
      ∑ k ∈ Finset.range (N + 1), c k / (z - s) ^ (k + 1) = g z) :
    c N = 0

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.laurent_coeff_eq_zero_of_eventuallyEq
decls.doc:
A finite principal part agreeing with a function continuous at `s` is zero: all its
coefficients vanish.
decls.statement:
theorem laurent_coeff_eq_zero_of_eventuallyEq {s : ℂ} {g : ℂ → ℂ}
    (hg : ContinuousAt g s) :
    ∀ {N : ℕ} {c : ℕ → ℂ},
      (∀ᶠ z in 𝓝[≠] s, ∑ k ∈ Finset.range N, c k / (z - s) ^ (k + 1) = g z) →
      ∀ k < N, c k = 0

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.sum_fin_div_pow_eq_sum_range
decls.doc:
A `Fin`-indexed principal-part sum as a `Finset.range` sum of its zero-padding, extended
to any length `L ≥ N`.
decls.statement:
theorem sum_fin_div_pow_eq_sum_range {s : ℂ} {N L : ℕ} (hNL : N ≤ L)
    (a : Fin N → ℂ) (z : ℂ) :
    ∑ k : Fin N, a k / (z - s) ^ (k.val + 1)
      = ∑ k ∈ Finset.range L,
        (if hk : k < N then a ⟨k, hk⟩ else 0) / (z - s) ^ (k + 1)

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.laurent_coeff_unique
decls.doc:
**Uniqueness of finite principal-part expansions**: two expansions of the same function
near `s` with remainders continuous at `s` have the same coefficients, compared through
their zero-paddings.
decls.title: Uniqueness of finite principal-part expansions
decls.statement:
theorem laurent_coeff_unique {s : ℂ} {N M : ℕ} {a : Fin N → ℂ} {b : Fin M → ℂ}
    {g h : ℂ → ℂ} (hg : ContinuousAt g s) (hh : ContinuousAt h s)
    (h_eq : ∀ᶠ z in 𝓝[≠] s,
      g z + ∑ k : Fin N, a k / (z - s) ^ (k.val + 1)
        = h z + ∑ k : Fin M, b k / (z - s) ^ (k.val + 1)) (k : ℕ) :
    (if hk : k < N then a ⟨k, hk⟩ else 0) = (if hk : k < M then b ⟨k, hk⟩ else 0)

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.laurent_coeff_eq_meromorphicPolarCoeffAt
decls.doc:
**Any Laurent witness has the canonical coefficients**: an eventual finite principal-part
expansion of a meromorphic `f` at `s` with remainder continuous at `s` agrees, coefficient by
coefficient through zero-padding, with the canonical polar data. This is what transfers the
sector condition (B)'s resonance constraints from its own Laurent witness to
`meromorphicPolarCoeffAt`.
decls.title: Any Laurent witness has the canonical coefficients
decls.statement:
theorem laurent_coeff_eq_meromorphicPolarCoeffAt {f : ℂ → ℂ} {s : ℂ}
    (hMero : MeromorphicAt f s) {N : ℕ} {a : Fin N → ℂ} {g : ℂ → ℂ}
    (hg : ContinuousAt g s)
    (h_eq : ∀ᶠ z in 𝓝[≠] s, f z = g z + ∑ k : Fin N, a k / (z - s) ^ (k.val + 1)) (k : ℕ) :
    (if hk : k < N then a ⟨k, hk⟩ else 0)
      = (if hk : k < meromorphicPolarOrderAt f s then
          meromorphicPolarCoeffAt hMero ⟨k, hk⟩ else 0)

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.modelSector
decls.doc:
**The Hungerbühler–Wasem model sector** of radius `r` and opening angle `α` at `z₀`, with the
incoming radius at angle `φ + α` and the outgoing one at angle `φ`.

For `0 ≤ r` and `0 ≤ α`: on `[-r, r]` it is the two-ray corner through `z₀`, running from
`z₀ + r e^{i(φ+α)}` in to `z₀` and back out to `z₀ + r e^{iφ}`; on `[r, r + α]` it is the arc of
radius `r` from angle `φ` to `φ + α`, returning to the start. At `r = 0` or `α = 0` the
corresponding piece degenerates to a point. For negative `r` or `α` the two intervals reverse and
the branches no longer line up that way.
decls.title: The Hungerbühler–Wasem model sector
decls.statement: def modelSector (z₀ : ℂ) (r φ α : ℝ) : ℝ → ℂ

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.modelSector_of_le
decls.doc: Pointwise value of the model sector on the corner interval.
decls.statement:
theorem modelSector_of_le {z₀ : ℂ} {r φ α t : ℝ} (ht : t ≤ r) :
    modelSector z₀ r φ α t =
      twoRayCorner z₀ (Complex.exp ((φ + α : ℝ) * Complex.I))
        (Complex.exp ((φ : ℝ) * Complex.I)) t

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.modelSector_of_lt
decls.doc: Pointwise value of the model sector on the arc interval.
decls.statement:
theorem modelSector_of_lt {z₀ : ℂ} {r φ α t : ℝ} (ht : r < t) :
    modelSector z₀ r φ α t = circleMap z₀ r (φ + (t - r))

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.modelSector_neg
decls.doc: The model sector starts at the outer end of the incoming radius.
decls.statement:
theorem modelSector_neg (z₀ : ℂ) {r : ℝ} (hr : 0 ≤ r) (φ α : ℝ) :
    modelSector z₀ r φ α (-r) = circleMap z₀ r (φ + α)

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.modelSector_add
decls.doc:
The model sector ends at the outer end of the incoming radius, the same point it started
from.
decls.statement:
theorem modelSector_add (z₀ : ℂ) {r : ℝ} (hr : 0 ≤ r) (φ : ℝ) {α : ℝ} (hα : 0 ≤ α) :
    modelSector z₀ r φ α (r + α) = circleMap z₀ r (φ + α)

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.modelSector_closed
decls.doc: **The model sector is a closed curve** for `0 ≤ r` and `0 ≤ α`.
decls.title: The model sector is a closed curve
decls.statement:
theorem modelSector_closed (z₀ : ℂ) {r : ℝ} (hr : 0 ≤ r) (φ : ℝ) {α : ℝ} (hα : 0 ≤ α) :
    modelSector z₀ r φ α (-r) = modelSector z₀ r φ α (r + α)

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.modelSector_eqOn_corner
decls.doc: On the corner interval the model sector is its two-ray corner.
decls.statement:
theorem modelSector_eqOn_corner (z₀ : ℂ) {r : ℝ} (hr : 0 ≤ r) (φ α : ℝ) :
    EqOn (twoRayCorner z₀ (Complex.exp ((φ + α : ℝ) * Complex.I))
        (Complex.exp ((φ : ℝ) * Complex.I))) (modelSector z₀ r φ α) (uIoo (-r) r)

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.modelSector_eqOn_arc
decls.doc: On the arc interval the model sector is the reparametrised circle map.
decls.statement:
theorem modelSector_eqOn_arc (z₀ : ℂ) (r φ : ℝ) {α : ℝ} (hα : 0 ≤ α) :
    EqOn (circleMap z₀ r ∘ fun t => 1 * t + (φ - r)) (modelSector z₀ r φ α) (uIoo r (r + α))

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.norm_modelSector_dirs
decls.doc: The two ray directions of the model sector have equal (unit) length.
decls.statement:
theorem norm_modelSector_dirs (φ α : ℝ) :
    ‖Complex.exp ((φ + α : ℝ) * Complex.I)‖ = ‖Complex.exp ((φ : ℝ) * Complex.I)‖

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.windingNumber_closedModelSector
decls.doc:
**The swept-arc curve has winding number `α / 2π` about its corner.** The two radial segments
contribute nothing and the arc contributes its swept angle.

This holds for every `0 ≤ α`, and is the roadmap's acceptance criterion. The curve is the
Hungerbühler–Wasem model sector of *interior angle* `α` only for `0 < α < 2π`: at `α = 0` the two
radii coincide, and at `α ≥ 2π` the arc wraps — `α = 4π` traverses the circle twice, giving winding
`2`. At both ends the formula stands; it is the corner reading that lapses.
decls.title: The swept-arc curve has winding number `α / 2π` about its corner
decls.statement:
theorem windingNumber_closedModelSector
    {z₀ : ℂ} {r : ℝ} (hr : 0 < r) (φ : ℝ) {α : ℝ} (hα : 0 ≤ α) :
    windingNumber (modelSector z₀ r φ α) (-r) (r + α) z₀ = (α : ℂ) / (2 * (Real.pi : ℂ))

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.windingNumber_closedModelSector_eq_half
decls.doc:
**A smooth crossing contributes winding `½`** — the `α = π` model sector (HW (2.4)). This is
the coefficient of `ord_i f` in the valence formula: at the smooth boundary point `i` the contour
indents by a semicircle.
decls.title: A smooth crossing contributes winding `½`
decls.statement:
theorem windingNumber_closedModelSector_eq_half {z₀ : ℂ} {r : ℝ} (hr : 0 < r) (φ : ℝ) :
    windingNumber (modelSector z₀ r φ Real.pi) (-r) (r + Real.pi) z₀ = 1 / 2

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.windingNumber_closedModelSector_eq_one_div_six
decls.doc:
**A `π/3` corner contributes winding `1/6`** — the `α = π/3` model sector (HW (2.4)). The two
such corners `ρ` and `ρ + 1` of the fundamental domain sum to the `1/3` coefficient of
`ord_ρ f`.
decls.title: A `π/3` corner contributes winding `1/6`
decls.statement:
theorem windingNumber_closedModelSector_eq_one_div_six {z₀ : ℂ} {r : ℝ} (hr : 0 < r) (φ : ℝ) :
    windingNumber (modelSector z₀ r φ (Real.pi / 3)) (-r) (r + Real.pi / 3) z₀ = 1 / 6

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.twoRayCorner
decls.doc:
**The two-ray corner at `z₀`.** For `t < 0` the curve sits at distance `|t| ‖u‖` from `z₀`
along `u`, and for `t ≥ 0` at distance `t ‖v‖` along `v`; it meets `z₀` at `t = 0`. If both
directions are nonzero that is the only such parameter; if one of them vanishes the corresponding
ray is constant at `z₀`.

On `[-R, R]` with `‖u‖ = ‖v‖` the two endpoints lie on the circle of radius `|R| ‖v‖` about `z₀`,
so concatenating with the arc between them gives the Hungerbühler–Wasem model sector, parametrised
from the far end of one radius rather than from the corner. For unequal norms it is simply a
two-ray curve.
decls.title: The two-ray corner at `z₀`
decls.statement: def twoRayCorner (z₀ u v : ℂ) : ℝ → ℂ

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.twoRayCorner_of_neg
decls.doc: Evaluation of the corner curve on the incoming ray.
decls.statement:
theorem twoRayCorner_of_neg {z₀ u v : ℂ} {t : ℝ} (ht : t < 0) :
    twoRayCorner z₀ u v t = z₀ - (t : ℂ) * u

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.twoRayCorner_of_nonneg
decls.doc: Evaluation of the corner curve on the outgoing ray, including the corner itself.
decls.statement:
theorem twoRayCorner_of_nonneg {z₀ u v : ℂ} {t : ℝ} (ht : 0 ≤ t) :
    twoRayCorner z₀ u v t = z₀ + (t : ℂ) * v

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.twoRayCorner_eventuallyEq_neg
decls.doc: On the negative ray the corner curve is the affine map `t ↦ z₀ - t u`.
decls.statement:
theorem twoRayCorner_eventuallyEq_neg {z₀ u v : ℂ} {t : ℝ} (ht : t < 0) :
    twoRayCorner z₀ u v =ᶠ[𝓝 t] fun s : ℝ => z₀ - (s : ℂ) * u

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.twoRayCorner_eventuallyEq_pos
decls.doc: On the positive ray the corner curve is the affine map `t ↦ z₀ + t v`.
decls.statement:
theorem twoRayCorner_eventuallyEq_pos {z₀ u v : ℂ} {t : ℝ} (ht : 0 < t) :
    twoRayCorner z₀ u v =ᶠ[𝓝 t] fun s : ℝ => z₀ + (s : ℂ) * v

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.deriv_twoRayCorner_of_ne
decls.doc:
The derivative of the corner curve off the corner: `-u` on the negative ray, `v` on the
positive ray.
decls.statement:
theorem deriv_twoRayCorner_of_ne {z₀ u v : ℂ} {t : ℝ} (ht : t ≠ 0) :
    deriv (twoRayCorner z₀ u v) t = if t < 0 then -u else v

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.integrand_twoRayCorner
decls.doc:
**The index integrand along a two-ray corner is `1 / t`,** on both rays: the direction cancels
against itself, leaving the same real function on either side of the corner.
decls.title: The index integrand along a two-ray corner is `1 / t`,

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.norm_twoRayCorner_sub
decls.doc: The distance from the corner is `|t|` times the common ray length.
decls.statement:
theorem norm_twoRayCorner_sub {z₀ u v : ℂ} (huv : ‖u‖ = ‖v‖) (t : ℝ) :
    ‖twoRayCorner z₀ u v t - z₀‖ = |t| * ‖v‖

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.truncated_inv_twoRayCorner_odd
decls.doc: The `ε`-truncated index integrand of a two-ray corner is odd.
decls.statement:
theorem truncated_inv_twoRayCorner_odd {z₀ u v : ℂ} (hu : u ≠ 0) (hv : v ≠ 0)
    (huv : ‖u‖ = ‖v‖) (ε : ℝ) :
    Function.Odd (fun t : ℝ =>
      if ‖twoRayCorner z₀ u v t - z₀‖ > ε then
        (twoRayCorner z₀ u v t - z₀)⁻¹ * deriv (twoRayCorner z₀ u v) t else 0)

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.integral_truncated_inv_twoRayCorner
decls.doc: Every `ε`-truncated index integral along a two-ray corner over `[-R, R]` vanishes.
decls.statement:
theorem integral_truncated_inv_twoRayCorner {z₀ u v : ℂ} (hu : u ≠ 0) (hv : v ≠ 0)
    (huv : ‖u‖ = ‖v‖) (R ε : ℝ) :
    ∫ t in (-R)..R, (if ‖twoRayCorner z₀ u v t - z₀‖ > ε then
      (twoRayCorner z₀ u v t - z₀)⁻¹ * deriv (twoRayCorner z₀ u v) t else 0) = 0

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.measurable_twoRayCorner
decls.doc: The corner curve is measurable: it is affine on each ray.
decls.statement: theorem measurable_twoRayCorner (z₀ u v : ℂ) : Measurable (twoRayCorner z₀ u v)

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.deriv_twoRayCorner_ae
decls.doc: Off the corner the derivative is the step function `-u` / `v`.
decls.statement:
theorem deriv_twoRayCorner_ae (z₀ u v : ℂ) (R : ℝ) :
    deriv (twoRayCorner z₀ u v) =ᵐ[volume.restrict (uIoc (-R) R)]
      fun t : ℝ => if t < 0 then -u else v

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.intervalIntegrable_deriv_twoRayCorner
decls.doc: The derivative of the corner curve is interval integrable: a bounded step function.
decls.statement:
theorem intervalIntegrable_deriv_twoRayCorner (z₀ u v : ℂ) (R : ℝ) :
    IntervalIntegrable (deriv (twoRayCorner z₀ u v)) volume (-R) R

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.hasCauchyPVAt_inv_sub_twoRayCorner
decls.doc:
**The index principal value along a two-ray corner vanishes.** For nonzero rays of equal
length the excision `‖γ t - z₀‖ > ε` is the symmetric condition `|t| ‖v‖ > ε`, and the integrand is
the odd function `1 / t` on both rays, so *every* truncated integral is `0` — not merely its limit.
Equal norms also permit `u = v = 0`, where the curve is constant at `z₀` and the integrand vanishes
identically; that case is immediate.
decls.title: The index principal value along a two-ray corner vanishes
decls.statement:
theorem hasCauchyPVAt_inv_sub_twoRayCorner {z₀ u v : ℂ} (huv : ‖u‖ = ‖v‖) (R : ℝ) :
    HasCauchyPVAt (twoRayCorner z₀ u v) (-R) R (fun z => (z - z₀)⁻¹) z₀ 0

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.cauchyPVExistsAt_inv_sub_twoRayCorner
decls.doc:
Existence form of `hasCauchyPVAt_inv_sub_twoRayCorner`, matching the existence-form API that
the winding-number composition lemmas consume.
decls.statement:
theorem cauchyPVExistsAt_inv_sub_twoRayCorner {z₀ u v : ℂ} (huv : ‖u‖ = ‖v‖) (R : ℝ) :
    CauchyPVExistsAt (twoRayCorner z₀ u v) (-R) R (fun z => (z - z₀)⁻¹) z₀

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.windingNumber_eq_zero_twoRayCorner
decls.doc:
**The generalized winding number of a two-ray corner vanishes.** The radial approach and
departure contribute nothing to the model sector's index; all of it comes from the arc.
decls.title: The generalized winding number of a two-ray corner vanishes
decls.statement:
theorem windingNumber_eq_zero_twoRayCorner {z₀ u v : ℂ} (huv : ‖u‖ = ‖v‖) (R : ℝ) :
    windingNumber (twoRayCorner z₀ u v) (-R) R z₀ = 0

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.windingNumber_at_i
decls.doc:
**The winding number `½` at `i`** — the coefficient of `ord_i(f)` in the valence formula. The
semicircle (`[0, π]`) specialization of `indexIntegral_arc` (`π / 2π = ½`): `i` is a
*smooth* boundary point of the fundamental domain, so the valence contour indents around it by a
**semicircle** (opening angle `α = π`). The statement is the generic arc computation; the point `i`
names its downstream valence-formula role.
decls.title: The winding number `½` at `i`
decls.statement:
theorem windingNumber_at_i {z₀ : ℂ} {r : ℝ} (hr : r ≠ 0) :
    (2 * (Real.pi : ℂ) * Complex.I)⁻¹ *
        ∫ θ in (0 : ℝ)..Real.pi, deriv (circleMap z₀ r) θ / (circleMap z₀ r θ - z₀)
      = 1 / 2

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.windingNumber_at_rho
decls.doc:
**The winding number `1/6` at `ρ`** — the per-corner coefficient in the valence formula. The
`[0, π/3]` specialization of `indexIntegral_arc` (`(π/3) / 2π = 1/6`): `ρ` is a `π/3` corner
of the fundamental domain, so the contour indents around it by a `π/3` arc, and the two such corners
(`ρ` and `ρ+1`) each contribute `1/6`, summing to the `1/3` coefficient of `ord_ρ(f)`. The statement
is the generic arc computation; the point `ρ` names its downstream valence-formula role.
decls.title: The winding number `1/6` at `ρ`
decls.statement:
theorem windingNumber_at_rho {z₀ : ℂ} {r : ℝ} (hr : r ≠ 0) :
    (2 * (Real.pi : ℂ) * Complex.I)⁻¹ *
        ∫ θ in (0 : ℝ)..(Real.pi / 3), deriv (circleMap z₀ r) θ / (circleMap z₀ r θ - z₀)
      = 1 / 6

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.isNullHomologous_univ
decls.doc: A curve is null-homologous in the whole plane, since there are no exterior points.
decls.statement:
theorem isNullHomologous_univ (γ : ℝ → ℂ) (a b : ℝ) :
    IsNullHomologous γ a b (Set.univ : Set ℂ)

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.isNullHomologous_const
decls.doc: A constant curve is null-homologous in every ambient set and on every parameter interval.
decls.statement:
theorem isNullHomologous_const (x : ℂ) (a b : ℝ) (Ω : Set ℂ) :
    IsNullHomologous (fun _ : ℝ => x) a b Ω

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.isNullHomologous_empty_iff
decls.doc: Null-homology in the empty set is exactly vanishing of the winding number about every point.
decls.statement:
theorem isNullHomologous_empty_iff :
    IsNullHomologous γ a b (∅ : Set ℂ) ↔ ∀ w, windingNumber γ a b w = 0

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.IsNullHomologous.refl
decls.doc: Every zero-length parameter interval is null-homologous in every ambient set.
decls.statement:
theorem IsNullHomologous.refl (γ : ℝ → ℂ) (a : ℝ) (Ω : Set ℂ) :
    IsNullHomologous γ a a Ω

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.IsNullHomologous.of_eq
decls.doc:
If the two endpoints are equal, the parameter interval is null-homologous in every ambient
set.
decls.statement:
theorem IsNullHomologous.of_eq (γ : ℝ → ℂ) {a b : ℝ} (hab : a = b) (Ω : Set ℂ) :
    IsNullHomologous γ a b Ω

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.isNullHomologous_empty_of_forall_windingNumber_eq_zero
decls.doc: If every winding number vanishes, then the curve is null-homologous in the empty set.
decls.statement:
theorem isNullHomologous_empty_of_forall_windingNumber_eq_zero
    (h : ∀ w, windingNumber γ a b w = 0) :
    IsNullHomologous γ a b (∅ : Set ℂ)

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.IsNullHomologous.mono
decls.doc: Null-homology is monotone in the ambient domain: enlarging the domain shrinks its complement.
decls.statement:
theorem IsNullHomologous.mono (h : IsNullHomologous γ a b Ω) (hΩ : Ω ⊆ Ω') :
    IsNullHomologous γ a b Ω'

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.IsNullHomologous.of_empty
decls.doc: A curve null-homologous in the empty set is null-homologous in every set.
decls.statement:
theorem IsNullHomologous.of_empty (h : IsNullHomologous γ a b (∅ : Set ℂ)) :
    IsNullHomologous γ a b Ω

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.IsNullHomologous.mono_compl
decls.doc: A complement-subset form of `Contour.IsNullHomologous.mono`.
decls.statement:
theorem IsNullHomologous.mono_compl (h : IsNullHomologous γ a b Ω) (hΩ : Ω'ᶜ ⊆ Ωᶜ) :
    IsNullHomologous γ a b Ω'

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.isNullHomologous_of_compl_subset
decls.doc: It suffices to prove winding-number vanishing on any set containing the complement of `Ω`.
decls.statement:
theorem isNullHomologous_of_compl_subset {E : Set ℂ} (hE : Ωᶜ ⊆ E)
    (h : ∀ w ∈ E, windingNumber γ a b w = 0) :
    IsNullHomologous γ a b Ω

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.IsNullHomologous.congr_windingNumber
decls.doc:
If two curves have the same winding numbers outside `Ω`, null-homology transfers from one to
the other. This is the replacement principle used by homotopy or decomposition arguments before the
homology Cauchy theorem.
decls.statement:
theorem IsNullHomologous.congr_windingNumber (h : IsNullHomologous γ a b Ω)
    (hwind : ∀ w ∉ Ω, windingNumber η c d w = windingNumber γ a b w) :
    IsNullHomologous η c d Ω

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.IsNullHomologous.union_left
decls.doc: If a curve is null-homologous in `Ω`, then it is null-homologous in `Ω ∪ Ω'`.
decls.statement:
theorem IsNullHomologous.union_left (h : IsNullHomologous γ a b Ω) :
    IsNullHomologous γ a b (Ω ∪ Ω')

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.IsNullHomologous.union_right
decls.doc: If a curve is null-homologous in `Ω'`, then it is null-homologous in `Ω ∪ Ω'`.
decls.statement:
theorem IsNullHomologous.union_right (h : IsNullHomologous γ a b Ω') :
    IsNullHomologous γ a b (Ω ∪ Ω')

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.IsNullHomologous.inter
decls.doc:
If a curve is null-homologous in each of two domains, it is null-homologous in their
intersection.
decls.statement:
theorem IsNullHomologous.inter (hΩ : IsNullHomologous γ a b Ω)
    (hΩ' : IsNullHomologous γ a b Ω') :
    IsNullHomologous γ a b (Ω ∩ Ω')

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.isNullHomologous_iInter
decls.doc:
If a curve is null-homologous in every member of an indexed family, then it is
null-homologous in the intersection of the family.

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.intervalIntegrable_inv_sub_truncated
decls.doc:
The `ε`-truncated simple-pole integrand is interval-integrable: off the `ε`-ball the
integrand is dominated by `(1/ε) · ‖deriv γ‖`.
decls.statement:
theorem intervalIntegrable_inv_sub_truncated {γ : ℝ → ℂ} {s : ℂ} {a b : ℝ}
    (hγ_cont : ContinuousOn γ (uIcc a b))
    (hderiv_int : IntervalIntegrable (fun t => deriv γ t) MeasureTheory.volume a b)
    {ε : ℝ} (hε : 0 < ε) :
    IntervalIntegrable (fun t => if ‖γ t - s‖ > ε then (γ t - s)⁻¹ * deriv γ t else 0)
      MeasureTheory.volume a b

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.integral_inv_sub_mul_deriv_eq_log_window
decls.doc:
The winding integral is the log of the chord quotient on an ordered pole-free interval
with the chord quotients anchored at the left endpoint in the slit plane: the `Icc`-hypothesis
form of `integral_inv_sub_mul_deriv_eq_log`, with the integrability discharged.
decls.statement:
theorem integral_inv_sub_mul_deriv_eq_log_window {γ : ℝ → ℂ} {s : ℂ} {P : Set ℝ}
    {l u : ℝ} (hlu : l ≤ u) (hP : P.Countable)
    (hγ_cont : ContinuousOn γ (Icc l u))
    (hγ_diffP : ∀ t ∈ Ioo l u \ P, DifferentiableAt ℝ γ t)
    (hderiv_int : IntervalIntegrable (fun t => deriv γ t) MeasureTheory.volume l u)
    (h_ne : ∀ t ∈ Icc l u, γ t ≠ s)
    (h_slit : ∀ t ∈ Icc l u, (γ t - s) / (γ l - s) ∈ Complex.slitPlane) :
    ∫ t in l..u, (γ t - s)⁻¹ * deriv γ t =
      Complex.log ((γ u - s) / (γ l - s))

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.log_sum_decomp
decls.doc:
**Real/imaginary decomposition of a sum of two chord logarithms with matching inner
radii**: for nonzero chords with `‖B‖ = ‖C‖`, the inner `log`-radius terms cancel, leaving the
outer log-norm difference plus the argument parts.
decls.statement:
theorem log_sum_decomp {A B C D : ℂ} (hA : A ≠ 0) (hB : B ≠ 0) (hC : C ≠ 0)
    (hD : D ≠ 0) (hnorm : ‖B‖ = ‖C‖) :
    Complex.log (B / A) + Complex.log (D / C) =
      ((Real.log ‖D‖ - Real.log ‖A‖ : ℝ) : ℂ) +
        (((B / A).arg + (D / C).arg : ℝ) : ℂ) * Complex.I

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.arg_annular_quotient_exitTime_tendsto_right
decls.doc:
**Right annular argument limit along a right exit-time function.** If `τR ε → t₀` from the
right (within `Ioi t₀`) as `ε → 0⁺`, and `γ` is continuous at `t₀`,
differentiable from the right with `deriv γ → L_R` from the right, and the tangent-side chord
`(γ (t₀ + r) - s) / L_R` lies in the slit plane, then the argument of the annular quotient
`(γ (t₀ + r) - s) / (γ (τR ε) - s)` converges as `ε → 0⁺` to `((γ (t₀ + r) - s) / L_R).arg`.
decls.title: Right annular argument limit along a right exit-time function
decls.statement:
theorem arg_annular_quotient_exitTime_tendsto_right {γ : ℝ → ℂ} {s : ℂ} {t₀ r : ℝ}
    {L_R : ℂ} {τR : ℝ → ℝ} (hγ_at : ContinuousAt γ t₀)
    (h_diff_R : ∀ᶠ t in 𝓝[>] t₀, DifferentiableAt ℝ γ t)
    (h_tendsto_R : Tendsto (deriv γ) (𝓝[>] t₀) (𝓝 L_R)) (h_at : γ t₀ = s)
    (h_slit_plus : (γ (t₀ + r) - s) / L_R ∈ Complex.slitPlane)
    (h_toR : Tendsto τR (𝓝[>] (0 : ℝ)) (𝓝[>] t₀)) :
    Tendsto (fun ε : ℝ => Complex.arg ((γ (t₀ + r) - s) / (γ (τR ε) - s)))
      (𝓝[>] (0 : ℝ)) (𝓝 ((γ (t₀ + r) - s) / L_R).arg)

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.arg_annular_quotient_exitTime_tendsto_left
decls.doc:
**Left annular argument limit along a left exit-time function.** If `τL ε → t₀` from the left
(within `Iio t₀`) as `ε → 0⁺`, and `γ` is continuous at `t₀`,
differentiable from the left with `deriv γ → L_L` from the left, and the tangent-side chord
`(-L_L) / (γ (t₀ - r) - s)` lies in the slit plane, then the argument of the annular quotient
`(γ (τL ε) - s) / (γ (t₀ - r) - s)` converges as `ε → 0⁺` to `((-L_L) / (γ (t₀ - r) - s)).arg`.
decls.title: Left annular argument limit along a left exit-time function
decls.statement:
theorem arg_annular_quotient_exitTime_tendsto_left {γ : ℝ → ℂ} {s : ℂ} {t₀ r : ℝ}
    {L_L : ℂ} {τL : ℝ → ℝ} (hγ_at : ContinuousAt γ t₀)
    (h_diff_L : ∀ᶠ t in 𝓝[<] t₀, DifferentiableAt ℝ γ t)
    (h_tendsto_L : Tendsto (deriv γ) (𝓝[<] t₀) (𝓝 L_L)) (h_at : γ t₀ = s)
    (h_slit_minus : (-L_L) / (γ (t₀ - r) - s) ∈ Complex.slitPlane)
    (h_toL : Tendsto τL (𝓝[>] (0 : ℝ)) (𝓝[<] t₀)) :
    Tendsto (fun ε : ℝ => Complex.arg ((γ (τL ε) - s) / (γ (t₀ - r) - s)))
      (𝓝[>] (0 : ℝ)) (𝓝 ((-L_L) / (γ (t₀ - r) - s)).arg)

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.perWindow_truncated_integral_eq_log_form
decls.doc:
**Closed form of the truncated window integral at a fixed truncation level.** For exit points
`τl ∈ Ioo (t₀ - r) t₀` and `τr ∈ Ioo t₀ (t₀ + r)` with common exit radius

window, an interval-integrable derivative, continuity on the window, the condition that any
crossing of `s` in the window occurs at `t₀` (at most one crossing; existence is not assumed),
the anchored slit-plane chord quotients on each side, and the window-split identity for the
`ε`-truncated simple-pole integrand, the truncated window integral equals the log-norm difference
of the window endpoints plus the two boundary chord arguments times `I`.
decls.title: Closed form of the truncated window integral at a fixed truncation level
decls.statement:
theorem perWindow_truncated_integral_eq_log_form {γ : ℝ → ℂ} {s : ℂ} {t₀ r ε : ℝ}

    (hderiv_int : IntervalIntegrable (fun t => deriv γ t) MeasureTheory.volume
      (t₀ - r) (t₀ + r))
    (h_unique : ∀ t ∈ Icc (t₀ - r) (t₀ + r), γ t = s → t = t₀)
    (h_slit_R : ∀ a b, t₀ < a → a ≤ b → b ≤ t₀ + r →
      (γ b - s) / (γ a - s) ∈ Complex.slitPlane)

      (γ b - s) / (γ (t₀ - r) - s) ∈ Complex.slitPlane)

    (hradL : ‖γ τl - s‖ = ε) (hradR : ‖γ τr - s‖ = ε) (hε : 0 < ε)
    (hsplit : ∫ u in (t₀ - r)..(t₀ + r),

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.intervalIntegrable_pow_inv_mul_deriv
decls.doc:
The order-`k` polar integrand is interval-integrable off the pole: the polar factor is
continuous there.
decls.statement:
theorem intervalIntegrable_pow_inv_mul_deriv {γ : ℝ → ℂ} {s : ℂ} {l u : ℝ}
    (c : ℂ) (k : ℕ) (hlu : l ≤ u) (hγ_cont : ContinuousOn γ (Icc l u))
    (h_ne : ∀ t ∈ Icc l u, γ t ≠ s)
    (hderiv_int : IntervalIntegrable (fun t => deriv γ t) MeasureTheory.volume l u) :
    IntervalIntegrable (fun t => c / (γ t - s) ^ k * deriv γ t)
      MeasureTheory.volume l u

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.intervalIntegrable_pow_inv_mul_deriv_truncated
decls.doc:
The `ε`-truncated order-`k` polar integrand is interval-integrable: off the `ε`-ball it is
dominated by `(‖c‖ / ε^k) · ‖deriv γ‖`.
decls.statement:
theorem intervalIntegrable_pow_inv_mul_deriv_truncated {γ : ℝ → ℂ} {s : ℂ} {a b : ℝ}
    (c : ℂ) (k : ℕ) (hγ_cont : ContinuousOn γ (uIcc a b))
    (hderiv_int : IntervalIntegrable (fun t => deriv γ t) MeasureTheory.volume a b)
    {ε : ℝ} (hε : 0 < ε) :
    IntervalIntegrable
      (fun t => if ‖γ t - s‖ > ε then c / (γ t - s) ^ k * deriv γ t else 0)
      MeasureTheory.volume a b

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.integral_pow_inv_mul_deriv_eq_sub
decls.doc:
The fundamental theorem of calculus for the order-`k` polar term along the curve, on an
interval avoiding the pole: the integral is the boundary difference of the antiderivative
`c · (-(k-1)⁻¹ (· - s)^{-(k-1)}) ∘ γ`.
decls.statement:
theorem integral_pow_inv_mul_deriv_eq_sub {γ : ℝ → ℂ} {s : ℂ} {k : ℕ} (hk : 2 ≤ k) (c : ℂ)
    {l u : ℝ} (hlu : l ≤ u) {P : Set ℝ} (hP : P.Countable)
    (h_ne : ∀ t ∈ Icc l u, γ t ≠ s)
    (h_diff : ∀ t ∈ Ioo l u \ P, DifferentiableAt ℝ γ t)
    (hγ_cont : ContinuousOn γ (Icc l u))
    (hderiv_int : IntervalIntegrable (fun t => deriv γ t) MeasureTheory.volume l u) :
    ∫ t in l..u, c / (γ t - s) ^ k * deriv γ t =
      c * (-(↑(k - 1) : ℂ)⁻¹ * ((γ u - s) ^ (k - 1))⁻¹) -
        c * (-(↑(k - 1) : ℂ)⁻¹ * ((γ l - s) ^ (k - 1))⁻¹)

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.integral_pow_inv_mul_deriv_eq_zero_of_closed_of_le
decls.doc: The oriented case of `Contour.integral_pow_inv_mul_deriv_eq_zero_of_closed`.
decls.statement:
theorem integral_pow_inv_mul_deriv_eq_zero_of_closed_of_le {γ : ℝ → ℂ} {s : ℂ} {k : ℕ}
    (hk : 2 ≤ k) (c : ℂ) {a b : ℝ} (hab : a ≤ b) (hγ : IsPiecewiseC1On γ a b)
    (hclosed : γ a = γ b) (h_ne : ∀ t ∈ Icc a b, γ t ≠ s) :
    ∫ t in a..b, c / (γ t - s) ^ k * deriv γ t = 0

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.integral_pow_inv_mul_deriv_eq_zero_of_closed
decls.doc:
**A Laurent term of order at least two integrates to zero around a closed curve.** On a
piecewise-`C¹` curve `γ` with `γ a = γ b` that never meets `s`, the integrand
`c/(z − s)^k · γ'` with `k ≥ 2` is the derivative of `c · (−(k−1)⁻¹ (γ · − s)^{−(k−1)})`, so
`Contour.integral_pow_inv_mul_deriv_eq_sub` returns the endpoint difference, which the closedness
kills. This is why only the simple-pole coefficient of a Laurent tail survives in the residue
theorem.
decls.title: A Laurent term of order at least two integrates to zero around a closed curve
decls.statement:
theorem integral_pow_inv_mul_deriv_eq_zero_of_closed {γ : ℝ → ℂ} {s : ℂ} {k : ℕ}
    (hk : 2 ≤ k) (c : ℂ) {a b : ℝ} (hγ : IsPiecewiseC1On γ a b) (hclosed : γ a = γ b)
    (h_ne : ∀ t ∈ uIcc a b, γ t ≠ s) :
    ∫ t in a..b, c / (γ t - s) ^ k * deriv γ t = 0

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.integral_pow_inv_mul_deriv_eq_sub_of_subinterval
decls.doc:
**Antiderivative evaluation on a subinterval missing the crossing.** On a subinterval
`[l, u]` of the window `[t_i - r, t_i + r]`, where the curve meets `s` only at `t_i` and
`t_i ∉ [l, u]`, the higher-order integrand integrates to the difference of antiderivative values
at the endpoints. The two pieces a truncated window integral splits into — left of the entry time
and right of the exit time — are both instances.
decls.title: Antiderivative evaluation on a subinterval missing the crossing
decls.statement:
lemma integral_pow_inv_mul_deriv_eq_sub_of_subinterval {γ : ℝ → ℂ} {s : ℂ} {t_i r : ℝ}
    {k : ℕ} (hk : 2 ≤ k) (c : ℂ) {P : Set ℝ} (hP : P.Countable)
    (hγ_cont : ContinuousOn γ (Icc (t_i - r) (t_i + r)))
    (hγ_diffP : ∀ t ∈ Ioo (t_i - r) (t_i + r) \ P, DifferentiableAt ℝ γ t)
    (hderiv_int : IntervalIntegrable (fun t => deriv γ t) MeasureTheory.volume
      (t_i - r) (t_i + r))
    (h_unique : ∀ t ∈ Icc (t_i - r) (t_i + r), γ t = s → t = t_i)
    {l u : ℝ} (hlu : l ≤ u) (hl : t_i - r ≤ l) (hu : u ≤ t_i + r) (h_excl : t_i ∉ Icc l u) :
    ∫ t in l..u, c / (γ t - s) ^ k * deriv γ t =
      c * (-(↑(k - 1) : ℂ)⁻¹ * ((γ u - s) ^ (k - 1))⁻¹) -
        c * (-(↑(k - 1) : ℂ)⁻¹ * ((γ l - s) ^ (k - 1))⁻¹)

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.perWindow_higherOrder_truncated_integral_tendsto
decls.doc:
**The per-window principal value at a higher-order pole**: at a transverse crossing
`γ t_i = s`, flat of order `n ≥ k ≥ 2` and satisfying the condition-(B) power identity, with
unique crossing on the window, the `ε`-truncated window integral of the order-`k` polar term
`c / (z - s)^k` converges as `ε → 0⁺` to the boundary difference of its antiderivative.
decls.title: The per-window principal value at a higher-order pole
decls.statement:
theorem perWindow_higherOrder_truncated_integral_tendsto {γ : ℝ → ℂ} {s : ℂ} {t_i r : ℝ}
    {L_R L_L : ℂ} {n k : ℕ} {P : Set ℝ} (hr_pos : 0 < r) (h_at : γ t_i = s)
    (hγ_cont : ContinuousOn γ (Icc (t_i - r) (t_i + r)))
    (hL_R : L_R ≠ 0) (hL_L : L_L ≠ 0)
    (h_tendsto_R : Tendsto (deriv γ) (𝓝[>] t_i) (𝓝 L_R))
    (h_tendsto_L : Tendsto (deriv γ) (𝓝[<] t_i) (𝓝 L_L))
    (h_diff_R : ∀ᶠ t in 𝓝[>] t_i, DifferentiableAt ℝ γ t)
    (h_diff_L : ∀ᶠ t in 𝓝[<] t_i, DifferentiableAt ℝ γ t)
    (hP : P.Countable)
    (hγ_diffP : ∀ t ∈ Ioo (t_i - r) (t_i + r) \ P, DifferentiableAt ℝ γ t)
    (hderiv_int : IntervalIntegrable (fun t => deriv γ t) MeasureTheory.volume
      (t_i - r) (t_i + r))
    (h_unique : ∀ t ∈ Icc (t_i - r) (t_i + r), γ t = s → t = t_i)
    (h_flat : FlatOfOrder γ t_i n) (hk : 2 ≤ k) (hkn : k ≤ n)
    (h_B : (L_R / (‖L_R‖ : ℂ)) ^ (k - 1) = ((-L_L) / (‖L_L‖ : ℂ)) ^ (k - 1))
    (c : ℂ) :
    Tendsto (fun ε : ℝ => ∫ t in (t_i - r)..(t_i + r),
        if ‖γ t - s‖ > ε then c / (γ t - s) ^ k * deriv γ t else 0)
      (𝓝[>] (0 : ℝ))
      (𝓝 (c * (-(↑(k - 1) : ℂ)⁻¹ * ((γ (t_i + r) - s) ^ (k - 1))⁻¹) -
        c * (-(↑(k - 1) : ℂ)⁻¹ * ((γ (t_i - r) - s) ^ (k - 1))⁻¹)))

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.IsPiecewiseC1On
decls.doc:
**Piecewise `C¹` on the interval between `a` and `b`.** The curve `γ : ℝ → ℂ` is continuous on
the closed interval `[[a, b]]` (unordered, hence orientation-robust), and there is a finite set of
breakpoints `p ⊆ (min a b, max a b)` such that `γ` is `C¹` on every closed subinterval of `[[a, b]]`
whose interior avoids `p`. Equivalently `γ` is continuously differentiable on each piece between
consecutive breakpoints, with corners allowed only at the breakpoints; an unbounded-derivative cusp
such as `t ↦ √|t|` is excluded, being not `C¹` up to the breakpoint. This is the raw-function form
of the roadmap's piecewise-`C¹` curve — a `Prop` on `γ` itself, with no bundled path type.
decls.title: Piecewise `C¹` on the interval between `a` and `b`
decls.statement: def IsPiecewiseC1On (γ : ℝ → ℂ) (a b : ℝ) : Prop

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.isPiecewiseC1On_iff
decls.doc:
`IsPiecewiseC1On` unfolded to its defining clauses: continuity on `[[a, b]]`, and a finite
breakpoint set off which every breakpoint-free closed subinterval carries a `C¹` restriction.
decls.statement:
theorem isPiecewiseC1On_iff :
    IsPiecewiseC1On γ a b ↔
      ContinuousOn γ (uIcc a b) ∧
        ∃ p : Finset ℝ, ↑p ⊆ Ioo (min a b) (max a b) ∧
          ∀ c d : ℝ, Icc c d ⊆ uIcc a b → Disjoint (↑p : Set ℝ) (Ioo c d) →
            ContDiffOn ℝ 1 γ (Icc c d)

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.IsPiecewiseC1On.continuousOn
decls.doc: A piecewise-`C¹` curve is continuous on the parameter interval `[[a, b]]`.
decls.statement:
theorem IsPiecewiseC1On.continuousOn (h : IsPiecewiseC1On γ a b) :
    ContinuousOn γ (uIcc a b)

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.IsPiecewiseC1On.of_contDiffOn
decls.doc: A `C¹` curve on `[[a, b]]` is piecewise `C¹`, with no breakpoints.
decls.statement:
theorem IsPiecewiseC1On.of_contDiffOn (h : ContDiffOn ℝ 1 γ (uIcc a b)) :
    IsPiecewiseC1On γ a b

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.IsPiecewiseC1On.of_breakpoints
decls.doc:
Build a piecewise-`C¹` curve from continuity on `[[a, b]]` together with a finite breakpoint set
off which every breakpoint-free closed subinterval carries a `C¹` restriction.
decls.statement:
theorem IsPiecewiseC1On.of_breakpoints (hcont : ContinuousOn γ (uIcc a b)) (p : Finset ℝ)
    (hp : ↑p ⊆ Ioo (min a b) (max a b))
    (hC1 : ∀ c d : ℝ, Icc c d ⊆ uIcc a b → Disjoint (↑p : Set ℝ) (Ioo c d) →
      ContDiffOn ℝ 1 γ (Icc c d)) :
    IsPiecewiseC1On γ a b

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.IsPiecewiseC1On.exists_breakpoints
decls.doc:
Extract the finite breakpoint set of a piecewise-`C¹` curve, together with the `C¹` restriction
it induces on every breakpoint-free closed subinterval of `[[a, b]]`.
decls.statement:
theorem IsPiecewiseC1On.exists_breakpoints (h : IsPiecewiseC1On γ a b) :
    ∃ p : Finset ℝ, ↑p ⊆ Ioo (min a b) (max a b) ∧
      ∀ c d : ℝ, Icc c d ⊆ uIcc a b → Disjoint (↑p : Set ℝ) (Ioo c d) →
        ContDiffOn ℝ 1 γ (Icc c d)

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.IsPiecewiseC1On.mono
decls.doc:
Piecewise-`C¹` regularity restricts to any subinterval: if `γ` is piecewise `C¹` on `[[a, b]]`
and `[[c, d]] ⊆ [[a, b]]`, then `γ` is piecewise `C¹` on `[[c, d]]`, with the breakpoint set cut
down to the smaller interior.
decls.statement:
theorem IsPiecewiseC1On.mono (h : IsPiecewiseC1On γ a b) {c d : ℝ}
    (hsub : uIcc c d ⊆ uIcc a b) : IsPiecewiseC1On γ c d

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.isPiecewiseC1On_comm
decls.doc: Piecewise-`C¹` regularity is symmetric in the endpoints, since `[[a, b]] = [[b, a]]`.
decls.statement: theorem isPiecewiseC1On_comm : IsPiecewiseC1On γ a b ↔ IsPiecewiseC1On γ b a

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.IsPiecewiseC1On.symm
decls.doc: Piecewise-`C¹` regularity is invariant under swapping the endpoints of the interval.
decls.statement: theorem IsPiecewiseC1On.symm (h : IsPiecewiseC1On γ a b) : IsPiecewiseC1On γ b a

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.exists_Icc_subset_uIcc_disjoint
decls.doc:
Around any interior parameter outside a closed set `s` there is a closed subinterval of
`[[a, b]]` whose interior contains `t` and is disjoint from `s`.

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.IsPiecewiseC1On.exists_finset_differentiableAt
decls.doc:
**Differentiability off a finite set.** A piecewise-`C¹` curve is differentiable at every
interior parameter outside a finite set — the breakpoints.
decls.title: Differentiability off a finite set
decls.statement:
theorem IsPiecewiseC1On.exists_finset_differentiableAt (h : IsPiecewiseC1On γ a b) :
    ∃ p : Finset ℝ,
      ∀ t ∈ Ioo (min a b) (max a b) \ (↑p : Set ℝ), DifferentiableAt ℝ γ t

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.IsPiecewiseC1On.exists_countable_differentiableAt
decls.doc:
**Differentiability off a countable set.** A piecewise-`C¹` curve is differentiable at every
interior parameter outside a countable set — the breakpoints. This is the exact regularity shape
consumed by the raw contour-integral development (Dixon's argument and the winding-number
machinery).
decls.title: Differentiability off a countable set
decls.statement:
theorem IsPiecewiseC1On.exists_countable_differentiableAt (h : IsPiecewiseC1On γ a b) :
    ∃ P : Set ℝ, P.Countable ∧
      ∀ t ∈ Ioo (min a b) (max a b) \ P, DifferentiableAt ℝ γ t

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.IsPiecewiseC1On.eventually_differentiableAt
decls.doc:
**Eventual differentiability near an interior parameter**, on any within-filter avoiding
the parameter itself.
decls.title: Eventual differentiability near an interior parameter

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.IsPiecewiseC1On.eventually_differentiableAt_right
decls.doc: Eventual differentiability from the right at an interior parameter.
decls.statement:
theorem IsPiecewiseC1On.eventually_differentiableAt_right (h : IsPiecewiseC1On γ a b)
    {t₀ : ℝ} (ht₀ : t₀ ∈ Ioo (min a b) (max a b)) :
    ∀ᶠ t in 𝓝[>] t₀, DifferentiableAt ℝ γ t

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.IsPiecewiseC1On.eventually_differentiableAt_left
decls.doc: Eventual differentiability from the left at an interior parameter.
decls.statement:
theorem IsPiecewiseC1On.eventually_differentiableAt_left (h : IsPiecewiseC1On γ a b)
    {t₀ : ℝ} (ht₀ : t₀ ∈ Ioo (min a b) (max a b)) :
    ∀ᶠ t in 𝓝[<] t₀, DifferentiableAt ℝ γ t

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.intervalIntegrable_deriv_of_contDiffOn
decls.doc:
The derivative of a curve that is `C¹` on `[c, d]` is interval-integrable on `c..d`: the
within-interval derivative is continuous on the compact piece, and agrees with `deriv` on the
interior, hence almost everywhere.
decls.statement:
theorem intervalIntegrable_deriv_of_contDiffOn {c d : ℝ} (hcd : c ≤ d)
    (hC1 : ContDiffOn ℝ 1 γ (Icc c d)) :
    IntervalIntegrable (fun t ↦ deriv γ t) volume c d

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.intervalIntegrable_deriv_aux
decls.doc:
Gluing step for `IsPiecewiseC1On.intervalIntegrable_deriv`: interval-integrability of the
derivative on any subinterval `[c, d] ⊆ [[a, b]]`, by induction on the number of breakpoints
strictly inside `(c, d)`, splitting off the largest one.
decls.statement:
theorem intervalIntegrable_deriv_aux {p : Finset ℝ}
    (hC1 : ∀ c d : ℝ, Icc c d ⊆ uIcc a b → Disjoint (↑p : Set ℝ) (Ioo c d) →
      ContDiffOn ℝ 1 γ (Icc c d)) :
    ∀ n (c d : ℝ), (p.filter (· ∈ Ioo c d)).card ≤ n → c ≤ d → Icc c d ⊆ uIcc a b →
      IntervalIntegrable (fun t ↦ deriv γ t) volume c d

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.IsPiecewiseC1On.intervalIntegrable_deriv
decls.doc:
**Interval-integrability of the derivative.** The derivative of a piecewise-`C¹` curve is
interval-integrable on `a..b`: on each piece the within-derivative is continuous on a compact
interval and agrees with `deriv` almost everywhere, and the pieces glue across the finitely many
breakpoints. This discharges the `hderiv_int` hypothesis of the raw contour-integral lemmas.
decls.title: Interval-integrability of the derivative
decls.statement:
theorem IsPiecewiseC1On.intervalIntegrable_deriv (h : IsPiecewiseC1On γ a b) :
    IntervalIntegrable (fun t ↦ deriv γ t) volume a b

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.PolarPartDecomposition.hasCauchyPVAt_polarPart_term
decls.doc:
One Laurent term of the polar part: the simple-pole term carries the value
`coeff · cauchyPVAt` of the winding kernel, and every higher-order term carries zero around a
closed curve.
decls.statement:
theorem hasCauchyPVAt_polarPart_term (decomp : PolarPartDecomposition f S U) (s : S)
    {γ : ℝ → ℂ} {a b : ℝ} (h_imm : IsPwC1ImmersionOn γ a b) (hab : a ≤ b)
    (hclosed : γ a = γ b)
    (h_interior : ∀ t ∈ Icc a b, γ t = (s : ℂ) → t ∈ Ioo a b)
    (h_flat : ∀ k : Fin (decomp.order s), 1 ≤ k.val → decomp.coeff s k ≠ 0 →
      ∀ t ∈ Icc a b, γ t = (s : ℂ) → FlatOfOrder γ t (k.val + 1))
    (h_B : ∀ k : Fin (decomp.order s), 1 ≤ k.val → decomp.coeff s k ≠ 0 →
      ∀ t ∈ Icc a b, γ t = (s : ℂ) → ∀ L_R L_L : ℂ,
        Tendsto (deriv γ) (𝓝[>] t) (𝓝 L_R) → Tendsto (deriv γ) (𝓝[<] t) (𝓝 L_L) →
        (L_R / (‖L_R‖ : ℂ)) ^ k.val = ((-L_L) / (‖L_L‖ : ℂ)) ^ k.val)
    (k : Fin (decomp.order s)) :
    HasCauchyPVAt γ a b (fun z => decomp.coeff s k / (z - (s : ℂ)) ^ (k.val + 1)) (s : ℂ)
      (if k.val = 0 then
        decomp.coeff s k * cauchyPVAt γ a b (fun z => (z - (s : ℂ))⁻¹) (s : ℂ) else 0)

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.PolarPartDecomposition.hasCauchyPVAt_polarPart
decls.doc:
**The principal value of a polar part is the winding-weighted residue**: along a closed
piecewise-`C¹` immersion whose crossings of `s` are interior and, at every surviving
higher-order coefficient, flat and sector-compatible, the single-point Cauchy
principal value of `decomp.polarPart s` at `s` is `2πi · n_s(γ) · Res_s f`. The higher-order
coefficients contribute nothing — this is the term the Hungerbühler–Wasem sum attributes to
`s`.
decls.title: The principal value of a polar part is the winding-weighted residue
decls.statement:
theorem hasCauchyPVAt_polarPart (decomp : PolarPartDecomposition f S U) (s : S)
    {γ : ℝ → ℂ} {a b : ℝ} (h_imm : IsPwC1ImmersionOn γ a b) (hab : a ≤ b)
    (hclosed : γ a = γ b)
    (h_interior : ∀ t ∈ Icc a b, γ t = (s : ℂ) → t ∈ Ioo a b)
    (h_flat : ∀ k : Fin (decomp.order s), 1 ≤ k.val → decomp.coeff s k ≠ 0 →
      ∀ t ∈ Icc a b, γ t = (s : ℂ) → FlatOfOrder γ t (k.val + 1))
    (h_B : ∀ k : Fin (decomp.order s), 1 ≤ k.val → decomp.coeff s k ≠ 0 →
      ∀ t ∈ Icc a b, γ t = (s : ℂ) → ∀ L_R L_L : ℂ,
        Tendsto (deriv γ) (𝓝[>] t) (𝓝 L_R) → Tendsto (deriv γ) (𝓝[<] t) (𝓝 L_L) →
        (L_R / (‖L_R‖ : ℂ)) ^ k.val = ((-L_L) / (‖L_L‖ : ℂ)) ^ k.val) :
    HasCauchyPVAt γ a b (decomp.polarPart s) (s : ℂ)
      (2 * (Real.pi : ℂ) * Complex.I * windingNumber γ a b s * residue f s)

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.PolarPartDecomposition
decls.doc:
**Polar-part decomposition** of `f` on `U` at the finite singular set `S`: explicit finite
Laurent tails at the points of `S` whose removal from `f` leaves a function differentiable on all
of `U`, with the residue at each `s ∈ S` read off as the first Laurent coefficient. The data is
indexed by `S`, so a decomposition carries nothing beyond what its laws constrain; the polar part
is pinned for every `z` (at `z = s` the Laurent sum takes the junk value `0`, by division by
zero in `ℂ`).
decls.title: Polar-part decomposition
decls.statement: structure PolarPartDecomposition (f : ℂ → ℂ) (S : Finset ℂ) (U : Set ℂ)

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.PolarPartDecomposition.sum_ite_coeff_eq_residue_mul
decls.doc:
**Only the simple-pole coefficient survives.** Summing the Laurent coefficients at `s` against
a weight `c` carried by the simple-pole term alone leaves `Res_s f · c`, the empty polar part
included (both sides are then `0`). Every evaluation of a polar part term by term — as a contour
integral or as a principal value — bottoms out here, the higher-order terms having already been
shown to contribute nothing.
decls.title: Only the simple-pole coefficient survives
decls.statement:
theorem sum_ite_coeff_eq_residue_mul (decomp : PolarPartDecomposition f S U) (s : S) (c : ℂ) :
    (∑ k : Fin (decomp.order s), if k.val = 0 then decomp.coeff s k * c else 0)
      = residue f s * c

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.PolarPartDecomposition.intervalIntegral_deriv_smul_analyticRemainder_eq_zero
decls.doc:
**The analytic remainder integrates to zero** along any closed null-homologous
piecewise-`C¹` curve in `U` — even one passing through the poles of `f`, since the remainder
extends differentiably to all of `U`. The homology Cauchy theorem applied to the remainder.
decls.title: The analytic remainder integrates to zero
decls.statement:
theorem intervalIntegral_deriv_smul_analyticRemainder_eq_zero
    (decomp : PolarPartDecomposition f S U)
    (hU : IsOpen U) {γ : ℝ → ℂ} {a b : ℝ} (hγ_pc1 : IsPiecewiseC1On γ a b)
    (hγ : ∀ t ∈ uIcc a b, γ t ∈ U) (hclosed : γ a = γ b)
    (hnull : IsNullHomologous γ a b U) :
    ∫ t in a..b, deriv γ t • decomp.analyticRemainder (γ t) = 0

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.meromorphicPolarPartTotal
decls.doc:
**The total polar part** over the singular set: the sum of the canonical per-point polar
parts.
decls.title: The total polar part
decls.statement:
def meromorphicPolarPartTotal {f : ℂ → ℂ} {S : Finset ℂ}
    (hMero : ∀ s ∈ S, MeromorphicAt f s) (z : ℂ) : ℂ

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.meromorphicPolarPartTotal_eq_sum
decls.doc: The total polar part, unfolded to the sum of the canonical per-point polar parts.
decls.statement:
theorem meromorphicPolarPartTotal_eq_sum {f : ℂ → ℂ} {S : Finset ℂ}
    (hMero : ∀ s ∈ S, MeromorphicAt f s) (z : ℂ) :
    meromorphicPolarPartTotal hMero z =
      ∑ s ∈ S.attach, meromorphicPolarPartAt (hMero s.1 s.2) z

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.otherPolar_analyticAt
decls.doc: The polar parts of the other poles are analytic at `s`.
decls.statement:
theorem otherPolar_analyticAt {f : ℂ → ℂ} {S : Finset ℂ}
    (hMero : ∀ s ∈ S, MeromorphicAt f s) (s : ℂ) :
    AnalyticAt ℂ (fun z => ∑ s' ∈ S.attach.filter (fun s' => s'.1 ≠ s),
      meromorphicPolarPartAt (hMero s'.1 s'.2) z) s

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.exists_analyticAt_sub_polarPartTotal
decls.doc:
Near each pole, `f` minus the total polar part has an analytic germ: the per-point analytic
part minus the other poles' (locally analytic) polar parts.
decls.statement:
theorem exists_analyticAt_sub_polarPartTotal {f : ℂ → ℂ} {S : Finset ℂ}
    (hMero : ∀ s ∈ S, MeromorphicAt f s) {s : ℂ} (hs : s ∈ S) :
    ∃ g : ℂ → ℂ, AnalyticAt ℂ g s ∧
      ∀ᶠ z in 𝓝[≠] s, f z - meromorphicPolarPartTotal hMero z = g z

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.remainder_eventuallyEq_off
decls.doc: Off the singular set, the extended remainder is `f` minus the total polar part.
decls.statement:
theorem remainder_eventuallyEq_off {f : ℂ → ℂ} {S : Finset ℂ}
    (hMero : ∀ s ∈ S, MeromorphicAt f s) {z : ℂ} (hz : z ∉ (↑S : Set ℂ)) :
    (fun w => if w ∈ (↑S : Set ℂ) then
        limUnder (𝓝[≠] w) (fun u => f u - meromorphicPolarPartTotal hMero u)
      else f w - meromorphicPolarPartTotal hMero w) =ᶠ[𝓝 z]
      fun w => f w - meromorphicPolarPartTotal hMero w

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.eventually_notMem_nhdsNE
decls.doc: A punctured neighbourhood eventually avoids a finite set.
decls.statement:
theorem eventually_notMem_nhdsNE (S : Finset ℂ) (z : ℂ) :
    ∀ᶠ w in 𝓝[≠] z, w ∉ (↑S : Set ℂ)

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.remainder_differentiableAt_mem
decls.doc:
At a singular point, the limit-patched remainder is differentiable: on a punctured
neighbourhood it agrees with the analytic germ of `f` minus the total polar part
(`exists_analyticAt_sub_polarPartTotal`), and at the point itself it takes the germ's value.
decls.statement:
theorem remainder_differentiableAt_mem {f : ℂ → ℂ} {S : Finset ℂ}
    (hMero : ∀ s ∈ S, MeromorphicAt f s) {z : ℂ} (hzS : z ∈ (↑S : Set ℂ)) :
    DifferentiableAt ℂ (fun w => if w ∈ (↑S : Set ℂ) then
        limUnder (𝓝[≠] w) (fun u => f u - meromorphicPolarPartTotal hMero u)
      else f w - meromorphicPolarPartTotal hMero w) z

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.PolarPartDecomposition.ofMeromorphic
decls.doc:
**The decomposition of a meromorphic integrand.** From `f` differentiable on `U \ S` and
meromorphic at each `s ∈ S`, the canonical Laurent data assembles into a
`PolarPartDecomposition f S U`: the orders are the canonical polar orders — so they are
evaluable by callers, in particular `1` at simple poles — and the analytic remainder is
`f` minus the total polar part, extended across the poles by its limits.
decls.title: The decomposition of a meromorphic integrand

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.PolarPartDecomposition.ofMeromorphic_order
decls.doc:
The constructed order is the canonical polar order — evaluable by callers, in particular
`1` at simple poles (`meromorphicPolarOrderAt_eq_one`).
decls.statement:
theorem ofMeromorphic_order (s : S) :
    (ofMeromorphic hU hf hMero).order s = meromorphicPolarOrderAt f s

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.PolarPartDecomposition.ofMeromorphic_coeff
decls.doc:
The constructed coefficients are the canonical Laurent coefficients, along the index
identification `ofMeromorphic_order`.
decls.statement:
theorem ofMeromorphic_coeff (s : S) (k : Fin ((ofMeromorphic hU hf hMero).order s)) :
    (ofMeromorphic hU hf hMero).coeff s k =
      meromorphicPolarCoeffAt (hMero s s.2) (Fin.cast (ofMeromorphic_order s) k)

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.PolarPartDecomposition.ofMeromorphic_polarPart
decls.doc: The constructed polar part is the canonical polar part.
decls.statement:
theorem ofMeromorphic_polarPart (s : S) (z : ℂ) :
    (ofMeromorphic hU hf hMero).polarPart s z = meromorphicPolarPartAt (hMero s s.2) z

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.PolarPartDecomposition.ofMeromorphic_analyticRemainder
decls.doc:
Off the singular set, the constructed analytic remainder is `f` minus the total polar
part.
decls.statement:
theorem ofMeromorphic_analyticRemainder {z : ℂ} (hz : z ∉ (↑S : Set ℂ)) :
    (ofMeromorphic hU hf hMero).analyticRemainder z =
      f z - meromorphicPolarPartTotal hMero z

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.PolarPartDecomposition.intervalIntegrable_polarPart_mul_deriv_truncated
decls.doc:
**The truncated polar-part integrand is interval-integrable** for every `ε > 0`: off the
`ε`-ball around the pole, the Laurent tail is bounded by `∑ k, ‖coeff s k‖ / ε ^ (k+1)`, so the
integrand is dominated by a constant multiple of `‖deriv γ‖` — the integrability clause of
`HasCauchyPVAt` for a polar part along a curve crossing the pole.
decls.title: The truncated polar-part integrand is interval-integrable
decls.statement:
theorem intervalIntegrable_polarPart_mul_deriv_truncated (decomp : PolarPartDecomposition f S U)
    (s : S) {γ : ℝ → ℂ} {a b : ℝ} (hγ_meas : Measurable γ)
    (hderiv_int : IntervalIntegrable (fun t => deriv γ t) MeasureTheory.volume a b)
    {ε : ℝ} (hε : 0 < ε) :
    IntervalIntegrable
      (fun t => if ‖γ t - (s : ℂ)‖ > ε then decomp.polarPart s (γ t) * deriv γ t else 0)
      MeasureTheory.volume a b

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.PolarPartDecomposition.polarPart_eq_residue_div_of_order_le_one
decls.doc:
A polar part of order at most one is its residue divided by the simple factor. For order zero,
both sides vanish; for order one, the unique Laurent coefficient is the residue.
decls.statement:
theorem polarPart_eq_residue_div_of_order_le_one
    (decomp : PolarPartDecomposition f S U) (s : S) (horder : decomp.order s ≤ 1) (z : ℂ) :
    decomp.polarPart s z = residue f s / (z - (s : ℂ))

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.PolarPartDecomposition.f_eq_analyticRemainder_add_residue_div
decls.doc:
Pointwise simple-pole form of a polar-part decomposition. If every bundled polar order is at
most one, then off `S` the function is its analytic remainder plus the sum of the residue terms.
decls.statement:
theorem f_eq_analyticRemainder_add_residue_div
    (decomp : PolarPartDecomposition f S U) (horder : ∀ s, decomp.order s ≤ 1)
    {z : ℂ} (hz : z ∈ U \ (↑S : Set ℂ)) :
    f z = decomp.analyticRemainder z + ∑ s ∈ S, residue f s / (z - s)

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.exists_simplePoleDecomposition
decls.doc:
**Simple-pole decomposition.** Let `U` be open and `S` finite. If `f` is differentiable on
`U \ S`, meromorphic at every point of `S`, and has at most a simple pole there, then there is a
function `g` differentiable throughout `U` such that, away from `S`,

`f z = g z + ∑ s ∈ S, residue f s / (z - s)`.

Points of `S` where `f` is analytic are allowed: their residue terms are zero.
decls.title: Simple-pole decomposition
decls.statement:
theorem exists_simplePoleDecomposition {f : ℂ → ℂ} {S : Finset ℂ} {U : Set ℂ}
    (hU : IsOpen U) (hf : DifferentiableOn ℂ f (U \ (↑S : Set ℂ)))
    (hmero : ∀ s ∈ S, MeromorphicAt f s)
    (horder : ∀ s ∈ S, ((-1 : ℤ) : WithTop ℤ) ≤ meromorphicOrderAt f s) :
    ∃ g : ℂ → ℂ, DifferentiableOn ℂ g U ∧
      ∀ z ∈ U \ (↑S : Set ℂ),
        f z = g z + ∑ s ∈ S, residue f s / (z - s)

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.IsPwC1ImmersionOn
decls.doc:
**Piecewise-`C¹` immersion on the interval between `a` and `b`.** The curve `γ : ℝ → ℂ` is
continuous on `[[a, b]]` and, over a common finite breakpoint set
`p ⊆ (min a b, max a b)`, every breakpoint-free closed subinterval `[c, d]` carries a `C¹`
restriction whose within-piece derivative is non-vanishing on **all** of `[c, d]` — one-sided at
the piece endpoints, including at `a` and `b`. This strengthens `IsPiecewiseC1On` by a
non-vanishing tangent on every piece (`IsPwC1ImmersionOn.isPiecewiseC1On`); the `c < d` guard
excludes degenerate pieces, on which `derivWithin` is not meaningful.
decls.title: Piecewise-`C¹` immersion on the interval between `a` and `b`
decls.statement: def IsPwC1ImmersionOn (γ : ℝ → ℂ) (a b : ℝ) : Prop

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.isPwC1ImmersionOn_iff
decls.doc:
`IsPwC1ImmersionOn` unfolded to its defining clauses: continuity on `[[a, b]]`, and a finite
breakpoint set off which every breakpoint-free closed subinterval carries a `C¹` restriction with
non-vanishing within-piece derivative.
decls.statement:
theorem isPwC1ImmersionOn_iff :
    IsPwC1ImmersionOn γ a b ↔
      ContinuousOn γ (uIcc a b) ∧
        ∃ p : Finset ℝ, ↑p ⊆ Ioo (min a b) (max a b) ∧
          ∀ c d : ℝ, c < d → Icc c d ⊆ uIcc a b → Disjoint (↑p : Set ℝ) (Ioo c d) →
            ContDiffOn ℝ 1 γ (Icc c d) ∧
              ∀ t ∈ Icc c d, derivWithin γ (Icc c d) t ≠ 0

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.IsPwC1ImmersionOn.continuousOn
decls.doc: A piecewise-`C¹` immersion is continuous on the parameter interval `[[a, b]]`.
decls.statement:
theorem IsPwC1ImmersionOn.continuousOn (h : IsPwC1ImmersionOn γ a b) :
    ContinuousOn γ (uIcc a b)

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.IsPwC1ImmersionOn.of_breakpoints
decls.doc:
Build a piecewise-`C¹` immersion from continuity on `[[a, b]]` together with a finite
breakpoint set off which every breakpoint-free closed subinterval carries a `C¹` restriction with
non-vanishing within-piece derivative.
decls.statement:
theorem IsPwC1ImmersionOn.of_breakpoints (hcont : ContinuousOn γ (uIcc a b)) (p : Finset ℝ)
    (hp : ↑p ⊆ Ioo (min a b) (max a b))
    (hpieces : ∀ c d : ℝ, c < d → Icc c d ⊆ uIcc a b → Disjoint (↑p : Set ℝ) (Ioo c d) →
      ContDiffOn ℝ 1 γ (Icc c d) ∧ ∀ t ∈ Icc c d, derivWithin γ (Icc c d) t ≠ 0) :
    IsPwC1ImmersionOn γ a b

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.IsPwC1ImmersionOn.exists_breakpoints
decls.doc:
Extract the finite breakpoint set of a piecewise-`C¹` immersion, together with the `C¹`
restriction and the non-vanishing within-piece derivative it induces on every breakpoint-free
closed subinterval of `[[a, b]]`.
decls.statement:
theorem IsPwC1ImmersionOn.exists_breakpoints (h : IsPwC1ImmersionOn γ a b) :
    ∃ p : Finset ℝ, ↑p ⊆ Ioo (min a b) (max a b) ∧
      ∀ c d : ℝ, c < d → Icc c d ⊆ uIcc a b → Disjoint (↑p : Set ℝ) (Ioo c d) →
        ContDiffOn ℝ 1 γ (Icc c d) ∧
          ∀ t ∈ Icc c d, derivWithin γ (Icc c d) t ≠ 0

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.IsPwC1ImmersionOn.isPiecewiseC1On
decls.doc:
A piecewise-`C¹` immersion is in particular piecewise `C¹`, with the same breakpoint
witness.
decls.statement:
theorem IsPwC1ImmersionOn.isPiecewiseC1On (h : IsPwC1ImmersionOn γ a b) :
    IsPiecewiseC1On γ a b

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.isPwC1ImmersionOn_comm
decls.doc:
Piecewise-`C¹`-immersion regularity is symmetric in the endpoints, since
`[[a, b]] = [[b, a]]`.
decls.statement: theorem isPwC1ImmersionOn_comm : IsPwC1ImmersionOn γ a b ↔ IsPwC1ImmersionOn γ b a

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.IsPwC1ImmersionOn.symm
decls.doc:
Piecewise-`C¹`-immersion regularity is invariant under swapping the endpoints of the
interval.
decls.statement: theorem IsPwC1ImmersionOn.symm (h : IsPwC1ImmersionOn γ a b) : IsPwC1ImmersionOn γ b a

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.exists_Icc_right_avoiding
decls.doc:
Given a finite breakpoint set, every parameter `t₀ < max a b` in `[[a, b]]` has a
breakpoint-free closed piece `[t₀, d]` to its right inside `[[a, b]]`.

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.exists_Icc_left_avoiding
decls.doc:
Given a finite breakpoint set, every parameter `min a b < t₀` in `[[a, b]]` has a
breakpoint-free closed piece `[c, t₀]` to its left inside `[[a, b]]`.

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.IsPwC1ImmersionOn.exists_Icc_piece_right
decls.doc:
**The piece to the right of a parameter**: every `t₀ ∈ [min, max)` begins a breakpoint-free
closed piece `[t₀, d] ⊆ [[a, b]]` on which the immersion is `C¹` with non-vanishing within-piece
derivative.
decls.title: The piece to the right of a parameter
decls.statement:
theorem IsPwC1ImmersionOn.exists_Icc_piece_right (h : IsPwC1ImmersionOn γ a b) {t₀ : ℝ}
    (ht₀ : t₀ ∈ Ico (min a b) (max a b)) :
    ∃ d : ℝ, t₀ < d ∧ Icc t₀ d ⊆ uIcc a b ∧ ContDiffOn ℝ 1 γ (Icc t₀ d) ∧
      ∀ t ∈ Icc t₀ d, derivWithin γ (Icc t₀ d) t ≠ 0

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.IsPwC1ImmersionOn.exists_Icc_piece_left
decls.doc:
**The piece to the left of a parameter**: every `t₀ ∈ (min, max]` ends a breakpoint-free
closed piece `[c, t₀] ⊆ [[a, b]]` on which the immersion is `C¹` with non-vanishing within-piece
derivative.
decls.title: The piece to the left of a parameter
decls.statement:
theorem IsPwC1ImmersionOn.exists_Icc_piece_left (h : IsPwC1ImmersionOn γ a b) {t₀ : ℝ}
    (ht₀ : t₀ ∈ Ioc (min a b) (max a b)) :
    ∃ c : ℝ, c < t₀ ∧ Icc c t₀ ⊆ uIcc a b ∧ ContDiffOn ℝ 1 γ (Icc c t₀) ∧
      ∀ t ∈ Icc c t₀, derivWithin γ (Icc c t₀) t ≠ 0

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.IsPwC1ImmersionOn.exists_deriv_slope_right_limit
decls.doc:
**Non-zero one-sided tangent of an immersion, from the right.** At every parameter
`t₀ ∈ [min, max)` a piecewise-`C¹` immersion has a non-zero limit of `deriv γ` from the right —
the within-piece derivative there — and the chord slope `(γ t - γ t₀) / (t - t₀)` converges from
the right to the **same** value.

Both limits are stated together, and about one `L`, because they are the same tangent: the
derivative form is what the flatness conditions are stated against, while the chord form is what
the direction of `γ t - z₀` at a crossing is computed from. Splitting them into two existentials
would lose the fact that they agree.
decls.title: Non-zero one-sided tangent of an immersion, from the right
decls.statement:
theorem IsPwC1ImmersionOn.exists_deriv_slope_right_limit (h : IsPwC1ImmersionOn γ a b) {t₀ : ℝ}
    (ht₀ : t₀ ∈ Ico (min a b) (max a b)) :
    ∃ L : ℂ, L ≠ 0 ∧ Tendsto (deriv γ) (𝓝[>] t₀) (𝓝 L) ∧
      Tendsto (slope γ t₀) (𝓝[>] t₀) (𝓝 L)

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.IsPwC1ImmersionOn.exists_deriv_right_limit
decls.doc: The tangent-limit half of `IsPwC1ImmersionOn.exists_deriv_slope_right_limit`.

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.IsPwC1ImmersionOn.exists_deriv_slope_left_limit
decls.doc:
**Non-zero one-sided tangent of an immersion, from the left.** The left-hand companion of
`IsPwC1ImmersionOn.exists_deriv_slope_right_limit`: at every parameter `t₀ ∈ (min, max]` both
`deriv γ` and the chord slope converge from the left to the same non-zero within-piece
derivative.
decls.title: Non-zero one-sided tangent of an immersion, from the left
decls.statement:
theorem IsPwC1ImmersionOn.exists_deriv_slope_left_limit (h : IsPwC1ImmersionOn γ a b) {t₀ : ℝ}
    (ht₀ : t₀ ∈ Ioc (min a b) (max a b)) :
    ∃ L : ℂ, L ≠ 0 ∧ Tendsto (deriv γ) (𝓝[<] t₀) (𝓝 L) ∧
      Tendsto (slope γ t₀) (𝓝[<] t₀) (𝓝 L)

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.IsPwC1ImmersionOn.exists_deriv_left_limit
decls.doc: The tangent-limit half of `IsPwC1ImmersionOn.exists_deriv_slope_left_limit`.

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.crossingAngle
decls.doc:
**Crossing angle** of `γ : ℝ → ℂ` at a time `t₀`, valued in `[0, 2π)`: the opening angle of the
model sector, from the exit tangent `L₊` to the reversed entry tangent `−L₋`, taken `mod 2π`. Here
`L₋ = lim_{t → t₀⁻} γ'(t)`, `L₊ = lim_{t → t₀⁺} γ'(t)` are the one-sided limits of `deriv γ`. This
is the orientation of Hungerbühler–Wasem's model sector-curve, whose arc of opening angle `α` runs
counterclockwise from the exit ray to the reversed entry ray and contributes `α / 2π`
(`indexIntegral_arc`). The normalization keeps it nonnegative: a **smooth** crossing
(`L₊ = L₋`) gives `π`, as in HW §3, and a cusp (`L₋ = -L₊`) gives `0`, the tangents alone not
distinguishing a degenerate sector from a full turn. As a `limUnder`-based value it is junk when a
one-sided tangent fails to exist; it is meaningful at the corners/crossings of a piecewise-`C¹`
curve.
decls.title: Crossing angle
decls.statement: def crossingAngle (γ : ℝ → ℂ) (t₀ : ℝ) : ℝ

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.basepointAngle
decls.doc:
**Basepoint crossing angle** of a closed curve `γ` on `[a, b]`, valued in `[0, 2π)`: the opening
angle at the join `γ a = γ b`, from the outgoing tangent `L₊` to the reversed incoming tangent
`−L₋`, where `L₋ = lim_{t → b⁻} γ'(t)` and `L₊ = lim_{t → a⁺} γ'(t)`. This is `crossingAngle`'s
analogue at the basepoint, where the two tangents come from opposite ends of `[a, b]`; a smooth join
(`L₊ = L₋`) gives `π`.
decls.title: Basepoint crossing angle
decls.statement: def basepointAngle (γ : ℝ → ℂ) (a b : ℝ) : ℝ

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.toIcoMod_arg_neg_sub_arg
decls.doc:
For a nonzero `L : ℂ`, the normalized angle from `L` to `−L` is `π`. This is the engine behind
the smooth-crossing values of `crossingAngle` and `basepointAngle`.
decls.statement:
theorem toIcoMod_arg_neg_sub_arg {L : ℂ} (hL : L ≠ 0) :
    toIcoMod Real.two_pi_pos 0 (Complex.arg (-L) - Complex.arg L) = Real.pi

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.crossingAngle_eq_of_tendsto
decls.doc:
**Characteristic equation for `crossingAngle`.** When `deriv γ` tends to `L_L` from the left
and to `L_R` from the right at `t₀`, the crossing angle is the normalized angle from the exit
tangent `L_R` to the reversed entry tangent `−L_L`. This is the form consumers should rewrite with:
the body of `crossingAngle` is not exposed across module boundaries, so it cannot be unfolded
downstream.
decls.title: Characteristic equation for `crossingAngle`
decls.statement:
theorem crossingAngle_eq_of_tendsto {γ : ℝ → ℂ} {t₀ : ℝ} {L_R L_L : ℂ}
    (h_R : Filter.Tendsto (deriv γ) (𝓝[>] t₀) (𝓝 L_R))
    (h_L : Filter.Tendsto (deriv γ) (𝓝[<] t₀) (𝓝 L_L)) :
    crossingAngle γ t₀ =
      toIcoMod Real.two_pi_pos 0 (Complex.arg (-L_L) - Complex.arg L_R)

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.basepointAngle_eq_of_tendsto
decls.doc:
**Characteristic equation for `basepointAngle`.** The join analogue of
`crossingAngle_eq_of_tendsto`, with the outgoing tangent limit at `a` and the incoming one
at `b`.
decls.title: Characteristic equation for `basepointAngle`
decls.statement:
theorem basepointAngle_eq_of_tendsto {γ : ℝ → ℂ} {a b : ℝ} {L_R L_L : ℂ}
    (h_R : Filter.Tendsto (deriv γ) (𝓝[>] a) (𝓝 L_R))
    (h_L : Filter.Tendsto (deriv γ) (𝓝[<] b) (𝓝 L_L)) :
    basepointAngle γ a b =
      toIcoMod Real.two_pi_pos 0 (Complex.arg (-L_L) - Complex.arg L_R)

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.crossingAngle_mem_Ico
decls.doc:
`crossingAngle γ t₀` lies in `[0, 2π)`, the range of the model-sector normalization. Its two
projections `crossingAngle_nonneg`/`crossingAngle_lt_two_pi` are the `@[simp]` normal forms.
decls.statement:
theorem crossingAngle_mem_Ico (γ : ℝ → ℂ) (t₀ : ℝ) :
    crossingAngle γ t₀ ∈ Set.Ico 0 (2 * Real.pi)

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.crossingAngle_nonneg
decls.statement: theorem crossingAngle_nonneg (γ : ℝ → ℂ) (t₀ : ℝ) : 0 ≤ crossingAngle γ t₀

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.crossingAngle_lt_two_pi
decls.statement:
theorem crossingAngle_lt_two_pi (γ : ℝ → ℂ) (t₀ : ℝ) :
    crossingAngle γ t₀ < 2 * Real.pi

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.crossingAngle_eq_pi
decls.doc:
**Smooth-crossing value.** If the one-sided tangents of `γ` at `t₀` agree and are nonzero, the
crossing angle is `π`: there is no genuine corner.
decls.title: Smooth-crossing value
decls.statement:
theorem crossingAngle_eq_pi {γ : ℝ → ℂ} {t₀ : ℝ}
    (h : limUnder (𝓝[<] t₀) (deriv γ) = limUnder (𝓝[>] t₀) (deriv γ))
    (hL : limUnder (𝓝[>] t₀) (deriv γ) ≠ 0) :
    crossingAngle γ t₀ = Real.pi

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.coe_crossingAngle_eq_arg_neg_div_add_arg_div_sub_arg_div
decls.doc:
**The crossing angle is what the boundary arguments carry beyond the endpoint sweep.** Fix
non-zero one-sided tangent limits `L_L`, `L_R` at `t₀` and non-zero `w_L`, `w_R`. Then the two
sum `arg (−L_L / w_L) + arg (w_R / L_R)` is the argument `arg (w_R / w_L)` swept from `w_L` to
`w_R`, plus exactly the crossing angle.

The intended reading takes `w_L = γ (t₀ − r) − s` and `w_R = γ (t₀ + r) − s` at the ends of a
crossing window, where the first two
arguments on the right are precisely the boundary arguments of the per-window principal value
(`perWindow_truncated_integral_tendsto`): the identity says that limit sees the crossing angle plus
a term depending only on the window endpoints. Nothing in the proof uses that reading, so `w_L` and
`w_R` are left free.

The equation is between `Real.Angle`s. That is not a weakening for convenience but the exact
statement: `Complex.arg` is additive only mod `2π`, and `crossingAngle` is itself a `toIcoMod`
normalization, so no `ℝ`-valued form is available without pinning a branch.
decls.title: The crossing angle is what the boundary arguments carry beyond the endpoint sweep
decls.statement:
theorem coe_crossingAngle_eq_arg_neg_div_add_arg_div_sub_arg_div {γ : ℝ → ℂ} {t₀ : ℝ}
    {L_R L_L w_L w_R : ℂ} (hL_L : L_L ≠ 0) (hL_R : L_R ≠ 0) (hw_L : w_L ≠ 0) (hw_R : w_R ≠ 0)
    (h_R : Filter.Tendsto (deriv γ) (𝓝[>] t₀) (𝓝 L_R))
    (h_L : Filter.Tendsto (deriv γ) (𝓝[<] t₀) (𝓝 L_L)) :
    (crossingAngle γ t₀ : Real.Angle)
      = ((((-L_L) / w_L).arg : ℝ) : Real.Angle) + (((w_R / L_R).arg : ℝ) : Real.Angle)
        - (((w_R / w_L).arg : ℝ) : Real.Angle)

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.basepointAngle_mem_Ico
decls.doc:
`basepointAngle γ a b` lies in `[0, 2π)`, the range of the model-sector normalization. Its two
projections `basepointAngle_nonneg`/`basepointAngle_lt_two_pi` are the `@[simp]` normal forms.
decls.statement:
theorem basepointAngle_mem_Ico (γ : ℝ → ℂ) (a b : ℝ) :
    basepointAngle γ a b ∈ Set.Ico 0 (2 * Real.pi)

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.basepointAngle_nonneg
decls.statement: theorem basepointAngle_nonneg (γ : ℝ → ℂ) (a b : ℝ) : 0 ≤ basepointAngle γ a b

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.basepointAngle_lt_two_pi
decls.statement:
theorem basepointAngle_lt_two_pi (γ : ℝ → ℂ) (a b : ℝ) :
    basepointAngle γ a b < 2 * Real.pi

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.basepointAngle_eq_pi
decls.doc:
**Smooth-join value.** If the incoming tangent at `b` and the outgoing tangent at `a` agree and
are nonzero, the basepoint angle is `π`: the closed curve joins smoothly.
decls.title: Smooth-join value
decls.statement:
theorem basepointAngle_eq_pi {γ : ℝ → ℂ} {a b : ℝ}
    (h : limUnder (𝓝[<] b) (deriv γ) = limUnder (𝓝[>] a) (deriv γ))
    (hL : limUnder (𝓝[>] a) (deriv γ) ≠ 0) :
    basepointAngle γ a b = Real.pi

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.FlatOfOrder
decls.doc:
**Flatness of order `n`** of `γ : ℝ → ℂ` at `t₀` (HW Def. 3.2): from each side, `γ` hugs a
one-sided **tangent line** through `γ t₀`, its perpendicular distance to that line vanishing faster
than `‖γ t − γ t₀‖ⁿ`. There are nonzero one-sided directions `v_plus` (right) and `v_minus` (left)
for which the component of `γ t − γ t₀` orthogonal to `v` — of length
`|((γ t − γ t₀) · conj v).im| / ‖v‖`, the distance from `γ t` to the line `γ t₀ + ℝ • v` — is
`o(‖γ t − γ t₀‖ⁿ)` as `t → t₀⁺`, symmetrically as `t → t₀⁻`. Order `1` is first-order tangency to a
line; larger `n` forces it to hug the line ever more tightly. Distance is measured to the tangent
*line*, not to a moving point on it, so flatness ignores the along-tangent speed, as in HW.
decls.title: Flatness of order `n`
decls.statement: def FlatOfOrder (γ : ℝ → ℂ) (t₀ : ℝ) (n : ℕ) : Prop

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.FlatOfOrderBasepoint
decls.doc:
**Flatness of order `n` at the basepoint** of a closed curve `γ` on `[a, b]`, at the join
`γ a = γ b`: the outgoing branch at `a` (from the right) and the incoming branch at `b` (from the
left) each hug their one-sided tangent line in the perpendicular sense of `FlatOfOrder`, to order
`n`. The two branches come from opposite ends of `[a, b]`.
decls.title: Flatness of order `n` at the basepoint
decls.statement: def FlatOfOrderBasepoint (γ : ℝ → ℂ) (a b : ℝ) (n : ℕ) : Prop

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.flatOfOrder_iff
decls.doc:
`FlatOfOrder` unfolded: the one-sided little-o clauses that build the flatness hypothesis, so
downstream code can construct or destruct it without unfolding the definition.
decls.statement:
theorem flatOfOrder_iff {γ : ℝ → ℂ} {t₀ : ℝ} {n : ℕ} :
    FlatOfOrder γ t₀ n ↔
      ∃ v_plus v_minus : ℂ, v_plus ≠ 0 ∧ v_minus ≠ 0 ∧
        (fun t => |((γ t - γ t₀) * star v_plus).im| / ‖v_plus‖)
            =o[𝓝[>] t₀] (fun t => ‖γ t - γ t₀‖ ^ n) ∧
        (fun t => |((γ t - γ t₀) * star v_minus).im| / ‖v_minus‖)
            =o[𝓝[<] t₀] (fun t => ‖γ t - γ t₀‖ ^ n)

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.flatOfOrder_of_eventually_collinear
decls.doc:
**A curve with straight one-sided branches at `t₀` is flat there to every order.** If, on each
side of `t₀`, the curve eventually stays on the line through `γ t₀` with direction `v` — which for
complex numbers is exactly the vanishing of `Im ((γ t - γ t₀) * conj v)` — then the perpendicular
deviation is identically `0` near `t₀`, hence `o` of anything. The two directions are allowed to
differ, so a curve with a *corner* at `t₀` still qualifies. This supplies the **flatness** clause
of Hungerbühler–Wasem condition (A′) for indented and polygonal contours; the finite-crossing and
basepoint clauses are separate and must be established independently.
decls.title: A curve with straight one-sided branches at `t₀` is flat there to every order
decls.statement:
theorem flatOfOrder_of_eventually_collinear {γ : ℝ → ℂ} {t₀ : ℝ} {v_plus v_minus : ℂ}
    (hv_plus : v_plus ≠ 0) (hv_minus : v_minus ≠ 0) (n : ℕ)
    (hplus : ∀ᶠ t in 𝓝[>] t₀, ((γ t - γ t₀) * star v_plus).im = 0)
    (hminus : ∀ᶠ t in 𝓝[<] t₀, ((γ t - γ t₀) * star v_minus).im = 0) :
    FlatOfOrder γ t₀ n

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.flatOfOrderBasepoint_iff
decls.doc:
`FlatOfOrderBasepoint` unfolded: the two one-sided little-o clauses (outgoing at `a`, incoming
at `b`) that build the basepoint flatness hypothesis, exposed without unfolding the definition.
decls.statement:
theorem flatOfOrderBasepoint_iff {γ : ℝ → ℂ} {a b : ℝ} {n : ℕ} :
    FlatOfOrderBasepoint γ a b n ↔
      ∃ v_plus v_minus : ℂ, v_plus ≠ 0 ∧ v_minus ≠ 0 ∧
        (fun t => |((γ t - γ a) * star v_plus).im| / ‖v_plus‖)
            =o[𝓝[>] a] (fun t => ‖γ t - γ a‖ ^ n) ∧
        (fun t => |((γ t - γ b) * star v_minus).im| / ‖v_minus‖)
            =o[𝓝[<] b] (fun t => ‖γ t - γ b‖ ^ n)

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.ConditionAprime
decls.doc:
**Hungerbühler–Wasem condition (A′)** for `γ` along `[a, b]`, at the prescribed singular set `S`
of the integrand `f`: `γ` meets each singularity only **finitely often** and is **flat** to the
order of `f`'s pole there. Wherever `γ` meets a point of `S` at which `f` has a pole of order `n`,
the curve is flat of order `n` — tangent to a line at a simple pole, flatter at a higher pole — and
each such `s` is met only finitely often. Together with
condition (B) it is a regularity hypothesis of the generalized residue theorem (HW Thm 3.3). It is
imposed at each *interior* crossing `t₀` strictly between the endpoints and at the *basepoint*
`γ (min a b)` (`= γ (max a b)` for a closed curve), so a join singularity is not left free. The
clauses are stated over `min`/`max`, so the condition is invariant under swapping the endpoints
(`conditionAprime_comm`), like the curve predicates it accompanies. Pole orders are read from
`f` via `meromorphicOrderAt`; `S` selects the singularities to constrain.
decls.title: Hungerbühler–Wasem condition (A′)
decls.statement: structure ConditionAprime (γ : ℝ → ℂ) (a b : ℝ) (f : ℂ → ℂ) (S : Finset ℂ) : Prop

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.conditionAprime_iff
decls.doc:
Characterization of `ConditionAprime` by its three clauses, for rewriting the hypothesis into
the `finite_crossings ∧ interior ∧ basepoint` conjunction (and back via the anonymous constructor).
decls.statement:
theorem conditionAprime_iff {γ : ℝ → ℂ} {a b : ℝ} {f : ℂ → ℂ} {S : Finset ℂ} :
    ConditionAprime γ a b f S ↔
      (∀ s ∈ S, (Set.uIcc a b ∩ γ ⁻¹' {s}).Finite) ∧
      (∀ t₀ ∈ Set.Ioo (min a b) (max a b), γ t₀ ∈ S → ∀ n : ℕ, 1 ≤ n →
          meromorphicOrderAt f (γ t₀) = (-(n : ℤ) : WithTop ℤ) → FlatOfOrder γ t₀ n) ∧
        (γ (min a b) ∈ S → ∀ n : ℕ, 1 ≤ n →
          meromorphicOrderAt f (γ (min a b)) = (-(n : ℤ) : WithTop ℤ) →
          FlatOfOrderBasepoint γ (min a b) (max a b) n)

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.conditionAprime_comm
decls.doc:
Condition (A′) is invariant under swapping the endpoints: all its clauses are stated over
`min`/`max`.
decls.statement:
theorem conditionAprime_comm {γ : ℝ → ℂ} {a b : ℝ} {f : ℂ → ℂ} {S : Finset ℂ} :
    ConditionAprime γ a b f S ↔ ConditionAprime γ b a f S

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.SectorCompatible
decls.doc:
**Sector compatibility** of `f` at an on-curve singularity `z₀` whose sector opens at angle `θ`
(the Hungerbühler–Wasem condition at one crossing): the angle is a rational multiple of `π` and the
finite Laurent principal part of `f` at `z₀` resonates with `θ` under the sector-cancellation
identity `k · θ ∈ 2π · ℤ`.
decls.title: Sector compatibility
decls.statement: structure SectorCompatible (f : ℂ → ℂ) (z₀ : ℂ) (θ : ℝ) : Prop

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.sectorCompatible_iff
decls.doc:
Characterization of `SectorCompatible` by its two fields, for rewriting the hypothesis into the
`angle_rational ∧ laurent_compatible` conjunction (and back via the anonymous constructor).
decls.statement:
theorem sectorCompatible_iff {f : ℂ → ℂ} {z₀ : ℂ} {θ : ℝ} :
    SectorCompatible f z₀ θ ↔
      (∃ p q : ℕ,
        q ≠ 0 ∧ Nat.Coprime p q ∧ θ = (p : ℝ) * Real.pi / (q : ℝ)) ∧
      ∃ (N : ℕ) (coeff : Fin N → ℂ) (g : ℂ → ℂ), AnalyticAt ℂ g z₀ ∧
        (∀ᶠ z in 𝓝[≠] z₀, f z = g z + ∑ k : Fin N, coeff k / (z - z₀) ^ (k.val + 1)) ∧
        ∀ k : Fin N, coeff k ≠ 0 → 1 ≤ k.val →
          ∃ m : ℤ, (k.val : ℝ) * θ = (m : ℝ) * (2 * Real.pi)

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.ConditionB
decls.doc:
**Hungerbühler–Wasem condition (B)** for `f` along `γ` on `[a, b]`: at each higher-order
on-curve pole of `f` the crossing sector is `SectorCompatible`. Together with condition (A′)
it is a hypothesis of the generalized residue theorem (HW Thm 3.3), where it forces the
order-`> 1` principal parts to cancel, so that the `PV ∮_γ f` the theorem evaluates is
well-defined. Imposed at each *interior* crossing `t₀` strictly between the endpoints and at
the *basepoint* `γ (min a b)` (via `basepointAngle`), so a join singularity is not left free;
stated over `min`/`max`, the condition is invariant under swapping the endpoints
(`conditionB_comm`). Higher-order poles are found intrinsically via
`meromorphicOrderAt f (γ t₀) < -1`; simple poles need no sector
condition, so the predicate is `S`-free.
decls.title: Hungerbühler–Wasem condition (B)
decls.statement: structure ConditionB (γ : ℝ → ℂ) (a b : ℝ) (f : ℂ → ℂ) : Prop

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.conditionB_iff
decls.doc:
