`indexIntegral_arc_interval`. This is the `windingNumber`-definition form of that raw
index-integral computation.
decls.title: The winding number of a circular arc about its own centre is its angular extent over `2π`
decls.statement:
theorem windingNumber_circleMap_center {c : ℂ} {R : ℝ} (hR : R ≠ 0) (a b : ℝ) :
    windingNumber (circleMap c R) a b c = ((b - a : ℝ) : ℂ) / (2 * (Real.pi : ℂ))

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.windingNumber_circleMap_center_eq_one
decls.doc:
**`n_c(circle) = 1`** — the closed-curve normalization at the centre. The generalized winding
number of the counterclockwise circle `circleMap c R` (`R ≠ 0`) over `[0, 2π]` about its centre `c`
is `1`, the interior value. This is the `[0, 2π]` specialization of `windingNumber_circleMap_center`
(`2π / 2π = 1`); it reconciles with `circleIntegral.integral_sub_center_inv`. Unlike
`windingNumber_circleMap_eq_one_of_dist_lt`, this covers a negative radius `R` as well.
decls.title: `n_c(circle) = 1`
decls.statement:
theorem windingNumber_circleMap_center_eq_one {c : ℂ} {R : ℝ} (hR : R ≠ 0) :
    windingNumber (circleMap c R) 0 (2 * Real.pi) c = 1

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.windingNumber_circleMap_center_eq_half
decls.doc:
**`n_c(semicircle) = ½` at the centre**, the `[0, π]` specialization of
`windingNumber_circleMap_center`.

This is one of the two ingredients of a half-disc contour computation: the arc about the point
supplies `½`, and `windingNumber_eq_zero_segment` supplies `0` for a diameter *through* it. The
combined contour, and the additivity argument assembling the two, are not established here.
decls.title: `n_c(semicircle) = ½` at the centre
decls.statement:
theorem windingNumber_circleMap_center_eq_half {c : ℂ} {R : ℝ} (hR : R ≠ 0) :
    windingNumber (circleMap c R) 0 Real.pi c = 1 / 2

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.windingNumber_circleMap_eq_zero_of_lt_dist
decls.doc:
**`n_w(circle) = 0` outside the disc** — the roadmap's "`n` is `0` outside" companion to the
centre normalization. For a point `w` strictly outside the closed disc (`R < dist w c`, with
`R ≥ 0`), the generalized winding number of `circleMap c R` over `[0, 2π]` about `w` vanishes: the
kernel is holomorphic across the disc, so the Cauchy-kernel circle integral is `0`.
decls.title: `n_w(circle) = 0` outside the disc
decls.statement:
theorem windingNumber_circleMap_eq_zero_of_lt_dist {c w : ℂ} {R : ℝ} (hR : 0 ≤ R)
    (hw : R < dist w c) : windingNumber (circleMap c R) 0 (2 * Real.pi) w = 0

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.windingNumber_eq_add_of_hasCauchyPVAt
decls.doc:
**Additivity of the generalized winding number from explicit principal-value witnesses.**
If the index-integrand principal values about `z₀` on `[a, b]` and `[b, c]` are `L₁` and `L₂`,
then the winding number over `[a, c]` is the sum of the two winding numbers.
decls.title: Additivity of the generalized winding number from explicit principal-value witnesses
decls.statement:
theorem windingNumber_eq_add_of_hasCauchyPVAt {L₁ L₂ : ℂ}
    (h_ab : HasCauchyPVAt γ a b κ[z₀] z₀ L₁)
    (h_bc : HasCauchyPVAt γ b c κ[z₀] z₀ L₂) :
    windingNumber γ a c z₀ = windingNumber γ a b z₀ + windingNumber γ b c z₀

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.windingNumber_concat
decls.doc:
**Additivity of the generalized winding number over adjacent intervals.** It is enough to know
that the principal values defining the two summand winding numbers exist; the principal value on
the concatenated interval is then supplied by `HasCauchyPVAt.concat`.
decls.title: Additivity of the generalized winding number over adjacent intervals
decls.statement:
theorem windingNumber_concat
    (h_ab : CauchyPVExistsAt γ a b κ[z₀] z₀)
    (h_bc : CauchyPVExistsAt γ b c κ[z₀] z₀) :
    windingNumber γ a c z₀ = windingNumber γ a b z₀ + windingNumber γ b c z₀

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.windingNumber_eq_zero_concat
decls.doc:
If the winding numbers about `z₀` vanish on two adjacent intervals, and the two corresponding
principal values exist, then the winding number about `z₀` also vanishes on the concatenated
interval.
decls.statement:
theorem windingNumber_eq_zero_concat
    (h_ab : windingNumber γ a b z₀ = 0)
    (h_bc : windingNumber γ b c z₀ = 0)
    (hpv_ab : CauchyPVExistsAt γ a b κ[z₀] z₀)
    (hpv_bc : CauchyPVExistsAt γ b c κ[z₀] z₀) :
    windingNumber γ a c z₀ = 0

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.IsNullHomologous.concat
decls.doc:
Null-homology is preserved by concatenating adjacent parameter intervals, provided the
pointwise principal values defining the exterior winding numbers exist on the two pieces. This is
the form used by finite decomposition arguments: after proving the exterior winding numbers vanish
piecewise, they vanish on the concatenation.
decls.statement:
theorem IsNullHomologous.concat
    (h_ab : IsNullHomologous γ a b Ω)
    (h_bc : IsNullHomologous γ b c Ω)
    (hpv_ab : ∀ z ∉ Ω, CauchyPVExistsAt γ a b κ[z] z)
    (hpv_bc : ∀ z ∉ Ω, CauchyPVExistsAt γ b c κ[z] z) :
    IsNullHomologous γ a c Ω

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.IsNullHomologous.concat_of_avoidance
decls.doc:
Null-homology is preserved by concatenating adjacent intervals in the ordinary avoided-pole
case. If both pieces of the curve lie in `Ω`, then every exterior point is avoided; under
continuity and interval-integrability of the exterior index integrands, the needed principal values
are supplied by `cauchyPVExistsAt_of_avoidance`.
decls.statement:
theorem IsNullHomologous.concat_of_avoidance
    (h_ab : IsNullHomologous γ a b Ω)
    (h_bc : IsNullHomologous γ b c Ω)
    (hγ_ab : ∀ t ∈ Set.uIcc a b, γ t ∈ Ω)
    (hγ_bc : ∀ t ∈ Set.uIcc b c, γ t ∈ Ω)
    (hcont_ab : ContinuousOn γ (Set.uIcc a b))
    (hcont_bc : ContinuousOn γ (Set.uIcc b c))
    (hint_ab : ∀ z ∉ Ω,
      IntervalIntegrable (fun t => (γ t - z)⁻¹ * deriv γ t) MeasureTheory.volume a b)
    (hint_bc : ∀ z ∉ Ω,
      IntervalIntegrable (fun t => (γ t - z)⁻¹ * deriv γ t) MeasureTheory.volume b c) :
    IsNullHomologous γ a c Ω

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.indexForm
decls.statement: def indexForm (w : ℂ) : ℂ → ℂ →L[ℂ] ℂ

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.indexFormDeriv
decls.statement: def indexFormDeriv (w z : ℂ) : ℂ →L[ℝ] (ℂ →L[ℂ] ℂ)

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.hasFDerivAt_indexForm
decls.statement:
theorem hasFDerivAt_indexForm {w z : ℂ} (hzw : z ≠ w) :
    HasFDerivAt (indexForm w) (indexFormDeriv w z) z

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.indexFormDeriv_apply_comm
decls.statement:
theorem indexFormDeriv_apply_comm (w z u v : ℂ) :
    indexFormDeriv w z u v = indexFormDeriv w z v u

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.windingNumber_eq_two_pi_I_inv_mul_curveIntegral
decls.doc:
For a piecewise-`C¹` path avoiding `w`, its winding number about `w` is the normalized curve
integral of the closed `1`-form `z ↦ (z - w)⁻¹ dz`. This is the bridge from Tau Ceti's raw-function
winding number to Mathlib's path-based curve integral.
decls.statement:
theorem windingNumber_eq_two_pi_I_inv_mul_curveIntegral {x y w : ℂ} {p : Path x y}
    (hp : IsPiecewiseC1On p.extend 0 1) (havoid : ∀ t : Set.Icc (0 : ℝ) 1, p t ≠ w) :
    windingNumber p.extend 0 1 w =
      (2 * (Real.pi : ℂ) * Complex.I)⁻¹ *
        ∫ᶜ z in p, (z - w)⁻¹ • ContinuousLinearMap.id ℂ ℂ

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.isPiecewiseC1On_eval_of_smoothPathHomotopy
decls.doc:
If the extension of a path homotopy is `C²` on the unit square, then every intermediate
path, extended constantly from the unit interval to `ℝ`, is piecewise `C¹` on `[0, 1]`.
decls.statement:
theorem isPiecewiseC1On_eval_of_smoothPathHomotopy {x y : ℂ} {p q : Path x y}
    (φ : p.Homotopy q)
    (hφsmooth : ContDiffOn ℝ 2
      (fun st : ℝ × ℝ ↦ Set.IccExtend zero_le_one (φ.toHomotopy.extend st.1) st.2)
      (Set.Icc 0 1))
    (s : I) :
    IsPiecewiseC1On (φ.eval s).extend 0 1

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.windingNumber_eq_of_pathHomotopy
decls.doc:
**Homotopy invariance of the winding number off the curve.** Two closed paths joined through
`ℂ \ {w}` by a path homotopy whose extension to the unit square is `C²` have the same winding number
about `w`.
decls.title: Homotopy invariance of the winding number off the curve
decls.statement:
theorem windingNumber_eq_of_pathHomotopy {x w : ℂ} {p q : Path x x}
    (φ : p.Homotopy q)
    (hφsmooth : ContDiffOn ℝ 2
      (fun st : ℝ × ℝ ↦ Set.IccExtend zero_le_one (φ.toHomotopy.extend st.1) st.2)
      (Set.Icc 0 1))
    (havoid : ∀ st : Set.Icc (0 : ℝ) 1 × Set.Icc (0 : ℝ) 1, φ st ≠ w) :
    windingNumber p.extend 0 1 w = windingNumber q.extend 0 1 w

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.isNullHomologous_iff_of_pathHomotopy
decls.doc: Null-homology in `Ω` is invariant under a `C²` path homotopy whose image lies in `Ω`.
decls.statement:
theorem isNullHomologous_iff_of_pathHomotopy {x : ℂ} {p q : Path x x} {Ω : Set ℂ}
    (φ : p.Homotopy q)
    (hφsmooth : ContDiffOn ℝ 2
      (fun st : ℝ × ℝ ↦ Set.IccExtend zero_le_one (φ.toHomotopy.extend st.1) st.2)
      (Set.Icc 0 1))
    (hφΩ : ∀ st : Set.Icc (0 : ℝ) 1 × Set.Icc (0 : ℝ) 1, φ st ∈ Ω) :
    IsNullHomologous p.extend 0 1 Ω ↔ IsNullHomologous q.extend 0 1 Ω

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.windingNumber_comp_reparam
decls.doc:
**Reparametrization invariance of the generalized winding number** (HW Def 2.1), for a point
`z₀` off the curve. Precomposing with a change of parameter `φ` that has an ambient derivative
`φ' t` at each `t ∈ [[a, b]]`, with `φ'` continuous, leaves the winding number unchanged, the
parameter interval `[[a, b]]` being replaced by `[[φ a, φ b]]`.

The hypotheses on `γ` are stated on the swept image `φ '' [[a, b]]`, which contains `[[φ a, φ b]]`
by the intermediate value theorem, so `φ` need not be monotone. Off-curve is essential: on the
curve the winding number is a principal value, whose excision windows are themselves
reparametrized.
decls.title: Reparametrization invariance of the generalized winding number
decls.statement:
theorem windingNumber_comp_reparam
    (hφ : ∀ t ∈ Set.uIcc a b, HasDerivAt φ (φ' t) t)
    (hφ' : ContinuousOn φ' (Set.uIcc a b))
    (hγ : ∀ u ∈ φ '' Set.uIcc a b, DifferentiableAt ℝ γ u)
    (hγ' : ContinuousOn (deriv γ) (φ '' Set.uIcc a b))
    (havoid : ∀ u ∈ φ '' Set.uIcc a b, γ u ≠ z₀) :
    windingNumber (γ ∘ φ) a b z₀ = windingNumber γ (φ a) (φ b) z₀

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.windingNumber_comp_mul_add
decls.doc:
The affine special case of `windingNumber_comp_reparam`: precomposing a curve with
`t ↦ r * t + s` moves the parameter interval to `[[r * a + s, r * b + s]]` and leaves the winding
number about an off-curve point unchanged. Unlike the general statement this needs no separate
continuity hypothesis on the parameter speed, the derivative being the constant `r`.
decls.statement:
theorem windingNumber_comp_mul_add {r s : ℝ}
    (hγ : ∀ u ∈ Set.uIcc (r * a + s) (r * b + s), DifferentiableAt ℝ γ u)
    (hγ' : ContinuousOn (deriv γ) (Set.uIcc (r * a + s) (r * b + s)))
    (havoid : ∀ u ∈ Set.uIcc (r * a + s) (r * b + s), γ u ≠ z₀) :
    windingNumber (γ ∘ fun t => r * t + s) a b z₀
      = windingNumber γ (r * a + s) (r * b + s) z₀

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.IsNullHomologous.comp_reparam
decls.doc:
**Null-homology transports along a reparametrization.** If a curve lies in `Ω` and is
null-homologous there, then so is its precomposition with any change of parameter `φ` that has an
ambient derivative `φ' t` at each `t ∈ [[a, b]]`, with `φ'` continuous.
decls.title: Null-homology transports along a reparametrization
decls.statement:
theorem IsNullHomologous.comp_reparam
    (h : IsNullHomologous γ (φ a) (φ b) Ω)
    (hφ : ∀ t ∈ Set.uIcc a b, HasDerivAt φ (φ' t) t)
    (hφ' : ContinuousOn φ' (Set.uIcc a b))
    (hγ : ∀ u ∈ φ '' Set.uIcc a b, DifferentiableAt ℝ γ u)
    (hγ' : ContinuousOn (deriv γ) (φ '' Set.uIcc a b))
    (hγΩ : ∀ u ∈ φ '' Set.uIcc a b, γ u ∈ Ω) :
    IsNullHomologous (γ ∘ φ) a b Ω

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.windingNumber_symm
decls.doc:
The generalized winding number changes sign when the interval orientation is reversed,
provided the principal value defining the original winding number exists.
decls.statement:
theorem windingNumber_symm (h : CauchyPVExistsAt γ a b κ[z₀] z₀) :
    windingNumber γ b a z₀ = -windingNumber γ a b z₀

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.windingNumber_eq_zero_symm
decls.doc:
Pointwise vanishing of a winding number is preserved by reversing the interval orientation,
under the principal-value existence hypothesis that makes the two winding-number values honest.
decls.statement:
theorem windingNumber_eq_zero_symm (hzero : windingNumber γ a b z₀ = 0)
    (hpv : CauchyPVExistsAt γ a b κ[z₀] z₀) :
    windingNumber γ b a z₀ = 0

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.IsNullHomologous.symm
decls.doc:
Null-homology is preserved by reversing orientation, provided the pointwise principal values
defining the exterior winding numbers exist.
decls.statement:
theorem IsNullHomologous.symm (h : IsNullHomologous γ a b Ω)
    (hpv : ∀ z ∉ Ω, CauchyPVExistsAt γ a b κ[z] z) :
    IsNullHomologous γ b a Ω

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.IsNullHomologous.symm_of_avoidance
decls.doc:
Null-homology is preserved by reversing orientation in the ordinary avoided-pole case. If the
curve lies in `Ω`, every exterior point is avoided, so the required principal values are ordinary
integrals.
decls.statement:
theorem IsNullHomologous.symm_of_avoidance (h : IsNullHomologous γ a b Ω)
    (hγ : ∀ t ∈ Set.uIcc a b, γ t ∈ Ω)
    (hcont : ContinuousOn γ (Set.uIcc a b))
    (hint : ∀ z ∉ Ω,
      IntervalIntegrable (fun t => (γ t - z)⁻¹ * deriv γ t) MeasureTheory.volume a b) :
    IsNullHomologous γ b a Ω

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.inv_sub_const_mul_eq
decls.statement:
lemma inv_sub_const_mul_eq (hc : c ≠ 0) (w : ℂ) :
    c⁻¹ * (c⁻¹ * (c * w) - z₀)⁻¹ = (c * w - c * z₀)⁻¹

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.hasCauchyPVAt_inv_sub_const_mul
decls.doc:
**Index principal value under nonzero scaling.** Multiplying the curve and the base point by a
nonzero complex number `c` transports the single-point Cauchy principal value of the winding kernel
`κ[z₀]` about `z₀` to that of `κ[c * z₀]` about `c * z₀`, with the same value. This specializes the
general `HasCauchyPVAt.const_mul_curve` to the winding kernel, where the rescaled integrand
`z ↦ c⁻¹ * κ[z₀] (c⁻¹ * z)` agrees with `κ[c * z₀]` along the scaled curve. Exposed so downstream
normalization steps can chain further principal-value APIs from the scaled fact.
decls.title: Index principal value under nonzero scaling
decls.statement:
theorem hasCauchyPVAt_inv_sub_const_mul
    (h : HasCauchyPVAt γ a b κ[z₀] z₀ L) (hc : c ≠ 0) :
    HasCauchyPVAt (fun t => c * γ t) a b κ[c * z₀] (c * z₀) L

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.cauchyPVExistsAt_inv_sub_const_mul
decls.doc:
Existence form of `hasCauchyPVAt_inv_sub_const_mul`: nonzero scaling of the curve and base
point preserves existence of the index principal value, exposed for the same downstream chaining.
decls.statement:
theorem cauchyPVExistsAt_inv_sub_const_mul
    (h : CauchyPVExistsAt γ a b κ[z₀] z₀) (hc : c ≠ 0) :
    CauchyPVExistsAt (fun t => c * γ t) a b κ[c * z₀] (c * z₀)

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.windingNumber_const_mul
decls.doc:
The generalized winding number is invariant under simultaneous multiplication of the curve
and the base point by a nonzero complex number.
decls.statement:
theorem windingNumber_const_mul (hc : c ≠ 0) :
    windingNumber (fun t => c * γ t) a b (c * z₀) = windingNumber γ a b z₀

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.windingNumber_eq_zero_const_mul
decls.doc:
Pointwise vanishing of a winding number is preserved by simultaneous multiplication of the
curve and base point by a nonzero complex number.
decls.statement:
theorem windingNumber_eq_zero_const_mul (hzero : windingNumber γ a b z₀ = 0) (hc : c ≠ 0) :
    windingNumber (fun t => c * γ t) a b (c * z₀) = 0

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.IsNullHomologous.const_mul
decls.doc: Null-homology is preserved by nonzero complex scaling of both the curve and the ambient set.
decls.statement:
theorem IsNullHomologous.const_mul (h : IsNullHomologous γ a b Ω) (hc : c ≠ 0) :
    IsNullHomologous (fun t => c * γ t) a b ((fun z => c * z) '' Ω)

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.truncated_inv_ofReal_odd
decls.doc: The `ε`-truncated index integrand of the real segment through the origin is odd.

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.integral_truncated_inv_ofReal
decls.doc: Every `ε`-truncated index integral of the real segment through the origin vanishes.
decls.statement:
theorem integral_truncated_inv_ofReal (R ε : ℝ) :
    ∫ t in (-R)..R, (if ‖(Complex.ofRealCLM t) - 0‖ > ε then
      ((Complex.ofRealCLM t) - 0)⁻¹ * deriv (⇑Complex.ofRealCLM) t else 0) = 0

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.hasCauchyPVAt_inv_sub_ofReal
decls.doc:
**The real segment through the origin has vanishing index principal value.** The index
integrand `1 / t` is odd, so every truncated integral over `[-R, R]` is `0`, and the principal
value of `∫_γ dz / z` along the segment exists with value `0`.
decls.title: The real segment through the origin has vanishing index principal value
decls.statement:
theorem hasCauchyPVAt_inv_sub_ofReal (R : ℝ) :
    HasCauchyPVAt (⇑Complex.ofRealCLM) (-R) R (fun z => (z - 0)⁻¹) 0 0

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.hasCauchyPVAt_inv_sub_segment
decls.doc:
**A straight segment through its reference point has vanishing index principal value.** The
segment `γ t = v · t + z₀` traversed over the symmetric interval `[-R, R]` passes through `z₀` at
`t = 0`, and the principal value of `∫_γ dz / (z - z₀)` along it is `0`. For `v ≠ 0` this is the
real-axis case transported by the affine change of coordinates; for `v = 0` the curve is constant
at `z₀`, so every positive-radius truncation is identically zero.
decls.title: A straight segment through its reference point has vanishing index principal value
decls.statement:
theorem hasCauchyPVAt_inv_sub_segment (v z₀ : ℂ) (R : ℝ) :
    HasCauchyPVAt (fun t : ℝ => v * (t : ℂ) + z₀) (-R) R (fun z => (z - z₀)⁻¹) z₀ 0

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.cauchyPVExistsAt_inv_sub_segment
decls.doc:
Existence form of `hasCauchyPVAt_inv_sub_segment`, matching the existence-form API of the
adjacent scaling and affine coordinate changes.
decls.statement:
theorem cauchyPVExistsAt_inv_sub_segment (v z₀ : ℂ) (R : ℝ) :
    CauchyPVExistsAt (fun t : ℝ => v * (t : ℂ) + z₀) (-R) R (fun z => (z - z₀)⁻¹) z₀

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.windingNumber_eq_zero_segment
decls.doc: **The winding number of a straight segment through its reference point vanishes.**
decls.title: The winding number of a straight segment through its reference point vanishes
decls.statement:
theorem windingNumber_eq_zero_segment (v z₀ : ℂ) (R : ℝ) :
    windingNumber (fun t : ℝ => v * (t : ℂ) + z₀) (-R) R z₀ = 0

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.windingNumber_translate
decls.doc:
The generalized winding number is invariant under simultaneous translation of the curve and
the base point.
decls.statement:
theorem windingNumber_translate (c : ℂ) :
    windingNumber (fun t => γ t + c) a b (z₀ + c) = windingNumber γ a b z₀

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.IsNullHomologous.translate
decls.doc: Null-homology is preserved by translating the curve and the ambient set together.
decls.statement:
theorem IsNullHomologous.translate (h : IsNullHomologous γ a b Ω) (c : ℂ) :
    IsNullHomologous (fun t => γ t + c) a b ((fun z => z + c) '' Ω)

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.windingNumber_eq_real_integral_of_closed
decls.doc:
**The real bounded-integrand formula for the winding number** (Hungerbühler–Wasem Prop 2.3,
off-curve case). For a curve `γ` on the oriented interval with endpoints `a`, `b` that returns to
its start (`γ a = γ b`), is continuous on `Set.uIcc a b`, differentiable off a countable set `P`,
avoids
`w` throughout, and has an interval-integrable index integrand, the generalized winding number about
`w` is the real integral

`n_w(γ) = (1 / 2π) ∫_a^b (x ẏ − y ẋ) / (x² + y²) dt`,   `x + i y = γ − w`,

with bounded real integrand and no principal value. The winding number is a genuine integer here
(`exists_int_windingNumber_of_closed`), so the index integral is purely imaginary; its imaginary
part is this real integral (`realWindingIntegrand_eq_div`), while its real part — the
increment of `log ‖γ − w‖` —
vanishes by closedness.
decls.title: The real bounded-integrand formula for the winding number
decls.statement:
theorem windingNumber_eq_real_integral_of_closed {γ : ℝ → ℂ} {w : ℂ} {a b : ℝ} {P : Set ℝ}
    (hclosed : γ a = γ b) (hP : P.Countable)
    (hγ_cont : ContinuousOn γ (Set.uIcc a b))
    (hγ_diff : ∀ t ∈ Set.Ioo (min a b) (max a b) \ P, DifferentiableAt ℝ γ t)
    (h_avoid : ∀ t ∈ Set.uIcc a b, γ t ≠ w)
    (h_int : IntervalIntegrable (fun t ↦ (γ t - w)⁻¹ * deriv γ t) MeasureTheory.volume a b) :
    windingNumber γ a b w
      = ((1 / (2 * Real.pi)
          * ∫ t in a..b,
              ((γ t - w).re * (deriv γ t).im - (γ t - w).im * (deriv γ t).re)
                / Complex.normSq (γ t - w) : ℝ) : ℂ)

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.integral_deriv_div_sub_eq_sum_log
decls.doc:
**Index integral as a sum of segment logarithm increments.** For a monotone partition
`a = s 0 ≤ ⋯ ≤ s N = b` of `[a, b]` with `γ` continuous there, differentiable with derivative `γ'`
off a countable set `P`, and with the normalized segment ratio `(γ t - w) / (γ (s j) - w)` in
`Complex.slitPlane` on each `[s j, s (j+1)]`, the integral of `γ' t / (γ t - w)` equals the sum of
the per-segment `Complex.log` increments.
decls.title: Index integral as a sum of segment logarithm increments
decls.statement:
theorem integral_deriv_div_sub_eq_sum_log {γ γ' : ℝ → ℂ} {w : ℂ} {a b : ℝ} {P : Set ℝ}
    {N : ℕ} {s : ℕ → ℝ} (hP : P.Countable)
    (hs_zero : s 0 = a) (hs_N : s N = b) (hs_mono : Monotone s)
    (hγ_cont : ContinuousOn γ (Icc a b))
    (hγ_diff : ∀ t ∈ Ioo a b \ P, HasDerivAt γ (γ' t) t)
    (h_slit : ∀ j, j < N → ∀ t ∈ Icc (s j) (s (j + 1)),
      (γ t - w) / (γ (s j) - w) ∈ slitPlane)
    (h_int : IntervalIntegrable (fun t ↦ γ' t / (γ t - w)) volume a b) :
    ∫ t in a..b, γ' t / (γ t - w)
      = ∑ j ∈ Finset.range N, Complex.log ((γ (s (j + 1)) - w) / (γ (s j) - w))

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.integral_inv_sub_mul_deriv_eq_sum_log
decls.doc:
**Winding-integrand form.** The `γ' = deriv γ` specialization of
`integral_deriv_div_sub_eq_sum_log` with the winding integrand `(γ t - w)⁻¹ * deriv γ t`, as
consumed by the winding-number computation.
decls.title: Winding-integrand form
decls.statement:
theorem integral_inv_sub_mul_deriv_eq_sum_log {γ : ℝ → ℂ} {w : ℂ} {a b : ℝ} {P : Set ℝ}
    {N : ℕ} {s : ℕ → ℝ} (hP : P.Countable)
    (hs_zero : s 0 = a) (hs_N : s N = b) (hs_mono : Monotone s)
    (hγ_cont : ContinuousOn γ (Icc a b))
    (hγ_diff : ∀ t ∈ Ioo a b \ P, DifferentiableAt ℝ γ t)
    (h_slit : ∀ j, j < N → ∀ t ∈ Icc (s j) (s (j + 1)),
      (γ t - w) / (γ (s j) - w) ∈ slitPlane)
    (h_int : IntervalIntegrable (fun t ↦ (γ t - w)⁻¹ * deriv γ t) volume a b) :
    ∫ t in a..b, (γ t - w)⁻¹ * deriv γ t
      = ∑ j ∈ Finset.range N, Complex.log ((γ (s (j + 1)) - w) / (γ (s j) - w))

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.integral_deriv_div_sub_eq_log_norm_add_I_mul_sum_log_im
decls.doc:
**Real/imaginary decomposition of the index integral (explicit velocity).** Refining
`integral_deriv_div_sub_eq_sum_log`, over the same slit-compatible monotone partition the integral
of `γ' t / (γ t - w)` splits into a real logarithm-of-modulus increment
`Real.log ‖γ b - w‖ - Real.log ‖γ a - w‖` plus `I` times the imaginary part of the segment
logarithm sum. For a closed curve the real increment vanishes, isolating the total argument
change.
decls.title: Real/imaginary decomposition of the index integral (explicit velocity)
decls.statement:
theorem integral_deriv_div_sub_eq_log_norm_add_I_mul_sum_log_im {γ γ' : ℝ → ℂ} {w : ℂ}
    {a b : ℝ} {P : Set ℝ} {N : ℕ} {s : ℕ → ℝ} (hP : P.Countable)
    (hs_zero : s 0 = a) (hs_N : s N = b) (hs_mono : Monotone s)
    (hγ_cont : ContinuousOn γ (Icc a b))
    (hγ_diff : ∀ t ∈ Ioo a b \ P, HasDerivAt γ (γ' t) t)
    (h_slit : ∀ j, j < N → ∀ t ∈ Icc (s j) (s (j + 1)),
      (γ t - w) / (γ (s j) - w) ∈ slitPlane)
    (h_int : IntervalIntegrable (fun t ↦ γ' t / (γ t - w)) volume a b) :
    ∫ t in a..b, γ' t / (γ t - w)
      = ((Real.log ‖γ b - w‖ - Real.log ‖γ a - w‖ : ℝ) : ℂ)
        + Complex.I * ((∑ j ∈ Finset.range N,
            (Complex.log ((γ (s (j + 1)) - w) / (γ (s j) - w))).im : ℝ) : ℂ)

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.integral_inv_sub_mul_deriv_eq_log_norm_add_I_mul_sum_log_im
decls.doc:
**Winding-integrand form of the index-integral decomposition.** The `γ' = deriv γ`
specialization of `integral_deriv_div_sub_eq_log_norm_add_I_mul_sum_log_im`, stated with the
winding integrand `(γ t - w)⁻¹ * deriv γ t`, as consumed by the closed-curve winding-number
computation.
decls.title: Winding-integrand form of the index-integral decomposition
decls.statement:
theorem integral_inv_sub_mul_deriv_eq_log_norm_add_I_mul_sum_log_im {γ : ℝ → ℂ} {w : ℂ}
    {a b : ℝ} {P : Set ℝ} {N : ℕ} {s : ℕ → ℝ} (hP : P.Countable)
    (hs_zero : s 0 = a) (hs_N : s N = b) (hs_mono : Monotone s)
    (hγ_cont : ContinuousOn γ (Icc a b))
    (hγ_diff : ∀ t ∈ Ioo a b \ P, DifferentiableAt ℝ γ t)
    (h_slit : ∀ j, j < N → ∀ t ∈ Icc (s j) (s (j + 1)),
      (γ t - w) / (γ (s j) - w) ∈ slitPlane)
    (h_int : IntervalIntegrable (fun t ↦ (γ t - w)⁻¹ * deriv γ t) volume a b) :
    ∫ t in a..b, (γ t - w)⁻¹ * deriv γ t
      = ((Real.log ‖γ b - w‖ - Real.log ‖γ a - w‖ : ℝ) : ℂ)
        + Complex.I * ((∑ j ∈ Finset.range N,
            (Complex.log ((γ (s (j + 1)) - w) / (γ (s j) - w))).im : ℝ) : ℂ)

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.windingNumber_eq_zero_of_unbounded_component
decls.doc:
**The winding number vanishes on every unbounded component of the curve complement.**
For a closed curve with the usual off-curve regularity, if the connected component of `w` in
`ℂ \ γ '' [[a, b]]` is unbounded, then the winding number about `w` is zero. Unboundedness also
ensures that `w` lies outside the curve.

Indeed, far-field vanishing holds outside some compact set. An unbounded component cannot be
contained in that compact set, so it contains a far-field point with winding number zero; the
winding number is constant on the component.
decls.title: The winding number vanishes on every unbounded component of the curve complement
decls.statement:
theorem windingNumber_eq_zero_of_unbounded_component {γ : ℝ → ℂ} {a b : ℝ} {P : Set ℝ}
    (hclosed : γ a = γ b) (hP : P.Countable) (hγ_cont : ContinuousOn γ (uIcc a b))
    (hγ_diff : ∀ t ∈ Ioo (min a b) (max a b) \ P, DifferentiableAt ℝ γ t)
    (hderiv_int : IntervalIntegrable (fun t ↦ deriv γ t) volume a b)
    {w : ℂ} (hcomp : ¬IsBounded (connectedComponentIn ((γ '' uIcc a b)ᶜ) w)) :
    windingNumber γ a b w = 0

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.IsPiecewiseC1On.windingNumber_eq_zero_of_unbounded_component
decls.doc:
**Piecewise-`C¹` form of vanishing on the unbounded component.** If the component of `w` in the
complement of a closed piecewise-`C¹` curve is unbounded, its winding number about `w` is zero. The
finite breakpoint set supplies all raw regularity hypotheses of
`windingNumber_eq_zero_of_unbounded_component`.
decls.title: Piecewise-`C¹` form of vanishing on the unbounded component
decls.statement:
theorem IsPiecewiseC1On.windingNumber_eq_zero_of_unbounded_component {γ : ℝ → ℂ} {a b : ℝ}
    (hγ : IsPiecewiseC1On γ a b) (hclosed : γ a = γ b)
    {w : ℂ} (hcomp : ¬IsBounded (connectedComponentIn ((γ '' uIcc a b)ᶜ) w)) :
    windingNumber γ a b w = 0

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.norm_inv_two_pi_I
decls.doc: The value `‖(2πi)⁻¹‖ = (2π)⁻¹` normalizing the index integral to the winding number.
decls.statement: theorem norm_inv_two_pi_I : ‖(2 * (Real.pi : ℂ) * Complex.I)⁻¹‖ = (2 * Real.pi)⁻¹

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.windingNumber_eq_zero_of_far
decls.doc:
**The winding number vanishes for a point far from a bounded closed curve.** If the closed curve
`γ` lies in the closed ball of radius `R` and `‖w‖` exceeds `R + (∫ ‖deriv γ‖) / (2π)`, then the
integer-valued winding number about `w` has absolute value below `1`, hence is `0`.
decls.title: The winding number vanishes for a point far from a bounded closed curve
decls.statement:
theorem windingNumber_eq_zero_of_far {γ : ℝ → ℂ} {a b R : ℝ} {P : Set ℝ} {w : ℂ}
    (hclosed : γ a = γ b) (hP : P.Countable) (hγ_cont : ContinuousOn γ (uIcc a b))
    (hγ_diff : ∀ t ∈ Ioo (min a b) (max a b) \ P, DifferentiableAt ℝ γ t)
    (hderiv_int : IntervalIntegrable (fun t ↦ deriv γ t) volume a b)
    (hR : ∀ t ∈ uIcc a b, ‖γ t‖ ≤ R)
    (hw : R + (∫ t in Ι a b, ‖deriv γ t‖) / (2 * Real.pi) < ‖w‖) :
    windingNumber γ a b w = 0

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.windingNumber_eventually_zero_cocompact
decls.doc:
**The winding number is eventually zero far from a bounded closed curve.** For a closed curve
`γ` (`γ a = γ b`) continuous on `Set.uIcc a b`, differentiable off a countable set `P`, with
interval-integrable derivative, every point `w` far enough from the origin lies off the curve and
has winding number `0`; equivalently, `fun w ↦ (γ avoids w) ∧ windingNumber γ a b w = 0` holds
eventually along `cocompact ℂ`. The bounded image (continuity on the compact interval) and the
integer-valuedness of the winding number for a closed curve force the small far-field value to be
exactly `0`.
decls.title: The winding number is eventually zero far from a bounded closed curve
decls.statement:
theorem windingNumber_eventually_zero_cocompact {γ : ℝ → ℂ} {a b : ℝ} {P : Set ℝ}
    (hclosed : γ a = γ b) (hP : P.Countable) (hγ_cont : ContinuousOn γ (uIcc a b))
    (hγ_diff : ∀ t ∈ Ioo (min a b) (max a b) \ P, DifferentiableAt ℝ γ t)
    (hderiv_int : IntervalIntegrable (fun t ↦ deriv γ t) volume a b) :
    ∀ᶠ w in Filter.cocompact ℂ,
      (∀ t ∈ uIcc a b, γ t ≠ w) ∧ windingNumber γ a b w = 0

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.integral_truncated_eq_zero
decls.doc: The truncated integral vanishes on an interval where the curve stays within radius `ε`.

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.integral_truncated_eq_of_ae_gt
decls.doc:
The truncated integral is the plain integral on an interval where the curve stays at
distance `> ε` almost everywhere.
decls.statement:
theorem integral_truncated_eq_of_ae_gt {γ : ℝ → ℂ} {g : ℂ → ℂ} {s : ℂ} {l u ε : ℝ}
    (hlu : l ≤ u) (h_gt : ∀ᵐ t ∂MeasureTheory.volume, t ∈ Ioc l u → ε < ‖γ t - s‖) :
    ∫ t in l..u, (if ‖γ t - s‖ > ε then g (γ t) * deriv γ t else 0) =
      ∫ t in l..u, g (γ t) * deriv γ t

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.exists_monotone_leave_radius
decls.doc:
**The monotone exit substrate at a transverse crossing**: a radius `ρ ≤ r` on whose
one-sided windows the distance profile is strictly monotone and the curve leaves the crossed
point.
decls.title: The monotone exit substrate at a transverse crossing
decls.statement:
theorem exists_monotone_leave_radius {γ : ℝ → ℂ} {s : ℂ} {t₀ r : ℝ}
    {L_R L_L : ℂ} (hr_pos : 0 < r) (h_at : γ t₀ = s)
    (hγ_cont : ContinuousOn γ (Icc (t₀ - r) (t₀ + r)))
    (hL_R : L_R ≠ 0) (hL_L : L_L ≠ 0)
    (h_tendsto_R : Tendsto (deriv γ) (𝓝[>] t₀) (𝓝 L_R))
    (h_tendsto_L : Tendsto (deriv γ) (𝓝[<] t₀) (𝓝 L_L))
    (h_diff_R : ∀ᶠ t in 𝓝[>] t₀, DifferentiableAt ℝ γ t)
    (h_diff_L : ∀ᶠ t in 𝓝[<] t₀, DifferentiableAt ℝ γ t) :
    ∃ ρ > 0, ρ ≤ r ∧
      StrictMonoOn (fun t => ‖γ t - s‖) (Icc t₀ (t₀ + ρ)) ∧
      StrictAntiOn (fun t => ‖γ t - s‖) (Icc (t₀ - ρ) t₀) ∧
      (∀ t ∈ Ioc t₀ (t₀ + ρ), γ t ≠ s) ∧
      (∀ t ∈ Ico (t₀ - ρ) t₀, γ t ≠ s)

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.integral_truncated_eq_zero_between_exits
decls.doc:
**The truncated integral vanishes between the two exit points.** With `cₗ < t₀ < cᵣ` inside the
monotone half-windows and both exit radii equal to `ε`, the curve stays within the closed `ε`-ball
on `[cₗ, cᵣ]`, so the `ε`-truncation annihilates the integrand there.
decls.title: The truncated integral vanishes between the two exit points
decls.statement:
theorem integral_truncated_eq_zero_between_exits {γ : ℝ → ℂ} {g : ℂ → ℂ} {s : ℂ}
    {t₀ ρ ε cₗ cᵣ : ℝ}
    (hmono : MonotoneOn (fun t => ‖γ t - s‖) (Icc t₀ (t₀ + ρ)))
    (hanti : AntitoneOn (fun t => ‖γ t - s‖) (Icc (t₀ - ρ) t₀))
    (hcₗ : cₗ ∈ Ioo (t₀ - ρ) t₀) (hcᵣ : cᵣ ∈ Ioo t₀ (t₀ + ρ))
    (hεₗ : ‖γ cₗ - s‖ = ε) (hεᵣ : ‖γ cᵣ - s‖ = ε) :
    ∫ u in cₗ..cᵣ, (if ‖γ u - s‖ > ε then g (γ u) * deriv γ u else 0) = 0

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.integral_truncated_eq_of_left_exit
decls.doc:
**The left window truncation is inert.** On `[t₀ - r, cₗ]`, where `cₗ < t₀` is the left exit
point with radius `ε`, the curve stays at distance `> ε` almost everywhere — strictly before `cₗ`
inside the antitone window, and at least `m > ε` beyond it — so the `ε`-truncated integral equals
the plain one.
decls.title: The left window truncation is inert
decls.statement:
theorem integral_truncated_eq_of_left_exit {γ : ℝ → ℂ} {g : ℂ → ℂ} {s : ℂ}
    {t₀ ρ r m ε cₗ : ℝ} (h_lb : t₀ - r ≤ cₗ) (hcₗ : cₗ ∈ Ioo (t₀ - ρ) t₀)
    (hεₗ : ‖γ cₗ - s‖ = ε) (hεm : ε < m)
    (hanti : StrictAntiOn (fun t => ‖γ t - s‖) (Icc (t₀ - ρ) t₀))
    (h_far : ∀ t ∈ Icc (t₀ - r) (t₀ - ρ), m ≤ ‖γ t - s‖) :
    ∫ u in (t₀ - r)..cₗ, (if ‖γ u - s‖ > ε then g (γ u) * deriv γ u else 0) =
      ∫ u in (t₀ - r)..cₗ, g (γ u) * deriv γ u

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.integral_truncated_eq_of_right_exit
decls.doc:
**The right window truncation is inert.** On `[cᵣ, t₀ + r]`, where `cᵣ > t₀` is the right exit
point with radius `ε`, the curve stays at distance `> ε` almost everywhere — strictly after `cᵣ`
inside the monotone window, and at least `m > ε` beyond it — so the `ε`-truncated integral equals
the plain one.
decls.title: The right window truncation is inert
decls.statement:
theorem integral_truncated_eq_of_right_exit {γ : ℝ → ℂ} {g : ℂ → ℂ} {s : ℂ}
    {t₀ ρ r m ε cᵣ : ℝ} (h_ub : cᵣ ≤ t₀ + r) (hcᵣ : cᵣ ∈ Ioo t₀ (t₀ + ρ))
    (hεᵣ : ‖γ cᵣ - s‖ = ε) (hεm : ε < m)
    (hmono : StrictMonoOn (fun t => ‖γ t - s‖) (Icc t₀ (t₀ + ρ)))
    (h_far : ∀ t ∈ Icc (t₀ + ρ) (t₀ + r), m ≤ ‖γ t - s‖) :
    ∫ u in cᵣ..(t₀ + r), (if ‖γ u - s‖ > ε then g (γ u) * deriv γ u else 0) =
      ∫ u in cᵣ..(t₀ + r), g (γ u) * deriv γ u

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.exists_exit_times_truncated_integral_split
decls.doc:
**Shared window-splitting core.** At a transverse crossing `γ t₀ = s` (non-zero one-sided
derivative limits `L_R`, `L_L`, unique crossing on the window `[t₀ - r, t₀ + r]`), there are
exit-time functions `τL, τR` tending to `t₀` one-sidedly with exit radius exactly `ε`, such
that for every integrand `g` with interval-integrable `ε`-truncations on the window, the
truncated integral over the window eventually equals the sum of the two plain side integrals
up to the exit times.
decls.title: Shared window-splitting core
decls.statement:
theorem exists_exit_times_truncated_integral_split {γ : ℝ → ℂ} {s : ℂ} {t₀ r : ℝ}
    {L_R L_L : ℂ} (hr_pos : 0 < r) (h_at : γ t₀ = s)
    (hγ_cont : ContinuousOn γ (Icc (t₀ - r) (t₀ + r)))
    (hL_R : L_R ≠ 0) (hL_L : L_L ≠ 0)
    (h_tendsto_R : Tendsto (deriv γ) (𝓝[>] t₀) (𝓝 L_R))
    (h_tendsto_L : Tendsto (deriv γ) (𝓝[<] t₀) (𝓝 L_L))

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.halfDiscBoundary
decls.doc:
**The half-disc boundary contour.** On `[-R, R + π]`: the diameter `t ↦ t` for `t ≤ R`, then
the semicircular arc `t ↦ R e^{i(t-R)}` from `R` back to `-R`.
decls.title: The half-disc boundary contour
decls.statement: def halfDiscBoundary (R : ℝ) : ℝ → ℂ

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.halfDiscBoundary_of_le
decls.statement: theorem halfDiscBoundary_of_le {t : ℝ} (h : t ≤ R) : halfDiscBoundary R t = (t : ℂ)

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.halfDiscBoundary_of_lt
decls.statement:
theorem halfDiscBoundary_of_lt {t : ℝ} (h : R < t) :
    halfDiscBoundary R t = circleMap 0 R (t - R)

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.halfDiscBoundary_left
decls.doc: The contour starts at `-R`.
decls.statement: theorem halfDiscBoundary_left (hR : 0 ≤ R) : halfDiscBoundary R (-R) = (-R : ℝ)

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.halfDiscBoundary_right
decls.doc: The contour ends at `-R`, so it is closed.
decls.statement:
theorem halfDiscBoundary_right (R : ℝ) :
    halfDiscBoundary R (R + Real.pi) = (-R : ℝ)

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.eqOn_halfDiscBoundary_segment
decls.doc: On the diameter's parameter interval the contour is the real segment.
decls.statement:
theorem eqOn_halfDiscBoundary_segment (hR : 0 ≤ R) :
    EqOn (fun t : ℝ => (1 : ℂ) * (t : ℂ) + 0) (halfDiscBoundary R) (uIoo (-R) R)

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.deriv_halfDiscBoundary_of_lt_radius
decls.doc:
**The derivative on the open diameter.** Strictly before the junction the half-disc boundary
is the real inclusion on a whole neighbourhood, so the two derivatives agree.
decls.title: The derivative on the open diameter
decls.statement:
theorem deriv_halfDiscBoundary_of_lt_radius {R t : ℝ} (h : t < R) :
    deriv (halfDiscBoundary R) t = deriv (fun s : ℝ => (s : ℂ)) t

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.deriv_halfDiscBoundary_of_lt
decls.doc:
**The derivative on the open arc.** Strictly beyond the junction the half-disc boundary
coincides with the shifted circle map on a whole neighbourhood, so its derivative is the circle
map's, evaluated at the shifted parameter. (At the junction `t = R` itself the contour has a
corner, and no such identity is claimed.)
decls.title: The derivative on the open arc
decls.statement:
theorem deriv_halfDiscBoundary_of_lt {R t : ℝ} (h : R < t) :
    deriv (halfDiscBoundary R) t = deriv (circleMap 0 R) (t - R)

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.integral_halfDiscBoundary_arc
decls.doc:
**The arc piece of the contour integral is the circle-map integral.** Beyond the junction the
half-disc boundary is the circle map shifted by `R`, so translating the parameter identifies the
`[R, R + π]` piece of `∮_γ f` with the integral of `circleMap 0 R` over `[0, π]`. The junction
`t = R` itself, where the contour has a corner, is a single point and does not affect the integral.

The identity holds for every `R`. For `0 < R` the right-hand side is the *upper* semicircle
traversed counterclockwise — the form Jordan's lemma bounds; for `R < 0` the same parametrization
traces the lower semicircle instead, and `R = 0` is degenerate, `circleMap 0 0` being the constant
path at the origin.
decls.title: The arc piece of the contour integral is the circle-map integral
decls.statement:
theorem integral_halfDiscBoundary_arc (f : ℂ → ℂ) (R : ℝ) :
    (∫ t in R..(R + Real.pi), f (halfDiscBoundary R t) * deriv (halfDiscBoundary R) t)
      = ∫ θ in (0 : ℝ)..Real.pi, f (circleMap 0 R θ) * deriv (circleMap 0 R) θ

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.eqOn_halfDiscBoundary_arc
decls.doc:
On the arc's parameter interval — including both endpoints, where the two agree — the contour
is the circle reparametrized by `t ↦ t - R`.
decls.statement:
theorem eqOn_halfDiscBoundary_arc (R : ℝ) :
    EqOn (circleMap 0 R ∘ fun s : ℝ => s - R) (halfDiscBoundary R) (uIcc R (R + Real.pi))

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.continuous_halfDiscBoundary
decls.doc:
**The half-disc boundary is continuous**, the two branches agreeing at the junction `t = R`
(where `circleMap 0 R 0 = R`).
decls.title: The half-disc boundary is continuous
decls.statement: theorem continuous_halfDiscBoundary (R : ℝ) : Continuous (halfDiscBoundary R)

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.eqOn_left_piece
decls.doc: On a subinterval left of the junction the contour is the real inclusion.
decls.statement:
theorem eqOn_left_piece {c d : ℝ} (hd : d ≤ R) :
    EqOn (halfDiscBoundary R) (fun t : ℝ => (t : ℂ)) (Icc c d)

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.eqOn_right_piece
decls.doc: On a subinterval right of the junction the contour is the shifted circle.
decls.statement:
theorem eqOn_right_piece {c d : ℝ} (hc : R ≤ c) :
    EqOn (halfDiscBoundary R) (circleMap 0 R ∘ fun s : ℝ => s - R) (Icc c d)

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.isPwC1ImmersionOn_halfDiscBoundary
decls.doc:
**The half-disc boundary is a piecewise-`C¹` immersion**, with the single breakpoint `R` where
the diameter meets the arc. Off that breakpoint each piece is one of the two smooth branches: the
real inclusion, of derivative `1`, or the shifted circle, of derivative `R e^{i(t-R)} · i`; both
are nonzero for `0 < R`, so the tangent never vanishes.
decls.title: The half-disc boundary is a piecewise-`C¹` immersion
decls.statement:
theorem isPwC1ImmersionOn_halfDiscBoundary (hR : 0 < R) :
    IsPwC1ImmersionOn (halfDiscBoundary R) (-R) (R + Real.pi)

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.cauchyPVExistsAt_arc
decls.doc:
The index principal value of the reparametrized arc about the origin exists: for `R ≠ 0` the
arc misses the origin, so the truncation is vacuous and the ordinary index integral converges;
at `R = 0` the arc is constant at the origin and every truncated integrand vanishes. Either way no
positivity hypothesis is needed.
decls.statement:
theorem cauchyPVExistsAt_arc :
    CauchyPVExistsAt (circleMap 0 R ∘ fun s : ℝ => s - R) R (R + Real.pi)
      (fun z => (z - 0)⁻¹) 0

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.arc_eq_comp_mul_add
decls.doc: The reparametrized arc in the `r · t + s` shape `windingNumber_comp_mul_add` expects.
decls.statement:
theorem arc_eq_comp_mul_add (R : ℝ) :
    (circleMap 0 R ∘ fun s : ℝ => s - R) = circleMap 0 R ∘ fun s : ℝ => 1 * s + (-R)

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.windingNumber_arc
decls.doc: The arc contributes `½`: it is a half-circle about its own centre.
decls.statement:
theorem windingNumber_arc (hR : 0 < R) :
    windingNumber (circleMap 0 R ∘ fun s : ℝ => s - R) R (R + Real.pi) 0 = 1 / 2

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.windingNumber_halfDiscBoundary
decls.doc:
**The half-disc boundary has winding number `½` about the origin.** The diameter through the
origin contributes `0` and the semicircular arc about it contributes `½`.
decls.title: The half-disc boundary has winding number `½` about the origin
decls.statement:
theorem windingNumber_halfDiscBoundary (hR : 0 < R) :
    windingNumber (halfDiscBoundary R) (-R) (R + Real.pi) 0 = 1 / 2

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.halfDiscBoundary_eq_zero_iff
decls.doc:
**The half-disc boundary meets the origin exactly once**, at `t = 0`: on the diameter
`γ t = t` vanishes only there, and the arc stays at distance `|R|` from the origin.
decls.title: The half-disc boundary meets the origin exactly once
decls.statement:
theorem halfDiscBoundary_eq_zero_iff (hR : 0 < R) {t : ℝ} :
    halfDiscBoundary R t = 0 ↔ t = 0

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.flatOfOrder_halfDiscBoundary
decls.doc:
**The half-disc boundary is flat to every order at the origin.** With tangent direction
`v = 1` the perpendicular deviation `|Im (γ t - γ 0)|` vanishes *identically* near `t = 0`, which
is `o` of anything. For `R > 0` that is because the contour is locally the real diameter; for the
degenerate radius `R = 0` the arc collapses to the origin, so both one-sided branches still lie on
the real line.
decls.title: The half-disc boundary is flat to every order at the origin
decls.statement:
theorem flatOfOrder_halfDiscBoundary (hR : 0 ≤ R) (n : ℕ) :
    FlatOfOrder (halfDiscBoundary R) 0 n

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.conditionAprime_halfDiscBoundary
decls.doc:
**Condition (A′) holds for the half-disc boundary at the origin**, for any integrand. The
origin is met exactly once, the contour is flat there to every order (it is locally the real
diameter), and the basepoint `γ(-R) = -R` is not the origin, so that clause is vacuous.
decls.title: Condition (A′) holds for the half-disc boundary at the origin
decls.statement:
theorem conditionAprime_halfDiscBoundary (hR : 0 < R) (f : ℂ → ℂ) :
    ConditionAprime (halfDiscBoundary R) (-R) (R + Real.pi) f {0}

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.dirichletIntegrand
decls.doc: The oscillatory Dirichlet integrand `e^{iaz} / z`, for a frequency `a`.
decls.statement: def dirichletIntegrand (a : ℝ) (z : ℂ) : ℂ

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.dirichletIntegrand_eq
decls.statement:
theorem dirichletIntegrand_eq (a : ℝ) (z : ℂ) :
    dirichletIntegrand a z = Complex.exp (Complex.I * (a : ℂ) * z) * z⁻¹

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.meromorphicAt_dirichletIntegrand
decls.statement:
theorem meromorphicAt_dirichletIntegrand (a : ℝ) :
    MeromorphicAt (dirichletIntegrand a) 0

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.tendsto_sub_mul_dirichletIntegrand
decls.doc:
Near the origin `z · e^{iaz}/z = e^{iaz} → 1`. This single limit yields both the residue and
the simplicity of the pole.
decls.statement:
theorem tendsto_sub_mul_dirichletIntegrand (a : ℝ) :
    Tendsto (fun z : ℂ => (z - 0) * dirichletIntegrand a z) (𝓝[≠] 0) (𝓝 1)

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.residue_dirichletIntegrand
decls.doc: **The residue of `e^{iaz}/z` at the origin is `1`**, for every frequency.
decls.title: The residue of `e^{iaz}/z` at the origin is `1`
decls.statement: theorem residue_dirichletIntegrand (a : ℝ) : residue (dirichletIntegrand a) 0 = 1

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.differentiableOn_dirichletIntegrand
decls.doc: The Dirichlet integrand is holomorphic away from the origin.
decls.statement:
theorem differentiableOn_dirichletIntegrand (a : ℝ) :
    DifferentiableOn ℂ (dirichletIntegrand a) (univ \ {0})

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.neg_one_le_meromorphicOrderAt_dirichletIntegrand
decls.doc:
**The pole at the origin is at worst simple**, for every frequency: the punctured limit of
`z · e^{iaz}/z` exists, which is exactly the criterion of
`neg_one_le_meromorphicOrderAt_of_tendsto_sub_mul`. This is the hypothesis the half-residue
theorem consumes.
decls.title: The pole at the origin is at worst simple
decls.statement:
theorem neg_one_le_meromorphicOrderAt_dirichletIntegrand (a : ℝ) :
    ((-1 : ℤ) : WithTop ℤ) ≤ meromorphicOrderAt (dirichletIntegrand a) 0

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.hasCauchyPV_realSegment_dirichlet
decls.doc:
**The identity along the real segment.** For each positive radius the principal value of
`e^{iaz}/z` along `[-R, R]` on the real axis is `π i` minus the arc contribution. The pole sits on
the path of integration, so this is a genuine principal value, not an ordinary integral.
decls.title: The identity along the real segment
decls.statement:
theorem hasCauchyPV_realSegment_dirichlet (a : ℝ) {R : ℝ} (hR : 0 < R) :
    HasCauchyPV (fun t : ℝ => (t : ℂ)) (-R) R (dirichletIntegrand a)
      ((Real.pi : ℂ) * Complex.I -
        ∫ θ in (0 : ℝ)..Real.pi,
          dirichletIntegrand a (circleMap 0 R θ) * deriv (circleMap 0 R) θ)

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.tendsto_integral_arc_dirichlet_atTop
decls.doc:
**The arc contribution vanishes** for a positive frequency. This is Jordan's lemma: on the
semicircle the amplitude bound is `‖1/z‖ = 1/R → 0`, which the naive `ML` bound could not
exploit.
decls.title: The arc contribution vanishes
decls.statement:
theorem tendsto_integral_arc_dirichlet_atTop {a : ℝ} (ha : 0 < a) :
    Tendsto (fun R : ℝ => ∫ θ in (0 : ℝ)..Real.pi,
      dirichletIntegrand a (circleMap 0 R θ) * deriv (circleMap 0 R) θ) atTop (𝓝 0)

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.tendsto_sub_integral_arc_dirichlet
decls.doc: The auxiliary limit: `π i` minus the arc contribution converges to `π i`.
decls.statement:
theorem tendsto_sub_integral_arc_dirichlet {a : ℝ} (ha : 0 < a) :
    Tendsto (fun R : ℝ => (Real.pi : ℂ) * Complex.I -
      ∫ θ in (0 : ℝ)..Real.pi,
        dirichletIntegrand a (circleMap 0 R θ) * deriv (circleMap 0 R) θ)
      atTop (𝓝 ((Real.pi : ℂ) * Complex.I))

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.tendsto_cauchyPV_realSegment_dirichlet
decls.doc:
**The improper principal value.** As the radius grows, the Cauchy principal values of
`e^{iaz}/z` along `[-R, R]` on the real axis converge to `π i` — the half-residue, evaluated by
the Hungerbühler–Wasem theorem on a contour running through the pole, where the classical residue
theorem does not apply.

This is the roadmap's improper-integral acceptance criterion: the statement is about `cauchyPV`
along the real line, with no reference to the auxiliary half-disc contour used to prove it.
decls.title: The improper principal value
decls.statement:
theorem tendsto_cauchyPV_realSegment_dirichlet {a : ℝ} (ha : 0 < a) :
    Tendsto (fun R : ℝ => cauchyPV (fun t : ℝ => (t : ℂ)) (-R) R (dirichletIntegrand a))
      atTop (𝓝 ((Real.pi : ℂ) * Complex.I))

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.hasCauchyPV_halfDiscBoundary_of_simple_pole
decls.doc:
**The half-residue theorem on the half-disc boundary.** If `f` is holomorphic off the origin
and has at worst a simple pole there (the hypotheses also permit a removable singularity, or
`f` holomorphic at `0`, in which case the residue is `0`), then along the half-disc boundary —
which passes *through*
the origin — the Cauchy principal value of `∫ f` is `π i · residue f 0`: half of what the classical
residue theorem would give for a pole enclosed by the contour, because the generalized winding
number at a smooth crossing is `½`.
decls.title: The half-residue theorem on the half-disc boundary
decls.statement:
theorem hasCauchyPV_halfDiscBoundary_of_simple_pole {f : ℂ → ℂ} (hR : 0 < R)
    (hf : DifferentiableOn ℂ f (univ \ {0})) (hmero : MeromorphicAt f 0)
    (h_simple : ((-1 : ℤ) : WithTop ℤ) ≤ meromorphicOrderAt f 0) :
    HasCauchyPV (halfDiscBoundary R) (-R) (R + Real.pi) f
      ((Real.pi : ℂ) * Complex.I * residue f 0)

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.hasCauchyPV_halfDiscBoundary_inv
decls.doc:
**The motivating example**: the principal value of `∫ dz / z` along the half-disc
boundary is `π i`. The pole sits *on* the contour, so the classical residue theorem does not
apply and the integral exists only as a principal value; the generalized theorem evaluates it as
half the enclosed-pole answer `2π i`.
decls.title: The motivating example
decls.statement:
theorem hasCauchyPV_halfDiscBoundary_inv (hR : 0 < R) :
    HasCauchyPV (halfDiscBoundary R) (-R) (R + Real.pi) (fun z => z⁻¹)
      ((Real.pi : ℂ) * Complex.I)

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.hasCauchyPV_halfDiscBoundary_diameter
decls.doc:
**Splitting the half-disc: the diameter piece.** Subtracting the arc contribution from the
half-residue identity leaves the principal value along the diameter alone.

The arc term is expressed as a `circleMap` integral, which is the form Jordan's lemma bounds. It
vanishes as `R → ∞` for an integrand `e^{iaz} · g z` (`a > 0`) whose sup bound on the semicircle
tends to `0` — oscillation alone is not enough, the amplitude must decay. The concrete case
`f z = e^{iz}/z`, where that bound is `1/R`, is the Hungerbühler–Wasem motivating example.
decls.title: Splitting the half-disc: the diameter piece
decls.statement:
theorem hasCauchyPV_halfDiscBoundary_diameter {f : ℂ → ℂ} (hR : 0 < R)
    (hf : DifferentiableOn ℂ f (univ \ {0})) (hmero : MeromorphicAt f 0)
    (h_simple : ((-1 : ℤ) : WithTop ℤ) ≤ meromorphicOrderAt f 0) :
    HasCauchyPV (halfDiscBoundary R) (-R) R f
      ((Real.pi : ℂ) * Complex.I * residue f 0 -
        ∫ θ in (0 : ℝ)..Real.pi, f (circleMap 0 R θ) * deriv (circleMap 0 R) θ)

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.hasCauchyPV_realSegment_diameter
decls.doc:
**The identity along the real segment.** The diameter of the half-disc traces the straight
line `t ↦ t`, so the principal value can be stated along that curve directly — the form the
real-axis improper integral consumes, with no reference to the auxiliary contour.
decls.title: The identity along the real segment
decls.statement:
theorem hasCauchyPV_realSegment_diameter {f : ℂ → ℂ} (hR : 0 < R)
    (hf : DifferentiableOn ℂ f (univ \ {0})) (hmero : MeromorphicAt f 0)
    (h_simple : ((-1 : ℤ) : WithTop ℤ) ≤ meromorphicOrderAt f 0) :
    HasCauchyPV (fun t : ℝ => (t : ℂ)) (-R) R f
      ((Real.pi : ℂ) * Complex.I * residue f 0 -
        ∫ θ in (0 : ℝ)..Real.pi, f (circleMap 0 R θ) * deriv (circleMap 0 R) θ)

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.twoPrincipalParts
decls.doc:
The rational function with prescribed principal parts `A / (z - s₁)` and
`B / (z - s₂)`.
decls.statement: def twoPrincipalParts (A B s₁ s₂ : ℂ) (z : ℂ) : ℂ

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.twoPrincipalParts_apply
decls.doc: The value of `twoPrincipalParts` at a point.
decls.statement:
theorem twoPrincipalParts_apply (A B s₁ s₂ z : ℂ) :
    twoPrincipalParts A B s₁ s₂ z = A * (z - s₁)⁻¹ + B * (z - s₂)⁻¹

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.twoPrincipalParts_eq
decls.doc: The function-level defining equation for `twoPrincipalParts`.
decls.statement:
theorem twoPrincipalParts_eq (A B s₁ s₂ : ℂ) :
    twoPrincipalParts A B s₁ s₂ = fun z => A * (z - s₁)⁻¹ + B * (z - s₂)⁻¹

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.analyticAt_twoPrincipalParts
decls.doc:
`twoPrincipalParts` is analytic where each nonzero principal part is away from its designated
point, or where coincident principal parts cancel.
decls.statement:
theorem analyticAt_twoPrincipalParts {A B s₁ s₂ z : ℂ}
    (h : ((A = 0 ∨ z ≠ s₁) ∧ (B = 0 ∨ z ≠ s₂)) ∨
      (s₁ = s₂ ∧ A + B = 0)) :
    AnalyticAt ℂ (twoPrincipalParts A B s₁ s₂) z

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.meromorphicAt_twoPrincipalParts
decls.doc: The function `twoPrincipalParts` is meromorphic everywhere.
decls.statement:
theorem meromorphicAt_twoPrincipalParts (A B s₁ s₂ z : ℂ) :
    MeromorphicAt (twoPrincipalParts A B s₁ s₂) z

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.residue_twoPrincipalParts_left
decls.doc:
At the first designated point, the residue of `twoPrincipalParts` is the first coefficient if
the other principal part vanishes or is designated at a distinct point.
decls.statement:
theorem residue_twoPrincipalParts_left {A B s₁ s₂ : ℂ} (h : B = 0 ∨ s₁ ≠ s₂) :
    residue (twoPrincipalParts A B s₁ s₂) s₁ = A

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.residue_twoPrincipalParts_right
decls.doc:
At the second designated point, the residue of `twoPrincipalParts` is the second coefficient if
the other principal part vanishes or is designated at a distinct point.
decls.statement:
theorem residue_twoPrincipalParts_right {A B s₁ s₂ : ℂ} (h : A = 0 ∨ s₁ ≠ s₂) :
    residue (twoPrincipalParts A B s₁ s₂) s₂ = B

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.circleIntegrable_const_mul_sub_inv
decls.doc: A reciprocal simple pole strictly inside a circle is circle integrable.
decls.statement:
theorem circleIntegrable_const_mul_sub_inv {A c s : ℂ} {R : ℝ} (hs : s ∈ ball c R) :
    CircleIntegrable (fun z => A * (z - s)⁻¹) c R

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.circleIntegral_twoPrincipalParts
decls.doc:
**Two-pole circle integral.** If the designated point of each nonzero principal part lies
strictly inside the circle `C(c, R)`, then the integral of `A / (z - s₁) + B / (z - s₂)` around
that circle is `2πi (A + B)`.  Together with
`residue_twoPrincipalParts_left` and `residue_twoPrincipalParts_right`, this is the roadmap's worked
example of the classical residue theorem with two simple poles.
decls.title: Two-pole circle integral
decls.statement:
theorem circleIntegral_twoPrincipalParts {A B c s₁ s₂ : ℂ} {R : ℝ}
    (hs₁ : A = 0 ∨ s₁ ∈ ball c R) (hs₂ : B = 0 ∨ s₂ ∈ ball c R) :
    circleIntegral (twoPrincipalParts A B s₁ s₂) c R =
      2 * (Real.pi : ℂ) * Complex.I * (A + B)

decls.name: TauCeti.Contour.circleIntegral_twoPrincipalParts_eq_residue_sum
decls.doc:
The two-pole calculation in residue-theorem form: for distinct designated points, with the
point of each nonzero principal part inside the circle, the integral is `2πi` times the sum of the
two residues.
decls.statement:
theorem circleIntegral_twoPrincipalParts_eq_residue_sum {A B c s₁ s₂ : ℂ} {R : ℝ}
    (hs : s₁ ≠ s₂) (hs₁ : A = 0 ∨ s₁ ∈ ball c R)
    (hs₂ : B = 0 ∨ s₂ ∈ ball c R) :
    circleIntegral (twoPrincipalParts A B s₁ s₂) c R =
      2 * (Real.pi : ℂ) * Complex.I *
        (residue (twoPrincipalParts A B s₁ s₂) s₁ +
          residue (twoPrincipalParts A B s₁ s₂) s₂)

decls.name: TauCeti.ContinuousLinearMap.orthogonalKerEquivRange
decls.doc:
The restriction of a closed-range operator to the orthogonal complement of its kernel is a
continuous linear equivalence onto its range.
decls.statement:
def orthogonalKerEquivRange (T : E →L[𝕜] F)
    (hT : IsClosed (LinearMap.range (T : E →ₗ[𝕜] F) : Set F)) :
    (LinearMap.ker (T : E →ₗ[𝕜] F))ᗮ ≃L[𝕜]
      LinearMap.range (T : E →ₗ[𝕜] F)

decls.name: TauCeti.ContinuousLinearMap.orthogonalKerEquivRange_apply
decls.doc: The closed-range restriction equivalence acts by the original operator.
decls.statement:
theorem orthogonalKerEquivRange_apply (T : E →L[𝕜] F)
    (hT : IsClosed (LinearMap.range (T : E →ₗ[𝕜] F) : Set F))
    (x : (LinearMap.ker (T : E →ₗ[𝕜] F))ᗮ) :
    (orthogonalKerEquivRange T hT x :
      F) = T x

decls.name: TauCeti.ContinuousLinearMap.orthogonalKerEquivRange_symm_apply
decls.doc:
Applying a closed-range operator to the inverse of its orthogonal-kernel restriction
recovers the given range element.
decls.statement:
theorem orthogonalKerEquivRange_symm_apply (T : E →L[𝕜] F)
    (hT : IsClosed (LinearMap.range (T : E →ₗ[𝕜] F) : Set F))
    (y : LinearMap.range (T : E →ₗ[𝕜] F)) :
    T ((orthogonalKerEquivRange T hT).symm y) = (y : F)

decls.name: TauCeti.ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint_bijective
decls.doc: The adjoint of a continuous linear equivalence is bijective.
decls.statement:
theorem adjoint_bijective (e : E ≃L[𝕜] F) :
    Function.Bijective ((e : E →L[𝕜] F)†)

decls.name: TauCeti.ContinuousLinearMap.range_adjoint_eq_orthogonal_ker_of_isClosed_range
decls.doc:
A continuous linear map with closed range has adjoint range equal to the orthogonal
complement of its kernel.
decls.statement:
theorem range_adjoint_eq_orthogonal_ker_of_isClosed_range (T : E →L[𝕜] F)
    (hT : IsClosed (LinearMap.range (T : E →ₗ[𝕜] F) : Set F)) :
    LinearMap.range (T† : F →ₗ[𝕜] E) =
      (LinearMap.ker (T : E →ₗ[𝕜] F))ᗮ

decls.name: TauCeti.ContinuousLinearMap.isClosed_range_adjoint_of_isClosed_range
decls.doc:
If a continuous linear map between Hilbert spaces has closed range, then so does its
adjoint.
decls.statement:
theorem isClosed_range_adjoint_of_isClosed_range (T : E →L[𝕜] F)
    (hT : IsClosed (LinearMap.range (T : E →ₗ[𝕜] F) : Set F)) :
    IsClosed (LinearMap.range (T† : F →ₗ[𝕜] E) : Set E)

decls.name: TauCeti.ContinuousLinearMap.isClosed_range_adjoint_iff
decls.doc:
A continuous linear map between Hilbert spaces has closed range if and only if its adjoint
does.
decls.statement:
theorem isClosed_range_adjoint_iff (T : E →L[𝕜] F) :
    IsClosed (LinearMap.range (T† : F →ₗ[𝕜] E) : Set E) ↔
      IsClosed (LinearMap.range (T : E →ₗ[𝕜] F) : Set F)

decls.name: TauCeti.ContinuousLinearMap.cokerEquivKerAdjoint
decls.doc:
The cokernel of a closed-range operator is continuously linearly equivalent to the kernel of
its adjoint.
decls.statement:
def cokerEquivKerAdjoint (T : E →L[𝕜] F)
    (hT : IsClosed (LinearMap.range (T : E →ₗ[𝕜] F) : Set F)) :
    (F ⧸ LinearMap.range (T : E →ₗ[𝕜] F)) ≃L[𝕜]
      LinearMap.ker (T† : F →ₗ[𝕜] E)

decls.name: TauCeti.ContinuousLinearMap.coe_cokerEquivKerAdjoint_apply_mk
decls.doc:
On quotient representatives, the cokernel--adjoint-kernel equivalence is orthogonal
projection onto the orthogonal complement of the range.
decls.statement:
theorem coe_cokerEquivKerAdjoint_apply_mk (T : E →L[𝕜] F)
    (hT : IsClosed (LinearMap.range (T : E →ₗ[𝕜] F) : Set F)) (y : F) :
    (cokerEquivKerAdjoint T hT (Submodule.Quotient.mk y) : F) =
      ((LinearMap.range (T : E →ₗ[𝕜] F))ᗮ.orthogonalProjectionOnto y : F)

decls.name: TauCeti.ContinuousLinearMap.cokerEquivKerAdjoint_symm_apply
decls.doc:
The inverse cokernel--adjoint-kernel equivalence sends a kernel vector to its quotient
class.
decls.statement:
theorem cokerEquivKerAdjoint_symm_apply (T : E →L[𝕜] F)
    (hT : IsClosed (LinearMap.range (T : E →ₗ[𝕜] F) : Set F))
    (y : LinearMap.ker (T† : F →ₗ[𝕜] E)) :
    (cokerEquivKerAdjoint T hT).symm y = Submodule.Quotient.mk (y : F)

decls.name: TauCeti.ContinuousLinearMap.cokerAdjointEquivKer
decls.doc:
The cokernel of the adjoint of a closed-range operator is continuously linearly equivalent to
the original kernel.
decls.statement:
def cokerAdjointEquivKer (T : E →L[𝕜] F)
    (hT : IsClosed (LinearMap.range (T : E →ₗ[𝕜] F) : Set F)) :
    (E ⧸ LinearMap.range (T† : F →ₗ[𝕜] E)) ≃L[𝕜]
      LinearMap.ker (T : E →ₗ[𝕜] F)

decls.name: TauCeti.ContinuousLinearMap.coe_cokerAdjointEquivKer_apply_mk
decls.doc:
On quotient representatives, the adjoint-cokernel--kernel equivalence is orthogonal
projection onto the orthogonal complement of the adjoint range.
decls.statement:
theorem coe_cokerAdjointEquivKer_apply_mk (T : E →L[𝕜] F)
    (hT : IsClosed (LinearMap.range (T : E →ₗ[𝕜] F) : Set F)) (x : E) :
    (cokerAdjointEquivKer T hT (Submodule.Quotient.mk x) : E) =
      ((LinearMap.range (T† : F →ₗ[𝕜] E))ᗮ.orthogonalProjectionOnto x : E)

decls.name: TauCeti.ContinuousLinearMap.cokerAdjointEquivKer_symm_apply
decls.doc:
The inverse adjoint-cokernel--kernel equivalence sends a kernel vector to its quotient
class.
decls.statement:
theorem cokerAdjointEquivKer_symm_apply (T : E →L[𝕜] F)
    (hT : IsClosed (LinearMap.range (T : E →ₗ[𝕜] F) : Set F))
    (x : LinearMap.ker (T : E →ₗ[𝕜] F)) :
    (cokerAdjointEquivKer T hT).symm x = Submodule.Quotient.mk (x : E)

decls.name: TauCeti.IsFredholm.adjoint
decls.doc: The adjoint of a Fredholm operator between Hilbert spaces is Fredholm.
decls.statement:
theorem IsFredholm.adjoint {T : E →L[𝕜] F} (hT : IsFredholm T) :
    IsFredholm (T†)

decls.name: TauCeti.isFredholm_adjoint_iff
decls.doc:
A continuous linear map between Hilbert spaces is Fredholm if and only if its adjoint is
Fredholm.
decls.statement:
theorem isFredholm_adjoint_iff (T : E →L[𝕜] F) :
    IsFredholm (T†) ↔ IsFredholm T

decls.name: TauCeti.ContinuousLinearMap.index_adjoint
decls.doc: Taking the adjoint of a Fredholm operator negates its index.
decls.statement:
theorem index_adjoint (T : E →L[𝕜] F) (hT : IsFredholm T) :
    index (T†) = -index T

decls.name: TauCeti.IsFredholm
decls.doc:
A continuous linear map between normed spaces is a **Fredholm operator** if its kernel is
finite dimensional, its range is closed, and its cokernel is finite dimensional.

Closedness of the range is a genuine hypothesis: over an incomplete space a finite-dimensional
cokernel need not force it. It is bundled here following the standard convention (McDuff--Salamon,
Appendix A.1).
decls.statement: structure IsFredholm (T : E →L[𝕜] F) : Prop

decls.name: TauCeti.coe_continuousLinearEquiv
decls.doc:
The underlying linear map of a continuous linear equivalence, written with the
linear-equivalence coercion so that submodule lemmas apply.
decls.statement:
lemma coe_continuousLinearEquiv (e : E ≃L[𝕜] F) :
    ((e : E →L[𝕜] F) : E →ₗ[𝕜] F) = (e.toLinearEquiv : E →ₗ[𝕜] F)

decls.name: TauCeti.IsFredholm.of_continuousLinearEquiv
decls.doc: A continuous linear equivalence is a Fredholm operator.
decls.statement: lemma IsFredholm.of_continuousLinearEquiv (e : E ≃L[𝕜] F) : IsFredholm (e : E →L[𝕜] F)

decls.name: TauCeti.isFredholm_id
decls.doc: The identity operator is Fredholm: its kernel is trivial and its range is everything.
decls.statement: lemma isFredholm_id : IsFredholm (ContinuousLinearMap.id 𝕜 E)

decls.name: TauCeti.isFredholm_of_finiteDimensional
decls.doc: Every continuous linear map between finite-dimensional spaces is Fredholm.
decls.statement: lemma isFredholm_of_finiteDimensional (T : E →L[𝕜] F) : IsFredholm T

decls.name: TauCeti.IsFredholm.smul
decls.doc: A nonzero scalar multiple of a Fredholm operator is Fredholm.
decls.statement:
lemma IsFredholm.smul {T : E →L[𝕜] F} (hT : IsFredholm T) {c : 𝕜} (hc : c ≠ 0) :
    IsFredholm (c • T)

decls.name: TauCeti.IsFredholm.neg
decls.doc: The negation of a Fredholm operator is Fredholm.
decls.statement: lemma IsFredholm.neg {T : E →L[𝕜] F} (hT : IsFredholm T) : IsFredholm (-T)

decls.name: TauCeti.coe_equiv_comp
decls.doc:
The underlying linear map of `e.comp T`, for a continuous linear equivalence `e`, written with
the linear-equivalence coercion so that submodule and quotient lemmas apply.
decls.statement:
lemma coe_equiv_comp (e : F ≃L[𝕜] G) :
    (((e : F →L[𝕜] G).comp T : E →L[𝕜] G) : E →ₗ[𝕜] G) =
      (e.toLinearEquiv : F →ₗ[𝕜] G).comp (T : E →ₗ[𝕜] F)

decls.name: TauCeti.coe_comp_equiv
decls.doc: The underlying linear map of `T.comp e`, for a continuous linear equivalence `e`.
decls.statement:
lemma coe_comp_equiv (e : G ≃L[𝕜] E) :
    ((T.comp (e : G →L[𝕜] E) : G →L[𝕜] F) : G →ₗ[𝕜] F) =
      (T : E →ₗ[𝕜] F).comp (e.toLinearEquiv : G →ₗ[𝕜] E)

decls.name: TauCeti.quotientEquivMap
decls.doc:
A linear equivalence `e : F ≃ₗ G` sends the cokernel by a submodule `p` to the cokernel by
its image `p.map e`, linearly equivalently. Transports the cokernel along a postcomposed
equivalence in both `equiv_comp` and `index_equiv_comp`.
decls.statement:
def quotientEquivMap (e : F ≃ₗ[𝕜] G) (p : Submodule 𝕜 F) :
    (F ⧸ p) ≃ₗ[𝕜] G ⧸ p.map (e : F →ₗ[𝕜] G)

decls.name: TauCeti.ker_comp_equiv
decls.doc:
The kernel of `T.comp e`, for a continuous linear equivalence `e : G ≃L[𝕜] E`, is the image
of `ker T` under `e⁻¹`. Transports the kernel along a precomposed equivalence in both
`comp_equiv` and `index_comp_equiv`.
decls.statement:
lemma ker_comp_equiv (e : G ≃L[𝕜] E) :
    LinearMap.ker ((T.comp (e : G →L[𝕜] E) : G →L[𝕜] F) : G →ₗ[𝕜] F) =
      (LinearMap.ker (T : E →ₗ[𝕜] F)).map (e.toLinearEquiv.symm : E →ₗ[𝕜] G)

decls.name: TauCeti.ker_equiv_comp
decls.doc:
The kernel of `e.comp T`, for a continuous linear equivalence `e : F ≃L[𝕜] G`, is `ker T`
unchanged, `e` being injective. Shared by `equiv_comp` and `index_equiv_comp`.
decls.statement:
lemma ker_equiv_comp (e : F ≃L[𝕜] G) :
    LinearMap.ker (((e : F →L[𝕜] G).comp T : E →L[𝕜] G) : E →ₗ[𝕜] G) =
      LinearMap.ker (T : E →ₗ[𝕜] F)

decls.name: TauCeti.range_comp_equiv
decls.doc:
The range of `T.comp e`, for a continuous linear equivalence `e : G ≃L[𝕜] E`, is `range T`
unchanged, `e` being surjective. Shared by `comp_equiv` and `index_comp_equiv`.
decls.statement:
lemma range_comp_equiv (e : G ≃L[𝕜] E) :
    LinearMap.range ((T.comp (e : G →L[𝕜] E) : G →L[𝕜] F) : G →ₗ[𝕜] F) =
      LinearMap.range (T : E →ₗ[𝕜] F)

decls.name: TauCeti.IsFredholm.equiv_comp
decls.doc:
Postcomposing a Fredholm operator with a continuous linear equivalence yields a Fredholm
operator.
decls.statement:
lemma IsFredholm.equiv_comp (hT : IsFredholm T) (e : F ≃L[𝕜] G) :
    IsFredholm ((e : F →L[𝕜] G).comp T)

decls.name: TauCeti.IsFredholm.comp_equiv
decls.doc:
Precomposing a Fredholm operator with a continuous linear equivalence yields a Fredholm
operator.
decls.statement:
lemma IsFredholm.comp_equiv (hT : IsFredholm T) (e : G ≃L[𝕜] E) :
    IsFredholm (T.comp (e : G →L[𝕜] E))

decls.name: TauCeti.ContinuousLinearMap.index
decls.doc:
The **index** of a continuous linear map, `dim ker T − dim coker T`, defined as the index of
the underlying linear map. For non-Fredholm operators the value is junk, matching the convention of
`LinearMap.index`.
decls.statement: def index (T : E →L[𝕜] F) : ℤ

decls.name: TauCeti.ContinuousLinearMap.index_def
decls.doc:
The Fredholm index unfolds to the algebraic `LinearMap.index` of the underlying linear map.
Internal bridge to the reused Mathlib API; the public characteristic equation is
`index_eq_finrank_sub`.
decls.statement: lemma index_def (T : E →L[𝕜] F) : index T = (T : E →ₗ[𝕜] F).index

decls.name: TauCeti.ContinuousLinearMap.index_eq_finrank_sub
decls.doc: The index is `dim ker T − dim coker T`.
decls.statement:
lemma index_eq_finrank_sub (T : E →L[𝕜] F) :
    index T = (finrank 𝕜 (LinearMap.ker (T : E →ₗ[𝕜] F)) : ℤ) -
      finrank 𝕜 (F ⧸ LinearMap.range (T : E →ₗ[𝕜] F))

decls.name: TauCeti.ContinuousLinearMap.index_id
decls.doc: The identity operator has index `0`.
decls.statement: lemma index_id : index (ContinuousLinearMap.id 𝕜 E) = 0

decls.name: TauCeti.ContinuousLinearMap.index_continuousLinearEquiv_eq_zero
decls.doc: A continuous linear equivalence has index `0`.
decls.statement:
lemma index_continuousLinearEquiv_eq_zero (e : E ≃L[𝕜] F) :
    index (e : E →L[𝕜] F) = 0

decls.name: TauCeti.ContinuousLinearMap.index_eq_of_finiteDimensional
decls.doc: Between finite-dimensional spaces the index is `dim E − dim F`, for any operator.
decls.statement:
lemma index_eq_of_finiteDimensional [FiniteDimensional 𝕜 E] [FiniteDimensional 𝕜 F]
    (T : E →L[𝕜] F) : index T = (finrank 𝕜 E : ℤ) - finrank 𝕜 F

decls.name: TauCeti.ContinuousLinearMap.index_smul
decls.doc: The index is unchanged by a nonzero scalar multiple.
decls.statement: lemma index_smul (T : E →L[𝕜] F) {c : 𝕜} (hc : c ≠ 0) : index (c • T) = index T

decls.name: TauCeti.ContinuousLinearMap.index_neg
decls.doc: The index is unchanged by negation.
decls.statement: lemma index_neg (T : E →L[𝕜] F) : index (-T) = index T

decls.name: TauCeti.ContinuousLinearMap.index_equiv_comp
decls.doc: Postcomposing with a continuous linear equivalence leaves the index unchanged.
decls.statement:
lemma index_equiv_comp (e : F ≃L[𝕜] G) :
    index ((e : F →L[𝕜] G).comp T) = index T

decls.name: TauCeti.ContinuousLinearMap.index_comp_equiv
decls.doc: Precomposing with a continuous linear equivalence leaves the index unchanged.
decls.statement:
lemma index_comp_equiv (e : G ≃L[𝕜] E) :
    index (T.comp (e : G →L[𝕜] E)) = index T

decls.name: TauCeti.ContinuousLinearMap.isClosed_range_of_finiteDimensional_coker
decls.doc:
A continuous linear map between Banach spaces whose cokernel `F ⧸ range T` is finite
dimensional has closed range.

Closedness of the range is therefore not an independent hypothesis in the Banach setting: it is
forced by finite dimensionality of the cokernel. The proof runs the Banach open mapping theorem on
the surjection `Φ(x, n) = T x + n` from `E × N`, where `N` is a finite-dimensional algebraic
complement of `range T`.
decls.statement:
theorem isClosed_range_of_finiteDimensional_coker (T : E →L[𝕜] F)
    [FiniteDimensional 𝕜 (F ⧸ LinearMap.range (T : E →ₗ[𝕜] F))] :
    IsClosed (LinearMap.range (T : E →ₗ[𝕜] F) : Set F)

decls.name: TauCeti.IsFredholm.of_finiteDimensional_ker_coker
decls.doc:
Over Banach spaces, a continuous linear map with finite-dimensional kernel and cokernel is
Fredholm: the closed-range condition is automatic.

This is the Banach-space form of the Fredholm criterion, complementing the direct constructor of
`TauCeti.IsFredholm` by removing the closed-range obligation.
decls.statement:
theorem IsFredholm.of_finiteDimensional_ker_coker (T : E →L[𝕜] F)
    (hker : FiniteDimensional 𝕜 (LinearMap.ker (T : E →ₗ[𝕜] F)))
    (hcoker : FiniteDimensional 𝕜 (F ⧸ LinearMap.range (T : E →ₗ[𝕜] F))) :
    IsFredholm T

decls.name: TauCeti.isFredholm_iff_finiteDimensional_ker_coker
decls.doc:
Over Banach spaces the Fredholm predicate is equivalent to finite dimensionality of the kernel
and cokernel; closedness of the range is not an independent condition.
decls.statement:
theorem isFredholm_iff_finiteDimensional_ker_coker (T : E →L[𝕜] F) :
    IsFredholm T ↔
      FiniteDimensional 𝕜 (LinearMap.ker (T : E →ₗ[𝕜] F)) ∧
        FiniteDimensional 𝕜 (F ⧸ LinearMap.range (T : E →ₗ[𝕜] F))

decls.name: TauCeti.IsFredholm.comp
decls.doc:
The composite of two Fredholm operators is Fredholm.

Only the source and target of the composite need to be complete: completeness of the intermediate
space is not used.
decls.statement:
theorem IsFredholm.comp (hS : IsFredholm S) (hT : IsFredholm T) :
    IsFredholm (S.comp T)

decls.name: TauCeti.ContinuousLinearMap.index_comp
decls.doc: The Fredholm index is additive under composition.
decls.statement:
theorem index_comp (S : F →L[𝕜] G) (T : E →L[𝕜] F)
    (hS : IsFredholm S) (hT : IsFredholm T) :
    index (S.comp T) = index S + index T

decls.name: TauCeti.IsFredholm.pow
decls.doc: Every natural-number power of a Fredholm endomorphism is Fredholm.
decls.statement: theorem IsFredholm.pow (hA : IsFredholm A) : ∀ n : ℕ, IsFredholm (A ^ n)

decls.name: TauCeti.ContinuousLinearMap.index_pow
decls.doc: The index of the `n`th power of a Fredholm endomorphism is `n` times its index.
decls.statement:
theorem index_pow (A : X →L[𝕜] X) (hA : IsFredholm A) (n : ℕ) :
    index (A ^ n) = (n : ℤ) * index A

decls.name: TauCeti.IsFredholm.of_surjective
decls.doc: A surjective continuous linear map with finite-dimensional kernel is Fredholm.
decls.statement:
lemma IsFredholm.of_surjective (hT : Function.Surjective T)
    [FiniteDimensional K (LinearMap.ker (T : E →ₗ[K] F))] : IsFredholm T

decls.name: TauCeti.isFredholm_iff_finiteDimensional_ker_of_surjective
decls.doc:
For a surjective continuous linear map, Fredholmness is equivalent to finite-dimensionality of
the kernel.
decls.statement:
lemma isFredholm_iff_finiteDimensional_ker_of_surjective (hT : Function.Surjective T) :
    IsFredholm T ↔ FiniteDimensional K (LinearMap.ker (T : E →ₗ[K] F))

decls.name: TauCeti.IsFredholm.of_injective
decls.doc:
An injective continuous linear map with closed range and finite-dimensional cokernel is
Fredholm.
decls.statement:
lemma IsFredholm.of_injective (hT : Function.Injective T)
    (hclosed : IsClosed (LinearMap.range (T : E →ₗ[K] F) : Set F))
    [FiniteDimensional K (F ⧸ LinearMap.range (T : E →ₗ[K] F))] : IsFredholm T

decls.name: TauCeti.isFredholm_iff_finiteDimensional_coker_of_injective
decls.doc:
For an injective continuous linear map with closed range, Fredholmness is equivalent to
finite-dimensionality of the cokernel.
decls.statement:
lemma isFredholm_iff_finiteDimensional_coker_of_injective (hT : Function.Injective T)
    (hclosed : IsClosed (LinearMap.range (T : E →ₗ[K] F) : Set F)) :
    IsFredholm T ↔ FiniteDimensional K (F ⧸ LinearMap.range (T : E →ₗ[K] F))

decls.name: TauCeti.isFredholm_ker_subtypeL
decls.doc:
The inclusion of the kernel of an operator of finite rank is Fredholm: the kernel is closed
and, by the first isomorphism theorem, of finite codimension.
decls.statement:
lemma isFredholm_ker_subtypeL (hT : FiniteDimensional K (LinearMap.range (T : E →ₗ[K] F))) :
    IsFredholm (LinearMap.ker (T : E →ₗ[K] F)).subtypeL

decls.name: TauCeti.ContinuousLinearMap.index_of_surjective
decls.doc: A surjective continuous linear map has index the dimension of its kernel.
decls.statement:
lemma index_of_surjective (T : E →L[K] F) (hT : Function.Surjective T) :
    index T = (finrank K (LinearMap.ker (T : E →ₗ[K] F)) : ℤ)

decls.name: TauCeti.ContinuousLinearMap.index_of_injective
decls.doc: An injective continuous linear map has index the negative of the dimension of its cokernel.
decls.statement:
lemma index_of_injective (T : E →L[K] F) (hT : Function.Injective T) :
    index T = -(finrank K (F ⧸ LinearMap.range (T : E →ₗ[K] F)) : ℤ)

decls.name: TauCeti.ContinuousLinearMap.index_eq_zero_of_bijective
decls.doc:
A bijective continuous linear map has Fredholm index zero. This formulation applies directly
when bijectivity is known before a continuous inverse has been bundled.
decls.statement: lemma index_eq_zero_of_bijective (T : E →L[K] F) (hT : Function.Bijective T) : index T = 0

decls.name: TauCeti.IsFredholm.of_bijective
decls.doc:
A bijective continuous linear map is Fredholm. This formulation does not require bundling its
inverse as a continuous linear equivalence.
decls.statement: lemma IsFredholm.of_bijective (hT : Function.Bijective T) : IsFredholm T

decls.name: TauCeti.finiteDimensional_ker_of_comp_eq_id_sub
decls.doc:
A left inverse modulo a finite-rank error forces a finite-dimensional kernel: on `ker T` the
identity agrees with the error term, so `ker T` sits inside its range.
decls.statement:
theorem finiteDimensional_ker_of_comp_eq_id_sub {P : E →L[𝕜] E}
    (hP : FiniteDimensional 𝕜 (LinearMap.range (P : E →ₗ[𝕜] E)))
    (h : S.comp T = ContinuousLinearMap.id 𝕜 E - P) :
    FiniteDimensional 𝕜 (LinearMap.ker (T : E →ₗ[𝕜] F))

decls.name: TauCeti.finiteDimensional_coker_of_comp_eq_id_sub
decls.doc:
A right inverse modulo a finite-rank error forces a finite-dimensional cokernel: every vector
differs from its error term by an element of `range T`, so the finite-dimensional `range Q`
already surjects onto `F ⧸ range T`.
decls.statement:
theorem finiteDimensional_coker_of_comp_eq_id_sub {Q : F →L[𝕜] F}
    (hQ : FiniteDimensional 𝕜 (LinearMap.range (Q : F →ₗ[𝕜] F)))
    (h : T.comp S = ContinuousLinearMap.id 𝕜 F - Q) :
    FiniteDimensional 𝕜 (F ⧸ LinearMap.range (T : E →ₗ[𝕜] F))

decls.name: TauCeti.IsFredholm.of_parametrix
decls.doc:
**Atkinson's criterion.** An operator between Banach spaces that has a left inverse modulo a
finite-rank error and a right inverse modulo a finite-rank error is Fredholm. The two one-sided
inverses need not agree.
decls.title: Atkinson's criterion
decls.statement:
theorem IsFredholm.of_parametrix {S₁ S₂ : F →L[𝕜] E} {P : E →L[𝕜] E} {Q : F →L[𝕜] F}
    (hP : FiniteDimensional 𝕜 (LinearMap.range (P : E →ₗ[𝕜] E)))
    (hQ : FiniteDimensional 𝕜 (LinearMap.range (Q : F →ₗ[𝕜] F)))
    (h₁ : S₁.comp T = ContinuousLinearMap.id 𝕜 E - P)
    (h₂ : T.comp S₂ = ContinuousLinearMap.id 𝕜 F - Q) :
    IsFredholm T

decls.name: TauCeti.IsFredholm.kerProjection
decls.doc:
The projection of the domain onto `ker T` along the chosen kernel complement
`TauCeti.IsFredholm.kerComplement`. It is the finite-rank error term of
`TauCeti.IsFredholm.parametrix_comp_self`, named because the unfolded projection is unreadable at
the point of use.
decls.statement: def kerProjection (hT : _root_.TauCeti.IsFredholm T) : E →L[𝕜] E

decls.name: TauCeti.IsFredholm.cokerProjection
decls.doc:
The projection of the codomain onto the chosen cokernel representative
`TauCeti.IsFredholm.cokerComplement` along `range T`. It is the finite-rank error term of
`TauCeti.IsFredholm.self_comp_parametrix`.
decls.statement: def cokerProjection (hT : _root_.TauCeti.IsFredholm T) : F →L[𝕜] F

decls.name: TauCeti.IsFredholm.ker_kerProjection
decls.doc:
The kernel of the first error term is the chosen kernel complement: it is the subspace
`TauCeti.IsFredholm.kerProjection` projects along.
decls.statement:
theorem ker_kerProjection (hT : _root_.TauCeti.IsFredholm T) :
    LinearMap.ker (hT.kerProjection : E →ₗ[𝕜] E) = hT.kerComplement

decls.name: TauCeti.IsFredholm.ker_cokerProjection
decls.doc:
The kernel of the second error term is `range T`: it is the subspace
`TauCeti.IsFredholm.cokerProjection` projects along.
decls.statement:
theorem ker_cokerProjection (hT : _root_.TauCeti.IsFredholm T) :
    LinearMap.ker (hT.cokerProjection : F →ₗ[𝕜] F) = LinearMap.range (T : E →ₗ[𝕜] F)

decls.name: TauCeti.IsFredholm.kerProjection_apply_of_mem_ker
decls.doc: The first error term is the identity on `ker T`.
decls.statement:
theorem kerProjection_apply_of_mem_ker (hT : _root_.TauCeti.IsFredholm T) {x : E}
    (hx : x ∈ LinearMap.ker (T : E →ₗ[𝕜] F)) : hT.kerProjection x = x

decls.name: TauCeti.IsFredholm.kerProjection_apply_eq_zero_of_mem_kerComplement
decls.doc: The first error term vanishes on the chosen kernel complement.
decls.statement:
theorem kerProjection_apply_eq_zero_of_mem_kerComplement (hT : _root_.TauCeti.IsFredholm T)
    {x : E} (hx : x ∈ hT.kerComplement) : hT.kerProjection x = 0

decls.name: TauCeti.IsFredholm.kerProjection_apply_mem_ker
decls.doc: The first error term takes values in `ker T`.
decls.statement:
theorem kerProjection_apply_mem_ker (hT : _root_.TauCeti.IsFredholm T) (x : E) :
    hT.kerProjection x ∈ LinearMap.ker (T : E →ₗ[𝕜] F)

decls.name: TauCeti.IsFredholm.apply_kerProjection
decls.doc: `T` annihilates the first error term, which projects onto `ker T`.
decls.statement:
theorem apply_kerProjection (hT : _root_.TauCeti.IsFredholm T) (x : E) :
    T (hT.kerProjection x) = 0

decls.name: TauCeti.IsFredholm.cokerProjection_apply_of_mem_cokerComplement
decls.doc: The second error term is the identity on the chosen cokernel representative.
decls.statement:
theorem cokerProjection_apply_of_mem_cokerComplement (hT : _root_.TauCeti.IsFredholm T) {y : F}
    (hy : y ∈ hT.cokerComplement) : hT.cokerProjection y = y

decls.name: TauCeti.IsFredholm.cokerProjection_apply_eq_zero_of_mem_range
decls.doc: The second error term vanishes on `range T`.
decls.statement:
theorem cokerProjection_apply_eq_zero_of_mem_range (hT : _root_.TauCeti.IsFredholm T) {y : F}
    (hy : y ∈ LinearMap.range (T : E →ₗ[𝕜] F)) : hT.cokerProjection y = 0

decls.name: TauCeti.IsFredholm.cokerProjection_apply_apply
decls.doc: The second error term annihilates every value of `T`.
decls.statement:
theorem cokerProjection_apply_apply (hT : _root_.TauCeti.IsFredholm T) (x : E) :
    hT.cokerProjection (T x) = 0

decls.name: TauCeti.IsFredholm.isIdempotentElem_kerProjection
decls.doc: The first error term is idempotent: it is a projection.
