decls.statement:
theorem isIdempotentElem_kerProjection (hT : _root_.TauCeti.IsFredholm T) :
    IsIdempotentElem hT.kerProjection

decls.name: TauCeti.IsFredholm.isIdempotentElem_cokerProjection
decls.doc: The second error term is idempotent: it is a projection.
decls.statement:
theorem isIdempotentElem_cokerProjection (hT : _root_.TauCeti.IsFredholm T) :
    IsIdempotentElem hT.cokerProjection

decls.name: TauCeti.IsFredholm.parametrix
decls.doc:
A **parametrix** for a Fredholm operator: project the codomain onto `range T`, invert `T`
there against the chosen kernel complement, and include the result back into the domain.
decls.statement: def parametrix (hT : _root_.TauCeti.IsFredholm T) : F →L[𝕜] E

decls.name: TauCeti.IsFredholm.parametrix_apply
decls.doc:
The parametrix, unfolded: invert `T` on the `range T` component of the argument. Internal
bridge to the definition; the public API is the pair of parametrix identities.
decls.statement:
theorem parametrix_apply (hT : _root_.TauCeti.IsFredholm T) (y : F) :
    hT.parametrix y =
      (hT.kerComplementEquivRange.symm
        ((LinearMap.range (T : E →ₗ[𝕜] F)).projectionOntoL hT.cokerComplement
          hT.isTopCompl_range_cokerComplement y) : E)

decls.name: TauCeti.IsFredholm.apply_parametrix
decls.doc:
Applying `T` to a parametrix recovers the argument up to its cokernel component: the
pointwise form of `TauCeti.IsFredholm.self_comp_parametrix`.
decls.statement:
theorem apply_parametrix (hT : _root_.TauCeti.IsFredholm T) (y : F) :
    T (hT.parametrix y) = y - hT.cokerProjection y

decls.name: TauCeti.IsFredholm.parametrix_apply_apply
decls.doc:
A parametrix recovers the argument of `T` up to its kernel component: the pointwise form of
`TauCeti.IsFredholm.parametrix_comp_self`.
decls.statement:
theorem parametrix_apply_apply (hT : _root_.TauCeti.IsFredholm T) (x : E) :
    hT.parametrix (T x) = x - hT.kerProjection x

decls.name: TauCeti.IsFredholm.parametrix_comp_self
decls.doc: The first parametrix identity: `S ∘ T` is the identity minus the projection onto `ker T`.
decls.statement:
theorem parametrix_comp_self (hT : _root_.TauCeti.IsFredholm T) :
    hT.parametrix.comp T = ContinuousLinearMap.id 𝕜 E - hT.kerProjection

decls.name: TauCeti.IsFredholm.self_comp_parametrix
decls.doc:
The second parametrix identity: `T ∘ S` is the identity minus the projection onto the chosen
cokernel representative.
decls.statement:
theorem self_comp_parametrix (hT : _root_.TauCeti.IsFredholm T) :
    T.comp hT.parametrix = ContinuousLinearMap.id 𝕜 F - hT.cokerProjection

decls.name: TauCeti.IsFredholm.range_kerProjection
decls.doc: The error term of the first parametrix identity has range `ker T`.
decls.statement:
theorem range_kerProjection (hT : _root_.TauCeti.IsFredholm T) :
    LinearMap.range (hT.kerProjection : E →ₗ[𝕜] E) = LinearMap.ker (T : E →ₗ[𝕜] F)

decls.name: TauCeti.IsFredholm.range_cokerProjection
decls.doc:
The error term of the second parametrix identity has range the chosen cokernel
representative.
decls.statement:
theorem range_cokerProjection (hT : _root_.TauCeti.IsFredholm T) :
    LinearMap.range (hT.cokerProjection : F →ₗ[𝕜] F) = hT.cokerComplement

decls.name: TauCeti.IsFredholm.finiteDimensional_range_kerProjection
decls.doc: The error term of the first parametrix identity has finite rank.
decls.statement:
theorem finiteDimensional_range_kerProjection (hT : _root_.TauCeti.IsFredholm T) :
    FiniteDimensional 𝕜 (LinearMap.range (hT.kerProjection : E →ₗ[𝕜] E))

decls.name: TauCeti.IsFredholm.finiteDimensional_range_cokerProjection
decls.doc: The error term of the second parametrix identity has finite rank.
decls.statement:
theorem finiteDimensional_range_cokerProjection (hT : _root_.TauCeti.IsFredholm T) :
    FiniteDimensional 𝕜 (LinearMap.range (hT.cokerProjection : F →ₗ[𝕜] F))

decls.name: TauCeti.IsFredholm.exists_parametrix
decls.doc:
A Fredholm operator is invertible modulo finite-rank operators: the existential form of the
two parametrix identities, and the direction of Atkinson's theorem that consumes the
kernel/cokernel splittings.
decls.statement:
theorem exists_parametrix (hT : _root_.TauCeti.IsFredholm T) :
    ∃ (S : F →L[𝕜] E) (P : E →L[𝕜] E) (Q : F →L[𝕜] F),
      FiniteDimensional 𝕜 (LinearMap.range (P : E →ₗ[𝕜] E)) ∧
        FiniteDimensional 𝕜 (LinearMap.range (Q : F →ₗ[𝕜] F)) ∧
          S.comp T = ContinuousLinearMap.id 𝕜 E - P ∧
            T.comp S = ContinuousLinearMap.id 𝕜 F - Q

decls.name: TauCeti.isFredholm_iff_exists_parametrix
decls.doc:
**Atkinson's theorem.** Between Banach spaces, a continuous linear map is Fredholm exactly
when it is invertible modulo finite-rank operators.
decls.title: Atkinson's theorem
decls.statement:
theorem isFredholm_iff_exists_parametrix (T : E →L[𝕜] F) :
    IsFredholm T ↔
      ∃ (S : F →L[𝕜] E) (P : E →L[𝕜] E) (Q : F →L[𝕜] F),
        FiniteDimensional 𝕜 (LinearMap.range (P : E →ₗ[𝕜] E)) ∧
          FiniteDimensional 𝕜 (LinearMap.range (Q : F →ₗ[𝕜] F)) ∧
            S.comp T = ContinuousLinearMap.id 𝕜 E - P ∧
              T.comp S = ContinuousLinearMap.id 𝕜 F - Q

decls.name: TauCeti.IsFredholm.ker_parametrix
decls.doc:
The kernel of the parametrix is the chosen cokernel representative: the parametrix kills
exactly the part of the codomain that `T` misses.
decls.statement:
theorem ker_parametrix (hT : _root_.TauCeti.IsFredholm T) :
    LinearMap.ker (hT.parametrix : F →ₗ[𝕜] E) = hT.cokerComplement

decls.name: TauCeti.IsFredholm.range_parametrix
decls.doc:
The range of the parametrix is the chosen kernel complement: the parametrix is a genuine
inverse between `range T` and that complement.
decls.statement:
theorem range_parametrix (hT : _root_.TauCeti.IsFredholm T) :
    LinearMap.range (hT.parametrix : F →ₗ[𝕜] E) = hT.kerComplement

decls.name: TauCeti.IsFredholm.self_comp_parametrix_comp_self
decls.doc:
A parametrix is a generalized inverse of `T`: the two error terms cancel in
`T ∘ S ∘ T`, which is `T` again.
decls.statement:
theorem self_comp_parametrix_comp_self (hT : _root_.TauCeti.IsFredholm T) :
    T.comp (hT.parametrix.comp T) = T

decls.name: TauCeti.IsFredholm.parametrix_comp_self_comp_parametrix
decls.doc:
A parametrix is a generalized inverse of `T`: the two error terms cancel in
`S ∘ T ∘ S`, which is `S` again.
decls.statement:
theorem parametrix_comp_self_comp_parametrix (hT : _root_.TauCeti.IsFredholm T) :
    hT.parametrix.comp (T.comp hT.parametrix) = hT.parametrix

decls.name: TauCeti.IsFredholm.isFredholm_parametrix
decls.doc:
The parametrix of a Fredholm operator is itself Fredholm: its kernel is the
finite-dimensional cokernel representative and its range is the closed kernel complement, whose
quotient is the finite-dimensional `ker T`.
decls.statement:
theorem isFredholm_parametrix (hT : _root_.TauCeti.IsFredholm T) :
    _root_.TauCeti.IsFredholm hT.parametrix

decls.name: TauCeti.ContinuousLinearMap.index_parametrix
decls.doc:
The parametrix of a Fredholm operator has the opposite index: it exchanges the roles of the
kernel and the cokernel.
decls.statement: theorem index_parametrix (hT : IsFredholm T) : index hT.parametrix = -index T

decls.name: TauCeti.IsFredholm.add_of_finiteDimensional_range
decls.doc:
Perturbing a Fredholm operator by an operator of finite rank leaves it Fredholm: a parametrix
`S` for `T` remains one for `T + K` once `S ∘ K` and `K ∘ S`, both of finite rank, are absorbed
into the two error terms.
decls.statement:
theorem IsFredholm.add_of_finiteDimensional_range (hT : IsFredholm T)
    (hK : FiniteDimensional 𝕜 (LinearMap.range (K : E →ₗ[𝕜] F))) :
    IsFredholm (T + K)

decls.name: TauCeti.ContinuousLinearMap.index_add_of_finiteDimensional_range
decls.doc:
Perturbing a Fredholm operator by an operator of finite rank leaves its index unchanged: both
operators restrict to the same map on the closed, finite-codimensional subspace `ker K`, and
additivity of the index cancels the index shift of that restriction.
decls.statement:
theorem index_add_of_finiteDimensional_range (hT : IsFredholm T)
    (hK : FiniteDimensional 𝕜 (LinearMap.range (K : E →ₗ[𝕜] F))) :
    index (T + K) = index T

decls.name: TauCeti.Submodule.prodSubtypeEquiv
decls.doc: A product submodule, as a module, is the product of the two submodules.
decls.statement:
def prodSubtypeEquiv (p : Submodule K F₁) (q : Submodule K F₂) :
    ↥(p.prod q) ≃ₗ[K] p × q

decls.name: TauCeti.Submodule.quotientProdEquiv
decls.doc:
The quotient by a product of submodules is linearly equivalent to the product of the
quotients. This is kept private because the construction is general Mathlib infrastructure; only
its Fredholm consequences form the public API of this file.
decls.statement:
def quotientProdEquiv (p : Submodule K F₁) (q : Submodule K F₂) :
    ((F₁ × F₂) ⧸ p.prod q) ≃ₗ[K] (F₁ ⧸ p) × (F₂ ⧸ q)

decls.name: TauCeti.Submodule.finrank_quotient_prod
decls.doc:
The cokernel of a product submodule has dimension equal to the sum of the dimensions of the
two cokernels.
decls.statement:
lemma finrank_quotient_prod (p : Submodule K F₁) (q : Submodule K F₂)
    [FiniteDimensional K (F₁ ⧸ p)] [FiniteDimensional K (F₂ ⧸ q)] :
    finrank K ((F₁ × F₂) ⧸ p.prod q) = finrank K (F₁ ⧸ p) + finrank K (F₂ ⧸ q)

decls.name: TauCeti.IsFredholm.prodMap
decls.doc: The Cartesian product of two Fredholm operators is Fredholm.
decls.statement:
lemma IsFredholm.prodMap (hT : IsFredholm T) (hS : IsFredholm S) :
    IsFredholm (T.prodMap S)

decls.name: TauCeti.ContinuousLinearMap.index_prodMap_of_finiteDimensional
decls.doc:
The index is additive under Cartesian products when both kernels and cokernels are finite
dimensional.
decls.statement:
lemma index_prodMap_of_finiteDimensional (T : E₁ →L[K] F₁) (S : E₂ →L[K] F₂)
    [FiniteDimensional K (LinearMap.ker (T : E₁ →ₗ[K] F₁))]
    [FiniteDimensional K (LinearMap.ker (S : E₂ →ₗ[K] F₂))]
    [FiniteDimensional K (F₁ ⧸ LinearMap.range (T : E₁ →ₗ[K] F₁))]
    [FiniteDimensional K (F₂ ⧸ LinearMap.range (S : E₂ →ₗ[K] F₂))] :
    index (T.prodMap S) = index T + index S

decls.name: TauCeti.ContinuousLinearMap.index_prodMap
decls.doc: The Fredholm index is additive under Cartesian products of Fredholm operators.
decls.statement:
lemma index_prodMap (T : E₁ →L[K] F₁) (S : E₂ →L[K] F₂)
    (hT : IsFredholm T) (hS : IsFredholm S) :
    index (T.prodMap S) = index T + index S

decls.name: TauCeti.IsFredholm.cokerEquivKerOfKerAdjointEq
decls.doc:
The cokernel of a Fredholm operator is linearly equivalent to its kernel if the operator and
its adjoint have the same kernel.
decls.statement:
def IsFredholm.cokerEquivKerOfKerAdjointEq {T : E →L[𝕜] E}
    (hT : IsFredholm T)
    (hker : (ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint T).ker = T.ker) :
    (E ⧸ LinearMap.range (T : E →ₗ[𝕜] E)) ≃ₗ[𝕜]
      LinearMap.ker (T : E →ₗ[𝕜] E)

decls.name: TauCeti.IsFredholm.cokerEquivKer
decls.doc: The cokernel of a self-adjoint Fredholm operator is linearly equivalent to its kernel.
decls.statement:
def IsFredholm.cokerEquivKer {T : E →L[𝕜] E} (hT : IsFredholm T)
    (hself : IsSelfAdjoint T) :
    (E ⧸ LinearMap.range (T : E →ₗ[𝕜] E)) ≃ₗ[𝕜]
      LinearMap.ker (T : E →ₗ[𝕜] E)

decls.name: TauCeti.ContinuousLinearMap.index_eq_zero_of_ker_adjoint_eq
decls.doc: A Fredholm operator has index zero if it and its adjoint have the same kernel.
decls.statement:
theorem index_eq_zero_of_ker_adjoint_eq {T : E →L[𝕜] E} (hT : IsFredholm T)
    (hker : (ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint T).ker = T.ker) :
    index T = 0

decls.name: TauCeti.ContinuousLinearMap.index_eq_zero_of_isSelfAdjoint
decls.doc: A self-adjoint Fredholm operator on a Hilbert space has Fredholm index zero.
decls.statement:
theorem index_eq_zero_of_isSelfAdjoint {T : E →L[𝕜] E} (hT : IsFredholm T)
    (hself : IsSelfAdjoint T) : index T = 0

decls.name: TauCeti.ContinuousLinearMap.index_eq_zero_of_isSymmetric
decls.doc: A symmetric Fredholm operator on a Hilbert space has Fredholm index zero.
decls.statement:
theorem index_eq_zero_of_isSymmetric {T : E →L[𝕜] E} (hT : IsFredholm T)
    (hsymm : T.IsSymmetric) : index T = 0

decls.name: TauCeti.blockCorner
decls.statement:
def blockCorner
    {K X Y C : Type*}
    [NormedAddCommGroup K] [NormedSpace 𝕜 K]
    [NormedAddCommGroup X] [NormedSpace 𝕜 X]
    [NormedAddCommGroup Y] [NormedSpace 𝕜 Y]
    [NormedAddCommGroup C] [NormedSpace 𝕜 C]
    (A : K × X →L[𝕜] Y × C) : X →L[𝕜] Y

decls.name: TauCeti.exists_factorization_of_blocks
decls.doc:
Block elimination. Write the operator as the block matrix `!![a, e; c, d]`, acting by
`(k, x) ↦ (a k + e x, c k + d x)`, and suppose the corner `e : X → Y` is invertible. Shearing the
domain by `x ↦ x - e⁻¹ a k` kills `a`, and then shearing the codomain by `z ↦ z - d e⁻¹ y` kills
`d`. What survives is the anti-diagonal `!![0, e; c - d e⁻¹ a, 0]` — the direct sum of `e` with
the Schur complement `c - d e⁻¹ a`, with the two target factors interchanged, which is where the
swap in the statement comes from.

Only the factorization is recorded, not the Schur complement itself: all the index computation
needs is that the remaining factor is *some* operator `K → C`, since between finite-dimensional
spaces every operator has index `finrank K - finrank C`.
decls.statement:
theorem exists_factorization_of_blocks
    {K X Y C : Type*}
    [NormedAddCommGroup K] [NormedSpace 𝕜 K]
    [NormedAddCommGroup X] [NormedSpace 𝕜 X]
    [NormedAddCommGroup Y] [NormedSpace 𝕜 Y]
    [NormedAddCommGroup C] [NormedSpace 𝕜 C]
    (A : K × X →L[𝕜] Y × C) (a : K →L[𝕜] Y) (c : K →L[𝕜] C) (d : X →L[𝕜] C) (e : X ≃L[𝕜] Y)
    (hA : ∀ (k : K) (x : X), A (k, x) = (a k + e x, c k + d x)) :
    ∃ (f : K →L[𝕜] C) (P : (K × X) ≃L[𝕜] (K × X)) (Q : (C × Y) ≃L[𝕜] (Y × C)),
      A = (Q : C × Y →L[𝕜] Y × C).comp
        ((f.prodMap (e : X →L[𝕜] Y)).comp (P : K × X →L[𝕜] K × X))

decls.name: TauCeti.isFredholm_and_index_eq_of_blocks
decls.statement:
theorem isFredholm_and_index_eq_of_blocks
    {K X Y C : Type*}
    [NormedAddCommGroup K] [NormedSpace 𝕜 K] [FiniteDimensional 𝕜 K]
    [NormedAddCommGroup X] [NormedSpace 𝕜 X]
    [NormedAddCommGroup Y] [NormedSpace 𝕜 Y]
    [NormedAddCommGroup C] [NormedSpace 𝕜 C] [FiniteDimensional 𝕜 C]
    (A : K × X →L[𝕜] Y × C) (a : K →L[𝕜] Y) (c : K →L[𝕜] C) (d : X →L[𝕜] C) (e : X ≃L[𝕜] Y)
    (hA : ∀ (k : K) (x : X), A (k, x) = (a k + e x, c k + d x)) :
    IsFredholm A ∧
      ContinuousLinearMap.index A = (finrank 𝕜 K : ℤ) - finrank 𝕜 C

decls.name: TauCeti.isFredholm_and_index_eq_of_blockCorner_equiv
decls.statement:
theorem isFredholm_and_index_eq_of_blockCorner_equiv
    {K X Y C : Type*}
    [NormedAddCommGroup K] [NormedSpace 𝕜 K] [FiniteDimensional 𝕜 K]
    [NormedAddCommGroup X] [NormedSpace 𝕜 X]
    [NormedAddCommGroup Y] [NormedSpace 𝕜 Y]
    [NormedAddCommGroup C] [NormedSpace 𝕜 C] [FiniteDimensional 𝕜 C]
    (A : K × X →L[𝕜] Y × C) (e : X ≃L[𝕜] Y)
    (he : blockCorner A = (e : X →L[𝕜] Y)) :
    IsFredholm A ∧
      ContinuousLinearMap.index A = (finrank 𝕜 K : ℤ) - finrank 𝕜 C

decls.name: TauCeti.eventually_exists_continuousLinearEquiv_eq
decls.doc:
**Invertibility is an open condition along a family continuous at a point.** If `D T` is an
equivalence and `D` is continuous at `T`, then `D S` is an equivalence for every `S` near `T`.

This is the sole topological input to the stability theorem; nothing in it is specific to block
forms.
decls.title: Invertibility is an open condition along a family continuous at a point
decls.statement:
theorem eventually_exists_continuousLinearEquiv_eq {G : Type*} [TopologicalSpace G]
    {X Y : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup X] [NormedSpace 𝕜 X] [CompleteSpace X]
    [SeminormedAddCommGroup Y] [NormedSpace 𝕜 Y]
    {D : G → (X →L[𝕜] Y)} {T : G} (hD : ContinuousAt D T) {e₀ : X ≃L[𝕜] Y}
    (hT : D T = (e₀ : X →L[𝕜] Y)) :
    ∀ᶠ S in 𝓝 T, ∃ e : X ≃L[𝕜] Y, D S = (e : X →L[𝕜] Y)

decls.name: TauCeti.isFredholm_and_index_eq_of_splitting
decls.doc:
**A splitting with an invertible corner makes an operator Fredholm.** Suppose the domain splits
as `K × X` and the codomain as `Y × C`, with `K` and `C` finite-dimensional, and that in the
resulting block form of `S` the corner `X → Y` is an equivalence. Then `S` is Fredholm of index
`finrank K - finrank C`.
decls.title: A splitting with an invertible corner makes an operator Fredholm
decls.statement:
theorem isFredholm_and_index_eq_of_splitting
    {K X Y C : Type*}
    [NormedAddCommGroup K] [NormedSpace 𝕜 K] [FiniteDimensional 𝕜 K]
    [NormedAddCommGroup X] [NormedSpace 𝕜 X]
    [NormedAddCommGroup Y] [NormedSpace 𝕜 Y]
    [NormedAddCommGroup C] [NormedSpace 𝕜 C] [FiniteDimensional 𝕜 C]
    (S : E →L[𝕜] F) (p : (K × X) ≃L[𝕜] E) (q : (Y × C) ≃L[𝕜] F) {e : X ≃L[𝕜] Y}
    (he : blockCorner ((q.symm : F →L[𝕜] Y × C).comp (S.comp (p : K × X →L[𝕜] E))) =
      (e : X →L[𝕜] Y)) :
    IsFredholm S ∧
      ContinuousLinearMap.index S = (finrank 𝕜 K : ℤ) - finrank 𝕜 C

decls.name: TauCeti.IsFredholm.eventually_isFredholm_and_index_eq
decls.doc: Fredholmness and the Fredholm index are stable in a neighbourhood of a Fredholm operator.
decls.statement:
theorem IsFredholm.eventually_isFredholm_and_index_eq {T : E →L[𝕜] F}
    (hT : IsFredholm T) :
    ∀ᶠ S : E →L[𝕜] F in 𝓝 T,
      IsFredholm S ∧ ContinuousLinearMap.index S = ContinuousLinearMap.index T

decls.name: TauCeti.IsFredholm.exists_pos_isFredholm_and_index_eq_of_norm_sub_lt
decls.doc:
A sufficiently small operator-norm perturbation of a Fredholm operator is Fredholm with the
same index.
decls.statement:
theorem IsFredholm.exists_pos_isFredholm_and_index_eq_of_norm_sub_lt
    {T : E →L[𝕜] F} (hT : IsFredholm T) :
    ∃ ε > 0, ∀ S : E →L[𝕜] F, ‖S - T‖ < ε →
      IsFredholm S ∧ ContinuousLinearMap.index S = ContinuousLinearMap.index T

decls.name: TauCeti.isOpen_setOf_isFredholm
decls.doc:
The set of Fredholm operators between two Banach spaces is open in the operator norm
topology.
decls.statement:
theorem isOpen_setOf_isFredholm :
    IsOpen {T : E →L[𝕜] F | IsFredholm T}

decls.name: TauCeti.isOpen_setOf_isFredholm_index_eq
decls.doc:
For every integer `n`, the set of Fredholm operators of index `n` is open in the operator
norm topology.

decls.name: TauCeti.IsFredholm.closedComplemented_ker
decls.doc: The kernel of a Fredholm operator is topologically complemented.
decls.statement:
theorem closedComplemented_ker (hT : _root_.TauCeti.IsFredholm T) :
    (LinearMap.ker (T : E →ₗ[𝕜] F)).ClosedComplemented

decls.name: TauCeti.IsFredholm.closedComplemented_range
decls.doc: The range of a Fredholm operator is topologically complemented.
decls.statement:
theorem closedComplemented_range (hT : _root_.TauCeti.IsFredholm T) :
    (LinearMap.range (T : E →ₗ[𝕜] F)).ClosedComplemented

decls.name: TauCeti.IsFredholm.kerComplement
decls.doc: A chosen closed complement to the kernel of a Fredholm operator.
decls.statement: def kerComplement : Submodule 𝕜 E

decls.name: TauCeti.IsFredholm.cokerComplement
decls.doc:
A chosen finite-dimensional complement to the range of a Fredholm operator. It represents
the cokernel inside the codomain.
decls.statement: def cokerComplement : Submodule 𝕜 F

decls.name: TauCeti.IsFredholm.isTopCompl_ker_kerComplement
decls.doc: The kernel and its chosen complement are topological complements.
decls.statement:
theorem isTopCompl_ker_kerComplement :
    Submodule.IsTopCompl (LinearMap.ker (T : E →ₗ[𝕜] F)) hT.kerComplement

decls.name: TauCeti.IsFredholm.isTopCompl_range_cokerComplement
decls.doc: The range and its chosen complement are topological complements.
decls.statement:
theorem isTopCompl_range_cokerComplement :
    Submodule.IsTopCompl (LinearMap.range (T : E →ₗ[𝕜] F)) hT.cokerComplement

decls.name: TauCeti.IsFredholm.isClosed_kerComplement
decls.doc: The chosen complement to the kernel is closed.
decls.statement: theorem isClosed_kerComplement : IsClosed (hT.kerComplement : Set E)

decls.name: TauCeti.IsFredholm.isClosed_cokerComplement
decls.doc: The chosen complement to the range is closed.
decls.statement: theorem isClosed_cokerComplement : IsClosed (hT.cokerComplement : Set F)

decls.name: TauCeti.IsFredholm.rangeProdCokerComplementEquiv
decls.doc:
The codomain is continuously linearly equivalent to the product of the range and a chosen
cokernel representative.
decls.statement:
def rangeProdCokerComplementEquiv :
    (LinearMap.range (T : E →ₗ[𝕜] F) × hT.cokerComplement) ≃L[𝕜] F

decls.name: TauCeti.IsFredholm.rangeProdCokerComplementEquiv_apply
decls.statement:
theorem rangeProdCokerComplementEquiv_apply
    (x : LinearMap.range (T : E →ₗ[𝕜] F) × hT.cokerComplement) :
    hT.rangeProdCokerComplementEquiv x = (x.1 : F) + x.2

decls.name: TauCeti.IsFredholm.rangeProdCokerComplementEquiv_symm_apply
decls.statement:
theorem rangeProdCokerComplementEquiv_symm_apply (x : F) :
    hT.rangeProdCokerComplementEquiv.symm x =
      ((LinearMap.range (T : E →ₗ[𝕜] F)).projectionOntoL hT.cokerComplement
        hT.isTopCompl_range_cokerComplement x,
      hT.cokerComplement.projectionOntoL (LinearMap.range (T : E →ₗ[𝕜] F))
        hT.isTopCompl_range_cokerComplement.symm x)

decls.name: TauCeti.IsFredholm.kerProdComplementEquiv
decls.doc:
The domain is continuously linearly equivalent to the product of the kernel and a chosen
kernel complement.
decls.statement:
def kerProdComplementEquiv :
    (LinearMap.ker (T : E →ₗ[𝕜] F) × hT.kerComplement) ≃L[𝕜] E

decls.name: TauCeti.IsFredholm.kerProdComplementEquiv_apply
decls.statement:
theorem kerProdComplementEquiv_apply
    (x : LinearMap.ker (T : E →ₗ[𝕜] F) × hT.kerComplement) :
    hT.kerProdComplementEquiv x = (x.1 : E) + x.2

decls.name: TauCeti.IsFredholm.kerProdComplementEquiv_symm_apply
decls.statement:
theorem kerProdComplementEquiv_symm_apply (x : E) :
    hT.kerProdComplementEquiv.symm x =
      ((LinearMap.ker (T : E →ₗ[𝕜] F)).projectionOntoL hT.kerComplement
        hT.isTopCompl_ker_kerComplement x,
      hT.kerComplement.projectionOntoL (LinearMap.ker (T : E →ₗ[𝕜] F))
        hT.isTopCompl_ker_kerComplement.symm x)

decls.name: TauCeti.IsFredholm.kerComplementEquivRange
decls.doc:
A Fredholm operator restricts to a continuous linear equivalence from its chosen kernel
complement onto its range.
decls.statement:
def kerComplementEquivRange :
    hT.kerComplement ≃L[𝕜] LinearMap.range (T : E →ₗ[𝕜] F)

decls.name: TauCeti.IsFredholm.kerComplementEquivRange_apply
decls.statement:
theorem kerComplementEquivRange_apply (x : hT.kerComplement) :
    (hT.kerComplementEquivRange x : F) = T x

decls.name: TauCeti.IsFredholm.cokerEquivComplement
decls.doc:
The cokernel of a Fredholm operator is continuously linearly equivalent to its chosen
complement in the codomain.
decls.statement:
def cokerEquivComplement :
    (F ⧸ LinearMap.range (T : E →ₗ[𝕜] F)) ≃L[𝕜] hT.cokerComplement

decls.name: TauCeti.IsFredholm.cokerEquivComplement_symm_apply
decls.statement:
theorem cokerEquivComplement_symm_apply (x : hT.cokerComplement) :
    hT.cokerEquivComplement.symm x = (LinearMap.range (T : E →ₗ[𝕜] F)).mkQ x

decls.name: TauCeti.IsFredholm.cokerEquivComplement_apply_mk
decls.statement:
theorem cokerEquivComplement_apply_mk (x : F) :
    hT.cokerEquivComplement (Submodule.Quotient.mk x) =
      hT.cokerComplement.projectionOnto (LinearMap.range (T : E →ₗ[𝕜] F))
        hT.isTopCompl_range_cokerComplement.isCompl.symm x

decls.name: TauCeti.IsFredholm.finiteDimensional_cokerComplement
decls.statement:
instance finiteDimensional_cokerComplement :
    FiniteDimensional 𝕜 hT.cokerComplement

decls.name: TauCeti.finiteDimensional_domain_of_isFredholm_zero
decls.statement:
lemma finiteDimensional_domain_of_isFredholm_zero
    (hT : IsFredholm (0 : E →L[𝕜] F)) : FiniteDimensional 𝕜 E

decls.name: TauCeti.finiteDimensional_codomain_of_isFredholm_zero
decls.statement:
lemma finiteDimensional_codomain_of_isFredholm_zero
    (hT : IsFredholm (0 : E →L[𝕜] F)) : FiniteDimensional 𝕜 F

decls.name: TauCeti.isFredholm_zero_iff
decls.doc:
The zero continuous linear map is Fredholm exactly when its domain and codomain are both
finite dimensional.
decls.statement:
lemma isFredholm_zero_iff :
    IsFredholm (0 : E →L[𝕜] F) ↔
      Nonempty (FiniteDimensional 𝕜 E) ∧ Nonempty (FiniteDimensional 𝕜 F)

decls.name: TauCeti.ContinuousLinearMap.index_zero
decls.doc:
The index of the zero continuous linear map is the dimension of its domain minus the
dimension of its codomain.
decls.statement:
lemma index_zero :
    index (0 : E →L[𝕜] F) = (finrank 𝕜 E : ℤ) - finrank 𝕜 F

decls.name: TauCeti.harmonicOnNhd_comp_const_add_smul_ball_radius_iff
decls.doc:
Harmonicity on a neighbourhood of `Metric.ball x (‖c‖ * r)` is equivalent to harmonicity
of `y ↦ f (x + c • y)` on a neighbourhood of `Metric.ball 0 r`, for nonzero scale `c`.
decls.statement:
theorem harmonicOnNhd_comp_const_add_smul_ball_radius_iff (x : E) {c : ℝ} (hc : c ≠ 0)
    (r : ℝ) {f : E → F} :
    HarmonicOnNhd (fun y ↦ f (x + c • y)) (Metric.ball 0 r) ↔
      HarmonicOnNhd f (Metric.ball x (‖c‖ * r))

decls.name: TauCeti.harmonicOnNhd_comp_add_right_ball_zero_iff
decls.doc:
Translation-normalized harmonicity on a ball. The function `y ↦ f (y + x)` is harmonic
near the radius-`r` ball centered at `0` exactly when `f` is harmonic near the corresponding
ball centered at `x`.
decls.statement:
theorem harmonicOnNhd_comp_add_right_ball_zero_iff (x : E) (r : ℝ) {f : E → F} :
    HarmonicOnNhd (fun y ↦ f (y + x)) (Metric.ball 0 r) ↔
      HarmonicOnNhd f (Metric.ball x r)

decls.name: TauCeti.harmonicOnNhd_comp_const_add_smul_ball_iff
decls.doc:
Harmonicity on a neighbourhood of `Metric.ball x r` is equivalent to harmonicity of the
normalized function `y ↦ f (x + r • y)` on a neighbourhood of the unit ball.
decls.statement:
theorem harmonicOnNhd_comp_const_add_smul_ball_iff (x : E) {r : ℝ} (hr : 0 < r)
    {f : E → F} :
    HarmonicOnNhd (fun y ↦ f (x + r • y)) (Metric.ball 0 1) ↔
      HarmonicOnNhd f (Metric.ball x r)

decls.name: TauCeti.homothetyHomeomorph
decls.doc:
Homotheties of a finite-dimensional normed affine space are homeomorphisms when the scale is
nonzero.
decls.statement: abbrev homothetyHomeomorph (a : E) (c : ℝ) (hc : c ≠ 0) : E ≃ₜ E

decls.name: TauCeti.homothetyHomeomorph_apply
decls.statement:
lemma homothetyHomeomorph_apply (a : E) (c : ℝ) (hc : c ≠ 0) (x : E) :
    homothetyHomeomorph a c hc x = AffineMap.homothety a c x

decls.name: TauCeti.contDiffAt_homothety
decls.statement:
lemma contDiffAt_homothety (a : E) (c : ℝ) (x : E) :
    ContDiffAt ℝ 2 (fun y : E ↦ AffineMap.homothety a c y) x

decls.name: TauCeti.contDiffAt_comp_homothety_right_iff
decls.doc:
Twice continuous differentiability at a point is invariant under nonzero homothety.

For `c ≠ 0`, the function `y ↦ f (AffineMap.homothety a c y)` is `C²` at `x` iff `f` is `C²`
at `AffineMap.homothety a c x`.
decls.statement:
lemma contDiffAt_comp_homothety_right_iff (a : E) (c : ℝ) (hc : c ≠ 0) {f : E → F}
    {x : E} :
    ContDiffAt ℝ 2 (fun y : E ↦ f (AffineMap.homothety a c y)) x ↔
      ContDiffAt ℝ 2 f (AffineMap.homothety a c x)

decls.name: TauCeti.laplacian_eventuallyEq_zero_comp_homothety_right_iff
decls.doc:
Local vanishing of the Laplacian is invariant under nonzero homothety.

For `c ≠ 0`, the Laplacian of `y ↦ f (AffineMap.homothety a c y)` vanishes near `x` iff the
Laplacian of `f` vanishes near `AffineMap.homothety a c x`.
decls.statement:
lemma laplacian_eventuallyEq_zero_comp_homothety_right_iff (a : E) (c : ℝ) (hc : c ≠ 0)
    {f : E → F} {x : E} :
    (Δ (fun y : E ↦ f (AffineMap.homothety a c y)) =ᶠ[𝓝 x] 0) ↔
      (Δ f =ᶠ[𝓝 (AffineMap.homothety a c x)] 0)

decls.name: TauCeti.harmonicAt_comp_homothety_right_iff
decls.doc:
**Harmonicity is invariant under nonzero homothety.**

For `c ≠ 0`, the function `y ↦ f (AffineMap.homothety a c y)` is harmonic at `x` iff `f`
is harmonic at `AffineMap.homothety a c x`.
decls.title: Harmonicity is invariant under nonzero homothety
decls.statement:
theorem harmonicAt_comp_homothety_right_iff (a : E) (c : ℝ) (hc : c ≠ 0) {f : E → F}
    {x : E} :
    HarmonicAt (fun y ↦ f (AffineMap.homothety a c y)) x ↔
      HarmonicAt f (AffineMap.homothety a c x)

decls.name: TauCeti.harmonicOnNhd_comp_homothety_right_iff
decls.doc: Harmonicity on a neighbourhood of a set is invariant under nonzero homothety.
decls.statement:
theorem harmonicOnNhd_comp_homothety_right_iff (a : E) (c : ℝ) (hc : c ≠ 0) {f : E → F}
    {s : Set E} :
    HarmonicOnNhd (fun y ↦ f (AffineMap.homothety a c y))
        ((fun y ↦ AffineMap.homothety a c y) ⁻¹' s) ↔
      HarmonicOnNhd f s

decls.name: TauCeti.harmonicAt_comp_smul_right_iff
decls.doc:
**Harmonicity is invariant under nonzero dilation.**

For `c ≠ 0`, the function `x ↦ f (c • x)` is harmonic at `x` iff `f` is harmonic at
`c • x`.
decls.title: Harmonicity is invariant under nonzero dilation
decls.statement:
theorem harmonicAt_comp_smul_right_iff (c : ℝ) (hc : c ≠ 0) {f : E → F} {x : E} :
    HarmonicAt (fun y ↦ f (c • y)) x ↔ HarmonicAt f (c • x)

decls.name: TauCeti.harmonicOnNhd_comp_smul_right_iff
decls.doc: Harmonicity on a neighbourhood of a set is invariant under nonzero dilation.
decls.statement:
theorem harmonicOnNhd_comp_smul_right_iff (c : ℝ) (hc : c ≠ 0) {f : E → F}
    {s : Set E} :
    HarmonicOnNhd (fun y ↦ f (c • y)) ((fun y ↦ c • y) ⁻¹' s) ↔
      HarmonicOnNhd f s

decls.name: TauCeti.harmonicAt_comp_const_add_smul_iff
decls.doc:
**Harmonicity is invariant under the affine normalization `z ↦ x + c • z`** when the scale
is nonzero.

For `c ≠ 0`, the function `z ↦ f (x + c • z)` is harmonic at `y` iff `f` is harmonic at
`x + c • y`.
decls.title: Harmonicity is invariant under the affine normalization `z ↦ x + c • z`
decls.statement:
theorem harmonicAt_comp_const_add_smul_iff (x : E) {c : ℝ} (hc : c ≠ 0) {f : E → F} {y : E} :
    HarmonicAt (fun z ↦ f (x + c • z)) y ↔ HarmonicAt f (x + c • y)

decls.name: TauCeti.harmonicOnNhd_comp_const_add_smul_iff
decls.doc:
**Harmonicity on a neighbourhood of a set is invariant under the affine normalization
`z ↦ x + c • z`** when the scale is nonzero.

For `c ≠ 0`, the function `z ↦ f (x + c • z)` is harmonic near `(fun z ↦ x + c • z) ⁻¹' s`
iff `f` is harmonic near `s`.
decls.statement:
theorem harmonicOnNhd_comp_const_add_smul_iff (x : E) {c : ℝ} (hc : c ≠ 0) {f : E → F}
    {s : Set E} :
    HarmonicOnNhd (fun z ↦ f (x + c • z)) ((fun z ↦ x + c • z) ⁻¹' s) ↔
      HarmonicOnNhd f s

decls.name: TauCeti.harmonicAt_comp_linearIsometryEquiv_right_iff
decls.doc:
**Harmonicity is invariant under isometric changes of variable.** For a linear isometry
equivalence `l`, the function `f ∘ l` is harmonic at `x` iff `f` is harmonic at `l x`.
decls.title: Harmonicity is invariant under isometric changes of variable
decls.statement:
theorem harmonicAt_comp_linearIsometryEquiv_right_iff (l : E ≃ₗᵢ[ℝ] E') {f : E' → F}
    {x : E} : HarmonicAt (f ∘ l) x ↔ HarmonicAt f (l x)

decls.name: TauCeti.harmonicAt_comp_add_right_iff
decls.doc:
**Harmonicity is invariant under translation.** The function `y ↦ f (y + a)` is harmonic
at `x` iff `f` is harmonic at `x + a`.
decls.title: Harmonicity is invariant under translation
decls.statement:
theorem harmonicAt_comp_add_right_iff {f : E → F} {x a : E} :
    HarmonicAt (fun y ↦ f (y + a)) x ↔ HarmonicAt f (x + a)

decls.name: TauCeti.harmonicAt_comp_affineIsometryEquiv_right_iff
decls.doc:
**Harmonicity is invariant under affine isometries.** For an affine isometry equivalence
`e`, the function `f ∘ e` is harmonic at `x` iff `f` is harmonic at `e x`.
decls.title: Harmonicity is invariant under affine isometries
decls.statement:
theorem harmonicAt_comp_affineIsometryEquiv_right_iff (e : E ≃ᵃⁱ[ℝ] E') {f : E' → F}
    {x : E} : HarmonicAt (f ∘ e) x ↔ HarmonicAt f (e x)

decls.name: TauCeti.harmonicOnNhd_comp_affineIsometryEquiv_right_iff
decls.doc: Harmonicity on a neighbourhood of a set is invariant under an affine isometry equivalence.
decls.statement:
theorem harmonicOnNhd_comp_affineIsometryEquiv_right_iff (e : E ≃ᵃⁱ[ℝ] E') {f : E' → F}
    {s : Set E'} : HarmonicOnNhd (f ∘ e) (e ⁻¹' s) ↔ HarmonicOnNhd f s

decls.name: TauCeti.harmonicOnNhd_comp_linearIsometryEquiv_right_iff
decls.doc:
Harmonicity on a neighbourhood of a set is invariant under a linear isometric change of
variable.
decls.statement:
theorem harmonicOnNhd_comp_linearIsometryEquiv_right_iff (l : E ≃ₗᵢ[ℝ] E') {f : E' → F}
    {s : Set E'} : HarmonicOnNhd (f ∘ l) (l ⁻¹' s) ↔ HarmonicOnNhd f s

decls.name: TauCeti.harmonicOnNhd_comp_add_right_iff
decls.doc: Harmonicity on a neighbourhood of a set is invariant under translation.
decls.statement:
theorem harmonicOnNhd_comp_add_right_iff {f : E → F} {s : Set E} (a : E) :
    HarmonicOnNhd (fun y ↦ f (y + a)) ((fun y ↦ y + a) ⁻¹' s) ↔ HarmonicOnNhd f s

decls.name: HilbertBasis.mapₗᵢ
decls.doc: Transport a Hilbert basis along a linear isometric equivalence.
decls.statement:
def _root_.HilbertBasis.mapₗᵢ
    (b : _root_.HilbertBasis ι 𝕜 E) (e : E ≃ₗᵢ[𝕜] F) :
    _root_.HilbertBasis ι 𝕜 F

decls.name: HilbertBasis.repr_mapₗᵢ
decls.doc: The coordinate representation of `b.mapₗᵢ e` is `b.repr` after applying `e.symm`.
decls.statement:
theorem _root_.HilbertBasis.repr_mapₗᵢ
    (b : _root_.HilbertBasis ι 𝕜 E) (e : E ≃ₗᵢ[𝕜] F) :
    (b.mapₗᵢ e).repr = e.symm.trans b.repr

decls.name: HilbertBasis.mapₗᵢ_apply
decls.doc: The `i`th vector of the transported basis is the image of the `i`th vector.
decls.statement:
theorem _root_.HilbertBasis.mapₗᵢ_apply
    (b : _root_.HilbertBasis ι 𝕜 E) (e : E ≃ₗᵢ[𝕜] F) (i : ι) :
    b.mapₗᵢ e i = e (b i)

decls.name: HilbertBasis.coe_mapₗᵢ
decls.doc: Function-level form of `HilbertBasis.mapₗᵢ_apply`.
decls.statement:
theorem _root_.HilbertBasis.coe_mapₗᵢ
    (b : _root_.HilbertBasis ι 𝕜 E) (e : E ≃ₗᵢ[𝕜] F) :
    ⇑(b.mapₗᵢ e) = e ∘ b

decls.name: HilbertBasis.mapₗᵢ_refl
decls.doc: Transport along the identity isometry leaves a Hilbert basis unchanged.
decls.statement:
theorem _root_.HilbertBasis.mapₗᵢ_refl (b : _root_.HilbertBasis ι 𝕜 E) :
    b.mapₗᵢ (LinearIsometryEquiv.refl 𝕜 E) = b

decls.name: HilbertBasis.mapₗᵢ_trans
decls.doc:
Transporting along two linear isometric equivalences is the same as transporting along their
composition.
decls.statement:
theorem _root_.HilbertBasis.mapₗᵢ_trans {G : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup G] [InnerProductSpace 𝕜 G]
    (b : _root_.HilbertBasis ι 𝕜 E) (e : E ≃ₗᵢ[𝕜] F) (f : F ≃ₗᵢ[𝕜] G) :
    (b.mapₗᵢ e).mapₗᵢ f = b.mapₗᵢ (e.trans f)

decls.name: HilbertBasis.mapₗᵢ_symm
decls.doc:
Transporting a Hilbert basis across an isometry and then back across the inverse isometry
recovers the original basis.
decls.statement:
theorem _root_.HilbertBasis.mapₗᵢ_symm
    (b : _root_.HilbertBasis ι 𝕜 E) (e : E ≃ₗᵢ[𝕜] F) :
    (b.mapₗᵢ e).mapₗᵢ e.symm = b

decls.name: HilbertBasis.mapₗᵢ_symm_self
decls.doc:
Transporting a Hilbert basis back across an inverse isometry and then forward again recovers
the original basis.
decls.statement:
theorem _root_.HilbertBasis.mapₗᵢ_symm_self
    (b : _root_.HilbertBasis ι 𝕜 F) (e : E ≃ₗᵢ[𝕜] F) :
    (b.mapₗᵢ e.symm).mapₗᵢ e = b

decls.name: TauCeti.memLp_pi_prod
decls.doc: The pointwise product `x ↦ ∏ i, f i (x i)` of `L²` functions is `L²` for the product measure.
decls.statement:
theorem memLp_pi_prod {f : ∀ i, α i → 𝕜} (hf : ∀ i, MemLp (f i) 2 (μ i)) :
    MemLp (fun x : ∀ i, α i => ∏ i, f i (x i)) 2 (Measure.pi μ)

decls.name: TauCeti.L2piMul
decls.doc:
The pointwise product `x ↦ ∏ i, F i (x i)` of a family of `L²(μ i)` vectors, as a vector of
`L²(Measure.pi μ)`.
decls.statement: def L2piMul (F : ∀ i, Lp 𝕜 2 (μ i)) : Lp 𝕜 2 (Measure.pi μ)

decls.name: TauCeti.coeFn_L2piMul
decls.doc: The `Lp` representative of `L2piMul F` is the pointwise product of the representatives.
decls.statement:
theorem coeFn_L2piMul (F : ∀ i, Lp 𝕜 2 (μ i)) :
    ⇑(L2piMul F) =ᵐ[Measure.pi μ] fun x : ∀ i, α i => ∏ i, F i (x i)

decls.name: TauCeti.inner_L2piMul
decls.doc:
**The tensor inner-product identity, `Fintype`-indexed.** The inner product of two pointwise
products factors as the product of the coordinatewise inner products.
decls.title: The tensor inner-product identity, `Fintype`-indexed
decls.statement:
theorem inner_L2piMul (F G : ∀ i, Lp 𝕜 2 (μ i)) :
    inner 𝕜 (L2piMul F) (L2piMul G) = ∏ i, inner 𝕜 (F i) (G i)

decls.name: TauCeti.orthonormal_L2piMul
decls.doc:
**Orthonormality of the tensor family, `Fintype`-indexed.** Coordinatewise orthonormal families
multiply to an orthonormal family of `L²(Measure.pi μ)`, indexed by the dependent function type.
decls.title: Orthonormality of the tensor family, `Fintype`-indexed

decls.name: TauCeti.norm_L2piMul
decls.doc: The tensor construction is norm-multiplicative.
decls.statement: theorem norm_L2piMul (F : ∀ i, Lp 𝕜 2 (μ i)) : ‖L2piMul F‖ = ∏ i, ‖F i‖

decls.name: TauCeti.coeFn_L2piMul_update
decls.doc: Splitting off the `j`-th coordinate of a tensor.
decls.statement:
theorem coeFn_L2piMul_update (j : ι) (F : ∀ i, Lp 𝕜 2 (μ i)) (v : Lp 𝕜 2 (μ j)) :
    ⇑(L2piMul (Function.update F j v)) =ᵐ[Measure.pi μ]
      fun x : ∀ i, α i => v (x j) * ∏ i ∈ Finset.univ.erase j, F i (x i)

decls.name: TauCeti.L2piMul_update_add
decls.doc: The tensor is additive in the `j`-th coordinate.
decls.statement:
theorem L2piMul_update_add (j : ι) (F : ∀ i, Lp 𝕜 2 (μ i)) (v w : Lp 𝕜 2 (μ j)) :
    L2piMul (Function.update F j (v + w))
      = L2piMul (Function.update F j v) + L2piMul (Function.update F j w)

decls.name: TauCeti.L2piMul_update_smul
decls.doc: The tensor is homogeneous in the `j`-th coordinate.
decls.statement:
theorem L2piMul_update_smul (j : ι) (F : ∀ i, Lp 𝕜 2 (μ i)) (c : 𝕜) (v : Lp 𝕜 2 (μ j)) :
    L2piMul (Function.update F j (c • v)) = c • L2piMul (Function.update F j v)

decls.name: TauCeti.L2piMul_update_zero
decls.doc: The tensor vanishes when its `j`-th coordinate does.
decls.statement:
theorem L2piMul_update_zero (j : ι) (F : ∀ i, Lp 𝕜 2 (μ i)) :
    L2piMul (Function.update F j 0) = 0

decls.name: TauCeti.norm_L2piMul_update
decls.doc: The norm of a tensor with its `j`-th coordinate replaced.
decls.statement:
theorem norm_L2piMul_update (j : ι) (F : ∀ i, Lp 𝕜 2 (μ i)) (v : Lp 𝕜 2 (μ j)) :
    ‖L2piMul (Function.update F j v)‖ = (∏ i ∈ Finset.univ.erase j, ‖F i‖) * ‖v‖

decls.name: TauCeti.L2piMulSlot
decls.doc: Tensoring with all coordinates but `j` held fixed, as a continuous linear map.
decls.statement:
def L2piMulSlot (j : ι) (F : ∀ i, Lp 𝕜 2 (μ i)) :
    Lp 𝕜 2 (μ j) →L[𝕜] Lp 𝕜 2 (Measure.pi μ)

decls.name: TauCeti.L2piMulSlot_apply
decls.doc: `L2piMulSlot` applies as the tensor.
decls.statement:
theorem L2piMulSlot_apply (j : ι) (F : ∀ i, Lp 𝕜 2 (μ i)) (v : Lp 𝕜 2 (μ j)) :
    L2piMulSlot j F v = L2piMul (Function.update F j v)

decls.name: TauCeti.inner_L2piMul_eq_zero_of_forall_basis
decls.doc:
**Basis tensors detect all tensors.** A vector orthogonal to every tensor built from
coordinatewise Hilbert bases is orthogonal to *every* elementary tensor.
decls.title: Basis tensors detect all tensors

decls.name: TauCeti.setIntegral_pi_eq_zero_of_forall_inner
decls.doc:
The tensor of indicators is the indicator of the box, so orthogonality to every elementary
tensor makes the integral over every finite-measure box vanish.
decls.statement:
theorem setIntegral_pi_eq_zero_of_forall_inner {h : Lp 𝕜 2 (Measure.pi μ)}
    (hz : ∀ F : ∀ i, Lp 𝕜 2 (μ i), inner 𝕜 (L2piMul F) h = 0)
    (s : ∀ i, Set (α i)) (hs : ∀ i, MeasurableSet (s i)) (hfin : ∀ i, μ i (s i) ≠ ⊤) :
    ∫ x in Set.univ.pi s, h x ∂(Measure.pi μ) = 0

decls.name: TauCeti.setIntegral_eq_zero_of_forall_inner_pi
decls.doc:
A vector orthogonal to every elementary tensor has vanishing integral over every measurable set
of finite measure.
decls.statement:
theorem setIntegral_eq_zero_of_forall_inner_pi {h : Lp 𝕜 2 (Measure.pi μ)}
    (hz : ∀ F : ∀ i, Lp 𝕜 2 (μ i), inner 𝕜 (L2piMul F) h = 0)
    (u : Set (∀ i, α i)) (hu : MeasurableSet u) (hfin : Measure.pi μ u < ⊤) :
    ∫ x in u, h x ∂(Measure.pi μ) = 0

decls.name: TauCeti.orthogonal_span_range_L2piMul_eq_bot
decls.doc:
**Completeness of the tensor family.** The tensors built from coordinatewise Hilbert bases have
trivial orthogonal complement in `L²(Measure.pi μ)`.
decls.title: Completeness of the tensor family

decls.name: TauCeti.piHilbertBasis
decls.doc:
**The `Fintype`-indexed product Hilbert basis.** Pointwise products of coordinatewise Hilbert
bases form a Hilbert basis of `L²(Measure.pi μ)`, indexed by the dependent function type.
decls.title: The `Fintype`-indexed product Hilbert basis

decls.name: TauCeti.piHilbertBasis_apply
decls.doc: The `k`-th vector of `piHilbertBasis` is the tensor of the `k i`-th basis vectors.

decls.name: TauCeti.coeFn_piHilbertBasis
decls.doc: The `k`-th vector of `piHilbertBasis` is a.e. the pointwise product `∏ i, b i (k i)`.

decls.name: TauCeti.memLp_mul_prod
decls.doc:
The pointwise product `(x, y) ↦ f x * g y` of an `L²(μ)` and an `L²(ν)` function is `L²` for the
product measure `μ ⊗ ν`.

decls.name: TauCeti.L2prodMul
decls.doc:
The pointwise product `(x, y) ↦ F x * G y` of `F : L²(μ)` and `G : L²(ν)`, as a vector of
`L²(μ ⊗ ν)`.
decls.statement:
def L2prodMul [SFinite μ] [SFinite ν] (F : Lp 𝕜 2 μ) (G : Lp 𝕜 2 ν) :
    Lp 𝕜 2 (μ.prod ν)

decls.name: TauCeti.coeFn_L2prodMul
decls.doc: The `Lp` representative of `L2prodMul F G` is the pointwise product of the representatives.
decls.statement:
theorem coeFn_L2prodMul [SFinite μ] [SFinite ν] (F : Lp 𝕜 2 μ) (G : Lp 𝕜 2 ν) :
    ⇑(L2prodMul F G) =ᵐ[μ.prod ν] fun p : α × β => F p.1 * G p.2

decls.name: TauCeti.L2prodMul_add_left
decls.doc: The tensor is additive in its first argument.
decls.statement:
theorem L2prodMul_add_left [SFinite μ] [SFinite ν] (F₁ F₂ : Lp 𝕜 2 μ) (G : Lp 𝕜 2 ν) :
    L2prodMul (F₁ + F₂) G = L2prodMul F₁ G + L2prodMul F₂ G

decls.name: TauCeti.L2prodMul_add_right
decls.doc: The tensor is additive in its second argument.
decls.statement:
theorem L2prodMul_add_right [SFinite μ] [SFinite ν] (F : Lp 𝕜 2 μ) (G₁ G₂ : Lp 𝕜 2 ν) :
    L2prodMul F (G₁ + G₂) = L2prodMul F G₁ + L2prodMul F G₂

decls.name: TauCeti.L2prodMul_smul_left
decls.doc: The tensor is homogeneous in its first argument.
decls.statement:
theorem L2prodMul_smul_left [SFinite μ] [SFinite ν] (c : 𝕜) (F : Lp 𝕜 2 μ) (G : Lp 𝕜 2 ν) :
    L2prodMul (c • F) G = c • L2prodMul F G

decls.name: TauCeti.L2prodMul_smul_right
decls.doc: The tensor is homogeneous in its second argument.
decls.statement:
theorem L2prodMul_smul_right [SFinite μ] [SFinite ν] (c : 𝕜) (F : Lp 𝕜 2 μ) (G : Lp 𝕜 2 ν) :
    L2prodMul F (c • G) = c • L2prodMul F G

decls.name: TauCeti.L2prodMul_zero_left
decls.doc: The tensor vanishes when its first argument does.
decls.statement:
theorem L2prodMul_zero_left [SFinite μ] [SFinite ν] (G : Lp 𝕜 2 ν) :
    L2prodMul (0 : Lp 𝕜 2 μ) G = 0

decls.name: TauCeti.L2prodMul_zero_right
decls.doc: The tensor vanishes when its second argument does.
decls.statement:
theorem L2prodMul_zero_right [SFinite μ] [SFinite ν] (F : Lp 𝕜 2 μ) :
    L2prodMul F (0 : Lp 𝕜 2 ν) = 0

decls.name: TauCeti.inner_L2prodMul
decls.doc:
**The tensor inner-product identity.** The inner product of two pointwise-product vectors in
`L²(μ ⊗ ν)` factors as the product of the inner products of the factors.
decls.title: The tensor inner-product identity
decls.statement:
theorem inner_L2prodMul [SFinite μ] [SFinite ν] (F₁ F₂ : Lp 𝕜 2 μ) (G₁ G₂ : Lp 𝕜 2 ν) :
    inner 𝕜 (L2prodMul F₁ G₁) (L2prodMul F₂ G₂) = inner 𝕜 F₁ F₂ * inner 𝕜 G₁ G₂

decls.name: TauCeti.orthonormal_L2prodMul
decls.doc:
**Orthonormality of the tensor family.** If `b` and `c` are orthonormal families of `L²(μ)` and
`L²(ν)`, their pointwise products form an orthonormal family of `L²(μ ⊗ ν)`, indexed by the product
of index types.
decls.title: Orthonormality of the tensor family

decls.name: TauCeti.norm_L2prodMul
decls.doc: The tensor construction is norm-multiplicative.
decls.statement:
theorem norm_L2prodMul [SFinite μ] [SFinite ν] (F : Lp 𝕜 2 μ) (G : Lp 𝕜 2 ν) :
    ‖L2prodMul F G‖ = ‖F‖ * ‖G‖

decls.name: TauCeti.L2prodMulL
decls.doc:
**The tensor as a bounded bilinear map.** `L2prodMulL F G = L2prodMul F G`, packaged so that
either operand can be fixed: `L2prodMulL F` fixes the left factor, `L2prodMulL.flip G` the right.
The operator norm bound is `1`, since `norm_L2prodMul` is an equality.
decls.title: The tensor as a bounded bilinear map
decls.statement:
def L2prodMulL [SFinite μ] [SFinite ν] :
    Lp 𝕜 2 μ →L[𝕜] Lp 𝕜 2 ν →L[𝕜] Lp 𝕜 2 (μ.prod ν)

decls.name: TauCeti.L2prodMulL_apply
decls.statement:
theorem L2prodMulL_apply [SFinite μ] [SFinite ν] (F : Lp 𝕜 2 μ) (G : Lp 𝕜 2 ν) :
    L2prodMulL F G = L2prodMul F G

decls.name: TauCeti.inner_L2prodMul_eq_zero_of_forall_basis
decls.doc:
**Basis tensors detect all tensors.** A vector orthogonal to every tensor built from two Hilbert
bases is orthogonal to *every* elementary tensor. This is the countability-free half of the
completeness argument: it is pure Hilbert-space geometry, with no null-set bookkeeping.
decls.title: Basis tensors detect all tensors
decls.statement:
theorem inner_L2prodMul_eq_zero_of_forall_basis [SFinite μ] [SFinite ν] {ι₁ ι₂ : Type*}
    (b₁ : HilbertBasis ι₁ 𝕜 (Lp 𝕜 2 μ)) (b₂ : HilbertBasis ι₂ 𝕜 (Lp 𝕜 2 ν))
    {h : Lp 𝕜 2 (μ.prod ν)} (hz : ∀ i j, inner 𝕜 h (L2prodMul (b₁ i) (b₂ j)) = 0)
    (F : Lp 𝕜 2 μ) (G : Lp 𝕜 2 ν) : inner 𝕜 h (L2prodMul F G) = 0

decls.name: TauCeti.setIntegral_prod_eq_zero_of_forall_inner
decls.doc:
The tensor of two indicators is the indicator of the rectangle, so orthogonality to every
elementary tensor makes the integral over every finite-measure rectangle vanish.
decls.statement:
theorem setIntegral_prod_eq_zero_of_forall_inner [SFinite μ] [SFinite ν]
    {h : Lp 𝕜 2 (μ.prod ν)}
    (hz : ∀ (F : Lp 𝕜 2 μ) (G : Lp 𝕜 2 ν), inner 𝕜 (L2prodMul F G) h = 0)
    {A : Set α} (hA : MeasurableSet A) (hμA : μ A ≠ ⊤)
    {B : Set β} (hB : MeasurableSet B) (hνB : ν B ≠ ⊤) :
    ∫ p in A ×ˢ B, h p ∂(μ.prod ν) = 0

decls.name: TauCeti.setIntegral_eq_zero_of_forall_inner
decls.doc:
**Orthogonality kills every finite-measure set integral.** Exhaust the product space by finite
boxes `spanningSets μ n ×ˢ spanningSets ν n`, run the Dynkin step inside each box, and pass to the
monotone limit.
decls.title: Orthogonality kills every finite-measure set integral
decls.statement:
theorem setIntegral_eq_zero_of_forall_inner [SigmaFinite μ] [SigmaFinite ν]
    {h : Lp 𝕜 2 (μ.prod ν)}
    (hz : ∀ (F : Lp 𝕜 2 μ) (G : Lp 𝕜 2 ν), inner 𝕜 (L2prodMul F G) h = 0)
    (u : Set (α × β)) (hu : MeasurableSet u) (hfin : (μ.prod ν) u < ⊤) :
    ∫ p in u, h p ∂(μ.prod ν) = 0

decls.name: TauCeti.orthogonal_span_range_L2prodMul_eq_bot
decls.doc:
**Completeness of the tensor family.** The elementary tensors built from two Hilbert bases have
trivial orthogonal complement in `L²(μ ⊗ ν)`: a vector orthogonal to all of them is orthogonal to
every elementary tensor, hence integrates to zero on every rectangle, hence on every finite-measure
set, hence vanishes.
decls.title: Completeness of the tensor family
decls.statement:
theorem orthogonal_span_range_L2prodMul_eq_bot [SigmaFinite μ] [SigmaFinite ν] {ι₁ ι₂ : Type*}
    (b₁ : HilbertBasis ι₁ 𝕜 (Lp 𝕜 2 μ)) (b₂ : HilbertBasis ι₂ 𝕜 (Lp 𝕜 2 ν)) :
    (Submodule.span 𝕜
      (Set.range (fun ij : ι₁ × ι₂ => L2prodMul (b₁ ij.1) (b₂ ij.2))))ᗮ = ⊥

decls.name: TauCeti.prodHilbertBasis
decls.doc:
**The product Hilbert basis.** Pointwise products of two Hilbert bases form a Hilbert basis of
`L²(μ ⊗ ν)`, indexed by the product of the index types.
decls.title: The product Hilbert basis

decls.name: TauCeti.prodHilbertBasis_apply
decls.doc:
The `(i, j)` vector of `prodHilbertBasis` is the tensor of the `i`-th and `j`-th basis
vectors.

decls.name: TauCeti.coeFn_prodHilbertBasis
decls.doc: The `(i, j)` vector of `prodHilbertBasis` is a.e. the pointwise product `b₁ i ⊗ b₂ j`.

decls.name: TauCeti.smulLeftContinuousLinearEquiv
decls.doc: Scalar dilation as a continuous linear equivalence.
decls.statement: abbrev smulLeftContinuousLinearEquiv (c : ℝ) (hc : c ≠ 0) : E ≃L[ℝ] E

decls.name: TauCeti.iteratedFDeriv_comp_linearIsometryEquiv_apply
decls.doc:
The iterated derivative transforms under a linear isometry equivalence on the right by
pulling the directions through the isometry. This is the unconditional engine behind the
geometric invariance of the Laplacian.
decls.statement:
theorem iteratedFDeriv_comp_linearIsometryEquiv_apply (l : E ≃ₗᵢ[ℝ] E') (f : E' → F)
    (i : ℕ) (x : E) (m : Fin i → E) :
    iteratedFDeriv ℝ i (f ∘ l) x m = iteratedFDeriv ℝ i f (l x) (fun j ↦ l (m j))

decls.name: TauCeti.laplacian_comp_linearIsometryEquiv_right
decls.doc:
**Geometric invariance of the Laplacian under isometries.** For a linear isometry
equivalence `l`, the Laplacian commutes with right composition by `l`:
`Δ (f ∘ l) = (Δ f) ∘ l`. No differentiability hypothesis is needed.
decls.title: Geometric invariance of the Laplacian under isometries
decls.statement:
theorem laplacian_comp_linearIsometryEquiv_right (l : E ≃ₗᵢ[ℝ] E') (f : E' → F) :
    Δ (f ∘ l) = (Δ f) ∘ l

decls.name: TauCeti.laplacian_comp_add_right
decls.doc:
**Translation invariance of the Laplacian.** Shifting the argument by a constant `a`
commutes with the Laplacian: `Δ (fun y ↦ f (y + a)) = fun y ↦ (Δ f) (y + a)`. No
differentiability hypothesis is needed.
decls.title: Translation invariance of the Laplacian
decls.statement:
theorem laplacian_comp_add_right (f : E → F) (a : E) :
    Δ (fun y ↦ f (y + a)) = fun y ↦ (Δ f) (y + a)

decls.name: TauCeti.laplacian_comp_affineIsometryEquiv_right
decls.doc:
**Geometric invariance of the Laplacian under affine isometries.** For an affine isometry
equivalence `e`, the Laplacian commutes with right composition by `e`:
`Δ (f ∘ e) = (Δ f) ∘ e`. No differentiability hypothesis is needed.
decls.title: Geometric invariance of the Laplacian under affine isometries
decls.statement:
theorem laplacian_comp_affineIsometryEquiv_right (e : E ≃ᵃⁱ[ℝ] E') (f : E' → F) :
    Δ (f ∘ e) = (Δ f) ∘ e

decls.name: TauCeti.laplacian_comp_smul_right
decls.doc:
**Scaling law for the Laplacian under origin-centered dilation.**

Right-composition by `x ↦ c • x` multiplies the Laplacian by `c ^ 2`. The statement is
unconditional in `f`, matching Mathlib's unconditional definition of `Δ` through iterated
Fréchet derivatives.
decls.title: Scaling law for the Laplacian under origin-centered dilation
decls.statement:
theorem laplacian_comp_smul_right (c : ℝ) (f : E → F) :
    Δ (fun x ↦ f (c • x)) = fun x ↦ c ^ 2 • (Δ f) (c • x)

decls.name: TauCeti.laplacian_comp_homothety_right
decls.doc:
**Scaling law for the Laplacian under a homothety.**

Right-composition by `AffineMap.homothety a c` multiplies the Laplacian by `c ^ 2`.
decls.title: Scaling law for the Laplacian under a homothety
decls.statement:
theorem laplacian_comp_homothety_right (a : E) (c : ℝ) (f : E → F) :
    Δ (fun x ↦ f (AffineMap.homothety a c x)) =
      fun x ↦ c ^ 2 • (Δ f) (AffineMap.homothety a c x)

decls.name: TauCeti.laplacian_norm_sq
decls.doc:
The Laplacian of the squared norm on a finite-dimensional real inner product space is twice
the dimension.
decls.statement:
theorem laplacian_norm_sq (x : E) :
    Δ (fun y : E => ‖y‖ ^ 2) x = 2 * (Module.finrank ℝ E : ℝ)

decls.name: TauCeti.le_of_laplacian_le_of_le_frontier
decls.doc:
**Comparison principle for the Laplacian.**

Let `K` be compact, and let `f`, `g` be continuous on `K` and `C²` on `interior K`. If `f` is at
least as subharmonic as `g` there (`Δ g ≤ Δ f`) and `f ≤ g` on `frontier K`, then `f ≤ g` on all of
`K`. This is the two-function form of the weak maximum principle
`le_of_laplacian_nonneg_le_frontier`, applied to the difference `f - g`.
decls.title: Comparison principle for the Laplacian
decls.statement:
theorem le_of_laplacian_le_of_le_frontier (hK : IsCompact K)
    (hfcont : ContinuousOn f K) (hgcont : ContinuousOn g K)
    (hfcd : ∀ ⦃x⦄, x ∈ interior K → ContDiffAt ℝ 2 f x)
    (hgcd : ∀ ⦃x⦄, x ∈ interior K → ContDiffAt ℝ 2 g x)
    (hlap : ∀ ⦃x⦄, x ∈ interior K → Δ g x ≤ Δ f x)
    (hbdry : ∀ ⦃x⦄, x ∈ frontier K → f x ≤ g x) :
    ∀ ⦃x⦄, x ∈ K → f x ≤ g x

decls.name: TauCeti.eqOn_of_laplacian_eqOn_of_eqOn_frontier
decls.doc:
**Uniqueness for the Poisson equation.**

If `f` and `g` are continuous on a compact set `K`, `C²` on `interior K` with the *same* Laplacian
there, and agree on `frontier K`, then they agree on all of `K`. A solution of `Δ u = h` in
`interior K` is thus determined by its boundary values.
decls.title: Uniqueness for the Poisson equation
decls.statement:
theorem eqOn_of_laplacian_eqOn_of_eqOn_frontier (hK : IsCompact K)
    (hfcont : ContinuousOn f K) (hgcont : ContinuousOn g K)
    (hfcd : ∀ ⦃x⦄, x ∈ interior K → ContDiffAt ℝ 2 f x)
    (hgcd : ∀ ⦃x⦄, x ∈ interior K → ContDiffAt ℝ 2 g x)
    (hlap : ∀ ⦃x⦄, x ∈ interior K → Δ f x = Δ g x)
    (hbdry : ∀ ⦃x⦄, x ∈ frontier K → f x = g x) :
    Set.EqOn f g K

decls.name: TauCeti.laplacian_eq_zero_of_harmonicAt
decls.doc: The Laplacian of a function harmonic near `x` vanishes at `x`.
decls.statement: theorem laplacian_eq_zero_of_harmonicAt {x : E} (hf : HarmonicAt f x) : Δ f x = 0

decls.name: TauCeti.eqOn_of_harmonicOnNhd_of_eqOn_frontier
decls.doc:
**Uniqueness of the Dirichlet problem for the Laplace equation.**

Two functions that are harmonic on the interior of a compact set `K`, continuous on `K`, and equal
on `frontier K` are equal on all of `K`.
decls.title: Uniqueness of the Dirichlet problem for the Laplace equation
decls.statement:
theorem eqOn_of_harmonicOnNhd_of_eqOn_frontier (hK : IsCompact K)
    (hfcont : ContinuousOn f K) (hgcont : ContinuousOn g K)
    (hf : HarmonicOnNhd f (interior K)) (hg : HarmonicOnNhd g (interior K))
    (hbdry : ∀ ⦃x⦄, x ∈ frontier K → f x = g x) :
    Set.EqOn f g K

decls.name: TauCeti.exists_mem_frontier_isMaxOn_of_harmonicOnNhd
decls.doc:
A function harmonic on the interior of a nonempty compact set and continuous on `K` attains its
maximum on `frontier K`.
decls.statement: theorem exists_mem_frontier_isMaxOn_of_harmonicOnNhd : ∃ x ∈ frontier K, IsMaxOn f K x

decls.name: TauCeti.exists_mem_frontier_isMinOn_of_harmonicOnNhd
decls.doc:
A function harmonic on the interior of a nonempty compact set and continuous on `K` attains its
minimum on `frontier K`.
decls.statement: theorem exists_mem_frontier_isMinOn_of_harmonicOnNhd : ∃ x ∈ frontier K, IsMinOn f K x

decls.name: TauCeti.abs_le_of_harmonicOnNhd_of_abs_le_frontier
decls.doc:
A function harmonic on the interior of a compact set `K` and continuous on `K` is bounded on all
of `K` by any bound `M` its absolute value respects on `frontier K`. This is the two-sided
consequence of the maximum principle for harmonic functions.
decls.statement:
theorem abs_le_of_harmonicOnNhd_of_abs_le_frontier (hK : IsCompact K)
    (hcont : ContinuousOn f K) (hf : HarmonicOnNhd f (interior K))
    (hbdry : ∀ ⦃x⦄, x ∈ frontier K → |f x| ≤ M) :
    ∀ ⦃x⦄, x ∈ K → |f x| ≤ M

decls.name: TauCeti.hasFDerivAt_exp_inner
decls.doc:
The exponential barrier `y ↦ exp (α ⟪u, y⟫)` has derivative `exp (α ⟪u, x⟫) • (α • ⟪u, ·⟫)`.
This is the shared first-derivative computation feeding both `laplacian_exp_inner` and
`fderiv_exp_inner_apply`.
decls.statement:
theorem hasFDerivAt_exp_inner (α : ℝ) (u x : E) :
    HasFDerivAt (fun y : E => Real.exp (α * ⟪u, y⟫))
      (Real.exp (α * ⟪u, x⟫) • (α • innerSL ℝ u)) x

decls.name: TauCeti.fderiv_exp_inner_apply
decls.doc: The directional derivative of the exponential barrier `y ↦ exp (α ⟪u, y⟫)`.
decls.statement:
theorem fderiv_exp_inner_apply (α : ℝ) (u x v : E) :
    fderiv ℝ (fun y : E => Real.exp (α * ⟪u, y⟫)) x v
      = Real.exp (α * ⟪u, x⟫) * (α * ⟪u, v⟫)

decls.name: TauCeti.laplacian_exp_inner
decls.doc:
**The Laplacian of the exponential barrier.** For a fixed vector `u`, the function
`y ↦ exp (α ⟪u, y⟫)` has Laplacian `α² ‖u‖² exp (α ⟪u, y⟫)`, because it is an exponential of
a linear form: the second directional derivative along an orthonormal basis vector `eᵢ`
contributes `α² ⟪u, eᵢ⟫²`, and these sum to `α² ‖u‖²`. This is the barrier for the weak
maximum principle with drift.
decls.title: The Laplacian of the exponential barrier
decls.statement:
theorem laplacian_exp_inner (α : ℝ) (u x : E) :
    Δ (fun y : E => Real.exp (α * ⟪u, y⟫)) x
      = α ^ 2 * ‖u‖ ^ 2 * Real.exp (α * ⟪u, x⟫)

decls.name: TauCeti.not_isLocalMax_of_laplacian_add_fderiv_pos
decls.doc:
**Strict interior obstruction.** If `0 < Δ f x + fderiv ℝ f x v` at a point where `f` is
`C²`, then `f` has no local maximum at `x`. The direction `v` is arbitrary: at a local
maximum the derivative `fderiv ℝ f x` vanishes, so the first-order term contributes nothing
and only the Laplacian's nonpositivity survives.
decls.title: Strict interior obstruction

decls.name: TauCeti.not_isLocalMin_of_laplacian_add_fderiv_neg
decls.doc:
**Strict interior obstruction, minimum form.** If `Δ f x + fderiv ℝ f x v < 0` at a point
where `f` is `C²`, then `f` has no local minimum at `x`.
decls.title: Strict interior obstruction, minimum form

decls.name: TauCeti.exists_mem_frontier_isMaxOn_of_laplacian_add_fderiv_pos
decls.doc:
**Strict boundary maximum principle for `Δ + b·∇`.** Let `K` be compact and nonempty. If
`f` is continuous on `K`, is `C²` on `interior K`, and satisfies
`0 < Δ f x + fderiv ℝ f x (b x)` throughout `interior K`, then some maximum point of `f` on
`K` lies on `frontier K`. No hypothesis on the drift field `b` is needed.
decls.title: Strict boundary maximum principle for `Δ + b·∇`
decls.statement:
theorem exists_mem_frontier_isMaxOn_of_laplacian_add_fderiv_pos {K : Set E} (hK : IsCompact K)
    (hne : K.Nonempty) {f : E → ℝ} {b : E → E} (hcont : ContinuousOn f K)
    (hcd : ∀ ⦃x⦄, x ∈ interior K → ContDiffAt ℝ 2 f x)
    (hpos : ∀ ⦃x⦄, x ∈ interior K → 0 < Δ f x + fderiv ℝ f x (b x)) :
    ∃ x ∈ frontier K, IsMaxOn f K x

decls.name: TauCeti.exists_mem_frontier_isMinOn_of_laplacian_add_fderiv_neg
decls.doc:
**Strict boundary minimum principle for `Δ + b·∇`.** The dual of
`exists_mem_frontier_isMaxOn_of_laplacian_add_fderiv_pos`.
decls.title: Strict boundary minimum principle for `Δ + b·∇`
decls.statement:
theorem exists_mem_frontier_isMinOn_of_laplacian_add_fderiv_neg {K : Set E} (hK : IsCompact K)
    (hne : K.Nonempty) {f : E → ℝ} {b : E → E} (hcont : ContinuousOn f K)
    (hcd : ∀ ⦃x⦄, x ∈ interior K → ContDiffAt ℝ 2 f x)
    (hneg : ∀ ⦃x⦄, x ∈ interior K → Δ f x + fderiv ℝ f x (b x) < 0) :
    ∃ x ∈ frontier K, IsMinOn f K x

decls.name: TauCeti.laplacian_add_fderiv_exp_inner_pos_of_norm_le
decls.doc:
The normalized exponential barrier for a drift bounded by `β` is a strict subsolution of
`Δ + b·∇`.
decls.statement:
theorem laplacian_add_fderiv_exp_inner_pos_of_norm_le {u b : E} {β : ℝ}
    (hu : ‖u‖ = 1) (hb : ‖b‖ ≤ β) (x : E) :
    0 < Δ (fun y => Real.exp ((β + 1) * ⟪u, y⟫)) x +
      fderiv ℝ (fun y => Real.exp ((β + 1) * ⟪u, y⟫)) x b

decls.name: TauCeti.laplacian_add_fderiv_add_const_smul
decls.doc: The operator `Δ + b·∇` is linear under addition of a constant multiple.
decls.statement:
theorem laplacian_add_fderiv_add_const_smul (f w : E → ℝ) (b : E) (ε : ℝ) (x : E)
    (hf : ContDiffAt ℝ 2 f x) (hw : ContDiffAt ℝ 2 w x) :
    Δ (fun y => f y + ε • w y) x + fderiv ℝ (fun y => f y + ε • w y) x b =
      (Δ f x + fderiv ℝ f x b) + ε * (Δ w x + fderiv ℝ w x b)

decls.name: TauCeti.le_of_strict_subsolution_barrier
decls.doc:
**Weak maximum principle via a strict-subsolution barrier.** Let `K` be compact and `f`
continuous on `K` and `C²` on `interior K`. If `f` is a subsolution of `Δ + b·∇` there
(`0 ≤ Δ f + fderiv ℝ f (b)`) that is bounded by `m` on `frontier K`, and `w` is a barrier —
continuous on `K` and a `C²` *strict* subsolution on `interior K` (`0 < Δ w + fderiv ℝ w (b)`) —
then `f ≤ m` throughout `K`.
decls.title: Weak maximum principle via a strict-subsolution barrier
decls.statement:
theorem le_of_strict_subsolution_barrier {K : Set E} (hK : IsCompact K)
    {f w : E → ℝ} {b : E → E} {m : ℝ} (hcont : ContinuousOn f K)
    (hcd : ∀ ⦃x⦄, x ∈ interior K → ContDiffAt ℝ 2 f x)
    (hlap : ∀ ⦃x⦄, x ∈ interior K → 0 ≤ Δ f x + fderiv ℝ f x (b x))
    (hbdry : ∀ ⦃x⦄, x ∈ frontier K → f x ≤ m)
    (hwcont : ContinuousOn w K) (hwcd : ∀ ⦃x⦄, x ∈ interior K → ContDiffAt ℝ 2 w x)
    (hwlap : ∀ ⦃x⦄, x ∈ interior K → 0 < Δ w x + fderiv ℝ w x (b x)) :
    ∀ ⦃x⦄, x ∈ K → f x ≤ m

decls.name: TauCeti.le_of_laplacian_add_fderiv_nonneg_le_frontier
decls.doc:
**Weak maximum principle for `Δ + b·∇` with bounded drift.**

Let `K` be compact. If `f` is continuous on `K`, is `C²` on `interior K`, the drift field is
bounded there (`‖b x‖ ≤ β`), and `0 ≤ Δ f x + fderiv ℝ f x (b x)` (a subsolution of
`Δ + b·∇`), then any bound `m` that `f` respects on `frontier K` bounds `f` on all of `K`.
decls.title: Weak maximum principle for `Δ + b·∇` with bounded drift
decls.statement:
theorem le_of_laplacian_add_fderiv_nonneg_le_frontier {K : Set E} (hK : IsCompact K)
    {f : E → ℝ} {b : E → E} {β m : ℝ} (hcont : ContinuousOn f K)
    (hcd : ∀ ⦃x⦄, x ∈ interior K → ContDiffAt ℝ 2 f x)
    (hb : ∀ ⦃x⦄, x ∈ interior K → ‖b x‖ ≤ β)
    (hlap : ∀ ⦃x⦄, x ∈ interior K → 0 ≤ Δ f x + fderiv ℝ f x (b x))
    (hbdry : ∀ ⦃x⦄, x ∈ frontier K → f x ≤ m) :
    ∀ ⦃x⦄, x ∈ K → f x ≤ m

decls.name: TauCeti.ge_of_laplacian_add_fderiv_nonpos_ge_frontier
decls.doc:
**Weak minimum principle for `Δ + b·∇` with bounded drift.** The dual of
`le_of_laplacian_add_fderiv_nonneg_le_frontier` for supersolutions
(`Δ f x + fderiv ℝ f x (b x) ≤ 0`).
decls.title: Weak minimum principle for `Δ + b·∇` with bounded drift
decls.statement:
theorem ge_of_laplacian_add_fderiv_nonpos_ge_frontier {K : Set E} (hK : IsCompact K)
    {f : E → ℝ} {b : E → E} {β m : ℝ} (hcont : ContinuousOn f K)
    (hcd : ∀ ⦃x⦄, x ∈ interior K → ContDiffAt ℝ 2 f x)
    (hb : ∀ ⦃x⦄, x ∈ interior K → ‖b x‖ ≤ β)
    (hlap : ∀ ⦃x⦄, x ∈ interior K → Δ f x + fderiv ℝ f x (b x) ≤ 0)
    (hbdry : ∀ ⦃x⦄, x ∈ frontier K → m ≤ f x) :
    ∀ ⦃x⦄, x ∈ K → m ≤ f x

decls.name: TauCeti.le_of_laplacian_add_fderiv_le_laplacian_add_fderiv_of_le_frontier
decls.doc:
**Comparison principle for `Δ + b·∇`.** Two functions acted on by the same bounded drift
are ordered on a compact set if their operator values and frontier values are ordered.
decls.title: Comparison principle for `Δ + b·∇`
decls.statement:
theorem le_of_laplacian_add_fderiv_le_laplacian_add_fderiv_of_le_frontier {K : Set E}
    (hK : IsCompact K) {f g : E → ℝ} {b : E → E} {β : ℝ}
    (hfcont : ContinuousOn f K) (hgcont : ContinuousOn g K)
    (hfcd : ∀ ⦃x⦄, x ∈ interior K → ContDiffAt ℝ 2 f x)
    (hgcd : ∀ ⦃x⦄, x ∈ interior K → ContDiffAt ℝ 2 g x)
    (hb : ∀ ⦃x⦄, x ∈ interior K → ‖b x‖ ≤ β)
    (hL : ∀ ⦃x⦄, x ∈ interior K →
      Δ g x + fderiv ℝ g x (b x) ≤ Δ f x + fderiv ℝ f x (b x))
    (hbdry : ∀ ⦃x⦄, x ∈ frontier K → f x ≤ g x) :
    ∀ ⦃x⦄, x ∈ K → f x ≤ g x

decls.name: TauCeti.eqOn_of_laplacian_add_fderiv_eq_of_eqOn_frontier
decls.doc:
**Uniqueness principle for `Δ + b·∇`.** Functions with equal operator values for the same
bounded drift and equal frontier data agree throughout the compact set.
decls.title: Uniqueness principle for `Δ + b·∇`
decls.statement:
theorem eqOn_of_laplacian_add_fderiv_eq_of_eqOn_frontier {K : Set E} (hK : IsCompact K)
    {f g : E → ℝ} {b : E → E} {β : ℝ} (hfcont : ContinuousOn f K)
    (hgcont : ContinuousOn g K)
    (hfcd : ∀ ⦃x⦄, x ∈ interior K → ContDiffAt ℝ 2 f x)
    (hgcd : ∀ ⦃x⦄, x ∈ interior K → ContDiffAt ℝ 2 g x)
    (hb : ∀ ⦃x⦄, x ∈ interior K → ‖b x‖ ≤ β)
    (hL : ∀ ⦃x⦄, x ∈ interior K →
      Δ f x + fderiv ℝ f x (b x) = Δ g x + fderiv ℝ g x (b x))
    (hbdry : Set.EqOn f g (frontier K)) :
    Set.EqOn f g K

decls.name: TauCeti.exists_mem_frontier_isMaxOn_of_laplacian_add_fderiv_nonneg
decls.doc:
The `∃`-form of the weak maximum principle for `Δ + b·∇`: a subsolution with bounded drift
on a nonempty compact set attains a maximum on the frontier.
decls.statement:
theorem exists_mem_frontier_isMaxOn_of_laplacian_add_fderiv_nonneg {K : Set E} (hK : IsCompact K)
    (hne : K.Nonempty) {f : E → ℝ} {b : E → E} {β : ℝ} (hcont : ContinuousOn f K)
    (hcd : ∀ ⦃x⦄, x ∈ interior K → ContDiffAt ℝ 2 f x)
    (hb : ∀ ⦃x⦄, x ∈ interior K → ‖b x‖ ≤ β)
    (hlap : ∀ ⦃x⦄, x ∈ interior K → 0 ≤ Δ f x + fderiv ℝ f x (b x)) :
    ∃ x ∈ frontier K, IsMaxOn f K x

decls.name: TauCeti.exists_mem_frontier_isMinOn_of_laplacian_add_fderiv_nonpos
decls.doc:
The `∃`-form of the weak minimum principle for `Δ + b·∇`: a supersolution with bounded
drift on a nonempty compact set attains a minimum on the frontier.
decls.statement:
theorem exists_mem_frontier_isMinOn_of_laplacian_add_fderiv_nonpos {K : Set E} (hK : IsCompact K)
    (hne : K.Nonempty) {f : E → ℝ} {b : E → E} {β : ℝ} (hcont : ContinuousOn f K)
    (hcd : ∀ ⦃x⦄, x ∈ interior K → ContDiffAt ℝ 2 f x)
    (hb : ∀ ⦃x⦄, x ∈ interior K → ‖b x‖ ≤ β)
    (hlap : ∀ ⦃x⦄, x ∈ interior K → Δ f x + fderiv ℝ f x (b x) ≤ 0) :
    ∃ x ∈ frontier K, IsMinOn f K x

decls.name: TauCeti.contDiffAt_line
decls.doc: The affine line `t ↦ x + t • w` is smooth at `0`.
decls.statement: theorem contDiffAt_line (x w : E) : ContDiffAt ℝ 2 (fun t : ℝ => x + t • w) 0

decls.name: TauCeti.tendsto_line
decls.doc: The affine line `t ↦ x + t • w` tends to `x` as `t → 0`.
decls.statement:
theorem tendsto_line (x w : E) :
    Filter.Tendsto (fun t : ℝ => x + t • w) (𝓝 0) (𝓝 x)

decls.name: TauCeti.isLocalMax_comp_line
decls.doc: The restriction of `f` to a line inherits a local maximum from `f`.
decls.statement:
theorem isLocalMax_comp_line {f : E → ℝ} {x : E} (hmax : IsLocalMax f x) (w : E) :
    IsLocalMax (fun t : ℝ => f (x + t • w)) 0

decls.name: TauCeti.isLocalMin_comp_line
decls.doc: The restriction of `f` to a line inherits a local minimum from `f`.
decls.statement:
theorem isLocalMin_comp_line {f : E → ℝ} {x : E} (hmin : IsLocalMin f x) (w : E) :
    IsLocalMin (fun t : ℝ => f (x + t • w)) 0

decls.name: TauCeti.contDiffAt_comp_line
decls.doc: The restriction of a `C²` function `f` to a line is `C²` at `0`.
decls.statement:
theorem contDiffAt_comp_line {F : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup F] [NormedSpace ℝ F]
    {f : E → F} {x : E} (hf : ContDiffAt ℝ 2 f x) (w : E) :
    ContDiffAt ℝ 2 (fun t : ℝ => f (x + t • w)) 0

decls.name: TauCeti.deriv_deriv_comp_line
decls.doc:
The second derivative of the restriction of `f` to the line `t ↦ x + t • w` is the diagonal
Hessian entry `fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ f) x w w`.
decls.statement:
theorem deriv_deriv_comp_line {F : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup F] [NormedSpace ℝ F]
    {f : E → F} {x : E} (hf : ContDiffAt ℝ 2 f x) (w : E) :
    deriv (deriv fun t : ℝ => f (x + t • w)) 0 = fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ f) x w w

decls.name: TauCeti.fderiv_fderiv_self_nonpos_of_isLocalMax
decls.doc:
At an interior local maximum of a `C²` function `f : E → ℝ`, every diagonal Hessian entry is
nonpositive.

decls.name: TauCeti.fderiv_fderiv_self_nonneg_of_isLocalMin
decls.doc:
At an interior local minimum of a `C²` function `f : E → ℝ`, every diagonal Hessian entry is
nonnegative.

decls.name: TauCeti.laplacian_nonpos_of_isLocalMax
decls.doc:
**Maximum principle, second-derivative form.** At an interior local maximum of a `C²`
function the Laplacian is nonpositive.
decls.title: Maximum principle, second-derivative form

decls.name: TauCeti.laplacian_nonneg_of_isLocalMin
decls.doc:
**Minimum principle, second-derivative form.** At an interior local minimum of a `C²`
function the Laplacian is nonnegative.
decls.title: Minimum principle, second-derivative form

decls.name: TauCeti.not_isLocalMax_of_laplacian_pos
decls.doc:
A strictly subharmonic `C²` function (`0 < Δ f x`) has no interior local maximum at `x`. This
is the classical opening move of the maximum principle.

decls.name: TauCeti.not_isLocalMin_of_laplacian_neg
decls.doc: A strictly superharmonic `C²` function (`Δ f x < 0`) has no interior local minimum at `x`.

decls.name: TauCeti.le_of_mul_le_laplacian_add_fderiv_le_frontier
decls.doc:
**Weak maximum principle for `-Δ - b·∇ + c`.**

If `c` is nonnegative, `b` has norm at most `β` on the interior of a compact set, and
`c x * f x ≤ Δ f x + fderiv ℝ f x (b x)`, then every nonnegative frontier bound for `f` is a
bound on the whole set.
decls.title: Weak maximum principle for `-Δ - b·∇ + c`
decls.statement:
theorem le_of_mul_le_laplacian_add_fderiv_le_frontier {K : Set E} (hK : IsCompact K)
    {c f : E → ℝ} {b : E → E} {β m : ℝ} (hm : 0 ≤ m) (hcont : ContinuousOn f K)
    (hcd : ∀ ⦃x⦄, x ∈ interior K → ContDiffAt ℝ 2 f x)
    (hc : ∀ ⦃x⦄, x ∈ interior K → 0 ≤ c x)
    (hb : ∀ ⦃x⦄, x ∈ interior K → ‖b x‖ ≤ β)
    (hsub : ∀ ⦃x⦄, x ∈ interior K → c x * f x ≤ Δ f x + fderiv ℝ f x (b x))
    (hbdry : ∀ ⦃x⦄, x ∈ frontier K → f x ≤ m) :
    ∀ ⦃x⦄, x ∈ K → f x ≤ m

decls.name: TauCeti.ge_of_laplacian_add_fderiv_le_mul_ge_frontier
decls.doc:
**Weak minimum principle for `-Δ - b·∇ + c`.** This is the negation-dual of
`le_of_mul_le_laplacian_add_fderiv_le_frontier`.
decls.title: Weak minimum principle for `-Δ - b·∇ + c`
decls.statement:
theorem ge_of_laplacian_add_fderiv_le_mul_ge_frontier {K : Set E} (hK : IsCompact K)
    {c f : E → ℝ} {b : E → E} {β m : ℝ} (hm : m ≤ 0) (hcont : ContinuousOn f K)
    (hcd : ∀ ⦃x⦄, x ∈ interior K → ContDiffAt ℝ 2 f x)
    (hc : ∀ ⦃x⦄, x ∈ interior K → 0 ≤ c x)
    (hb : ∀ ⦃x⦄, x ∈ interior K → ‖b x‖ ≤ β)
    (hsuper : ∀ ⦃x⦄, x ∈ interior K →
      Δ f x + fderiv ℝ f x (b x) ≤ c x * f x)
    (hbdry : ∀ ⦃x⦄, x ∈ frontier K → m ≤ f x) :
    ∀ ⦃x⦄, x ∈ K → m ≤ f x

decls.name: TauCeti.abs_le_of_laplacian_add_fderiv_eq_mul_abs_le_frontier
decls.doc:
A solution of `-Δ f - b·∇f + c f = 0` is bounded in absolute value by every
nonnegative bound for its absolute value on the frontier.
decls.statement:
theorem abs_le_of_laplacian_add_fderiv_eq_mul_abs_le_frontier {K : Set E} (hK : IsCompact K)
    {c f : E → ℝ} {b : E → E} {β M : ℝ} (hM : 0 ≤ M) (hcont : ContinuousOn f K)
    (hcd : ∀ ⦃x⦄, x ∈ interior K → ContDiffAt ℝ 2 f x)
    (hc : ∀ ⦃x⦄, x ∈ interior K → 0 ≤ c x)
    (hb : ∀ ⦃x⦄, x ∈ interior K → ‖b x‖ ≤ β)
    (hsol : ∀ ⦃x⦄, x ∈ interior K →
      Δ f x + fderiv ℝ f x (b x) = c x * f x)
    (hbdry : ∀ ⦃x⦄, x ∈ frontier K → |f x| ≤ M) :
    ∀ ⦃x⦄, x ∈ K → |f x| ≤ M

decls.name: TauCeti.le_of_laplacian_add_fderiv_sub_mul_le_laplacian_add_fderiv_sub_mul_of_le_frontier
decls.doc:
**Comparison principle for `-Δ - b·∇ + c`.** Functions acted on by the same lower-order
coefficients are ordered on a compact set when their operator values and frontier values are
ordered.
decls.title: Comparison principle for `-Δ - b·∇ + c`
decls.statement:
theorem le_of_laplacian_add_fderiv_sub_mul_le_laplacian_add_fderiv_sub_mul_of_le_frontier
    {K : Set E} (hK : IsCompact K) {c f g : E → ℝ}
    {b : E → E} {β : ℝ} (hfcont : ContinuousOn f K) (hgcont : ContinuousOn g K)
    (hfcd : ∀ ⦃x⦄, x ∈ interior K → ContDiffAt ℝ 2 f x)
    (hgcd : ∀ ⦃x⦄, x ∈ interior K → ContDiffAt ℝ 2 g x)
    (hc : ∀ ⦃x⦄, x ∈ interior K → 0 ≤ c x)
    (hb : ∀ ⦃x⦄, x ∈ interior K → ‖b x‖ ≤ β)
    (hL : ∀ ⦃x⦄, x ∈ interior K →
      Δ g x + fderiv ℝ g x (b x) - c x * g x ≤
        Δ f x + fderiv ℝ f x (b x) - c x * f x)
    (hbdry : ∀ ⦃x⦄, x ∈ frontier K → f x ≤ g x) :
    ∀ ⦃x⦄, x ∈ K → f x ≤ g x

decls.name: TauCeti.eqOn_of_laplacian_add_fderiv_sub_mul_eq_of_eqOn_frontier
decls.doc:
**Dirichlet uniqueness for `-Δ - b·∇ + c`.** Equal operator values and equal frontier data
force two functions to agree throughout the compact set.
decls.title: Dirichlet uniqueness for `-Δ - b·∇ + c`
decls.statement:
theorem eqOn_of_laplacian_add_fderiv_sub_mul_eq_of_eqOn_frontier {K : Set E} (hK : IsCompact K)
    {c f g : E → ℝ} {b : E → E} {β : ℝ} (hfcont : ContinuousOn f K)
    (hgcont : ContinuousOn g K)
    (hfcd : ∀ ⦃x⦄, x ∈ interior K → ContDiffAt ℝ 2 f x)
    (hgcd : ∀ ⦃x⦄, x ∈ interior K → ContDiffAt ℝ 2 g x)
    (hc : ∀ ⦃x⦄, x ∈ interior K → 0 ≤ c x)
    (hb : ∀ ⦃x⦄, x ∈ interior K → ‖b x‖ ≤ β)
    (hL : ∀ ⦃x⦄, x ∈ interior K →
      Δ f x + fderiv ℝ f x (b x) - c x * f x =
        Δ g x + fderiv ℝ g x (b x) - c x * g x)
    (hbdry : Set.EqOn f g (frontier K)) : Set.EqOn f g K

decls.name: TauCeti.exists_mem_frontier_isMaxOn_of_forall_mem_interior_not_isLocalMax
decls.doc:
If every interior point of a compact set is forbidden from being a local maximum, then a
continuous function on the compact set has a maximum point on the frontier.

decls.name: TauCeti.exists_mem_frontier_isMinOn_of_forall_mem_interior_not_isLocalMin
decls.doc:
If every interior point of a compact set is forbidden from being a local minimum, then a
continuous function on the compact set has a minimum point on the frontier.

decls.name: TauCeti.exists_mem_frontier_isMaxOn_of_laplacian_pos
decls.doc:
**Boundary maximum principle for strictly subharmonic functions.**

Let `K` be compact and nonempty. If `f` is continuous on `K`, is `C²` at every interior point,
and satisfies `0 < Δ f x` throughout `interior K`, then some maximum point of `f` on `K` lies on
`frontier K`.
decls.title: Boundary maximum principle for strictly subharmonic functions
decls.statement:
theorem exists_mem_frontier_isMaxOn_of_laplacian_pos {K : Set E} (hK : IsCompact K)
    (hne : K.Nonempty) {f : E → ℝ} (hcont : ContinuousOn f K)
    (hcd : ∀ ⦃x⦄, x ∈ interior K → ContDiffAt ℝ 2 f x)
    (hlap : ∀ ⦃x⦄, x ∈ interior K → 0 < Δ f x) :
    ∃ x ∈ frontier K, IsMaxOn f K x

decls.name: TauCeti.exists_mem_frontier_isMinOn_of_laplacian_neg
decls.doc:
**Boundary minimum principle for strictly superharmonic functions.**

Let `K` be compact and nonempty. If `f` is continuous on `K`, is `C²` at every interior point,
and satisfies `Δ f x < 0` throughout `interior K`, then some minimum point of `f` on `K` lies on
`frontier K`.
decls.title: Boundary minimum principle for strictly superharmonic functions
decls.statement:
theorem exists_mem_frontier_isMinOn_of_laplacian_neg {K : Set E} (hK : IsCompact K)
    (hne : K.Nonempty) {f : E → ℝ} (hcont : ContinuousOn f K)
    (hcd : ∀ ⦃x⦄, x ∈ interior K → ContDiffAt ℝ 2 f x)
    (hlap : ∀ ⦃x⦄, x ∈ interior K → Δ f x < 0) :
    ∃ x ∈ frontier K, IsMinOn f K x

decls.name: TauCeti.le_of_forall_pos_mul_le
decls.doc:
The `ε → 0` limit of a perturbation estimate: if `a ≤ m + ε * C` for every `ε > 0`, with a
nonnegative constant `C`, then `a ≤ m`. This packages the endgame of the perturbation arguments in
the weak maximum principles.
decls.statement:
theorem le_of_forall_pos_mul_le {a m C : ℝ} (hC : 0 ≤ C) (h : ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → a ≤ m + ε * C) :
    a ≤ m

decls.name: TauCeti.exists_mem_frontier_isMaxOn_of_le_frontier
decls.doc:
If every upper bound for a continuous function on the frontier of a nonempty compact set is
also an upper bound on the whole set, then the function attains a maximum on the frontier.
decls.statement:
theorem exists_mem_frontier_isMaxOn_of_le_frontier {K : Set E} (hK : IsCompact K)
    [Nontrivial E] (hne : K.Nonempty) {f : E → ℝ} (hcont : ContinuousOn f K)
    (hbound : ∀ {m : ℝ}, (∀ ⦃x⦄, x ∈ frontier K → f x ≤ m) →
      ∀ ⦃x⦄, x ∈ K → f x ≤ m) :
    ∃ x ∈ frontier K, IsMaxOn f K x

decls.name: TauCeti.laplacian_add_const_smul_norm_sq
decls.doc:
The Laplacian of the perturbation `f + ε‖·‖²` at a point where `f` is `C²`: it exceeds `Δ f` by
the contribution `ε * (2 * dim E)` of the strictly convex term `ε‖·‖²`. This is the computation the
bare-Laplacian and the `-Δ + c` weak maximum principles both run on the perturbed function.
decls.statement:
theorem laplacian_add_const_smul_norm_sq {f : E → ℝ} {x : E} (ε : ℝ) (hf : ContDiffAt ℝ 2 f x) :
    Δ (fun y : E => f y + ε • ‖y‖ ^ 2) x = Δ f x + ε * (2 * (Module.finrank ℝ E : ℝ))

decls.name: TauCeti.le_of_forall_pos_exists_isMaxOn_perturbation
decls.doc:
**The `ε → 0` perturbation engine of the weak maximum principles.** To bound `f x ≤ m` on a
bounded set `K`, it suffices to produce, for every `ε > 0`, a point `z ∈ K` at which the
perturbation `f + ε‖·‖²` attains its maximum over `K` and where `f z ≤ m`: bounding `‖·‖²` by a
constant on the bounded `K` and letting `ε → 0` then gives `f x ≤ m`. The bare-Laplacian and
`-Δ + c` weak maximum principles differ only in how they produce such a maximizer, so this lemma
packages everything they share.
decls.title: The `ε → 0` perturbation engine of the weak maximum principles
decls.statement:
theorem le_of_forall_pos_exists_isMaxOn_perturbation {K : Set E} (hK : Bornology.IsBounded K)
    {f : E → ℝ} {m : ℝ} {x : E} (hxK : x ∈ K)
    (H : ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ∃ z ∈ K, IsMaxOn (fun y : E => f y + ε • ‖y‖ ^ 2) K z ∧ f z ≤ m) :
    f x ≤ m

decls.name: TauCeti.le_of_laplacian_nonneg_le_frontier
decls.doc:
**Weak maximum principle for subharmonic functions.**

Let `K` be compact. If `f` is continuous on `K`, is `C²` on `interior K`, and is subharmonic
there (`0 ≤ Δ f`), then any bound `m` that `f` respects on `frontier K` bounds `f` on all of `K`.
decls.title: Weak maximum principle for subharmonic functions
decls.statement:
theorem le_of_laplacian_nonneg_le_frontier {K : Set E} (hK : IsCompact K) {f : E → ℝ} {m : ℝ}
    (hcont : ContinuousOn f K) (hcd : ∀ ⦃x⦄, x ∈ interior K → ContDiffAt ℝ 2 f x)
    (hlap : ∀ ⦃x⦄, x ∈ interior K → 0 ≤ Δ f x) (hbdry : ∀ ⦃x⦄, x ∈ frontier K → f x ≤ m) :
    ∀ ⦃x⦄, x ∈ K → f x ≤ m

decls.name: TauCeti.ge_of_laplacian_nonpos_ge_frontier
decls.doc:
**Weak minimum principle for superharmonic functions.**

The dual of `le_of_laplacian_nonneg_le_frontier`: a continuous, `C²`, superharmonic (`Δ f ≤ 0`)
function on a compact set is bounded below on `K` by any lower bound it respects on `frontier K`.
decls.title: Weak minimum principle for superharmonic functions
decls.statement:
theorem ge_of_laplacian_nonpos_ge_frontier {K : Set E} (hK : IsCompact K) {f : E → ℝ} {m : ℝ}
    (hcont : ContinuousOn f K) (hcd : ∀ ⦃x⦄, x ∈ interior K → ContDiffAt ℝ 2 f x)
    (hlap : ∀ ⦃x⦄, x ∈ interior K → Δ f x ≤ 0) (hbdry : ∀ ⦃x⦄, x ∈ frontier K → m ≤ f x) :
    ∀ ⦃x⦄, x ∈ K → m ≤ f x

decls.name: TauCeti.exists_mem_frontier_isMaxOn_of_laplacian_nonneg
decls.doc:
A subharmonic (`0 ≤ Δ f`) continuous function on a nonempty compact set in a nontrivial
finite-dimensional real inner product space attains a maximum on the frontier. This is the
`∃`-form of the weak maximum principle, mirroring
`exists_mem_frontier_isMaxOn_of_laplacian_pos` for the strict case.
decls.statement:
theorem exists_mem_frontier_isMaxOn_of_laplacian_nonneg {K : Set E} (hK : IsCompact K)
    (hne : K.Nonempty) {f : E → ℝ} (hcont : ContinuousOn f K)
    (hcd : ∀ ⦃x⦄, x ∈ interior K → ContDiffAt ℝ 2 f x)
    (hlap : ∀ ⦃x⦄, x ∈ interior K → 0 ≤ Δ f x) :
    ∃ x ∈ frontier K, IsMaxOn f K x

decls.name: TauCeti.exists_mem_frontier_isMinOn_of_laplacian_nonpos
decls.doc:
A superharmonic (`Δ f ≤ 0`) continuous function on a nonempty compact set in a nontrivial
finite-dimensional real inner product space attains a minimum on the frontier.
decls.statement:
theorem exists_mem_frontier_isMinOn_of_laplacian_nonpos {K : Set E} (hK : IsCompact K)
    (hne : K.Nonempty) {f : E → ℝ} (hcont : ContinuousOn f K)
    (hcd : ∀ ⦃x⦄, x ∈ interior K → ContDiffAt ℝ 2 f x)
    (hlap : ∀ ⦃x⦄, x ∈ interior K → Δ f x ≤ 0) :
    ∃ x ∈ frontier K, IsMinOn f K x

decls.name: TauCeti.le_of_mul_le_laplacian_le_frontier
decls.doc:
**Weak maximum principle for the operator `-Δ + c` with `c ≥ 0`.**

Let `K` be compact. If `f` is continuous on `K`, is `C²` on `interior K`, and is a subsolution of
`-Δ + c` there (`c x * f x ≤ Δ f x`) with a nonnegative coefficient (`0 ≤ c x`), then any
**nonnegative** bound `m` that `f` respects on `frontier K` bounds `f` on all of `K`.

The nonnegativity of `m` cannot be dropped once `c ≠ 0`; it encodes the `sup u ≤ sup_{∂} u⁺` shape
of the estimate.
decls.title: Weak maximum principle for the operator `-Δ + c` with `c ≥ 0`
decls.statement:
theorem le_of_mul_le_laplacian_le_frontier {K : Set E} (hK : IsCompact K) {c f : E → ℝ} {m : ℝ}
    (hm : 0 ≤ m) (hcont : ContinuousOn f K) (hcd : ∀ ⦃x⦄, x ∈ interior K → ContDiffAt ℝ 2 f x)
    (hc : ∀ ⦃x⦄, x ∈ interior K → 0 ≤ c x)
    (hsub : ∀ ⦃x⦄, x ∈ interior K → c x * f x ≤ Δ f x)
    (hbdry : ∀ ⦃x⦄, x ∈ frontier K → f x ≤ m) :
    ∀ ⦃x⦄, x ∈ K → f x ≤ m

decls.name: TauCeti.le_of_mul_le_laplacian_le_of_le_frontier
decls.doc:
**Comparison principle for `-Δ + c` with `c ≥ 0`.**
