decls.name: TauCeti.PDE.energyIntegrand_zero_drift_transpose_apply
decls.doc: With zero drift, transposing the principal coefficient swaps the two jet arguments.
decls.statement:
lemma energyIntegrand_zero_drift_transpose_apply (A : Matrix n n ℝ) (c : ℝ)
    (U V : ℝ × EuclideanSpace ℝ n) :
    energyIntegrand Aᵀ 0 c U V = energyIntegrand A 0 c V U

decls.name: TauCeti.PDE.energyIntegrand_zero_drift_comm_of_isSymm
decls.doc: A symmetric principal coefficient gives a symmetric zero-drift jet form.
decls.statement:
lemma energyIntegrand_zero_drift_comm_of_isSymm {A : Matrix n n ℝ} (hA : A.IsSymm)
    (c : ℝ) (U V : ℝ × EuclideanSpace ℝ n) :
    energyIntegrand A 0 c U V = energyIntegrand A 0 c V U

decls.name: TauCeti.PDE.energyIntegrand_zero_drift_flip_eq_of_isSymm
decls.doc:
Bundled-map form of symmetry for the zero-drift jet integrand.

Downstream energy forms that need the same integrand to be both symmetric and bounded below
pair this with `min_lam_mass_mul_norm_sq_le_energyIntegrand_zero_drift_self`.  For a
nonsymmetric principal coefficient, first pass to `coefficientSymmetricPart` using the uniform
ellipticity API in `TauCeti.Analysis.PDE.Uniform.Ellipticity`, then apply this lemma to the
symmetric coefficient field.
decls.statement:
lemma energyIntegrand_zero_drift_flip_eq_of_isSymm {A : Matrix n n ℝ} (hA : A.IsSymm)
    (c : ℝ) :
    (energyIntegrand A 0 c).flip = energyIntegrand A 0 c

decls.name: TauCeti.PDE.energyIntegrand_coefficientSymmetricPart_zero_drift_apply
decls.doc:
The symmetric part's zero-drift jet form is the average of the original form and its
transpose.
decls.statement:
lemma energyIntegrand_coefficientSymmetricPart_zero_drift_apply (A : Matrix n n ℝ)
    (c : ℝ) (U V : ℝ × EuclideanSpace ℝ n) :
    energyIntegrand (coefficientSymmetricPart A) 0 c U V =
      (energyIntegrand A 0 c U V + energyIntegrand A 0 c V U) / 2

decls.name: TauCeti.PDE.energyIntegrand_coefficientSymmetricPart_self
decls.doc:
Replacing the principal coefficient by its symmetric part does not change the diagonal
energy density.
decls.statement:
lemma energyIntegrand_coefficientSymmetricPart_self (A : Matrix n n ℝ)
    (b : EuclideanSpace ℝ n) (c : ℝ) (U : ℝ × EuclideanSpace ℝ n) :
    energyIntegrand (coefficientSymmetricPart A) b c U U =
      energyIntegrand A b c U U

decls.name: TauCeti.PDE.energyIntegrand_coefficientSymmetricPart_zero_drift_flip_eq
decls.doc: Bundled-map form of symmetry for the symmetric-part zero-drift jet integrand.
decls.statement:
lemma energyIntegrand_coefficientSymmetricPart_zero_drift_flip_eq (A : Matrix n n ℝ)
    (c : ℝ) :
    (energyIntegrand (coefficientSymmetricPart A) 0 c).flip =
      energyIntegrand (coefficientSymmetricPart A) 0 c

decls.name: TauCeti.PDE.energyIntegrand_zero_drift_comm_on
decls.doc:
A pointwise symmetric coefficient field gives symmetric zero-drift jet forms at every
point of the domain.
decls.statement:
lemma energyIntegrand_zero_drift_comm_on {Ω : Set X} {a : X → Matrix n n ℝ}
    (ha : ∀ ⦃x⦄, x ∈ Ω → (a x).IsSymm) {x : X} (hx : x ∈ Ω) (c : X → ℝ)
    (U V : ℝ × EuclideanSpace ℝ n) :
    energyIntegrand (a x) 0 (c x) U V = energyIntegrand (a x) 0 (c x) V U

decls.name: TauCeti.PDE.energyIntegrand_zero_drift_flip_eq_on
decls.doc:
A pointwise symmetric coefficient field gives a bundled symmetric zero-drift jet form at
each point of the domain.

decls.name: TauCeti.PDE.energyIntegrand_one_zero_mass_flip_eq
decls.doc: Bundled symmetry of the shifted Laplacian jet form.
decls.statement:
lemma energyIntegrand_one_zero_mass_flip_eq (c : ℝ) :
    (energyIntegrand (1 : Matrix n n ℝ) 0 c).flip =

decls.name: TauCeti.PDE.UniformlyEllipticOn.norm_energyIntegrand_apply_le
decls.doc:
Pointwise boundedness of the energy integrand from uniform ellipticity of the principal
coefficient and pointwise bounds on the drift and mass coefficients.
decls.statement:
lemma norm_energyIntegrand_apply_le (h : UniformlyEllipticOn Ω a lam Lam)
    {x : X} (hx : x ∈ Ω) {b₀ : EuclideanSpace ℝ n} {c₀ : ℝ}
    (hb : ‖b₀‖ ≤ beta) (hc : ‖c₀‖ ≤ gamma)
    (U V : ℝ × EuclideanSpace ℝ n) :
    ‖energyIntegrand (a x) b₀ c₀ U V‖ ≤ (Lam + beta + gamma) * ‖U‖ * ‖V‖

decls.name: TauCeti.PDE.UniformlyEllipticOn.opNorm_energyIntegrand_le
decls.doc:
Operator-norm boundedness of the energy integrand from uniform ellipticity of the
principal coefficient and pointwise bounds on the drift and mass coefficients.
decls.statement:
lemma opNorm_energyIntegrand_le (h : UniformlyEllipticOn Ω a lam Lam)
    {x : X} (hx : x ∈ Ω) {b₀ : EuclideanSpace ℝ n} {c₀ : ℝ}
    (hb : ‖b₀‖ ≤ beta) (hc : ‖c₀‖ ≤ gamma) :
    ‖energyIntegrand (a x) b₀ c₀‖ ≤ Lam + beta + gamma

decls.name: TauCeti.PDE.UniformlyEllipticOn.garding_energyIntegrand_self
decls.doc:
Pointwise Gårding inequality for a uniformly elliptic principal coefficient.

With nonnegative mass coefficient and drift bound `β`, the diagonal energy density is bounded
below by `(λ/2)‖∇u‖² - (β²/2λ)|u|²`.
decls.statement:
lemma garding_energyIntegrand_self (h : UniformlyEllipticOn Ω a lam Lam)
    {x : X} (hx : x ∈ Ω) {b₀ : EuclideanSpace ℝ n} {c₀ : ℝ}
    (hb : ‖b₀‖ ≤ beta) (hc : 0 ≤ c₀)
    (U : ℝ × EuclideanSpace ℝ n) :
    lam / 2 * ‖U.2‖ ^ 2 - beta ^ 2 / (2 * lam) * U.1 ^ 2
      ≤ energyIntegrand (a x) b₀ c₀ U U

decls.name: TauCeti.PDE.UniformlyEllipticOn.garding_energyIntegrand_self_of_mass_lower_bound
decls.doc:
Pointwise Gårding lower bound with a mass floor for a uniformly elliptic principal
coefficient.

With drift bound `β` and mass lower bound `μ`, the diagonal energy density is bounded below
by `(λ / 2)‖∇u‖² + (μ - β² / (2λ))u²`.
decls.statement:
lemma garding_energyIntegrand_self_of_mass_lower_bound (h : UniformlyEllipticOn Ω a lam Lam)
    {x : X} (hx : x ∈ Ω) {b₀ : EuclideanSpace ℝ n} {c₀ : ℝ}
    (hb : ‖b₀‖ ≤ beta) (hc : mu ≤ c₀) (U : ℝ × EuclideanSpace ℝ n) :
    lam / 2 * ‖U.2‖ ^ 2 + (mu - beta ^ 2 / (2 * lam)) * U.1 ^ 2
      ≤ energyIntegrand (a x) b₀ c₀ U U

decls.name: TauCeti.PDE.UniformlyEllipticOn.min_diagonal_lower_bound_mul_norm_sq_le_energyIntegrand_self
decls.doc:
The lower-bound estimate implies the explicit diagonal estimate with constant
`min (λ / 2) (μ - β² / (2λ))`, assuming this second coefficient is nonnegative.
decls.statement:
lemma min_diagonal_lower_bound_mul_norm_sq_le_energyIntegrand_self
    (h : UniformlyEllipticOn Ω a lam Lam)
    {x : X} (hx : x ∈ Ω) {b₀ : EuclideanSpace ℝ n} {c₀ : ℝ}
    (hb : ‖b₀‖ ≤ beta) (hc : mu ≤ c₀) (hmu : beta ^ 2 / (2 * lam) ≤ mu)
    (U : ℝ × EuclideanSpace ℝ n) :
    min (lam / 2) (mu - beta ^ 2 / (2 * lam)) * ‖U‖ ^ 2
      ≤ energyIntegrand (a x) b₀ c₀ U U

decls.name: TauCeti.PDE.UniformlyEllipticOn.min_lam_mass_mul_norm_sq_le_energyIntegrand_zero_drift_self
decls.doc:
Zero-drift diagonal lower bound for a uniformly elliptic principal coefficient and a
nonnegative mass coefficient.
decls.statement:
lemma min_lam_mass_mul_norm_sq_le_energyIntegrand_zero_drift_self
    (h : UniformlyEllipticOn Ω a lam Lam)
    {x : X} (hx : x ∈ Ω) {c₀ : ℝ} (hc : 0 ≤ c₀)
    (U : ℝ × EuclideanSpace ℝ n) :
    min lam c₀ * ‖U‖ ^ 2 ≤ energyIntegrand (a x) 0 c₀ U U

decls.name: TauCeti.PDE.toQuadraticForm'_eq_dotProduct
decls.doc: Mathlib's matrix quadratic form is the dot-product expression `ξᵀ A ξ`.
decls.statement:
lemma toQuadraticForm'_eq_dotProduct (A : Matrix n n ℝ) (ξ : EuclideanSpace ℝ n) :
    A.toQuadraticForm' ξ = ξ ⬝ᵥ (A *ᵥ ξ)

decls.name: TauCeti.PDE.toQuadraticForm'_one
decls.doc: The identity matrix has quadratic form `‖ξ‖²`.
decls.statement:
lemma toQuadraticForm'_one (ξ : EuclideanSpace ℝ n) :
    (1 : Matrix n n ℝ).toQuadraticForm' ξ = ‖ξ‖ ^ 2

decls.name: TauCeti.PDE.matrixBilinearForm
decls.doc:
The continuous bilinear form attached to a real matrix on Euclidean space.

For a coefficient matrix `A`, this is the pointwise weak-form integrand
`(η, ξ) ↦ ηᵀ A ξ`. It is bundled as a continuous bilinear map so it can feed directly into
Mathlib's bounded-bilinear-form and Lax--Milgram APIs once the corresponding Sobolev spaces
are available.
decls.statement:
def matrixBilinearForm (A : Matrix n n ℝ) :
    EuclideanSpace ℝ n →L[ℝ] EuclideanSpace ℝ n →L[ℝ] ℝ

decls.name: TauCeti.PDE.matrixBilinearForm_apply
decls.doc: The matrix bilinear form is the dot-product expression `ηᵀ A ξ`.
decls.statement:
lemma matrixBilinearForm_apply (A : Matrix n n ℝ) (η ξ : EuclideanSpace ℝ n) :
    matrixBilinearForm A η ξ = η ⬝ᵥ (A *ᵥ ξ)

decls.name: TauCeti.PDE.matrixBilinearForm_one_apply
decls.doc: The matrix bilinear form associated to the identity matrix is the Euclidean dot product.
decls.statement:
lemma matrixBilinearForm_one_apply (η ξ : EuclideanSpace ℝ n) :
    matrixBilinearForm (1 : Matrix n n ℝ) η ξ = η ⬝ᵥ ξ

decls.name: TauCeti.PDE.toQuadraticForm'_smul
decls.doc: Matrix quadratic forms are linear in scalar multiplication of the coefficient matrix.
decls.statement:
lemma toQuadraticForm'_smul (c : ℝ) (A : Matrix n n ℝ) (ξ : EuclideanSpace ℝ n) :
    (c • A).toQuadraticForm' ξ = c * A.toQuadraticForm' ξ

decls.name: TauCeti.PDE.toQuadraticForm'_smul_one
decls.doc: The scalar identity matrix has quadratic form `c ‖ξ‖²`.
decls.statement:
lemma toQuadraticForm'_smul_one (c : ℝ) (ξ : EuclideanSpace ℝ n) :
    (c • (1 : Matrix n n ℝ)).toQuadraticForm' ξ = c * ‖ξ‖ ^ 2

decls.name: TauCeti.PDE.toQuadraticForm'_add
decls.doc: Matrix quadratic forms are additive in the coefficient matrix.
decls.statement:
lemma toQuadraticForm'_add (A B : Matrix n n ℝ) (ξ : EuclideanSpace ℝ n) :
    (A + B).toQuadraticForm' ξ = A.toQuadraticForm' ξ + B.toQuadraticForm' ξ

decls.name: TauCeti.PDE.matrixBilinearForm_smul_apply
decls.doc: Matrix bilinear forms are linear in scalar multiplication of the coefficient matrix.
decls.statement:
lemma matrixBilinearForm_smul_apply (c : ℝ) (A : Matrix n n ℝ)
    (η ξ : EuclideanSpace ℝ n) :
    matrixBilinearForm (c • A) η ξ = c * matrixBilinearForm A η ξ

decls.name: TauCeti.PDE.matrixBilinearForm_add_apply
decls.doc: Matrix bilinear forms are additive in the coefficient matrix.
decls.statement:
lemma matrixBilinearForm_add_apply (A B : Matrix n n ℝ) (η ξ : EuclideanSpace ℝ n) :
    matrixBilinearForm (A + B) η ξ = matrixBilinearForm A η ξ + matrixBilinearForm B η ξ

decls.name: TauCeti.PDE.toQuadraticForm'_transpose
decls.doc: Transposing the coefficient matrix does not change its quadratic form.
decls.statement:
lemma toQuadraticForm'_transpose (A : Matrix n n ℝ) (ξ : EuclideanSpace ℝ n) :
    Aᵀ.toQuadraticForm' ξ = A.toQuadraticForm' ξ

decls.name: TauCeti.PDE.matrixBilinearForm_transpose_apply
decls.doc:
Transposing the coefficient matrix swaps the arguments of the bundled matrix bilinear
form.
decls.statement:
lemma matrixBilinearForm_transpose_apply (A : Matrix n n ℝ) (η ξ : EuclideanSpace ℝ n) :
    matrixBilinearForm Aᵀ η ξ = matrixBilinearForm A ξ η

decls.name: TauCeti.PDE.matrixBilinearForm_smul_one_apply
decls.doc: The matrix bilinear form associated to `c • 1` is `c` times the Euclidean dot product.
decls.statement:
lemma matrixBilinearForm_smul_one_apply (c : ℝ) (η ξ : EuclideanSpace ℝ n) :
    matrixBilinearForm (c • (1 : Matrix n n ℝ)) η ξ = c * (η ⬝ᵥ ξ)

decls.name: TauCeti.PDE.matrixBilinearForm_self
decls.doc: The quadratic part of the matrix bilinear form is the matrix quadratic form.
decls.statement:
lemma matrixBilinearForm_self (A : Matrix n n ℝ) (ξ : EuclideanSpace ℝ n) :
    matrixBilinearForm A ξ ξ = A.toQuadraticForm' ξ

decls.name: TauCeti.PDE.matrixBilinearFormLinear
decls.doc: The principal coefficient matrix-to-bilinear-form map as a continuous linear map.
decls.statement:
def matrixBilinearFormLinear :
    Matrix n n ℝ →L[ℝ] EuclideanSpace ℝ n →L[ℝ] EuclideanSpace ℝ n →L[ℝ] ℝ

decls.name: TauCeti.PDE.matrixBilinearFormLinear_apply
decls.doc: Applying `matrixBilinearFormLinear` recovers `matrixBilinearForm`.
decls.statement:
lemma matrixBilinearFormLinear_apply (A : Matrix n n ℝ) :
    matrixBilinearFormLinear (n := n) A = matrixBilinearForm A

decls.name: TauCeti.PDE.continuous_matrixBilinearForm
decls.doc: The principal coefficient-to-bilinear-form map is continuous.
decls.statement:
lemma continuous_matrixBilinearForm :
    Continuous (fun A : Matrix n n ℝ => matrixBilinearForm A)

decls.name: TauCeti.PDE.Continuous.matrixBilinearForm
decls.doc:
A continuous principal coefficient field gives a continuous field of principal bilinear
forms.
decls.statement:
lemma matrixBilinearForm {a : X → Matrix n n ℝ} (ha : Continuous a) :
    Continuous (fun x => PDE.matrixBilinearForm (a x))

decls.name: TauCeti.PDE.ContinuousOn.matrixBilinearForm
decls.doc:
A continuous principal coefficient field on a set gives a continuous field of principal
bilinear forms on that set.
decls.statement:
lemma matrixBilinearForm {s : Set X} {a : X → Matrix n n ℝ} (ha : ContinuousOn a s) :
    ContinuousOn (fun x => PDE.matrixBilinearForm (a x)) s

decls.name: TauCeti.PDE.coefficientSymmetricPart
decls.doc:
The symmetric part `(A + Aᵀ) / 2` of a coefficient matrix.

For energy estimates the diagonal quadratic form of `A` agrees with that of
`coefficientSymmetricPart A`, while the resulting matrix is symmetric. This is the
finite-dimensional bookkeeping needed before the integrated energy form is specialized to
self-adjoint elliptic operators.
decls.statement: def coefficientSymmetricPart (A : Matrix n n ℝ) : Matrix n n ℝ

decls.name: TauCeti.PDE.coefficientSymmetricPart_isSymm
decls.doc: The symmetric part of a coefficient matrix is symmetric.
decls.statement:
lemma coefficientSymmetricPart_isSymm (A : Matrix n n ℝ) :
    (coefficientSymmetricPart A).IsSymm

decls.name: TauCeti.PDE.coefficientSymmetricPart_apply
decls.doc: The entries of the symmetric part are the averages of opposite entries.
decls.statement:
lemma coefficientSymmetricPart_apply (A : Matrix n n ℝ) (i j : n) :
    coefficientSymmetricPart A i j = (A i j + A j i) / 2

decls.name: TauCeti.PDE.coefficientSymmetricPart_eq_self_of_isSymm
decls.doc: A symmetric coefficient matrix is unchanged by taking its symmetric part.
decls.statement:
lemma coefficientSymmetricPart_eq_self_of_isSymm {A : Matrix n n ℝ} (hA : A.IsSymm) :
    coefficientSymmetricPart A = A

decls.name: TauCeti.PDE.toQuadraticForm'_coefficientSymmetricPart
decls.doc: The symmetric part has the same quadratic form as the original coefficient matrix.
decls.statement:
lemma toQuadraticForm'_coefficientSymmetricPart (A : Matrix n n ℝ)
    (ξ : EuclideanSpace ℝ n) :
    (coefficientSymmetricPart A).toQuadraticForm' ξ = A.toQuadraticForm' ξ

decls.name: TauCeti.PDE.matrixBilinearForm_coefficientSymmetricPart_apply
decls.doc:
The bundled bilinear form of the symmetric part is the average of the original bilinear
form and its transpose.
decls.statement:
lemma matrixBilinearForm_coefficientSymmetricPart_apply (A : Matrix n n ℝ)
    (η ξ : EuclideanSpace ℝ n) :
    matrixBilinearForm (coefficientSymmetricPart A) η ξ =
      (matrixBilinearForm A η ξ + matrixBilinearForm A ξ η) / 2

decls.name: TauCeti.PDE.norm_matrixBilinearForm_le_of_upper_bound
decls.doc:
A pointwise bilinear upper bound gives the corresponding norm estimate for the bundled
continuous bilinear form.
decls.statement:
lemma norm_matrixBilinearForm_le_of_upper_bound (A : Matrix n n ℝ) {Lam : ℝ}
    (hA : ∀ η ξ : EuclideanSpace ℝ n, |η ⬝ᵥ (A *ᵥ ξ)| ≤ Lam * ‖η‖ * ‖ξ‖)
    (η ξ : EuclideanSpace ℝ n) :
    ‖matrixBilinearForm A η ξ‖ ≤ Lam * ‖η‖ * ‖ξ‖

decls.name: TauCeti.PDE.matrixBilinearForm_opNorm_le_of_upper_bound
decls.doc:
A pointwise bilinear upper bound controls the operator norm of the bundled matrix
bilinear form.

This is the matrix-coefficient specialization of Mathlib's
`ContinuousLinearMap.opNorm_le_bound₂`.
decls.statement:
lemma matrixBilinearForm_opNorm_le_of_upper_bound (A : Matrix n n ℝ) {Lam : ℝ}
    (hLam_nonneg : 0 ≤ Lam)
    (hA : ∀ η ξ : EuclideanSpace ℝ n, |η ⬝ᵥ (A *ᵥ ξ)| ≤ Lam * ‖η‖ * ‖ξ‖) :
    ‖matrixBilinearForm A‖ ≤ Lam

decls.name: TauCeti.PDE.matrixBilinearForm_apply_norm_le_of_upper_bound
decls.doc:
A pointwise bilinear upper bound gives a radius-restricted estimate for the bundled
matrix bilinear form.
decls.statement:
lemma matrixBilinearForm_apply_norm_le_of_upper_bound {A : Matrix n n ℝ} {Lam R S : ℝ}
    (hLam_nonneg : 0 ≤ Lam)
    (hA : ∀ η ξ : EuclideanSpace ℝ n, |η ⬝ᵥ (A *ᵥ ξ)| ≤ Lam * ‖η‖ * ‖ξ‖)
    {η ξ : EuclideanSpace ℝ n} (hη : ‖η‖ ≤ R) (hξ : ‖ξ‖ ≤ S) :
    ‖matrixBilinearForm A η ξ‖ ≤ Lam * R * S

decls.name: TauCeti.PDE.abs_dotProduct_smul_one_mulVec_le_of_abs_le
decls.doc:
A scalar multiple of the identity has operator integrand bounded by any upper bound for
the absolute value of the scalar.
decls.statement:
lemma abs_dotProduct_smul_one_mulVec_le_of_abs_le {c Lam : ℝ} (hc : |c| ≤ Lam)
    (η ξ : EuclideanSpace ℝ n) :
    |η ⬝ᵥ ((c • (1 : Matrix n n ℝ)) *ᵥ ξ)| ≤ Lam * ‖η‖ * ‖ξ‖

decls.name: TauCeti.PDE.norm_matrixBilinearForm_smul_one_le_of_abs_le
decls.doc:
A scalar multiple of the identity has operator integrand bounded by any upper bound for
the absolute value of the scalar.
decls.statement:
lemma norm_matrixBilinearForm_smul_one_le_of_abs_le {c Lam : ℝ} (hc : |c| ≤ Lam)
    (η ξ : EuclideanSpace ℝ n) :
    ‖matrixBilinearForm (c • (1 : Matrix n n ℝ)) η ξ‖ ≤ Lam * ‖η‖ * ‖ξ‖

decls.name: TauCeti.PDE.abs_dotProduct_add_mulVec_le
decls.doc: Adding two pointwise bilinear upper bounds adds the constants.
decls.statement:
lemma abs_dotProduct_add_mulVec_le {A B : Matrix n n ℝ} {Lam Mu : ℝ}
    (hA : ∀ η ξ : EuclideanSpace ℝ n, |η ⬝ᵥ (A *ᵥ ξ)| ≤ Lam * ‖η‖ * ‖ξ‖)
    (hB : ∀ η ξ : EuclideanSpace ℝ n, |η ⬝ᵥ (B *ᵥ ξ)| ≤ Mu * ‖η‖ * ‖ξ‖)
    (η ξ : EuclideanSpace ℝ n) :
    |η ⬝ᵥ ((A + B) *ᵥ ξ)| ≤ (Lam + Mu) * ‖η‖ * ‖ξ‖

decls.name: TauCeti.PDE.abs_dotProduct_coefficientSymmetricPart_mulVec_le
decls.doc:
The symmetric part of a pointwise bounded coefficient matrix satisfies the same bilinear
upper bound.
decls.statement:
lemma abs_dotProduct_coefficientSymmetricPart_mulVec_le {A : Matrix n n ℝ} {Lam : ℝ}
    (hA : ∀ η ξ : EuclideanSpace ℝ n, |η ⬝ᵥ (A *ᵥ ξ)| ≤ Lam * ‖η‖ * ‖ξ‖)
    (η ξ : EuclideanSpace ℝ n) :
    |η ⬝ᵥ (coefficientSymmetricPart A *ᵥ ξ)| ≤ Lam * ‖η‖ * ‖ξ‖

decls.name: TauCeti.PDE.lower_bound_toQuadraticForm'_add
decls.doc: Adding a nonnegative quadratic form preserves a lower quadratic bound.
decls.statement:
lemma lower_bound_toQuadraticForm'_add {A B : Matrix n n ℝ} {lam : ℝ}
    (hA : ∀ ξ : EuclideanSpace ℝ n, lam * ‖ξ‖ ^ 2 ≤ A.toQuadraticForm' ξ)
    (hB : ∀ ξ : EuclideanSpace ℝ n, 0 ≤ B.toQuadraticForm' ξ)
    (ξ : EuclideanSpace ℝ n) :
    lam * ‖ξ‖ ^ 2 ≤ (A + B).toQuadraticForm' ξ

decls.name: TauCeti.PDE.lower_bound_toQuadraticForm'_add_of_lower_bound
decls.doc:
Adding a coefficient with a one-sided quadratic lower bound lowers a quadratic lower
bound by the size of that perturbation.
decls.statement:
lemma lower_bound_toQuadraticForm'_add_of_lower_bound {A B : Matrix n n ℝ} {lam Mu : ℝ}
    (hA : ∀ ξ : EuclideanSpace ℝ n, lam * ‖ξ‖ ^ 2 ≤ A.toQuadraticForm' ξ)
    (hB : ∀ ξ : EuclideanSpace ℝ n, -(Mu * ‖ξ‖ ^ 2) ≤ B.toQuadraticForm' ξ)
    (ξ : EuclideanSpace ℝ n) :
    (lam - Mu) * ‖ξ‖ ^ 2 ≤ (A + B).toQuadraticForm' ξ

decls.name: TauCeti.PDE.abs_toQuadraticForm'_le_of_abs_dotProduct_mulVec_le
decls.doc:
A bilinear upper bound for a coefficient matrix bounds its quadratic form in absolute
value by the same constant.
decls.statement:
lemma abs_toQuadraticForm'_le_of_abs_dotProduct_mulVec_le {B : Matrix n n ℝ} {Mu : ℝ}
    (hB : ∀ η ξ : EuclideanSpace ℝ n, |η ⬝ᵥ (B *ᵥ ξ)| ≤ Mu * ‖η‖ * ‖ξ‖)
    (ξ : EuclideanSpace ℝ n) :
    |B.toQuadraticForm' ξ| ≤ Mu * ‖ξ‖ ^ 2

decls.name: TauCeti.PDE.isCoercive_matrixBilinearForm_of_lower_bound
decls.doc:
A pointwise quadratic lower bound makes the associated matrix bilinear form coercive in
Mathlib's Lax--Milgram sense.
decls.statement:
lemma isCoercive_matrixBilinearForm_of_lower_bound (A : Matrix n n ℝ) {lam : ℝ}
    (hlam : 0 < lam)
    (hA : ∀ ξ : EuclideanSpace ℝ n, lam * ‖ξ‖ ^ 2 ≤ A.toQuadraticForm' ξ) :
    IsCoercive (matrixBilinearForm A)

decls.name: TauCeti.PDE.isCoercive_matrixBilinearForm_one
decls.doc: The identity matrix bilinear form is coercive with constant `1`.
decls.statement:
lemma isCoercive_matrixBilinearForm_one :
    IsCoercive (matrixBilinearForm (1 : Matrix n n ℝ))

decls.name: TauCeti.PDE.isCoercive_matrixBilinearForm_smul_one
decls.doc: A positive scalar multiple of the identity matrix gives a coercive bilinear form.
decls.statement:
lemma isCoercive_matrixBilinearForm_smul_one {c : ℝ} (hc : 0 < c) :
    IsCoercive (matrixBilinearForm (c • (1 : Matrix n n ℝ)))

decls.name: TauCeti.PDE.UniformlyEllipticOn
decls.doc:
Uniform ellipticity and boundedness with explicit constants on a domain.

The predicate says that for every `x ∈ Ω`, the matrix `a x` has quadratic form bounded below
by `λ‖ξ‖²` and bilinear form bounded above by `Λ‖η‖‖ξ‖`, uniformly in `x`, `η`, and `ξ`.
The side conditions `0 < λ` and `λ ≤ Λ` are part of the predicate so later energy estimates can
recover them directly.
decls.statement: def UniformlyEllipticOn (Ω : Set X) (a : X → Matrix n n ℝ) (lam Lam : ℝ) : Prop

decls.name: TauCeti.PDE.uniformlyEllipticOn_iff
decls.doc: Characteristic restatement of uniform ellipticity and boundedness on a domain.
decls.statement:
lemma uniformlyEllipticOn_iff :
    UniformlyEllipticOn Ω a lam Lam ↔
      0 < lam ∧ lam ≤ Lam ∧
        ∀ ⦃x⦄, x ∈ Ω →
          (∀ ξ : EuclideanSpace ℝ n,
            lam * ‖ξ‖ ^ 2 ≤ (a x).toQuadraticForm' ξ) ∧
            ∀ η ξ : EuclideanSpace ℝ n, |η ⬝ᵥ (a x *ᵥ ξ)| ≤ Lam * ‖η‖ * ‖ξ‖

decls.name: TauCeti.PDE.UniformlyEllipticOn.pos
decls.doc: The lower ellipticity constant is positive.
decls.statement: lemma pos (h : UniformlyEllipticOn Ω a lam Lam) : 0 < lam

decls.name: TauCeti.PDE.UniformlyEllipticOn.le
decls.doc: The lower ellipticity constant is no larger than the upper constant.
decls.statement: lemma le (h : UniformlyEllipticOn Ω a lam Lam) : lam ≤ Lam

decls.name: TauCeti.PDE.UniformlyEllipticOn.upper_nonneg
decls.doc: The upper ellipticity constant is nonnegative.
decls.statement: lemma upper_nonneg (h : UniformlyEllipticOn Ω a lam Lam) : 0 ≤ Lam

decls.name: TauCeti.PDE.UniformlyEllipticOn.lower_bound
decls.doc: The lower quadratic-form bound supplied by uniform ellipticity.
decls.statement:
lemma lower_bound (h : UniformlyEllipticOn Ω a lam Lam) {x : X} (hx : x ∈ Ω)
    (ξ : EuclideanSpace ℝ n) :
    lam * ‖ξ‖ ^ 2 ≤ (a x).toQuadraticForm' ξ

decls.name: TauCeti.PDE.UniformlyEllipticOn.upper_bound
decls.doc: The bilinear upper bound supplied by uniform ellipticity.
decls.statement:
lemma upper_bound (h : UniformlyEllipticOn Ω a lam Lam) {x : X} (hx : x ∈ Ω)
    (η ξ : EuclideanSpace ℝ n) :
    |η ⬝ᵥ (a x *ᵥ ξ)| ≤ Lam * ‖η‖ * ‖ξ‖

decls.name: TauCeti.PDE.UniformlyEllipticOn.quadraticForm_nonneg
decls.doc: Uniform ellipticity implies pointwise nonnegativity of the coefficient quadratic form.
decls.statement:
lemma quadraticForm_nonneg (h : UniformlyEllipticOn Ω a lam Lam) {x : X} (hx : x ∈ Ω)
    (ξ : EuclideanSpace ℝ n) :
    0 ≤ (a x).toQuadraticForm' ξ

decls.name: TauCeti.PDE.UniformlyEllipticOn.quadraticForm_pos
decls.doc: Uniform ellipticity gives a positive quadratic form on every nonzero vector.
decls.statement:
lemma quadraticForm_pos (h : UniformlyEllipticOn Ω a lam Lam) {x : X} (hx : x ∈ Ω)
    {ξ : EuclideanSpace ℝ n} (hξ : ξ ≠ 0) :
    0 < (a x).toQuadraticForm' ξ

decls.name: TauCeti.PDE.UniformlyEllipticOn.mono_set
decls.doc: Restricting the domain preserves uniform ellipticity with the same constants.
decls.statement:
lemma mono_set (h : UniformlyEllipticOn Ω a lam Lam) (hΩ : Ω' ⊆ Ω) :
    UniformlyEllipticOn Ω' a lam Lam

decls.name: TauCeti.PDE.UniformlyEllipticOn.mono_constants
decls.doc:
Weakening the lower constant and increasing the upper constant preserves uniform
ellipticity.
decls.statement:
lemma mono_constants (h : UniformlyEllipticOn Ω a lam Lam) (hlam' : 0 < lam')
    (hlam'_le : lam' ≤ lam) (hLam_le : Lam ≤ Lam') :
    UniformlyEllipticOn Ω a lam' Lam'

decls.name: TauCeti.PDE.UniformlyEllipticOn.of_bounds
decls.doc:
A constructor when the side conditions and pointwise quadratic-form bounds are already
available separately.
decls.statement:
lemma of_bounds (hlam : 0 < lam) (hlamLam : lam ≤ Lam)
    (hbounds : ∀ ⦃x⦄, x ∈ Ω → ∀ ξ : EuclideanSpace ℝ n,
      lam * ‖ξ‖ ^ 2 ≤ (a x).toQuadraticForm' ξ)
    (hupper : ∀ ⦃x⦄, x ∈ Ω → ∀ η ξ : EuclideanSpace ℝ n,
      |η ⬝ᵥ (a x *ᵥ ξ)| ≤ Lam * ‖η‖ * ‖ξ‖) :
    UniformlyEllipticOn Ω a lam Lam

decls.name: TauCeti.PDE.UniformlyEllipticOn.congr
decls.doc: Uniform ellipticity depends only on the coefficient values on the domain.
decls.statement:
lemma congr (h : UniformlyEllipticOn Ω a lam Lam) (hab : Set.EqOn b a Ω) :
    UniformlyEllipticOn Ω b lam Lam

decls.name: TauCeti.PDE.UniformlyEllipticOn.norm_point_matrixBilinearForm_le
decls.doc:
At every point of the domain, uniform ellipticity gives a norm bound for the attached
matrix bilinear form.

decls.name: TauCeti.PDE.UniformlyEllipticOn.opNorm_matrixBilinearForm_le
decls.doc:
At every point of the domain, uniform ellipticity bounds the operator norm of the
attached matrix bilinear form by the upper ellipticity constant.

decls.name: TauCeti.PDE.UniformlyEllipticOn.norm_point_matrixBilinearForm_le_mul_of_norm_le
decls.doc:
Uniform ellipticity gives a radius-restricted pointwise bound for the coefficient
integrand.
decls.statement:
lemma norm_point_matrixBilinearForm_le_mul_of_norm_le
    (h : UniformlyEllipticOn Ω a lam Lam) {x : X} (hx : x ∈ Ω) {R S : ℝ}
    {η ξ : EuclideanSpace ℝ n} (hη : ‖η‖ ≤ R) (hξ : ‖ξ‖ ≤ S) :
    ‖matrixBilinearForm (a x) η ξ‖ ≤ Lam * R * S

decls.name: TauCeti.PDE.UniformlyEllipticOn.isCoercive_matrixBilinearForm
decls.doc:
At every point of the domain, uniform ellipticity gives coercivity of the attached matrix
bilinear form.

decls.name: TauCeti.PDE.UniformlyEllipticOn.transpose
decls.doc:
Transposing the coefficient field preserves uniform ellipticity with the same constants.

The quadratic lower bound is unchanged, and the bilinear upper bound follows by swapping the
two Euclidean arguments.
decls.statement:
lemma transpose (h : UniformlyEllipticOn Ω a lam Lam) :
    UniformlyEllipticOn Ω (fun x => (a x)ᵀ) lam Lam

decls.name: TauCeti.PDE.UniformlyEllipticOn.coefficientSymmetricPart
decls.doc:
Replacing a coefficient field by its symmetric part preserves uniform ellipticity with
the same constants.

This lets the energy-method API pass from a nonsymmetric uniformly elliptic principal
coefficient to the symmetric coefficient with the same diagonal energy, which is the
finite-dimensional prerequisite for self-adjoint model problems.
decls.statement:
lemma coefficientSymmetricPart (h : UniformlyEllipticOn Ω a lam Lam) :
    UniformlyEllipticOn Ω (fun x => coefficientSymmetricPart (a x)) lam Lam

decls.name: TauCeti.PDE.UniformlyEllipticOn.add_nonneg
decls.doc:
Adding a pointwise nonnegative bounded coefficient field preserves uniform ellipticity.

The lower ellipticity constant is unchanged, while the upper bilinear-form constant is
increased by the upper bound for the perturbation. This is the pointwise matrix estimate
used when an energy form is split into a uniformly elliptic principal part plus a
nonnegative bounded perturbation.
decls.statement:
lemma add_nonneg (h : UniformlyEllipticOn Ω a lam Lam) {b : X → Matrix n n ℝ}
    {Mu : ℝ} (hMu : 0 ≤ Mu)
    (hb_nonneg : ∀ ⦃x⦄, x ∈ Ω → ∀ ξ : EuclideanSpace ℝ n,
      0 ≤ (b x).toQuadraticForm' ξ)
    (hb_upper : ∀ ⦃x⦄, x ∈ Ω → ∀ η ξ : EuclideanSpace ℝ n,
      |η ⬝ᵥ (b x *ᵥ ξ)| ≤ Mu * ‖η‖ * ‖ξ‖) :
    UniformlyEllipticOn Ω (fun x => a x + b x) lam (Lam + Mu)

decls.name: TauCeti.PDE.UniformlyEllipticOn.add_bounded
decls.doc:
Adding a bounded coefficient perturbation preserves uniform ellipticity after reducing
the lower ellipticity constant by the perturbation size.

If `a` is uniformly elliptic with constants `λ, Λ` and `b` has pointwise bilinear bound
`μ`, then `a + b` is uniformly elliptic with constants `λ - μ, Λ + μ`, provided `μ < λ`.
This is the finite-dimensional coefficient stability estimate used when perturbing a
uniformly elliptic divergence-form operator.
decls.statement:
lemma add_bounded (h : UniformlyEllipticOn Ω a lam Lam) {b : X → Matrix n n ℝ}
    {Mu : ℝ} (hMu_nonneg : 0 ≤ Mu) (hMu_lt : Mu < lam)
    (hb_upper : ∀ ⦃x⦄, x ∈ Ω → ∀ η ξ : EuclideanSpace ℝ n,
      |η ⬝ᵥ (b x *ᵥ ξ)| ≤ Mu * ‖η‖ * ‖ξ‖) :
    UniformlyEllipticOn Ω (fun x => a x + b x) (lam - Mu) (Lam + Mu)

decls.name: TauCeti.PDE.UniformlyEllipticOn.add_smul_one_bounded
decls.doc:
Adding a bounded scalar multiple of the identity preserves uniform ellipticity after
reducing the lower ellipticity constant by the scalar bound.

This is the scalar-coefficient specialization of `UniformlyEllipticOn.add_bounded`: no sign
condition is imposed on `c`, only the pointwise bound `|c x| ≤ μ`.
decls.statement:
lemma add_smul_one_bounded (h : UniformlyEllipticOn Ω a lam Lam) {c : X → ℝ} {Mu : ℝ}
    (hMu_nonneg : 0 ≤ Mu) (hMu_lt : Mu < lam)
    (hc_abs : ∀ ⦃x⦄, x ∈ Ω → |c x| ≤ Mu) :
    UniformlyEllipticOn Ω (fun x => a x + c x • (1 : Matrix n n ℝ)) (lam - Mu)
      (Lam + Mu)

decls.name: TauCeti.PDE.UniformlyEllipticOn.add_const_smul_one_bounded
decls.doc:
Adding a constant bounded scalar multiple of the identity preserves uniform ellipticity
after reducing the lower ellipticity constant by the absolute value bound.
decls.statement:
lemma add_const_smul_one_bounded (h : UniformlyEllipticOn Ω a lam Lam) {c Mu : ℝ}
    (hMu_lt : Mu < lam) (hc_abs : |c| ≤ Mu) :
    UniformlyEllipticOn Ω (fun y => a y + c • (1 : Matrix n n ℝ)) (lam - Mu)
      (Lam + Mu)

decls.name: TauCeti.PDE.UniformlyEllipticOn.add_smul_one
decls.doc:
Adding a bounded nonnegative scalar multiple of the identity preserves uniform
ellipticity, with the upper constant increased by the scalar bound.
decls.statement:
lemma add_smul_one (h : UniformlyEllipticOn Ω a lam Lam) {c : X → ℝ} {Mu : ℝ}
    (hMu : 0 ≤ Mu) (hc_nonneg : ∀ ⦃x⦄, x ∈ Ω → 0 ≤ c x)
    (hc_upper : ∀ ⦃x⦄, x ∈ Ω → c x ≤ Mu) :
    UniformlyEllipticOn Ω (fun x => a x + c x • (1 : Matrix n n ℝ)) lam (Lam + Mu)

decls.name: TauCeti.PDE.UniformlyEllipticOn.add_const_smul_one
decls.doc:
Adding a constant nonnegative scalar multiple of the identity preserves uniform
ellipticity, with the upper constant increased by that scalar.
decls.statement:
lemma add_const_smul_one (h : UniformlyEllipticOn Ω a lam Lam) {c : ℝ} (hc : 0 ≤ c) :
    UniformlyEllipticOn Ω (fun x => a x + c • (1 : Matrix n n ℝ)) lam (Lam + c)

decls.name: TauCeti.PDE.uniformlyEllipticOn_congr
decls.doc: Equal coefficient fields on the domain give equivalent uniform-ellipticity hypotheses.
decls.statement:
lemma uniformlyEllipticOn_congr (hab : Set.EqOn a b Ω) :
    UniformlyEllipticOn Ω a lam Lam ↔ UniformlyEllipticOn Ω b lam Lam

decls.name: TauCeti.PDE.uniformlyEllipticOn_const_one
decls.doc:
The constant identity coefficient field is uniformly elliptic with any constants
`λ ≤ 1 ≤ Λ` and `0 < λ`. This is the coefficient field of the Laplacian model problem.
decls.statement:
lemma uniformlyEllipticOn_const_one (Ω : Set X) {lam Lam : ℝ} (hlam : 0 < lam)
    (hlam_one : lam ≤ 1) (hone_Lam : 1 ≤ Lam) :
    UniformlyEllipticOn Ω (fun _ => (1 : Matrix n n ℝ)) lam Lam

decls.name: TauCeti.PDE.uniformlyEllipticOn_const_one_one
decls.doc:
In particular, the identity coefficient field is uniformly elliptic with constants
`λ = Λ = 1`.
decls.statement:
lemma uniformlyEllipticOn_const_one_one (Ω : Set X) :
    UniformlyEllipticOn Ω (fun _ => (1 : Matrix n n ℝ)) 1 1

decls.name: TauCeti.PDE.uniformlyEllipticOn_smul_one
decls.doc:
An isotropic scalar coefficient field is uniformly elliptic when its scalar coefficient
lies between the lower and upper constants.

This packages the common model `a(x) = c(x) I`: if `λ ≤ c x ≤ Λ` on `Ω`, then `c x • 1`
satisfies the lower quadratic bound and the bilinear upper bound with constants `λ` and `Λ`.
decls.statement:
lemma uniformlyEllipticOn_smul_one (Ω : Set X) (c : X → ℝ) {lam Lam : ℝ}
    (hlam : 0 < lam) (hlamLam : lam ≤ Lam)
    (hbound : ∀ ⦃x⦄, x ∈ Ω → lam ≤ c x ∧ c x ≤ Lam) :
    UniformlyEllipticOn Ω (fun x => c x • (1 : Matrix n n ℝ)) lam Lam

decls.name: TauCeti.PDE.uniformlyEllipticOn_const_smul_one_self
decls.doc:
A constant positive isotropic coefficient field is uniformly elliptic with matching
lower and upper constants.
decls.statement:
lemma uniformlyEllipticOn_const_smul_one_self (Ω : Set X) {c : ℝ} (hc : 0 < c) :
    UniformlyEllipticOn Ω (fun _ => c • (1 : Matrix n n ℝ)) c c

decls.name: TauCeti.PDE.uniformlyEllipticOn_const_smul_one
decls.doc:
A constant isotropic coefficient field is uniformly elliptic for any explicit constants
`λ ≤ c ≤ Λ` with `0 < λ`.
decls.statement:
lemma uniformlyEllipticOn_const_smul_one (Ω : Set X) {c lam Lam : ℝ} (hlam : 0 < lam)
    (hlamc : lam ≤ c) (hcLam : c ≤ Lam) :
    UniformlyEllipticOn Ω (fun _ => c • (1 : Matrix n n ℝ)) lam Lam

decls.name: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefinite
decls.doc:
A function `F : M → ℂ` on an involutive additive monoid is **positive definite** when, for
every finite family of scalars `c : Fin n → ℂ` and points `v : Fin n → M`, the Hermitian form
`∑_{i,j} c i · conj (c j) · F (v i + star (v j))` is a nonnegative real number (using the order on
`ℂ` for which `0 ≤ z` means `z` is real and nonnegative).
decls.statement: def IsPositiveDefinite (F : M → ℂ) : Prop

decls.name: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefinite.sum_nonneg
decls.doc:
Positive-definiteness holds for an arbitrary finite index type, not just `Fin n`: for every
finite family of scalars `c : ι → ℂ` and points `v : ι → M`, the Hermitian form
`∑_{i,j} c i · conj (c j) · F (v i + star (v j))` is a nonnegative real number.
decls.statement:
theorem sum_nonneg (hF : IsPositiveDefinite F) {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι]
    (c : ι → ℂ) (v : ι → M) :
    0 ≤ ∑ i, ∑ j, c i * conj (c j) * F (v i + star (v j))

decls.name: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefinite.quadForm_two_nonneg
decls.doc:
The `2 × 2` Hermitian sub-form of a positive-definite function at the points `a, b` with
coefficients `c₀, c₁` is nonnegative.
decls.statement:
theorem quadForm_two_nonneg (hF : IsPositiveDefinite F) (a b : M) (c₀ c₁ : ℂ) :
    0 ≤ c₀ * conj c₀ * F (a + star a) + c₀ * conj c₁ * F (a + star b)
      + c₁ * conj c₀ * F (b + star a) + c₁ * conj c₁ * F (b + star b)

decls.name: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefinite.add_star_self_nonneg
decls.doc:
A positive-definite function takes a real, nonnegative value at every "norm point"
`a + star a`.
decls.statement: theorem add_star_self_nonneg (hF : IsPositiveDefinite F) (a : M) : 0 ≤ F (a + star a)

decls.name: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefinite.add_star_self_im
decls.doc:
The value of a positive-definite function at a "norm point" `a + star a` has zero imaginary
part.
decls.statement: theorem add_star_self_im (hF : IsPositiveDefinite F) (a : M) : (F (a + star a)).im = 0

decls.name: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefinite.add_star_self_re_nonneg
decls.doc:
The value of a positive-definite function at a "norm point" `a + star a` has nonnegative real
part.
decls.statement: theorem add_star_self_re_nonneg (hF : IsPositiveDefinite F) (a : M) : 0 ≤ (F (a + star a)).re

decls.name: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefinite.map_zero_nonneg
decls.doc: The value of a positive-definite function at `0` is real and nonnegative.
decls.statement: theorem map_zero_nonneg (hF : IsPositiveDefinite F) : 0 ≤ F 0

decls.name: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefinite.map_zero_im
decls.doc: The value of a positive-definite function at `0` has zero imaginary part.
decls.statement: theorem map_zero_im (hF : IsPositiveDefinite F) : (F 0).im = 0

decls.name: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefinite.map_zero_re_nonneg
decls.doc: The real part of the value of a positive-definite function at `0` is nonnegative.
decls.statement: theorem map_zero_re_nonneg (hF : IsPositiveDefinite F) : 0 ≤ (F 0).re

decls.name: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefinite.map_zero_eq_ofReal_re
decls.doc:
The value at the origin of a positive-definite function is equal to the real number
`(F 0).re`, viewed as a complex number.
decls.statement: theorem map_zero_eq_ofReal_re (hF : IsPositiveDefinite F) : F 0 = ((F 0).re : ℂ)

decls.name: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefinite.map_zero_re_pos_of_ne_zero
decls.doc:
If a positive-definite function is nonzero at the origin, then the real part of that value is
strictly positive.
decls.statement:
theorem map_zero_re_pos_of_ne_zero (hF : IsPositiveDefinite F) (h0 : F 0 ≠ 0) :
    0 < (F 0).re

decls.name: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefinite.conj_symm
decls.doc:
A positive-definite function is conjugate symmetric in the involution:
`conj (F (b + star a)) = F (a + star b)`.
decls.statement:
theorem conj_symm (hF : IsPositiveDefinite F) (a b : M) :
    conj (F (b + star a)) = F (a + star b)

decls.name: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefinite.isPositiveDefiniteKernel
decls.doc:
A positive-definite function `F` induces the positive-definite kernel `K(a, b) = F(a + b⋆)`.
This is the forward half of the function ↔ kernel correspondence.
decls.statement:
theorem isPositiveDefiniteKernel (hF : IsPositiveDefinite F) :
    IsPositiveDefiniteKernel (fun a b => F (a + star b))

decls.name: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefinite.of_isPositiveDefiniteKernel
decls.doc:
If the kernel `K(a, b) = F(a + b⋆)` is positive definite, then so is the function `F`. This is
the reverse half of the function ↔ kernel correspondence.
decls.statement:
theorem of_isPositiveDefiniteKernel
    (hK : IsPositiveDefiniteKernel (fun a b => F (a + star b))) : IsPositiveDefinite F

decls.name: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefinite.normSq_le
decls.doc:
The Cauchy–Schwarz inequality for a positive-definite function: the squared norm of an
off-diagonal value is bounded by the product of the two diagonal values.
decls.statement:
theorem normSq_le (hF : IsPositiveDefinite F) (a b : M) :
    Complex.normSq (F (a + star b))
      ≤ (F (a + star a)).re * (F (b + star b)).re

decls.name: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefinite.norm_apply_le_map_zero_re_of_add_star_eq_zero
decls.doc:
If `a + star a = 0`, then a positive-definite function is bounded at `a` by its value at
zero.
decls.statement:
theorem norm_apply_le_map_zero_re_of_add_star_eq_zero (hF : IsPositiveDefinite F)
    (a : M) (ha : a + star a = 0) : ‖F a‖ ≤ (F 0).re

decls.name: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefinite.apply_eq_zero_of_map_zero_re_eq_zero
decls.doc:
**A positive-definite function with `(F 0).re = 0` vanishes identically.**

No hypothesis on the point is required, and none on the ambient structure beyond an
involutive additive monoid (`AddMonoid` and `StarAddMonoid`).
decls.title: A positive-definite function with `(F 0).re = 0` vanishes identically
decls.statement:
theorem apply_eq_zero_of_map_zero_re_eq_zero (hF : IsPositiveDefinite F)
    (h0 : (F 0).re = 0) (a : M) : F a = 0

decls.name: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefinite.norm_apply_le_map_zero_re_of_star_eq_neg
decls.doc:
If the involution negates the point `a`, then a positive-definite function is bounded at `a`
by its value at zero. In particular this applies on an additive group whose involution is
negation.
decls.statement:
theorem norm_apply_le_map_zero_re_of_star_eq_neg (hH : IsPositiveDefinite H)
    (a : N) (hstar_a : star a = -a) : ‖H a‖ ≤ (H 0).re

decls.name: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefinite.add
decls.doc: Positive-definite functions are closed under addition.
decls.statement:
theorem add (hF : IsPositiveDefinite F) (hG : IsPositiveDefinite G) :
    IsPositiveDefinite (fun x => F x + G x)

decls.name: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefinite.const_mul
decls.doc: Positive-definite functions are closed under multiplication by a nonnegative complex scalar.
decls.statement:
theorem const_mul {k : ℂ} (hk : 0 ≤ k) (hF : IsPositiveDefinite F) :
    IsPositiveDefinite (fun x => k * F x)

decls.name: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefinite.gram_posSemidef
decls.doc: The Gram matrix of a positive-definite function is positive semidefinite.
decls.statement:
theorem gram_posSemidef (hF : IsPositiveDefinite F) {ι : Type*} (v : ι → M) :
    Matrix.PosSemidef (fun i j => F (v i + star (v j)))

decls.name: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefinite.mul
decls.doc: Positive-definite functions are closed under pointwise multiplication (Schur product).
decls.statement:
theorem mul (hF : IsPositiveDefinite F) (hG : IsPositiveDefinite G) :
    IsPositiveDefinite (fun x => F x * G x)

decls.name: TauCeti.isPositiveDefinite_const
decls.doc: A nonnegative real constant is a positive-definite function.
decls.statement:
theorem isPositiveDefinite_const {k : ℂ} (hk : 0 ≤ k) :
    IsPositiveDefinite (fun _ : M => k)

decls.name: TauCeti.isPositiveDefinite_zero
decls.doc: The zero function is positive definite.
decls.statement: theorem isPositiveDefinite_zero : IsPositiveDefinite (fun _ : M => (0 : ℂ))

decls.name: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefinite.sum
decls.doc: Positive-definite functions are closed under finite sums.

decls.name: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefinite.prod
decls.doc: Positive-definite functions are closed under finite products (Schur product).

decls.name: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefinite.gram_three_add_star_expand_of_values
decls.statement:
theorem gram_three_add_star_expand_of_values
    {x y : E} {lam : ℂ} {c : Fin 3 → ℂ} {p : Fin 3 → E}
    (hc0 : c 0 = 1) (hc1 : c 1 = -1) (hc2 : c 2 = lam)
    (hp0 : p 0 = x) (hp1 : p 1 = y) (hp2 : p 2 = 0)
    (hx : x + star x = 0) (hy : y + star y = 0)
    (hyx : F (y + star x) = conj (F (x + star y)))
    (hnx : F (star x) = conj (F x)) (hny : F (0 + star y) = conj (F y)) :
    (∑ i : Fin 3, ∑ j : Fin 3,
      c i * conj (c j) * F (p i + star (p j)))
      = F 0 - F (x + star y) + conj lam * F x - conj (F (x + star y)) + F 0
        - conj lam * F y + lam * conj (F x) - lam * conj (F y)
        + lam * conj lam * F 0

decls.name: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefinite.gram_three_add_star_expand
decls.statement:
theorem gram_three_add_star_expand
    {x y : E} (hx : x + star x = 0) (hy : y + star y = 0)
    (hyx : F (y + star x) = conj (F (x + star y)))
    (hnx : F (star x) = conj (F x)) (hny : F (0 + star y) = conj (F y))
    {lam : ℂ} :
    (∑ i : Fin 3, ∑ j : Fin 3,
      ![1, -1, lam] i * conj (![1, -1, lam] j) *
        F (![x, y, 0] i + star (![x, y, 0] j)))
      = F 0 - F (x + star y) + conj lam * F x - conj (F (x + star y)) + F 0
        - conj lam * F y + lam * conj (F x) - lam * conj (F y)
        + lam * conj lam * F 0

decls.name: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefinite.gram_three_sub_re_complex_algebra
decls.statement:
theorem gram_three_sub_re_complex_algebra {r : ℝ} {z d lam : ℂ}
    (hlam : lam = -d / (r : ℂ)) (hr : 0 < r) :
    ((r : ℂ) - z + conj lam * d - conj z + (r : ℂ) + lam * conj d
        + lam * conj lam * (r : ℂ)).re
      = 2 * r - 2 * z.re - Complex.normSq d / r

decls.name: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefinite.gram_three_add_star_re_algebra
decls.statement:
theorem gram_three_add_star_re_algebra (hF : IsPositiveDefinite F)
    {x y : E} (hx : x + star x = 0) (hy : y + star y = 0)
    (hyx : F (y + star x) = conj (F (x + star y)))
    (hnx : F (star x) = conj (F x)) (hny : F (0 + star y) = conj (F y))
    {C d lam : ℂ}
    (hC : C = F 0) (hd : d = F x - F y) (hlam : lam = -d / C)
    (hCpos : 0 < (F 0).re) :
    (∑ i : Fin 3, ∑ j : Fin 3,
      ![1, -1, lam] i * conj (![1, -1, lam] j) *
        F (![x, y, 0] i + star (![x, y, 0] j))).re
      = 2 * (F 0).re - 2 * (F (x + star y)).re - Complex.normSq d / (F 0).re

decls.name: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefinite.gram_three_add_star_re_eq
decls.statement:
theorem gram_three_add_star_re_eq (hF : IsPositiveDefinite F)
    {x y : E} (hx : x + star x = 0) (hy : y + star y = 0) {C d lam : ℂ}
    (hC : C = F 0) (hd : d = F x - F y) (hlam : lam = -d / C)
    (hCpos : 0 < (F 0).re) :
    (∑ i : Fin 3, ∑ j : Fin 3,
      ![1, -1, lam] i * conj (![1, -1, lam] j) *
        F (![x, y, 0] i + star (![x, y, 0] j))).re
      = 2 * (F 0).re - 2 * (F (x + star y)).re - Complex.normSq d / (F 0).re

decls.name: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefinite.norm_sub_sq_le_two_mul_map_zero_re_mul_re_sub_of_add_star_eq_zero
decls.doc: The local monoid-level real-part form of the standard positive-definite continuity estimate.
decls.statement:
theorem norm_sub_sq_le_two_mul_map_zero_re_mul_re_sub_of_add_star_eq_zero
    (hF : IsPositiveDefinite F)
    {x y : E} (hx : x + star x = 0) (hy : y + star y = 0) :
    ‖F x - F y‖ ^ 2
      ≤ 2 * (F 0).re * ((F 0).re - (F (x + star y)).re)

decls.name: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefinite.norm_sub_sq_le_two_mul_map_zero_re_mul_norm_sub_of_add_star_eq_zero
decls.doc:
The local monoid-level norm-valued form of the standard positive-definite continuity
estimate.
decls.statement:
theorem norm_sub_sq_le_two_mul_map_zero_re_mul_norm_sub_of_add_star_eq_zero
    (hF : IsPositiveDefinite F)
    {x y : E} (hx : x + star x = 0) (hy : y + star y = 0) :
    ‖F x - F y‖ ^ 2 ≤ 2 * (F 0).re * ‖F (x + star y) - F 0‖

decls.name: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefinite.norm_sub_sq_le_two_mul_map_zero_re_mul_re_sub_of_star_eq_neg
decls.doc: The local real-part form of the standard positive-definite continuity estimate.
decls.statement:
theorem norm_sub_sq_le_two_mul_map_zero_re_mul_re_sub_of_star_eq_neg
    (hF : IsPositiveDefinite F)
    {x y : E} (hx : star x = -x) (hy : star y = -y) :
    ‖F x - F y‖ ^ 2
      ≤ 2 * (F 0).re * ((F 0).re - (F (x - y)).re)

decls.name: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefinite.norm_sub_sq_le_two_mul_map_zero_re_mul_re_sub_of_forall_star_eq_neg
decls.doc:
The real-part form of the standard positive-definite continuity estimate under a globally
negating involution.
decls.statement:
theorem norm_sub_sq_le_two_mul_map_zero_re_mul_re_sub_of_forall_star_eq_neg
    (hF : IsPositiveDefinite F)
    (hstar : ∀ x : E, star x = -x) (x y : E) :
    ‖F x - F y‖ ^ 2
      ≤ 2 * (F 0).re * ((F 0).re - (F (x - y)).re)

decls.name: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefinite.norm_sub_sq_le_two_mul_map_zero_re_mul_norm_sub_of_star_eq_neg
decls.doc: The local norm-valued form of the standard positive-definite continuity estimate.
decls.statement:
theorem norm_sub_sq_le_two_mul_map_zero_re_mul_norm_sub_of_star_eq_neg
    (hF : IsPositiveDefinite F)
    {x y : E} (hx : star x = -x) (hy : star y = -y) :
    ‖F x - F y‖ ^ 2 ≤ 2 * (F 0).re * ‖F (x - y) - F 0‖

decls.name: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefinite.norm_sub_sq_le_two_mul_map_zero_re_mul_norm_sub_of_forall_star_eq_neg
decls.doc:
The norm-valued form of the standard positive-definite continuity estimate under a globally
negating involution.
decls.statement:
theorem norm_sub_sq_le_two_mul_map_zero_re_mul_norm_sub_of_forall_star_eq_neg
    (hF : IsPositiveDefinite F)
    (hstar : ∀ x : E, star x = -x) (x y : E) :
    ‖F x - F y‖ ^ 2 ≤ 2 * (F 0).re * ‖F (x - y) - F 0‖

decls.name: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefinite.uniformContinuous_of_continuousAt_zero_of_forall_star_eq_neg
decls.doc:
A positive-definite function on a seminormed additive group with the negation involution is
uniformly continuous as soon as it is continuous at the origin.
decls.statement:
theorem uniformContinuous_of_continuousAt_zero_of_forall_star_eq_neg (hF : IsPositiveDefinite F)
    (hstar : ∀ x : E, star x = -x) (hcont : ContinuousAt F 0) :
    UniformContinuous F

decls.name: TauCeti.fourierAtom
decls.doc: The Fourier atom at frequency `q`, using Mathlib's `2π` Fourier convention.
decls.statement: def fourierAtom (q : V) (v : V) : ℂ

decls.name: TauCeti.fourierAtom_eq_fourierChar
decls.doc: The `Real.fourierChar` form of a Fourier atom.
decls.statement:
theorem fourierAtom_eq_fourierChar (q : V) (v : V) :
    fourierAtom q v = (Real.fourierChar (-(inner ℝ v q)) : ℂ)

decls.name: TauCeti.fourierAtom_apply
decls.doc: The raw exponential form of a Fourier atom.
decls.statement:
theorem fourierAtom_apply (q : V) (v : V) :
    fourierAtom q v =
      Complex.exp (-2 * ((Real.pi : ℝ) : ℂ) * Complex.I * ((inner ℝ v q : ℝ) : ℂ))

decls.name: TauCeti.fourierAtom_sub
decls.doc: Fourier atoms turn spatial subtraction into a rank-one positive-definite kernel.
decls.statement:
theorem fourierAtom_sub (q v w : V) :
    fourierAtom q (v - w) =
      conj (Complex.exp (2 * ((Real.pi : ℝ) : ℂ) * Complex.I * ((inner ℝ v q : ℝ) : ℂ))) *
        Complex.exp (2 * ((Real.pi : ℝ) : ℂ) * Complex.I * ((inner ℝ w q : ℝ) : ℂ))

decls.name: TauCeti.isPositiveDefiniteKernel_fourierAtom
decls.doc: The spatial subtraction kernel supplied by a Fourier atom is positive definite.
decls.statement:

decls.name: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefinite.sum_smul_apply_eq_one

decls.name: TauCeti.isPositiveDefinite_iff_isPositiveDefiniteKernel
decls.doc:
A function `F` on an involutive additive monoid is positive definite if and only if the
two-variable kernel `K(a, b) = F(a + b⋆)` is positive definite.
decls.statement:
theorem isPositiveDefinite_iff_isPositiveDefiniteKernel :
    IsPositiveDefinite F ↔ IsPositiveDefiniteKernel (fun a b => F (a + star b))

decls.name: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefinite.isPositiveDefiniteKernel_sub
decls.doc:
Under the negation involution `a⋆ = -a`, a positive-definite function `F` gives the
translation-invariant positive-definite kernel `K(a, b) = F(a - b)`. This is the form in which
positive definiteness is usually stated on groups such as `ℝᵈ` or a real inner-product space.
decls.statement:
theorem isPositiveDefiniteKernel_sub (hstar : ∀ a : G, star a = -a) (hF : IsPositiveDefinite F) :
    IsPositiveDefiniteKernel (fun a b => F (a - b))

decls.name: TauCeti.isPositiveDefinite_iff_isPositiveDefiniteKernel_sub
decls.doc:
Under the negation involution `a⋆ = -a`, `F` is positive definite if and only if the
translation-invariant kernel `K(a, b) = F(a - b)` is positive definite.
decls.statement:
theorem isPositiveDefinite_iff_isPositiveDefiniteKernel_sub (hstar : ∀ a : G, star a = -a) :
    IsPositiveDefinite F ↔ IsPositiveDefiniteKernel (fun a b => F (a - b))

decls.name: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefiniteKernel
decls.doc:
A kernel `K : α → α → 𝕜` is *positive definite* when the matrix indexed by all points of `α`
is positive semidefinite.
decls.statement: def IsPositiveDefiniteKernel (K : α → α → 𝕜) : Prop

decls.name: TauCeti.isPositiveDefiniteKernel_def
decls.doc:
The named kernel predicate is definitionally Mathlib's positive semidefinite predicate on the
full kernel matrix.
decls.statement:
theorem isPositiveDefiniteKernel_def (K : α → α → 𝕜) :
    IsPositiveDefiniteKernel K ↔ (Matrix.of fun a b => K a b).PosSemidef

decls.name: TauCeti.isPositiveDefiniteKernel_apply_self_nonneg
decls.doc: Diagonal values of a positive-definite kernel are nonnegative.
decls.statement:
theorem isPositiveDefiniteKernel_apply_self_nonneg {K : α → α → 𝕜}
    (hK : IsPositiveDefiniteKernel K) (a : α) : 0 ≤ K a a

decls.name: TauCeti.isPositiveDefiniteKernel_conj_symm
decls.doc: Positive-definite kernels are conjugate-symmetric.
decls.statement:
theorem isPositiveDefiniteKernel_conj_symm {K : α → α → 𝕜}
    (hK : IsPositiveDefiniteKernel K) (a b : α) : conj (K a b) = K b a

decls.name: TauCeti.isPositiveDefiniteKernel_comp
decls.doc: Pulling back a positive-definite kernel along a map preserves positive definiteness.

decls.name: TauCeti.isPositiveDefiniteKernel_add
decls.doc: Sums of positive-definite kernels are positive definite.

decls.name: TauCeti.isPositiveDefiniteKernel_smul_of_nonneg
decls.doc:
Nonnegative scalar multiples in the codomain of positive-definite kernels are positive
definite.
decls.statement:
theorem isPositiveDefiniteKernel_smul_of_nonneg {K : α → α → 𝕜} {c : 𝕜} (hc : 0 ≤ c)
    (hK : IsPositiveDefiniteKernel K) :
    IsPositiveDefiniteKernel (fun a b => c • K a b)

decls.name: TauCeti.isPositiveDefiniteKernel_smul
decls.doc: Nonnegative real scalar multiples of positive-definite kernels are positive definite.
decls.statement:
theorem isPositiveDefiniteKernel_smul {K : α → α → 𝕜} {r : ℝ} (hr : 0 ≤ r)
    (hK : IsPositiveDefiniteKernel K) :
    IsPositiveDefiniteKernel (fun a b => r • K a b)

decls.name: TauCeti.isPositiveDefiniteKernel_mul
decls.doc: Pointwise products of positive-definite kernels are positive definite.

decls.name: TauCeti.posSemidef_of_support_posSemidef
decls.statement:
theorem posSemidef_of_support_posSemidef (K : α → α → 𝕜)
    (hHerm : (Matrix.of fun a b => K a b).IsHermitian)
    (hgram : ∀ x : α →₀ 𝕜,
      (Matrix.of fun i j : x.support => K (i : α) (j : α)).PosSemidef) :
    (Matrix.of fun a b => K a b).PosSemidef

decls.name: TauCeti.isPositiveDefiniteKernel_conj_mul
decls.doc:
The rank-one kernels `(a, b) ↦ conj (g a) · g b` are positive definite. With `g ≡ 1` this gives
the constant kernel `1`; with general `g` these are building blocks whose nonnegative mixtures
and Schur products generate further positive-definite kernels.
decls.statement:
theorem isPositiveDefiniteKernel_conj_mul (g : α → 𝕜) :
    IsPositiveDefiniteKernel (fun a b => conj (g a) * g b)

decls.name: TauCeti.isPositiveDefiniteKernel_zero
decls.doc: The zero kernel is positive definite.
decls.statement:
theorem isPositiveDefiniteKernel_zero :
    IsPositiveDefiniteKernel (fun _ _ : α => (0 : 𝕜))

decls.name: TauCeti.isPositiveDefiniteKernel_one
decls.doc: The constant kernel with value `1` is positive definite.
decls.statement:
theorem isPositiveDefiniteKernel_one :
    IsPositiveDefiniteKernel (fun _ _ : α => (1 : 𝕜))

decls.name: TauCeti.isPositiveDefiniteKernel_const_of_nonneg
decls.doc: A nonnegative constant gives a positive-definite constant kernel.
decls.statement:
theorem isPositiveDefiniteKernel_const_of_nonneg {c : 𝕜} (hc : 0 ≤ c) :
    IsPositiveDefiniteKernel (fun _ _ : α => c)

decls.name: TauCeti.isPositiveDefiniteKernel_iff
decls.doc:
The quadratic-form characterization of a positive-definite kernel: `K` is positive definite if
and only if it is conjugate-symmetric and every Hermitian form
`∑ᵢⱼ conj (x i) · x j · K (v i) (v j)` is nonnegative. The reverse direction is the introduction
rule that builds a positive-definite kernel directly from the quadratic-form condition (for
instance for the `K(a, b) = F(a + b⋆)` construction), without unfolding `Matrix.PosSemidef`.
decls.statement:
theorem isPositiveDefiniteKernel_iff {K : α → α → 𝕜} :
    IsPositiveDefiniteKernel K ↔
      (∀ a b, conj (K a b) = K b a) ∧
        ∀ {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] (v : ι → α) (x : ι → 𝕜),
          0 ≤ ∑ i, ∑ j, conj (x i) * x j * K (v i) (v j)

decls.name: TauCeti.isPositiveDefiniteKernel_finTwo_posSemidef
decls.doc: The `2 × 2` Gram submatrix of a positive-definite kernel is positive semidefinite.
decls.statement:
theorem isPositiveDefiniteKernel_finTwo_posSemidef
    (hK : IsPositiveDefiniteKernel K) (a b : α) :
    (Matrix.of fun i j : Fin 2 => K (![a, b] i) (![a, b] j)).PosSemidef

decls.name: TauCeti.isPositiveDefiniteKernel_normSq_le
decls.doc:
The kernel Cauchy--Schwarz inequality: for an `RCLike`-valued positive-definite kernel, the
squared norm of an off-diagonal entry is bounded by the product of the two diagonal real parts.
decls.statement:
theorem isPositiveDefiniteKernel_normSq_le (hK : IsPositiveDefiniteKernel K) (a b : α) :
    RCLike.normSq (K a b) ≤ RCLike.re (K a a) * RCLike.re (K b b)

decls.name: TauCeti.isPositiveDefiniteKernel_eq_zero_of_apply_self_eq_zero_left
decls.doc:
If the left diagonal entry of a positive-definite kernel is zero, then the corresponding
row entry is zero.
decls.statement:
theorem isPositiveDefiniteKernel_eq_zero_of_apply_self_eq_zero_left
    (hK : IsPositiveDefiniteKernel K) {a b : α} (ha : K a a = 0) : K a b = 0

decls.name: TauCeti.isPositiveDefiniteKernel_eq_zero_of_apply_self_eq_zero_right
decls.doc:
If the right diagonal entry of a positive-definite kernel is zero, then the corresponding
column entry is zero.
decls.statement:
theorem isPositiveDefiniteKernel_eq_zero_of_apply_self_eq_zero_right
    (hK : IsPositiveDefiniteKernel K) {a b : α} (hb : K b b = 0) : K a b = 0

decls.name: TauCeti.isPositiveDefiniteKernel_norm_le_one_of_apply_self_eq_one
decls.doc:
If both diagonal entries are `1`, then the corresponding off-diagonal entry has norm at
most `1`. This is the common normalized-kernel form of the kernel Cauchy--Schwarz inequality.
decls.statement:
theorem isPositiveDefiniteKernel_norm_le_one_of_apply_self_eq_one
    (hK : IsPositiveDefiniteKernel K) {a b : α} (ha : K a a = 1) (hb : K b b = 1) :
    ‖K a b‖ ≤ 1

decls.name: TauCeti.isPositiveDefiniteKernel_sum
decls.doc: Finite sums of positive-definite kernels are positive definite.

decls.name: TauCeti.isPositiveDefiniteKernel_prod
decls.doc: Finite pointwise products of positive-definite kernels are positive definite.

decls.name: TauCeti.isPositiveDefiniteKernel_sum_smul
decls.doc:
Finite sums of positive-definite kernels with nonnegative weights are positive
definite. This is the weighted finite-mixture form most often used in examples.
decls.statement:
theorem isPositiveDefiniteKernel_sum_smul {ι : Type w} {s : Finset ι}
    {r : ι → 𝕜} {K : ι → α → α → 𝕜} (hr : ∀ i ∈ s, 0 ≤ r i)
    (hK : ∀ i ∈ s, IsPositiveDefiniteKernel (K i)) :
    IsPositiveDefiniteKernel (fun a b => ∑ i ∈ s, r i • K i a b)

decls.name: TauCeti.isPositiveDefiniteKernel_pow
decls.doc: Schur powers of a positive-definite kernel are positive definite.

decls.name: TauCeti.isPositiveDefiniteKernel_sum_conj_mul
decls.doc:
Finite sums of rank-one kernels `(a, b) ↦ conj (gᵢ a) * gᵢ b` are positive definite.
These are the finite-rank positive-definite kernels used as the elementary building blocks for
the later GNS/Kolmogorov decomposition.
decls.statement:
theorem isPositiveDefiniteKernel_sum_conj_mul {ι : Type w} (s : Finset ι)
    (g : ι → α → 𝕜) :
    IsPositiveDefiniteKernel
      (fun a b => ∑ i ∈ s, conj (g i a) * g i b)

decls.name: TauCeti.isPositiveDefiniteKernel_prod_conj_mul
decls.doc:
Finite products of rank-one kernels are positive definite. This is the Schur-product
companion to `TauCeti.isPositiveDefiniteKernel_sum_conj_mul`.
decls.statement:
theorem isPositiveDefiniteKernel_prod_conj_mul {ι : Type w} (s : Finset ι)
    (g : ι → α → 𝕜) :
    IsPositiveDefiniteKernel
      (fun a b => ∏ i ∈ s, conj (g i a) * g i b)

decls.name: TauCeti.isPositiveDefiniteKernel_sum_smul_conj_mul
decls.doc: Finite nonnegative combinations of rank-one kernels are positive definite.
decls.statement:
theorem isPositiveDefiniteKernel_sum_smul_conj_mul {ι : Type w} {s : Finset ι}
    {r : ι → 𝕜} (hr : ∀ i ∈ s, 0 ≤ r i) (g : ι → α → 𝕜) :
    IsPositiveDefiniteKernel
      (fun a b => ∑ i ∈ s, r i • (conj (g i a) * g i b))

decls.name: TauCeti.positiveDefiniteKernelFinsuppForm
decls.doc:
The finitely supported Gram expression associated to a kernel `K`.

For positive-definite `K`, the diagonal value
`positiveDefiniteKernelFinsuppForm K x x` is nonnegative, and the form is Hermitian. This is the
pre-inner-product expression used before quotienting by its null space in the GNS/Kolmogorov
construction.
decls.statement:
def positiveDefiniteKernelFinsuppForm (K : α → α → 𝕜)
    (x y : α →₀ 𝕜) : 𝕜

decls.name: TauCeti.positiveDefiniteKernelFinsuppForm_def
decls.doc: The finitely supported Gram form unfolds to the double `Finsupp.sum` expression.
decls.statement:
theorem positiveDefiniteKernelFinsuppForm_def (K : α → α → 𝕜) (x y : α →₀ 𝕜) :
    positiveDefiniteKernelFinsuppForm K x y =
      x.sum fun a xa => y.sum fun b yb => conj xa * yb * K a b

decls.name: TauCeti.positiveDefiniteKernelFinsuppForm_zero_left
decls.doc: The finitely supported Gram form is zero when the left vector is zero.
decls.statement:
theorem positiveDefiniteKernelFinsuppForm_zero_left (y : α →₀ 𝕜) :
    positiveDefiniteKernelFinsuppForm K 0 y = 0

decls.name: TauCeti.positiveDefiniteKernelFinsuppForm_zero_right
decls.doc: The finitely supported Gram form is zero when the right vector is zero.
decls.statement:
theorem positiveDefiniteKernelFinsuppForm_zero_right (x : α →₀ 𝕜) :
    positiveDefiniteKernelFinsuppForm K x 0 = 0

decls.name: TauCeti.positiveDefiniteKernelFinsuppForm_eq_posSemidef_sum
decls.statement:
theorem positiveDefiniteKernelFinsuppForm_eq_posSemidef_sum (x : α →₀ 𝕜) :
    positiveDefiniteKernelFinsuppForm K x x =
      x.sum fun i xi => x.sum fun j xj => star xi * (Matrix.of fun a b => K a b) i j * xj

decls.name: TauCeti.positiveDefiniteKernelFinsuppForm_self_nonneg
decls.doc: The diagonal finitely supported Gram form of a positive-definite kernel is nonnegative.
decls.statement:
theorem positiveDefiniteKernelFinsuppForm_self_nonneg
    (hK : IsPositiveDefiniteKernel K) (x : α →₀ 𝕜) :
    0 ≤ positiveDefiniteKernelFinsuppForm K x x

decls.name: TauCeti.positiveDefiniteKernelFinsuppForm_add_left
decls.doc: The finitely supported Gram form is additive in the left argument.
decls.statement:
theorem positiveDefiniteKernelFinsuppForm_add_left (x y z : α →₀ 𝕜) :
    positiveDefiniteKernelFinsuppForm K (x + y) z =
      positiveDefiniteKernelFinsuppForm K x z + positiveDefiniteKernelFinsuppForm K y z

decls.name: TauCeti.positiveDefiniteKernelFinsuppForm_add_right
decls.doc: The finitely supported Gram form is additive in the right argument.
decls.statement:
theorem positiveDefiniteKernelFinsuppForm_add_right (x y z : α →₀ 𝕜) :
    positiveDefiniteKernelFinsuppForm K x (y + z) =
      positiveDefiniteKernelFinsuppForm K x y + positiveDefiniteKernelFinsuppForm K x z

decls.name: TauCeti.positiveDefiniteKernelFinsuppForm_smul_left
decls.doc: The finitely supported Gram form is conjugate-linear in the left scalar.
decls.statement:
theorem positiveDefiniteKernelFinsuppForm_smul_left (c : 𝕜) (x y : α →₀ 𝕜) :
    positiveDefiniteKernelFinsuppForm K (c • x) y =
      conj c * positiveDefiniteKernelFinsuppForm K x y

decls.name: TauCeti.positiveDefiniteKernelFinsuppForm_smul_right
decls.doc: The finitely supported Gram form is linear in the right scalar.
decls.statement:
theorem positiveDefiniteKernelFinsuppForm_smul_right (c : 𝕜) (x y : α →₀ 𝕜) :
    positiveDefiniteKernelFinsuppForm K x (c • y) =
      c * positiveDefiniteKernelFinsuppForm K x y

decls.name: TauCeti.positiveDefiniteKernelFinsuppForm_zero_kernel
decls.doc: The finitely supported Gram form is zero for the zero kernel.
decls.statement:
theorem positiveDefiniteKernelFinsuppForm_zero_kernel (x y : α →₀ 𝕜) :
    positiveDefiniteKernelFinsuppForm (fun _ _ : α => (0 : 𝕜)) x y = 0

decls.name: TauCeti.positiveDefiniteKernelFinsuppForm_add_kernel
decls.doc: The finitely supported Gram form is additive in the kernel.
decls.statement:
theorem positiveDefiniteKernelFinsuppForm_add_kernel
    (K L : α → α → 𝕜) (x y : α →₀ 𝕜) :
    positiveDefiniteKernelFinsuppForm (fun a b => K a b + L a b) x y =
      positiveDefiniteKernelFinsuppForm K x y + positiveDefiniteKernelFinsuppForm L x y

decls.name: TauCeti.positiveDefiniteKernelFinsuppForm_smul_kernel
decls.doc: The finitely supported Gram form is homogeneous in the kernel.
decls.statement:
theorem positiveDefiniteKernelFinsuppForm_smul_kernel
    (c : 𝕜) (K : α → α → 𝕜) (x y : α →₀ 𝕜) :
    positiveDefiniteKernelFinsuppForm (fun a b => c • K a b) x y =
      c * positiveDefiniteKernelFinsuppForm K x y

decls.name: TauCeti.positiveDefiniteKernelFinsuppForm_real_smul_kernel
decls.doc: The finitely supported Gram form is homogeneous in a real scalar on the kernel.
decls.statement:
theorem positiveDefiniteKernelFinsuppForm_real_smul_kernel
    (r : ℝ) (K : α → α → 𝕜) (x y : α →₀ 𝕜) :
    positiveDefiniteKernelFinsuppForm (fun a b => r • K a b) x y =
      r • positiveDefiniteKernelFinsuppForm K x y

decls.name: TauCeti.positiveDefiniteKernelFinsuppForm_sum_kernel
decls.doc: The finitely supported Gram form sends finite sums of kernels to sums of Gram forms.
decls.statement:
theorem positiveDefiniteKernelFinsuppForm_sum_kernel {ι : Type*}
    (s : Finset ι) (K : ι → α → α → 𝕜) (x y : α →₀ 𝕜) :
    positiveDefiniteKernelFinsuppForm (fun a b => ∑ i ∈ s, K i a b) x y =
      ∑ i ∈ s, positiveDefiniteKernelFinsuppForm (K i) x y

decls.name: TauCeti.positiveDefiniteKernelFinsuppSesqForm
decls.doc: The finitely supported Gram form bundled as a sesquilinear form.
decls.statement:
def positiveDefiniteKernelFinsuppSesqForm (K : α → α → 𝕜) :
    (α →₀ 𝕜) →ₗ⋆[𝕜] (α →₀ 𝕜) →ₗ[𝕜] 𝕜

decls.name: TauCeti.positiveDefiniteKernelFinsuppSesqForm_apply
decls.doc: Applying the bundled sesquilinear form gives the finitely supported Gram expression.
decls.statement:
theorem positiveDefiniteKernelFinsuppSesqForm_apply
    (K : α → α → 𝕜) (x y : α →₀ 𝕜) :
    positiveDefiniteKernelFinsuppSesqForm K x y =
      positiveDefiniteKernelFinsuppForm K x y

decls.name: TauCeti.positiveDefiniteKernelFinsuppForm_conj_symm_of_conj_symm
decls.doc:
A pointwise conjugate-symmetric kernel gives a conjugate-symmetric finitely supported Gram
form.
decls.statement:
theorem positiveDefiniteKernelFinsuppForm_conj_symm_of_conj_symm
    (hsymm : ∀ a b, conj (K a b) = K b a) (x y : α →₀ 𝕜) :
    conj (positiveDefiniteKernelFinsuppForm K x y)
      = positiveDefiniteKernelFinsuppForm K y x

decls.name: TauCeti.positiveDefiniteKernelFinsuppForm_conj_symm
decls.doc:
The finitely supported Gram form attached to a positive-definite kernel is conjugate
symmetric.
decls.statement:
theorem positiveDefiniteKernelFinsuppForm_conj_symm
    (hK : IsPositiveDefiniteKernel K) (x y : α →₀ 𝕜) :
    conj (positiveDefiniteKernelFinsuppForm K x y)
      = positiveDefiniteKernelFinsuppForm K y x

decls.name: TauCeti.positiveDefiniteKernelFinsuppSesqForm_isPosSemidef
decls.doc: Positive-definite kernels give positive-semidefinite finitely supported sesquilinear forms.
decls.statement:
theorem positiveDefiniteKernelFinsuppSesqForm_isPosSemidef
    (hK : IsPositiveDefiniteKernel K) :
    (positiveDefiniteKernelFinsuppSesqForm K).IsPosSemidef

decls.name: TauCeti.positiveDefiniteKernelFinsuppForm_isPositiveDefiniteKernel
decls.doc:
The finitely supported Gram form of a positive-definite kernel is itself a positive-definite
kernel on the finitely supported coefficient space.
decls.statement:
theorem positiveDefiniteKernelFinsuppForm_isPositiveDefiniteKernel
    (hK : IsPositiveDefiniteKernel K) :
    IsPositiveDefiniteKernel fun x y : α →₀ 𝕜 =>
      positiveDefiniteKernelFinsuppForm K x y

decls.name: TauCeti.positiveDefiniteKernelFinsuppForm_single_single
decls.doc: The finitely supported Gram form takes the expected value on two basis vectors.
decls.statement:
theorem positiveDefiniteKernelFinsuppForm_single_single (a b : α) (r s : 𝕜) :
    positiveDefiniteKernelFinsuppForm K (Finsupp.single a r) (Finsupp.single b s)
      = conj r * s * K a b

decls.name: TauCeti.RCLike.cast_normSq_eq_norm_sq
decls.statement:
theorem RCLike.cast_normSq_eq_norm_sq (r : 𝕜) :
    ((‖r‖ : 𝕜) ^ 2) = (RCLike.normSq r : 𝕜)

decls.name: TauCeti.positiveDefiniteKernelFinsuppForm_single_self
decls.doc:
On a single finitely supported basis vector, the diagonal Gram form is the scalar norm-square
times the corresponding diagonal kernel value.
decls.statement:
theorem positiveDefiniteKernelFinsuppForm_single_self (a : α) (r : 𝕜) :
    positiveDefiniteKernelFinsuppForm K (Finsupp.single a r) (Finsupp.single a r)
      = RCLike.normSq r * K a a

decls.name: TauCeti.positiveDefiniteKernelFinsuppSesqFormKer
decls.doc:
The radical, or null submodule, of the finitely supported Gram form attached to a kernel.

This is the submodule by which the free space `α →₀ 𝕜` is quotiented in the algebraic
GNS/Kolmogorov construction. It is defined as the kernel of the bundled sesquilinear form, so
membership means pairing to zero with every finitely supported vector.
decls.statement:
def positiveDefiniteKernelFinsuppSesqFormKer
    (K : α → α → 𝕜) : Submodule 𝕜 (α →₀ 𝕜)

decls.name: TauCeti.mem_positiveDefiniteKernelFinsuppSesqFormKer
decls.doc:
Membership in the null submodule means that the finitely supported vector pairs to zero with
every vector.
decls.statement:
theorem mem_positiveDefiniteKernelFinsuppSesqFormKer
    (x : α →₀ 𝕜) :
    x ∈ positiveDefiniteKernelFinsuppSesqFormKer K ↔
      ∀ y : α →₀ 𝕜, positiveDefiniteKernelFinsuppForm K x y = 0

decls.name: TauCeti.positiveDefiniteKernelFinsuppForm_eq_zero_of_mem_ker_left
decls.doc: A vector in the null submodule pairs to zero with every vector on the left.
decls.statement:
theorem positiveDefiniteKernelFinsuppForm_eq_zero_of_mem_ker_left
    {x y : α →₀ 𝕜} (hx : x ∈ positiveDefiniteKernelFinsuppSesqFormKer K) :
    positiveDefiniteKernelFinsuppForm K x y = 0

decls.name: TauCeti.positiveDefiniteKernelFinsuppForm_self_eq_zero_of_mem_ker
decls.doc: A vector in the null submodule has zero diagonal Gram value.
decls.statement:
theorem positiveDefiniteKernelFinsuppForm_self_eq_zero_of_mem_ker
    {x : α →₀ 𝕜} (hx : x ∈ positiveDefiniteKernelFinsuppSesqFormKer K) :
    positiveDefiniteKernelFinsuppForm K x x = 0

decls.name: TauCeti.positiveDefiniteKernelFinsuppForm_self_eq_zero_iff_mem_ker
decls.doc:
For a positive-definite kernel, zero finitely supported Gram seminorm characterizes the null
submodule.
decls.statement:
theorem positiveDefiniteKernelFinsuppForm_self_eq_zero_iff_mem_ker
    (hK : IsPositiveDefiniteKernel K) {x : α →₀ 𝕜} :
    positiveDefiniteKernelFinsuppForm K x x = 0 ↔
      x ∈ positiveDefiniteKernelFinsuppSesqFormKer K

decls.name: TauCeti.positiveDefiniteKernelFinsuppForm_eq_zero_of_mem_ker_right_of_conj_symm
decls.doc:
For a conjugate-symmetric kernel, a vector in the null submodule also pairs to zero on the
right. This is the column-vanishing form obtained from symmetry of the bundled sesquilinear
form.
decls.statement:
theorem positiveDefiniteKernelFinsuppForm_eq_zero_of_mem_ker_right_of_conj_symm
    (hsymm : ∀ a b, conj (K a b) = K b a) {x y : α →₀ 𝕜}
    (hy : y ∈ positiveDefiniteKernelFinsuppSesqFormKer K) :
    positiveDefiniteKernelFinsuppForm K x y = 0

decls.name: TauCeti.positiveDefiniteKernelFinsuppForm_eq_zero_of_mem_ker_right
decls.doc:
For a positive-definite kernel, a vector in the null submodule also pairs to zero on the
right. This is the column-vanishing form obtained from conjugate symmetry.
decls.statement:
theorem positiveDefiniteKernelFinsuppForm_eq_zero_of_mem_ker_right
    (hK : IsPositiveDefiniteKernel K) {x y : α →₀ 𝕜}
    (hy : y ∈ positiveDefiniteKernelFinsuppSesqFormKer K) :
    positiveDefiniteKernelFinsuppForm K x y = 0

decls.name: TauCeti.isPositiveDefiniteKernel_of_tendsto
decls.doc:
Positive-definite kernels are preserved under pointwise limits along a nontrivial filter. The
hypothesis on positive-definiteness is eventual, so this applies equally to nets that are
eventually positive definite.
decls.statement:
theorem isPositiveDefiniteKernel_of_tendsto {ι : Type*} {l : Filter ι} [NeBot l]
    {K : ι → α → α → 𝕜} {L : α → α → 𝕜}
    (hK : ∀ᶠ i in l, IsPositiveDefiniteKernel (K i))
    (hlim : ∀ a b : α, Tendsto (fun i => K i a b) l (𝓝 (L a b))) :
    IsPositiveDefiniteKernel L

decls.name: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefinite.of_tendsto
decls.doc:
Positive-definiteness is preserved under pointwise limits along a nontrivial filter. The
hypothesis on positive-definiteness is eventual, so this applies equally to nets that are
eventually positive definite.
decls.statement:
theorem of_tendsto {ι : Type*} {l : Filter ι} [NeBot l] {F : ι → M → ℂ} {G : M → ℂ}
    (hF : ∀ᶠ i in l, IsPositiveDefinite (F i))
    (hlim : ∀ x : M, Tendsto (fun i => F i x) l (𝓝 (G x))) :
    IsPositiveDefinite G

decls.name: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefinite.of_forall_tendsto
decls.doc:
A pointwise limit of a family of positive-definite functions is positive definite. This is the
non-eventual form of `TauCeti.IsPositiveDefinite.of_tendsto`.
decls.statement:
theorem of_forall_tendsto {ι : Type*} {l : Filter ι} [NeBot l] {F : ι → M → ℂ} {G : M → ℂ}
    (hF : ∀ i, IsPositiveDefinite (F i))
    (hlim : ∀ x : M, Tendsto (fun i => F i x) l (𝓝 (G x))) :
    IsPositiveDefinite G

decls.name: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefinite.of_seq_tendsto
decls.doc: Sequential pointwise limits of eventually positive-definite functions are positive definite.
decls.statement:
theorem of_seq_tendsto {F : ℕ → M → ℂ} {G : M → ℂ}
    (hF : ∀ᶠ n in atTop, IsPositiveDefinite (F n))
    (hlim : ∀ x : M, Tendsto (fun n => F n x) atTop (𝓝 (G x))) :
    IsPositiveDefinite G

decls.name: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefinite.of_tendstoLocallyUniformly
decls.doc:
A locally uniform limit of eventually positive-definite functions is positive definite.

Unlike continuity, positive-definiteness itself only needs pointwise convergence; local uniform
convergence is converted to pointwise convergence before applying
`TauCeti.IsPositiveDefinite.of_tendsto`.
decls.statement:
theorem of_tendstoLocallyUniformly {ι : Type*} {l : Filter ι} [NeBot l]
    {F : ι → M → ℂ} {G : M → ℂ}
    (hF : ∀ᶠ i in l, IsPositiveDefinite (F i))
    (hlim : TendstoLocallyUniformly F G l) :
    IsPositiveDefinite G

decls.name: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefinite.normalizeScalar_nonneg
decls.doc: The normalizing scalar `((F 0).re)⁻¹`, viewed as a complex number, is nonnegative.
decls.statement:
theorem normalizeScalar_nonneg (hF : IsPositiveDefinite F) :
    0 ≤ (((F 0).re)⁻¹ : ℂ)

decls.name: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefinite.normalize
decls.doc:
Multiplying a positive-definite function by the reciprocal of its real value at the origin
preserves positive-definiteness. If `F 0 = 0` this gives the zero scaling; the separate
`normalize_apply_zero` lemma below records the useful nonzero case.
decls.statement:
theorem normalize (hF : IsPositiveDefinite F) :
    IsPositiveDefinite (fun x => (((F 0).re)⁻¹ : ℂ) * F x)

decls.name: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefinite.normalize_apply_zero
decls.doc: The normalized positive-definite function has value `1` at the origin.
decls.statement:
theorem normalize_apply_zero (hF : IsPositiveDefinite F) (h0 : F 0 ≠ 0) :
    (((F 0).re)⁻¹ : ℂ) * F 0 = 1

decls.name: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefinite.norm_normalize_apply_le_one_of_add_star_eq_zero
decls.doc:
At points satisfying `a + star a = 0`, the normalized positive-definite function is bounded
by `1`. When `F 0 = 0` the normalizing scalar is `0`, so the bound holds trivially.
decls.statement:
theorem norm_normalize_apply_le_one_of_add_star_eq_zero (hF : IsPositiveDefinite F)
    (a : M) (ha : a + star a = 0) :
    ‖(((F 0).re)⁻¹ : ℂ) * F a‖ ≤ 1

decls.name: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefinite.norm_normalize_apply_le_one_of_star_eq_neg
decls.doc:
Under the negation involution, the normalized positive-definite function is bounded by `1` at
every point.
decls.statement:
theorem norm_normalize_apply_le_one_of_star_eq_neg (hH : IsPositiveDefinite H)
    (a : G) (hstar_a : star a = -a) :
    ‖(((H 0).re)⁻¹ : ℂ) * H a‖ ≤ 1

decls.name: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefinite.norm_normalize_apply_le_one_of_forall_star_eq_neg
decls.doc:
If the involution is negation everywhere, the normalized positive-definite function is
uniformly bounded by `1`.
decls.statement:
theorem norm_normalize_apply_le_one_of_forall_star_eq_neg (hH : IsPositiveDefinite H)
    (hstar : ∀ a : G, star a = -a) (a : G) :
    ‖(((H 0).re)⁻¹ : ℂ) * H a‖ ≤ 1

decls.name: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefinite.comp
decls.doc:
Positive-definiteness is preserved by pullback along a star-preserving additive
homomorphism. This is stated for Mathlib's homomorphism classes so it applies to bundled
additive homomorphisms, star algebra homomorphisms, and similar maps.
decls.statement:
theorem comp {Φ : Type*} [FunLike Φ N M] [AddHomClass Φ N M] [StarHomClass Φ N M]
    (hF : IsPositiveDefinite F) (φ : Φ) : IsPositiveDefinite (fun x : N => F (φ x))

decls.name: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefinite.comp_addMonoidHom
decls.doc:
The explicit `AddMonoidHom` form of pullback: a star-preserving additive homomorphism
pulls back positive-definite functions to positive-definite functions.
decls.statement:
theorem comp_addMonoidHom (hF : IsPositiveDefinite F) (φ : N →+ M)
    (hstar : ∀ x : N, φ (star x) = star (φ x)) :
    IsPositiveDefinite (fun x : N => F (φ x))

decls.name: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefinite.comp_smul
decls.doc:
Rescaling the argument by a scalar preserves positive-definiteness, whenever the involution
on the domain is negation: if `F` is positive definite then so is `x ↦ F (r • x)`.
decls.statement:
theorem comp_smul {G : Type*} [AddGroup G] [StarAddMonoid G] {R : Type*} [DistribSMul R G]
    {F : G → ℂ} (hF : IsPositiveDefinite F) (hstar : ∀ x : G, star x = -x) (r : R) :
    IsPositiveDefinite fun x : G => F (r • x)

decls.name: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefinite.of_comp_surjective
decls.doc:
Positive-definiteness descends along a surjective star-preserving additive homomorphism:
if `F ∘ φ` is positive definite and every point of the codomain is in the range of `φ`, then
`F` is positive definite.
decls.statement:
theorem of_comp_surjective {Φ : Type*} [FunLike Φ N M] [AddHomClass Φ N M]
    (φ : Φ) (hstar : ∀ x : N, φ (star x) = star (φ x))
    (hsurj : Function.Surjective φ) (hcomp : IsPositiveDefinite (fun x : N => F (φ x))) :
    IsPositiveDefinite F

decls.name: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefinite.comp_iff_of_surjective
decls.doc:
Along a surjective star-preserving additive homomorphism, a function is positive definite
if and only if its pullback is positive definite.
decls.statement:
theorem comp_iff_of_surjective {Φ : Type*} [FunLike Φ N M] [AddHomClass Φ N M]
    [StarHomClass Φ N M] (φ : Φ) (hsurj : Function.Surjective φ) :
    IsPositiveDefinite (fun x : N => F (φ x)) ↔ IsPositiveDefinite F

decls.name: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefinite.comp_addMonoidHom_iff_of_surjective
decls.doc: The explicit `AddMonoidHom` form of the pullback equivalence for surjective maps.
decls.statement:
theorem comp_addMonoidHom_iff_of_surjective (φ : N →+ M)
    (hstar : ∀ x : N, φ (star x) = star (φ x)) (hsurj : Function.Surjective φ) :
    IsPositiveDefinite (fun x : N => F (φ x)) ↔ IsPositiveDefinite F

decls.name: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefinite.comp_addEquiv_iff
decls.doc:
Positive-definiteness is invariant under precomposition with a star-preserving additive
equivalence.
decls.statement:
theorem comp_addEquiv_iff (e : N ≃+ M) (hstar : ∀ x : N, e (star x) = star (e x)) :
    IsPositiveDefinite (fun x : N => F (e x)) ↔ IsPositiveDefinite F

decls.name: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefinite.comp_fst
decls.doc:
Pulling back a positive-definite function along the first projection from a product
preserves positive-definiteness.
decls.statement:
theorem comp_fst (hF : IsPositiveDefinite F) :
    IsPositiveDefinite (fun x : M × N => F x.1)

decls.name: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefinite.comp_snd
decls.doc:
Pulling back a positive-definite function along the second projection from a product
preserves positive-definiteness.
decls.statement:
theorem comp_snd (hG : IsPositiveDefinite G) :
    IsPositiveDefinite (fun x : M × N => G x.2)

decls.name: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefinite.mul_comp_fst_snd
decls.doc:
The product of two positive-definite functions, pulled back from the two factors of a
product monoid, is positive definite. This is the basic product-domain construction obtained by
combining pullback along projections with the Schur product closure.
decls.statement:
theorem mul_comp_fst_snd (hF : IsPositiveDefinite F) (hG : IsPositiveDefinite G) :
    IsPositiveDefinite (fun x : M × N => F x.1 * G x.2)

decls.name: TauCeti.BCRPoint
decls.doc:
The additive monoid `ℝ≥0 × V` equipped with the BCR involution `(t, v) ↦ (t, -v)`.

This wrapper avoids installing a global negation `StarAddMonoid` instance on an arbitrary
additive group `V`.
decls.statement: structure BCRPoint (V : Type*)

decls.name: TauCeti.BCRPoint.ofProd
decls.doc:
Convert a product point to the local BCR wrapper. Internal helper, not part of the public
API.
decls.statement: def ofProd (p : ℝ≥0 × V) : BCRPoint V

decls.name: TauCeti.BCRPoint.toProd
decls.doc:
Convert a local BCR wrapper back to the product type. Internal helper, not part of the public
API.
decls.statement: def toProd (p : BCRPoint V) : ℝ≥0 × V

decls.name: TauCeti.BCRPoint.ext
decls.statement:
theorem ext {p q : BCRPoint V} (ht : p.time = q.time) (hv : p.point = q.point) :
    p = q

decls.name: TauCeti.BCRPoint.instZeroBCRPointOfAddCommGroup
decls.statement: instance [AddCommGroup V] : Zero (BCRPoint V)

decls.name: TauCeti.BCRPoint.instAddBCRPointOfAddCommGroup
decls.statement: instance [AddCommGroup V] : Add (BCRPoint V)

decls.name: TauCeti.BCRPoint.instStarBCRPointOfAddCommGroup
decls.statement: instance [AddCommGroup V] : Star (BCRPoint V)

decls.name: TauCeti.BCRPoint.zero_time
decls.statement: theorem zero_time [AddCommGroup V] : (0 : BCRPoint V).time = 0

decls.name: TauCeti.BCRPoint.zero_point
