decls.statement: theorem zero_point [AddCommGroup V] : (0 : BCRPoint V).point = 0

decls.name: TauCeti.BCRPoint.add_time
decls.statement:
theorem add_time [AddCommGroup V] (p q : BCRPoint V) :
    (p + q).time = p.time + q.time

decls.name: TauCeti.BCRPoint.add_point
decls.statement:
theorem add_point [AddCommGroup V] (p q : BCRPoint V) :
    (p + q).point = p.point + q.point

decls.name: TauCeti.BCRPoint.star_time
decls.statement: theorem star_time [AddCommGroup V] (p : BCRPoint V) : (star p).time = p.time

decls.name: TauCeti.BCRPoint.star_point
decls.statement: theorem star_point [AddCommGroup V] (p : BCRPoint V) : (star p).point = -p.point

decls.name: TauCeti.BCRPoint.instAddCommMonoidBCRPointOfAddCommGroup
decls.statement: instance [AddCommGroup V] : AddCommMonoid (BCRPoint V)

decls.name: TauCeti.BCRPoint.instStarAddMonoidBCRPoint
decls.statement: instance [AddCommGroup V] : StarAddMonoid (BCRPoint V)

decls.name: TauCeti.IsSemigroupGroupPD
decls.doc:
A function on `ℝ≥0 × V` is semigroup-group positive definite, in the
Berg--Christensen--Ressel sense, if all finite quadratic forms formed using the involution
`(t, v) ↦ (t, -v)` are nonnegative:
`∑ᵢⱼ cᵢ conj(cⱼ) F(tᵢ + tⱼ, vᵢ - vⱼ) ≥ 0`.
decls.statement: def IsSemigroupGroupPD (F : ℝ≥0 × V → ℂ) : Prop

decls.name: TauCeti.isSemigroupGroupPD_iff_isPositiveDefiniteKernel
decls.doc:
The bridge from semigroup-group positive definiteness to the associated positive-definite
kernel.
decls.statement:
theorem isSemigroupGroupPD_iff_isPositiveDefiniteKernel :
    IsSemigroupGroupPD F ↔
      IsPositiveDefiniteKernel fun p q : ℝ≥0 × V => F (p.1 + q.1, p.2 - q.2)

decls.name: TauCeti.IsSemigroupGroupPD.isPositiveDefiniteKernel
decls.doc: The kernel associated to a semigroup-group positive-definite function is positive definite.
decls.statement:
theorem IsSemigroupGroupPD.isPositiveDefiniteKernel (hF : IsSemigroupGroupPD F) :
    IsPositiveDefiniteKernel fun p q : ℝ≥0 × V => F (p.1 + q.1, p.2 - q.2)

decls.name: TauCeti.IsSemigroupGroupPD.of_isPositiveDefiniteKernel
decls.doc:
Build a semigroup-group positive-definite function from the associated positive-definite
kernel.
decls.statement:
theorem IsSemigroupGroupPD.of_isPositiveDefiniteKernel
    (hF : IsPositiveDefiniteKernel fun p q : ℝ≥0 × V => F (p.1 + q.1, p.2 - q.2)) :
    IsSemigroupGroupPD F

decls.name: TauCeti.isSemigroupGroupPD_const_of_nonneg
decls.doc: A nonnegative complex constant is semigroup-group positive definite.
decls.statement:
theorem isSemigroupGroupPD_const_of_nonneg {k : ℂ} (hk : 0 ≤ k) :
    IsSemigroupGroupPD (fun _ : ℝ≥0 × V => k)

decls.name: TauCeti.isSemigroupGroupPD_zero
decls.doc: The zero function is semigroup-group positive definite.
decls.statement:
theorem isSemigroupGroupPD_zero :
    IsSemigroupGroupPD (fun _ : ℝ≥0 × V => (0 : ℂ))

decls.name: TauCeti.isSemigroupGroupPD_one
decls.doc: The constant-one function is semigroup-group positive definite.
decls.statement:
theorem isSemigroupGroupPD_one :
    IsSemigroupGroupPD (fun _ : ℝ≥0 × V => (1 : ℂ))

decls.name: TauCeti.isSemigroupGroupPD_iff
decls.doc: The finite quadratic-form characterization of semigroup-group positive definiteness.
decls.statement:
theorem isSemigroupGroupPD_iff :
    IsSemigroupGroupPD F ↔
      (∀ p q : ℝ≥0 × V, conj (F (p.1 + q.1, p.2 - q.2))
        = F (q.1 + p.1, q.2 - p.2)) ∧
        ∀ {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] (c : ι → ℂ) (p : ι → ℝ≥0 × V),
          0 ≤ ∑ i, ∑ j, c i * conj (c j) *
            F ((p i).1 + (p j).1, (p i).2 - (p j).2)

decls.name: TauCeti.IsSemigroupGroupPD.sum_nonneg
decls.doc:
Positive-definiteness holds for arbitrary finite BCR families: for every finite family of
scalars `c` and points `p`, the quadratic form
`∑ i, ∑ j, c i * conj (c j) * F ((p i).1 + (p j).1, (p i).2 - (p j).2)` is nonnegative.
decls.statement:
theorem sum_nonneg (hF : IsSemigroupGroupPD F) {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι]
    (c : ι → ℂ) (p : ι → ℝ≥0 × V) :
    0 ≤ ∑ i, ∑ j, c i * conj (c j) *
      F ((p i).1 + (p j).1, (p i).2 - (p j).2)

decls.name: TauCeti.IsSemigroupGroupPD.quadForm_two_nonneg
decls.doc: The `2 × 2` BCR Hermitian sub-form at two points.
decls.statement:
theorem quadForm_two_nonneg (hF : IsSemigroupGroupPD F) (p q : ℝ≥0 × V) (c₀ c₁ : ℂ) :
    0 ≤ c₀ * conj c₀ * F (p.1 + p.1, p.2 - p.2)
      + c₀ * conj c₁ * F (p.1 + q.1, p.2 - q.2)
      + c₁ * conj c₀ * F (q.1 + p.1, q.2 - p.2)
      + c₁ * conj c₁ * F (q.1 + q.1, q.2 - q.2)

decls.name: TauCeti.IsSemigroupGroupPD.conj_symm
decls.doc:
A semigroup-group positive-definite function is conjugate symmetric for the BCR kernel:
`conj (F (t + u, v - w)) = F (u + t, w - v)`.
decls.statement:
theorem conj_symm (hF : IsSemigroupGroupPD F) (p q : ℝ≥0 × V) :
    conj (F (p.1 + q.1, p.2 - q.2)) = F (q.1 + p.1, q.2 - p.2)

decls.name: TauCeti.IsSemigroupGroupPD.diagonal_nonneg
decls.doc:
Values of a semigroup-group positive-definite function on the time diagonal `(t + t, 0)` are
real and nonnegative.
decls.statement: theorem diagonal_nonneg (hF : IsSemigroupGroupPD F) (t : ℝ≥0) : 0 ≤ F (t + t, 0)

decls.name: TauCeti.IsSemigroupGroupPD.diagonal_im
decls.doc:
Values of a semigroup-group positive-definite function on the time diagonal `(t + t, 0)` have
zero imaginary part.
decls.statement: theorem diagonal_im (hF : IsSemigroupGroupPD F) (t : ℝ≥0) : (F (t + t, 0)).im = 0

decls.name: TauCeti.IsSemigroupGroupPD.diagonal_re_nonneg
decls.doc:
The real part of a semigroup-group positive-definite function on the time diagonal
`(t + t, 0)` is nonnegative.
decls.statement:
theorem diagonal_re_nonneg (hF : IsSemigroupGroupPD F) (t : ℝ≥0) :
    0 ≤ (F (t + t, 0)).re

decls.name: TauCeti.IsSemigroupGroupPD.diagonal_eq_ofReal_re
decls.doc:
A semigroup-group positive-definite function on the time diagonal `(t + t, 0)` is equal to
its real part, viewed as a complex number.
decls.statement:
theorem diagonal_eq_ofReal_re (hF : IsSemigroupGroupPD F) (t : ℝ≥0) :
    F (t + t, 0) = ((F (t + t, 0)).re : ℂ)

decls.name: TauCeti.IsSemigroupGroupPD.map_zero_nonneg
decls.doc:
The value of a semigroup-group positive-definite function at `(0, 0)` is real and
nonnegative.
decls.statement: theorem map_zero_nonneg (hF : IsSemigroupGroupPD F) : 0 ≤ F (0, 0)

decls.name: TauCeti.IsSemigroupGroupPD.map_zero_im
decls.doc:
The value of a semigroup-group positive-definite function at `(0, 0)` has zero imaginary
part.
decls.statement: theorem map_zero_im (hF : IsSemigroupGroupPD F) : (F (0, 0)).im = 0

decls.name: TauCeti.IsSemigroupGroupPD.map_zero_re_nonneg
decls.doc:
The real part of the value of a semigroup-group positive-definite function at `(0, 0)` is
nonnegative.
decls.statement: theorem map_zero_re_nonneg (hF : IsSemigroupGroupPD F) : 0 ≤ (F (0, 0)).re

decls.name: TauCeti.IsSemigroupGroupPD.map_zero_eq_ofReal_re
decls.doc:
The value at `(0, 0)` of a semigroup-group positive-definite function is equal to its real
part, viewed as a complex number.
decls.statement: theorem map_zero_eq_ofReal_re (hF : IsSemigroupGroupPD F) : F (0, 0) = ((F (0, 0)).re : ℂ)

decls.name: TauCeti.IsSemigroupGroupPD.map_zero_re_pos_of_ne_zero
decls.doc:
If a semigroup-group positive-definite function is nonzero at the origin, then the real
part of its value at the origin is strictly positive.
decls.statement:
theorem map_zero_re_pos_of_ne_zero (hF : IsSemigroupGroupPD F) (h0 : F (0, 0) ≠ 0) :
    0 < (F (0, 0)).re

decls.name: TauCeti.IsSemigroupGroupPD.add
decls.doc: Semigroup-group positive-definite functions are closed under addition.
decls.statement:
theorem add (hF : IsSemigroupGroupPD F) (hG : IsSemigroupGroupPD G) :
    IsSemigroupGroupPD fun x => F x + G x

decls.name: TauCeti.IsSemigroupGroupPD.const_mul
decls.doc:
Semigroup-group positive-definite functions are closed under multiplication by a
nonnegative complex scalar.
decls.statement:
theorem const_mul {k : ℂ} (hk : 0 ≤ k) (hF : IsSemigroupGroupPD F) :
    IsSemigroupGroupPD fun x => k * F x

decls.name: TauCeti.IsSemigroupGroupPD.smul_of_nonneg
decls.doc:
Semigroup-group positive-definite functions are closed under multiplication by a
nonnegative real scalar.
decls.statement:
theorem smul_of_nonneg {r : ℝ} (hr : 0 ≤ r) (hF : IsSemigroupGroupPD F) :
    IsSemigroupGroupPD fun x => r • F x

decls.name: TauCeti.IsSemigroupGroupPD.mul
decls.doc:
Semigroup-group positive-definite functions are closed under pointwise multiplication
(Schur product).
decls.statement:
theorem mul (hF : IsSemigroupGroupPD F) (hG : IsSemigroupGroupPD G) :
    IsSemigroupGroupPD fun x => F x * G x

decls.name: TauCeti.IsSemigroupGroupPD.sum
decls.doc: Semigroup-group positive-definite functions are closed under finite sums.

decls.name: TauCeti.IsSemigroupGroupPD.prod
decls.doc:
Semigroup-group positive-definite functions are closed under finite products
(Schur products).

decls.name: TauCeti.IsSemigroupGroupPD.normSq_le
decls.doc:
The BCR Cauchy--Schwarz estimate. For a semigroup-group positive-definite function, the
kernel entry `F (p.1 + q.1, p.2 - q.2)` has squared norm bounded by the product of the two
time-diagonal real parts.
decls.statement:
theorem normSq_le (hF : IsSemigroupGroupPD F) (p q : ℝ≥0 × V) :
    RCLike.normSq (F (p.1 + q.1, p.2 - q.2))
      ≤ RCLike.re (F (p.1 + p.1, 0)) * RCLike.re (F (q.1 + q.1, 0))

decls.name: TauCeti.IsSemigroupGroupPD.normSq_apply_le
decls.doc: Coordinate form of the BCR Cauchy--Schwarz estimate.
decls.statement:
theorem normSq_apply_le (hF : IsSemigroupGroupPD F) (t u : ℝ≥0) (v w : V) :
    RCLike.normSq (F (t + u, v - w))
      ≤ RCLike.re (F (t + t, 0)) * RCLike.re (F (u + u, 0))

decls.name: TauCeti.IsSemigroupGroupPD.eq_zero_of_diagonal_eq_zero_left
decls.doc:
If the left time-diagonal value is zero, then the corresponding BCR-kernel row entry is
zero.
decls.statement:
theorem eq_zero_of_diagonal_eq_zero_left (hF : IsSemigroupGroupPD F) {p q : ℝ≥0 × V}
    (hp : F (p.1 + p.1, 0) = 0) : F (p.1 + q.1, p.2 - q.2) = 0

decls.name: TauCeti.IsSemigroupGroupPD.apply_eq_zero_of_diagonal_eq_zero_left
decls.doc: Coordinate form of `eq_zero_of_diagonal_eq_zero_left`.
decls.statement:
theorem apply_eq_zero_of_diagonal_eq_zero_left (hF : IsSemigroupGroupPD F)
    {t u : ℝ≥0} {v w : V} (ht : F (t + t, 0) = 0) : F (t + u, v - w) = 0

decls.name: TauCeti.IsSemigroupGroupPD.eq_zero_of_diagonal_eq_zero_right
decls.doc:
If the right time-diagonal value is zero, then the corresponding BCR-kernel column entry is
zero.
decls.statement:
theorem eq_zero_of_diagonal_eq_zero_right (hF : IsSemigroupGroupPD F) {p q : ℝ≥0 × V}
    (hq : F (q.1 + q.1, 0) = 0) : F (p.1 + q.1, p.2 - q.2) = 0

decls.name: TauCeti.IsSemigroupGroupPD.apply_eq_zero_of_diagonal_eq_zero_right
decls.doc: Coordinate form of `eq_zero_of_diagonal_eq_zero_right`.
decls.statement:
theorem apply_eq_zero_of_diagonal_eq_zero_right (hF : IsSemigroupGroupPD F)
    {t u : ℝ≥0} {v w : V} (hu : F (u + u, 0) = 0) : F (t + u, v - w) = 0

decls.name: TauCeti.IsSemigroupGroupPD.norm_le_one_of_diagonal_eq_one
decls.doc:
If both time-diagonal entries are normalized to `1`, then the corresponding BCR-kernel entry
has norm at most `1`.

decls.name: TauCeti.IsSemigroupGroupPD.norm_apply_le_one_of_diagonal_eq_one
decls.doc: Coordinate form of the normalized BCR-kernel bound.
decls.statement:
theorem norm_apply_le_one_of_diagonal_eq_one (hF : IsSemigroupGroupPD F)
    {t u : ℝ≥0} {v w : V} (ht : F (t + t, 0) = 1) (hu : F (u + u, 0) = 1) :
    ‖F (t + u, v - w)‖ ≤ 1

decls.name: TauCeti.laplaceAtom
decls.doc: The Laplace atom at `p : ℝ≥0`, as a complex-valued function on nonnegative time.
decls.statement: def laplaceAtom (p : ℝ≥0) (t : ℝ≥0) : ℂ

decls.name: TauCeti.laplaceAtom_def
decls.doc: The definitional exponential form of a Laplace atom.
decls.statement:
theorem laplaceAtom_def (p : ℝ≥0) (t : ℝ≥0) :
    laplaceAtom p t = (Real.exp (-(t : ℝ) * (p : ℝ)) : ℂ)

decls.name: TauCeti.laplaceAtom_add
decls.doc: Laplace atoms turn time addition into a rank-one positive-definite kernel.
decls.statement:
theorem laplaceAtom_add (p t u : ℝ≥0) :
    laplaceAtom p (t + u) = conj (laplaceAtom p t) * laplaceAtom p u

decls.name: TauCeti.isPositiveDefiniteKernel_laplaceAtom
decls.doc: The time kernel supplied by a Laplace atom is positive definite.
decls.statement:
theorem isPositiveDefiniteKernel_laplaceAtom (p : ℝ≥0) :
    IsPositiveDefiniteKernel fun t u : ℝ≥0 => laplaceAtom p (t + u)

decls.name: TauCeti.continuous_laplaceAtom
decls.doc: Laplace atoms are continuous in the nonnegative time variable.
decls.statement: theorem continuous_laplaceAtom (p : ℝ≥0) : Continuous (laplaceAtom p)

decls.name: TauCeti.isSemigroupGroupPD_laplaceFourierAtom
decls.doc: The separated Laplace--Fourier atom is semigroup-group positive definite.
decls.statement:
theorem isSemigroupGroupPD_laplaceFourierAtom (p : ℝ≥0) (q : V) :
    IsSemigroupGroupPD fun x : ℝ≥0 × V => laplaceAtom p x.1 * fourierAtom q x.2

decls.name: TauCeti.isSemigroupGroupPD_laplaceFourierAtom_and_continuous
decls.doc: The separated Laplace--Fourier atom is semigroup-group positive definite and continuous.
decls.statement:
theorem isSemigroupGroupPD_laplaceFourierAtom_and_continuous (p : ℝ≥0) (q : V) :
    IsSemigroupGroupPD (fun x : ℝ≥0 × V => laplaceAtom p x.1 * fourierAtom q x.2) ∧
      Continuous (fun x : ℝ≥0 × V => laplaceAtom p x.1 * fourierAtom q x.2)

decls.name: TauCeti.IsSemigroupGroupPD.normalizeScalar_nonneg
decls.doc: The normalizing scalar `((F (0, 0)).re)⁻¹`, viewed as a complex number, is nonnegative.
decls.statement:
theorem normalizeScalar_nonneg (hF : IsSemigroupGroupPD F) :
    0 ≤ (((F (0, 0)).re)⁻¹ : ℂ)

decls.name: TauCeti.IsSemigroupGroupPD.normalize
decls.doc:
Multiplying a semigroup-group positive-definite function by the reciprocal of its real value
at the origin preserves semigroup-group positive-definiteness. If `F (0, 0) = 0`, this is the
zero scaling; the separate `normalize_apply_zero` lemma records the useful nonzero case.
decls.statement:
theorem normalize (hF : IsSemigroupGroupPD F) :
    IsSemigroupGroupPD fun p => (((F (0, 0)).re)⁻¹ : ℂ) * F p

decls.name: TauCeti.IsSemigroupGroupPD.normalize_apply_zero
decls.doc: The normalized semigroup-group positive-definite function has value `1` at the origin.
decls.statement:
theorem normalize_apply_zero (hF : IsSemigroupGroupPD F) (h0 : F (0, 0) ≠ 0) :
    (((F (0, 0)).re)⁻¹ : ℂ) * F (0, 0) = 1

decls.name: TauCeti.IsSemigroupGroupPD.normalize_map_zero
decls.doc:
A normalized semigroup-group positive-definite function has origin value `1`, stated as the
map-zero lemma for the normalized function.
decls.statement:
theorem normalize_map_zero (hF : IsSemigroupGroupPD F) (h0 : F (0, 0) ≠ 0) :
    (fun p => (((F (0, 0)).re)⁻¹ : ℂ) * F p) (0, 0) = 1

decls.name: TauCeti.IsSemigroupGroupPD.normalize_apply_of_map_zero_eq_one
decls.doc:
If a semigroup-group positive-definite function is already normalized at the origin, the
explicit normalization leaves it unchanged pointwise.
decls.statement:
theorem normalize_apply_of_map_zero_eq_one (hF0 : F (0, 0) = 1) (p : ℝ≥0 × V) :
    (((F (0, 0)).re)⁻¹ : ℂ) * F p = F p

decls.name: TauCeti.IsSemigroupGroupPD.normalize_continuous
decls.doc: Normalization preserves continuity.
decls.statement:
theorem normalize_continuous [TopologicalSpace V] (hFcont : Continuous F) :
    Continuous fun p : ℝ≥0 × V => (((F (0, 0)).re)⁻¹ : ℂ) * F p

decls.name: TauCeti.IsSemigroupGroupPD.normalize_and_continuous
decls.doc: Package normalization with continuity preservation.
decls.statement:
theorem normalize_and_continuous (hFpd : IsSemigroupGroupPD F) (hFcont : Continuous F) :
    IsSemigroupGroupPD (fun p => (((F (0, 0)).re)⁻¹ : ℂ) * F p) ∧
      Continuous (fun p : ℝ≥0 × V => (((F (0, 0)).re)⁻¹ : ℂ) * F p)

decls.name: TauCeti.IsSemigroupGroupPD.norm_normalize_apply_le_one_of_norm_le_map_zero_re
decls.doc:
A function bounded by its origin value becomes bounded by `1` after normalization. This keeps
the boundedness hypothesis separate, as in the BCR representation theorem.
decls.statement:
theorem norm_normalize_apply_le_one_of_norm_le_map_zero_re
    (hbound : ∀ p : ℝ≥0 × V, ‖F p‖ ≤ (F (0, 0)).re) (p : ℝ≥0 × V) :
    ‖(((F (0, 0)).re)⁻¹ : ℂ) * F p‖ ≤ 1

decls.name: TauCeti.IsSemigroupGroupPD.norm_normalize_apply_le_one_of_norm_le_one_of_map_zero_eq_one
decls.doc:
If a semigroup-group positive-definite function is already bounded by `1` and normalized at
the origin, then applying the explicit normalization preserves the same bound.
decls.statement:
theorem norm_normalize_apply_le_one_of_norm_le_one_of_map_zero_eq_one
    (hF0 : F (0, 0) = 1) (hbound : ∀ p : ℝ≥0 × V, ‖F p‖ ≤ 1) (p : ℝ≥0 × V) :
    ‖(((F (0, 0)).re)⁻¹ : ℂ) * F p‖ ≤ 1

decls.name: TauCeti.isSemigroupGroupPD_mul_time_spatial_of_kernels
decls.doc:
If the time factor gives a positive-definite kernel `(t, u) ↦ f (t + u)`, and the spatial
factor gives a positive-definite subtraction kernel `(v, w) ↦ g (v - w)`, then their separated
product is semigroup-group positive definite.
decls.statement:
theorem isSemigroupGroupPD_mul_time_spatial_of_kernels
    {f : ℝ≥0 → ℂ} {g : V → ℂ}
    (hf : IsPositiveDefiniteKernel fun t u : ℝ≥0 => f (t + u))
    (hg : IsPositiveDefiniteKernel fun v w : V => g (v - w)) :
    IsSemigroupGroupPD fun p : ℝ≥0 × V => f p.1 * g p.2

decls.name: TauCeti.isSemigroupGroupPD_mul_time_spatial
decls.doc:
A separated product of a time positive-definite function and a spatial positive-definite
function is semigroup-group positive definite. The time factor uses Mathlib's trivial involution
on `ℝ≥0`; the spatial factor uses the supplied negation-involution hypothesis.
decls.statement:
theorem isSemigroupGroupPD_mul_time_spatial [StarAddMonoid V]
    {f : ℝ≥0 → ℂ} {g : V → ℂ}
    (hf : IsPositiveDefinite f) (hg : IsPositiveDefinite g)
    (hstar : ∀ v : V, star v = -v) :
    IsSemigroupGroupPD fun p : ℝ≥0 × V => f p.1 * g p.2

decls.name: TauCeti.continuous_mul_time_spatial
decls.doc: Separated products are continuous when both factors are continuous.
decls.statement:
theorem continuous_mul_time_spatial (hf : Continuous f) (hg : Continuous g) :
    Continuous fun p : ℝ≥0 × V => f p.1 * g p.2

decls.name: TauCeti.isSemigroupGroupPD_mul_time_spatial_and_continuous
decls.doc: Package the separated-product construction with continuity of the resulting BCR function.
decls.statement:
theorem isSemigroupGroupPD_mul_time_spatial_and_continuous [StarAddMonoid V]
    (hfpd : IsPositiveDefinite f) (hgpd : IsPositiveDefinite g)
    (hstar : ∀ v : V, star v = -v) (hfcont : Continuous f) (hgcont : Continuous g) :
    IsSemigroupGroupPD (fun p : ℝ≥0 × V => f p.1 * g p.2) ∧
      Continuous (fun p : ℝ≥0 × V => f p.1 * g p.2)

decls.name: TauCeti.isSemigroupGroupPD_mul_time_spatial_of_kernels_and_continuous
decls.doc: Kernel-supplied version of the separated-product construction, packaged with continuity.
decls.statement:
theorem isSemigroupGroupPD_mul_time_spatial_of_kernels_and_continuous
    (hf : IsPositiveDefiniteKernel fun t u : ℝ≥0 => f (t + u))
    (hg : IsPositiveDefiniteKernel fun v w : V => g (v - w))
    (hfcont : Continuous f) (hgcont : Continuous g) :
    IsSemigroupGroupPD (fun p : ℝ≥0 × V => f p.1 * g p.2) ∧
      Continuous (fun p : ℝ≥0 × V => f p.1 * g p.2)

decls.name: TauCeti.IsSemigroupGroupPD.map_sub_of_addHomClass
decls.statement:
theorem map_sub_of_addHomClass {Φ : Type*} [FunLike Φ W V] [AddHomClass Φ W V]
    (φ : Φ) (x y : W) : φ (x - y) = φ x - φ y

decls.name: TauCeti.IsSemigroupGroupPD.comp_spatial
decls.doc:
Pulling back the spatial coordinate of a semigroup-group positive-definite function along an
additive homomorphism preserves semigroup-group positive-definiteness. This is stated for
Mathlib's homomorphism classes so it applies to bundled additive homomorphisms, additive
equivalences, continuous linear maps, and similar maps.
decls.statement:
theorem comp_spatial {Φ : Type*} [FunLike Φ W V] [AddHomClass Φ W V]
    (hF : IsSemigroupGroupPD F) (φ : Φ) :
    IsSemigroupGroupPD fun p : ℝ≥0 × W => F (p.1, φ p.2)

decls.name: TauCeti.IsSemigroupGroupPD.comp_spatial_addMonoidHom
decls.doc: The explicit `AddMonoidHom` form of spatial pullback.
decls.statement:
theorem comp_spatial_addMonoidHom (hF : IsSemigroupGroupPD F) (φ : W →+ V) :
    IsSemigroupGroupPD fun p : ℝ≥0 × W => F (p.1, φ p.2)

decls.name: TauCeti.IsSemigroupGroupPD.comp_spatial_comp
decls.doc: Spatial pullbacks compose as expected.
decls.statement:
theorem comp_spatial_comp {Φ Ψ : Type*} [FunLike Φ W V] [AddHomClass Φ W V]
    [FunLike Ψ U W] [AddHomClass Ψ U W] (hF : IsSemigroupGroupPD F) (φ : Φ) (ψ : Ψ) :
    IsSemigroupGroupPD fun p : ℝ≥0 × U => F (p.1, φ (ψ p.2))

decls.name: TauCeti.IsSemigroupGroupPD.of_comp_spatial_surjective
decls.doc:
Semigroup-group positive-definiteness descends along a surjective spatial additive
homomorphism.
decls.statement:
theorem of_comp_spatial_surjective {Φ : Type*} [FunLike Φ W V] [AddHomClass Φ W V]
    (φ : Φ) (hsurj : Function.Surjective φ)
    (hcomp : IsSemigroupGroupPD fun p : ℝ≥0 × W => F (p.1, φ p.2)) :
    IsSemigroupGroupPD F

decls.name: TauCeti.IsSemigroupGroupPD.comp_spatial_iff_of_surjective
decls.doc:
Along a surjective spatial additive homomorphism, a function is semigroup-group positive
definite if and only if its spatial pullback is.
decls.statement:
theorem comp_spatial_iff_of_surjective {Φ : Type*} [FunLike Φ W V] [AddHomClass Φ W V]
    (φ : Φ) (hsurj : Function.Surjective φ) :
    IsSemigroupGroupPD (fun p : ℝ≥0 × W => F (p.1, φ p.2)) ↔ IsSemigroupGroupPD F

decls.name: TauCeti.IsSemigroupGroupPD.comp_spatial_addMonoidHom_iff_of_surjective
decls.doc: The explicit `AddMonoidHom` form of the spatial pullback equivalence for surjective maps.
decls.statement:
theorem comp_spatial_addMonoidHom_iff_of_surjective (φ : W →+ V)
    (hsurj : Function.Surjective φ) :
    IsSemigroupGroupPD (fun p : ℝ≥0 × W => F (p.1, φ p.2)) ↔ IsSemigroupGroupPD F

decls.name: TauCeti.IsSemigroupGroupPD.comp_spatial_addEquiv_iff
decls.doc:
Semigroup-group positive-definiteness is invariant under precomposition by a spatial
additive equivalence.
decls.statement:
theorem comp_spatial_addEquiv_iff (e : W ≃+ V) :
    IsSemigroupGroupPD (fun p : ℝ≥0 × W => F (p.1, e p.2)) ↔ IsSemigroupGroupPD F

decls.name: TauCeti.IsSemigroupGroupPD.continuous_comp_spatial
decls.doc: If the spatial map is continuous, spatial pullback preserves continuity.
decls.statement:
theorem continuous_comp_spatial (hF : Continuous F) (φ : W → V) (hφ : Continuous φ) :
    Continuous fun p : ℝ≥0 × W => F (p.1, φ p.2)

decls.name: TauCeti.IsSemigroupGroupPD.comp_spatial_and_continuous
decls.doc:
Package spatial pullback of a semigroup-group positive-definite function with continuity
of the pulled-back function.
decls.statement:
theorem comp_spatial_and_continuous {Φ : Type*} [FunLike Φ W V] [AddHomClass Φ W V]
    (hFpd : IsSemigroupGroupPD F) (hFcont : Continuous F) (φ : Φ) (hφ : Continuous φ) :
    IsSemigroupGroupPD (fun p : ℝ≥0 × W => F (p.1, φ p.2)) ∧
      Continuous (fun p : ℝ≥0 × W => F (p.1, φ p.2))

decls.name: TauCeti.IsSemigroupGroupPD.comp_spatial_continuousLinearMap
decls.doc:
Spatial pullback along a continuous linear map preserves semigroup-group
positive-definiteness.
decls.statement:
theorem comp_spatial_continuousLinearMap (hG : IsSemigroupGroupPD G) (φ : E' →L[ℝ] E) :
    IsSemigroupGroupPD fun p : ℝ≥0 × E' => G (p.1, φ p.2)

decls.name: TauCeti.IsSemigroupGroupPD.comp_spatial_continuousLinearEquiv_iff
decls.doc:
Spatial pullback along a continuous linear equivalence is an equivalence on
semigroup-group positive-definiteness.
decls.statement:
theorem comp_spatial_continuousLinearEquiv_iff (e : E' ≃L[ℝ] E) :
    IsSemigroupGroupPD (fun p : ℝ≥0 × E' => G (p.1, e p.2)) ↔ IsSemigroupGroupPD G

decls.name: TauCeti.IsSemigroupGroupPD.comp_spatial_continuousLinearMap_and_continuous
decls.doc: Package spatial pullback along a continuous linear map with preservation of continuity.
decls.statement:
theorem comp_spatial_continuousLinearMap_and_continuous (hGpd : IsSemigroupGroupPD G)
    (hGcont : Continuous G) (φ : E' →L[ℝ] E) :
    IsSemigroupGroupPD (fun p : ℝ≥0 × E' => G (p.1, φ p.2)) ∧
      Continuous (fun p : ℝ≥0 × E' => G (p.1, φ p.2))

decls.name: TauCeti.IsSemigroupGroupPD.timeAxis_isPositiveDefiniteKernel
decls.doc:
The zero-spatial time-axis kernel of a semigroup-group positive-definite function is positive
definite: `(t, u) ↦ F (t + u, 0)`.
decls.statement:
theorem timeAxis_isPositiveDefiniteKernel (hF : IsSemigroupGroupPD F) :
    IsPositiveDefiniteKernel fun t u : ℝ≥0 => F (t + u, 0)

decls.name: TauCeti.IsSemigroupGroupPD.timeAxis_conj_symm
decls.doc:
The zero-spatial time-axis kernel is conjugate symmetric:
`conj (F (t + u, 0)) = F (u + t, 0)`.
decls.statement:
theorem timeAxis_conj_symm (hF : IsSemigroupGroupPD F) (t u : ℝ≥0) :
    conj (F (t + u, 0)) = F (u + t, 0)

decls.name: TauCeti.IsSemigroupGroupPD.timeAxis_sum_nonneg
decls.doc: The finite quadratic form of the zero-spatial time-axis kernel is nonnegative.
decls.statement:
theorem timeAxis_sum_nonneg (hF : IsSemigroupGroupPD F) {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι]
    (t : ι → ℝ≥0) (x : ι → ℂ) :
    0 ≤ ∑ i, ∑ j, conj (x i) * x j * F (t i + t j, 0)

decls.name: TauCeti.IsSemigroupGroupPD.timeAxis_isPositiveDefinite
decls.doc:
The zero-spatial time-axis function `t ↦ F (t, 0)` is positive definite for the trivial
involution on `ℝ≥0`.
decls.statement:
theorem timeAxis_isPositiveDefinite (hF : IsSemigroupGroupPD F) :
    IsPositiveDefinite fun t : ℝ≥0 => F (t, 0)

decls.name: TauCeti.IsSemigroupGroupPD.timeAxis_normSq_le
decls.doc: The time-axis Cauchy--Schwarz estimate for `F (t + u, 0)`.
decls.statement:
theorem timeAxis_normSq_le (hF : IsSemigroupGroupPD F) (t u : ℝ≥0) :
    RCLike.normSq (F (t + u, 0))
      ≤ RCLike.re (F (t + t, 0)) * RCLike.re (F (u + u, 0))

decls.name: TauCeti.IsSemigroupGroupPD.timeAxis_isPositiveDefiniteKernel_and_continuous
decls.doc:
Package the positive-definite zero-spatial time-axis kernel with continuity of the
one-variable time-axis slice.
decls.statement:
theorem IsSemigroupGroupPD.timeAxis_isPositiveDefiniteKernel_and_continuous
    (hFpd : IsSemigroupGroupPD F) (hFcont : Continuous F) :
    IsPositiveDefiniteKernel (fun t u : ℝ≥0 => F (t + u, 0)) ∧
      Continuous (fun t : ℝ≥0 => F (t, 0))

decls.name: TauCeti.IsSemigroupGroupPD.timeSlice_isPositiveDefiniteKernel
decls.doc:
At every fixed time `t`, a semigroup-group positive-definite function gives the spatial
positive-definite kernel `(v, w) ↦ F (t, v - w)`.
decls.statement:
theorem timeSlice_isPositiveDefiniteKernel (hF : IsSemigroupGroupPD F) (t : ℝ≥0) :
    IsPositiveDefiniteKernel fun v w : V => F (t, v - w)

decls.name: TauCeti.IsSemigroupGroupPD.timeSlice_conj_symm
decls.doc:
Fixed-time slices are conjugate-symmetric in the spatial variable:
`conj (F (t, v - w)) = F (t, w - v)`.
decls.statement:
theorem timeSlice_conj_symm (hF : IsSemigroupGroupPD F) (t : ℝ≥0) (v w : V) :
    conj (F (t, v - w)) = F (t, w - v)

decls.name: TauCeti.IsSemigroupGroupPD.timeSlice_diagonal_nonneg
decls.doc: The diagonal value `F (t, 0)` of a fixed-time slice is real and nonnegative.
decls.statement: theorem timeSlice_diagonal_nonneg (hF : IsSemigroupGroupPD F) (t : ℝ≥0) : 0 ≤ F (t, 0)

decls.name: TauCeti.IsSemigroupGroupPD.timeSlice_diagonal_im
decls.doc: The diagonal value `F (t, 0)` of a fixed-time slice has zero imaginary part.
decls.statement: theorem timeSlice_diagonal_im (hF : IsSemigroupGroupPD F) (t : ℝ≥0) : (F (t, 0)).im = 0

decls.name: TauCeti.IsSemigroupGroupPD.timeSlice_diagonal_re_nonneg
decls.doc: The real part of the diagonal value `F (t, 0)` of a fixed-time slice is nonnegative.
decls.statement:
theorem timeSlice_diagonal_re_nonneg (hF : IsSemigroupGroupPD F) (t : ℝ≥0) :
    0 ≤ (F (t, 0)).re

decls.name: TauCeti.IsSemigroupGroupPD.timeSlice_diagonal_eq_ofReal_re
decls.doc:
The diagonal value `F (t, 0)` of a fixed-time slice is equal to its real part, viewed as a
complex number.
decls.statement:
theorem timeSlice_diagonal_eq_ofReal_re (hF : IsSemigroupGroupPD F) (t : ℝ≥0) :
    F (t, 0) = ((F (t, 0)).re : ℂ)

decls.name: TauCeti.IsSemigroupGroupPD.timeSlice_sum_nonneg
decls.doc: The fixed-time spatial quadratic form is nonnegative for arbitrary finite families.
decls.statement:
theorem timeSlice_sum_nonneg (hF : IsSemigroupGroupPD F) (t : ℝ≥0) {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι]
    (v : ι → V) (x : ι → ℂ) :
    0 ≤ ∑ i, ∑ j, conj (x i) * x j * F (t, v i - v j)

decls.name: TauCeti.IsSemigroupGroupPD.timeSlice_normSq_le
decls.doc: The fixed-time spatial Cauchy--Schwarz bound for the kernel entry `F (t, v - w)`.
decls.statement:
theorem timeSlice_normSq_le (hF : IsSemigroupGroupPD F) (t : ℝ≥0) (v w : V) :
    RCLike.normSq (F (t, v - w)) ≤ RCLike.re (F (t, 0)) * RCLike.re (F (t, 0))

decls.name: TauCeti.IsSemigroupGroupPD.norm_apply_le_timeSlice_diagonal_re
decls.doc:
At a fixed time, a semigroup-group positive-definite function is bounded by the real part of
its zero-spatial value.
decls.statement:
theorem norm_apply_le_timeSlice_diagonal_re (hF : IsSemigroupGroupPD F) (t : ℝ≥0) (v : V) :
    ‖F (t, v)‖ ≤ (F (t, 0)).re

decls.name: TauCeti.IsSemigroupGroupPD.timeSlice_eq_zero_of_timeSlice_diagonal_eq_zero
decls.doc: If the fixed-time diagonal value is zero, then the whole fixed-time spatial slice is zero.
decls.statement:
theorem timeSlice_eq_zero_of_timeSlice_diagonal_eq_zero (hF : IsSemigroupGroupPD F)
    {t : ℝ≥0} (ht : F (t, 0) = 0) (v : V) : F (t, v) = 0

decls.name: TauCeti.IsSemigroupGroupPD.norm_apply_le_one_of_timeSlice_diagonal_eq_one
decls.doc: Normalized fixed-time slices are bounded by `1`.
decls.statement:
theorem norm_apply_le_one_of_timeSlice_diagonal_eq_one (hF : IsSemigroupGroupPD F)
    {t : ℝ≥0} (ht : F (t, 0) = 1) (v : V) : ‖F (t, v)‖ ≤ 1

decls.name: TauCeti.IsSemigroupGroupPD.timeSlice_isPositiveDefinite
decls.doc:
If the spatial type is equipped with the negation involution, then each fixed-time slice is a
positive-definite function in the generic `IsPositiveDefinite` sense.
decls.statement:
theorem timeSlice_isPositiveDefinite [StarAddMonoid V]
    (hF : IsSemigroupGroupPD F) (hstar : ∀ v : V, star v = -v) (t : ℝ≥0) :
    IsPositiveDefinite fun v : V => F (t, v)

decls.name: TauCeti.IsSemigroupGroupPD.timeSlice_isPositiveDefiniteKernel_and_continuous
decls.doc:
Package the positive-definite kernel on a fixed-time slice with continuity of the
one-variable fixed-time slice.
decls.statement:
theorem IsSemigroupGroupPD.timeSlice_isPositiveDefiniteKernel_and_continuous
    (hFpd : IsSemigroupGroupPD F) (hFcont : Continuous F) (t : ℝ≥0) :
    IsPositiveDefiniteKernel (fun v w : V => F (t, v - w)) ∧ Continuous (fun v : V => F (t, v))

decls.name: TauCeti.Semigroups.StronglyContinuousSemigroup
decls.doc:
A strongly continuous one-parameter semigroup (C₀-semigroup) on a Banach space.

The semigroup is indexed by nonnegative real time. The axioms are `S 0 = Id`,
`S (s + t) = S s ∘ S t`, and strong continuity at `0`.
decls.statement: structure StronglyContinuousSemigroup

decls.name: TauCeti.Semigroups.StronglyContinuousSemigroup.instFunLike
decls.statement: instance instFunLike : FunLike (StronglyContinuousSemigroup X) ℝ≥0 (X →L[ℝ] X)

decls.name: TauCeti.Semigroups.StronglyContinuousSemigroup.ext
decls.statement: theorem ext {S T : StronglyContinuousSemigroup X} (h : ∀ t, S t = T t) : S = T

decls.name: TauCeti.Semigroups.StronglyContinuousSemigroup.map_zero
decls.doc: The native nonnegative-time operator at zero is the identity.
decls.statement:
theorem map_zero (S : StronglyContinuousSemigroup X) :
    S 0 = ContinuousLinearMap.id ℝ X

decls.name: TauCeti.Semigroups.StronglyContinuousSemigroup.map_zero_apply
decls.doc: Pointwise form of `StronglyContinuousSemigroup.map_zero`.
decls.statement:
theorem map_zero_apply (S : StronglyContinuousSemigroup X) (x : X) :
    S 0 x = x

decls.name: TauCeti.Semigroups.StronglyContinuousSemigroup.map_add
decls.doc: The native nonnegative-time semigroup law.
decls.statement:
theorem map_add (S : StronglyContinuousSemigroup X) (s t : ℝ≥0) :
    S (s + t) = (S s).comp (S t)

decls.name: TauCeti.Semigroups.StronglyContinuousSemigroup.map_add_apply
decls.doc: Pointwise form of `StronglyContinuousSemigroup.map_add`.
decls.statement:
theorem map_add_apply (S : StronglyContinuousSemigroup X) (s t : ℝ≥0) (x : X) :
    S (s + t) x = S s (S t x)

decls.name: TauCeti.Semigroups.StronglyContinuousSemigroup.norm_map_add_le
decls.doc: Submultiplicativity of the native nonnegative-time operator norm.
decls.statement:
theorem norm_map_add_le (S : StronglyContinuousSemigroup X) (s t : ℝ≥0) :
    ‖S (s + t)‖ ≤ ‖S s‖ * ‖S t‖

decls.name: TauCeti.Semigroups.StronglyContinuousSemigroup.continuousAt_zero
decls.doc: Strong continuity at zero for the native nonnegative-time action.
decls.statement:
theorem continuousAt_zero (S : StronglyContinuousSemigroup X) (x : X) :
    ContinuousAt (fun t : ℝ≥0 => S t x) 0

decls.name: TauCeti.Semigroups.StronglyContinuousSemigroup.continuousAt_zero_tendsto
decls.doc: Tendsto form of `StronglyContinuousSemigroup.continuousAt_zero`.
decls.statement:
theorem continuousAt_zero_tendsto (S : StronglyContinuousSemigroup X) (x : X) :
    Filter.Tendsto (fun t : ℝ≥0 => S t x) (nhds 0) (nhds x)

decls.name: TauCeti.Semigroups.StronglyContinuousSemigroup.realOperator
decls.doc: The semigroup as a function of real time, extended by `id` for `t < 0`.
decls.statement: def realOperator (S : StronglyContinuousSemigroup X) (t : ℝ) : X →L[ℝ] X

decls.name: TauCeti.Semigroups.StronglyContinuousSemigroup.realOperator_coe
decls.statement:
lemma realOperator_coe (S : StronglyContinuousSemigroup X) (t : ℝ≥0) :
    S.realOperator t = S t

decls.name: TauCeti.Semigroups.StronglyContinuousSemigroup.realOperator_zero
decls.doc: The real-time operator at zero is the identity: `S.realOperator 0 = id`.
decls.statement:
theorem realOperator_zero (S : StronglyContinuousSemigroup X) :
    S.realOperator 0 = ContinuousLinearMap.id ℝ X

decls.name: TauCeti.Semigroups.StronglyContinuousSemigroup.realOperator_add
decls.doc: The real-time shim satisfies the semigroup law at nonnegative real times.
decls.statement:
theorem realOperator_add (S : StronglyContinuousSemigroup X) (s t : ℝ) (hs : 0 ≤ s) (ht : 0 ≤ t) :
    S.realOperator (s + t) = (S.realOperator s).comp (S.realOperator t)

decls.name: TauCeti.Semigroups.StronglyContinuousSemigroup.norm_realOperator_add_le
decls.doc:
Submultiplicativity of the real-time operator norm at nonnegative times: the semigroup law
`S.realOperator (s + t) = S.realOperator s ∘ S.realOperator t` bounds the norm of the composite
by the product of the norms.
decls.statement:
theorem norm_realOperator_add_le (S : StronglyContinuousSemigroup X) (s t : ℝ)
    (hs : 0 ≤ s) (ht : 0 ≤ t) :
    ‖S.realOperator (s + t)‖ ≤ ‖S.realOperator s‖ * ‖S.realOperator t‖

decls.name: TauCeti.Semigroups.StronglyContinuousSemigroup.realOperator_continuousWithinAt_zero
decls.doc: Strong continuity at zero of `t ↦ S.realOperator t x` along `0 ≤ t`.
decls.statement:
theorem realOperator_continuousWithinAt_zero (S : StronglyContinuousSemigroup X) (x : X) :
    ContinuousWithinAt (fun t => S.realOperator t x) (Set.Ici 0) 0

decls.name: TauCeti.Semigroups.ContractionSemigroup
decls.doc:
A contraction semigroup: `‖S(t)‖ ≤ 1` for all `t ≥ 0`
([EN] Def. I.5.6, [Linares] Def. 3). Has the growth estimate `M = 1`, `ω = 0`.
decls.statement: structure ContractionSemigroup extends StronglyContinuousSemigroup X

decls.name: TauCeti.Semigroups.ContractionSemigroup.instFunLike
decls.statement: instance instFunLike : FunLike (ContractionSemigroup X) ℝ≥0 (X →L[ℝ] X)

decls.name: TauCeti.Semigroups.ContractionSemigroup.ext
decls.statement: theorem ext {S T : ContractionSemigroup X} (h : ∀ t, S t = T t) : S = T

decls.name: TauCeti.Semigroups.ContractionSemigroup.toStronglyContinuousSemigroup_apply
decls.statement:
theorem toStronglyContinuousSemigroup_apply (S : ContractionSemigroup X) (t : ℝ≥0) :
    S.toStronglyContinuousSemigroup t = S t

decls.name: TauCeti.Semigroups.ContractionSemigroup.contracting_real
decls.doc: A contraction semigroup is contractive at nonnegative real times.
decls.statement:
theorem ContractionSemigroup.contracting_real (S : ContractionSemigroup X)
    (t : ℝ) (ht : 0 ≤ t) : ‖S.realOperator t‖ ≤ 1

decls.name: TauCeti.Semigroups.StronglyContinuousSemigroup.realOperator_zero_apply
decls.doc: `S(t) x` at `t = 0` equals `x`, pointwise version.
decls.statement:
theorem StronglyContinuousSemigroup.realOperator_zero_apply
    (S : StronglyContinuousSemigroup X) (x : X) :
    S.realOperator 0 x = x

decls.name: TauCeti.Semigroups.StronglyContinuousSemigroup.norm_realOperator_apply_le_pow_mul_of_near_zero
decls.doc:
A pointwise orbit bound `‖S.realOperator t x‖ ≤ B` valid on the initial interval `[0, δ)`
propagates, via the semigroup law, to the geometric bound `(max ‖S.realOperator δ‖ 1) ^ k * B`
on `[0, (k + 1) * δ)`.
decls.statement:
theorem StronglyContinuousSemigroup.norm_realOperator_apply_le_pow_mul_of_near_zero
    (S : StronglyContinuousSemigroup X) (x : X) {δ B : ℝ} (hδ_pos : 0 < δ)
    (h_near : ∀ t : ℝ, 0 ≤ t → t < δ → ‖S.realOperator t x‖ ≤ B) :
    ∀ (k : ℕ) (t : ℝ), 0 ≤ t → t < (↑k + 1) * δ →
      ‖S.realOperator t x‖ ≤ (max ‖S.realOperator δ‖ 1) ^ k * B

decls.name: TauCeti.Semigroups.StronglyContinuousSemigroup.pointwiseBoundedOnUnitInterval
decls.doc: Pointwise boundedness on `[0, 1]`, the hypothesis needed for Banach-Steinhaus.
decls.statement:
theorem StronglyContinuousSemigroup.pointwiseBoundedOnUnitInterval
    (S : StronglyContinuousSemigroup X) :
    ∀ x : X, ∃ C, ∀ (i : Set.Icc (0 : ℝ) 1),
      ‖(fun j : Set.Icc (0 : ℝ) 1 => S.realOperator j.val) i x‖ ≤ C

decls.name: TauCeti.Semigroups.StronglyContinuousSemigroup.normBoundedOnUnitInterval
decls.doc:
The operator norm of a C₀-semigroup is bounded on `[0, 1]`.

One direction of [EN] Prop. I.5.3: strong continuity implies uniform boundedness
on compact intervals.
decls.statement:
theorem StronglyContinuousSemigroup.normBoundedOnUnitInterval
    (S : StronglyContinuousSemigroup X) :
    ∃ (M : ℝ), 1 ≤ M ∧
      ∀ (t : ℝ), 0 ≤ t → t ≤ 1 → ‖S.realOperator t‖ ≤ M

decls.name: TauCeti.Semigroups.StronglyContinuousSemigroup.normBoundedOnInterval
decls.doc: The operator norm of a C₀-semigroup is bounded on `[0, n]` for any `n : ℕ`.
decls.statement:
theorem StronglyContinuousSemigroup.normBoundedOnInterval
    (S : StronglyContinuousSemigroup X) (n : ℕ) :
    ∃ (C : ℝ), 0 < C ∧
      ∀ (t : ℝ), 0 ≤ t → t ≤ n → ‖S.realOperator t‖ ≤ C

decls.name: TauCeti.Semigroups.StronglyContinuousSemigroup.strongContWithinAt_left
decls.statement:
theorem StronglyContinuousSemigroup.strongContWithinAt_left
    (S : StronglyContinuousSemigroup X) (x : X) (t₀ : ℝ) (_ht₀ : 0 ≤ t₀) :
    Filter.Tendsto (fun t => S.realOperator t x)
      (nhdsWithin t₀ (Set.Icc 0 t₀)) (nhds (S.realOperator t₀ x))

decls.name: TauCeti.Semigroups.StronglyContinuousSemigroup.strongContWithinAt_right
decls.statement:
theorem StronglyContinuousSemigroup.strongContWithinAt_right
    (S : StronglyContinuousSemigroup X) (x : X) (t₀ : ℝ) (ht₀ : 0 ≤ t₀) :
    Filter.Tendsto (fun t => S.realOperator t x)
      (nhdsWithin t₀ (Set.Ici t₀)) (nhds (S.realOperator t₀ x))

decls.name: TauCeti.Semigroups.StronglyContinuousSemigroup.realOperator_continuousWithinAt
decls.doc:
Strong continuity at every `t₀ ≥ 0`, not just at 0
([EN] Prop. I.5.3, [Linares] Cor. 1).

Strong continuity holds at every `t₀ ≥ 0`, not only at `0`.
decls.statement:
theorem StronglyContinuousSemigroup.realOperator_continuousWithinAt
    (S : StronglyContinuousSemigroup X) (x : X) (t₀ : ℝ) (ht₀ : 0 ≤ t₀) :
    ContinuousWithinAt (fun t => S.realOperator t x) (Set.Ici 0) t₀

decls.name: TauCeti.Semigroups.StronglyContinuousSemigroup.realOperator_continuousOn_Ici
decls.doc:
The real-time orbit of a strongly continuous semigroup is continuous on the
nonnegative half-line.
decls.statement:
theorem StronglyContinuousSemigroup.realOperator_continuousOn_Ici
    (S : StronglyContinuousSemigroup X) (x : X) :
    ContinuousOn (fun t : ℝ => S.realOperator t x) (Set.Ici 0)

decls.name: TauCeti.Semigroups.StronglyContinuousSemigroup.realOperator_continuousAt_of_pos
decls.doc: The real-time orbit of a strongly continuous semigroup is continuous at positive times.
decls.statement:
theorem StronglyContinuousSemigroup.realOperator_continuousAt_of_pos
    (S : StronglyContinuousSemigroup X) (x : X) {t : ℝ} (ht : 0 < t) :
    ContinuousAt (fun u : ℝ => S.realOperator u x) t

decls.name: TauCeti.Semigroups.StronglyContinuousSemigroup.norm_exp_le_exp_norm
decls.doc:
In the Banach algebra `X →L[ℝ] X`, the operator exponential is norm-bounded by the scalar
exponential of the norm: `‖exp x‖ ≤ Real.exp ‖x‖`.  This is the termwise triangle inequality
on the exponential series, using submultiplicativity `‖xⁿ‖ ≤ ‖x‖ⁿ`.
decls.statement: lemma norm_exp_le_exp_norm (x : X →L[ℝ] X) : ‖exp x‖ ≤ Real.exp ‖x‖

decls.name: TauCeti.Semigroups.StronglyContinuousSemigroup.exp_add_of_commute
decls.doc:
The operator exponential is additive on commuting elements of `X →L[ℝ] X`, phrased over the
scalar field `ℝ` (the `ℚ`-algebra instance required by `NormedSpace.exp_add_of_commute` is not
available here).
decls.statement:
lemma exp_add_of_commute {x y : X →L[ℝ] X} (h : Commute x y) :
    exp (x + y) = exp x * exp y

decls.name: TauCeti.Semigroups.StronglyContinuousSemigroup.ofBounded
decls.doc:
The uniformly continuous C₀-semigroup `S(t) = exp (t • A)` generated by a bounded operator
`A : X →L[ℝ] X`.
decls.statement: def ofBounded (A : X →L[ℝ] X) : StronglyContinuousSemigroup X

decls.name: TauCeti.Semigroups.StronglyContinuousSemigroup.ofBounded_apply
decls.doc: The operator of `ofBounded A` at nonnegative time `t` is `exp (t • A)`.
decls.statement:
theorem ofBounded_apply (A : X →L[ℝ] X) (t : ℝ≥0) :
    (ofBounded A) t = exp ((t : ℝ) • A)

decls.name: TauCeti.Semigroups.StronglyContinuousSemigroup.ofBounded_apply_apply
decls.doc: The operator of `ofBounded A` at nonnegative time `t`, applied to `x`, is `exp (t • A) x`.
decls.statement:
theorem ofBounded_apply_apply (A : X →L[ℝ] X) (t : ℝ≥0) (x : X) :
    (ofBounded A) t x = exp ((t : ℝ) • A) x

decls.name: TauCeti.Semigroups.StronglyContinuousSemigroup.ofBounded_realOperator_of_nonneg
decls.doc: The real-time operator of `ofBounded A` at `t ≥ 0` is `exp (t • A)`.
decls.statement:
theorem ofBounded_realOperator_of_nonneg (A : X →L[ℝ] X) {t : ℝ} (ht : 0 ≤ t) :
    (ofBounded A).realOperator t = exp (t • A)

decls.name: TauCeti.Semigroups.StronglyContinuousSemigroup.ofBounded_realOperator_apply_of_nonneg
decls.doc: The real-time operator of `ofBounded A` at `t ≥ 0`, applied to `x`, is `exp (t • A) x`.
decls.statement:
theorem ofBounded_realOperator_apply_of_nonneg (A : X →L[ℝ] X) {t : ℝ} (ht : 0 ≤ t) (x : X) :
    (ofBounded A).realOperator t x = exp (t • A) x

decls.name: TauCeti.Semigroups.StronglyContinuousSemigroup.ofBounded_continuous
decls.doc: The bounded-generator semigroup is norm-continuous in nonnegative time.
decls.statement:
theorem ofBounded_continuous (A : X →L[ℝ] X) :
    Continuous fun t : ℝ≥0 => (ofBounded A) t

decls.name: TauCeti.Semigroups.StronglyContinuousSemigroup.ofBounded_realOperator_continuousOn_Ici
decls.doc: The real-time operator of `ofBounded A` is norm-continuous on the nonnegative half-line.
decls.statement:
theorem ofBounded_realOperator_continuousOn_Ici (A : X →L[ℝ] X) :
    ContinuousOn (fun t : ℝ => (ofBounded A).realOperator t) (Set.Ici 0)

decls.name: TauCeti.Semigroups.StronglyContinuousSemigroup.ofBounded_hasGrowthBound
decls.doc: The semigroup `ofBounded A` has the growth bound `(‖A‖, 1)`: `‖exp (t • A)‖ ≤ e^{‖A‖ t}`.
decls.statement:
theorem ofBounded_hasGrowthBound (A : X →L[ℝ] X) :
    (ofBounded A).HasGrowthBound ‖A‖ 1

decls.name: TauCeti.Semigroups.StronglyContinuousSemigroup.ofBounded_genQuot_tendsto
decls.doc:
The difference quotient `(exp (t • A) x - x)/t` tends to `A x` as `t → 0⁺`: the strong
derivative of `ofBounded A` at time `0` is `A`.
decls.statement:
theorem ofBounded_genQuot_tendsto (A : X →L[ℝ] X) (x : X) :
    Filter.Tendsto (fun t => (1 / t) • ((ofBounded A).realOperator t x - x))
      (nhdsWithin 0 (Set.Ioi 0)) (nhds (A x))

decls.name: TauCeti.Semigroups.StronglyContinuousSemigroup.mem_ofBounded_domain
decls.doc: Every vector lies in the generator domain of `ofBounded A`: its generator is bounded.
decls.statement:
theorem mem_ofBounded_domain (A : X →L[ℝ] X) (x : X) :
    x ∈ (ofBounded A).domain

decls.name: TauCeti.Semigroups.StronglyContinuousSemigroup.ofBounded_domain_eq_top
decls.doc: The generator domain of `ofBounded A` is the whole space.
decls.statement:
theorem ofBounded_domain_eq_top (A : X →L[ℝ] X) :
    (ofBounded A).domain = ⊤

decls.name: TauCeti.Semigroups.StronglyContinuousSemigroup.ofBounded_generator
decls.doc: The generator of `ofBounded A` is `A` itself, viewed as a total unbounded operator.
decls.statement:
theorem ofBounded_generator (A : X →L[ℝ] X) :
    (ofBounded A).generator = (A : X →ₗ[ℝ] X).toPMap ⊤

decls.name: TauCeti.Semigroups.StronglyContinuousSemigroup.norm_inv_smul_lt_one
decls.statement:
theorem norm_inv_smul_lt_one (A : X →L[ℝ] X) {lambda : ℝ}
    (hlambda : ‖A‖ < |lambda|) : ‖lambda⁻¹ • A‖ < 1

decls.name: TauCeti.Semigroups.StronglyContinuousSemigroup.inv_smul_tsum_pow_mul_sub
TauCeti.Semigroups.StronglyContinuousSemigroup.ofBounded_resolvent_eq_inv_smul_tsum_pow
decls.doc:
For `λ > ‖A‖`, the Laplace-transform resolvent of `t ↦ exp (tA)` is the Neumann series
`λ⁻¹ ∑' n, (λ⁻¹ A)ⁿ`.
decls.statement:
theorem ofBounded_resolvent_eq_inv_smul_tsum_pow (A : X →L[ℝ] X) {lambda : ℝ}
    (hlambda : ‖A‖ < lambda) :
    (ofBounded A).resolvent (ofBounded_hasGrowthBound A) lambda hlambda =
      lambda⁻¹ • ∑' n : ℕ, (lambda⁻¹ • A) ^ n

decls.name: TauCeti.Semigroups.StronglyContinuousSemigroup.ofBounded_resolvent_eq_resolvent
decls.doc:
For `λ > ‖A‖`, the Laplace-transform resolvent of `t ↦ exp (tA)` agrees with
Mathlib's Banach-algebra resolvent of `A`.
decls.statement:
theorem ofBounded_resolvent_eq_resolvent (A : X →L[ℝ] X) {lambda : ℝ}
    (hlambda : ‖A‖ < lambda) :
    (ofBounded A).resolvent (ofBounded_hasGrowthBound A) lambda hlambda =
      _root_.resolvent A lambda

decls.name: TauCeti.Semigroups.IsClassicalSolution
decls.doc:
A classical solution of `u' = A u`, `u(0) = x`, on `[0, ∞)`. Its values belong to the
domain of `A`, and it has a continuous derivative within `[0, ∞)` equal to `A (u t)`.
decls.statement: def IsClassicalSolution (A : X →ₗ.[ℝ] X) (x : X) (u : ℝ → X) : Prop

decls.name: TauCeti.Semigroups.IsClassicalSolution.apply_zero
decls.doc: A classical solution takes its prescribed initial value at time zero.
decls.statement:
theorem IsClassicalSolution.apply_zero {A : X →ₗ.[ℝ] X} {x : X} {u : ℝ → X}
    (hu : IsClassicalSolution A x u) : u 0 = x

decls.name: TauCeti.Semigroups.isClassicalSolution_iff
decls.doc:
Characterization of a classical solution by its initial value and continuously
differentiable equation.
decls.statement:
theorem isClassicalSolution_iff {A : X →ₗ.[ℝ] X} {x : X} {u : ℝ → X} :
    IsClassicalSolution A x u ↔
      u 0 = x ∧ ∃ u' : ℝ → X, ContinuousOn u' (Set.Ici 0) ∧
        ∀ t : ℝ, 0 ≤ t → ∃ hut : u t ∈ A.domain,
          HasDerivWithinAt u (u' t) (Set.Ici 0) t ∧ u' t = A ⟨u t, hut⟩

decls.name: TauCeti.Semigroups.IsClassicalSolution.mem_domain
decls.doc: Every value of a classical solution at nonnegative time belongs to the operator domain.
decls.statement:
theorem IsClassicalSolution.mem_domain {A : X →ₗ.[ℝ] X} {x : X} {u : ℝ → X}
    (hu : IsClassicalSolution A x u) {t : ℝ} (ht : 0 ≤ t) : u t ∈ A.domain

decls.name: TauCeti.Semigroups.IsClassicalSolution.hasDerivWithinAt
decls.doc:
The derivative within the nonnegative half-line of a classical solution is the operator
applied to its value.

decls.name: TauCeti.Semigroups.IsClassicalSolution.continuousOn
decls.doc: A classical solution is continuous on the nonnegative half-line.
decls.statement:
theorem IsClassicalSolution.continuousOn {A : X →ₗ.[ℝ] X} {x : X} {u : ℝ → X}
    (hu : IsClassicalSolution A x u) : ContinuousOn u (Set.Ici 0)

decls.name: TauCeti.Semigroups.IsMildSolution
decls.doc:
A mild solution of `u' = A u`, `u(0) = x`, on `[0, ∞)`.  The integral is pointwise
Bochner integration in `X`.  Requiring the integral to lie in the domain makes the expression
`A (∫ s in (0, t], u s)` meaningful for an unbounded operator.
decls.statement: def IsMildSolution [CompleteSpace X] (A : X →ₗ.[ℝ] X) (x : X) (u : ℝ → X) : Prop

decls.name: TauCeti.Semigroups.IsMildSolution.continuousOn
decls.doc: A mild solution is continuous on the nonnegative half-line.
decls.statement:
theorem IsMildSolution.continuousOn [CompleteSpace X] {A : X →ₗ.[ℝ] X} {x : X} {u : ℝ → X}
    (hu : IsMildSolution A x u) : ContinuousOn u (Set.Ici 0)

decls.name: TauCeti.Semigroups.IsMildSolution.apply_zero
decls.doc: A mild solution takes its prescribed initial value at time zero.
decls.statement:
theorem IsMildSolution.apply_zero [CompleteSpace X] {A : X →ₗ.[ℝ] X} {x : X} {u : ℝ → X}
    (hu : IsMildSolution A x u) : u 0 = x

decls.name: TauCeti.Semigroups.isMildSolution_iff
decls.doc: Characterization of a mild solution by continuity and its integrated Cauchy equation.
decls.statement:
theorem isMildSolution_iff [CompleteSpace X] {A : X →ₗ.[ℝ] X} {x : X} {u : ℝ → X} :
    IsMildSolution A x u ↔ ContinuousOn u (Set.Ici 0) ∧ u 0 = x ∧
      ∀ t : ℝ, 0 ≤ t → ∃ hut : (∫ s in Set.Ioc 0 t, u s) ∈ A.domain,
        A ⟨∫ s in Set.Ioc 0 t, u s, hut⟩ = u t - x

decls.name: TauCeti.Semigroups.IsMildSolution.integral_mem_domain
decls.doc: The time integral of a mild solution belongs to the operator domain.
decls.statement:
theorem IsMildSolution.integral_mem_domain [CompleteSpace X]
    {A : X →ₗ.[ℝ] X} {x : X} {u : ℝ → X}
    (hu : IsMildSolution A x u) {t : ℝ} (ht : 0 ≤ t) :
    (∫ s in Set.Ioc 0 t, u s) ∈ A.domain

decls.name: TauCeti.Semigroups.IsMildSolution.map_integral_eq_sub
decls.doc: The integrated Cauchy equation satisfied by a mild solution.
decls.statement:
theorem IsMildSolution.map_integral_eq_sub [CompleteSpace X]
    {A : X →ₗ.[ℝ] X} {x : X} {u : ℝ → X}
    (hu : IsMildSolution A x u) {t : ℝ} (ht : 0 ≤ t) :
    A ⟨∫ s in Set.Ioc 0 t, u s, hu.integral_mem_domain ht⟩ = u t - x

decls.name: TauCeti.Semigroups.StronglyContinuousSemigroup.isClassicalSolution_realOperator
decls.doc:
The orbit of a generator-domain vector is a classical solution of the abstract Cauchy
problem for the generator.
decls.statement:
theorem isClassicalSolution_realOperator (S : StronglyContinuousSemigroup X) (x : S.domain) :
    IsClassicalSolution S.generator (x : X) (fun t => S.realOperator t x)

decls.name: TauCeti.Semigroups.StronglyContinuousSemigroup.isMildSolution_realOperator
decls.doc: Every orbit is a mild solution of the abstract Cauchy problem for the generator.
decls.statement:
theorem isMildSolution_realOperator (S : StronglyContinuousSemigroup X) (x : X) :
    IsMildSolution S.generator x (fun t => S.realOperator t x)

decls.name: TauCeti.Semigroups.IsDissipative
decls.doc:
An unbounded operator `A : X →ₗ.[ℝ] X` is **dissipative** when
`lambda * ‖x‖ ≤ ‖lambda • x - A x‖` for every `lambda > 0` and every `x` in its domain.

This is the Banach-space form of the condition: it says exactly that `lambda • I - A` is
injective on `D(A)` with `‖(lambda • I - A)⁻¹‖ ≤ 1 / lambda` on its range, for every
`lambda > 0`. In a Hilbert space it is equivalent to `⟪A x, x⟫ ≤ 0`.
decls.statement: def IsDissipative (A : X →ₗ.[ℝ] X) : Prop

decls.name: TauCeti.Semigroups.isDissipative_iff
decls.doc:
`IsDissipative A` unfolds to its defining inequality: `lambda * ‖x‖ ≤ ‖lambda • x - A x‖`
for every `lambda > 0` and every `x ∈ D(A)`.
decls.statement:
theorem isDissipative_iff {A : X →ₗ.[ℝ] X} :
    IsDissipative A ↔
      ∀ lambda : ℝ, 0 < lambda → ∀ x : A.domain,
        lambda * ‖(x : X)‖ ≤ ‖lambda • (x : X) - A x‖

decls.name: TauCeti.Semigroups.IsDissipative.norm_le_of_smul_sub_eq
decls.doc:
The a priori estimate carried by dissipativity: a solution of `lambda x - A x = y` obeys
`‖x‖ ≤ ‖y‖ / lambda`.

decls.name: TauCeti.Semigroups.IsDissipative.smul_sub_injective
decls.doc:
A dissipative operator has `lambda • I - A` injective on its domain, for every
`lambda > 0`.
decls.statement:
theorem IsDissipative.smul_sub_injective {A : X →ₗ.[ℝ] X} (hA : IsDissipative A)
    {lambda : ℝ} (hlambda : 0 < lambda) :
    Function.Injective fun x : A.domain => lambda • (x : X) - A x

decls.name: TauCeti.Semigroups.IsDissipative.of_le
decls.doc:
Dissipativity passes to restrictions: if `A ≤ B` as unbounded operators and `B` is
dissipative, then so is `A`.
decls.statement:
theorem IsDissipative.of_le {A B : X →ₗ.[ℝ] X} (hB : IsDissipative B) (hAB : A ≤ B) :
    IsDissipative A

decls.name: TauCeti.Semigroups.isDissipative_zero
decls.doc: The zero operator, defined on all of `X`, is dissipative.
decls.statement: theorem isDissipative_zero : IsDissipative (0 : X →ₗ.[ℝ] X)

decls.name: TauCeti.Semigroups.IsDissipative.smul
decls.doc: A nonnegative scalar multiple of a dissipative operator is dissipative.
decls.statement:
theorem IsDissipative.smul {A : X →ₗ.[ℝ] X} (hA : IsDissipative A) {c : ℝ} (hc : 0 ≤ c) :
    IsDissipative (c • A)

decls.name: TauCeti.Semigroups.IsMDissipative
decls.doc:
An unbounded operator is **m-dissipative** (maximally dissipative) when it is dissipative
and `lambda • I - A` maps `D(A)` onto `X` for *some* `lambda > 0`.

The range condition is what upgrades the one-sided estimate of `IsDissipative` to a genuine
resolvent, and one positive `lambda` already suffices: over a Banach space it propagates to
every `lambda > 0` (`IsMDissipative.smul_sub_surjective`), so that `lambda • I - A : D(A) → X`
is bijective there (`IsMDissipative.smul_sub_bijective`), with inverse bounded by `1 / lambda`
through `IsDissipative.norm_le_of_smul_sub_eq`. Asking for a single `lambda` is the form the
hypothesis takes in the Lumer--Phillips generation theorem — that a densely defined
m-dissipative operator *is* the generator of a contraction semigroup — which is not yet
available in this library; its converse half is `ContractionSemigroup.isMDissipative_generator`
below.
decls.statement: def IsMDissipative (A : X →ₗ.[ℝ] X) : Prop

decls.name: TauCeti.Semigroups.isMDissipative_iff
decls.doc:
`IsMDissipative A` unfolds to its defining conjunction: `A` is dissipative and
`lambda • I - A` maps `D(A)` onto `X` for some `lambda > 0`.
decls.statement:
theorem isMDissipative_iff {A : X →ₗ.[ℝ] X} :
    IsMDissipative A ↔
      IsDissipative A ∧
        ∃ lambda : ℝ, 0 < lambda ∧
          Function.Surjective fun x : A.domain => lambda • (x : X) - A x

decls.name: TauCeti.Semigroups.IsDissipative.isMDissipative
decls.doc:
A dissipative operator whose `lambda • I - A` maps `D(A)` onto `X` for a single `lambda > 0`
is m-dissipative.
decls.statement:
theorem IsDissipative.isMDissipative {A : X →ₗ.[ℝ] X} (hA : IsDissipative A) {lambda : ℝ}
    (hlambda : 0 < lambda)
    (hrange : Function.Surjective fun x : A.domain => lambda • (x : X) - A x) :
    IsMDissipative A

decls.name: TauCeti.Semigroups.IsMDissipative.isDissipative
decls.doc: An m-dissipative operator is dissipative.
decls.statement:
theorem IsMDissipative.isDissipative {A : X →ₗ.[ℝ] X} (hA : IsMDissipative A) :
    IsDissipative A

decls.name: TauCeti.Semigroups.IsMDissipative.exists_smul_sub_surjective
decls.doc:
The range condition of an m-dissipative operator: `lambda • I - A` maps `D(A)` onto `X` for
at least one `lambda > 0`.
decls.statement:
theorem IsMDissipative.exists_smul_sub_surjective {A : X →ₗ.[ℝ] X} (hA : IsMDissipative A) :
    ∃ lambda : ℝ, 0 < lambda ∧
      Function.Surjective fun x : A.domain => lambda • (x : X) - A x

decls.name: TauCeti.Semigroups.IsDissipative.exists_bounded_rightInverse
decls.doc:
**A bounded right inverse at a point of the range condition.** If `A` is dissipative and
`lambda • I - A` maps `D(A)` onto `X`, then it admits a right inverse `g` into `D(A)` which, read
as a map into `X`, is a bounded operator `J` of norm at most `1 / lambda`. Keeping `g` separate
from `J` is what lets `A` be applied to the result, since `A` only accepts elements of `D(A)`.

Dissipativity makes `g` a genuine two-sided inverse (`IsDissipative.smul_sub_injective`), but only
the right-inverse property is exposed, that being what the Neumann-series argument consumes.

Completeness of `X` is not needed: the bound comes from dissipativity
(`IsDissipative.norm_le_of_smul_sub_eq`) rather than from the open mapping theorem.
decls.title: A bounded right inverse at a point of the range condition
decls.statement:
theorem IsDissipative.exists_bounded_rightInverse {A : X →ₗ.[ℝ] X} (hA : IsDissipative A)
    {lambda : ℝ} (hlambda : 0 < lambda)
    (hrange : Function.Surjective fun x : A.domain => lambda • (x : X) - A x) :
    ∃ (g : X → A.domain) (J : X →L[ℝ] X), ‖J‖ ≤ lambda⁻¹ ∧ (∀ y : X, (g y : X) = J y) ∧
      ∀ y : X, lambda • (g y : X) - A (g y) = y

decls.name: TauCeti.Semigroups.IsDissipative.smul_sub_surjective_of_lt_two_mul
decls.doc:
**The range condition propagates along a Neumann series.** If `A` is dissipative and
`lambda • I - A` maps `D(A)` onto `X`, then so does `mu • I - A` for every `mu` in the interval
`(0, 2 lambda)`.

Dissipativity makes `lambda • I - A : D(A) → X` a bijection whose inverse `J` is bounded by
`1 / lambda`, and `mu • I - A = (I - (lambda - mu) • J) ∘ (lambda • I - A)`. The first factor is
invertible because `‖(lambda - mu) • J‖ ≤ |lambda - mu| / lambda < 1`, which is exactly the
constraint `0 < mu < 2 lambda`.
decls.title: The range condition propagates along a Neumann series
decls.statement:
theorem IsDissipative.smul_sub_surjective_of_lt_two_mul {A : X →ₗ.[ℝ] X} (hA : IsDissipative A)
    {lambda mu : ℝ} (hlambda : 0 < lambda)
    (hrange : Function.Surjective fun x : A.domain => lambda • (x : X) - A x)
    (hmu : 0 < mu) (hmu' : mu < 2 * lambda) :
    Function.Surjective fun x : A.domain => mu • (x : X) - A x

decls.name: TauCeti.Semigroups.IsMDissipative.smul_sub_surjective
decls.doc:
The range condition of an m-dissipative operator holds at *every* positive `lambda`, not
just at the one its definition provides: propagate the given `lambda₀` through
`IsDissipative.smul_sub_surjective_of_lt_two_mul` along the geometric sequence
`(3/2)^n lambda₀`, which passes every positive real.
decls.statement:
theorem IsMDissipative.smul_sub_surjective {A : X →ₗ.[ℝ] X} (hA : IsMDissipative A)
    {lambda : ℝ} (hlambda : 0 < lambda) :
    Function.Surjective fun x : A.domain => lambda • (x : X) - A x

decls.name: TauCeti.Semigroups.IsMDissipative.smul_sub_bijective
decls.doc:
For an m-dissipative operator, `lambda • I - A` is a bijection from `D(A)` onto `X` for
every `lambda > 0`: injectivity comes from dissipativity, surjectivity from the propagated
range condition.
decls.statement:
theorem IsMDissipative.smul_sub_bijective {A : X →ₗ.[ℝ] X} (hA : IsMDissipative A)
    {lambda : ℝ} (hlambda : 0 < lambda) :
    Function.Bijective fun x : A.domain => lambda • (x : X) - A x

decls.name: TauCeti.Semigroups.StronglyContinuousSemigroup.norm_le_norm_smul_sub_generator
decls.doc:
**Resolvent-range inequality.** For a C₀-semigroup with growth bound `(ω, M)` and
`lambda > ω`, every `x ∈ D(A)` satisfies `‖x‖ ≤ M / (lambda - ω) * ‖lambda x - A x‖`.

This is the Hille--Yosida resolvent bound `‖R(lambda)‖ ≤ M / (lambda - ω)` read backwards
through the left-inverse identity `R(lambda) (lambda x - A x) = x`.
decls.title: Resolvent-range inequality
decls.statement:
theorem norm_le_norm_smul_sub_generator (S : StronglyContinuousSemigroup X) {ω M : ℝ}
    (hb : S.HasGrowthBound ω M) {lambda : ℝ} (hlambda : ω < lambda)
    (x : S.generator.domain) :
    ‖(x : X)‖ ≤ M / (lambda - ω) * ‖lambda • (x : X) - S.generator x‖

decls.name: TauCeti.Semigroups.StronglyContinuousSemigroup.smul_sub_generator_injective
decls.doc:
For `lambda` beyond the growth exponent, `lambda • I - A` is injective on `D(A)`: the
resolvent is a left inverse of it.

decls.name: TauCeti.Semigroups.StronglyContinuousSemigroup.smul_sub_generator_surjective
decls.doc:
For `lambda` beyond the growth exponent, `lambda • I - A` maps `D(A)` onto `X`: the
resolvent supplies the preimage.

decls.name: TauCeti.Semigroups.StronglyContinuousSemigroup.smul_sub_generator_bijective
decls.doc:
Every `lambda` beyond the growth exponent lies in the resolvent set of the generator:
`lambda • I - A : D(A) → X` is bijective.

decls.name: TauCeti.Semigroups.ContractionSemigroup.isDissipative_generator
decls.doc:
**Converse of the Lumer--Phillips theorem**: the generator of a contraction semigroup is
dissipative.

It is the `(ω, M) = (0, 1)` case of the resolvent-range inequality
`StronglyContinuousSemigroup.norm_le_norm_smul_sub_generator`. Together with
`StronglyContinuousSemigroup.smul_sub_generator_surjective` and the density of the generator
domain, it shows that the hypotheses of the Lumer--Phillips generation theorem are also
necessary.
decls.title: Converse of the Lumer--Phillips theorem
decls.statement:
theorem isDissipative_generator (S : ContractionSemigroup X) :
    IsDissipative S.toStronglyContinuousSemigroup.generator

decls.name: TauCeti.Semigroups.ContractionSemigroup.isMDissipative_generator
decls.doc:
**The generator of a contraction semigroup is m-dissipative.** This is the full converse of
the Lumer--Phillips theorem apart from the density of the domain (which is
`StronglyContinuousSemigroup.dense_domain`): dissipativity is
`ContractionSemigroup.isDissipative_generator` and the range condition is witnessed at
`lambda = 1` by the surjectivity of `lambda • I - A` that the resolvent supplies (indeed at
every `lambda > 0`, by `StronglyContinuousSemigroup.smul_sub_generator_surjective`).
decls.title: The generator of a contraction semigroup is m-dissipative
decls.statement:
theorem isMDissipative_generator (S : ContractionSemigroup X) :
    IsMDissipative S.toStronglyContinuousSemigroup.generator

decls.name: TauCeti.Semigroups.ContractionSemigroup.norm_le_of_smul_sub_generator_eq
decls.doc:
The a priori estimate for the generator of a contraction semigroup: a solution of
`lambda x - A x = y` has `‖x‖ ≤ ‖y‖ / lambda`.

decls.name: TauCeti.Semigroups.norm_smul_sub_sq_real
decls.doc:
Expansion of `‖lambda • x - y‖²` on a real inner-product space, with the scalar `lambda`
pulled out of both the norm and the inner product.
decls.statement:
theorem norm_smul_sub_sq_real {lambda : ℝ} (hlambda : 0 ≤ lambda) (x y : X) :
    ‖lambda • x - y‖ ^ 2 = (lambda * ‖x‖) ^ 2 - 2 * (lambda * ⟪x, y⟫_ℝ) + ‖y‖ ^ 2

decls.name: TauCeti.Semigroups.isDissipative_iff_real_inner_nonpos
decls.doc:
**Dissipativity on a real inner-product space.** An unbounded operator is dissipative
exactly when `⟪A x, x⟫ ≤ 0` on its domain.
decls.title: Dissipativity on a real inner-product space
decls.statement:
theorem isDissipative_iff_real_inner_nonpos (A : X →ₗ.[ℝ] X) :
    IsDissipative A ↔ ∀ x : A.domain, ⟪A x, (x : X)⟫_ℝ ≤ 0

decls.name: TauCeti.Semigroups.ContractionSemigroup.real_inner_generator_nonpos
decls.doc:
**The converse of the Lumer--Phillips theorem on a Hilbert space.** The generator of a
contraction semigroup on a real Hilbert space satisfies `⟪A x, x⟫ ≤ 0` on its domain.
decls.title: The converse of the Lumer--Phillips theorem on a Hilbert space
decls.statement:
theorem real_inner_generator_nonpos (S : ContractionSemigroup X)
    (x : S.toStronglyContinuousSemigroup.generator.domain) :
    ⟪S.toStronglyContinuousSemigroup.generator x, (x : X)⟫_ℝ ≤ 0

decls.name: TauCeti.Semigroups.StronglyContinuousSemigroup.expShift
decls.doc:
The exponential shift of a C₀-semigroup by `lambda`.

At nonnegative time `t`, this is the semigroup `exp (-lambda t) • S(t)`.  It shifts
growth exponents by subtracting `lambda`; see `HasGrowthBound.expShift`.
decls.statement:
def expShift (S : StronglyContinuousSemigroup X) (lambda : ℝ) :
    StronglyContinuousSemigroup X

decls.name: TauCeti.Semigroups.StronglyContinuousSemigroup.expShift_apply
decls.doc: The native nonnegative-time operator of the exponential shift.
decls.statement:
theorem expShift_apply (S : StronglyContinuousSemigroup X) (lambda : ℝ) (t : ℝ≥0) :
    S.expShift lambda t = Real.exp (-(lambda * (t : ℝ))) • S t

decls.name: TauCeti.Semigroups.StronglyContinuousSemigroup.expShift_apply_apply
decls.doc: Pointwise form of `StronglyContinuousSemigroup.expShift_apply`.
decls.statement:
theorem expShift_apply_apply (S : StronglyContinuousSemigroup X) (lambda : ℝ)
    (t : ℝ≥0) (x : X) :
    S.expShift lambda t x = Real.exp (-(lambda * (t : ℝ))) • S t x

decls.name: TauCeti.Semigroups.StronglyContinuousSemigroup.expShift_zero
decls.doc: The zero exponential shift is the original semigroup.
decls.statement:
theorem expShift_zero (S : StronglyContinuousSemigroup X) :
    S.expShift 0 = S

decls.name: TauCeti.Semigroups.StronglyContinuousSemigroup.expShift_expShift
decls.doc: Successive exponential shifts add their parameters.
decls.statement:
theorem expShift_expShift (S : StronglyContinuousSemigroup X) (lambda μ : ℝ) :
    (S.expShift lambda).expShift μ = S.expShift (lambda + μ)

decls.name: TauCeti.Semigroups.StronglyContinuousSemigroup.expShift_realOperator_of_nonneg
decls.doc: Real-time form of the shifted operator at nonnegative times.
decls.statement:
theorem expShift_realOperator_of_nonneg (S : StronglyContinuousSemigroup X)
    (lambda t : ℝ) (ht : 0 ≤ t) :
    (S.expShift lambda).realOperator t = Real.exp (-(lambda * t)) • S.realOperator t

decls.name: TauCeti.Semigroups.StronglyContinuousSemigroup.expShift_realOperator_apply_of_nonneg
decls.doc: Pointwise real-time form of the shifted operator at nonnegative times.
decls.statement:
theorem expShift_realOperator_apply_of_nonneg (S : StronglyContinuousSemigroup X)
    (lambda t : ℝ) (ht : 0 ≤ t) (x : X) :
    (S.expShift lambda).realOperator t x =
      Real.exp (-(lambda * t)) • S.realOperator t x

decls.name: TauCeti.Semigroups.StronglyContinuousSemigroup.HasGrowthBound.expShift
decls.doc: Exponential shifting subtracts the shift parameter from the growth exponent.
decls.statement:
theorem expShift {S : StronglyContinuousSemigroup X} {ω M lambda : ℝ}
    (hb : S.HasGrowthBound ω M) : (S.expShift lambda).HasGrowthBound (ω - lambda) M

decls.name: TauCeti.Semigroups.StronglyContinuousSemigroup.expShiftContraction
decls.doc:
A semigroup with growth bound `(lambda, 1)` becomes a contraction semigroup after
exponential shifting by `lambda`.
decls.statement:
def expShiftContraction (S : StronglyContinuousSemigroup X) (lambda : ℝ)
    (hb : S.HasGrowthBound lambda 1) : ContractionSemigroup X

decls.name: TauCeti.Semigroups.StronglyContinuousSemigroup.expShiftContraction_toStronglyContinuousSemigroup
decls.doc: The C₀-semigroup underlying `expShiftContraction` is the exponential shift.
decls.statement:
theorem expShiftContraction_toStronglyContinuousSemigroup
    (S : StronglyContinuousSemigroup X) (lambda : ℝ) (hb : S.HasGrowthBound lambda 1) :
    (S.expShiftContraction lambda hb).toStronglyContinuousSemigroup = S.expShift lambda

decls.name: TauCeti.Semigroups.StronglyContinuousSemigroup.expShiftContraction_apply
decls.doc: Native operator formula for `expShiftContraction`.
decls.statement:
theorem expShiftContraction_apply (S : StronglyContinuousSemigroup X) (lambda : ℝ)
    (hb : S.HasGrowthBound lambda 1) (t : ℝ≥0) :
    S.expShiftContraction lambda hb t = Real.exp (-(lambda * (t : ℝ))) • S t

decls.name: TauCeti.Semigroups.tendsto_average_Ioc_zero_of_stronglyMeasurableAtFilter_continuousWithinAt_Ioi
decls.doc:
The integral averages `(1/t) • ∫_{(0,t]} g u du` of a function that is locally strongly
measurable and continuous at `0` from the right tend to `g 0` as `t → 0⁺`.
decls.statement:
theorem tendsto_average_Ioc_zero_of_stronglyMeasurableAtFilter_continuousWithinAt_Ioi
    {g : ℝ → X}
    (hmeas : StronglyMeasurableAtFilter g (nhdsWithin (0 : ℝ) (Set.Ioi 0)) volume)
    (hg0 : ContinuousWithinAt g (Set.Ioi 0) 0) :
    Filter.Tendsto
      (fun t => (1 / t) • ∫ u in Set.Ioc 0 t, g u)
      (nhdsWithin 0 (Set.Ioi 0)) (nhds (g 0))

decls.name: TauCeti.Semigroups.StronglyContinuousSemigroup.genQuot
decls.doc:
The generator difference quotient `(S t x - x)/t`; its `t → 0⁺` limit (when it
exists) is the generator value at `x`.
decls.statement:
def StronglyContinuousSemigroup.genQuot (S : StronglyContinuousSemigroup X)
    (x : X) (t : ℝ) : X

decls.name: TauCeti.Semigroups.StronglyContinuousSemigroup.genQuot_tendsto_add
decls.doc: The generator difference quotient is additive in the limit.
decls.statement:
theorem StronglyContinuousSemigroup.genQuot_tendsto_add
    (S : StronglyContinuousSemigroup X) {x y Ax Ay : X}
    (hx : Filter.Tendsto (S.genQuot x) (nhdsWithin 0 (Set.Ioi 0)) (nhds Ax))
    (hy : Filter.Tendsto (S.genQuot y) (nhdsWithin 0 (Set.Ioi 0)) (nhds Ay)) :
    Filter.Tendsto (S.genQuot (x + y)) (nhdsWithin 0 (Set.Ioi 0)) (nhds (Ax + Ay))

decls.name: TauCeti.Semigroups.StronglyContinuousSemigroup.genQuot_tendsto_smul
decls.doc: The generator difference quotient is `ℝ`-homogeneous in the limit.
decls.statement:
theorem StronglyContinuousSemigroup.genQuot_tendsto_smul
    (S : StronglyContinuousSemigroup X) (c : ℝ) {x Ax : X}
    (hx : Filter.Tendsto (S.genQuot x) (nhdsWithin 0 (Set.Ioi 0)) (nhds Ax)) :
    Filter.Tendsto (S.genQuot (c • x)) (nhdsWithin 0 (Set.Ioi 0)) (nhds (c • Ax))

decls.name: TauCeti.Semigroups.StronglyContinuousSemigroup.domain
decls.doc: The domain `D(A)` of the generator, as a `ℝ`-submodule of `X`.
decls.statement:
def StronglyContinuousSemigroup.domain (S : StronglyContinuousSemigroup X) :
    Submodule ℝ X

decls.name: TauCeti.Semigroups.StronglyContinuousSemigroup.generator
decls.doc:
The infinitesimal generator `A` as an unbounded operator (`LinearPMap`),
`A x = lim_{t→0⁺} (S t x - x)/t` on the domain `D(A)` where the limit exists
([EN] Def. II.1.2). Modelled as `X →ₗ.[ℝ] X` so it composes with Mathlib's
unbounded-operator API.
decls.statement:
def StronglyContinuousSemigroup.generator
    (S : StronglyContinuousSemigroup X) : X →ₗ.[ℝ] X

decls.name: TauCeti.Semigroups.StronglyContinuousSemigroup.generator_domain
decls.doc: `S.generator.domain` is the generator domain submodule.
decls.statement:
theorem StronglyContinuousSemigroup.generator_domain
    (S : StronglyContinuousSemigroup X) : S.generator.domain = S.domain

decls.name: TauCeti.Semigroups.StronglyContinuousSemigroup.mem_domain_iff_tendsto
decls.doc:
A vector lies in the generator domain iff its difference quotient `(S t x - x)/t`
converges as `t → 0⁺` ([EN] Def. II.1.2).
decls.statement:
theorem StronglyContinuousSemigroup.mem_domain_iff_tendsto
    (S : StronglyContinuousSemigroup X) (x : X) :
    x ∈ S.domain ↔ ∃ y, Filter.Tendsto (fun t => (1 / t) • (S.realOperator t x - x))
      (nhdsWithin 0 (Set.Ioi 0)) (nhds y)

decls.name: TauCeti.Semigroups.StronglyContinuousSemigroup.generator_tendsto
decls.doc:
Characteristic property of the generator: for `x` in the domain, the difference
quotient `(S t x - x)/t` converges to `S.generator x` as `t → 0⁺` ([EN] Def. II.1.2).
decls.statement:
theorem StronglyContinuousSemigroup.generator_tendsto
    (S : StronglyContinuousSemigroup X) (x : S.domain) :
    Filter.Tendsto (fun t => (1 / t) • (S.realOperator t (x : X) - (x : X)))
      (nhdsWithin 0 (Set.Ioi 0))
      (nhds (S.generator ⟨(x : X), by
        rw [S.generator_domain]
        exact x.property⟩))

decls.name: TauCeti.Semigroups.StronglyContinuousSemigroup.generator_eq_of_tendsto
decls.doc:
Eliminator for the generator: if the difference quotient `(S t x - x)/t` of an
`x ∈ D(A)` converges to `y`, then `A x = y`.
decls.statement:
theorem StronglyContinuousSemigroup.generator_eq_of_tendsto
    (S : StronglyContinuousSemigroup X) {x : X} (hx : x ∈ S.domain) {y : X}
    (h : Filter.Tendsto (fun t => (1 / t) • (S.realOperator t x - x))
      (nhdsWithin 0 (Set.Ioi 0)) (nhds y)) :
    S.generator ⟨x, by
      rw [S.generator_domain]
      exact hx⟩ = y

decls.name: TauCeti.Semigroups.StronglyContinuousSemigroup.generator_eq_toPMap_top_of_forall_tendsto
decls.doc:
If every generator difference quotient converges to `L x` for a linear operator `L`, then
the generator domain is the whole space and the generator is `L` as a total `LinearPMap`.
decls.statement:
theorem StronglyContinuousSemigroup.generator_eq_toPMap_top_of_forall_tendsto
    (S : StronglyContinuousSemigroup X) (L : X →ₗ[ℝ] X)
    (h : ∀ x, Filter.Tendsto (fun t => (1 / t) • (S.realOperator t x - x))
      (nhdsWithin 0 (Set.Ioi 0)) (nhds (L x))) :
    S.domain = ⊤ ∧ S.generator = L.toPMap ⊤

decls.name: TauCeti.Semigroups.StronglyContinuousSemigroup.tendsto_average_orbit_zero
decls.doc: The integral average `(1/t) • ∫_{(0,t]} S(u)x du` of the orbit tends to `x` as `t → 0⁺`.
decls.statement:
theorem StronglyContinuousSemigroup.tendsto_average_orbit_zero
    (S : StronglyContinuousSemigroup X) (x : X) :
    Filter.Tendsto
      (fun t => (1 / t) • ∫ u in Set.Ioc 0 t, S.realOperator u x)
      (nhdsWithin 0 (Set.Ioi 0)) (nhds x)

decls.name: TauCeti.Semigroups.StronglyContinuousSemigroup.intervalIntegrable_orbit
decls.statement:
theorem StronglyContinuousSemigroup.intervalIntegrable_orbit
    (S : StronglyContinuousSemigroup X) (x : X) {a b : ℝ} (ha : 0 ≤ a) (hb : 0 ≤ b) :
    IntervalIntegrable (fun u => S.realOperator u x) volume a b

decls.name: TauCeti.Semigroups.StronglyContinuousSemigroup.local_integral_shift_identity
decls.statement:
theorem StronglyContinuousSemigroup.local_integral_shift_identity
    (S : StronglyContinuousSemigroup X) (x : X) {t h : ℝ} (ht : 0 < t) (hh : 0 < h) :
    S.realOperator h (∫ u in (0 : ℝ)..t, S.realOperator u x) -
        ∫ u in (0 : ℝ)..t, S.realOperator u x =
      (∫ u in t..t + h, S.realOperator u x) - ∫ u in (0 : ℝ)..h, S.realOperator u x

decls.name: TauCeti.Semigroups.StronglyContinuousSemigroup.tendsto_average_orbit_at
decls.statement:
theorem StronglyContinuousSemigroup.tendsto_average_orbit_at
    (S : StronglyContinuousSemigroup X) (x : X) {t : ℝ} (ht : 0 < t) :
    Filter.Tendsto (fun h => (1 / h) • ∫ u in t..t + h, S.realOperator u x)
      (nhdsWithin 0 (Set.Ioi 0)) (nhds (S.realOperator t x))

decls.name: TauCeti.Semigroups.StronglyContinuousSemigroup.tendsto_quot_integral_orbit
decls.doc:
The difference quotient of the local orbit integral `∫₀ᵗ S(u)x du` converges to
`S t x - x` as the time-step `→ 0⁺` (the limit underlying [EN] Lemma II.1.3).
decls.statement:
theorem StronglyContinuousSemigroup.tendsto_quot_integral_orbit
    (S : StronglyContinuousSemigroup X) (x : X) {t : ℝ} (ht : 0 < t) :
    Filter.Tendsto (fun h => (1 / h) •
        (S.realOperator h (∫ u in Set.Ioc 0 t, S.realOperator u x)
        - ∫ u in Set.Ioc 0 t, S.realOperator u x))
      (nhdsWithin 0 (Set.Ioi 0)) (nhds (S.realOperator t x - x))

decls.name: TauCeti.Semigroups.StronglyContinuousSemigroup.integral_orbit_mem_domain
decls.doc:
The local orbit integral `∫₀ᵗ S(u)x du` lies in the generator domain `D(A)`
([EN] Lemma II.1.3).
decls.statement:
theorem StronglyContinuousSemigroup.integral_orbit_mem_domain
    (S : StronglyContinuousSemigroup X) (x : X) {t : ℝ} (ht : 0 < t) :
    (∫ u in Set.Ioc 0 t, S.realOperator u x) ∈ S.domain

decls.name: TauCeti.Semigroups.StronglyContinuousSemigroup.generator_integral_orbit
decls.doc:
The generator value on the local orbit integral: `A (∫₀ᵗ S(u)x du) = S t x - x`
([EN] Lemma II.1.3).
decls.statement:
theorem StronglyContinuousSemigroup.generator_integral_orbit
    (S : StronglyContinuousSemigroup X) (x : X) {t : ℝ} (ht : 0 < t) :
    S.generator ⟨∫ u in Set.Ioc 0 t, S.realOperator u x, by
      rw [S.generator_domain]
      exact S.integral_orbit_mem_domain x ht⟩
      = S.realOperator t x - x

decls.name: TauCeti.Semigroups.StronglyContinuousSemigroup.dense_domain
decls.doc:
The generator domain of a strongly continuous semigroup is dense
([EN] Lemma II.1.3 and its density corollary).
decls.statement:
theorem StronglyContinuousSemigroup.dense_domain
    (S : StronglyContinuousSemigroup X) : Dense (S.domain : Set X)

decls.name: TauCeti.Semigroups.StronglyContinuousSemigroup.tendsto_genQuot_apply
decls.doc:
The difference quotient based at `S s x` is `S s` applied to the difference quotient
based at `x`.
decls.statement:
theorem tendsto_genQuot_apply (S : StronglyContinuousSemigroup X) (s : ℝ≥0)
    {x y : X}
    (h : Filter.Tendsto (fun t => (1 / t) • (S.realOperator t x - x))
      (nhdsWithin 0 (Set.Ioi 0)) (nhds y)) :
    Filter.Tendsto (fun t => (1 / t) • (S.realOperator t (S s x) - S s x))
      (nhdsWithin 0 (Set.Ioi 0)) (nhds (S s y))

decls.name: TauCeti.Semigroups.StronglyContinuousSemigroup.map_mem_domain
decls.doc: Every semigroup operator preserves the domain of the infinitesimal generator.

decls.name: TauCeti.Semigroups.StronglyContinuousSemigroup.generator_map
decls.doc: The infinitesimal generator commutes with every semigroup operator on its domain.
decls.statement:
theorem generator_map (S : StronglyContinuousSemigroup X) (s : ℝ≥0) (x : S.domain) :
    S.generator ⟨S s x, by
      rw [S.generator_domain]
      exact S.map_mem_domain s x.property⟩ =
      S s (S.generator ⟨x, by rw [S.generator_domain]; exact x.property⟩)

decls.name: TauCeti.Semigroups.StronglyContinuousSemigroup.realOperator_mem_domain
decls.doc: Real-time form of domain invariance at nonnegative times.
decls.statement:
theorem realOperator_mem_domain (S : StronglyContinuousSemigroup X) {s : ℝ} (hs : 0 ≤ s)
    {x : X} (hx : x ∈ S.domain) :
    S.realOperator s x ∈ S.domain

decls.name: TauCeti.Semigroups.StronglyContinuousSemigroup.realOperator_generator_map
decls.doc: Real-time form of generator commutation at nonnegative times.
decls.statement:
theorem realOperator_generator_map (S : StronglyContinuousSemigroup X) {s : ℝ} (hs : 0 ≤ s)
    (x : S.domain) :
    S.generator ⟨S.realOperator s x, by
      rw [S.generator_domain]
      exact S.realOperator_mem_domain hs x.property⟩ =
      S.realOperator s (S.generator ⟨x, by rw [S.generator_domain]; exact x.property⟩)

decls.name: TauCeti.Semigroups.StronglyContinuousSemigroup.realOperator_hasDerivWithinAt_zero
decls.doc:
At time zero, the right derivative of the orbit of a generator-domain vector is its
generator.
decls.statement:
theorem realOperator_hasDerivWithinAt_zero (S : StronglyContinuousSemigroup X)
    (x : S.domain) :
    HasDerivWithinAt (fun s : ℝ => S.realOperator s (x : X))
      (S.generator ⟨x, by rw [S.generator_domain]; exact x.property⟩) (Set.Ici 0) 0

decls.name: TauCeti.Semigroups.StronglyContinuousSemigroup.realOperator_differentiableWithinAt_zero
decls.doc: The orbit of a generator-domain vector is right-differentiable at time zero.
decls.statement:
theorem realOperator_differentiableWithinAt_zero (S : StronglyContinuousSemigroup X)
    (x : S.domain) :
    DifferentiableWithinAt ℝ (fun s : ℝ => S.realOperator s (x : X)) (Set.Ici 0) 0

decls.name: TauCeti.Semigroups.StronglyContinuousSemigroup.realOperator_derivWithin_zero
decls.doc: The right derivative at zero of the orbit of a generator-domain vector is its generator.
decls.statement:
theorem realOperator_derivWithin_zero (S : StronglyContinuousSemigroup X)
    (x : S.domain) :
    derivWithin (fun s : ℝ => S.realOperator s (x : X)) (Set.Ici 0) 0 =
      S.generator ⟨x, by rw [S.generator_domain]; exact x.property⟩

decls.name: TauCeti.Semigroups.StronglyContinuousSemigroup.realOperator_hasDerivWithinAt_zero_iff
decls.doc:
The orbit has right derivative `y` at zero exactly when its initial vector belongs to the
generator domain and the generator value is `y`.
decls.statement:
theorem realOperator_hasDerivWithinAt_zero_iff (S : StronglyContinuousSemigroup X)
    (x y : X) :
    HasDerivWithinAt (fun s : ℝ => S.realOperator s x) y (Set.Ici 0) 0 ↔
      ∃ hx : x ∈ S.domain,
        S.generator ⟨x, by rw [S.generator_domain]; exact hx⟩ = y

decls.name: TauCeti.Semigroups.StronglyContinuousSemigroup.mem_domain_iff_differentiableWithinAt_realOperator_zero
decls.doc:
A vector belongs to the generator domain exactly when its orbit is right-differentiable
