at time zero.
decls.statement:
theorem mem_domain_iff_differentiableWithinAt_realOperator_zero
    (S : StronglyContinuousSemigroup X) (x : X) :
    x ∈ S.domain ↔
      DifferentiableWithinAt ℝ (fun s : ℝ => S.realOperator s x) (Set.Ici 0) 0

decls.name: TauCeti.Semigroups.StronglyContinuousSemigroup.realOperator_hasDerivWithinAt
decls.doc:
At every nonnegative time, if the evolved vector belongs to the generator domain, then the
right derivative of the orbit is the generator evaluated on that evolved vector.
decls.statement:
theorem realOperator_hasDerivWithinAt (S : StronglyContinuousSemigroup X)
    {x : X} {t : ℝ} (ht : 0 ≤ t) (hxt : S.realOperator t x ∈ S.domain) :
    HasDerivWithinAt (fun s : ℝ => S.realOperator s x)
      (S.generator ⟨S.realOperator t x, by rw [S.generator_domain]; exact hxt⟩)
      (Set.Ici t) t

decls.name: TauCeti.Semigroups.StronglyContinuousSemigroup.realOperator_hasDerivWithinAt_map_generator
decls.doc:
At every nonnegative time, the right derivative of the orbit is the semigroup operator
applied to the generator.
decls.statement:
theorem realOperator_hasDerivWithinAt_map_generator
    (S : StronglyContinuousSemigroup X) (x : S.domain) {t : ℝ} (ht : 0 ≤ t) :
    HasDerivWithinAt (fun s : ℝ => S.realOperator s (x : X))
      (S.realOperator t (S.generator ⟨x, by
        rw [S.generator_domain]
        exact x.property⟩)) (Set.Ici t) t

decls.name: TauCeti.Semigroups.StronglyContinuousSemigroup.realOperator_eq_add_integral_map_generator
decls.statement:
theorem realOperator_eq_add_integral_map_generator (S : StronglyContinuousSemigroup X)
    [CompleteSpace X] (x : S.domain) {s : ℝ} (hs : 0 ≤ s) :
    S.realOperator s (x : X) = (x : X) + ∫ u in (0 : ℝ)..s,
      S.realOperator u (S.generator ⟨x, by rw [S.generator_domain]; exact x.property⟩)

decls.name: TauCeti.Semigroups.StronglyContinuousSemigroup.realOperator_hasDerivWithinAt_Ici
decls.doc:
On the nonnegative half-line, the orbit of a generator-domain vector has derivative equal
to the generator evaluated on the evolved vector. At positive times this is a two-sided
derivative; only the derivative at zero is one-sided.
decls.statement:
theorem realOperator_hasDerivWithinAt_Ici (S : StronglyContinuousSemigroup X)
    [CompleteSpace X] (x : S.domain) {t : ℝ} (ht : 0 ≤ t) :
    HasDerivWithinAt (fun s : ℝ => S.realOperator s (x : X))
      (S.generator ⟨S.realOperator t x, by
        rw [S.generator_domain]
        exact S.realOperator_mem_domain ht x.property⟩) (Set.Ici 0) t

decls.name: TauCeti.Semigroups.StronglyContinuousSemigroup.realOperator_differentiableWithinAt
decls.doc: The orbit of a generator-domain vector is right-differentiable at every nonnegative time.
decls.statement:
theorem realOperator_differentiableWithinAt (S : StronglyContinuousSemigroup X)
    (x : S.domain) {t : ℝ} (ht : 0 ≤ t) :
    DifferentiableWithinAt ℝ (fun s : ℝ => S.realOperator s (x : X)) (Set.Ici t) t

decls.name: TauCeti.Semigroups.StronglyContinuousSemigroup.realOperator_derivWithin
decls.doc:
The right derivative of an orbit at a nonnegative time is the generator evaluated on the
evolved vector, provided that vector belongs to the generator domain.
decls.statement:
theorem realOperator_derivWithin (S : StronglyContinuousSemigroup X)
    {x : X} {t : ℝ} (ht : 0 ≤ t) (hxt : S.realOperator t x ∈ S.domain) :
    derivWithin (fun s : ℝ => S.realOperator s x) (Set.Ici t) t =
      S.generator ⟨S.realOperator t x, by rw [S.generator_domain]; exact hxt⟩

decls.name: TauCeti.Semigroups.StronglyContinuousSemigroup.realOperator_derivWithin_map_generator
decls.doc:
The right derivative of the orbit at a nonnegative time is the semigroup operator applied
to the generator.
decls.statement:
theorem realOperator_derivWithin_map_generator (S : StronglyContinuousSemigroup X)
    (x : S.domain) {t : ℝ} (ht : 0 ≤ t) :
    derivWithin (fun s : ℝ => S.realOperator s (x : X)) (Set.Ici t) t =
      S.realOperator t (S.generator ⟨x, by
        rw [S.generator_domain]
        exact x.property⟩)

decls.name: TauCeti.Semigroups.StronglyContinuousSemigroup.HasGrowthBound
decls.doc: A C₀-semigroup has exponential growth bound `(ω, M)`, with `M ≥ 1`.
decls.statement:
def StronglyContinuousSemigroup.HasGrowthBound
    (S : StronglyContinuousSemigroup X) (ω : ℝ) (M : ℝ) : Prop

decls.name: TauCeti.Semigroups.StronglyContinuousSemigroup.HasGrowthBound.one_le
decls.doc: The multiplicative constant in a growth bound is at least one.
decls.statement:
theorem StronglyContinuousSemigroup.HasGrowthBound.one_le
    {S : StronglyContinuousSemigroup X} {ω M : ℝ} (hb : S.HasGrowthBound ω M) :
    1 ≤ M

decls.name: TauCeti.Semigroups.StronglyContinuousSemigroup.HasGrowthBound.bound
decls.doc: The operator-norm estimate supplied by a growth bound.
decls.statement:
theorem StronglyContinuousSemigroup.HasGrowthBound.bound
    {S : StronglyContinuousSemigroup X} {ω M : ℝ} (hb : S.HasGrowthBound ω M)
    (t : ℝ) (ht : 0 ≤ t) : ‖S.realOperator t‖ ≤ M * Real.exp (ω * t)

decls.name: TauCeti.Semigroups.StronglyContinuousSemigroup.hasGrowthBound_of_bound
decls.doc:
Constructor for a growth bound from the multiplicative lower bound and operator-norm
estimate.
decls.statement:
theorem StronglyContinuousSemigroup.hasGrowthBound_of_bound
    {S : StronglyContinuousSemigroup X} {ω M : ℝ} (hM : 1 ≤ M)
    (hbound : ∀ (t : ℝ), 0 ≤ t → ‖S.realOperator t‖ ≤ M * Real.exp (ω * t)) :
    S.HasGrowthBound ω M

decls.name: TauCeti.Semigroups.StronglyContinuousSemigroup.HasGrowthBound.mono
decls.doc:
A growth bound can be weakened by increasing both the exponential rate and the multiplicative
constant.
decls.statement:
theorem StronglyContinuousSemigroup.HasGrowthBound.mono
    {S : StronglyContinuousSemigroup X} {ω M ω' M' : ℝ}
    (hb : S.HasGrowthBound ω M) (hω : ω ≤ ω') (hM : M ≤ M') :
    S.HasGrowthBound ω' M'

decls.name: TauCeti.Semigroups.StronglyContinuousSemigroup.HasGrowthBound.mono_omega
decls.doc: A growth bound can be weakened by increasing the exponential rate.
decls.statement:
theorem StronglyContinuousSemigroup.HasGrowthBound.mono_omega
    {S : StronglyContinuousSemigroup X} {ω M ω' : ℝ}
    (hb : S.HasGrowthBound ω M) (hω : ω ≤ ω') :
    S.HasGrowthBound ω' M

decls.name: TauCeti.Semigroups.StronglyContinuousSemigroup.HasGrowthBound.mono_const
decls.doc: A growth bound can be weakened by increasing the multiplicative constant.
decls.statement:
theorem StronglyContinuousSemigroup.HasGrowthBound.mono_const
    {S : StronglyContinuousSemigroup X} {ω M M' : ℝ}
    (hb : S.HasGrowthBound ω M) (hM : M ≤ M') :
    S.HasGrowthBound ω M'

decls.name: TauCeti.Semigroups.ContractionSemigroup.hasGrowthBound
decls.doc: A contraction semigroup has growth bound `(0, 1)`.
decls.statement:
theorem ContractionSemigroup.hasGrowthBound (S : ContractionSemigroup X) :
    S.toStronglyContinuousSemigroup.HasGrowthBound 0 1

decls.name: TauCeti.Semigroups.ContractionSemigroup.hasGrowthBound_of_nonneg_omega
decls.doc: A contraction semigroup has every nonnegative exponential growth rate with constant `1`.
decls.statement:
theorem ContractionSemigroup.hasGrowthBound_of_nonneg_omega
    (S : ContractionSemigroup X) {ω : ℝ} (hω : 0 ≤ ω) :
    S.toStronglyContinuousSemigroup.HasGrowthBound ω 1

decls.name: TauCeti.Semigroups.ContractionSemigroup.hasGrowthBound_of_one_le_const
decls.doc: A contraction semigroup has growth bound `(0, M)` for every `M ≥ 1`.
decls.statement:
theorem ContractionSemigroup.hasGrowthBound_of_one_le_const
    (S : ContractionSemigroup X) {M : ℝ} (hM : 1 ≤ M) :
    S.toStronglyContinuousSemigroup.HasGrowthBound 0 M

decls.name: TauCeti.Semigroups.ContractionSemigroup.hasGrowthBound_of_nonneg_omega_of_one_le_const
decls.doc: A contraction semigroup has growth bound `(ω, M)` whenever `0 ≤ ω` and `1 ≤ M`.
decls.statement:
theorem ContractionSemigroup.hasGrowthBound_of_nonneg_omega_of_one_le_const
    (S : ContractionSemigroup X) {ω M : ℝ} (hω : 0 ≤ ω) (hM : 1 ≤ M) :
    S.toStronglyContinuousSemigroup.HasGrowthBound ω M

decls.name: TauCeti.Semigroups.StronglyContinuousSemigroup.existsGrowthBound
decls.doc:
Every C₀-semigroup has a finite exponential growth bound
([EN] Prop. I.5.5, [Linares] Thm. 1).
decls.statement:
theorem StronglyContinuousSemigroup.existsGrowthBound
    (S : StronglyContinuousSemigroup X) :
    ∃ (ω : ℝ) (M : ℝ), S.HasGrowthBound ω M

decls.name: TauCeti.Semigroups.StronglyContinuousSemigroup.existsGrowthBound_ge_omega
decls.doc: A C₀-semigroup admits a growth bound with exponent at least any prescribed real number.
decls.statement:
theorem StronglyContinuousSemigroup.existsGrowthBound_ge_omega
    (S : StronglyContinuousSemigroup X) (ω₀ : ℝ) :
    ∃ (ω : ℝ) (M : ℝ), ω₀ ≤ ω ∧ S.HasGrowthBound ω M

decls.name: TauCeti.Semigroups.StronglyContinuousSemigroup.existsGrowthBound_ge_const
decls.doc:
A C₀-semigroup admits a growth bound with multiplicative constant at least any prescribed
real number.
decls.statement:
theorem StronglyContinuousSemigroup.existsGrowthBound_ge_const
    (S : StronglyContinuousSemigroup X) (M₀ : ℝ) :
    ∃ (ω : ℝ) (M : ℝ), M₀ ≤ M ∧ S.HasGrowthBound ω M

decls.name: TauCeti.Semigroups.StronglyContinuousSemigroup.existsGrowthBound_ge
decls.doc:
A C₀-semigroup admits a growth bound whose exponent and multiplicative constant are both at
least prescribed lower bounds.
decls.statement:
theorem StronglyContinuousSemigroup.existsGrowthBound_ge
    (S : StronglyContinuousSemigroup X) (ω₀ M₀ : ℝ) :
    ∃ (ω : ℝ) (M : ℝ), ω₀ ≤ ω ∧ M₀ ≤ M ∧ S.HasGrowthBound ω M

decls.name: TauCeti.Semigroups.StronglyContinuousSemigroup.id
decls.doc: The identity C₀-semigroup `S(t) = id`, generated by the zero operator.
decls.statement: def id : StronglyContinuousSemigroup X

decls.name: TauCeti.Semigroups.StronglyContinuousSemigroup.id_apply
decls.doc: The identity C₀-semigroup is constantly the identity operator.
decls.statement:
theorem id_apply (t : ℝ≥0) :
    (StronglyContinuousSemigroup.id X) t = ContinuousLinearMap.id ℝ X

decls.name: TauCeti.Semigroups.StronglyContinuousSemigroup.id_apply_apply
decls.doc: Pointwise form of `StronglyContinuousSemigroup.id_apply`.
decls.statement:
theorem id_apply_apply (t : ℝ≥0) (x : X) :
    (StronglyContinuousSemigroup.id X) t x = x

decls.name: TauCeti.Semigroups.ContractionSemigroup.id
decls.doc: The identity contraction semigroup.
decls.statement: def id : ContractionSemigroup X

decls.name: TauCeti.Semigroups.ContractionSemigroup.id_apply
decls.doc: The identity contraction semigroup is constantly the identity operator.
decls.statement:
theorem id_apply (t : ℝ≥0) :
    (ContractionSemigroup.id X) t = ContinuousLinearMap.id ℝ X

decls.name: TauCeti.Semigroups.ContractionSemigroup.id_apply_apply
decls.doc: Pointwise form of `ContractionSemigroup.id_apply`.
decls.statement:
theorem id_apply_apply (t : ℝ≥0) (x : X) :
    (ContractionSemigroup.id X) t x = x

decls.name: TauCeti.Semigroups.ContractionSemigroup.id_toStronglyContinuousSemigroup
decls.doc: The C₀-semigroup underlying the identity contraction semigroup.
decls.statement:
theorem id_toStronglyContinuousSemigroup :
    (ContractionSemigroup.id X).toStronglyContinuousSemigroup =
      StronglyContinuousSemigroup.id X

decls.name: TauCeti.Semigroups.StronglyContinuousSemigroup.id_hasGrowthBound
decls.doc: The identity semigroup has the contraction growth bound `(0, 1)`.
decls.statement:
theorem id_hasGrowthBound :
    (StronglyContinuousSemigroup.id X).HasGrowthBound 0 1

decls.name: TauCeti.Semigroups.StronglyContinuousSemigroup.id_genQuot_tendsto
decls.doc:
The difference quotient `(S t x - x)/t` of the identity semigroup is identically zero,
hence tends to `0` as `t → 0⁺`.
decls.statement:
theorem id_genQuot_tendsto (x : X) :
    Filter.Tendsto (fun t => (1 / t) • ((StronglyContinuousSemigroup.id X).realOperator t x - x))
      (nhdsWithin 0 (Set.Ioi 0)) (nhds 0)

decls.name: TauCeti.Semigroups.StronglyContinuousSemigroup.mem_id_domain
decls.doc: Every vector lies in the generator domain of the identity semigroup.
decls.statement:
theorem mem_id_domain (x : X) :
    x ∈ (StronglyContinuousSemigroup.id X).domain

decls.name: TauCeti.Semigroups.StronglyContinuousSemigroup.id_domain_eq_top
decls.doc: The generator domain of the identity semigroup is all of the space.
decls.statement:
theorem id_domain_eq_top :
    (StronglyContinuousSemigroup.id X).domain = ⊤

decls.name: TauCeti.Semigroups.StronglyContinuousSemigroup.id_generator_eq_zero
decls.doc: The generator of the identity semigroup is the zero operator.
decls.statement:
theorem id_generator_eq_zero :
    (StronglyContinuousSemigroup.id X).generator = 0

decls.name: TauCeti.Semigroups.StronglyContinuousSemigroup.norm_resolvent_integrand_le
decls.doc:
The growth-bound estimate for the Laplace-transform integrand:
`‖e^{-λt} S(t) x‖ ≤ M ‖x‖ e^{-(λ-ω)t}` for `t > 0`.
decls.statement:
lemma StronglyContinuousSemigroup.norm_resolvent_integrand_le
    (S : StronglyContinuousSemigroup X) {ω M : ℝ} (hb : S.HasGrowthBound ω M)
    (lambda : ℝ) (x : X) {t : ℝ} (ht : 0 < t) :
    ‖Real.exp (-(lambda * t)) • S.realOperator t x‖ ≤
      M * ‖x‖ * Real.exp (-(lambda - ω) * t)

decls.name: TauCeti.Semigroups.StronglyContinuousSemigroup.integrable_resolvent_integrand
decls.doc:
The Laplace-transform integrand `e^{-λt} S(t) x` is integrable on `(0, ∞)` for
`ω < λ`.
decls.statement:
lemma StronglyContinuousSemigroup.integrable_resolvent_integrand
    (S : StronglyContinuousSemigroup X) {ω M : ℝ} (hb : S.HasGrowthBound ω M)
    (lambda : ℝ) (hlam : ω < lambda) (x : X) :
    IntegrableOn (fun t => Real.exp (-(lambda * t)) • S.realOperator t x) (Set.Ioi 0)

decls.name: TauCeti.Semigroups.StronglyContinuousSemigroup.resolvent
decls.doc:
The resolvent `R(λ) x = ∫₀^∞ e^{-λt} S(t)x dt` of a C₀-semigroup with growth bound
`(ω, M)`, for `λ > ω`. A pointwise `X`-valued Bochner integral (so it is well-defined for
the merely strongly continuous `t ↦ S t`), with built-in norm bound `‖R λ‖ ≤ M/(λ-ω)`.
decls.statement:
def StronglyContinuousSemigroup.resolvent
    (S : StronglyContinuousSemigroup X) {ω M : ℝ} (hb : S.HasGrowthBound ω M)
    (lambda : ℝ) (hlam : ω < lambda) : X →L[ℝ] X

decls.name: TauCeti.Semigroups.StronglyContinuousSemigroup.resolvent_apply
decls.doc: The resolvent in integral form (characteristic lemma).
decls.statement:
theorem StronglyContinuousSemigroup.resolvent_apply
    (S : StronglyContinuousSemigroup X) {ω M : ℝ} (hb : S.HasGrowthBound ω M)
    (lambda : ℝ) (hlam : ω < lambda) (x : X) :
    S.resolvent hb lambda hlam x
      = ∫ t in Set.Ioi 0, Real.exp (-(lambda * t)) • S.realOperator t x

decls.name: TauCeti.Semigroups.integral_comp_add_right_Ioi
decls.doc: Translation of set integral: `∫_{Ioi 0} f(t + h) = ∫_{Ioi h} f(u)`.
decls.statement:
lemma integral_comp_add_right_Ioi (f : ℝ → X) (h : ℝ) :
    ∫ t in Set.Ioi 0, f (t + h) = ∫ u in Set.Ioi h, f u

decls.name: TauCeti.Semigroups.integral_Ioi_eq_Ioc_add_Ioi
decls.doc: Splitting `∫_{Ioi 0} = ∫_{Ioc 0 h} + ∫_{Ioi h}` for `h > 0`.
decls.statement:
lemma integral_Ioi_eq_Ioc_add_Ioi (f : ℝ → X) {h : ℝ} (hh : 0 < h)
    (hf : IntegrableOn f (Set.Ioi 0) volume) :
    ∫ t in Set.Ioi 0, f t = (∫ t in Set.Ioc 0 h, f t) + ∫ t in Set.Ioi h, f t

decls.name: TauCeti.Semigroups.StronglyContinuousSemigroup.resolvent_shift_identity
decls.doc: The resolvent shift identity for a positive time increment.
decls.statement:
theorem StronglyContinuousSemigroup.resolvent_shift_identity
    (S : StronglyContinuousSemigroup X) {ω M : ℝ} (hb : S.HasGrowthBound ω M)
    (lambda : ℝ) (hlam : ω < lambda) (x : X) {h : ℝ} (hh : 0 < h) :
    S.realOperator h (S.resolvent hb lambda hlam x) - S.resolvent hb lambda hlam x =
      (Real.exp (lambda * h) - 1) • S.resolvent hb lambda hlam x -
      Real.exp (lambda * h) •
        ∫ u in Set.Ioc 0 h, Real.exp (-(lambda * u)) • S.realOperator u x

decls.name: TauCeti.Semigroups.StronglyContinuousSemigroup.tendsto_average_resolvent_integrand
decls.doc:
The integral average `(1/t) • ∫_{(0,t]} e^{-λu} S(u)x du` of the resolvent integrand
tends to `x` as `t → 0⁺`.
decls.statement:
theorem StronglyContinuousSemigroup.tendsto_average_resolvent_integrand
    (S : StronglyContinuousSemigroup X) (lambda : ℝ) (x : X) :
    Filter.Tendsto
      (fun t => (1 / t) • ∫ u in Set.Ioc 0 t, Real.exp (-(lambda * u)) • S.realOperator u x)
      (nhdsWithin 0 (Set.Ioi 0)) (nhds x)

decls.name: TauCeti.Semigroups.StronglyContinuousSemigroup.resolvent_generator_tendsto
decls.doc: The generator difference quotient for `R(λ)x` converges to `λ R(λ)x - x`.
decls.statement:
theorem StronglyContinuousSemigroup.resolvent_generator_tendsto
    (S : StronglyContinuousSemigroup X) {ω M : ℝ} (hb : S.HasGrowthBound ω M)
    (lambda : ℝ) (hlam : ω < lambda) (x : X) :
    Filter.Tendsto (fun t => (1 / t) • (S.realOperator t (S.resolvent hb lambda hlam x) -
      S.resolvent hb lambda hlam x))
      (nhdsWithin 0 (Set.Ioi 0))
      (nhds (lambda • S.resolvent hb lambda hlam x - x))

decls.name: TauCeti.Semigroups.StronglyContinuousSemigroup.resolvent_mem_domain
decls.doc:
The resolvent maps all of `X` into the domain of the generator
([EN] Thm. II.1.10(i), [Linares] eq. 0.15).
decls.statement:
theorem StronglyContinuousSemigroup.resolvent_mem_domain
    (S : StronglyContinuousSemigroup X) {ω M : ℝ} (hb : S.HasGrowthBound ω M)
    (lambda : ℝ) (hlam : ω < lambda) (x : X) :
    (S.resolvent hb lambda hlam x) ∈ S.domain

decls.name: TauCeti.Semigroups.StronglyContinuousSemigroup.resolventRightInv
decls.doc: The fundamental resolvent identity: `(λI - A) R(λ) x = x`.
decls.statement:
theorem StronglyContinuousSemigroup.resolventRightInv
    (S : StronglyContinuousSemigroup X) {ω M : ℝ} (hb : S.HasGrowthBound ω M)
    (lambda : ℝ) (hlam : ω < lambda) (x : X) :
    lambda • S.resolvent hb lambda hlam x
      - S.generator
          ⟨S.resolvent hb lambda hlam x, by
            rw [S.generator_domain]
            exact S.resolvent_mem_domain hb lambda hlam x⟩ = x

decls.name: TauCeti.Semigroups.StronglyContinuousSemigroup.resolvent_norm_le
decls.doc:
**Hille–Yosida resolvent bound**: `‖R λ‖ ≤ M/(λ-ω)` for a C₀ semigroup with
growth bound `(ω, M)` and `λ > ω` (Hille 1948, Yosida 1948; Engel–Nagel Ch. II).
decls.title: Hille–Yosida resolvent bound
decls.statement:
theorem StronglyContinuousSemigroup.resolvent_norm_le
    (S : StronglyContinuousSemigroup X) {ω M : ℝ} (hb : S.HasGrowthBound ω M)
    (lambda : ℝ) (hlam : ω < lambda) :
    ‖S.resolvent hb lambda hlam‖ ≤ M / (lambda - ω)

decls.name: TauCeti.Semigroups.ContractionSemigroup.resolvent
decls.doc: The resolvent of a contraction semigroup, the `(0, 1)` case.
decls.statement:
def ContractionSemigroup.resolvent (S : ContractionSemigroup X)
    (lambda : ℝ) (hlam : 0 < lambda) : X →L[ℝ] X

decls.name: TauCeti.Semigroups.ContractionSemigroup.resolvent_apply
decls.doc:
The contraction resolvent unfolds to the Laplace-transform integral
`R(λ) x = ∫₀^∞ e^{-λt} S(t)x dt`, the `(0, 1)` case.
decls.statement:
theorem ContractionSemigroup.resolvent_apply (S : ContractionSemigroup X)
    (lambda : ℝ) (hlam : 0 < lambda) (x : X) :
    S.resolvent lambda hlam x
      = ∫ t in Set.Ioi 0, Real.exp (-(lambda * t)) • S.realOperator t x

decls.name: TauCeti.Semigroups.ContractionSemigroup.resolvent_mem_domain
decls.doc: The contraction resolvent maps into the generator domain.
decls.statement:
theorem ContractionSemigroup.resolvent_mem_domain (S : ContractionSemigroup X)
    (lambda : ℝ) (hlam : 0 < lambda) (x : X) :
    (S.resolvent lambda hlam x) ∈ S.toStronglyContinuousSemigroup.domain

decls.name: TauCeti.Semigroups.ContractionSemigroup.resolventRightInv
decls.doc:
The contraction resolvent right-inverse identity `(λI - A) R(λ) x = x`, the `(0, 1)` case
(cf. `StronglyContinuousSemigroup.resolventRightInv`).
decls.statement:
theorem ContractionSemigroup.resolventRightInv (S : ContractionSemigroup X)
    (lambda : ℝ) (hlam : 0 < lambda) (x : X) :
    lambda • S.resolvent lambda hlam x
      - S.toStronglyContinuousSemigroup.generator
          ⟨S.resolvent lambda hlam x, by
            rw [StronglyContinuousSemigroup.generator_domain]
            exact S.resolvent_mem_domain lambda hlam x⟩ = x

decls.name: TauCeti.Semigroups.ContractionSemigroup.resolvent_norm_le
decls.doc: The contraction resolvent bound `‖R λ‖ ≤ 1/λ`, the `(0, 1)` case.
decls.statement:
theorem ContractionSemigroup.resolvent_norm_le (S : ContractionSemigroup X)
    (lambda : ℝ) (hlam : 0 < lambda) :
    ‖S.resolvent lambda hlam‖ ≤ 1 / lambda

decls.name: TauCeti.Semigroups.StronglyContinuousSemigroup.tendsto_exp_neg_smul_realOperator_atTop
decls.doc:
The exponentially weighted orbit of a generator-domain vector tends to zero when the
exponential rate is larger than the semigroup growth exponent.
decls.statement:
theorem tendsto_exp_neg_smul_realOperator_atTop (S : StronglyContinuousSemigroup X)
    {omega M lambda : ℝ} (hb : S.HasGrowthBound omega M) (hlambda : omega < lambda)
    (x : S.domain) :
    Filter.Tendsto (fun t : ℝ => Real.exp (-(lambda * t)) • S.realOperator t (x : X))
      Filter.atTop (nhds 0)

decls.name: TauCeti.Semigroups.StronglyContinuousSemigroup.hasDerivAt_exp_neg_smul_realOperator
decls.doc:
At a **positive** time the weighted orbit is two-sidedly differentiable: the orbit derivative
is already known within `Set.Ici 0`, which is a neighbourhood of any `t > 0`.
decls.statement:
theorem hasDerivAt_exp_neg_smul_realOperator
    (S : StronglyContinuousSemigroup X) [CompleteSpace X] (lambda : ℝ) (x : S.domain) {t : ℝ}
    (ht : 0 < t) :
    HasDerivAt
      (fun u : ℝ => Real.exp (-(lambda * u)) • S.realOperator u (x : X))
      (Real.exp (-(lambda * t)) •
        (S.realOperator t (S.generator
          ⟨x, by rw [S.generator_domain]; exact x.property⟩) -
          lambda • S.realOperator t (x : X))) t

decls.name: TauCeti.Semigroups.StronglyContinuousSemigroup.resolventLeftInv
decls.doc:
The Laplace-transform resolvent is a left inverse to `lambda • I - A` on the generator
domain: `R(lambda) (lambda x - A x) = x`.
decls.statement:
theorem resolventLeftInv (S : StronglyContinuousSemigroup X) {omega M : ℝ}
    [CompleteSpace X]
    (hb : S.HasGrowthBound omega M) (lambda : ℝ) (hlambda : omega < lambda)
    (x : S.domain) :
    S.resolvent hb lambda hlambda
        (lambda • (x : X) - S.generator
          ⟨x, by rw [S.generator_domain]; exact x.property⟩) = x

decls.name: TauCeti.Semigroups.StronglyContinuousSemigroup.resolvent_sub_resolvent_apply
decls.doc:
Pointwise form of the resolvent identity
`R(lambda) - R(mu) = (mu - lambda) R(lambda) R(mu)`.
decls.statement:
theorem resolvent_sub_resolvent_apply (S : StronglyContinuousSemigroup X)
    {omegaLambda MLambda omegaMu MMu : ℝ}
    [CompleteSpace X]
    (hbLambda : S.HasGrowthBound omegaLambda MLambda)
    (hbMu : S.HasGrowthBound omegaMu MMu) (lambda mu : ℝ)
    (hlambda : omegaLambda < lambda) (hmu : omegaMu < mu) (x : X) :
    S.resolvent hbLambda lambda hlambda x - S.resolvent hbMu mu hmu x =
      (mu - lambda) •
        S.resolvent hbLambda lambda hlambda (S.resolvent hbMu mu hmu x)

decls.name: TauCeti.Semigroups.StronglyContinuousSemigroup.resolvent_sub_resolvent
decls.doc:
The resolvent identity
`R(lambda) - R(mu) = (mu - lambda) R(lambda) R(mu)` as an equality of continuous linear maps.
decls.statement:
theorem resolvent_sub_resolvent (S : StronglyContinuousSemigroup X)
    {omegaLambda MLambda omegaMu MMu : ℝ} [CompleteSpace X]
    (hbLambda : S.HasGrowthBound omegaLambda MLambda)
    (hbMu : S.HasGrowthBound omegaMu MMu) (lambda mu : ℝ)
    (hlambda : omegaLambda < lambda) (hmu : omegaMu < mu) :
    S.resolvent hbLambda lambda hlambda - S.resolvent hbMu mu hmu =
      (mu - lambda) •
        (S.resolvent hbLambda lambda hlambda ∘L S.resolvent hbMu mu hmu)

decls.name: TauCeti.Semigroups.StronglyContinuousSemigroup.resolvent_comm
decls.doc: Resolvents at two admissible parameters commute.
decls.statement:
theorem resolvent_comm (S : StronglyContinuousSemigroup X)
    {omegaLambda MLambda omegaMu MMu : ℝ}
    [CompleteSpace X]
    (hbLambda : S.HasGrowthBound omegaLambda MLambda)
    (hbMu : S.HasGrowthBound omegaMu MMu) (lambda mu : ℝ)
    (hlambda : omegaLambda < lambda) (hmu : omegaMu < mu) :
    S.resolvent hbLambda lambda hlambda ∘L S.resolvent hbMu mu hmu =
      S.resolvent hbMu mu hmu ∘L S.resolvent hbLambda lambda hlambda

decls.name: TauCeti.Semigroups.ContractionSemigroup.resolvent_eq_stronglyContinuousSemigroup_resolvent
decls.statement:
theorem resolvent_eq_stronglyContinuousSemigroup_resolvent
    (S : ContractionSemigroup X) [CompleteSpace X] (lambda : ℝ) (hlambda : 0 < lambda) :
    S.resolvent lambda hlambda =
      S.toStronglyContinuousSemigroup.resolvent S.hasGrowthBound lambda
        (by simpa using hlambda)

decls.name: TauCeti.Semigroups.ContractionSemigroup.resolventLeftInv
decls.doc: The contraction resolvent is a left inverse to `lambda • I - A` on the generator domain.
decls.statement:
theorem resolventLeftInv (S : ContractionSemigroup X) [CompleteSpace X]
    (lambda : ℝ) (hlambda : 0 < lambda) (x : S.toStronglyContinuousSemigroup.domain) :
    S.resolvent lambda hlambda
        (lambda • (x : X) - S.toStronglyContinuousSemigroup.generator
          ⟨x, by rw [StronglyContinuousSemigroup.generator_domain]; exact x.property⟩) = x

decls.name: TauCeti.Semigroups.ContractionSemigroup.resolvent_sub_resolvent
decls.doc: The resolvent identity for a contraction semigroup.
decls.statement:
theorem resolvent_sub_resolvent (S : ContractionSemigroup X) [CompleteSpace X]
    (lambda mu : ℝ) (hlambda : 0 < lambda) (hmu : 0 < mu) :
    S.resolvent lambda hlambda - S.resolvent mu hmu =
      (mu - lambda) • (S.resolvent lambda hlambda ∘L S.resolvent mu hmu)

decls.name: TauCeti.Semigroups.ContractionSemigroup.resolvent_sub_resolvent_apply
decls.doc: Pointwise form of the resolvent identity for a contraction semigroup.
decls.statement:
theorem resolvent_sub_resolvent_apply (S : ContractionSemigroup X) [CompleteSpace X]
    (lambda mu : ℝ) (hlambda : 0 < lambda) (hmu : 0 < mu) (x : X) :
    S.resolvent lambda hlambda x - S.resolvent mu hmu x =
      (mu - lambda) • S.resolvent lambda hlambda (S.resolvent mu hmu x)

decls.name: TauCeti.Semigroups.ContractionSemigroup.resolvent_comm
decls.doc: Resolvents of a contraction semigroup commute.
decls.statement:
theorem resolvent_comm (S : ContractionSemigroup X) [CompleteSpace X]
    (lambda mu : ℝ) (hlambda : 0 < lambda) (hmu : 0 < mu) :
    S.resolvent lambda hlambda ∘L S.resolvent mu hmu =
      S.resolvent mu hmu ∘L S.resolvent lambda hlambda

decls.name: TauCeti.Semigroups.ContractionSemigroup.resolvent_pow_norm_le
decls.doc:
The iterated Hille--Yosida bound for a contraction semigroup:
`‖R(lambda)^n‖ ≤ lambda⁻ⁿ`.
decls.statement:
theorem resolvent_pow_norm_le (S : ContractionSemigroup X) (lambda : ℝ) (hlambda : 0 < lambda)
    (n : ℕ) :
    ‖S.resolvent lambda hlambda ^ n‖ ≤ (1 / lambda) ^ n

decls.name: TauCeti.Semigroups.ContractionSemigroup.norm_resolvent_pow_apply_le
decls.doc: Pointwise form of the iterated contraction resolvent bound.
decls.statement:
theorem norm_resolvent_pow_apply_le (S : ContractionSemigroup X) (lambda : ℝ)
    (hlambda : 0 < lambda) (n : ℕ) (x : X) :
    ‖(S.resolvent lambda hlambda ^ n) x‖ ≤ (1 / lambda) ^ n * ‖x‖

decls.name: TauCeti.Semigroups.ContractionSemigroup.norm_smul_resolvent_pow_le_one
decls.doc: Every power of the scaled contraction resolvent `lambda R(lambda)` has norm at most one.
decls.statement:
theorem norm_smul_resolvent_pow_le_one (S : ContractionSemigroup X) (lambda : ℝ)
    (hlambda : 0 < lambda) (n : ℕ) :
    ‖(lambda • S.resolvent lambda hlambda) ^ n‖ ≤ 1

decls.name: TauCeti.Semigroups.ContractionSemigroup.norm_smul_resolvent_pow_apply_le
decls.doc: Pointwise form of the power bound for the scaled contraction resolvent.
decls.statement:
theorem norm_smul_resolvent_pow_apply_le (S : ContractionSemigroup X) (lambda : ℝ)
    (hlambda : 0 < lambda) (n : ℕ) (x : X) :
    ‖((lambda • S.resolvent lambda hlambda) ^ n) x‖ ≤ ‖x‖

decls.name: TauCeti.hermiteFunction
decls.doc:
The real Hermite function
`ψₙ(x) = Hₙ(x√2) exp(-x² / 2) / sqrt(n! sqrt π)`, using Mathlib's
probabilists' Hermite polynomial `Polynomial.hermite`.
decls.statement: def hermiteFunction (n : ℕ) (x : ℝ) : ℝ

decls.name: TauCeti.hermiteFunction_def
decls.doc: The defining equation for the real Hermite function.
decls.statement:
lemma hermiteFunction_def (n : ℕ) (x : ℝ) :
    hermiteFunction n x =
      aeval (x * Real.sqrt 2) (hermite n) * Real.exp (-(x ^ 2 / 2)) /
        Real.sqrt ((n.factorial : ℝ) * Real.sqrt Real.pi)

decls.name: TauCeti.sqrt_factorial_mul_sqrt_pi_pos
decls.doc: The square root normalization factor in the Hermite function is positive.
decls.statement:
lemma sqrt_factorial_mul_sqrt_pi_pos (n : ℕ) :
    0 < Real.sqrt ((n.factorial : ℝ) * Real.sqrt Real.pi)

decls.name: TauCeti.sqrt_factorial_mul_sqrt_pi_ne_zero
decls.doc: The square root normalization factor in the Hermite function is nonzero.
decls.statement:
lemma sqrt_factorial_mul_sqrt_pi_ne_zero (n : ℕ) :
    Real.sqrt ((n.factorial : ℝ) * Real.sqrt Real.pi) ≠ 0

decls.name: TauCeti.gaussianEnvelope
decls.statement: def gaussianEnvelope (x : ℝ) : ℝ

decls.name: TauCeti.gaussianEnvelope_def
decls.statement:
lemma gaussianEnvelope_def (x : ℝ) :
    gaussianEnvelope x = Real.exp (-(x ^ 2 / 2))

decls.name: TauCeti.continuous_gaussianEnvelope
decls.statement: lemma continuous_gaussianEnvelope : Continuous gaussianEnvelope

decls.name: TauCeti.contDiff_gaussianEnvelope
decls.statement: lemma contDiff_gaussianEnvelope : ContDiff ℝ ⊤ gaussianEnvelope

decls.name: TauCeti.continuous_hermiteFunction_poly
decls.statement:
lemma continuous_hermiteFunction_poly (n : ℕ) :
    Continuous fun x : ℝ => aeval (x * Real.sqrt 2) (hermite n)

decls.name: TauCeti.contDiff_hermiteFunction_poly
decls.statement:
lemma contDiff_hermiteFunction_poly (n : ℕ) :
    ContDiff ℝ ⊤ fun x : ℝ => aeval (x * Real.sqrt 2) (hermite n)

decls.name: TauCeti.continuous_hermiteFunction
decls.doc: The real Hermite functions are continuous.
decls.statement: lemma continuous_hermiteFunction (n : ℕ) : Continuous (hermiteFunction n)

decls.name: TauCeti.contDiff_hermiteFunction
decls.doc: The real Hermite functions are smooth.
decls.statement: lemma contDiff_hermiteFunction (n : ℕ) : ContDiff ℝ ⊤ (hermiteFunction n)

decls.name: TauCeti.hermiteFunction_zero
decls.doc: The zeroth Hermite function is the Gaussian divided by `sqrt (sqrt π)`.
decls.statement:
lemma hermiteFunction_zero (x : ℝ) :
    hermiteFunction 0 x = Real.exp (-(x ^ 2 / 2)) / Real.sqrt (Real.sqrt Real.pi)

decls.name: TauCeti.hermiteFunction_one
decls.doc: The first Hermite function is `sqrt 2 * x` times the zeroth Hermite function.
decls.statement:
lemma hermiteFunction_one (x : ℝ) :
    hermiteFunction 1 x = Real.sqrt 2 * x * hermiteFunction 0 x

decls.name: TauCeti.hermiteFunction_one_eq
decls.doc: The first Hermite function as an explicit scalar multiple of the Gaussian envelope.
decls.statement:
lemma hermiteFunction_one_eq (x : ℝ) :
    hermiteFunction 1 x =
      Real.sqrt 2 * x * Real.exp (-(x ^ 2 / 2)) / Real.sqrt (Real.sqrt Real.pi)

decls.name: TauCeti.aeval_hermite_two
decls.doc: The second probabilists' Hermite polynomial is `X^2 - 1`, evaluated over `ℝ`.
decls.statement:
lemma aeval_hermite_two (x : ℝ) :
    aeval x (hermite 2) = x ^ 2 - 1

decls.name: TauCeti.hermiteFunction_two
decls.doc: The second Hermite function in pointwise form.
decls.statement:
lemma hermiteFunction_two (x : ℝ) :
    hermiteFunction 2 x =
      ((x * Real.sqrt 2) ^ 2 - 1) * Real.exp (-(x ^ 2 / 2)) /
        Real.sqrt ((2 : ℝ) * Real.sqrt Real.pi)

decls.name: TauCeti.hermiteFunction_neg
decls.doc:
**Target A2 (parity).** `ψₙ(-x) = (-1)ⁿ ψₙ(x)`: the Gaussian envelope `exp(-x²/2)` is even and
the polynomial factor `Hₙ(x√2)` carries the parity of `Hₙ` (`Polynomial.hermite_aeval_neg`).
decls.title: Target A2 (parity)
decls.statement:
theorem hermiteFunction_neg (n : ℕ) (x : ℝ) :
    hermiteFunction n (-x) = (-1) ^ n * hermiteFunction n x

decls.name: TauCeti.twoPiHermiteFunction
decls.doc:
The Hermite function rescaled to Mathlib's `exp (-2πixξ)` Fourier convention:
`Φₙ(x) = √(√(2π)) ψₙ(√(2π)x)`. The outer factor makes the dilation unitary on `L²`.
decls.statement: def twoPiHermiteFunction (n : ℕ) (x : ℝ) : ℝ

decls.name: TauCeti.twoPiHermiteFunction_def
decls.doc: The defining equation for the Hermite function rescaled to Mathlib's Fourier convention.
decls.statement:
theorem twoPiHermiteFunction_def (n : ℕ) (x : ℝ) :
    twoPiHermiteFunction n x =
      Real.sqrt (Real.sqrt (2 * Real.pi)) *
        hermiteFunction n (Real.sqrt (2 * Real.pi) * x)

decls.name: TauCeti.hermiteFourierScale_pos
decls.statement: lemma hermiteFourierScale_pos : 0 < Real.sqrt (2 * Real.pi)

decls.name: TauCeti.hermiteFourierScale_ne_zero
decls.statement: lemma hermiteFourierScale_ne_zero : Real.sqrt (2 * Real.pi) ≠ 0

decls.name: TauCeti.hermiteFourierScale_sq
decls.statement:
lemma hermiteFourierScale_sq :
    Real.sqrt (2 * Real.pi) ^ 2 = 2 * Real.pi

decls.name: TauCeti.twoPiHermiteFunction_zero
decls.doc:
The zeroth rescaled Hermite function is a constant multiple of the self-dual Gaussian
`exp (-πx²)`.
decls.statement:
theorem twoPiHermiteFunction_zero (x : ℝ) :
    twoPiHermiteFunction 0 x =
      (Real.sqrt (Real.sqrt (2 * Real.pi)) / Real.sqrt (Real.sqrt Real.pi)) *
        Real.exp (-Real.pi * x ^ 2)

decls.name: TauCeti.continuous_twoPiHermiteFunction
decls.doc: The rescaled Hermite functions are continuous.
decls.statement:
theorem continuous_twoPiHermiteFunction (n : ℕ) :
    Continuous (twoPiHermiteFunction n)

decls.name: TauCeti.mul_twoPiHermiteFunction
decls.doc: The position ladder relation after the `√(2π)` dilation.
decls.statement:
theorem mul_twoPiHermiteFunction (n : ℕ) (x : ℝ) :
    x * twoPiHermiteFunction n x =
      (Real.sqrt (((n : ℝ) + 1) / 2) / Real.sqrt (2 * Real.pi)) *
          twoPiHermiteFunction (n + 1) x
        + (Real.sqrt ((n : ℝ) / 2) / Real.sqrt (2 * Real.pi)) *
          twoPiHermiteFunction (n - 1) x

decls.name: TauCeti.hasDerivAt_twoPiHermiteFunction
decls.doc: The derivative ladder relation after the `√(2π)` dilation.
decls.statement:
theorem hasDerivAt_twoPiHermiteFunction (n : ℕ) (x : ℝ) :
    HasDerivAt (twoPiHermiteFunction n)
      (Real.sqrt (2 * Real.pi) *
        (Real.sqrt ((n : ℝ) / 2) * twoPiHermiteFunction (n - 1) x
          - Real.sqrt (((n : ℝ) + 1) / 2) * twoPiHermiteFunction (n + 1) x)) x

decls.name: TauCeti.deriv_twoPiHermiteFunction
decls.doc: The derivative form of `hasDerivAt_twoPiHermiteFunction`.
decls.statement:
theorem deriv_twoPiHermiteFunction (n : ℕ) (x : ℝ) :
    deriv (twoPiHermiteFunction n) x =
      Real.sqrt (2 * Real.pi) *
        (Real.sqrt ((n : ℝ) / 2) * twoPiHermiteFunction (n - 1) x
          - Real.sqrt (((n : ℝ) + 1) / 2) * twoPiHermiteFunction (n + 1) x)

decls.name: TauCeti.mul_sub_invScale_deriv_twoPiHermiteFunction
decls.doc: The creation relation for the rescaled family.
decls.statement:
theorem mul_sub_invScale_deriv_twoPiHermiteFunction (n : ℕ) (x : ℝ) :
    Real.sqrt (2 * Real.pi) * x * twoPiHermiteFunction n x
        - (Real.sqrt (2 * Real.pi))⁻¹ * deriv (twoPiHermiteFunction n) x
      = Real.sqrt (2 * ((n : ℝ) + 1)) * twoPiHermiteFunction (n + 1) x

decls.name: TauCeti.integrable_twoPiHermiteFunction
decls.doc: Every rescaled Hermite function is integrable.
decls.statement:
theorem integrable_twoPiHermiteFunction (n : ℕ) :
    Integrable (twoPiHermiteFunction n) volume

decls.name: TauCeti.integrable_mul_twoPiHermiteFunction
decls.statement:
theorem integrable_mul_twoPiHermiteFunction (n : ℕ) :
    Integrable (fun x : ℝ => x * twoPiHermiteFunction n x) volume

decls.name: TauCeti.integrable_deriv_twoPiHermiteFunction
decls.statement:
theorem integrable_deriv_twoPiHermiteFunction (n : ℕ) :
    Integrable (deriv (twoPiHermiteFunction n)) volume

decls.name: TauCeti.integrable_twoPiHermiteFunction_complex
decls.statement:
theorem integrable_twoPiHermiteFunction_complex (n : ℕ) :
    Integrable (fun x : ℝ => (twoPiHermiteFunction n x : ℂ)) volume

decls.name: TauCeti.integrable_mul_twoPiHermiteFunction_complex
decls.statement:
theorem integrable_mul_twoPiHermiteFunction_complex (n : ℕ) :
    Integrable (fun x : ℝ => x • (twoPiHermiteFunction n x : ℂ)) volume

decls.name: TauCeti.hasDerivAt_twoPiHermiteFunction_complex
decls.statement:
theorem hasDerivAt_twoPiHermiteFunction_complex (n : ℕ) (x : ℝ) :
    HasDerivAt (fun y : ℝ => (twoPiHermiteFunction n y : ℂ))
      ((deriv (twoPiHermiteFunction n) x : ℝ) : ℂ) x

decls.name: TauCeti.differentiable_twoPiHermiteFunction_complex
decls.statement:
theorem differentiable_twoPiHermiteFunction_complex (n : ℕ) :
    Differentiable ℝ fun x : ℝ => (twoPiHermiteFunction n x : ℂ)

decls.name: TauCeti.deriv_twoPiHermiteFunction_complex
decls.statement:
theorem deriv_twoPiHermiteFunction_complex (n : ℕ) :
    deriv (fun x : ℝ => (twoPiHermiteFunction n x : ℂ)) =
      fun x => ((deriv (twoPiHermiteFunction n) x : ℝ) : ℂ)

decls.name: TauCeti.integrable_deriv_twoPiHermiteFunction_complex
decls.statement:
theorem integrable_deriv_twoPiHermiteFunction_complex (n : ℕ) :
    Integrable (deriv fun x : ℝ => (twoPiHermiteFunction n x : ℂ)) volume

decls.name: TauCeti.fourier_const_smul
decls.statement:
theorem fourier_const_smul (c : ℂ) (f : ℝ → ℂ) :
    𝓕 (c • f) = c • 𝓕 f

decls.name: TauCeti.fourier_twoPiHermiteFunction_zero
decls.statement:
theorem fourier_twoPiHermiteFunction_zero :
    𝓕 (fun x : ℝ => (twoPiHermiteFunction 0 x : ℂ)) =
      fun x : ℝ => (twoPiHermiteFunction 0 x : ℂ)

decls.name: TauCeti.twoPiHermiteFunction_succ_complex
decls.statement:
theorem twoPiHermiteFunction_succ_complex (n : ℕ) :
    (fun x : ℝ => (twoPiHermiteFunction (n + 1) x : ℂ)) =
      (Real.sqrt (2 * ((n : ℝ) + 1)) : ℂ)⁻¹ •
        ((Real.sqrt (2 * Real.pi) : ℂ) •
            (fun x : ℝ => x • (twoPiHermiteFunction n x : ℂ))
          + (-(Real.sqrt (2 * Real.pi) : ℂ)⁻¹) •
            (fun x : ℝ => ((deriv (twoPiHermiteFunction n) x : ℝ) : ℂ)))

decls.name: TauCeti.fourier_mul_twoPiHermiteFunction_of_eigen
decls.statement:
theorem fourier_mul_twoPiHermiteFunction_of_eigen (n : ℕ) (eigen : ℂ)
    (hfourier :
      𝓕 (fun x : ℝ => (twoPiHermiteFunction n x : ℂ)) =
        fun x => eigen * twoPiHermiteFunction n x) :
    𝓕 (fun x : ℝ => x • (twoPiHermiteFunction n x : ℂ)) =
      fun w => Complex.I / (2 * Real.pi) * eigen *
        ((deriv (twoPiHermiteFunction n) w : ℝ) : ℂ)

decls.name: TauCeti.fourier_deriv_twoPiHermiteFunction_of_eigen
decls.statement:
theorem fourier_deriv_twoPiHermiteFunction_of_eigen (n : ℕ) (eigen : ℂ)
    (hfourier :
      𝓕 (fun x : ℝ => (twoPiHermiteFunction n x : ℂ)) =
        fun x => eigen * twoPiHermiteFunction n x) :
    𝓕 (fun x : ℝ => ((deriv (twoPiHermiteFunction n) x : ℝ) : ℂ)) =
      fun w => (2 * Real.pi * Complex.I * w) * eigen * twoPiHermiteFunction n w

decls.name: TauCeti.fourier_twoPiHermiteFunction_succ_eq
decls.doc:
The Fourier transform of the successor, in terms of the transforms of `x ↦ x · hₙ x` and of
`hₙ'`: the raising relation `twoPiHermiteFunction_succ_complex` pushed through linearity of the
transform. No eigenfunction hypothesis is involved, so this holds for every `n`.
decls.statement:
theorem fourier_twoPiHermiteFunction_succ_eq (n : ℕ) (w : ℝ) :
    𝓕 (fun x : ℝ => (twoPiHermiteFunction (n + 1) x : ℂ)) w =
      (Real.sqrt (2 * ((n : ℝ) + 1)) : ℂ)⁻¹ *
        ((Real.sqrt (2 * Real.pi) : ℂ) *
            𝓕 (fun x : ℝ => x • (twoPiHermiteFunction n x : ℂ)) w
          + (-(Real.sqrt (2 * Real.pi) : ℂ)⁻¹) *
            𝓕 (fun x : ℝ => ((deriv (twoPiHermiteFunction n) x : ℝ) : ℂ)) w)

decls.name: TauCeti.fourier_twoPiHermiteFunction_succ
decls.statement:
theorem fourier_twoPiHermiteFunction_succ (n : ℕ) (eigen : ℂ)
    (hfourier :
      𝓕 (fun x : ℝ => (twoPiHermiteFunction n x : ℂ)) =
        fun x => eigen * twoPiHermiteFunction n x) :
    𝓕 (fun x : ℝ => (twoPiHermiteFunction (n + 1) x : ℂ)) =
      fun x => (-Complex.I * eigen) * twoPiHermiteFunction (n + 1) x

decls.name: TauCeti.fourier_twoPiHermiteFunction
decls.doc:
**Fourier eigenfunction theorem.** For Mathlib's `exp (-2πixξ)` convention, the rescaled
Hermite function `Φₙ(x) = √(√(2π)) ψₙ(√(2π)x)` has eigenvalue `(-i)ⁿ`.
decls.title: Fourier eigenfunction theorem
decls.statement:
theorem fourier_twoPiHermiteFunction (n : ℕ) :
    𝓕 (fun x : ℝ => (twoPiHermiteFunction n x : ℂ)) =
      fun x : ℝ => (-Complex.I) ^ n * twoPiHermiteFunction n x

decls.name: TauCeti.degree_hermiteDilated
decls.doc:
The dilation preserves degrees: `Hₙ(√2 · X)` has degree exactly `n`.

`TauCeti.hermiteDilated` itself lives in the `MemLp` layer, where the membership results are
already stated about it; only this degree fact is new here, and only the basis construction
needs it.
decls.statement: theorem degree_hermiteDilated (n : ℕ) : (hermiteDilated n).degree = (n : WithBot ℕ)

decls.name: TauCeti.integrable_exp_mul_abs_gaussianWeight
decls.doc:
**Finite exponential moments of the Gaussian weight.** For every rate `a`, `e^{a|x|}` is
integrable against `e^{-x²}·dx`, because `a|x| ≤ (a² + x²)/2` gives the domination
`e^{a|x|}e^{-x²} ≤ e^{a²/2}·e^{-x²/2}`.
decls.title: Finite exponential moments of the Gaussian weight
decls.statement:
theorem integrable_exp_mul_abs_gaussianWeight (a : ℝ) :
    Integrable (fun x : ℝ => Real.exp (a * |x|))
      (volume.withDensity fun x => ENNReal.ofReal (Real.exp (-x ^ 2)))

decls.name: TauCeti.hermiteNormalization_pos
decls.doc: The Hermite normalization `cₙ = n!·√π` is positive.
decls.statement: theorem hermiteNormalization_pos (n : ℕ) : (0 : ℝ) < (n.factorial : ℝ) * Real.sqrt Real.pi

decls.name: TauCeti.integral_hermiteDilated_mul_hermiteDilated_mul_gaussianWeight
decls.doc:
**Orthogonality against the Gaussian weight.** `∫ Hₘ(x√2)Hₙ(x√2)e^{-x²} = δₘₙ·n!√π`. This is
the Hermite function orthonormality (milestone A2) with the normalizations put back.
decls.title: Orthogonality against the Gaussian weight
decls.statement:
theorem integral_hermiteDilated_mul_hermiteDilated_mul_gaussianWeight (m n : ℕ) :
    (∫ x : ℝ, (hermiteDilated m).eval x * (hermiteDilated n).eval x * Real.exp (-x ^ 2))
      = if m = n then (n.factorial : ℝ) * Real.sqrt Real.pi else 0

decls.name: TauCeti.memLp_hermiteDilated_normalized
decls.doc:
The `MemLp` obligation for the dilated Hermite family against the Gaussian weight. This is the
generic `TauCeti.memLp_two_bareNormalized` at `p = hermiteDilated`, `c n = n!√π`; the only content
specific to this family is the exponential moment of `e^{-x²}`.
decls.statement:
theorem memLp_hermiteDilated_normalized (n : ℕ) :
    MemLp (fun x : ℝ => (algebraMap ℝ 𝕜)
        ((hermiteDilated n).eval x / Real.sqrt ((n.factorial : ℝ) * Real.sqrt Real.pi))) 2
      (volume.withDensity fun x => ENNReal.ofReal (Real.exp (-x ^ 2)))

decls.name: TauCeti.hermiteHilbertBasis
decls.doc:
**Roadmap A3: the Hermite functions are a Hilbert basis of `L²(ℝ)`.** Orthonormality comes from
the weighted-measure machinery and completeness from moment determinacy
(`TauCeti.orthogonal_span_range_bareNormalizedLp_eq_bot`), applied to the exact-degree family
`Hₙ(x√2)` against the Gaussian weight `e^{-x²}`.
decls.title: Roadmap A3: the Hermite functions are a Hilbert basis of `L²(ℝ)`
decls.statement: def hermiteHilbertBasis : HilbertBasis ℕ 𝕜 (Lp 𝕜 2 (volume : Measure ℝ))

decls.name: TauCeti.coe_hermiteHilbertBasis
decls.doc:
**The basis vectors are the Hermite functions.** Without this the construction would only
exhibit *some* Hilbert basis; here the `√w`-envelope of `Hₙ(x√2)/√cₙ` is identified with `ψₙ`.
decls.title: The basis vectors are the Hermite functions
decls.statement: theorem coe_hermiteHilbertBasis : ⇑(hermiteHilbertBasis 𝕜) = hermiteFunctionLp 𝕜

decls.name: TauCeti.normFactor_succ
decls.doc: The Hermite normalization `√(n!·√π)` at successor index: `√((n+1)!·√π) = √(n+1)·√(n!·√π)`.
decls.statement:
lemma normFactor_succ (n : ℕ) :
    Real.sqrt (((n + 1).factorial : ℝ) * Real.sqrt Real.pi)
      = Real.sqrt (n + 1) * Real.sqrt ((n.factorial : ℝ) * Real.sqrt Real.pi)

decls.name: TauCeti.sqrt_four
decls.doc: `√4 = 2`, used to split the square factor out of `√(2k)`.
decls.statement: lemma sqrt_four : Real.sqrt 4 = 2

decls.name: TauCeti.two_mul_sqrt_half
decls.doc:
`2·√(k/2) = √(2k)`: the coefficient identity behind the ladder-operator normalizations.
Regroup `2·k = 4·(k/2)` so the square factor `√4 = 2` splits off `√(k/2)`.
decls.statement: lemma two_mul_sqrt_half (k : ℝ) : 2 * Real.sqrt (k / 2) = Real.sqrt (2 * k)

decls.name: TauCeti.sqrt_half_mul_sqrt_two
decls.doc:
`√(1/2)·√2 = 1`: the coefficient collapsing the `n = 0` boundary of the ladder relations, where
the `√((n+1)/2) = √(1/2)` prefactor meets the `√2` from the `x√2` argument of `H₀`.
decls.statement: lemma sqrt_half_mul_sqrt_two : Real.sqrt (1 / 2) * Real.sqrt 2 = 1

decls.name: TauCeti.sqrt_two_mul_aeval_derivative_hermite
decls.doc:
The Gaussian-weighted derivative factor produces the lower Hermite mode:
`H'ₙ(x√2)·√2·e^{-x²/2} / √(n!√π) = √(2n)·ψ_{n-1}(x)`. This isolates the normalization bookkeeping
that the derivative ladder relation shares with nothing else: it turns the `d/dx` of the polynomial
part into a clean multiple of `ψ_{n-1}`, so `hasDerivAt_hermiteFunction` reduces to
`mul_hermiteFunction` by pure algebra. At `n = 0` both sides vanish.
decls.statement:
lemma sqrt_two_mul_aeval_derivative_hermite (n : ℕ) (x : ℝ) :
    aeval (x * Real.sqrt 2) (derivative (hermite n)) * Real.sqrt 2 * Real.exp (-(x ^ 2 / 2))
        / Real.sqrt ((n.factorial : ℝ) * Real.sqrt Real.pi)
      = Real.sqrt (2 * (n : ℝ)) * hermiteFunction (n - 1) x

decls.name: TauCeti.mul_hermiteFunction
decls.doc:
**Target A2 (position ladder relation).** Multiplying `ψₙ` by `x` mixes the neighbouring modes:
`x·ψₙ = √((n+1)/2)·ψ_{n+1} + √(n/2)·ψ_{n-1}`.
decls.title: Target A2 (position ladder relation)
decls.statement:
theorem mul_hermiteFunction (n : ℕ) (x : ℝ) :
    x * hermiteFunction n x =
      Real.sqrt (((n : ℝ) + 1) / 2) * hermiteFunction (n + 1) x
        + Real.sqrt ((n : ℝ) / 2) * hermiteFunction (n - 1) x

decls.name: TauCeti.hasDerivAt_hermiteFunction
decls.doc:
**Target A2 (derivative ladder relation).** Differentiating `ψₙ` mixes the neighbouring modes:
`ψₙ' = √(n/2)·ψ_{n-1} - √((n+1)/2)·ψ_{n+1}`.
decls.title: Target A2 (derivative ladder relation)
decls.statement:
theorem hasDerivAt_hermiteFunction (n : ℕ) (x : ℝ) :
    HasDerivAt (hermiteFunction n)
      (Real.sqrt ((n : ℝ) / 2) * hermiteFunction (n - 1) x
        - Real.sqrt (((n : ℝ) + 1) / 2) * hermiteFunction (n + 1) x) x

decls.name: TauCeti.deriv_hermiteFunction
decls.doc: The `deriv` form of `hasDerivAt_hermiteFunction`.
decls.statement:
theorem deriv_hermiteFunction (n : ℕ) (x : ℝ) :
    deriv (hermiteFunction n) x =
      Real.sqrt ((n : ℝ) / 2) * hermiteFunction (n - 1) x
        - Real.sqrt (((n : ℝ) + 1) / 2) * hermiteFunction (n + 1) x

decls.name: TauCeti.mul_add_deriv_hermiteFunction
decls.doc:
**Annihilation identity.** The combination `x·ψₙ + ψₙ' = √(2n)·ψ_{n-1}`; this is the ladder
operator `a = (x + d/dx)/√2` acting as `a ψₙ = √n·ψ_{n-1}`.
decls.title: Annihilation identity
decls.statement:
theorem mul_add_deriv_hermiteFunction (n : ℕ) (x : ℝ) :
    x * hermiteFunction n x + deriv (hermiteFunction n) x
      = Real.sqrt (2 * (n : ℝ)) * hermiteFunction (n - 1) x

decls.name: TauCeti.mul_sub_deriv_hermiteFunction
decls.doc:
**Creation identity.** The combination `x·ψₙ - ψₙ' = √(2(n+1))·ψ_{n+1}`; this is the ladder
operator `a† = (x - d/dx)/√2` acting as `a† ψₙ = √(n+1)·ψ_{n+1}`.
decls.title: Creation identity
decls.statement:
theorem mul_sub_deriv_hermiteFunction (n : ℕ) (x : ℝ) :
    x * hermiteFunction n x - deriv (hermiteFunction n) x
      = Real.sqrt (2 * ((n : ℝ) + 1)) * hermiteFunction (n + 1) x

decls.name: TauCeti.inner_algebraMap_algebraMap
decls.doc: The inner product of two real scalar casts is the scalar cast of their product.
decls.statement:
lemma inner_algebraMap_algebraMap (a b : ℝ) :
    inner 𝕜 ((algebraMap ℝ 𝕜) a) ((algebraMap ℝ 𝕜) b) =
      (algebraMap ℝ 𝕜) (a * b)

decls.name: TauCeti.memLp_two_algebraMap_hermiteFunction
decls.doc: The `𝕜`-valued scalar cast of a Hermite function lies in `L²(volume)`.
decls.statement:
theorem memLp_two_algebraMap_hermiteFunction (n : ℕ) :
    MemLp (fun x : ℝ => (algebraMap ℝ 𝕜) (hermiteFunction n x)) 2 volume

decls.name: TauCeti.hermiteFunctionLp
decls.doc:
The `n`th Hermite function as a vector of `L²(ℝ, volume; 𝕜)`, with the real pointwise
function cast through `algebraMap ℝ 𝕜`.
decls.statement:
def hermiteFunctionLp (𝕜 : Type*) [RCLike 𝕜] (n : ℕ) :
    Lp 𝕜 2 (volume : Measure ℝ)

decls.name: TauCeti.coeFn_hermiteFunctionLp
decls.doc:
The `Lp` representative of `hermiteFunctionLp` is the scalar cast of the pointwise
Hermite function.
decls.statement:
lemma coeFn_hermiteFunctionLp (n : ℕ) :
    ⇑(hermiteFunctionLp 𝕜 n) =ᵐ[volume]
      fun x : ℝ => (algebraMap ℝ 𝕜) (hermiteFunction n x)

decls.name: TauCeti.coeFn_hermiteFunctionLp_real
decls.doc:
In real scalars, `hermiteFunctionLp` has the original pointwise Hermite function as an
a.e. representative.
decls.statement:
lemma coeFn_hermiteFunctionLp_real (n : ℕ) :
    ⇑(hermiteFunctionLp ℝ n) =ᵐ[volume] hermiteFunction n

decls.name: TauCeti.inner_hermiteFunctionLp_zero_zero
decls.doc:
The zeroth `Lp` Hermite function has inner product one with itself, over any `RCLike`
scalar field.
decls.statement:
lemma inner_hermiteFunctionLp_zero_zero :
    inner 𝕜 (hermiteFunctionLp 𝕜 0) (hermiteFunctionLp 𝕜 0) = 1

decls.name: TauCeti.norm_hermiteFunctionLp_zero
decls.doc: The zeroth `Lp` Hermite function is a unit vector, over any `RCLike` scalar field.
decls.statement: lemma norm_hermiteFunctionLp_zero : ‖hermiteFunctionLp 𝕜 0‖ = 1

decls.name: TauCeti.hermiteDilated
decls.doc:
The dilated Hermite polynomial `Hₙ(√2 · X)`, the polynomial whose Gaussian envelope is the
Hermite function `ψₙ`.

It is defined at this layer rather than at the basis layer because every `MemLp` result below is
already about it: `ψₙ` *is* this polynomial times `exp(-x²/2)`, up to normalization.
decls.statement: def hermiteDilated (n : ℕ) : Polynomial ℝ

decls.name: TauCeti.hermiteDilated_def
decls.doc:
The defining equation of `TauCeti.hermiteDilated`, exported so that consumers in other modules
can rewrite with it.
decls.statement:
theorem hermiteDilated_def (n : ℕ) :
    hermiteDilated n
      = (hermiteℝ n).comp (Polynomial.C (Real.sqrt 2) * Polynomial.X)

decls.name: TauCeti.eval_hermiteDilated
decls.doc: Evaluating the dilated Hermite polynomial is `aeval (·√2)`.
decls.statement:
theorem eval_hermiteDilated (n : ℕ) (x : ℝ) :
    (hermiteDilated n).eval x = aeval (x * Real.sqrt 2) (hermite n)

decls.name: TauCeti.integrable_hermiteFunction
decls.doc:
**Target A2 (`L¹`).** Each Hermite function is integrable against Lebesgue measure: it is a
polynomial in `x` times the Gaussian envelope `exp(-x²/2)`, the `v = 1` case of
`integrable_eval_mul_gaussianEnvelope`.
decls.title: Target A2 (`L¹`)
decls.statement: theorem integrable_hermiteFunction (n : ℕ) : Integrable (hermiteFunction n) volume

decls.name: TauCeti.memLp_two_hermiteFunction
decls.doc:
**Target A2 (`L²`).** Each Hermite function lies in `L²(volume)`. Its square is
`(Hₙ(x√2))² exp(-x²)` up to the constant `(n!√π)`, integrable by `integrable_eval_mul_exp_neg_sq`,
and `L²` membership is integrability of the square (`memLp_two_iff_integrable_sq`). This is the
membership `hermiteFunctionLp` needs to realize `ψₙ` as an element of `Lp ℝ 2 volume`.
decls.title: Target A2 (`L²`)
decls.statement: theorem memLp_two_hermiteFunction (n : ℕ) : MemLp (hermiteFunction n) 2 volume

decls.name: TauCeti.integral_hermiteFunction_zero_mul_self_expanded
decls.statement:
lemma integral_hermiteFunction_zero_mul_self_expanded :
    ∫ x : ℝ, Real.exp (-(x ^ 2 / 2)) / Real.sqrt (Real.sqrt Real.pi) *
      (Real.exp (-(x ^ 2 / 2)) / Real.sqrt (Real.sqrt Real.pi)) = 1

decls.name: TauCeti.integral_hermiteFunction_zero_mul_self
decls.doc:
The zeroth Hermite function has square integral one. This is the `n = 0` boundary case of
the roadmap's Hermite-function orthonormality target.
decls.statement:
lemma integral_hermiteFunction_zero_mul_self :
    ∫ x : ℝ, hermiteFunction 0 x * hermiteFunction 0 x = 1

decls.name: TauCeti.integral_hermiteFunction_mul_hermiteFunction
decls.doc:
**Target A2 (orthonormality).** The Hermite functions are pointwise orthonormal in `L²(ℝ)`:
`∫ x, ψₘ(x) · ψₙ(x) = if m = n then 1 else 0`. This is the polynomial orthogonality relation
`integral_hermite_mul_hermite_mul_gaussian` pushed through the dilation `u = x√2`.
decls.title: Target A2 (orthonormality)
decls.statement:
theorem integral_hermiteFunction_mul_hermiteFunction (m n : ℕ) :
    ∫ x : ℝ, hermiteFunction m x * hermiteFunction n x = if m = n then 1 else 0

decls.name: TauCeti.inner_hermiteFunctionLp
decls.doc:
**Target A3 (orthonormality, inner-product form).** The `Lp` Hermite vectors satisfy
`⟪ψₘ, ψₙ⟫ = if m = n then 1 else 0`, over any `RCLike` scalar field, by evaluating the `L²` inner
product as the pointwise integral `integral_hermiteFunction_mul_hermiteFunction`.
decls.title: Target A3 (orthonormality, inner-product form)
decls.statement:
theorem inner_hermiteFunctionLp (m n : ℕ) :
    inner 𝕜 (hermiteFunctionLp 𝕜 m) (hermiteFunctionLp 𝕜 n) = if m = n then (1 : 𝕜) else 0

decls.name: TauCeti.orthonormal_hermiteFunctionLp
decls.doc:
**Target A3 (orthonormality).** The `Lp` Hermite functions form an orthonormal system in
`L²(ℝ; 𝕜)`, for any `RCLike` scalar field `𝕜`. This is the orthonormality input the
`hermiteHilbertBasis` construction feeds to `HilbertBasis.mkOfOrthogonalEqBot`.
decls.title: Target A3 (orthonormality)
decls.statement: theorem orthonormal_hermiteFunctionLp : Orthonormal 𝕜 (hermiteFunctionLp 𝕜)

decls.name: TauCeti.hasDerivAt_deriv_hermiteFunction
decls.doc:
**Second derivative of the Hermite function** (the derivative form). The Hermite function `ψₙ`
solves `ψₙ'' = (x² - (2n+1))·ψₙ`; this states that the derivative of `ψₙ'` at `x` equals
`(x² - (2n+1))·ψₙ(x)`.
decls.title: Second derivative of the Hermite function
decls.statement:
theorem hasDerivAt_deriv_hermiteFunction (n : ℕ) (x : ℝ) :
    HasDerivAt (deriv (hermiteFunction n))
      ((x ^ 2 - (2 * n + 1)) * hermiteFunction n x) x

decls.name: TauCeti.deriv_deriv_hermiteFunction
decls.doc:
**Second derivative of the Hermite function.** `ψₙ'' = (x² - (2n+1))·ψₙ`; the closed form
behind the harmonic-oscillator eigen-equation.
decls.title: Second derivative of the Hermite function
decls.statement:
theorem deriv_deriv_hermiteFunction (n : ℕ) (x : ℝ) :
    deriv (deriv (hermiteFunction n)) x = (x ^ 2 - (2 * n + 1)) * hermiteFunction n x

decls.name: TauCeti.hermiteFunction_oscillator
decls.doc:
**The harmonic-oscillator eigen-equation.** The Hermite function `ψₙ` is an eigenfunction of the
Schrödinger operator `-d²/dx² + x²` with eigenvalue `2n+1`:

`-ψₙ'' + x²·ψₙ = (2n+1)·ψₙ`.
decls.title: The harmonic-oscillator eigen-equation
decls.statement:
theorem hermiteFunction_oscillator (n : ℕ) (x : ℝ) :
    -deriv (deriv (hermiteFunction n)) x + x ^ 2 * hermiteFunction n x
      = (2 * n + 1) * hermiteFunction n x

decls.name: TauCeti.iteratedDeriv_two_hermiteFunction
decls.doc: The oscillator eigen-equation phrased with `iteratedDeriv 2`.
decls.statement:
theorem iteratedDeriv_two_hermiteFunction (n : ℕ) (x : ℝ) :
    iteratedDeriv 2 (hermiteFunction n) x = (x ^ 2 - (2 * n + 1)) * hermiteFunction n x

decls.name: TauCeti.hermiteHilbertBasis_repr_apply
decls.doc:
The coordinates of `f` in the Hermite basis are its inner products against the Hermite
functions.
decls.statement:
theorem hermiteHilbertBasis_repr_apply (f : Lp 𝕜 2 (volume : Measure ℝ)) (n : ℕ) :
    (hermiteHilbertBasis 𝕜).repr f n = inner 𝕜 (hermiteFunctionLp 𝕜 n) f

decls.name: TauCeti.tsum_inner_mul_inner_hermiteFunctionLp
decls.doc:
**Parseval's identity for the Hermite basis** (polarized form): the Hermite coordinates of
`f` and `g` pair to their inner product.
decls.title: Parseval's identity for the Hermite basis
decls.statement:
theorem tsum_inner_mul_inner_hermiteFunctionLp (f g : Lp 𝕜 2 (volume : Measure ℝ)) :
    ∑' n : ℕ, inner 𝕜 f (hermiteFunctionLp 𝕜 n) * inner 𝕜 (hermiteFunctionLp 𝕜 n) g
      = inner 𝕜 f g

decls.name: TauCeti.tsum_norm_sq_inner_hermiteFunctionLp
decls.doc:
**Parseval's identity for the Hermite basis** (norm-square form): the squared Hermite
coordinates of `f` sum to `‖f‖²`. This is the roadmap's Part A3 acceptance criterion.
decls.title: Parseval's identity for the Hermite basis
decls.statement:
theorem tsum_norm_sq_inner_hermiteFunctionLp (f : Lp 𝕜 2 (volume : Measure ℝ)) :
    ∑' n : ℕ, ‖inner 𝕜 (hermiteFunctionLp 𝕜 n) f‖ ^ 2 = ‖f‖ ^ 2

decls.name: TauCeti.summable_norm_sq_inner_hermiteFunctionLp
decls.doc: The squared Hermite coordinate family of an `L²` function is summable.
decls.statement:
theorem summable_norm_sq_inner_hermiteFunctionLp (f : Lp 𝕜 2 (volume : Measure ℝ)) :
    Summable fun n : ℕ => ‖inner 𝕜 (hermiteFunctionLp 𝕜 n) f‖ ^ 2

decls.name: TauCeti.hasSum_hermiteFunctionLp_expansion
decls.doc: **The Hermite expansion.** Every `f ∈ L²(ℝ)` is the sum of its Hermite series.
decls.title: The Hermite expansion
decls.statement:
theorem hasSum_hermiteFunctionLp_expansion (f : Lp 𝕜 2 (volume : Measure ℝ)) :
    HasSum (fun n : ℕ => inner 𝕜 (hermiteFunctionLp 𝕜 n) f • hermiteFunctionLp 𝕜 n) f

decls.name: TauCeti.hermiteHilbertBasis_repr_self
decls.doc: The coordinates of the `n`-th Hermite function are a single `1` in position `n`.
decls.statement:
theorem hermiteHilbertBasis_repr_self (n : ℕ) :
    (hermiteHilbertBasis 𝕜).repr (hermiteFunctionLp 𝕜 n) = lp.single 2 n (1 : 𝕜)

decls.name: TauCeti.hermiteFunctionPiBasis
decls.doc:
**The multidimensional Hermite-function basis.** `piHilbertBasis` over the one-dimensional
Hermite-function basis in every coordinate — the eigenbasis of the `ℝ^ι` harmonic oscillator.
decls.title: The multidimensional Hermite-function basis
decls.statement:
def hermiteFunctionPiBasis :
    HilbertBasis (ι → ℕ) 𝕜 (Lp 𝕜 2 (Measure.pi fun _ : ι => (volume : Measure ℝ)))

decls.name: TauCeti.coeFn_hermiteFunctionPiBasis
decls.doc:
**The basis vectors are the multi-index Hermite-function products.** Without this the
construction would only exhibit *some* Hilbert basis of `L²(volume^ι)`. The coordinatewise
identification `⇑(hermiteHilbertBasis 𝕜) = hermiteFunctionLp 𝕜` transfers to the product measure
because each evaluation map pushes the product's a.e. filter into the factor's
(`MeasureTheory.Measure.tendsto_eval_ae_ae`).
decls.title: The basis vectors are the multi-index Hermite-function products
decls.statement:
theorem coeFn_hermiteFunctionPiBasis (a : ι → ℕ) :
    ⇑(hermiteFunctionPiBasis 𝕜 ι a)
      =ᵐ[Measure.pi fun _ : ι => (volume : Measure ℝ)]
        fun x => ∏ i, (algebraMap ℝ 𝕜) (hermiteFunction (a i) (x i))

decls.name: TauCeti.tendsto_pow_mul_eval_mul_gaussian
decls.statement:
theorem tendsto_pow_mul_eval_mul_gaussian (p : ℝ[X]) (k : ℕ) :
    Tendsto (fun x : ℝ => x ^ k * p.eval x * Real.exp (-(x ^ 2 / 2)))
      (cocompact ℝ) (𝓝 0)

decls.name: TauCeti.gaussianSchwartzMap
decls.statement: def gaussianSchwartzMap : 𝓢(ℝ, ℝ)

decls.name: TauCeti.gaussianSchwartzMap_apply
decls.statement:
theorem gaussianSchwartzMap_apply (x : ℝ) :
    gaussianSchwartzMap x = Real.exp (-(x ^ 2 / 2))

decls.name: TauCeti.hasTemperateGrowth_hermiteFactor
decls.statement:
theorem hasTemperateGrowth_hermiteFactor (n : ℕ) :
    Function.HasTemperateGrowth
      (fun x : ℝ => aeval (x * Real.sqrt 2) (hermite n) /
        Real.sqrt ((n.factorial : ℝ) * Real.sqrt Real.pi))

decls.name: TauCeti.hermiteSchwartzMap
decls.doc: The `n`th Hermite function, as an element of the real Schwartz space `𝓢(ℝ, ℝ)`.
decls.statement: def hermiteSchwartzMap (n : ℕ) : 𝓢(ℝ, ℝ)

decls.name: TauCeti.hermiteSchwartzMap_apply
decls.doc: The underlying function of `hermiteSchwartzMap n` is `hermiteFunction n`.
decls.statement:
theorem hermiteSchwartzMap_apply (n : ℕ) (x : ℝ) :
    hermiteSchwartzMap n x = hermiteFunction n x

decls.name: TauCeti.coe_hermiteSchwartzMap
decls.doc: The coercion of `hermiteSchwartzMap n` is the pointwise Hermite function.
decls.statement:
theorem coe_hermiteSchwartzMap (n : ℕ) :
    ⇑(hermiteSchwartzMap n) = hermiteFunction n

decls.name: TauCeti.mul_hermiteSchwartzMap
decls.doc: The position ladder relation, as an equality in Schwartz space.
decls.statement:
theorem mul_hermiteSchwartzMap (n : ℕ) :
    SchwartzMap.smulLeftCLM ℝ (fun x : ℝ => x) (hermiteSchwartzMap n) =
      Real.sqrt (((n : ℝ) + 1) / 2) • hermiteSchwartzMap (n + 1) +
        Real.sqrt ((n : ℝ) / 2) • hermiteSchwartzMap (n - 1)

decls.name: TauCeti.deriv_hermiteSchwartzMap
decls.doc: The derivative ladder relation, as an equality in Schwartz space.
decls.statement:
theorem deriv_hermiteSchwartzMap (n : ℕ) :
    SchwartzMap.derivCLM ℝ ℝ (hermiteSchwartzMap n) =
      Real.sqrt ((n : ℝ) / 2) • hermiteSchwartzMap (n - 1) -
        Real.sqrt (((n : ℝ) + 1) / 2) • hermiteSchwartzMap (n + 1)

decls.name: TauCeti.mul_add_deriv_hermiteSchwartzMap
decls.doc: The annihilation relation, as an equality in Schwartz space.
decls.statement:
theorem mul_add_deriv_hermiteSchwartzMap (n : ℕ) :
    SchwartzMap.smulLeftCLM ℝ (fun x : ℝ => x) (hermiteSchwartzMap n) +
        SchwartzMap.derivCLM ℝ ℝ (hermiteSchwartzMap n) =
      Real.sqrt (2 * (n : ℝ)) • hermiteSchwartzMap (n - 1)

decls.name: TauCeti.mul_sub_deriv_hermiteSchwartzMap
decls.doc: The creation relation, as an equality in Schwartz space.
decls.statement:
theorem mul_sub_deriv_hermiteSchwartzMap (n : ℕ) :
    SchwartzMap.smulLeftCLM ℝ (fun x : ℝ => x) (hermiteSchwartzMap n) -
        SchwartzMap.derivCLM ℝ ℝ (hermiteSchwartzMap n) =
      Real.sqrt (2 * ((n : ℝ) + 1)) • hermiteSchwartzMap (n + 1)

decls.name: TauCeti.integrable_aeval_mul_gaussian
decls.doc:
**Integrability of a polynomial against the Gaussian weight** `e^{-x²/2}`: every real
polynomial, evaluated pointwise and multiplied by the Gaussian weight, is Lebesgue-integrable.
decls.title: Integrability of a polynomial against the Gaussian weight
decls.statement:
theorem integrable_aeval_mul_gaussian (p : ℤ[X]) :
    Integrable (fun x : ℝ => aeval x p * Real.exp (-(x ^ 2 / 2)))

decls.name: TauCeti.aeval_derivative_hermite
decls.doc:
The Rodrigues-type step behind the recursion, at the level of `aeval`: from Mathlib's defining
recursion `hermite (n+1) = X · hermite n - derivative (hermite n)`,
`H'ₙ(x) = x · Hₙ(x) - H_{n+1}(x)`.
decls.statement:
theorem aeval_derivative_hermite (n : ℕ) (x : ℝ) :
    aeval x (derivative (hermite n)) = x * aeval x (hermite n) - aeval x (hermite (n + 1))

decls.name: TauCeti.integrable_aeval_mul_aeval_mul_gaussian
decls.doc:
A product of two `aeval`s of polynomials against the Gaussian weight `e^{-x²/2}` is
Lebesgue-integrable.
decls.statement:
theorem integrable_aeval_mul_aeval_mul_gaussian (p q : ℤ[X]) :
    Integrable (fun x : ℝ => aeval x p * aeval x q * Real.exp (-(x ^ 2 / 2)))

decls.name: TauCeti.integral_aeval_mul_hermite_succ
decls.doc:
**One-step weighted-pairing recursion** (target A1): the weighted pairing of `p` with `H_{n+1}`
equals the weighted pairing of its derivative `p'` with `Hₙ`,
`∫ p · H_{n+1} · e^{-x²/2} = ∫ p' · Hₙ · e^{-x²/2}`.
decls.title: One-step weighted-pairing recursion
decls.statement:
theorem integral_aeval_mul_hermite_succ (p : ℤ[X]) (n : ℕ) :
    (∫ x : ℝ, aeval x p * aeval x (hermite (n + 1)) * Real.exp (-(x ^ 2 / 2)))
      = ∫ x : ℝ, aeval x (derivative p) * aeval x (hermite n) * Real.exp (-(x ^ 2 / 2))

decls.name: TauCeti.integral_aeval_mul_hermite
decls.doc:
**Iterated recursion**: pairing `p` with `Hₙ` against the Gaussian weight equals pairing the
`n`-th derivative of `p` with `H₀ = 1`, i.e. `∫ p · Hₙ · e^{-x²/2} = ∫ (dⁿ/dxⁿ p) · e^{-x²/2}`.
decls.title: Iterated recursion
decls.statement:
theorem integral_aeval_mul_hermite (p : ℤ[X]) (n : ℕ) :
    (∫ x : ℝ, aeval x p * aeval x (hermite n) * Real.exp (-(x ^ 2 / 2)))
      = ∫ x : ℝ, aeval x (derivative^[n] p) * Real.exp (-(x ^ 2 / 2))

decls.name: TauCeti.integral_gaussian_half
decls.doc: The Gaussian integral of the bare weight: `∫ x, e^{-x²/2} = √(2π)`.
decls.statement:
theorem integral_gaussian_half :
    (∫ x : ℝ, Real.exp (-(x ^ 2 / 2))) = Real.sqrt (2 * π)

decls.name: TauCeti.integral_hermite_swap
decls.doc: Commuting the two factors under the integral.
decls.statement:
theorem integral_hermite_swap (m n : ℕ) :
    (∫ x : ℝ, aeval x (hermite m) * aeval x (hermite n) * Real.exp (-(x ^ 2 / 2)))
      = ∫ x : ℝ, aeval x (hermite n) * aeval x (hermite m) * Real.exp (-(x ^ 2 / 2))

decls.name: TauCeti.integral_hermite_mul_hermite_mul_gaussian
decls.doc:
**The Hermite orthogonality relation, Lebesgue form** (milestone A1):
`∫ x, Hₘ(x) · Hₙ(x) · e^{-x²/2} = if m = n then n! · √(2π) else 0`.
decls.title: The Hermite orthogonality relation, Lebesgue form
decls.statement:
theorem integral_hermite_mul_hermite_mul_gaussian (m n : ℕ) :
    (∫ x : ℝ, aeval x (hermite m) * aeval x (hermite n) * Real.exp (-(x ^ 2 / 2)))
      = if m = n then (n.factorial : ℝ) * Real.sqrt (2 * π) else 0

decls.name: TauCeti.integral_hermite_mul_hermite_gaussianReal
decls.doc:
**The Hermite orthogonality relation, Gaussian-measure form** (milestone A1):
`∫ x, Hₘ(x) · Hₙ(x) ∂(gaussianReal 0 1) = if m = n then n! else 0`. This is the Lebesgue form
divided by the `√(2π)` density; it is the relation the Gaussian Hermite basis (A3′) consumes.
decls.title: The Hermite orthogonality relation, Gaussian-measure form
decls.statement:
theorem integral_hermite_mul_hermite_gaussianReal (m n : ℕ) :
    (∫ x : ℝ, aeval x (hermite m) * aeval x (hermite n) ∂(gaussianReal 0 1))
      = if m = n then (n.factorial : ℝ) else 0

decls.name: TauCeti.intervalIntegrable_exp_neg_mul_sin
decls.doc:
The exponential of a negative multiple of the sine is continuous, hence integrable on any
interval.
decls.statement:
theorem intervalIntegrable_exp_neg_mul_sin (c a b : ℝ) :
    IntervalIntegrable (fun θ => Real.exp (-c * Real.sin θ)) volume a b

decls.name: TauCeti.integral_exp_neg_mul
decls.doc: The elementary decaying exponential integral `∫₀^b e^{-kθ} dθ = (1 - e^{-kb})/k`.
decls.statement:
theorem integral_exp_neg_mul (k b : ℝ) (hk : k ≠ 0) :
    ∫ θ in (0 : ℝ)..b, Real.exp (-k * θ) = (1 - Real.exp (-k * b)) / k

decls.name: TauCeti.exp_neg_mul_sin_le
decls.doc: On `[0, π/2]` Jordan's inequality bounds the integrand by a decaying exponential.
decls.statement:
theorem exp_neg_mul_sin_le (c : ℝ) (hc : 0 ≤ c) {θ : ℝ} (hθ : θ ∈ Icc (0 : ℝ) (π / 2)) :
    Real.exp (-c * Real.sin θ) ≤ Real.exp (-(2 * c / π) * θ)

decls.name: TauCeti.integral_exp_neg_mul_sin_eq_two_mul
decls.doc:
Half the interval carries half the integral: `θ ↦ π - θ` exchanges `[0, π/2]` and
`[π/2, π]` and fixes `sin`.
decls.statement:
theorem integral_exp_neg_mul_sin_eq_two_mul (c : ℝ) :
    ∫ θ in (0 : ℝ)..π, Real.exp (-c * Real.sin θ)
      = 2 * ∫ θ in (0 : ℝ)..(π / 2), Real.exp (-c * Real.sin θ)

decls.name: TauCeti.integral_exp_neg_mul_sin_le
decls.doc:
**Jordan's integral bound.** For `c > 0`,
`∫₀^π e^{-c sin θ} dθ ≤ π / c`.
decls.title: Jordan's integral bound
decls.statement:
theorem integral_exp_neg_mul_sin_le (c : ℝ) (hc : 0 < c) :
    (∫ θ in (0 : ℝ)..π, Real.exp (-c * Real.sin θ)) ≤ π / c

decls.name: TauCeti.chebyshevCosineHilbertBasis
decls.doc:
The normalized cosine Hilbert basis of `L²((0, π])`, obtained by transporting the normalized
Chebyshev `T` basis under `x = cos θ`.
decls.statement:
def chebyshevCosineHilbertBasis :
    HilbertBasis ℕ 𝕜 (Lp 𝕜 2 chebyshevAngleMeasure)

decls.name: TauCeti.coeFn_chebyshevCosineHilbertBasis
decls.doc:
**Chebyshev-cosine basis correspondence.** The `n`th vector of the transported Chebyshev basis
is almost everywhere the scalar-cast normalized cosine `cos (nθ) / √cₙ`.
decls.title: Chebyshev-cosine basis correspondence
decls.statement:
theorem coeFn_chebyshevCosineHilbertBasis (n : ℕ) :
    ⇑(chebyshevCosineHilbertBasis 𝕜 n) =ᵐ[chebyshevAngleMeasure]
      fun θ => (algebraMap ℝ 𝕜) (normalizedChebyshevCosine n θ)

decls.name: TauCeti.chebyshevAngleMeasure
decls.doc:
Lebesgue measure on the angular interval `(0, π]`. The choice of half-open endpoints matches
`intervalIntegral.integral_of_le`; changing either endpoint does not change the measure.
decls.statement: def chebyshevAngleMeasure : Measure ℝ

decls.name: TauCeti.chebyshevAngleMeasure_def
decls.doc: The angular Chebyshev measure is Lebesgue measure restricted to `(0, π]`.
decls.statement:
theorem chebyshevAngleMeasure_def :
    chebyshevAngleMeasure = volume.restrict (Set.Ioc 0 Real.pi)

decls.name: TauCeti.integral_chebyshevAngleMeasure
decls.doc: Integrating against `chebyshevAngleMeasure` is interval integration from `0` to `π`.
decls.statement:
theorem integral_chebyshevAngleMeasure {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E]
    (f : ℝ → E) :
    ∫ θ, f θ ∂chebyshevAngleMeasure = ∫ θ in (0)..Real.pi, f θ

decls.name: TauCeti.map_cos_chebyshevAngleMeasure
decls.doc: The pushforward of angular Lebesgue measure under `cos` is the Chebyshev measure.
decls.statement:
theorem map_cos_chebyshevAngleMeasure :
    Measure.map Real.cos chebyshevAngleMeasure = measureT

decls.name: TauCeti.measurePreserving_cos_chebyshev
decls.doc: The cosine change of variables preserves `chebyshevAngleMeasure` and `measureT`.
decls.statement:
theorem measurePreserving_cos_chebyshev :
    MeasurePreserving Real.cos chebyshevAngleMeasure measureT

decls.name: TauCeti.cos_comp_arccos_ae
decls.doc:
The Chebyshev measure is concentrated on `[-1, 1]`, so `cos (arccos x) = x` almost
everywhere.
decls.statement:
theorem cos_comp_arccos_ae :
    Real.cos ∘ Real.arccos =ᵐ[measureT] id

decls.name: TauCeti.arccos_comp_cos_ae
decls.doc:
Angular Lebesgue measure is concentrated on `(0, π]`, so `arccos (cos θ) = θ` almost
everywhere.
decls.statement:
theorem arccos_comp_cos_ae :
    Real.arccos ∘ Real.cos =ᵐ[chebyshevAngleMeasure] id

decls.name: TauCeti.measurePreserving_arccos_chebyshev
decls.doc: The inverse change of variables `arccos` preserves the Chebyshev and angular measures.
decls.statement:
theorem measurePreserving_arccos_chebyshev :
    MeasurePreserving Real.arccos measureT chebyshevAngleMeasure

decls.name: TauCeti.chebyshevCosineL2Isometry
decls.statement:
def chebyshevCosineL2Isometry :
    Lp 𝕜 2 measureT →ₗᵢ[𝕜] Lp 𝕜 2 chebyshevAngleMeasure

decls.name: TauCeti.chebyshevArccosL2LinearMap
decls.statement:
def chebyshevArccosL2LinearMap :
    Lp 𝕜 2 chebyshevAngleMeasure →ₗ[𝕜] Lp 𝕜 2 measureT

decls.name: TauCeti.chebyshevCosineL2Isometry_toLinearMap_apply
decls.statement:
theorem chebyshevCosineL2Isometry_toLinearMap_apply (f : Lp 𝕜 2 measureT) :
    (chebyshevCosineL2Isometry 𝕜).toLinearMap f =
      Lp.compMeasurePreserving Real.cos measurePreserving_cos_chebyshev f

decls.name: TauCeti.chebyshevCosineL2Isometry_apply
decls.statement:
theorem chebyshevCosineL2Isometry_apply (f : Lp 𝕜 2 measureT) :
    chebyshevCosineL2Isometry 𝕜 f =
      Lp.compMeasurePreserving Real.cos measurePreserving_cos_chebyshev f

decls.name: TauCeti.chebyshevArccosL2LinearMap_apply
decls.statement:
theorem chebyshevArccosL2LinearMap_apply (f : Lp 𝕜 2 chebyshevAngleMeasure) :
    chebyshevArccosL2LinearMap 𝕜 f =
      Lp.compMeasurePreserving Real.arccos measurePreserving_arccos_chebyshev f

decls.name: TauCeti.chebyshevCosineL2Isometry_comp_arccos
decls.statement:
theorem chebyshevCosineL2Isometry_comp_arccos :
    (chebyshevCosineL2Isometry 𝕜).toLinearMap.comp (chebyshevArccosL2LinearMap 𝕜) =

decls.statement:
theorem chebyshevArccosL2LinearMap_comp_cosine :
